533 @functools.lru_cache(maxsize=1)
534 def _get_assertion_exprs(src: bytes) -> Dict[int, str]:
535     """Return a mapping from {lineno: "assertion test expression"}."""
536     ret: Dict[int, str] = {}
537 
538     depth = 0
539     lines: List[str] = []
540     assert_lineno: Optional[int] = None
541     seen_lines: Set[int] = set()
542 
543     def _write_and_reset() -> None:
544         nonlocal depth, lines, assert_lineno, seen_lines
545         assert assert_lineno is not None
546         ret[assert_lineno] = "".join(lines).rstrip().rstrip("\\")
547         depth = 0
548         lines = []
549         assert_lineno = None
550         seen_lines = set()
551 
552     tokens = tokenize.tokenize(io.BytesIO(src).readline)
553     for tp, source, (lineno, offset), _, line in tokens:
554         if tp == tokenize.NAME and source == "assert":
555             assert_lineno = lineno
556         elif assert_lineno is not None:
557             # keep track of depth for the assert-message `,` lookup
558             if tp == tokenize.OP and source in "([{":
559                 depth += 1
560             elif tp == tokenize.OP and source in ")]}":
561                 depth -= 1
562 
563             if not lines:
564                 lines.append(line[offset:])
565                 seen_lines.add(lineno)
566             # a non-nested comma separates the expression from the message
567             elif depth == 0 and tp == tokenize.OP and source == ",":
568                 # one line assert with message
569                 if lineno in seen_lines and len(lines) == 1:
570                     offset_in_trimmed = offset + len(lines[-1]) - len(line)
571                     lines[-1] = lines[-1][:offset_in_trimmed]
572                 # multi-line assert with message
573                 elif lineno in seen_lines:
574                     lines[-1] = lines[-1][:offset]
575                 # multi line assert with escapd newline before message
576                 else:
577                     lines.append(line[:offset])
578                 _write_and_reset()
579             elif tp in {tokenize.NEWLINE, tokenize.ENDMARKER}:
580                 _write_and_reset()
581             elif lines and lineno not in seen_lines:
582                 lines.append(line)
583                 seen_lines.add(lineno)
584 
585     return ret

588 class AssertionRewriter(ast.NodeVisitor):
589     """Assertion rewriting implementation.
590 
591     The main entrypoint is to call .run() with an ast.Module instance,
592     this will then find all the assert statements and rewrite them to
593     provide intermediate values and a detailed assertion error.  See
594     http://pybites.blogspot.be/2011/07/behind-scenes-of-pytests-new-assertion.html
595     for an overview of how this works.
596 
597     The entry point here is .run() which will iterate over all the
598     statements in an ast.Module and for each ast.Assert statement it
599     finds call .visit() with it.  Then .visit_Assert() takes over and
600     is responsible for creating new ast statements to replace the
601     original assert statement: it rewrites the test of an assertion
602     to provide intermediate values and replace it with an if statement
603     which raises an assertion error with a detailed explanation in
604     case the expression is false and calls pytest_assertion_pass hook
605     if expression is true.
606 
607     For this .visit_Assert() uses the visitor pattern to visit all the
608     AST nodes of the ast.Assert.test field, each visit call returning
609     an AST node and the corresponding explanation string.  During this
610     state is kept in several instance attributes:
611 
612     :statements: All the AST statements which will replace the assert
613        statement.
614 
615     :variables: This is populated by .variable() with each variable
616        used by the statements so that they can all be set to None at
617        the end of the statements.
618 
619     :variable_counter: Counter to create new unique variables needed
620        by statements.  Variables are created using .variable() and
621        have the form of "@py_assert0".
622 
623     :expl_stmts: The AST statements which will be executed to get
624        data from the assertion.  This is the code which will construct
625        the detailed assertion message that is used in the AssertionError
626        or for the pytest_assertion_pass hook.
627 
628     :explanation_specifiers: A dict filled by .explanation_param()
629        with %-formatting placeholders and their corresponding
630        expressions to use in the building of an assertion message.
631        This is used by .pop_format_context() to build a message.
632 
633     :stack: A stack of the explanation_specifiers dicts maintained by
634        .push_format_context() and .pop_format_context() which allows
635        to build another %-formatted string while already building one.
636 
637     :variables_overwrite: A dict filled with references to variables
638        that change value within an assert. This happens when a variable is
639        reassigned with the walrus operator
640 
641     This state, except the variables_overwrite,  is reset on every new assert
642     statement visited and used by the other visitors.
643     """
644 
645     def __init__(
646         self, module_path: Optional[str], config: Optional[Config], source: bytes
647     ) -> None:
648         super().__init__()
649         self.module_path = module_path
650         self.config = config
651         if config is not None:
652             self.enable_assertion_pass_hook = config.getini(
653                 "enable_assertion_pass_hook"
654             )
655         else:
656             self.enable_assertion_pass_hook = False
657         self.source = source

text: You will be provided with a partial code base and an issue statement explaining a problem to resolve. Point.vel() should calculate the velocity if possible If you specify the orientation of two reference frames and then ask for the angular velocity between the two reference frames the angular velocity will be calculated. But if you try to do the same thing with velocities, this doesn't work. See below: ``` In [1]: import sympy as sm In [2]: import sympy.physics.mechanics as me In [3]: A = me.ReferenceFrame('A') In [5]: q = me.dynamicsymbols('q') In [6]: B = A.orientnew('B', 'Axis', (q, A.x)) In [7]: B.ang_vel_in(A) Out[7]: q'*A.x In [9]: P = me.Point('P') In [10]: Q = me.Point('Q') In [11]: r = q*A.x + 2*q*A.y In [12]: Q.set_pos(P, r) In [13]: Q.vel(A) --------------------------------------------------------------------------- ValueError Traceback (most recent call last) in ----> 1 Q.vel(A) ~/miniconda3/lib/python3.6/site-packages/sympy/physics/vector/point.py in vel(self, frame) 453 if not (frame in self._vel_dict): 454 raise ValueError('Velocity of point ' + self.name + ' has not been' --> 455 ' defined in ReferenceFrame ' + frame.name) 456 return self._vel_dict[frame] 457 ValueError: Velocity of point Q has not been defined in ReferenceFrame A ``` The expected result of the `Q.vel(A)` should be: ``` In [14]: r.dt(A) Out[14]: q'*A.x + 2*q'*A.y ``` I think that this is possible. Maybe there is a reason it isn't implemented. But we should try to implement it because it is confusing why this works for orientations and not positions. problem_statement:
Point.vel() should calculate the velocity if possible
If you specify the orientation of two reference frames and then ask for the angular velocity between the two reference frames the angular velocity will be calculated. But if you try to do the same thing with velocities, this doesn't work. See below:

```
In [1]: import sympy as sm                                                                               

In [2]: import sympy.physics.mechanics as me                                                             

In [3]: A = me.ReferenceFrame('A')                                                                       

In [5]: q = me.dynamicsymbols('q')                                                                       

In [6]: B = A.orientnew('B', 'Axis', (q, A.x))                                                           

In [7]: B.ang_vel_in(A)                                                                                  
Out[7]: q'*A.x

In [9]: P = me.Point('P')                                                                                

In [10]: Q = me.Point('Q')                                                                               

In [11]: r = q*A.x + 2*q*A.y                                                                             

In [12]: Q.set_pos(P, r)                                                                                 

In [13]: Q.vel(A)                                                                                        
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
ValueError                                Traceback (most recent call last)
<ipython-input-13-0fc8041904cc> in <module>
----> 1 Q.vel(A)

~/miniconda3/lib/python3.6/site-packages/sympy/physics/vector/point.py in vel(self, frame)
    453         if not (frame in self._vel_dict):
    454             raise ValueError('Velocity of point ' + self.name + ' has not been'
--> 455                              ' defined in ReferenceFrame ' + frame.name)
    456         return self._vel_dict[frame]
    457 

ValueError: Velocity of point Q has not been defined in ReferenceFrame A
```

The expected result of the `Q.vel(A)` should be:

```
In [14]: r.dt(A)                                                                                         
Out[14]: q'*A.x + 2*q'*A.y
```

I think that this is possible. Maybe there is a reason it isn't implemented. But we should try to implement it because it is confusing why this works for orientations and not positions.

problem_statement:
Wrong Derivative kind attribute
I'm playing around with the `kind` attribute.

The following is correct:

```
from sympy import Integral, Derivative
from sympy import MatrixSymbol
from sympy.abc import x
A = MatrixSymbol('A', 2, 2)
i = Integral(A, x)
i.kind
# MatrixKind(NumberKind)
```

This one is wrong:
```
d = Derivative(A, x)
d.kind
# UndefinedKind
```
hints_text:
As I dig deeper into this issue, the problem is much larger than `Derivative`. As a matter of facts, all functions should be able to deal with `kind`. At the moment:

```
from sympy import MatrixSymbol
A = MatrixSymbol('A', 2, 2)
sin(A).kind
# UndefinedKind
```
The kind attribute is new and is not fully implemented or used across the codebase.

For `sin` and other functions I don't think that we should allow the ordinary `sin` function to be used for the Matrix sin. There should be a separate `MatrixSin` function for that.

For Derivative the handler for kind just needs to be added.

346     def run(self) -> List[Node]:
347         node = addnodes.glossary()
348         node.document = self.state.document
349 
350         # This directive implements a custom format of the reST definition list
351         # that allows multiple lines of terms before the definition.  This is
352         # easy to parse since we know that the contents of the glossary *must
353         # be* a definition list.
354 
355         # first, collect single entries
356         entries = []  # type: List[Tuple[List[Tuple[str, str, int]], StringList]]
357         in_definition = True
358         in_comment = False
359         was_empty = True
360         messages = []  # type: List[Node]
361         for line, (source, lineno) in zip(self.content, self.content.items):
362             # empty line -> add to last definition
363             if not line:
364                 if in_definition and entries:
365                     entries[-1][1].append('', source, lineno)
366                 was_empty = True
367                 continue
368             # unindented line -> a term
369             if line and not line[0].isspace():
370                 # enable comments
371                 if line.startswith('.. '):
372                     in_comment = True
373                     continue
374                 else:
375                     in_comment = False
376 
377                 # first term of definition
378                 if in_definition:
379                     if not was_empty:
380                         messages.append(self.state.reporter.warning(
381                             _('glossary term must be preceded by empty line'),
382                             source=source, line=lineno))
383                     entries.append(([(line, source, lineno)], StringList()))
384                     in_definition = False
385                 # second term and following
386                 else:
387                     if was_empty:
388                         messages.append(self.state.reporter.warning(
389                             _('glossary terms must not be separated by empty lines'),
390                             source=source, line=lineno))
391                     if entries:
392                         entries[-1][0].append((line, source, lineno))
393                     else:
394                         messages.append(self.state.reporter.warning(
395                             _('glossary seems to be misformatted, check indentation'),
396                             source=source, line=lineno))
397             elif in_comment:
398                 pass
399             else:
400                 if not in_definition:
401                     # first line of definition, determines indentation
402                     in_definition = True
403                     indent_len = len(line) - len(line.lstrip())
404                 if entries:
405                     entries[-1][1].append(line[indent_len:], source, lineno)
406                 else:
407                     messages.append(self.state.reporter.warning(
408                         _('glossary seems to be misformatted, check indentation'),
409                         source=source, line=lineno))
410             was_empty = False
411 
412         # now, parse all the entries into a big definition list
413         items = []
414         for terms, definition in entries:
415             termtexts = []          # type: List[str]
416             termnodes = []          # type: List[Node]
417             system_messages = []    # type: List[Node]
418             for line, source, lineno in terms:
419                 parts = split_term_classifiers(line)
420                 # parse the term with inline markup
421                 # classifiers (parts[1:]) will not be shown on doctree
422                 textnodes, sysmsg = self.state.inline_text(parts[0], lineno)
423 
424                 # use first classifier as a index key
425                 term = make_glossary_term(self.env, textnodes, parts[1], source, lineno,
426                                           document=self.state.document)
427                 term.rawsource = line
428                 system_messages.extend(sysmsg)
429                 termtexts.append(term.astext())
430                 termnodes.append(term)
431 
432             termnodes.extend(system_messages)
433 
434             defnode = nodes.definition()
435             if definition:
436                 self.state.nested_parse(definition, definition.items[0][1],
437                                         defnode)
438             termnodes.append(defnode)
439             items.append((termtexts,
440                           nodes.definition_list_item('', *termnodes)))
441 
442         if 'sorted' in self.options:

444                        unicodedata.normalize('NFD', x[0][0].lower()))

447         dlist['classes'].append('glossary')

453 def token_xrefs(text: str, productionGroup: str = '') -> List[Node]:
454     if len(productionGroup) != 0:
455         productionGroup += ':'
456     retnodes = []  # type: List[Node]
457     pos = 0
458     for m in token_re.finditer(text):
459         if m.start() > pos:
460             txt = text[pos:m.start()]
461             retnodes.append(nodes.Text(txt, txt))
462         refnode = pending_xref(m.group(1), reftype='token', refdomain='std',
463                                reftarget=productionGroup + m.group(1))
464         refnode += nodes.literal(m.group(1), m.group(1), classes=['xref'])
465         retnodes.append(refnode)
466         pos = m.end()
467     if pos < len(text):
468         retnodes.append(nodes.Text(text[pos:], text[pos:]))
469     return retnodes

472 class ProductionList(SphinxDirective):
473     """
474     Directive to list grammar productions.
475     """
476 
477     has_content = False
478     required_arguments = 1
479     optional_arguments = 0
480     final_argument_whitespace = True
481     option_spec = {}  # type: Dict
482 
483     def run(self) -> List[Node]:
484         domain = cast(StandardDomain, self.env.get_domain('std'))
485         node = addnodes.productionlist()  # type: Element
486         self.set_source_info(node)
487         # The backslash handling is from ObjectDescription.get_signatures
488         nl_escape_re = re.compile(r'\\\n')
489         lines = nl_escape_re.sub('', self.arguments[0]).split('\n')
490 
491         productionGroup = ""
492         i = 0
493         for rule in lines:
494             if i == 0 and ':' not in rule:
495                 productionGroup = rule.strip()
496                 continue
497             i += 1
498             try:
499                 name, tokens = rule.split(':', 1)
500             except ValueError:
501                 break
502             subnode = addnodes.production(rule)
503             name = name.strip()
504             subnode['tokenname'] = name
505             if subnode['tokenname']:
506                 prefix = 'grammar-token-%s' % productionGroup
507                 node_id = make_id(self.env, self.state.document, prefix, name)
508                 subnode['ids'].append(node_id)
509 
510                 # Assign old styled node_id not to break old hyperlinks (if possible)
511                 # Note: Will be removed in Sphinx-5.0 (RemovedInSphinx50Warning)
512                 old_node_id = self.make_old_id(name)
513                 if (old_node_id not in self.state.document.ids and
514                         old_node_id not in subnode['ids']):
515                     subnode['ids'].append(old_node_id)
516 
517                 self.state.document.note_implicit_target(subnode, subnode)
518 
519                 if len(productionGroup) != 0:
520                     objName = "%s:%s" % (productionGroup, name)
521                 else:
522                     objName = name
523                 domain.note_object('token', objName, node_id, location=node)
524             subnode.extend(token_xrefs(tokens, productionGroup))
525             node.append(subnode)
526         return [node]
527 
528     def make_old_id(self, token: str) -> str:
529         """Generate old styled node_id for tokens.
530 
531         .. note:: Old Styled node_id was used until Sphinx-3.0.
532                   This will be removed in Sphinx-5.0.
533         """
534         return nodes.make_id('grammar-token-' + token)

720     def process_doc(self, env: "BuildEnvironment", docname: str, document: nodes.document) -> None:  # NOQA
721         for name, explicit in document.nametypes.items():
722             if not explicit:
723                 continue
724             labelid = document.nameids[name]
725             if labelid is None:
726                 continue
727             node = document.ids[labelid]
728             if isinstance(node, nodes.target) and 'refid' in node:
729                 # indirect hyperlink targets
730                 node = document.ids.get(node['refid'])
731                 labelid = node['names'][0]
732             if (node.tagname == 'footnote' or
733                     'refuri' in node or
734                     node.tagname.startswith('desc_')):
735                 # ignore footnote labels, labels automatically generated from a
736                 # link and object descriptions
737                 continue
738             if name in self.labels:
739                 logger.warning(__('duplicate label %s, other instance in %s'),
740                                name, env.doc2path(self.labels[name][0]),
741                                location=node)
742             self.anonlabels[name] = docname, labelid
743             if node.tagname in ('section', 'rubric'):
744                 title = cast(nodes.title, node[0])
745                 sectname = clean_astext(title)
746             elif self.is_enumerable_node(node):
747                 sectname = self.get_numfig_title(node)
748                 if not sectname:
749                     continue
750             else:
751                 toctree = next(iter(node.traverse(addnodes.toctree)), None)
752                 if toctree and toctree.get('caption'):
753                     sectname = toctree.get('caption')
754                 else:
755                     # anonymous-only labels
756                     continue
757             self.labels[name] = docname, labelid, sectname

762     def build_reference_node(self, fromdocname: str, builder: "Builder", docname: str,
763                              labelid: str, sectname: str, rolename: str, **options: Any
764                              ) -> Element:
765         nodeclass = options.pop('nodeclass', nodes.reference)
766         newnode = nodeclass('', '', internal=True, **options)
767         innernode = nodes.inline(sectname, sectname)
768         if innernode.get('classes') is not None:
769             innernode['classes'].append('std')
770             innernode['classes'].append('std-' + rolename)
771         if docname == fromdocname:
772             newnode['refid'] = labelid
773         else:
774             # set more info in contnode; in case the
775             # get_relative_uri call raises NoUri,
776             # the builder will then have to resolve these
777             contnode = pending_xref('')
778             contnode['refdocname'] = docname
779             contnode['refsectname'] = sectname
780             newnode['refuri'] = builder.get_relative_uri(
781                 fromdocname, docname)
782             if labelid:
783                 newnode['refuri'] += '#' + labelid
784         newnode.append(innernode)
785         return newnode

787     def resolve_xref(self, env: "BuildEnvironment", fromdocname: str, builder: "Builder",
788                      typ: str, target: str, node: pending_xref, contnode: Element) -> Element:
789         if typ == 'ref':
790             resolver = self._resolve_ref_xref
791         elif typ == 'numref':
792             resolver = self._resolve_numref_xref
793         elif typ == 'keyword':
794             resolver = self._resolve_keyword_xref
795         elif typ == 'doc':
796             resolver = self._resolve_doc_xref
797         elif typ == 'option':
798             resolver = self._resolve_option_xref
799         elif typ == 'citation':
800             warnings.warn('pending_xref(domain=std, type=citation) is deprecated: %r' % node,
801                           RemovedInSphinx40Warning, stacklevel=2)
802             domain = env.get_domain('citation')
803             return domain.resolve_xref(env, fromdocname, builder, typ, target, node, contnode)
804         elif typ == 'term':
805             resolver = self._resolve_term_xref
806         else:
807             resolver = self._resolve_obj_xref
808 
809         return resolver(env, fromdocname, builder, typ, target, node, contnode)

811     def _resolve_ref_xref(self, env: "BuildEnvironment", fromdocname: str,
812                           builder: "Builder", typ: str, target: str, node: pending_xref,
813                           contnode: Element) -> Element:
814         if node['refexplicit']:
815             # reference to anonymous label; the reference uses
816             # the supplied link caption
817             docname, labelid = self.anonlabels.get(target, ('', ''))
818             sectname = node.astext()
819         else:
820             # reference to named label; the final node will
821             # contain the section name after the label
822             docname, labelid, sectname = self.labels.get(target, ('', '', ''))
823         if not docname:
824             return None
825 
826         return self.build_reference_node(fromdocname, builder,
827                                          docname, labelid, sectname, 'ref')
828 
829     def _resolve_numref_xref(self, env: "BuildEnvironment", fromdocname: str,
830                              builder: "Builder", typ: str, target: str,
831                              node: pending_xref, contnode: Element) -> Element:
832         if target in self.labels:
833             docname, labelid, figname = self.labels.get(target, ('', '', ''))
834         else:
835             docname, labelid = self.anonlabels.get(target, ('', ''))
836             figname = None
837 
838         if not docname:
839             return None
840 
841         target_node = env.get_doctree(docname).ids.get(labelid)
842         figtype = self.get_enumerable_node_type(target_node)
843         if figtype is None:
844             return None
845 
846         if figtype != 'section' and env.config.numfig is False:
847             logger.warning(__('numfig is disabled. :numref: is ignored.'), location=node)
848             return contnode
849 
850         try:
851             fignumber = self.get_fignumber(env, builder, figtype, docname, target_node)
852             if fignumber is None:
853                 return contnode
854         except ValueError:
855             logger.warning(__("no number is assigned for %s: %s"), figtype, labelid,
856                            location=node)
857             return contnode
858 
859         try:
860             if node['refexplicit']:
861                 title = contnode.astext()
862             else:
863                 title = env.config.numfig_format.get(figtype, '')
864 
865             if figname is None and '{name}' in title:
866                 logger.warning(__('the link has no caption: %s'), title, location=node)
867                 return contnode
868             else:
869                 fignum = '.'.join(map(str, fignumber))
870                 if '{name}' in title or 'number' in title:
871                     # new style format (cf. "Fig.{number}")
872                     if figname:
873                         newtitle = title.format(name=figname, number=fignum)
874                     else:
875                         newtitle = title.format(number=fignum)
876                 else:
877                     # old style format (cf. "Fig.%s")
878                     newtitle = title % fignum
879         except KeyError as exc:
880             logger.warning(__('invalid numfig_format: %s (%r)'), title, exc, location=node)
881             return contnode
882         except TypeError:
883             logger.warning(__('invalid numfig_format: %s'), title, location=node)
884             return contnode
885 
886         return self.build_reference_node(fromdocname, builder,
887                                          docname, labelid, newtitle, 'numref',
888                                          nodeclass=addnodes.number_reference,
889                                          title=title)
890

901     def _resolve_doc_xref(self, env: "BuildEnvironment", fromdocname: str,
902                           builder: "Builder", typ: str, target: str,
903                           node: pending_xref, contnode: Element) -> Element:
904         # directly reference to document by source name; can be absolute or relative
905         refdoc = node.get('refdoc', fromdocname)
906         docname = docname_join(refdoc, node['reftarget'])
907         if docname not in env.all_docs:
908             return None
909         else:
910             if node['refexplicit']:
911                 # reference with explicit title
912                 caption = node.astext()
913             else:
914                 caption = clean_astext(env.titles[docname])
915             innernode = nodes.inline(caption, caption, classes=['doc'])

918     def _resolve_option_xref(self, env: "BuildEnvironment", fromdocname: str,
919                              builder: "Builder", typ: str, target: str,
920                              node: pending_xref, contnode: Element) -> Element:
921         progname = node.get('std:program')
922         target = target.strip()
923         docname, labelid = self.progoptions.get((progname, target), ('', ''))
924         if not docname:
925             commands = []
926             while ws_re.search(target):
927                 subcommand, target = ws_re.split(target, 1)
928                 commands.append(subcommand)
929                 progname = "-".join(commands)
930 
931                 docname, labelid = self.progoptions.get((progname, target), ('', ''))
932                 if docname:
933                     break
934             else:
935                 return None
936 
937         return make_refnode(builder, fromdocname, docname,
938                             labelid, contnode)

940     def _resolve_term_xref(self, env: "BuildEnvironment", fromdocname: str,
941                            builder: "Builder", typ: str, target: str,
942                            node: pending_xref, contnode: Element) -> Element:
943         result = self._resolve_obj_xref(env, fromdocname, builder, typ,
944                                         target, node, contnode)
945         if result:
946             return result
947         else:
948             for objtype, term in self.objects:
949                 if objtype == 'term' and term.lower() == target.lower():
950                     docname, labelid = self.objects[objtype, term]
951                     logger.warning(__('term %s not found in case sensitive match.'
952                                       'made a reference to %s instead.'),
953                                    target, term, location=node, type='ref', subtype='term')
954                     break
955             else:
956                 docname, labelid = '', ''
957             if not docname:
958                 return None
959             return make_refnode(builder, fromdocname, docname,
960                                 labelid, contnode)

962     def _resolve_obj_xref(self, env: "BuildEnvironment", fromdocname: str,
963                           builder: "Builder", typ: str, target: str,
964                           node: pending_xref, contnode: Element) -> Element:
965         objtypes = self.objtypes_for_role(typ) or []
966         for objtype in objtypes:
967             if (objtype, target) in self.objects:
968                 docname, labelid = self.objects[objtype, target]
969                 break
970         else:
971             docname, labelid = '', ''
972         if not docname:
973             return None

975                             labelid, contnode)

977     def resolve_any_xref(self, env: "BuildEnvironment", fromdocname: str,
978                          builder: "Builder", target: str, node: pending_xref,
979                          contnode: Element) -> List[Tuple[str, Element]]:
980         results = []  # type: List[Tuple[str, Element]]
981         ltarget = target.lower()  # :ref: lowercases its target automatically
982         for role in ('ref', 'option'):  # do not try "keyword"
983             res = self.resolve_xref(env, fromdocname, builder, role,
984                                     ltarget if role == 'ref' else target,
985                                     node, contnode)
986             if res:
987                 results.append(('std:' + role, res))
988         # all others
989         for objtype in self.object_types:
990             key = (objtype, target)
991             if objtype == 'term':
992                 key = (objtype, ltarget)
993             if key in self.objects:
994                 docname, labelid = self.objects[key]
995                 results.append(('std:' + self.role_for_objtype(objtype),
996                                 make_refnode(builder, fromdocname, docname,
997                                              labelid, contnode)))
998         return results

1000     def get_objects(self) -> Iterator[Tuple[str, str, str, str, str, int]]:
1001         # handle the special 'doc' reference here
1002         for doc in self.env.all_docs:
1003             yield (doc, clean_astext(self.env.titles[doc]), 'doc', doc, '', -1)
1004         for (prog, option), info in self.progoptions.items():
1005             if prog:
1006                 fullname = ".".join([prog, option])
1007                 yield (fullname, fullname, 'cmdoption', info[0], info[1], 1)
1008             else:
1009                 yield (option, option, 'cmdoption', info[0], info[1], 1)
1010         for (type, name), info in self.objects.items():
1011             yield (name, name, type, info[0], info[1],
1012                    self.object_types[type].attrs['searchprio'])
1013         for name, (docname, labelid, sectionname) in self.labels.items():
1014             yield (name, sectionname, 'label', docname, labelid, -1)
1015         # add anonymous-only labels as well
1016         non_anon_labels = set(self.labels)
1017         for name, (docname, labelid) in self.anonlabels.items():
1018             if name not in non_anon_labels:
1019                 yield (name, name, 'label', docname, labelid, -1)

1028     def get_numfig_title(self, node: Node) -> str:
1029         """Get the title of enumerable nodes to refer them using its title"""
1030         if self.is_enumerable_node(node):
1031             elem = cast(Element, node)
1032             _, title_getter = self.enumerable_nodes.get(elem.__class__, (None, None))
1033             if title_getter:
1034                 return title_getter(elem)
1035             else:
1036                 for subnode in elem:
1037                     if isinstance(subnode, (nodes.caption, nodes.title)):
1038                         return clean_astext(subnode)
1039 
1040         return None

1042     def get_enumerable_node_type(self, node: Node) -> str:

problem_statement:
v3.3 upgrade started generating "WARNING: no number is assigned for table" warnings
We've updated to Sphinx 3.3 in our documentation, and suddenly the following warning started popping up in our builds when we build either `singlehtml` or `latex`.:

`WARNING: no number is assigned for table:`

I looked through the changelog but it didn't seem like there was anything related to `numref` that was changed, but perhaps I missed something? Could anyone point me to a change in the numref logic so I can figure out where these warnings are coming from?
hints_text: I digged into this a little bit more and it seems like the `id` of the table isn't properly making it into `env.toc_fignumbers`. If I set `:name: mylabel`, regardless the I see something like this in `env.toc_fignumbers` ``` 'pagename': {'table': {'id3': (1,)}, ``` So it seems like `id3` is being used for the table id instead of `mylabel` @choldgraf I suspect it's related to this: https://github.com/sphinx-doc/sphinx/commit/66dda1fc50249e9da62e79380251d8795b8e36df. Oooohhh good find! 👏👏👏 Confirmed that this was the issue - we had been referencing Tables that didn't have a title with `numref`, and this bugfix (I guess it was a bugfix?) caused us to start raising errors. Perhaps this restriction about tables needing a title could be documented more clearly? The `numfig` option has been described as follows. >If true, figures, tables and code-blocks are automatically numbered if they have a caption. https://www.sphinx-doc.org/en/master/usage/configuration.html#confval-numfig It says a table not having a title is not assigned a number. Then `numfig` can't refer it because of no table number. > It says a table not having a title is not assigned a number. Then `numfig` can't refer it because of no table number. This means that a user is not able to add a numbered table with no caption correct? I could understand such restrictions for Jupyter Book but it doesn't make a lot of sense for Sphinx IMO. I think Sphinx should allow users to have enumerable nodes with no caption. What do you think @choldgraf? >This means that a user is not able to add a numbered table with no caption correct? Yes. Since the beginning, numfig feature only supports captioned figures and tables. I don't know how many people want to assign numbers to non-captioned items. But this is the first feature request, AFAIK. I think my take is that I don't think it is super useful to be able to have numbered references for things that don't have titles/captions. However, it also didn't feel like it *shouldn't* be possible, and so I assumed that it was possible (and thus ran into what I thought was a bug). I think it would be more helpful to surface a more informative warning like "You attempted to add a numbered reference to a Table without a title, add a title for this to work." (or, surface this gotcha in the documentation more obviously like with a `warning` or `note` directive?) @tk0miya @choldgraf both make good points for restricting `figure` and `table` directives with no caption. My issue is that this is done at the enumerable node which implies that **all** enumerable nodes with no title/caption are skipped - not just `figure` and `table`. > Since the beginning, numfig feature only supports captioned figures and tables. Just to clarify, `numfig` feature has - prior to v3.3.0 - supported uncaptioned tables but it did not display the caption. The user was able to reference the table using `numref` role (see example below). In the event that the user tried to reference the caption (aka `name` placeholder), Sphinx threw a warning indicating that there was no caption. This solution seemed sensible to me because it allowed other extensions to utilize enumerable nodes regardless of caption/no caption restriction. My main motivation for wanting to revert back or restrict the bugfix to tables and figures is because both the extensions I've worked on depend on the utilization of enumerable nodes regardless of captions/no captions. I think it wouldn't be too difficult to add the information to `env.toc_fignumbers` but I wanted to make a case before I addressed this in [sphinx-proof](https://github.com/executablebooks/sphinx-proof) and [sphinx-exercise](https://github.com/executablebooks/sphinx-exercise). **Example** Sphinx Version - v3.2.1 ````md ```{list-table} :header-rows: 1 :name: table1 * - Training - Validation * - 0 - 5 * - 13720 - 2744 ``` Referencing table using `numref`: {numref}`table1`. ```{list-table} Caption here :header-rows: 1 :name: table2 * - Training - Validation * - 0 - 5 * - 13720 - 2744 ``` Referencing table using `numref`: {numref}`table2`. ```` So it sounds like the `tl;dr` from @najuzilu is that in other extensions, she is *using* the fact that you can reference non-captioned elements with a number, and that Sphinx now removing this ability is breaking those extensions. Is that right? That's correct @choldgraf This is a screenshot of the PDF that is generated from @najuzilu 's example with v3.2.1. As you see, it does not work correctly in LaTeX output. I'd not like to support assigning numbers to no captioned items until fixed this (if somebody needs it).

You can control print order as described [here](https://stackoverflow.com/a/58541713/1089161).
The default order should not break the multiline bracket of pretty print. Please see the output in constant width mode or paste it in a text editor. The second output is fine while the right bracket is broken in the other two.
I can verify that this seems to be an issue specific to pretty print. The Latex renderer outputs what you want. This should be fixable. Here is an image of the output for your vectors from the latex rendered in Jupyter.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1231317/153658279-1cf4d387-2101-4cb3-b182-131ed3cbe1b8.png)

Admittedly the small outer parenthesis are not stylistically great, but the ordering is what you expect.
The LaTeX printer ought to be using \left and \right for parentheses.

ascii.qdp Table format assumes QDP commands are upper case
### Description

ascii.qdp assumes that commands in a QDP file are upper case, for example, for errors they must be "READ SERR 1 2" whereas QDP itself is not case sensitive and case use "read serr 1 2". 

As many QDP files are created by hand, the expectation that all commands be all-caps should be removed.

### Expected behavior

The following qdp file should read into a `Table` with errors, rather than crashing.
```
read serr 1 2 
1 0.5 1 0.5
```

### How to Reproduce

Create a QDP file:
```
> cat > test.qdp
read serr 1 2 
1 0.5 1 0.5
<EOF>

 > python
Python 3.10.9 (main, Dec  7 2022, 02:03:23) [Clang 13.0.0 (clang-1300.0.29.30)] on darwin
Type "help", "copyright", "credits" or "license" for more information.
>>> from astropy.table import Table
>>> Table.read('test.qdp',format='ascii.qdp')
WARNING: table_id not specified. Reading the first available table [astropy.io.ascii.qdp]
Traceback (most recent call last):
...
    raise ValueError(f'Unrecognized QDP line: {line}')
ValueError: Unrecognized QDP line: read serr 1 2
```

Running "qdp test.qdp" works just fine.


### Versions

Python 3.10.9 (main, Dec  7 2022, 02:03:23) [Clang 13.0.0 (clang-1300.0.29.30)]
astropy 5.1
Numpy 1.24.1
pyerfa 2.0.0.1
Scipy 1.10.0
Matplotlib 3.6.3

66     if delimiter is None:

237 def _get_tables_from_qdp_file(qdp_file, input_colnames=None, delimiter=None):
238     """Get all tables from a QDP file.
239 
240     Parameters
241     ----------
242     qdp_file : str
243         Input QDP file name
244 
245     Other Parameters
246     ----------------
247     input_colnames : list of str
248         Name of data columns (defaults to ['col1', 'col2', ...]), _not_
249         including error columns.
250     delimiter : str
251         Delimiter for the values in the table.
252 
253     Returns
254     -------
255     list of `~astropy.table.Table`
256         List containing all the tables present inside the QDP file
257     """
258     lines = _get_lines_from_file(qdp_file)
259     contents, ncol = _get_type_from_list_of_lines(lines, delimiter=delimiter)
260 
261     table_list = []
262     err_specs = {}
263     colnames = None
264 
265     comment_text = ""
266     initial_comments = ""
267     command_lines = ""
268     current_rows = None
269 
270     for line, datatype in zip(lines, contents):
271         line = line.strip().lstrip("!")
272         # Is this a comment?
273         if datatype == "comment":
274             comment_text += line + "\n"
275             continue
276 
277         if datatype == "command":
278             # The first time I find commands, I save whatever comments into
279             # The initial comments.
280             if command_lines == "":
281                 initial_comments = comment_text
282                 comment_text = ""
283 
284             if err_specs != {}:
285                 warnings.warn(
286                     "This file contains multiple command blocks. Please verify",
287                     AstropyUserWarning,
288                 )
289             command_lines += line + "\n"
290             continue
291 
292         if datatype.startswith("data"):
293             # The first time I find data, I define err_specs
294             if err_specs == {} and command_lines != "":
295                 for cline in command_lines.strip().split("\n"):
296                     command = cline.strip().split()
297                     # This should never happen, but just in case.
298                     if len(command) < 3:
299                         continue
300                     err_specs[command[1].lower()] = [int(c) for c in command[2:]]
301             if colnames is None:
302                 colnames = _interpret_err_lines(err_specs, ncol, names=input_colnames)
303 
304             if current_rows is None:
305                 current_rows = []
306 
307             values = []
308             for v in line.split(delimiter):
309                 if v == "NO":
310                     values.append(np.ma.masked)
311                 else:
312                     # Understand if number is int or float
313                     try:
314                         values.append(int(v))
315                     except ValueError:
316                         values.append(float(v))
317             current_rows.append(values)
318             continue
319 
320         if datatype == "new":
321             # Save table to table_list and reset
322             if current_rows is not None:
323                 new_table = Table(names=colnames, rows=current_rows)
324                 new_table.meta["initial_comments"] = initial_comments.strip().split(
325                     "\n"
326                 )
327                 new_table.meta["comments"] = comment_text.strip().split("\n")
328                 # Reset comments
329                 comment_text = ""
330                 table_list.append(new_table)
331                 current_rows = None
332             continue
333 
334     # At the very end, if there is still a table being written, let's save
335     # it to the table_list
336     if current_rows is not None:
337         new_table = Table(names=colnames, rows=current_rows)
338         new_table.meta["initial_comments"] = initial_comments.strip().split("\n")
339         new_table.meta["comments"] = comment_text.strip().split("\n")
340         table_list.append(new_table)
341 
342     return table_list

345 def _understand_err_col(colnames):
346     """Get which column names are error columns.
347 
348     Examples
349     --------
350     >>> colnames = ['a', 'a_err', 'b', 'b_perr', 'b_nerr']
351     >>> serr, terr = _understand_err_col(colnames)
352     >>> np.allclose(serr, [1])
353     True
354     >>> np.allclose(terr, [2])
355     True
356     >>> serr, terr = _understand_err_col(['a', 'a_nerr'])
357     Traceback (most recent call last):
358     ...
359     ValueError: Missing positive error...
360     >>> serr, terr = _understand_err_col(['a', 'a_perr'])
361     Traceback (most recent call last):
362     ...
363     ValueError: Missing negative error...
364     """
365     shift = 0
366     serr = []
367     terr = []
368 
369     for i, col in enumerate(colnames):
370         if col.endswith("_err"):
371             # The previous column, but they're numbered from 1!
372             # Plus, take shift into account
373             serr.append(i - shift)
374             shift += 1
375         elif col.endswith("_perr"):
376             terr.append(i - shift)
377             if len(colnames) == i + 1 or not colnames[i + 1].endswith("_nerr"):
378                 raise ValueError("Missing negative error")
379             shift += 2
380         elif col.endswith("_nerr") and not colnames[i - 1].endswith("_perr"):
381             raise ValueError("Missing positive error")
382     return serr, terr

463         print(f"READ TERR {col_string}", file=fobj)

466         for line in table.meta["comments"]:
467             line = line.strip()

474     for row in table:

476         for val in row:
477             if not np.ma.is_masked(val):

523 class QDP(basic.Basic):
524     """Quick and Dandy Plot table.
525 
526     Example::
527 
528         ! Initial comment line 1
529         ! Initial comment line 2
530         READ TERR 1
531         READ SERR 3
532         ! Table 0 comment
533         !a a(pos) a(neg) b be c d
534         53000.5   0.25  -0.5   1  1.5  3.5 2
535         54000.5   1.25  -1.5   2  2.5  4.5 3
536         NO NO NO NO NO
537         ! Table 1 comment
538         !a a(pos) a(neg) b be c d
539         54000.5   2.25  -2.5   NO  3.5  5.5 5
540         55000.5   3.25  -3.5   4  4.5  6.5 nan
541 
542     The input table above contains some initial comments, the error commands,
543     then two tables.
544     This file format can contain multiple tables, separated by a line full
545     of ``NO``s. Comments are exclamation marks, and missing values are single
546     ``NO`` entries. The delimiter is usually whitespace, more rarely a comma.
547     The QDP format differentiates between data and error columns. The table
548     above has commands::
549 
550         READ TERR 1
551         READ SERR 3
552 
553     which mean that after data column 1 there will be two error columns
554     containing its positive and engative error bars, then data column 2 without
555     error bars, then column 3, then a column with the symmetric error of column
556     3, then the remaining data columns.
557 
558     As explained below, table headers are highly inconsistent. Possible
559     comments containing column names will be ignored and columns will be called
560     ``col1``, ``col2``, etc. unless the user specifies their names with the
561     ``names=`` keyword argument,
562     When passing column names, pass **only the names of the data columns, not
563     the error columns.**
564     Error information will be encoded in the names of the table columns.
565     (e.g. ``a_perr`` and ``a_nerr`` for the positive and negative error of
566     column ``a``, ``b_err`` the symmetric error of column ``b``.)
567 
568     When writing tables to this format, users can pass an ``err_specs`` keyword
569     passing a dictionary ``{'serr': [3], 'terr': [1, 2]}``, meaning that data
570     columns 1 and two will have two additional columns each with their positive
571     and negative errors, and data column 3 will have an additional column with
572     a symmetric error (just like the ``READ SERR`` and ``READ TERR`` commands
573     above)
574 
575     Headers are just comments, and tables distributed by various missions
576     can differ greatly in their use of conventions. For example, light curves
577     distributed by the Swift-Gehrels mission have an extra space in one header
578     entry that makes the number of labels inconsistent with the number of cols.
579     For this reason, we ignore the comments that might encode the column names
580     and leave the name specification to the user.
581 
582     Example::
583 
584         >               Extra space
585         >                   |
586         >                   v
587         >!     MJD       Err (pos)       Err(neg)        Rate            Error
588         >53000.123456   2.378e-05     -2.378472e-05     NO             0.212439
589 
590     These readers and writer classes will strive to understand which of the
591     comments belong to all the tables, and which ones to each single table.
592     General comments will be stored in the ``initial_comments`` meta of each
593     table. The comments of each table will be stored in the ``comments`` meta.
594 
595     Example::
596 
597         t = Table.read(example_qdp, format='ascii.qdp', table_id=1, names=['a', 'b', 'c', 'd'])
598 
599     reads the second table (``table_id=1``) in file ``example.qdp`` containing
600     the table above. There are four column names but seven data columns, why?
601     Because the ``READ SERR`` and ``READ TERR`` commands say that there are
602     three error columns.
603     ``t.meta['initial_comments']`` will contain the initial two comment lines
604     in the file, while ``t.meta['comments']`` will contain ``Table 1 comment``
605 
606     The table can be written to another file, preserving the same information,
607     as::
608 
609         t.write(test_file, err_specs={'terr': [1], 'serr': [3]})
610 
611     Note how the ``terr`` and ``serr`` commands are passed to the writer.
612 
613     """
614 
615     _format_name = "qdp"
616     _io_registry_can_write = True
617     _io_registry_suffix = ".qdp"
618     _description = "Quick and Dandy Plotter"
619 
620     header_class = QDPHeader
621     data_class = QDPData
622 
623     def __init__(self, table_id=None, names=None, err_specs=None, sep=None):
624         super().__init__()

626         self.names = names

628         self.delimiter = sep

634             table_id=self.table_id,

problem_statement:
ascii.qdp Table format assumes QDP commands are upper case
### Description

ascii.qdp assumes that commands in a QDP file are upper case, for example, for errors they must be "READ SERR 1 2" whereas QDP itself is not case sensitive and case use "read serr 1 2". 

As many QDP files are created by hand, the expectation that all commands be all-caps should be removed.

### Expected behavior

The following qdp file should read into a `Table` with errors, rather than crashing.
```
read serr 1 2 
1 0.5 1 0.5
```

### How to Reproduce

Create a QDP file:
```
> cat > test.qdp
read serr 1 2 
1 0.5 1 0.5
<EOF>

 > python
Python 3.10.9 (main, Dec  7 2022, 02:03:23) [Clang 13.0.0 (clang-1300.0.29.30)] on darwin
Type "help", "copyright", "credits" or "license" for more information.
>>> from astropy.table import Table
>>> Table.read('test.qdp',format='ascii.qdp')
WARNING: table_id not specified. Reading the first available table [astropy.io.ascii.qdp]
Traceback (most recent call last):
...
    raise ValueError(f'Unrecognized QDP line: {line}')
ValueError: Unrecognized QDP line: read serr 1 2
```

Running "qdp test.qdp" works just fine.


### Versions

Python 3.10.9 (main, Dec  7 2022, 02:03:23) [Clang 13.0.0 (clang-1300.0.29.30)]
astropy 5.1
Numpy 1.24.1
pyerfa 2.0.0.1
Scipy 1.10.0
Matplotlib 3.6.3

[Bug]: ax.bar raises for all-nan data on matplotlib 3.6.1 
### Bug summary

`ax.bar` raises an exception in 3.6.1 when passed only nan data. This irrevocably breaks seaborn's histogram function (which draws and then removes a "phantom" bar to trip the color cycle).

### Code for reproduction

```python
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
f, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.bar([np.nan], [np.nan])
```


### Actual outcome

### Expected outcome

On 3.6.0 this returns a `BarCollection` with one Rectangle, having `nan` for `x` and `height`.

### Additional information

I assume it's related to this bullet in the release notes:

- Fix barplot being empty when first element is NaN

But I don't know the context for it to investigate further (could these link to PRs?)

Further debugging:

```python
ax.bar([np.nan], [0])  # Raises
ax.bar([0], [np.nan])  # Works
```

187     def legend(self, *args, **kwargs):
188         """
189         Place a legend on the Axes.
190 
191         Call signatures::
192 
193             legend()
194             legend(handles, labels)
195             legend(handles=handles)
196             legend(labels)
197 
198         The call signatures correspond to the following different ways to use
199         this method:
200 
201         **1. Automatic detection of elements to be shown in the legend**
202 
203         The elements to be added to the legend are automatically determined,
204         when you do not pass in any extra arguments.
205 
206         In this case, the labels are taken from the artist. You can specify
207         them either at artist creation or by calling the
208         :meth:`~.Artist.set_label` method on the artist::
209 
210             ax.plot([1, 2, 3], label='Inline label')
211             ax.legend()
212 
213         or::
214 
215             line, = ax.plot([1, 2, 3])
216             line.set_label('Label via method')
217             ax.legend()
218 
219         .. note::
220             Specific artists can be excluded from the automatic legend element
221             selection by using a label starting with an underscore, "_".
222             A string starting with an underscore is the default label for all
223             artists, so calling `.Axes.legend` without any arguments and
224             without setting the labels manually will result in no legend being
225             drawn.
226 
227 
228         **2. Explicitly listing the artists and labels in the legend**
229 
230         For full control of which artists have a legend entry, it is possible
231         to pass an iterable of legend artists followed by an iterable of
232         legend labels respectively::
233 
234             ax.legend([line1, line2, line3], ['label1', 'label2', 'label3'])
235 
236 
237         **3. Explicitly listing the artists in the legend**
238 
239         This is similar to 2, but the labels are taken from the artists'
240         label properties. Example::
241 
242             line1, = ax.plot([1, 2, 3], label='label1')
243             line2, = ax.plot([1, 2, 3], label='label2')
244             ax.legend(handles=[line1, line2])
245 
246 
247         **4. Labeling existing plot elements**
248 
249         .. admonition:: Discouraged
250 
251             This call signature is discouraged, because the relation between
252             plot elements and labels is only implicit by their order and can
253             easily be mixed up.
254 
255         To make a legend for all artists on an Axes, call this function with
256         an iterable of strings, one for each legend item. For example::
257 
258             ax.plot([1, 2, 3])
259             ax.plot([5, 6, 7])
260             ax.legend(['First line', 'Second line'])
261 
262 
263         Parameters
264         ----------
265         handles : sequence of `.Artist`, optional
266             A list of Artists (lines, patches) to be added to the legend.
267             Use this together with *labels*, if you need full control on what
268             is shown in the legend and the automatic mechanism described above
269             is not sufficient.
270 
271             The length of handles and labels should be the same in this
272             case. If they are not, they are truncated to the smaller length.
273 
274         labels : list of str, optional
275             A list of labels to show next to the artists.
276             Use this together with *handles*, if you need full control on what
277             is shown in the legend and the automatic mechanism described above
278             is not sufficient.
279 
280         Returns
281         -------
282         `~matplotlib.legend.Legend`
283 
284         Other Parameters
285         ----------------
286         %(_legend_kw_doc)s
287 
288         See Also
289         --------
290         .Figure.legend
291 
292         Notes
293         -----
294         Some artists are not supported by this function.  See
295         :doc:`/tutorials/intermediate/legend_guide` for details.
296 
297         Examples
298         --------
299         .. plot:: gallery/text_labels_and_annotations/legend.py
300         """
301         handles, labels, extra_args, kwargs = mlegend._parse_legend_args(
302                 [self],
303                 *args,
304                 **kwargs)
305         if len(extra_args):
306             raise TypeError('legend only accepts two non-keyword arguments')
307         self.legend_ = mlegend.Legend(self, handles, labels, **kwargs)
308         self.legend_._remove_method = self._remove_legend

315         """
316         Add a child inset Axes to this existing Axes.
317 
318         Warnings
319         --------
320         This method is experimental as of 3.0, and the API may change.
321 
322         Parameters
323         ----------
324         bounds : [x0, y0, width, height]
325             Lower-left corner of inset Axes, and its width and height.
326 
327         transform : `.Transform`
328             Defaults to `ax.transAxes`, i.e. the units of *rect* are in
329             Axes-relative coordinates.

331         projection : {None, 'aitoff', 'hammer', 'lambert', 'mollweide', \
332 'polar', 'rectilinear', str}, optional
333             The projection type of the inset `~.axes.Axes`. *str* is the name
334             of a custom projection, see `~matplotlib.projections`. The default
335             None results in a 'rectilinear' projection.
336 
337         polar : bool, default: False
338             If True, equivalent to projection='polar'.
339 
340         axes_class : subclass type of `~.axes.Axes`, optional
341             The `.axes.Axes` subclass that is instantiated.  This parameter
342             is incompatible with *projection* and *polar*.  See
343             :ref:`axisartist_users-guide-index` for examples.
344 
345         zorder : number
346             Defaults to 5 (same as `.Axes.legend`).  Adjust higher or lower
347             to change whether it is above or below data plotted on the
348             parent Axes.
349 
350         **kwargs
351             Other keyword arguments are passed on to the inset Axes class.
352 
353         Returns
354         -------
355         ax
356             The created `~.axes.Axes` instance.
357 
358         Examples
359         --------
360         This example makes two inset Axes, the first is in Axes-relative
361         coordinates, and the second in data-coordinates::
362 
363             fig, ax = plt.subplots()
364             ax.plot(range(10))
365             axin1 = ax.inset_axes([0.8, 0.1, 0.15, 0.15])
366             axin2 = ax.inset_axes(
367                     [5, 7, 2.3, 2.3], transform=ax.transData)
368 
369         """
370         if transform is None:
371             transform = self.transAxes
372         kwargs.setdefault('label', 'inset_axes')
373 
374         # This puts the rectangle into figure-relative coordinates.
375         inset_locator = _TransformedBoundsLocator(bounds, transform)
376         bounds = inset_locator(self, None).bounds
377         projection_class, pkw = self.figure._process_projection_requirements(
378                 bounds, **kwargs)

382         # it gets called in `ax.apply_aspect() (of all places)
383         inset_ax.set_axes_locator(inset_locator)
384 
385         self.add_child_axes(inset_ax)
386 
387         return inset_ax

390     def indicate_inset(self, bounds, inset_ax=None, *, transform=None,
391                        facecolor='none', edgecolor='0.5', alpha=0.5,
392                        zorder=4.99, **kwargs):
393         """
394         Add an inset indicator to the Axes.  This is a rectangle on the plot
395         at the position indicated by *bounds* that optionally has lines that
396         connect the rectangle to an inset Axes (`.Axes.inset_axes`).
397 
398         Warnings
399         --------
400         This method is experimental as of 3.0, and the API may change.
401 
402         Parameters
403         ----------
404         bounds : [x0, y0, width, height]
405             Lower-left corner of rectangle to be marked, and its width
406             and height.
407 
408         inset_ax : `.Axes`
409             An optional inset Axes to draw connecting lines to.  Two lines are
410             drawn connecting the indicator box to the inset Axes on corners
411             chosen so as to not overlap with the indicator box.
412 
413         transform : `.Transform`
414             Transform for the rectangle coordinates. Defaults to
415             `ax.transAxes`, i.e. the units of *rect* are in Axes-relative
416             coordinates.
417 
418         facecolor : color, default: 'none'
419             Facecolor of the rectangle.
420 
421         edgecolor : color, default: '0.5'
422             Color of the rectangle and color of the connecting lines.
423 
424         alpha : float, default: 0.5
425             Transparency of the rectangle and connector lines.
426 
427         zorder : float, default: 4.99
428             Drawing order of the rectangle and connector lines.  The default,
429             4.99, is just below the default level of inset Axes.
430 
431         **kwargs
432             Other keyword arguments are passed on to the `.Rectangle` patch:
433 
434             %(Rectangle:kwdoc)s
435 
436         Returns
437         -------
438         rectangle_patch : `.patches.Rectangle`
439              The indicator frame.
440 
441         connector_lines : 4-tuple of `.patches.ConnectionPatch`
442             The four connector lines connecting to (lower_left, upper_left,
443             lower_right upper_right) corners of *inset_ax*. Two lines are
444             set with visibility to *False*,  but the user can set the
445             visibility to True if the automatic choice is not deemed correct.
446 
447         """
448         # to make the axes connectors work, we need to apply the aspect to
449         # the parent axes.
450         self.apply_aspect()
451 
452         if transform is None:
453             transform = self.transData
454         kwargs.setdefault('label', '_indicate_inset')
455 
456         x, y, width, height = bounds
457         rectangle_patch = mpatches.Rectangle(
458             (x, y), width, height,
459             facecolor=facecolor, edgecolor=edgecolor, alpha=alpha,
460             zorder=zorder, transform=transform, **kwargs)
461         self.add_patch(rectangle_patch)
462 
463         connects = []
464 
465         if inset_ax is not None:
466             # connect the inset_axes to the rectangle
467             for xy_inset_ax in [(0, 0), (0, 1), (1, 0), (1, 1)]:
468                 # inset_ax positions are in axes coordinates
469                 # The 0, 1 values define the four edges if the inset_ax
470                 # lower_left, upper_left, lower_right upper_right.
471                 ex, ey = xy_inset_ax
472                 if self.xaxis.get_inverted():
473                     ex = 1 - ex
474                 if self.yaxis.get_inverted():
475                     ey = 1 - ey
476                 xy_data = x + ex * width, y + ey * height
477                 p = mpatches.ConnectionPatch(
478                     xyA=xy_inset_ax, coordsA=inset_ax.transAxes,
479                     xyB=xy_data, coordsB=self.transData,
480                     arrowstyle="-", zorder=zorder,
481                     edgecolor=edgecolor, alpha=alpha)
482                 connects.append(p)
483                 self.add_patch(p)
484 
485             # decide which two of the lines to keep visible....
486             pos = inset_ax.get_position()
487             bboxins = pos.transformed(self.figure.transSubfigure)
488             rectbbox = mtransforms.Bbox.from_bounds(
489                 *bounds
490             ).transformed(transform)
491             x0 = rectbbox.x0 < bboxins.x0
492             x1 = rectbbox.x1 < bboxins.x1
493             y0 = rectbbox.y0 < bboxins.y0
494             y1 = rectbbox.y1 < bboxins.y1
495             connects[0].set_visible(x0 ^ y0)
496             connects[1].set_visible(x0 == y1)
497             connects[2].set_visible(x1 == y0)
498             connects[3].set_visible(x1 ^ y1)
499 
500         return rectangle_patch, tuple(connects) if connects else None

1234             If *positions* is 2D, this can be a sequence with length matching
1235             the length of *positions*.
1236 
1237         linewidths : float or array-like, default: :rc:`lines.linewidth`
1238             The line width(s) of the event lines, in points.
1239 
1240             If *positions* is 2D, this can be a sequence with length matching
1241             the length of *positions*.
1242 
1243         colors : color or list of colors, default: :rc:`lines.color`
1244             The color(s) of the event lines.
1245 
1246             If *positions* is 2D, this can be a sequence with length matching
1247             the length of *positions*.
1248 
1249         linestyles : str or tuple or list of such values, default: 'solid'
1250             Default is 'solid'. Valid strings are ['solid', 'dashed',
1251             'dashdot', 'dotted', '-', '--', '-.', ':']. Dash tuples
1252             should be of the form::
1253 
1254                 (offset, onoffseq),
1255 
1256             where *onoffseq* is an even length tuple of on and off ink
1257             in points.
1258 
1259             If *positions* is 2D, this can be a sequence with length matching
1260             the length of *positions*.
1261 
1262         data : indexable object, optional
1263             DATA_PARAMETER_PLACEHOLDER
1264 
1265         **kwargs
1266             Other keyword arguments are line collection properties.  See
1267             `.LineCollection` for a list of the valid properties.
1268 
1269         Returns
1270         -------
1271         list of `.EventCollection`
1272             The `.EventCollection` that were added.
1273 
1274         Notes
1275         -----
1276         For *linelengths*, *linewidths*, *colors*, and *linestyles*, if only
1277         a single value is given, that value is applied to all lines.  If an
1278         array-like is given, it must have the same length as *positions*, and
1279         each value will be applied to the corresponding row of the array.
1280 
1281         Examples
1282         --------
1283         .. plot:: gallery/lines_bars_and_markers/eventplot_demo.py
1284         """
1285 
1286         lineoffsets, linelengths = self._process_unit_info(
1287                 [("y", lineoffsets), ("y", linelengths)], kwargs)
1288 
1289         # fix positions, noting that it can be a list of lists:
1290         if not np.iterable(positions):
1291             positions = [positions]
1292         elif any(np.iterable(position) for position in positions):
1293             positions = [np.asanyarray(position) for position in positions]
1294         else:
1295             positions = [np.asanyarray(positions)]
1296 
1297         if len(positions) == 0:
1298             return []
1299 
1300         poss = []
1301         for position in positions:
1302             poss += self._process_unit_info([("x", position)], kwargs)
1303         positions = poss
1304 
1305         # prevent 'singular' keys from **kwargs dict from overriding the effect
1306         # of 'plural' keyword arguments (e.g. 'color' overriding 'colors')
1307         colors = cbook._local_over_kwdict(colors, kwargs, 'color')
1308         linewidths = cbook._local_over_kwdict(linewidths, kwargs, 'linewidth')
1309         linestyles = cbook._local_over_kwdict(linestyles, kwargs, 'linestyle')
1310 
1311         if not np.iterable(lineoffsets):
1312             lineoffsets = [lineoffsets]
1313         if not np.iterable(linelengths):
1314             linelengths = [linelengths]
1315         if not np.iterable(linewidths):
1316             linewidths = [linewidths]
1317         if not np.iterable(colors):
1318             colors = [colors]
1319         if hasattr(linestyles, 'lower') or not np.iterable(linestyles):
1320             linestyles = [linestyles]
1321 
1322         lineoffsets = np.asarray(lineoffsets)
1323         linelengths = np.asarray(linelengths)
1324         linewidths = np.asarray(linewidths)
1325 
1326         if len(lineoffsets) == 0:
1327             lineoffsets = [None]
1328         if len(linelengths) == 0:
1329             linelengths = [None]
1330         if len(linewidths) == 0:
1331             lineoffsets = [None]
1332         if len(linewidths) == 0:
1333             lineoffsets = [None]
1334         if len(colors) == 0:
1335             colors = [None]
1336         try:
1337             # Early conversion of the colors into RGBA values to take care
1338             # of cases like colors='0.5' or colors='C1'.  (Issue #8193)
1339             colors = mcolors.to_rgba_array(colors)
1340         except ValueError:
1341             # Will fail if any element of *colors* is None. But as long
1342             # as len(colors) == 1 or len(positions), the rest of the
1343             # code should process *colors* properly.
1344             pass
1345 
1346         if len(lineoffsets) == 1 and len(positions) != 1:
1347             lineoffsets = np.tile(lineoffsets, len(positions))
1348             lineoffsets[0] = 0
1349             lineoffsets = np.cumsum(lineoffsets)
1350         if len(linelengths) == 1:
1351             linelengths = np.tile(linelengths, len(positions))
1352         if len(linewidths) == 1:
1353             linewidths = np.tile(linewidths, len(positions))
1354         if len(colors) == 1:
1355             colors = list(colors)
1356             colors = colors * len(positions)
1357         if len(linestyles) == 1:
1358             linestyles = [linestyles] * len(positions)
1359 
1360         if len(lineoffsets) != len(positions):
1361             raise ValueError('lineoffsets and positions are unequal sized '
1362                              'sequences')
1363         if len(linelengths) != len(positions):
1364             raise ValueError('linelengths and positions are unequal sized '
1365                              'sequences')
1366         if len(linewidths) != len(positions):
1367             raise ValueError('linewidths and positions are unequal sized '
1368                              'sequences')
1369         if len(colors) != len(positions):
1370             raise ValueError('colors and positions are unequal sized '
1371                              'sequences')
1372         if len(linestyles) != len(positions):
1373             raise ValueError('linestyles and positions are unequal sized '
1374                              'sequences')
1375 
1376         colls = []
1377         for position, lineoffset, linelength, linewidth, color, linestyle in \
1378                 zip(positions, lineoffsets, linelengths, linewidths,
1379                     colors, linestyles):
1380             coll = mcoll.EventCollection(position,
1381                                          orientation=orientation,
1382                                          lineoffset=lineoffset,
1383                                          linelength=linelength,
1384                                          linewidth=linewidth,
1385                                          color=color,
1386                                          linestyle=linestyle)
1387             self.add_collection(coll, autolim=False)
1388             coll._internal_update(kwargs)
1389             colls.append(coll)
1390 
1391         if len(positions) > 0:
1392             # try to get min/max
1393             min_max = [(np.min(_p), np.max(_p)) for _p in positions
1394                        if len(_p) > 0]
1395             # if we have any non-empty positions, try to autoscale
1396             if len(min_max) > 0:
1397                 mins, maxes = zip(*min_max)
1398                 minpos = np.min(mins)
1399                 maxpos = np.max(maxes)
1400 
1401                 minline = (lineoffsets - linelengths).min()
1402                 maxline = (lineoffsets + linelengths).max()
1403 
1404                 if orientation == "vertical":
1405                     corners = (minline, minpos), (maxline, maxpos)
1406                 else:  # "horizontal"
1407                     corners = (minpos, minline), (maxpos, maxline)
1408                 self.update_datalim(corners)
1409                 self._request_autoscale_view()
1410 
1411         return colls
