413     def deconstruct(self):
414         """
415         Return enough information to recreate the field as a 4-tuple:
416 
417          * The name of the field on the model, if contribute_to_class() has
418            been run.
419          * The import path of the field, including the class:e.g.
420            django.db.models.IntegerField This should be the most portable
421            version, so less specific may be better.
422          * A list of positional arguments.
423          * A dict of keyword arguments.
424 
425         Note that the positional or keyword arguments must contain values of
426         the following types (including inner values of collection types):
427 
428          * None, bool, str, int, float, complex, set, frozenset, list, tuple,
429            dict
430          * UUID
431          * datetime.datetime (naive), datetime.date
432          * top-level classes, top-level functions - will be referenced by their
433            full import path
434          * Storage instances - these have their own deconstruct() method
435 
436         This is because the values here must be serialized into a text format
437         (possibly new Python code, possibly JSON) and these are the only types
438         with encoding handlers defined.
439 
440         There's no need to return the exact way the field was instantiated this
441         time, just ensure that the resulting field is the same - prefer keyword
442         arguments over positional ones, and omit parameters with their default
443         values.
444         """
445         # Short-form way of fetching all the default parameters
446         keywords = {}
447         possibles = {
448             "verbose_name": None,
449             "primary_key": False,
450             "max_length": None,
451             "unique": False,
452             "blank": False,
453             "null": False,
454             "db_index": False,
455             "default": NOT_PROVIDED,
456             "editable": True,
457             "serialize": True,
458             "unique_for_date": None,
459             "unique_for_month": None,
460             "unique_for_year": None,
461             "choices": None,
462             "help_text": '',
463             "db_column": None,
464             "db_tablespace": None,
465             "auto_created": False,
466             "validators": [],
467             "error_messages": None,
468         }
469         attr_overrides = {
470             "unique": "_unique",
471             "error_messages": "_error_messages",
472             "validators": "_validators",
473             "verbose_name": "_verbose_name",
474             "db_tablespace": "_db_tablespace",
475         }
476         equals_comparison = {"choices", "validators"}
477         for name, default in possibles.items():
478             value = getattr(self, attr_overrides.get(name, name))
479             # Unroll anything iterable for choices into a concrete list
480             if name == "choices" and isinstance(value, collections.abc.Iterable):
481                 value = list(value)
482             # Do correct kind of comparison
483             if name in equals_comparison:
484                 if value != default:
485                     keywords[name] = value
486             else:
487                 if value is not default:
488                     keywords[name] = value
489         # Work out path - we shorten it for known Django core fields
490         path = "%s.%s" % (self.__class__.__module__, self.__class__.__qualname__)
491         if path.startswith("django.db.models.fields.related"):
492             path = path.replace("django.db.models.fields.related", "django.db.models")
493         elif path.startswith("django.db.models.fields.files"):
494             path = path.replace("django.db.models.fields.files", "django.db.models")
495         elif path.startswith("django.db.models.fields.proxy"):
496             path = path.replace("django.db.models.fields.proxy", "django.db.models")
497         elif path.startswith("django.db.models.fields"):
498             path = path.replace("django.db.models.fields", "django.db.models")
499         # Return basic info - other fields should override this.
500         return (self.name, path, [], keywords)

544     def __reduce__(self):

620                     # options.

622                         if value == optgroup_key:

625                     return

627                 self.error_messages['invalid_choice'],
628                 code='invalid_choice',
629                 params={'value': value},

Cannot override get_FOO_display() in Django 2.2+.
Description
	
I cannot override the get_FIELD_display function on models since version 2.2. It works in version 2.1.
Example:
class FooBar(models.Model):
	foo_bar = models.CharField(_("foo"), choices=[(1, 'foo'), (2, 'bar')])
	def __str__(self):
		return self.get_foo_bar_display() # This returns 'foo' or 'bar' in 2.2, but 'something' in 2.1
	def get_foo_bar_display(self):
		return "something"
What I expect is that I should be able to override this function.

Thanks for this report. Regression in a68ea231012434b522ce45c513d84add516afa60. Reproduced at 54a7b021125d23a248e70ba17bf8b10bc8619234.
OK, I have a lead on this. Not at all happy about how it looks at first pass, but I'll a proof of concept PR together for it tomorrow AM.
I don't think it should be marked as blocker since it looks like it was never supported, because it depends on the order of attrs passed in ModelBase.__new__(). So on Django 2.1 and Python 3.7: In [1]: import django ...: django.VERSION In [2]: from django.db import models ...: ...: class FooBar(models.Model): ...: def get_foo_bar_display(self): ...: return "something" ...: ...: foo_bar = models.CharField("foo", choices=[(1, 'foo'), (2, 'bar')]) ...: ...: def __str__(self): ...: return self.get_foo_bar_display() # This returns 'foo' or 'bar' in 2.2, but 'something' in 2.1 ...: ...: class Meta: ...: app_label = 'test' ...: ...: FooBar(foo_bar=1) Out[2]: <FooBar: foo> Before ​Python 3.6 the order of attrs wasn't defined at all.
Sergey, an example from the ticket description works for me with Django 2.1 and Python 3.6, 3.7 and 3.8.
In [2]: import django ...: django.VERSION Out[2]: (2, 1, 13, 'final', 0) In [3]: import sys ...: sys.version Out[3]: '3.5.7 (default, Oct 17 2019, 07:04:41) \n[GCC 8.3.0]' In [4]: from django.db import models ...: ...: class FooBar(models.Model): ...: foo_bar = models.CharField("foo", choices=[(1, 'foo'), (2, 'bar')]) ...: ...: def __str__(self): ...: return self.get_foo_bar_display() # This returns 'foo' or 'bar' in 2.2, but 'something' in 2.1 ...: ...: def get_foo_bar_display(self): ...: return "something" ...: ...: class Meta: ...: app_label = 'test' ...: ...: FooBar(foo_bar=1) Out[4]: <FooBar: foo>
OK, so there is a behaviour change here, but Sergey is correct that it does depend on attr order, so it's hard to say that this can be said to ever have been thought of as supported, with the exact example provided. This example produces the opposite result on 2.1 (even on >=PY36): def test_overriding_display_backwards(self): class FooBar2(models.Model): def get_foo_bar_display(self): return "something" foo_bar = models.CharField("foo", choices=[(1, 'foo'), (2, 'bar')]) f = FooBar2(foo_bar=1) # This returns 'foo' or 'bar' in both 2.2 and 2.1 self.assertEqual(f.get_foo_bar_display(), "foo") Because get_foo_bar_display() is defined before foo_bar is gets replaced in the the add_to_class() step. Semantically order shouldn't make a difference. Given that it does, I can't see that we're bound to maintain that behaviour. (There's a possible fix in Field.contribute_to_class() but implementing that just reverses the pass/fail behaviour depending on order...) Rather, the correct way to implement this on 2.2+ is: def test_overriding_display(self): class FooBar(models.Model): foo_bar = models.CharField("foo", choices=[(1, 'foo'), (2, 'bar')]) def _get_FIELD_display(self, field): if field.attname == 'foo_bar': return "something" return super()._get_FIELD_display(field) f = FooBar(foo_bar=1) self.assertEqual(f.get_foo_bar_display(), "something") This is stable for declaration order on version 2.2+. This approach requires overriding _get_FIELD_display() before declaring fields on 2.1, because otherwise Model._get_FIELD_display() is picked up during Field.contribute_to_class(). This ordering dependency is, ultimately, the same issue that was addressed in a68ea231012434b522ce45c513d84add516afa60, and the follow-up in #30254. The behaviour in 2.1 (and before) was incorrect. Yes, there's a behaviour change here but it's a bugfix, and all bugfixes are breaking changes if you're depending on the broken behaviour. I'm going to downgrade this from Release Blocker accordingly. I'll reclassify this as a Documentation issue and provide the working example, as overriding _get_FIELD_display() is a legitimate use-case I'd guess.
Replying to Carlton Gibson: (There's a possible fix in Field.contribute_to_class() but implementing that just reverses the pass/fail behaviour depending on order...) Doesn't this fix it? if not hasattr(cls, 'get_%s_display' % self.name): setattr(cls, 'get_%s_display' % self.name, partialmethod(cls._get_FIELD_display, field=self))

Migration crashes deleting an index_together if there is a unique_together on the same fields
Description
	
Happens with Django 1.11.10
Steps to reproduce:
1) Create models with 2 fields, add 2 same fields to unique_together and to index_together
2) Delete index_together -> Fail
It will fail at django/db/backends/base/schema.py, line 378, in _delete_composed_index(), ValueError: Found wrong number (2) of constraints for as this one will find two constraints, the _uniq and the _idx one. No way to get out of this...

I think there are 2 different points here:
1) The deletion of index_together should be possible alone or made coherent (migrations side?) with unique_together
2) Moving the declaration of an index should not result in an index re-creation

227                     # Some databases can't take defaults as a parameter (oracle)
228                     # If this is the case, the individual schema backend should
229                     # implement prepare_default
230                     sql += column_default % self.prepare_default(default_value)
231                 else:
232                     sql += column_default
233                     params += [default_value]
234         # Oracle treats the empty string ('') as null, so coerce the null
235         # option whenever '' is a possible value.
236         if (field.empty_strings_allowed and not field.primary_key and
237                 self.connection.features.interprets_empty_strings_as_nulls):
238             null = True
239         if null and not self.connection.features.implied_column_null:
240             sql += " NULL"
241         elif not null:
242             sql += " NOT NULL"
243         # Primary key/unique outputs
244         if field.primary_key:
245             sql += " PRIMARY KEY"
246         elif field.unique:
247             sql += " UNIQUE"
248         # Optionally add the tablespace if it's an implicitly indexed column
249         tablespace = field.db_tablespace or model._meta.db_tablespace
250         if tablespace and self.connection.features.supports_tablespaces and field.unique:
251             sql += " %s" % self.connection.ops.tablespace_sql(tablespace, inline=True)
252         # Return the sql
253         return sql, params
254 
255     def skip_default(self, field):
256         """
257         Some backends don't accept default values for certain columns types
258         (i.e. MySQL longtext and longblob).
259         """
260         return False
261 
262     def prepare_default(self, value):
263         """
264         Only used for backends which have requires_literal_defaults feature
265         """
266         raise NotImplementedError(
267             'subclasses of BaseDatabaseSchemaEditor for backends which have '
268             'requires_literal_defaults must provide a prepare_default() method'
269         )

271     def _column_default_sql(self, field):
272         """
273         Return the SQL to use in a DEFAULT clause. The resulting string should
274         contain a '%s' placeholder for a default value.
275         """
276         return '%s'
277 
278     @staticmethod
279     def _effective_default(field):
280         # This method allows testing its logic without a connection.
281         if field.has_default():
282             default = field.get_default()
283         elif not field.null and field.blank and field.empty_strings_allowed:
284             if field.get_internal_type() == "BinaryField":
285                 default = b''
286             else:
287                 default = ''
288         elif getattr(field, 'auto_now', False) or getattr(field, 'auto_now_add', False):
289             default = datetime.now()
290             internal_type = field.get_internal_type()
291             if internal_type == 'DateField':
292                 default = default.date()
293             elif internal_type == 'TimeField':
294                 default = default.time()
295             elif internal_type == 'DateTimeField':
296                 default = timezone.now()
297         else:
298             default = None
299         return default
300 
301     def effective_default(self, field):
302         """Return a field's effective database default value."""
303         return field.get_db_prep_save(self._effective_default(field), self.connection)
304 
305     def quote_value(self, value):
306         """
307         Return a quoted version of the value so it's safe to use in an SQL
308         string. This is not safe against injection from user code; it is
309         intended only for use in making SQL scripts or preparing default values
310         for particularly tricky backends (defaults are not user-defined, though,
311         so this is safe).
312         """
313         raise NotImplementedError()

317     def create_model(self, model):
318         """
319         Create a table and any accompanying indexes or unique constraints for
320         the given `model`.
321         """
322         sql, params = self.table_sql(model)
323         # Prevent using [] as params, in the case a literal '%' is used in the definition
324         self.execute(sql, params or None)
325 
326         # Add any field index and index_together's (deferred as SQLite _remake_table needs it)
327         self.deferred_sql.extend(self._model_indexes_sql(model))
328 
329         # Make M2M tables
330         for field in model._meta.local_many_to_many:
331             if field.remote_field.through._meta.auto_created:
332                 self.create_model(field.remote_field.through)
333 
334     def delete_model(self, model):
335         """Delete a model from the database."""
336         # Handle auto-created intermediary models
337         for field in model._meta.local_many_to_many:
338             if field.remote_field.through._meta.auto_created:
339                 self.delete_model(field.remote_field.through)
340 
341         # Delete the table
342         self.execute(self.sql_delete_table % {
343             "table": self.quote_name(model._meta.db_table),
344         })
345         # Remove all deferred statements referencing the deleted table.
346         for sql in list(self.deferred_sql):
347             if isinstance(sql, Statement) and sql.references_table(model._meta.db_table):
348                 self.deferred_sql.remove(sql)
349 
350     def add_index(self, model, index):
351         """Add an index on a model."""
352         self.execute(index.create_sql(model, self), params=None)
353 
354     def remove_index(self, model, index):
355         """Remove an index from a model."""
356         self.execute(index.remove_sql(model, self))
357 
358     def add_constraint(self, model, constraint):
359         """Add a constraint to a model."""
360         sql = constraint.create_sql(model, self)
361         if sql:
362             self.execute(sql)
363 
364     def remove_constraint(self, model, constraint):
365         """Remove a constraint from a model."""
366         sql = constraint.remove_sql(model, self)
367         if sql:
368             self.execute(sql)
369 
370     def alter_unique_together(self, model, old_unique_together, new_unique_together):
371         """
372         Deal with a model changing its unique_together. The input
373         unique_togethers must be doubly-nested, not the single-nested
374         ["foo", "bar"] format.
375         """
376         olds = {tuple(fields) for fields in old_unique_together}
377         news = {tuple(fields) for fields in new_unique_together}
378         # Deleted uniques
379         for fields in olds.difference(news):
380             self._delete_composed_index(model, fields, {'unique': True}, self.sql_delete_unique)
381         # Created uniques
382         for fields in news.difference(olds):
383             columns = [model._meta.get_field(field).column for field in fields]
384             self.execute(self._create_unique_sql(model, columns))
385 
386     def alter_index_together(self, model, old_index_together, new_index_together):
387         """
388         Deal with a model changing its index_together. The input
389         index_togethers must be doubly-nested, not the single-nested
390         ["foo", "bar"] format.
391         """
392         olds = {tuple(fields) for fields in old_index_together}
393         news = {tuple(fields) for fields in new_index_together}
394         # Deleted indexes
395         for fields in olds.difference(news):
396             self._delete_composed_index(model, fields, {'index': True}, self.sql_delete_index)
397         # Created indexes
398         for field_names in news.difference(olds):
399             fields = [model._meta.get_field(field) for field in field_names]
400             self.execute(self._create_index_sql(model, fields, suffix="_idx"))
401 
402     def _delete_composed_index(self, model, fields, constraint_kwargs, sql):
403         meta_constraint_names = {constraint.name for constraint in model._meta.constraints}
404         meta_index_names = {constraint.name for constraint in model._meta.indexes}
405         columns = [model._meta.get_field(field).column for field in fields]
406         constraint_names = self._constraint_names(
407             model, columns, exclude=meta_constraint_names | meta_index_names,
408             **constraint_kwargs
409         )
410         if len(constraint_names) != 1:
411             raise ValueError("Found wrong number (%s) of constraints for %s(%s)" % (
412                 len(constraint_names),
413                 model._meta.db_table,
414                 ", ".join(columns),
415             ))
416         self.execute(self._delete_constraint_sql(sql, model, constraint_names[0]))
417 
418     def alter_db_table(self, model, old_db_table, new_db_table):
419         """Rename the table a model points to."""
420         if (old_db_table == new_db_table or
421             (self.connection.features.ignores_table_name_case and
422                 old_db_table.lower() == new_db_table.lower())):
423             return
424         self.execute(self.sql_rename_table % {
425             "old_table": self.quote_name(old_db_table),
426             "new_table": self.quote_name(new_db_table),
427         })
428         # Rename all references to the old table name.
429         for sql in self.deferred_sql:
430             if isinstance(sql, Statement):
431                 sql.rename_table_references(old_db_table, new_db_table)
432 
433     def alter_db_tablespace(self, model, old_db_tablespace, new_db_tablespace):
434         """Move a model's table between tablespaces."""
435         self.execute(self.sql_retablespace_table % {
436             "table": self.quote_name(model._meta.db_table),
437             "old_tablespace": self.quote_name(old_db_tablespace),
438             "new_tablespace": self.quote_name(new_db_tablespace),
439         })
440 
441     def add_field(self, model, field):
442         """
443         Create a field on a model. Usually involves adding a column, but may
444         involve adding a table instead (for M2M fields).
445         """
446         # Special-case implicit M2M tables
447         if field.many_to_many and field.remote_field.through._meta.auto_created:
448             return self.create_model(field.remote_field.through)
449         # Get the column's definition
450         definition, params = self.column_sql(model, field, include_default=True)
451         # It might not actually have a column behind it
452         if definition is None:
453             return
454         # Check constraints can go on the column SQL here
455         db_params = field.db_parameters(connection=self.connection)
456         if db_params['check']:
457             definition += " " + self.sql_check_constraint % db_params
458         if field.remote_field and self.connection.features.supports_foreign_keys and field.db_constraint:
459             constraint_suffix = '_fk_%(to_table)s_%(to_column)s'
460             # Add FK constraint inline, if supported.
461             if self.sql_create_column_inline_fk:
462                 to_table = field.remote_field.model._meta.db_table
463                 to_column = field.remote_field.model._meta.get_field(field.remote_field.field_name).column
464                 definition += " " + self.sql_create_column_inline_fk % {
465                     'name': self._fk_constraint_name(model, field, constraint_suffix),
466                     'column': self.quote_name(field.column),
467                     'to_table': self.quote_name(to_table),
468                     'to_column': self.quote_name(to_column),
469                     'deferrable': self.connection.ops.deferrable_sql()
470                 }
471             # Otherwise, add FK constraints later.
472             else:
473                 self.deferred_sql.append(self._create_fk_sql(model, field, constraint_suffix))
474         # Build the SQL and run it
475         sql = self.sql_create_column % {
476             "table": self.quote_name(model._meta.db_table),
477             "column": self.quote_name(field.column),
478             "definition": definition,
479         }
480         self.execute(sql, params)
481         # Drop the default if we need to
482         # (Django usually does not use in-database defaults)
483         if not self.skip_default(field) and self.effective_default(field) is not None:
484             changes_sql, params = self._alter_column_default_sql(model, None, field, drop=True)
485             sql = self.sql_alter_column % {
486                 "table": self.quote_name(model._meta.db_table),
487                 "changes": changes_sql,
488             }
489             self.execute(sql, params)
490         # Add an index, if required
491         self.deferred_sql.extend(self._field_indexes_sql(model, field))
492         # Reset connection if required
493         if self.connection.features.connection_persists_old_columns:
494             self.connection.close()
495 
496     def remove_field(self, model, field):
497         """
498         Remove a field from a model. Usually involves deleting a column,
499         but for M2Ms may involve deleting a table.
500         """
501         # Special-case implicit M2M tables
502         if field.many_to_many and field.remote_field.through._meta.auto_created:
503             return self.delete_model(field.remote_field.through)
504         # It might not actually have a column behind it
505         if field.db_parameters(connection=self.connection)['type'] is None:
506             return
507         # Drop any FK constraints, MySQL requires explicit deletion
508         if field.remote_field:
509             fk_names = self._constraint_names(model, [field.column], foreign_key=True)
510             for fk_name in fk_names:
511                 self.execute(self._delete_fk_sql(model, fk_name))
512         # Delete the column
513         sql = self.sql_delete_column % {
514             "table": self.quote_name(model._meta.db_table),
515             "column": self.quote_name(field.column),
516         }
517         self.execute(sql)
518         # Reset connection if required
519         if self.connection.features.connection_persists_old_columns:
520             self.connection.close()
521         # Remove all deferred statements referencing the deleted column.
522         for sql in list(self.deferred_sql):
523             if isinstance(sql, Statement) and sql.references_column(model._meta.db_table, field.column):
524                 self.deferred_sql.remove(sql)
525 
526     def alter_field(self, model, old_field, new_field, strict=False):
527         """
528         Allow a field's type, uniqueness, nullability, default, column,
529         constraints, etc. to be modified.
530         `old_field` is required to compute the necessary changes.
531         If `strict` is True, raise errors if the old column does not match
532         `old_field` precisely.
533         """
534         # Ensure this field is even column-based
535         old_db_params = old_field.db_parameters(connection=self.connection)
536         old_type = old_db_params['type']
537         new_db_params = new_field.db_parameters(connection=self.connection)
538         new_type = new_db_params['type']
539         if ((old_type is None and old_field.remote_field is None) or
540                 (new_type is None and new_field.remote_field is None)):
541             raise ValueError(
542                 "Cannot alter field %s into %s - they do not properly define "
543                 "db_type (are you using a badly-written custom field?)" %
544                 (old_field, new_field),
545             )
546         elif old_type is None and new_type is None and (
547                 old_field.remote_field.through and new_field.remote_field.through and
548                 old_field.remote_field.through._meta.auto_created and
549                 new_field.remote_field.through._meta.auto_created):
550             return self._alter_many_to_many(model, old_field, new_field, strict)
551         elif old_type is None and new_type is None and (
552                 old_field.remote_field.through and new_field.remote_field.through and
553                 not old_field.remote_field.through._meta.auto_created and
554                 not new_field.remote_field.through._meta.auto_created):
555             # Both sides have through models; this is a no-op.
556             return
557         elif old_type is None or new_type is None:
558             raise ValueError(
559                 "Cannot alter field %s into %s - they are not compatible types "
560                 "(you cannot alter to or from M2M fields, or add or remove "
561                 "through= on M2M fields)" % (old_field, new_field)
562             )
563 
564         self._alter_field(model, old_field, new_field, old_type, new_type,
565                           old_db_params, new_db_params, strict)
566 
567     def _alter_field(self, model, old_field, new_field, old_type, new_type,
568                      old_db_params, new_db_params, strict=False):
569         """Perform a "physical" (non-ManyToMany) field update."""
570         # Drop any FK constraints, we'll remake them later
571         fks_dropped = set()
572         if (
573             self.connection.features.supports_foreign_keys and
574             old_field.remote_field and
575             old_field.db_constraint
576         ):
577             fk_names = self._constraint_names(model, [old_field.column], foreign_key=True)
578             if strict and len(fk_names) != 1:
579                 raise ValueError("Found wrong number (%s) of foreign key constraints for %s.%s" % (
580                     len(fk_names),
581                     model._meta.db_table,
582                     old_field.column,
583                 ))
584             for fk_name in fk_names:
585                 fks_dropped.add((old_field.column,))
586                 self.execute(self._delete_fk_sql(model, fk_name))
587         # Has unique been removed?
588         if old_field.unique and (not new_field.unique or self._field_became_primary_key(old_field, new_field)):
589             # Find the unique constraint for this field
590             meta_constraint_names = {constraint.name for constraint in model._meta.constraints}
591             constraint_names = self._constraint_names(
592                 model, [old_field.column], unique=True, primary_key=False,
593                 exclude=meta_constraint_names,
594             )
595             if strict and len(constraint_names) != 1:
596                 raise ValueError("Found wrong number (%s) of unique constraints for %s.%s" % (
597                     len(constraint_names),
598                     model._meta.db_table,
599                     old_field.column,
600                 ))
601             for constraint_name in constraint_names:
602                 self.execute(self._delete_unique_sql(model, constraint_name))
603         # Drop incoming FK constraints if the field is a primary key or unique,
604         # which might be a to_field target, and things are going to change.
605         drop_foreign_keys = (
606             self.connection.features.supports_foreign_keys and (
607                 (old_field.primary_key and new_field.primary_key) or
608                 (old_field.unique and new_field.unique)
609             ) and old_type != new_type
610         )
611         if drop_foreign_keys:
612             # '_meta.related_field' also contains M2M reverse fields, these
613             # will be filtered out
614             for _old_rel, new_rel in _related_non_m2m_objects(old_field, new_field):
615                 rel_fk_names = self._constraint_names(
616                     new_rel.related_model, [new_rel.field.column], foreign_key=True
617                 )
618                 for fk_name in rel_fk_names:
619                     self.execute(self._delete_fk_sql(new_rel.related_model, fk_name))
620         # Removed an index? (no strict check, as multiple indexes are possible)
621         # Remove indexes if db_index switched to False or a unique constraint
622         # will now be used in lieu of an index. The following lines from the
623         # truth table show all True cases; the rest are False:
624         #
625         # old_field.db_index | old_field.unique | new_field.db_index | new_field.unique
626         # ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
627         # True               | False            | False              | False
628         # True               | False            | False              | True
629         # True               | False            | True               | True
630         if old_field.db_index and not old_field.unique and (not new_field.db_index or new_field.unique):
631             # Find the index for this field
632             meta_index_names = {index.name for index in model._meta.indexes}
633             # Retrieve only BTREE indexes since this is what's created with
634             # db_index=True.
635             index_names = self._constraint_names(
636                 model, [old_field.column], index=True, type_=Index.suffix,
637                 exclude=meta_index_names,
638             )
639             for index_name in index_names:
640                 # The only way to check if an index was created with
641                 # db_index=True or with Index(['field'], name='foo')
642                 # is to look at its name (refs #28053).
643                 self.execute(self._delete_index_sql(model, index_name))
644         # Change check constraints?
645         if old_db_params['check'] != new_db_params['check'] and old_db_params['check']:
646             meta_constraint_names = {constraint.name for constraint in model._meta.constraints}
647             constraint_names = self._constraint_names(
648                 model, [old_field.column], check=True,
649                 exclude=meta_constraint_names,
650             )
651             if strict and len(constraint_names) != 1:
652                 raise ValueError("Found wrong number (%s) of check constraints for %s.%s" % (
653                     len(constraint_names),
654                     model._meta.db_table,
655                     old_field.column,
656                 ))
657             for constraint_name in constraint_names:
658                 self.execute(self._delete_check_sql(model, constraint_name))
659         # Have they renamed the column?
660         if old_field.column != new_field.column:
661             self.execute(self._rename_field_sql(model._meta.db_table, old_field, new_field, new_type))
662             # Rename all references to the renamed column.
663             for sql in self.deferred_sql:
664                 if isinstance(sql, Statement):
665                     sql.rename_column_references(model._meta.db_table, old_field.column, new_field.column)
666         # Next, start accumulating actions to do
667         actions = []
668         null_actions = []
669         post_actions = []
670         # Type change?
671         if old_type != new_type:
672             fragment, other_actions = self._alter_column_type_sql(model, old_field, new_field, new_type)
673             actions.append(fragment)
674             post_actions.extend(other_actions)
675         # When changing a column NULL constraint to NOT NULL with a given
676         # default value, we need to perform 4 steps:
677         #  1. Add a default for new incoming writes
678         #  2. Update existing NULL rows with new default
679         #  3. Replace NULL constraint with NOT NULL
680         #  4. Drop the default again.
681         # Default change?
682         needs_database_default = False
683         if old_field.null and not new_field.null:
684             old_default = self.effective_default(old_field)
685             new_default = self.effective_default(new_field)
686             if (
687                 not self.skip_default(new_field) and
688                 old_default != new_default and
689                 new_default is not None
690             ):
691                 needs_database_default = True
692                 actions.append(self._alter_column_default_sql(model, old_field, new_field))
693         # Nullability change?
694         if old_field.null != new_field.null:
695             fragment = self._alter_column_null_sql(model, old_field, new_field)
696             if fragment:
697                 null_actions.append(fragment)
698         # Only if we have a default and there is a change from NULL to NOT NULL
699         four_way_default_alteration = (
700             new_field.has_default() and
701             (old_field.null and not new_field.null)
702         )
703         if actions or null_actions:
704             if not four_way_default_alteration:
705                 # If we don't have to do a 4-way default alteration we can
706                 # directly run a (NOT) NULL alteration
707                 actions = actions + null_actions
708             # Combine actions together if we can (e.g. postgres)
709             if self.connection.features.supports_combined_alters and actions:
710                 sql, params = tuple(zip(*actions))
711                 actions = [(", ".join(sql), sum(params, []))]
712             # Apply those actions
713             for sql, params in actions:
714                 self.execute(
715                     self.sql_alter_column % {
716                         "table": self.quote_name(model._meta.db_table),
717                         "changes": sql,
718                     },
719                     params,
720                 )
721             if four_way_default_alteration:
722                 # Update existing rows with default value
723                 self.execute(
724                     self.sql_update_with_default % {
725                         "table": self.quote_name(model._meta.db_table),
726                         "column": self.quote_name(new_field.column),
727                         "default": "%s",
728                     },
729                     [new_default],
730                 )
731                 # Since we didn't run a NOT NULL change before we need to do it
732                 # now
733                 for sql, params in null_actions:
734                     self.execute(
735                         self.sql_alter_column % {
736                             "table": self.quote_name(model._meta.db_table),
737                             "changes": sql,
738                         },
739                         params,
740                     )
741         if post_actions:
742             for sql, params in post_actions:
743                 self.execute(sql, params)
744         # If primary_key changed to False, delete the primary key constraint.
745         if old_field.primary_key and not new_field.primary_key:
746             self._delete_primary_key(model, strict)
747         # Added a unique?
748         if self._unique_should_be_added(old_field, new_field):
749             self.execute(self._create_unique_sql(model, [new_field.column]))
750         # Added an index? Add an index if db_index switched to True or a unique
751         # constraint will no longer be used in lieu of an index. The following
752         # lines from the truth table show all True cases; the rest are False:
753         #
754         # old_field.db_index | old_field.unique | new_field.db_index | new_field.unique
755         # ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
756         # False              | False            | True               | False
757         # False              | True             | True               | False
758         # True               | True             | True               | False
759         if (not old_field.db_index or old_field.unique) and new_field.db_index and not new_field.unique:
760             self.execute(self._create_index_sql(model, [new_field]))
761         # Type alteration on primary key? Then we need to alter the column
762         # referring to us.
763         rels_to_update = []
764         if drop_foreign_keys:
765             rels_to_update.extend(_related_non_m2m_objects(old_field, new_field))
766         # Changed to become primary key?
767         if self._field_became_primary_key(old_field, new_field):
768             # Make the new one
769             self.execute(self._create_primary_key_sql(model, new_field))
770             # Update all referencing columns
771             rels_to_update.extend(_related_non_m2m_objects(old_field, new_field))
772         # Handle our type alters on the other end of rels from the PK stuff above
773         for old_rel, new_rel in rels_to_update:
774             rel_db_params = new_rel.field.db_parameters(connection=self.connection)
775             rel_type = rel_db_params['type']

problem_statement:
Migration crashes deleting an index_together if there is a unique_together on the same fields
Description
	
Happens with Django 1.11.10
Steps to reproduce:
1) Create models with 2 fields, add 2 same fields to unique_together and to index_together
2) Delete index_together -> Fail
It will fail at django/db/backends/base/schema.py, line 378, in _delete_composed_index(), ValueError: Found wrong number (2) of constraints for as this one will find two constraints, the _uniq and the _idx one. No way to get out of this...
The worst in my case is that happened as I wanted to refactor my code to use the "new" (Dj 1.11) Options.indexes feature. I am actually not deleting the index, just the way it is declared in my code.
I think there are 2 different points here:
1) The deletion of index_together should be possible alone or made coherent (migrations side?) with unique_together
2) Moving the declaration of an index should not result in an index re-creation

problem_statement:
delete() on instances of models without any dependencies doesn't clear PKs.
Description
	
Deleting any model with no dependencies not updates the PK on the model. It should be set to None after .delete() call.
See Django.db.models.deletion:276-281. Should update the model line 280.

That said, if we want to be extra "safe" we can just move lines 320 - 326 into an extra function and call that from the old and new location (though I do not think it is needed).

Hmm I can reproduce your error, and now I understand the root cause. The root cause is following. The decision of skipping the path is here:

https://github.com/PyCQA/pylint/blob/3c5eca2ded3dd2b59ebaf23eb289453b5d2930f0/pylint/lint/pylinter.py#L600-L607

* When you execute pylint with `src/` argument following variables are present:
```python
(Pdb) p root
'src/gen'
(Pdb) p self.config.ignore_paths
[re.compile('^src\\\\gen\\\\.*$|^src/gen/.*$')]
```

* When you uexecute pylint with `.` argument following variables are present:
```python
(Pdb) p root
'./src/gen'
(Pdb) p self.config.ignore_paths
[re.compile('^src\\\\gen\\\\.*$|^src/gen/.*$')]
```

In the second case, the source is prefixed with `./` which causes that path is not matched. The simple fix should be to use  `os.path.normpath()` https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.path.html#os.path.normpath

problem_statement:
inaccurate rendering of pi**(1/E)
This claims to be version 1.5.dev; I just merged from the project master, so I hope this is current.  I didn't notice this bug among others in printing.pretty.

```
In [52]: pi**(1/E)                                                               
Out[52]: 
-1___
╲╱ π 

```
LaTeX and str not fooled:
```
In [53]: print(latex(pi**(1/E)))                                                 
\pi^{e^{-1}}

In [54]: str(pi**(1/E))                                                          
Out[54]: 'pi**exp(-1)'
```
hints_text:
I can confirm this bug on master. Looks like it's been there a while
https://github.com/sympy/sympy/blob/2d700c4b3c0871a26741456787b0555eed9d5546/sympy/printing/pretty/pretty.py#L1814

`1/E` is `exp(-1)` which has totally different arg structure than something like `1/pi`:

```
>>> (1/E).args
(-1,)
>>> (1/pi).args
(pi, -1)
```
@ethankward nice!  Also, the use of `str` there isn't correct:
```
>>> pprint(7**(1/(pi)))                                                                                                                                                          
pi___
╲╱ 7 

>>> pprint(pi**(1/(pi)))                                                                                                                                                        
pi___
╲╱ π 

>>> pprint(pi**(1/(EulerGamma)))                                                                                                                                                
EulerGamma___
        ╲╱ π 
```
(`pi` and `EulerGamma` were not pretty printed)
I guess str is used because it's hard to put 2-D stuff in the corner of the radical like that. But I think it would be better to recursively call the pretty printer, and if it is multiline, or maybe even if it is a more complicated expression than just a single number or symbol name, then print it without the radical like

```
  1
  ─
  e
π
```

or

```
 ⎛ -1⎞
 ⎝e  ⎠
π

Hi there,
I met with a problem:

#### Description
When I run KernelPCA for dimension reduction for the same datasets, the results are different in signs.

#### Steps/Code to Reproduce
Just to reduce the dimension to 7 with rbf kernel:
pca = KernelPCA(n_components=7, kernel='rbf', copy_X=False, n_jobs=-1)
pca.fit_transform(X)

#### Expected Results
The same result.

#### Actual Results

105         then all values are stored.
106 
107     alphas_ : array, (n_samples, n_components)
108         Eigenvectors of the centered kernel matrix. If `n_components` and
109         `remove_zero_eig` are not set, then all components are stored.
110 
111     dual_coef_ : array, (n_samples, n_features)
112         Inverse transform matrix. Only available when
113         ``fit_inverse_transform`` is True.
114 
115     X_transformed_fit_ : array, (n_samples, n_components)
116         Projection of the fitted data on the kernel principal components.
117         Only available when ``fit_inverse_transform`` is True.
118 
119     X_fit_ : (n_samples, n_features)
120         The data used to fit the model. If `copy_X=False`, then `X_fit_` is
121         a reference. This attribute is used for the calls to transform.
122 
123     Examples
124     --------
125     >>> from sklearn.datasets import load_digits
126     >>> from sklearn.decomposition import KernelPCA
127     >>> X, _ = load_digits(return_X_y=True)
128     >>> transformer = KernelPCA(n_components=7, kernel='linear')
129     >>> X_transformed = transformer.fit_transform(X)
130     >>> X_transformed.shape
131     (1797, 7)
132 
133     References
134     ----------
135     Kernel PCA was introduced in:
136         Bernhard Schoelkopf, Alexander J. Smola,
137         and Klaus-Robert Mueller. 1999. Kernel principal
138         component analysis. In Advances in kernel methods,
139         MIT Press, Cambridge, MA, USA 327-352.
140     """
141 
142     def __init__(self, n_components=None, kernel="linear",
143                  gamma=None, degree=3, coef0=1, kernel_params=None,
144                  alpha=1.0, fit_inverse_transform=False, eigen_solver='auto',
145                  tol=0, max_iter=None, remove_zero_eig=False,
146                  random_state=None, copy_X=True, n_jobs=None):
147         if fit_inverse_transform and kernel == 'precomputed':
148             raise ValueError(
149                 "Cannot fit_inverse_transform with a precomputed kernel.")
150         self.n_components = n_components
151         self.kernel = kernel
152         self.kernel_params = kernel_params
153         self.gamma = gamma
154         self.degree = degree
155         self.coef0 = coef0
156         self.alpha = alpha
157         self.fit_inverse_transform = fit_inverse_transform
158         self.eigen_solver = eigen_solver
159         self.remove_zero_eig = remove_zero_eig
160         self.tol = tol
161         self.max_iter = max_iter
162         self.random_state = random_state
163         self.n_jobs = n_jobs
164         self.copy_X = copy_X
165 
166     @property
167     def _pairwise(self):
168         return self.kernel == "precomputed"
169 
170     def _get_kernel(self, X, Y=None):
171         if callable(self.kernel):
172             params = self.kernel_params or {}
173         else:
174             params = {"gamma": self.gamma,
175                       "degree": self.degree,
176                       "coef0": self.coef0}
177         return pairwise_kernels(X, Y, metric=self.kernel,
178                                 filter_params=True, n_jobs=self.n_jobs,
179                                 **params)
180 
181     def _fit_transform(self, K):
182         """ Fit's using kernel K"""
183         # center kernel
184         K = self._centerer.fit_transform(K)
185 
186         if self.n_components is None:
187             n_components = K.shape[0]
188         else:
189             n_components = min(K.shape[0], self.n_components)
190 
191         # compute eigenvectors
192         if self.eigen_solver == 'auto':
193             if K.shape[0] > 200 and n_components < 10:
194                 eigen_solver = 'arpack'
195             else:
196                 eigen_solver = 'dense'
197         else:
198             eigen_solver = self.eigen_solver
199 
200         if eigen_solver == 'dense':
201             self.lambdas_, self.alphas_ = linalg.eigh(
202                 K, eigvals=(K.shape[0] - n_components, K.shape[0] - 1))
203         elif eigen_solver == 'arpack':
204             random_state = check_random_state(self.random_state)
205             # initialize with [-1,1] as in ARPACK
206             v0 = random_state.uniform(-1, 1, K.shape[0])
207             self.lambdas_, self.alphas_ = eigsh(K, n_components,
208                                                 which="LA",
209                                                 tol=self.tol,
210                                                 maxiter=self.max_iter,
211                                                 v0=v0)
212 
213         # sort eigenvectors in descending order
214         indices = self.lambdas_.argsort()[::-1]
215         self.lambdas_ = self.lambdas_[indices]
216         self.alphas_ = self.alphas_[:, indices]
217 
218         # remove eigenvectors with a zero eigenvalue
219         if self.remove_zero_eig or self.n_components is None:
220             self.alphas_ = self.alphas_[:, self.lambdas_ > 0]
221             self.lambdas_ = self.lambdas_[self.lambdas_ > 0]
222 
223         return K
224 
225     def _fit_inverse_transform(self, X_transformed, X):
226         if hasattr(X, "tocsr"):
227             raise NotImplementedError("Inverse transform not implemented for "
228                                       "sparse matrices!")
229 
230         n_samples = X_transformed.shape[0]
231         K = self._get_kernel(X_transformed)
232         K.flat[::n_samples + 1] += self.alpha
233         self.dual_coef_ = linalg.solve(K, X, sym_pos=True, overwrite_a=True)
234         self.X_transformed_fit_ = X_transformed
235 
236     def fit(self, X, y=None):
237         """Fit the model from data in X.
238 
239         Parameters
240         ----------
241         X : array-like, shape (n_samples, n_features)
242             Training vector, where n_samples in the number of samples
243             and n_features is the number of features.
244 
245         Returns
246         -------
247         self : object
248             Returns the instance itself.
249         """
250         X = check_array(X, accept_sparse='csr', copy=self.copy_X)
251         self._centerer = KernelCenterer()
252         K = self._get_kernel(X)
253         self._fit_transform(K)
254 
255         if self.fit_inverse_transform:
256             sqrt_lambdas = np.diag(np.sqrt(self.lambdas_))
257             X_transformed = np.dot(self.alphas_, sqrt_lambdas)
258             self._fit_inverse_transform(X_transformed, X)
259 
260         self.X_fit_ = X
261         return self
262 
263     def fit_transform(self, X, y=None, **params):
264         """Fit the model from data in X and transform X.
265 
266         Parameters
267         ----------
268         X : array-like, shape (n_samples, n_features)
269             Training vector, where n_samples in the number of samples
270             and n_features is the number of features.
271 
272         Returns
273         -------
274         X_new : array-like, shape (n_samples, n_components)
275         """
276         self.fit(X, **params)
277 
278         X_transformed = self.alphas_ * np.sqrt(self.lambdas_)
279 
280         if self.fit_inverse_transform:
281             self._fit_inverse_transform(X_transformed, X)
282 
283         return X_transformed
284 
285     def transform(self, X):
286         """Transform X.
287 
288         Parameters
289         ----------
290         X : array-like, shape (n_samples, n_features)
291 
292         Returns
293         -------
294         X_new : array-like, shape (n_samples, n_components)
295         """
296         check_is_fitted(self, 'X_fit_')
297 
298         K = self._centerer.transform(self._get_kernel(X, self.X_fit_))
299         return np.dot(K, self.alphas_ / np.sqrt(self.lambdas_))
300 
301     def inverse_transform(self, X):
302         """Transform X back to original space.
303 
304         Parameters
305         ----------
306         X : array-like, shape (n_samples, n_components)
307 
308         Returns
309         -------
310         X_new : array-like, shape (n_samples, n_features)
311 
312         References
313         ----------
314         "Learning to Find Pre-Images", G BakIr et al, 2004.
315         """
316         if not self.fit_inverse_transform:
317             raise NotFittedError("The fit_inverse_transform parameter was not"
318                                  " set to True when instantiating and hence "
319                                  "the inverse transform is not available.")
320 
321         K = self._get_kernel(X, self.X_transformed_fit_)
322 
323         return np.dot(K, self.dual_coef_)

Improve handling of skip for module level
This is potentially about updating docs, updating error messages or introducing a new API.

Consider the following scenario:

`pos_only.py` is using Python 3,8 syntax:
```python
def foo(a, /, b):
    return a + b
```

It should not be tested under Python 3.6 and 3.7.
This is a proper way to skip the test in Python older than 3.8:
```python
from pytest import raises, skip
import sys
if sys.version_info < (3, 8):
    skip(msg="Requires Python >= 3.8", allow_module_level=True)

# import must be after the module level skip:
from pos_only import *

def test_foo():
    assert foo(10, 20) == 30
    assert foo(10, b=20) == 30
    with raises(TypeError):
        assert foo(a=10, b=20)
```

My actual test involves parameterize and a 3.8 only class, so skipping the test itself is not sufficient because the 3.8 class was used in the parameterization.

A naive user will try to initially skip the module like:

```python
if sys.version_info < (3, 8):
    skip(msg="Requires Python >= 3.8")
```
This issues this error:

>Using pytest.skip outside of a test is not allowed. To decorate a test function, use the @pytest.mark.skip or @pytest.mark.skipif decorators instead, and to skip a module use `pytestmark = pytest.mark.{skip,skipif}.

The proposed solution `pytestmark = pytest.mark.{skip,skipif}`, does not work  in my case: pytest continues to process the file and fail when it hits the 3.8 syntax (when running with an older version of Python).

The correct solution, to use skip as a function is actively discouraged by the error message.

390     def _matches_prefix_or_glob_option(self, option_name: str, name: str) -> bool:
391         """Check if the given name matches the prefix or glob-pattern defined
392         in ini configuration."""
393         for option in self.config.getini(option_name):
394             if name.startswith(option):
395                 return True
396             # Check that name looks like a glob-string before calling fnmatch
397             # because this is called for every name in each collected module,
398             # and fnmatch is somewhat expensive to call.
399             elif ("*" in option or "?" in option or "[" in option) and fnmatch.fnmatch(
400                 name, option
401             ):

413             dicts.append(basecls.__dict__)

415         values: List[Union[nodes.Item, nodes.Collector]] = []
416         ihook = self.ihook

444         modulecol = self.getparent(Module)

446         module = modulecol.obj

451         definition = FunctionDefinition.from_parent(self, name=name, callobj=funcobj)

455             definition=definition,

459             module=module,

461         )
462         methods = []

572     def _importtestmodule(self):
573         # We assume we are only called once per module.
574         importmode = self.config.getoption("--import-mode")
575         try:
576             mod = import_path(self.path, mode=importmode, root=self.config.rootpath)
577         except SyntaxError as e:
578             raise self.CollectError(
579                 ExceptionInfo.from_current().getrepr(style="short")
580             ) from e
581         except ImportPathMismatchError as e:
582             raise self.CollectError(
583                 "import file mismatch:\n"
584                 "imported module %r has this __file__ attribute:\n"
585                 "  %s\n"
586                 "which is not the same as the test file we want to collect:\n"
587                 "  %s\n"
588                 "HINT: remove __pycache__ / .pyc files and/or use a "
589                 "unique basename for your test file modules" % e.args
590             ) from e
591         except ImportError as e:
592             exc_info = ExceptionInfo.from_current()
593             if self.config.getoption("verbose") < 2:
594                 exc_info.traceback = exc_info.traceback.filter(filter_traceback)
595             exc_repr = (
596                 exc_info.getrepr(style="short")
597                 if exc_info.traceback
598                 else exc_info.exconly()
599             )
600             formatted_tb = str(exc_repr)
601             raise self.CollectError(
602                 "ImportError while importing test module '{path}'.\n"
603                 "Hint: make sure your test modules/packages have valid Python names.\n"
604                 "Traceback:\n"
605                 "{traceback}".format(path=self.path, traceback=formatted_tb)
606             ) from e
607         except skip.Exception as e:
608             if e.allow_module_level:
609                 raise
610             raise self.CollectError(
611                 "Using pytest.skip outside of a test is not allowed. "
612                 "To decorate a test function, use the @pytest.mark.skip "
613                 "or @pytest.mark.skipif decorators instead, and to skip a "
614                 "module use `pytestmark = pytest.mark.{skip,skipif}."
615             ) from e
616         self.config.pluginmanager.consider_module(mod)
617         return mod

663         warnings.warn(FSCOLLECTOR_GETHOOKPROXY_ISINITPATH, stacklevel=2)

670     def _recurse(self, direntry: "os.DirEntry[str]") -> bool:
671         if direntry.name == "__pycache__":
672             return False
673         fspath = Path(direntry.path)
674         ihook = self.session.gethookproxy(fspath.parent)
675         if ihook.pytest_ignore_collect(fspath=fspath, config=self.config):
676             return False
677         norecursepatterns = self.config.getini("norecursedirs")
678         if any(fnmatch_ex(pat, fspath) for pat in norecursepatterns):
679             return False
680         return True
681 
682     def _collectfile(
683         self, fspath: Path, handle_dupes: bool = True
684     ) -> Sequence[nodes.Collector]:
685         assert (
686             fspath.is_file()
687         ), "{!r} is not a file (isdir={!r}, exists={!r}, islink={!r})".format(
688             fspath, fspath.is_dir(), fspath.exists(), fspath.is_symlink()
689         )
690         ihook = self.session.gethookproxy(fspath)
691         if not self.session.isinitpath(fspath):
692             if ihook.pytest_ignore_collect(fspath=fspath, config=self.config):
693                 return ()
694 
695         if handle_dupes:
696             keepduplicates = self.config.getoption("keepduplicates")
697             if not keepduplicates:
698                 duplicate_paths = self.config.pluginmanager._duplicatepaths
699                 if fspath in duplicate_paths:
700                     return ()
701                 else:
702                     duplicate_paths.add(fspath)
703 
704         return ihook.pytest_collect_file(fspath=fspath, parent=self)  # type: ignore[no-any-return]
705 
706     def collect(self) -> Iterable[Union[nodes.Item, nodes.Collector]]:
707         this_path = self.path.parent
708         init_module = this_path / "__init__.py"
709         if init_module.is_file() and path_matches_patterns(
710             init_module, self.config.getini("python_files")
711         ):
712             yield Module.from_parent(self, path=init_module)
713         pkg_prefixes: Set[Path] = set()
714         for direntry in visit(str(this_path), recurse=self._recurse):
715             path = Path(direntry.path)
716 
717             # We will visit our own __init__.py file, in which case we skip it.
718             if direntry.is_file():
719                 if direntry.name == "__init__.py" and path.parent == this_path:
720                     continue
721 
722             parts_ = parts(direntry.path)
723             if any(
724                 str(pkg_prefix) in parts_ and pkg_prefix / "__init__.py" != path
725                 for pkg_prefix in pkg_prefixes
726             ):
727                 continue
728 
729             if direntry.is_file():
730                 yield from self._collectfile(path)
731             elif not direntry.is_dir():
732                 # Broken symlink or invalid/missing file.
733                 continue
734             elif path.joinpath("__init__.py").is_file():
735                 pkg_prefixes.add(path)

738 def _call_with_optional_argument(func, arg) -> None:
739     """Call the given function with the given argument if func accepts one argument, otherwise
740     calls func without arguments."""
741     arg_count = func.__code__.co_argcount
742     if inspect.ismethod(func):
743         arg_count -= 1
744     if arg_count:
745         func(arg)
746     else:
747         func()

753     for name in names:

923     def setmulti2(

950 class Metafunc:
951     """Objects passed to the :func:`pytest_generate_tests <_pytest.hookspec.pytest_generate_tests>` hook.
952 
953     They help to inspect a test function and to generate tests according to
954     test configuration or values specified in the class or module where a
955     test function is defined.
956     """
957 
958     def __init__(
959         self,
960         definition: "FunctionDefinition",
961         fixtureinfo: fixtures.FuncFixtureInfo,
962         config: Config,
963         cls=None,
964         module=None,
965         *,
966         _ispytest: bool = False,
967     ) -> None:
968         check_ispytest(_ispytest)
969 
970         #: Access to the underlying :class:`_pytest.python.FunctionDefinition`.
971         self.definition = definition
972 
973         #: Access to the :class:`pytest.Config` object for the test session.
974         self.config = config
975 
976         #: The module object where the test function is defined in.
977         self.module = module
978 
979         #: Underlying Python test function.
980         self.function = definition.obj
981 
982         #: Set of fixture names required by the test function.
983         self.fixturenames = fixtureinfo.names_closure
984 
985         #: Class object where the test function is defined in or ``None``.
986         self.cls = cls
987 
988         self._calls: List[CallSpec2] = []
989         self._arg2fixturedefs = fixtureinfo.name2fixturedefs
990 
991     def parametrize(
992         self,
993         argnames: Union[str, List[str], Tuple[str, ...]],
994         argvalues: Iterable[Union[ParameterSet, Sequence[object], object]],
995         indirect: Union[bool, Sequence[str]] = False,
996         ids: Optional[
997             Union[
998                 Iterable[Union[None, str, float, int, bool]],
999                 Callable[[Any], Optional[object]],
1000             ]
1001         ] = None,
1002         scope: "Optional[_Scope]" = None,
1003         *,
1004         _param_mark: Optional[Mark] = None,
1005     ) -> None:
1006         """Add new invocations to the underlying test function using the list
1007         of argvalues for the given argnames.  Parametrization is performed
1008         during the collection phase.  If you need to setup expensive resources
1009         see about setting indirect to do it rather at test setup time.
1010 
1011         :param argnames:
1012             A comma-separated string denoting one or more argument names, or
1013             a list/tuple of argument strings.
1014 
1015         :param argvalues:
1016             The list of argvalues determines how often a test is invoked with
1017             different argument values.
1018 
1019             If only one argname was specified argvalues is a list of values.
1020             If N argnames were specified, argvalues must be a list of
1021             N-tuples, where each tuple-element specifies a value for its
1022             respective argname.
1023 
1024         :param indirect:
1025             A list of arguments' names (subset of argnames) or a boolean.
1026             If True the list contains all names from the argnames. Each
1027             argvalue corresponding to an argname in this list will
1028             be passed as request.param to its respective argname fixture
1029             function so that it can perform more expensive setups during the
1030             setup phase of a test rather than at collection time.
1031 
1032         :param ids:
1033             Sequence of (or generator for) ids for ``argvalues``,
1034             or a callable to return part of the id for each argvalue.
1035 
1036             With sequences (and generators like ``itertools.count()``) the
1037             returned ids should be of type ``string``, ``int``, ``float``,
1038             ``bool``, or ``None``.
1039             They are mapped to the corresponding index in ``argvalues``.
1040             ``None`` means to use the auto-generated id.
1041 
1042             If it is a callable it will be called for each entry in
1043             ``argvalues``, and the return value is used as part of the
1044             auto-generated id for the whole set (where parts are joined with
1045             dashes ("-")).
1046             This is useful to provide more specific ids for certain items, e.g.
1047             dates.  Returning ``None`` will use an auto-generated id.
1048 
1049             If no ids are provided they will be generated automatically from
1050             the argvalues.
1051 
1052         :param scope:
1053             If specified it denotes the scope of the parameters.
1054             The scope is used for grouping tests by parameter instances.
1055             It will also override any fixture-function defined scope, allowing
1056             to set a dynamic scope using test context or configuration.
1057         """
1058         from _pytest.fixtures import scope2index
1059 
1060         argnames, parameters = ParameterSet._for_parametrize(
1061             argnames,
1062             argvalues,
1063             self.function,
1064             self.config,
1065             nodeid=self.definition.nodeid,
1066         )
1067         del argvalues
1068 
1069         if "request" in argnames:
1070             fail(
1071                 "'request' is a reserved name and cannot be used in @pytest.mark.parametrize",
1072                 pytrace=False,
1073             )
1074 
1075         if scope is None:
1076             scope = _find_parametrized_scope(argnames, self._arg2fixturedefs, indirect)
1077 
1078         self._validate_if_using_arg_names(argnames, indirect)
1079 
1080         arg_values_types = self._resolve_arg_value_types(argnames, indirect)
1081 
1082         # Use any already (possibly) generated ids with parametrize Marks.
1083         if _param_mark and _param_mark._param_ids_from:
1084             generated_ids = _param_mark._param_ids_from._param_ids_generated
1085             if generated_ids is not None:
1086                 ids = generated_ids
1087 
1088         ids = self._resolve_arg_ids(
1089             argnames, ids, parameters, nodeid=self.definition.nodeid
1090         )
1091 
1092         # Store used (possibly generated) ids with parametrize Marks.
1093         if _param_mark and _param_mark._param_ids_from and generated_ids is None:
1094             object.__setattr__(_param_mark._param_ids_from, "_param_ids_generated", ids)
1095 
1096         scopenum = scope2index(
1097             scope, descr=f"parametrize() call in {self.function.__name__}"
1098         )
1099

problem_statement:
Improve handling of skip for module level
This is potentially about updating docs, updating error messages or introducing a new API.

Consider the following scenario:

`pos_only.py` is using Python 3,8 syntax:
```python
def foo(a, /, b):
    return a + b
```

It should not be tested under Python 3.6 and 3.7.
This is a proper way to skip the test in Python older than 3.8:
```python
from pytest import raises, skip
import sys
if sys.version_info < (3, 8):
    skip(msg="Requires Python >= 3.8", allow_module_level=True)

# import must be after the module level skip:
from pos_only import *

def test_foo():
    assert foo(10, 20) == 30
    assert foo(10, b=20) == 30
    with raises(TypeError):
        assert foo(a=10, b=20)
```

My actual test involves parameterize and a 3.8 only class, so skipping the test itself is not sufficient because the 3.8 class was used in the parameterization.

A naive user will try to initially skip the module like:

```python
if sys.version_info < (3, 8):
    skip(msg="Requires Python >= 3.8")
```
This issues this error:

>Using pytest.skip outside of a test is not allowed. To decorate a test function, use the @pytest.mark.skip or @pytest.mark.skipif decorators instead, and to skip a module use `pytestmark = pytest.mark.{skip,skipif}.

The proposed solution `pytestmark = pytest.mark.{skip,skipif}`, does not work  in my case: pytest continues to process the file and fail when it hits the 3.8 syntax (when running with an older version of Python).

The correct solution, to use skip as a function is actively discouraged by the error message.

This area feels a bit unpolished.
A few ideas to improve:

1. Explain skip with  `allow_module_level` in the error message. this seems in conflict with the spirit of the message.
2. Create an alternative API to skip a module to make things easier: `skip_module("reason")`, which can call `_skip(msg=msg, allow_module_level=True)`.

Hi @omry,

Thanks for raising this.

Definitely we should improve that message. 

> Explain skip with allow_module_level in the error message. this seems in conflict with the spirit of the message.

I'm 👍 on this. 2 is also good, but because `allow_module_level` already exists and is part of the public API, I don't think introducing a new API will really help, better to improve the docs of what we already have.

Perhaps improve the message to something like this:

```
Using pytest.skip outside of a test will skip the entire module, if that's your intention pass `allow_module_level=True`. 
If you want to skip a specific test or entire class, use the @pytest.mark.skip or @pytest.mark.skipif decorators.
```

I think we can drop the `pytestmark` remark from there, it is not skip-specific and passing `allow_module_level` already accomplishes the same.

Thanks @nicoddemus.

> Using pytest.skip outside of a test will skip the entire module, if that's your intention pass `allow_module_level=True`. 
If you want to skip a specific test or entire class, use the @pytest.mark.skip or @pytest.mark.skipif decorators.

This sounds clearer.
Can you give a bit of context of why the message is there in the first place?
It sounds like we should be able to automatically detect if this is skipping a test or skipping the entire module (based on the fact that we can issue the warning).

Maybe this is addressing some past confusion, or we want to push people toward `pytest.mark.skip[if]`, but if we can detect it automatically - we can also deprecate allow_module_level and make `skip()` do the right thing based on the context it's used in.
> Maybe this is addressing some past confusion

That's exactly it, people would use `@pytest.skip` instead of `@pytest.mark.skip` and skip the whole module:

https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/2338#issuecomment-290324255

For that reason we don't really want to automatically detect things, but want users to explicitly pass that flag which proves they are not doing it by accident.

Original issue: https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/607
Having looked at the links, I think the alternative API to skip a module is more appealing.
Here is a proposed end state:

1. pytest.skip_module is introduced, can be used to skip a module.
2. pytest.skip() is only legal inside of a test. If called outside of a test, an error message is issues.
Example:

> pytest.skip should only be used inside tests. To skip a module use pytest.skip_module. To completely skip a test function or a test class, use the @pytest.mark.skip or @pytest.mark.skipif decorators.

Getting to this end state would include deprecating allow_module_level first, directing people using pytest.skip(allow_module_level=True) to use pytest.skip_module().

I am also fine with just changing the message as you initially proposed but I feel this proposal will result in an healthier state.

-0.5 from my side - I think this is too minor to warrant another deprecation and change.
I agree it would be healthier, but -1 from me for the same reasons as @The-Compiler: we already had a deprecation/change period in order to introduce `allow_module_level`, having yet another one is frustrating/confusing to users, in comparison to the small gains.

<issue>
Allow returning IDs in QuerySet.bulk_create() when updating conflicts.
Description
	
Currently, when using bulk_create with a conflict handling flag turned on (e.g. ignore_conflicts or update_conflicts), the primary keys are not set in the returned queryset, as documented in bulk_create.
While I understand using ignore_conflicts can lead to PostgreSQL not returning the IDs when a row is ignored (see ​this SO thread), I don't understand why we don't return the IDs in the case of update_conflicts.
For instance:
MyModel.objects.bulk_create([MyModel(...)], update_conflicts=True, update_fields=[...], unique_fields=[...])
generates a query without a RETURNING my_model.id part:
INSERT INTO "my_model" (...)
VALUES (...)
	ON CONFLICT(...) DO UPDATE ...
If I append the RETURNING my_model.id clause, the query is indeed valid and the ID is returned (checked with PostgreSQL).
I investigated a bit and ​this in Django source is where the returning_fields gets removed.
I believe we could discriminate the cases differently so as to keep those returning_fields in the case of update_conflicts.
This would be highly helpful when using bulk_create as a bulk upsert feature.

</issue>

45 class BaseIterable:
46     def __init__(
47         self, queryset, chunked_fetch=False, chunk_size=GET_ITERATOR_CHUNK_SIZE
48     ):
49         self.queryset = queryset
50         self.chunked_fetch = chunked_fetch
51         self.chunk_size = chunk_size
52 
53     async def _async_generator(self):
54         # Generators don't actually start running until the first time you call
55         # next() on them, so make the generator object in the async thread and
56         # then repeatedly dispatch to it in a sync thread.
57         sync_generator = self.__iter__()
58 
59         def next_slice(gen):
60             return list(islice(gen, self.chunk_size))
61 
62         while True:
63             chunk = await sync_to_async(next_slice)(sync_generator)
64             for item in chunk:
65                 yield item
66             if len(chunk) < self.chunk_size:
67                 break
68 
69     # __aiter__() is a *synchronous* method that has to then return an
70     # *asynchronous* iterator/generator. Thus, nest an async generator inside
71     # it.
72     # This is a generic iterable converter for now, and is going to suffer a
73     # performance penalty on large sets of items due to the cost of crossing
74     # over the sync barrier for each chunk. Custom __aiter__() methods should
75     # be added to each Iterable subclass, but that needs some work in the
76     # Compiler first.
77     def __aiter__(self):
78         return self._async_generator()

84     def __iter__(self):

88         # Execute the query. This will also fill compiler.select, klass_info,
89         # and annotations.
90         results = compiler.execute_sql(
91             chunked_fetch=self.chunked_fetch, chunk_size=self.chunk_size
92         )
93         select, klass_info, annotation_col_map = (
94             compiler.select,
95             compiler.klass_info,
96             compiler.annotation_col_map,
97         )
98         model_cls = klass_info["model"]
99         select_fields = klass_info["select_fields"]
100         model_fields_start, model_fields_end = select_fields[0], select_fields[-1] + 1
101         init_list = [
102             f[0].target.attname for f in select[model_fields_start:model_fields_end]
103         ]
104         related_populators = get_related_populators(klass_info, select, db)
105         known_related_objects = [
106             (
107                 field,
108                 related_objs,
109                 operator.attrgetter(
110                     *[
111                         field.attname
112                         if from_field == "self"
113                         else queryset.model._meta.get_field(from_field).attname
114                         for from_field in field.from_fields
115                     ]
116                 ),
117             )
118             for field, related_objs in queryset._known_related_objects.items()
119         ]
120         for row in compiler.results_iter(results):
121             obj = model_cls.from_db(
122                 db, init_list, row[model_fields_start:model_fields_end]
123             )
124             for rel_populator in related_populators:
125                 rel_populator.populate(row, obj)
126             if annotation_col_map:
127                 for attr_name, col_pos in annotation_col_map.items():
128                     setattr(obj, attr_name, row[col_pos])
129

131             for field, rel_objs, rel_getter in known_related_objects:
132                 # Avoid overwriting objects loaded by, e.g., select_related().
133                 if field.is_cached(obj):
134                     continue
135                 rel_obj_id = rel_getter(obj)
136                 try:
137                     rel_obj = rel_objs[rel_obj_id]
138                 except KeyError:
139                     pass  # May happen in qs1 | qs2 scenarios.
140                 else:
141                     setattr(obj, field.name, rel_obj)
142 
143             yield obj

151     def __iter__(self):
152         # Cache some things for performance reasons outside the loop.
153         db = self.queryset.db
154         query = self.queryset.query
155         connection = connections[db]
156         compiler = connection.ops.compiler("SQLCompiler")(query, connection, db)
157         query_iterator = iter(query)

160             (

382     def __iter__(self):
383         """
384         The queryset iterator protocol uses three nested iterators in the
385         default case:
386             1. sql.compiler.execute_sql()
387                - Returns 100 rows at time (constants.GET_ITERATOR_CHUNK_SIZE)
388                  using cursor.fetchmany(). This part is responsible for
389                  doing some column masking, and returning the rows in chunks.
390             2. sql.compiler.results_iter()
391                - Returns one row at time. At this point the rows are still just
392                  tuples. In some cases the return values are converted to
393                  Python values at this location.
394             3. self.iterator()
395                - Responsible for turning the rows into model objects.
396         """
397         self._fetch_all()
398         return iter(self._result_cache)
