You will be provided with a partial code base and an issue statement explaining a problem to resolve.
<issue>
QuerySet.Delete - inconsistent result when zero objects deleted
Description
	
The result format of the QuerySet.Delete method is a tuple: (X, Y) 
X - is the total amount of deleted objects (including foreign key deleted objects)
Y - is a dictionary specifying counters of deleted objects for each specific model (the key is the _meta.label of the model and the value is counter of deleted objects of this model).
Example: <class 'tuple'>: (2, {'my_app.FileAccess': 1, 'my_app.File': 1})
When there are zero objects to delete in total - the result is inconsistent:
For models with foreign keys - the result will be: <class 'tuple'>: (0, {})
For "simple" models without foreign key - the result will be: <class 'tuple'>: (0, {'my_app.BlockLibrary': 0})
I would expect there will be no difference between the two cases: Either both will have the empty dictionary OR both will have dictionary with model-label keys and zero value.

</issue>

217         """
218         Add 'objs' to the collection of objects to be deleted as well as all
219         parent instances.  'objs' must be a homogeneous iterable collection of
220         model instances (e.g. a QuerySet).  If 'collect_related' is True,
221         related objects will be handled by their respective on_delete handler.
222 
223         If the call is the result of a cascade, 'source' should be the model
224         that caused it and 'nullable' should be set to True, if the relation
225         can be null.
226 
227         If 'reverse_dependency' is True, 'source' will be deleted before the
228         current model, rather than after. (Needed for cascading to parent
229         models, the one case in which the cascade follows the forwards
230         direction of an FK rather than the reverse direction.)
231 
232         If 'keep_parents' is True, data of parent model's will be not deleted.
233 
234         If 'fail_on_restricted' is False, error won't be raised even if it's
235         prohibited to delete such objects due to RESTRICT, that defers
236         restricted object checking in recursive calls where the top-level call
237         may need to collect more objects to determine whether restricted ones
238         can be deleted.
239         """
240         if self.can_fast_delete(objs):
241             self.fast_deletes.append(objs)
242             return
243         new_objs = self.add(objs, source, nullable,
244                             reverse_dependency=reverse_dependency)
245         if not new_objs:
246             return
247 
248         model = new_objs[0].__class__
249 
250         if not keep_parents:

252             # related objects. These will be found by meta.get_fields()

261                                  fail_on_restricted=False)

268         protected_objects = defaultdict(list)

problem_statement:
QuerySet.Delete - inconsistent result when zero objects deleted
Description
	
The result format of the QuerySet.Delete method is a tuple: (X, Y) 
X - is the total amount of deleted objects (including foreign key deleted objects)
Y - is a dictionary specifying counters of deleted objects for each specific model (the key is the _meta.label of the model and the value is counter of deleted objects of this model).
Example: <class 'tuple'>: (2, {'my_app.FileAccess': 1, 'my_app.File': 1})
When there are zero objects to delete in total - the result is inconsistent:
For models with foreign keys - the result will be: <class 'tuple'>: (0, {})
For "simple" models without foreign key - the result will be: <class 'tuple'>: (0, {'my_app.BlockLibrary': 0})
I would expect there will be no difference between the two cases: Either both will have the empty dictionary OR both will have dictionary with model-label keys and zero value.
hints_text: I guess we could adapt the code not to include any key if the count is zero in the second case.

urllib3 exceptions passing through requests API
I don't know if it's a design goal of requests to hide urllib3's exceptions and wrap them around requests.exceptions types.

(If it's not IMHO it should be, but that's another discussion)

If it is, I have at least two of them passing through that I have to catch in addition to requests' exceptions. They are requests.packages.urllib3.exceptions.DecodeError and requests.packages.urllib3.exceptions.TimeoutError (this one I get when a proxy timeouts)

Thanks!

<issue>
lambdify does not work with certain MatrixSymbol names even with dummify=True
`lambdify` is happy with curly braces in a symbol name and with `MatrixSymbol`s, but not with both at the same time, even if `dummify` is `True`.

Here is some basic code that gives the error.
```
import sympy as sy
curlyx = sy.symbols("{x}")
v = sy.MatrixSymbol("v", 2, 1)
curlyv = sy.MatrixSymbol("{v}", 2, 1)
```

The following two lines of code work:
```
curlyScalarId = sy.lambdify(curlyx, curlyx)
vectorId = sy.lambdify(v,v)
```

The following two lines of code give a `SyntaxError`:
```
curlyVectorId = sy.lambdify(curlyv, curlyv)
curlyVectorIdDummified = sy.lambdify(curlyv, curlyv, dummify=True)
```

166 def lambdify(args, expr, modules=None, printer=None, use_imps=True,
167              dummify=False):
168     """
169     Returns an anonymous function for fast calculation of numerical values.
170 
171     If not specified differently by the user, ``modules`` defaults to
172     ``["numpy"]`` if NumPy is installed, and ``["math", "mpmath", "sympy"]``
173     if it isn't, that is, SymPy functions are replaced as far as possible by
174     either ``numpy`` functions if available, and Python's standard library
175     ``math``, or ``mpmath`` functions otherwise. To change this behavior, the
176     "modules" argument can be used. It accepts:
177 
178      - the strings "math", "mpmath", "numpy", "numexpr", "sympy", "tensorflow"
179      - any modules (e.g. math)
180      - dictionaries that map names of sympy functions to arbitrary functions
181      - lists that contain a mix of the arguments above, with higher priority
182        given to entries appearing first.
183 
184     .. warning::
185         Note that this function uses ``eval``, and thus shouldn't be used on
186         unsanitized input.
187 
188     Arguments in the provided expression that are not valid Python identifiers
189     are substitued with dummy symbols. This allows for applied functions
190     (e.g. f(t)) to be supplied as arguments. Call the function with
191     dummify=True to replace all arguments with dummy symbols (if `args` is
192     not a string) - for example, to ensure that the arguments do not
193     redefine any built-in names.
194 
195     For functions involving large array calculations, numexpr can provide a
196     significant speedup over numpy.  Please note that the available functions
197     for numexpr are more limited than numpy but can be expanded with
198     implemented_function and user defined subclasses of Function.  If specified,
199     numexpr may be the only option in modules. The official list of numexpr
200     functions can be found at:
201     https://github.com/pydata/numexpr#supported-functions
202 
203     In previous releases ``lambdify`` replaced ``Matrix`` with ``numpy.matrix``
204     by default. As of release 1.0 ``numpy.array`` is the default.
205     To get the old default behavior you must pass in ``[{'ImmutableDenseMatrix':
206     numpy.matrix}, 'numpy']`` to the ``modules`` kwarg.
207 
208     >>> from sympy import lambdify, Matrix
209     >>> from sympy.abc import x, y
210     >>> import numpy
211     >>> array2mat = [{'ImmutableDenseMatrix': numpy.matrix}, 'numpy']
212     >>> f = lambdify((x, y), Matrix([x, y]), modules=array2mat)
213     >>> f(1, 2)
214     matrix([[1],
215             [2]])
216 
217     Usage
218     =====
219 
220     (1) Use one of the provided modules:
221 
222         >>> from sympy import sin, tan, gamma
223         >>> from sympy.abc import x, y
224         >>> f = lambdify(x, sin(x), "math")
225 
226         Attention: Functions that are not in the math module will throw a name
227                    error when the function definition is evaluated! So this
228                    would be better:
229 
230         >>> f = lambdify(x, sin(x)*gamma(x), ("math", "mpmath", "sympy"))
231 
232     (2) Use some other module:
233 
234         >>> import numpy
235         >>> f = lambdify((x,y), tan(x*y), numpy)
236 
237         Attention: There are naming differences between numpy and sympy. So if
238                    you simply take the numpy module, e.g. sympy.atan will not be
239                    translated to numpy.arctan. Use the modified module instead
240                    by passing the string "numpy":
241 
242         >>> f = lambdify((x,y), tan(x*y), "numpy")
243         >>> f(1, 2)
244         -2.18503986326
245         >>> from numpy import array
246         >>> f(array([1, 2, 3]), array([2, 3, 5]))
247         [-2.18503986 -0.29100619 -0.8559934 ]
248 
249         In the above examples, the generated functions can accept scalar
250         values or numpy arrays as arguments.  However, in some cases
251         the generated function relies on the input being a numpy array:
252 
253         >>> from sympy import Piecewise
254         >>> f = lambdify(x, Piecewise((x, x <= 1), (1/x, x > 1)), "numpy")
255         >>> f(array([-1, 0, 1, 2]))
256         [-1.   0.   1.   0.5]
257         >>> f(0)
258         Traceback (most recent call last):
259             ...
260         ZeroDivisionError: division by zero
261 
262         In such cases, the input should be wrapped in a numpy array:
263         >>> float(f(array([0])))
264         0.0
265 
266         Or if numpy functionality is not required another module can be used:
267         >>> f = lambdify(x, Piecewise((x, x <= 1), (1/x, x > 1)), "math")
268         >>> f(0)
269         0
270 
271     (3) Use a dictionary defining custom functions:
272 
273         >>> def my_cool_function(x): return 'sin(%s) is cool' % x
274         >>> myfuncs = {"sin" : my_cool_function}
275         >>> f = lambdify(x, sin(x), myfuncs); f(1)
276         'sin(1) is cool'
277 
278     Examples
279     ========
280 
281     >>> from sympy.utilities.lambdify import implemented_function
282     >>> from sympy import sqrt, sin, Matrix
283     >>> from sympy import Function
284     >>> from sympy.abc import w, x, y, z
285 
286     >>> f = lambdify(x, x**2)
287     >>> f(2)
288     4
289     >>> f = lambdify((x, y, z), [z, y, x])
290     >>> f(1,2,3)
291     [3, 2, 1]
292     >>> f = lambdify(x, sqrt(x))
293     >>> f(4)
294     2.0
295     >>> f = lambdify((x, y), sin(x*y)**2)
296     >>> f(0, 5)
297     0.0
298     >>> row = lambdify((x, y), Matrix((x, x + y)).T, modules='sympy')
299     >>> row(1, 2)
300     Matrix([[1, 3]])
301 
302     Tuple arguments are handled and the lambdified function should
303     be called with the same type of arguments as were used to create
304     the function.:
305 
306     >>> f = lambdify((x, (y, z)), x + y)
307     >>> f(1, (2, 4))
308     3
309 
310     A more robust way of handling this is to always work with flattened
311     arguments:
312 
313     >>> from sympy.utilities.iterables import flatten
314     >>> args = w, (x, (y, z))
315     >>> vals = 1, (2, (3, 4))
316     >>> f = lambdify(flatten(args), w + x + y + z)
317     >>> f(*flatten(vals))
318     10
319 
320     Functions present in `expr` can also carry their own numerical
321     implementations, in a callable attached to the ``_imp_``
322     attribute.  Usually you attach this using the
323     ``implemented_function`` factory:
324 
325     >>> f = implemented_function(Function('f'), lambda x: x+1)
326     >>> func = lambdify(x, f(x))
327     >>> func(4)
328     5
329 
330     ``lambdify`` always prefers ``_imp_`` implementations to implementations
331     in other namespaces, unless the ``use_imps`` input parameter is False.
332 
333     Usage with Tensorflow module:
334 
335     >>> import tensorflow as tf
336     >>> f = Max(x, sin(x))
337     >>> func = lambdify(x, f, 'tensorflow')
338     >>> result = func(tf.constant(1.0))
339     >>> result # a tf.Tensor representing the result of the calculation
340     <tf.Tensor 'Maximum:0' shape=() dtype=float32>
341     >>> sess = tf.Session()
342     >>> sess.run(result) # compute result
343     1.0
344     >>> var = tf.Variable(1.0)
345     >>> sess.run(tf.global_variables_initializer())
346     >>> sess.run(func(var)) # also works for tf.Variable and tf.Placeholder
347     1.0
348     >>> tensor = tf.constant([[1.0, 2.0], [3.0, 4.0]]) # works with any shape tensor
349     >>> sess.run(func(tensor))
350     array([[ 1.,  2.],
351            [ 3.,  4.]], dtype=float32)
352 
353     """
354     from sympy.core.symbol import Symbol
355     from sympy.utilities.iterables import flatten
356 
357     # If the user hasn't specified any modules, use what is available.
358     module_provided = True
359     if modules is None:
360         module_provided = False
361 
362         try:
363             _import("numpy")
364         except ImportError:
365             # Use either numpy (if available) or python.math where possible.
366             # XXX: This leads to different behaviour on different systems and
367             #      might be the reason for irreproducible errors.
368             modules = ["math", "mpmath", "sympy"]
369         else:
370             modules = ["numpy"]
371 
372     # Get the needed namespaces.
373     namespaces = []
374     # First find any function implementations
375     if use_imps:
376         namespaces.append(_imp_namespace(expr))
377     # Check for dict before iterating
378     if isinstance(modules, (dict, str)) or not hasattr(modules, '__iter__'):
379         namespaces.append(modules)
380     else:
381         # consistency check
382         if _module_present('numexpr', modules) and len(modules) > 1:
383             raise TypeError("numexpr must be the only item in 'modules'")
384         namespaces += list(modules)
385     # fill namespace with first having highest priority
386     namespace = {}
387     for m in namespaces[::-1]:
388         buf = _get_namespace(m)
389         namespace.update(buf)
390 
391     if hasattr(expr, "atoms"):
392         #Try if you can extract symbols from the expression.
393         #Move on if expr.atoms in not implemented.
394         syms = expr.atoms(Symbol)
395         for term in syms:
396             namespace.update({str(term): term})
397 
398     if printer is None:
399         if _module_present('mpmath', namespaces):
400             from sympy.printing.pycode import MpmathPrinter as Printer
401         elif _module_present('numpy', namespaces):
402             from sympy.printing.pycode import NumPyPrinter as Printer
403         elif _module_present('numexpr', namespaces):
404             from sympy.printing.lambdarepr import NumExprPrinter as Printer
405         elif _module_present('tensorflow', namespaces):
406             from sympy.printing.lambdarepr import TensorflowPrinter as Printer
407         elif _module_present('sympy', namespaces):
408             from sympy.printing.pycode import SymPyPrinter as Printer
409         else:
410             from sympy.printing.pycode import PythonCodePrinter as Printer
411         user_functions = {}
412         for m in namespaces[::-1]:
413             if isinstance(m, dict):
414                 for k in m:
415                     user_functions[k] = k
416         printer = Printer({'fully_qualified_modules': False, 'inline': True,
417                            'user_functions': user_functions})
418 
419     # Get the names of the args, for creating a docstring
420     if not iterable(args):
421         args = (args,)
422     names = []
423     # Grab the callers frame, for getting the names by inspection (if needed)
424     callers_local_vars = inspect.currentframe().f_back.f_locals.items()
425     for n, var in enumerate(args):
426         if hasattr(var, 'name'):
427             names.append(var.name)
428         else:
429             # It's an iterable. Try to get name by inspection of calling frame.
430             name_list = [var_name for var_name, var_val in callers_local_vars
431                     if var_val is var]
432             if len(name_list) == 1:
433                 names.append(name_list[0])
434             else:
435                 # Cannot infer name with certainty. arg_# will have to do.
436                 names.append('arg_' + str(n))
437 
438     imp_mod_lines = []
439     for mod, keys in (getattr(printer, 'module_imports', None) or {}).items():
440         for k in keys:
441             if k not in namespace:
442                 imp_mod_lines.append("from %s import %s" % (mod, k))
443     for ln in imp_mod_lines:
444         exec_(ln, {}, namespace)
445 
446     # Provide lambda expression with builtins, and compatible implementation of range
447     namespace.update({'builtins':builtins, 'range':range})
448 
449     # Create the function definition code and execute it
450 
451     funcname = '_lambdifygenerated'
452 
453     if _module_present('tensorflow', namespaces):
454         funcprinter = _TensorflowEvaluatorPrinter(printer, dummify)
455     else:
456         funcprinter = _EvaluatorPrinter(printer, dummify)
457 
458     funcstr = funcprinter.doprint(funcname, args, expr)
459 
460     funclocals = {}
461     global _lambdify_generated_counter
462     filename = '<lambdifygenerated-%s>' % _lambdify_generated_counter
463     _lambdify_generated_counter += 1
464     c = compile(funcstr, filename, 'exec')
465     exec_(c, namespace, funclocals)
466     # mtime has to be None or else linecache.checkcache will remove it
467     linecache.cache[filename] = (len(funcstr), None, funcstr.splitlines(True), filename)
468 
469     func = funclocals[funcname]
470 
471     # Apply the docstring
472     sig = "func({0})".format(", ".join(str(i) for i in names))
473     sig = textwrap.fill(sig, subsequent_indent=' '*8)
474     expr_str = str(expr)
475     if len(expr_str) > 78:
476         expr_str = textwrap.wrap(expr_str, 75)[0] + '...'
477     func.__doc__ = (
478         "Created with lambdify. Signature:\n\n"
479         "{sig}\n\n"
480         "Expression:\n\n"
481         "{expr}\n\n"
482         "Source code:\n\n"
483         "{src}\n\n"
484         "Imported modules:\n\n"
485         "{imp_mods}"
486         ).format(sig=sig, expr=expr_str, src=funcstr, imp_mods='\n'.join(imp_mod_lines))
487     return func
488

490     if modname in modlist:
491         return True
492     for m in modlist:
493         if hasattr(m, '__name__') and m.__name__ == modname:
494             return True
495     return False

512 def lambdastr(args, expr, printer=None, dummify=False):
513     """
514     Returns a string that can be evaluated to a lambda function.
515 
516     Examples
517     ========
518 
519     >>> from sympy.abc import x, y, z
520     >>> from sympy.utilities.lambdify import lambdastr
521     >>> lambdastr(x, x**2)
522     'lambda x: (x**2)'
523     >>> lambdastr((x,y,z), [z,y,x])
524     'lambda x,y,z: ([z, y, x])'
525 
526     Although tuples may not appear as arguments to lambda in Python 3,
527     lambdastr will create a lambda function that will unpack the original
528     arguments so that nested arguments can be handled:
529 
530     >>> lambdastr((x, (y, z)), x + y)
531     'lambda _0,_1: (lambda x,y,z: (x + y))(_0,_1[0],_1[1])'
532     """
533     # Transforming everything to strings.
534     from sympy.matrices import DeferredVector
535     from sympy import Dummy, sympify, Symbol, Function, flatten
536 
537     if printer is not None:
538         if inspect.isfunction(printer):
539             lambdarepr = printer
540         else:
541             if inspect.isclass(printer):
542                 lambdarepr = lambda expr: printer().doprint(expr)
543             else:
544                 lambdarepr = lambda expr: printer.doprint(expr)
545     else:
546         #XXX: This has to be done here because of circular imports
547         from sympy.printing.lambdarepr import lambdarepr
548 
549     def sub_args(args, dummies_dict):
550         if isinstance(args, str):
551             return args
552         elif isinstance(args, DeferredVector):
553             return str(args)
554         elif iterable(args):
555             dummies = flatten([sub_args(a, dummies_dict) for a in args])
556             return ",".join(str(a) for a in dummies)
557         else:
558             #Sub in dummy variables for functions or symbols
559             if isinstance(args, (Function, Symbol)):
560                 dummies = Dummy()
561                 dummies_dict.update({args : dummies})
562                 return str(dummies)
563             else:
564                 return str(args)
565 
566     def sub_expr(expr, dummies_dict):
567         try:
568             expr = sympify(expr).xreplace(dummies_dict)
569         except Exception:
570             if isinstance(expr, DeferredVector):
571                 pass
572             elif isinstance(expr, dict):
573                 k = [sub_expr(sympify(a), dummies_dict) for a in expr.keys()]
574                 v = [sub_expr(sympify(a), dummies_dict) for a in expr.values()]
575                 expr = dict(zip(k, v))
576             elif isinstance(expr, tuple):
577                 expr = tuple(sub_expr(sympify(a), dummies_dict) for a in expr)
578             elif isinstance(expr, list):
579                 expr = [sub_expr(sympify(a), dummies_dict) for a in expr]
580         return expr
581 
582     # Transform args
583     def isiter(l):
584         return iterable(l, exclude=(str, DeferredVector, NotIterable))
585 
586     def flat_indexes(iterable):
587         n = 0
588 
589         for el in iterable:
590             if isiter(el):
591                 for ndeep in flat_indexes(el):
592                     yield (n,) + ndeep
593             else:
594                 yield (n,)
595 
596             n += 1
597 
598     if isiter(args) and any(isiter(i) for i in args):
599         dum_args = [str(Dummy(str(i))) for i in range(len(args))]
600 
601         indexed_args = ','.join([
602             dum_args[ind[0]] + ''.join(["[%s]" % k for k in ind[1:]])
603                     for ind in flat_indexes(args)])
604 
605         lstr = lambdastr(flatten(args), expr, printer=printer, dummify=dummify)
606 
607         return 'lambda %s: (%s)(%s)' % (','.join(dum_args), lstr, indexed_args)
608 
609     dummies_dict = {}
610     if dummify:
611         args = sub_args(args, dummies_dict)
612     else:
613         if isinstance(args, str):
614             pass
615         elif iterable(args, exclude=DeferredVector):
616             args = ",".join(str(a) for a in args)
617 
618     # Transform expr
619     if dummify:
620         if isinstance(expr, str):
621             pass
622         else:
623             expr = sub_expr(expr, dummies_dict)
624     expr = lambdarepr(expr)
625     return "lambda %s: (%s)" % (args, expr)
626 
627 class _EvaluatorPrinter(object):
628     def __init__(self, printer=None, dummify=False):
629         self._dummify = dummify
630 
631         #XXX: This has to be done here because of circular imports
632         from sympy.printing.lambdarepr import LambdaPrinter
633 
634         if printer is None:
635             printer = LambdaPrinter()
636 
637         if inspect.isfunction(printer):
638             self._exprrepr = printer
639         else:
640             if inspect.isclass(printer):
641                 printer = printer()
642 
643             self._exprrepr = printer.doprint
644 
645             if hasattr(printer, '_print_Symbol'):
646                 symbolrepr = printer._print_Symbol
647 
648             if hasattr(printer, '_print_Dummy'):
649                 dummyrepr = printer._print_Dummy
650 
651         # Used to print the generated function arguments in a standard way
652         self._argrepr = LambdaPrinter().doprint
653 
654     def doprint(self, funcname, args, expr):
655         """Returns the function definition code as a string."""
656         from sympy import Dummy
657 
658         funcbody = []
659 
660         if not iterable(args):
661             args = [args]
662 
663         argstrs, expr = self._preprocess(args, expr)
664 
665         # Generate argument unpacking and final argument list
666         funcargs = []
667         unpackings = []
668 
669         for argstr in argstrs:
670             if iterable(argstr):
671                 funcargs.append(self._argrepr(Dummy()))
672                 unpackings.extend(self._print_unpacking(argstr, funcargs[-1]))
673             else:
674                 funcargs.append(argstr)
675 
676         funcsig = 'def {}({}):'.format(funcname, ', '.join(funcargs))
677 
678         # Wrap input arguments before unpacking
679         funcbody.extend(self._print_funcargwrapping(funcargs))
680 
681         funcbody.extend(unpackings)
682 
683         funcbody.append('return ({})'.format(self._exprrepr(expr)))
684 
685         funclines = [funcsig]
686         funclines.extend('    ' + line for line in funcbody)
687 
688         return '\n'.join(funclines) + '\n'
689 
690     if PY3:
691         @classmethod
692         def _is_safe_ident(cls, ident):
693             return isinstance(ident, str) and ident.isidentifier() \
694                     and not keyword.iskeyword(ident)
695     else:
696         _safe_ident_re = re.compile('^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$')
697 
698         @classmethod
699         def _is_safe_ident(cls, ident):
700             return isinstance(ident, str) and cls._safe_ident_re.match(ident) \
701                 and not (keyword.iskeyword(ident) or ident == 'None')

704     def _preprocess(self, args, expr):
705         """Preprocess args, expr to replace arguments that do not map
706         to valid Python identifiers.
707 
708         Returns string form of args, and updated expr.
709         """
710         from sympy import Dummy, Symbol, Function, flatten
711         from sympy.matrices import DeferredVector
712 
713         dummify = self._dummify
714 
715         # Args of type Dummy can cause name collisions with args
716         # of type Symbol.  Force dummify of everything in this
717         # situation.
718         if not dummify:
719             dummify = any(isinstance(arg, Dummy) for arg in flatten(args))
720 
721         argstrs = []
722         for arg in args:
723             if iterable(arg):
724                 nested_argstrs, expr = self._preprocess(arg, expr)
725                 argstrs.append(nested_argstrs)
726             elif isinstance(arg, DeferredVector):
727                 argstrs.append(str(arg))
728             elif isinstance(arg, Symbol):
729                 argrep = self._argrepr(arg)
730 
731                 if dummify or not self._is_safe_ident(argrep):
732                     dummy = Dummy()
733                     argstrs.append(self._argrepr(dummy))
734                     expr = self._subexpr(expr, {arg: dummy})
735                 else:
736                     argstrs.append(argrep)
737             elif isinstance(arg, Function):
738                 dummy = Dummy()
739                 argstrs.append(self._argrepr(dummy))
740                 expr = self._subexpr(expr, {arg: dummy})
741             else:
742                 argstrs.append(str(arg))
743 
744         return argstrs, expr
745 
746     def _subexpr(self, expr, dummies_dict):
747         from sympy.matrices import DeferredVector
748         from sympy import sympify
749 
750         try:
751             expr = sympify(expr).xreplace(dummies_dict)
752         except Exception:
753             if isinstance(expr, DeferredVector):
754                 pass
755             elif isinstance(expr, dict):
756                 k = [self._subexpr(sympify(a), dummies_dict) for a in expr.keys()]
757                 v = [self._subexpr(sympify(a), dummies_dict) for a in expr.values()]
758                 expr = dict(zip(k, v))
759             elif isinstance(expr, tuple):
760                 expr = tuple(self._subexpr(sympify(a), dummies_dict) for a in expr)
761             elif isinstance(expr, list):
762                 expr = [self._subexpr(sympify(a), dummies_dict) for a in expr]
763         return expr
764 
765     def _print_funcargwrapping(self, args):
766         """Generate argument wrapping code.
767 
768         args is the argument list of the generated function (strings).
769 
770         Return value is a list of lines of code that will be inserted  at
771         the beginning of the function definition.
772         """
773         return []
774 
775     def _print_unpacking(self, unpackto, arg):
776         """Generate argument unpacking code.
777 
778         arg is the function argument to be unpacked (a string), and
779         unpackto is a list or nested lists of the variable names (strings) to
780         unpack to.
781         """
782         def unpack_lhs(lvalues):
783             return '[{}]'.format(', '.join(
784                 unpack_lhs(val) if iterable(val) else val for val in lvalues))
785 
786         return ['{} = {}'.format(unpack_lhs(unpackto), arg)]

788 class _TensorflowEvaluatorPrinter(_EvaluatorPrinter):
789     def _print_unpacking(self, lvalues, rvalue):
790         """Generate argument unpacking code.
791 
792         This method is used when the input value is not interable,
793         but can be indexed (see issue #14655).
794         """
795         from sympy import flatten
796 
797         def flat_indexes(elems):
798             n = 0
799 
800             for el in elems:
801                 if iterable(el):
802                     for ndeep in flat_indexes(el):
803                         yield (n,) + ndeep
804                 else:
805                     yield (n,)
806 
807                 n += 1
808 
809         indexed = ', '.join('{}[{}]'.format(rvalue, ']['.join(map(str, ind)))
810                                 for ind in flat_indexes(lvalues))
811 
812         return ['[{}] = [{}]'.format(', '.join(flatten(lvalues)), indexed)]

814 def _imp_namespace(expr, namespace=None):
815     """ Return namespace dict with function implementations
816 
817     We need to search for functions in anything that can be thrown at
818     us - that is - anything that could be passed as `expr`.  Examples
819     include sympy expressions, as well as tuples, lists and dicts that may
820     contain sympy expressions.
821 
822     Parameters
823     ----------
824     expr : object
825        Something passed to lambdify, that will generate valid code from
826        ``str(expr)``.
827     namespace : None or mapping
828        Namespace to fill.  None results in new empty dict
829 
830     Returns
831     -------
832     namespace : dict
833        dict with keys of implemented function names within `expr` and
834        corresponding values being the numerical implementation of
835        function
836 
837     Examples
838     ========
839 
840     >>> from sympy.abc import x
841     >>> from sympy.utilities.lambdify import implemented_function, _imp_namespace
842     >>> from sympy import Function
843     >>> f = implemented_function(Function('f'), lambda x: x+1)
844     >>> g = implemented_function(Function('g'), lambda x: x*10)
845     >>> namespace = _imp_namespace(f(g(x)))
846     >>> sorted(namespace.keys())
847     ['f', 'g']
848     """
849     # Delayed import to avoid circular imports
850     from sympy.core.function import FunctionClass
851     if namespace is None:
852         namespace = {}
853     # tuples, lists, dicts are valid expressions
854     if is_sequence(expr):
855         for arg in expr:
856             _imp_namespace(arg, namespace)
857         return namespace
858     elif isinstance(expr, dict):
859         for key, val in expr.items():
860             # functions can be in dictionary keys
861             _imp_namespace(key, namespace)
862             _imp_namespace(val, namespace)
863         return namespace
864     # sympy expressions may be Functions themselves
865     func = getattr(expr, 'func', None)
866     if isinstance(func, FunctionClass):
867         imp = getattr(func, '_imp_', None)
868         if imp is not None:
869             name = expr.func.__name__
870             if name in namespace and namespace[name] != imp:
871                 raise ValueError('We found more than one '
872                                  'implementation with name '
873                                  '"%s"' % name)
874             namespace[name] = imp
875     # and / or they may take Functions as arguments
876     if hasattr(expr, 'args'):
877         for arg in expr.args:
878             _imp_namespace(arg, namespace)
879     return namespace
880

882 def implemented_function(symfunc, implementation):
883     """ Add numerical ``implementation`` to function ``symfunc``.
884 
885     ``symfunc`` can be an ``UndefinedFunction`` instance, or a name string.
886     In the latter case we create an ``UndefinedFunction`` instance with that
887     name.
888 
889     Be aware that this is a quick workaround, not a general method to create
890     special symbolic functions. If you want to create a symbolic function to be
891     used by all the machinery of SymPy you should subclass the ``Function``
892     class.
893 
894     Parameters
895     ----------
896     symfunc : ``str`` or ``UndefinedFunction`` instance
897        If ``str``, then create new ``UndefinedFunction`` with this as
898        name.  If `symfunc` is an Undefined function, create a new function
899        with the same name and the implemented function attached.
900     implementation : callable
901        numerical implementation to be called by ``evalf()`` or ``lambdify``
902 
903     Returns
904     -------
905     afunc : sympy.FunctionClass instance
906        function with attached implementation
907 
908     Examples
909     ========
910 
911     >>> from sympy.abc import x
912     >>> from sympy.utilities.lambdify import lambdify, implemented_function
913     >>> from sympy import Function
914     >>> f = implemented_function('f', lambda x: x+1)
915     >>> lam_f = lambdify(x, f(x))
916     >>> lam_f(4)
917     5
918     """
919     # Delayed import to avoid circular imports
920     from sympy.core.function import UndefinedFunction
921     # if name, create function to hold implementation
922     _extra_kwargs = {}
923     if isinstance(symfunc, UndefinedFunction):
924         _extra_kwargs = symfunc._extra_kwargs
925         symfunc = symfunc.__name__
926     if isinstance(symfunc, string_types):
927         # Keyword arguments to UndefinedFunction are added as attributes to

problem_statement:
lambdify does not work with certain MatrixSymbol names even with dummify=True
`lambdify` is happy with curly braces in a symbol name and with `MatrixSymbol`s, but not with both at the same time, even if `dummify` is `True`.

Here is some basic code that gives the error.
```
import sympy as sy
curlyx = sy.symbols("{x}")
v = sy.MatrixSymbol("v", 2, 1)
curlyv = sy.MatrixSymbol("{v}", 2, 1)
```

The following two lines of code work:
```
curlyScalarId = sy.lambdify(curlyx, curlyx)
vectorId = sy.lambdify(v,v)
```

The following two lines of code give a `SyntaxError`:
```
curlyVectorId = sy.lambdify(curlyv, curlyv)
curlyVectorIdDummified = sy.lambdify(curlyv, curlyv, dummify=True)
```

Recipients of a timestamp value in rfc850-date format, which uses a
two-digit year, MUST interpret a timestamp that appears to be more
than 50 years in the future as representing the most recent year in

django.utils.http.parse_http_date two digit year check is incorrect
Description
	 
		(last modified by Ad Timmering)
	 
RFC 850 does not mention this, but in RFC 7231 (and there's something similar in RFC 2822), there's the following quote:
Recipients of a timestamp value in rfc850-date format, which uses a
two-digit year, MUST interpret a timestamp that appears to be more
than 50 years in the future as representing the most recent year in
the past that had the same last two digits.
Current logic is hard coded to consider 0-69 to be in 2000-2069, and 70-99 to be 1970-1999, instead of comparing versus the current year.

<issue>
RenameModel with db_table should be a noop.
Description
	
A RenameModel operation that already has db_table defined must be a noop.
In Postgres, it drops and recreates foreign key constraints. In sqlite it recreates the table (as expected for a table renaming).

<issue>
Autoreloader with StatReloader doesn't track changes in manage.py.
Description
	 
		(last modified by Mariusz Felisiak)
	 
This is a bit convoluted, but here we go.
Environment (OSX 10.11):
$ python -V
Python 3.6.2
$ pip -V
pip 19.1.1
$ pip install Django==2.2.1
Steps to reproduce:
Run a server python manage.py runserver
Edit the manage.py file, e.g. add print(): 
def main():
	print('sth')
	os.environ.setdefault('DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE', 'ticket_30479.settings')
	...
Under 2.1.8 (and prior), this will trigger the auto-reloading mechanism. Under 2.2.1, it won't. As far as I can tell from the django.utils.autoreload log lines, it never sees the manage.py itself.

430         Watch a directory with a specific glob. If the directory doesn't yet
431         exist, attempt to watch the parent directory and amend the patterns to
432         include this. It's important this method isn't called more than one per
433         directory when updating all subscriptions. Subsequent calls will
434         overwrite the named subscription, so it must include all possible glob
435         expressions.
436         """
437         prefix = 'glob'
438         if not directory.exists():
439             if not directory.parent.exists():
440                 logger.warning('Unable to watch directory %s as neither it or its parent exist.', directory)
441                 return
442             prefix = 'glob-parent-%s' % directory.name
443             patterns = ['%s/%s' % (directory.name, pattern) for pattern in patterns]
444             directory = directory.parent
445 
446         expression = ['anyof']
447         for pattern in patterns:
448             expression.append(['match', pattern, 'wholename'])
449         self._subscribe(directory, '%s:%s' % (prefix, directory), expression)
450

452         extra_directories = self.directory_globs.keys()
453         watched_file_dirs = [f.parent for f in watched_files]
454         sys_paths = list(sys_path_directories())

456 
457     def _update_watches(self):
458         watched_files = list(self.watched_files(include_globs=False))

460         logger.debug('Watching %s files', len(watched_files))
461         logger.debug('Found common roots: %s', found_roots)
462         # Setup initial roots for performance, shortest roots first.
463         for root in sorted(found_roots):
464             self._watch_root(root)
465         for directory, patterns in self.directory_globs.items():
466             self._watch_glob(directory, patterns)
467         # Group sorted watched_files by their parent directory.
468         sorted_files = sorted(watched_files, key=lambda p: p.parent)
469         for directory, group in itertools.groupby(sorted_files, key=lambda p: p.parent):
470             # These paths need to be relative to the parent directory.
471             self._subscribe_dir(directory, [str(p.relative_to(directory)) for p in group])
472

474         try:
475             self._update_watches()
476         except Exception as ex:
477             # If the service is still available, raise the original exception.
478             if self.check_server_status(ex):

480 
481     def _check_subscription(self, sub):
482         subscription = self.client.getSubscription(sub)
483         if not subscription:
484             return
485         logger.debug('Watchman subscription %s has results.', sub)
486         for result in subscription:
487             # When using watch-project, it's not simple to get the relative
488             # directory without storing some specific state. Store the full
489             # path to the directory in the subscription name, prefixed by its
490             # type (glob, files).
491             root_directory = Path(result['subscription'].split(':', 1)[1])
492             logger.debug('Found root directory %s', root_directory)
493             for file in result.get('files', []):
494                 self.notify_file_changed(root_directory / file)
495

497         logger.debug('Request processed. Setting update_watches event.')
498         self.processed_request.set()
499

501         request_finished.connect(self.request_processed)
502         self.update_watches()

problem_statement:
Autoreloader with StatReloader doesn't track changes in manage.py.
Description
	 
		(last modified by Mariusz Felisiak)
	 
This is a bit convoluted, but here we go.
Environment (OSX 10.11):
$ python -V
Python 3.6.2
$ pip -V
pip 19.1.1
$ pip install Django==2.2.1
Steps to reproduce:
Run a server python manage.py runserver
Edit the manage.py file, e.g. add print(): 
def main():
	print('sth')
	os.environ.setdefault('DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE', 'ticket_30479.settings')
	...
Under 2.1.8 (and prior), this will trigger the auto-reloading mechanism. Under 2.2.1, it won't. As far as I can tell from the django.utils.autoreload log lines, it never sees the manage.py itself.

<issue>
Product pretty print could be improved
This is what the pretty printing for `Product` looks like:

```
>>> pprint(Product(1, (n, 1, oo)))
  ∞
┬───┬
│   │ 1
│   │
n = 1
>>> pprint(Product(1/n, (n, 1, oo)))
   ∞
┬──────┬
│      │ 1
│      │ ─
│      │ n
│      │
 n = 1
>>> pprint(Product(1/n**2, (n, 1, oo)))
    ∞
┬────────┬
│        │ 1
│        │ ──
│        │  2
│        │ n
│        │
  n = 1
>>> pprint(Product(1, (n, 1, oo)), use_unicode=False)
  oo
_____
|   | 1
|   |
n = 1
>>> pprint(Product(1/n, (n, 1, oo)), use_unicode=False)
   oo
________
|      | 1
|      | -
|      | n
|      |
 n = 1
>>> pprint(Product(1/n**2, (n, 1, oo)), use_unicode=False)
    oo
__________
|        | 1
|        | --
|        |  2
|        | n
|        |
  n = 1
```

(if those don't look good in your browser copy paste them into the terminal)

This could be improved:

- Why is there always an empty line at the bottom of the ∏? Keeping everything below the horizontal line is good, but the bottom looks asymmetric, and it makes the ∏ bigger than it needs to be.

- The ∏ is too fat IMO. 

- It might look better if we extended the top bar. I'm unsure about this. 

Compare this

```
    ∞
─┬─────┬─
 │     │  1
 │     │  ──
 │     │   2
 │     │  n
  n = 1
```

That's still almost twice as wide as the equivalent Sum, but if you make it much skinnier it starts to look bad.

```
  ∞
 ____
 ╲
  ╲   1
   ╲  ──
   ╱   2
  ╱   n
 ╱
 ‾‾‾‾
n = 1
```

</issue>

325         if requires_partial(deriv) and self._use_unicode:
326             deriv_symbol = U('PARTIAL DIFFERENTIAL')

397     def _print_Integral(self, integral):
398         f = integral.function
399 
400         # Add parentheses if arg involves addition of terms and
401         # create a pretty form for the argument
402         prettyF = self._print(f)
403         # XXX generalize parens
404         if f.is_Add:
405             prettyF = prettyForm(*prettyF.parens())
406 
407         # dx dy dz ...
408         arg = prettyF
409         for x in integral.limits:
410             prettyArg = self._print(x[0])
411             # XXX qparens (parens if needs-parens)
412             if prettyArg.width() > 1:
413                 prettyArg = prettyForm(*prettyArg.parens())
414 
415             arg = prettyForm(*arg.right(' d', prettyArg))
416 
417         # \int \int \int ...
418         firstterm = True
419         s = None
420         for lim in integral.limits:
421             x = lim[0]
422             # Create bar based on the height of the argument
423             h = arg.height()
424             H = h + 2
425 
426             # XXX hack!
427             ascii_mode = not self._use_unicode
428             if ascii_mode:
429                 H += 2
430 
431             vint = vobj('int', H)
432 
433             # Construct the pretty form with the integral sign and the argument
434             pform = prettyForm(vint)
435             pform.baseline = arg.baseline + (
436                 H - h)//2    # covering the whole argument
437 
438             if len(lim) > 1:
439                 # Create pretty forms for endpoints, if definite integral.
440                 # Do not print empty endpoints.
441                 if len(lim) == 2:
442                     prettyA = prettyForm("")
443                     prettyB = self._print(lim[1])
444                 if len(lim) == 3:
445                     prettyA = self._print(lim[1])
446                     prettyB = self._print(lim[2])
447 
448                 if ascii_mode:  # XXX hack
449                     # Add spacing so that endpoint can more easily be
450                     # identified with the correct integral sign
451                     spc = max(1, 3 - prettyB.width())
452                     prettyB = prettyForm(*prettyB.left(' ' * spc))
453 
454                     spc = max(1, 4 - prettyA.width())
455                     prettyA = prettyForm(*prettyA.right(' ' * spc))
456 
457                 pform = prettyForm(*pform.above(prettyB))
458                 pform = prettyForm(*pform.below(prettyA))
459 
460             if not ascii_mode:  # XXX hack
461                 pform = prettyForm(*pform.right(' '))
462 
463             if firstterm:
464                 s = pform   # first term
465                 firstterm = False
466             else:
467                 s = prettyForm(*s.left(pform))
468 
469         pform = prettyForm(*arg.left(s))
470         pform.binding = prettyForm.MUL
471         return pform

473     def _print_Product(self, expr):

475         pretty_func = self._print(func)
476 
477         horizontal_chr = xobj('_', 1)
478         corner_chr = xobj('_', 1)
479         vertical_chr = xobj('|', 1)
480 
481         if self._use_unicode:

483             horizontal_chr = xobj('-', 1)
484             corner_chr = u'\N{BOX DRAWINGS LIGHT DOWN AND HORIZONTAL}'
485

487 
488         first = True
489         max_upper = 0
490         sign_height = 0
491 
492         for lim in expr.limits:
493             width = (func_height + 2) * 5 // 3 - 2
494             sign_lines = []
495             sign_lines.append(corner_chr + (horizontal_chr*width) + corner_chr)
496             for i in range(func_height + 1):
497                 sign_lines.append(vertical_chr + (' '*width) + vertical_chr)
498 
499             pretty_sign = stringPict('')
500             pretty_sign = prettyForm(*pretty_sign.stack(*sign_lines))
501 
502             pretty_upper = self._print(lim[2])
503             pretty_lower = self._print(Equality(lim[0], lim[1]))
504 
505             max_upper = max(max_upper, pretty_upper.height())
506 
507             if first:
508                 sign_height = pretty_sign.height()
509 
510             pretty_sign = prettyForm(*pretty_sign.above(pretty_upper))
511             pretty_sign = prettyForm(*pretty_sign.below(pretty_lower))
512 
513             if first:
514                 pretty_func.baseline = 0
515                 first = False
516 
517             height = pretty_sign.height()
518             padding = stringPict('')
519             padding = prettyForm(*padding.stack(*[' ']*(height - 1)))
520             pretty_sign = prettyForm(*pretty_sign.right(padding))
521 
522             pretty_func = prettyForm(*pretty_sign.right(pretty_func))
523

526         return pretty_func

532             def adjust(s, wid=None, how='<^>'):
533                 if not wid or len(s) > wid:
534                     return s
535                 need = wid - len(s)
536                 if how == '<^>' or how == "<" or how not in list('<^>'):

541                     return " "*need + s

543 
544             h = max(hrequired, 2)
545             d = h//2
546             w = d + 1
547             more = hrequired % 2
548 
549             lines = []
550             if use_ascii:
551                 lines.append("_"*(w) + ' ')
552                 lines.append(r"\%s`" % (' '*(w - 1)))
553                 for i in range(1, d):
554                     lines.append('%s\\%s' % (' '*i, ' '*(w - i)))
555                 if more:
556                     lines.append('%s)%s' % (' '*(d), ' '*(w - d)))
557                 for i in reversed(range(1, d)):
558                     lines.append('%s/%s' % (' '*i, ' '*(w - i)))
559                 lines.append("/" + "_"*(w - 1) + ',')
560                 return d, h + more, lines, 0
561             else:
562                 w = w + more
563                 d = d + more
564                 vsum = vobj('sum', 4)
565                 lines.append("_"*(w))
566                 for i in range(0, d):
567                     lines.append('%s%s%s' % (' '*i, vsum[2], ' '*(w - i - 1)))
568                 for i in reversed(range(0, d)):
569                     lines.append('%s%s%s' % (' '*i, vsum[4], ' '*(w - i - 1)))
570                 lines.append(vsum[8]*(w))
571                 return d, h + 2*more, lines, more
572 
573         f = expr.function
574 
575         prettyF = self._print(f)
576 
577         if f.is_Add:  # add parens
578             prettyF = prettyForm(*prettyF.parens())
579 
580         H = prettyF.height() + 2
581 
582         # \sum \sum \sum ...
583         first = True
584         max_upper = 0
585         sign_height = 0
586 
587         for lim in expr.limits:
588             if len(lim) == 3:
589                 prettyUpper = self._print(lim[2])
590                 prettyLower = self._print(Equality(lim[0], lim[1]))
591             elif len(lim) == 2:
592                 prettyUpper = self._print("")
593                 prettyLower = self._print(Equality(lim[0], lim[1]))
594             elif len(lim) == 1:
595                 prettyUpper = self._print("")
596                 prettyLower = self._print(lim[0])
597 
598             max_upper = max(max_upper, prettyUpper.height())
599 
600             # Create sum sign based on the height of the argument
601             d, h, slines, adjustment = asum(
602                 H, prettyLower.width(), prettyUpper.width(), ascii_mode)
603             prettySign = stringPict('')
604             prettySign = prettyForm(*prettySign.stack(*slines))
605 
606             if first:
607                 sign_height = prettySign.height()
608 
609             prettySign = prettyForm(*prettySign.above(prettyUpper))
610             prettySign = prettyForm(*prettySign.below(prettyLower))
611 
612             if first:
613                 # change F baseline so it centers on the sign
614                 prettyF.baseline -= d - (prettyF.height()//2 -
615                                          prettyF.baseline) - adjustment
616                 first = False
617 
618             # put padding to the right
619             pad = stringPict('')
620             pad = prettyForm(*pad.stack(*[' ']*h))
621             prettySign = prettyForm(*prettySign.right(pad))
622             # put the present prettyF to the right
623             prettyF = prettyForm(*prettySign.right(prettyF))
624 
625         prettyF.baseline = max_upper + sign_height//2
626         prettyF.binding = prettyForm.MUL
627         return prettyF

657     def _print_matrix_contents(self, e):
658         """
659         This method factors out what is essentially grid printing.
660         """
661         M = e   # matrix
662         Ms = {}  # i,j -> pretty(M[i,j])
663         for i in range(M.rows):
664             for j in range(M.cols):
665                 Ms[i, j] = self._print(M[i, j])
666 
667         # h- and v- spacers
668         hsep = 2
669         vsep = 1
670 
671         # max width for columns
672         maxw = [-1] * M.cols
673 
674         for j in range(M.cols):
675             maxw[j] = max([Ms[i, j].width() for i in range(M.rows)] or [0])
676 
677         # drawing result
678         D = None
679 
680         for i in range(M.rows):
681 
682             D_row = None
683             for j in range(M.cols):
684                 s = Ms[i, j]
685 
686                 # reshape s to maxw
687                 # XXX this should be generalized, and go to stringPict.reshape ?
688                 assert s.width() <= maxw[j]
689 
690                 # hcenter it, +0.5 to the right                        2
691                 # ( it's better to align formula starts for say 0 and r )
692                 # XXX this is not good in all cases -- maybe introduce vbaseline?
693                 wdelta = maxw[j] - s.width()
694                 wleft = wdelta // 2
695                 wright = wdelta - wleft
696 
697                 s = prettyForm(*s.right(' '*wright))
698                 s = prettyForm(*s.left(' '*wleft))
699 
700                 # we don't need vcenter cells -- this is automatically done in
701                 # a pretty way because when their baselines are taking into
702                 # account in .right()
703 
704                 if D_row is None:
705                     D_row = s   # first box in a row
706                     continue
707 
708                 D_row = prettyForm(*D_row.right(' '*hsep))  # h-spacer
709                 D_row = prettyForm(*D_row.right(s))
710 
711             if D is None:
712                 D = D_row       # first row in a picture
713                 continue
714 
715             # v-spacer
716             for _ in range(vsep):
717                 D = prettyForm(*D.below(' '))
718 
719             D = prettyForm(*D.below(D_row))

721         if D is None:

992     def _print_NDimArray(self, expr):
993         from sympy import ImmutableMatrix
994 
995         if expr.rank() == 0:
996             return self._print(expr[()])
997 
998         level_str = [[]] + [[] for i in range(expr.rank())]
999         shape_ranges = [list(range(i)) for i in expr.shape]
1000         for outer_i in itertools.product(*shape_ranges):
1001             level_str[-1].append(expr[outer_i])
1002             even = True
1003             for back_outer_i in range(expr.rank()-1, -1, -1):
1004                 if len(level_str[back_outer_i+1]) < expr.shape[back_outer_i]:
1005                     break
1006                 if even:
1007                     level_str[back_outer_i].append(level_str[back_outer_i+1])
1008                 else:
1009                     level_str[back_outer_i].append(ImmutableMatrix(level_str[back_outer_i+1]))
1010                     if len(level_str[back_outer_i + 1]) == 1:
1011                         level_str[back_outer_i][-1] = ImmutableMatrix([[level_str[back_outer_i][-1]]])
1012                 even = not even
1013                 level_str[back_outer_i+1] = []
1014 
1015         out_expr = level_str[0][0]
1016         if expr.rank() % 2 == 1:
1017             out_expr = ImmutableMatrix([out_expr])
1018 
1019         return self._print(out_expr)

1567     def _print_Add(self, expr, order=None):
1568         if self.order == 'none':
1569             terms = list(expr.args)
1570         else:
1571             terms = self._as_ordered_terms(expr, order=order)
1572         pforms, indices = [], []
1573 
1574         def pretty_negative(pform, index):
1575             """Prepend a minus sign to a pretty form. """
1576             #TODO: Move this code to prettyForm
1577             if index == 0:
1578                 if pform.height() > 1:
1579                     pform_neg = '- '
1580                 else:
1581                     pform_neg = '-'
1582             else:
1583                 pform_neg = ' - '
1584 
1585             if (pform.binding > prettyForm.NEG
1586                 or pform.binding == prettyForm.ADD):
1587                 p = stringPict(*pform.parens())
1588             else:
1589                 p = pform
1590             p = stringPict.next(pform_neg, p)
1591             # Lower the binding to NEG, even if it was higher. Otherwise, it
1592             # will print as a + ( - (b)), instead of a - (b).
1593             return prettyForm(binding=prettyForm.NEG, *p)
1594 
1595         for i, term in enumerate(terms):
1596             if term.is_Mul and _coeff_isneg(term):
1597                 coeff, other = term.as_coeff_mul(rational=False)
1598                 pform = self._print(Mul(-coeff, *other, evaluate=False))
1599                 pforms.append(pretty_negative(pform, i))
1600             elif term.is_Rational and term.q > 1:
1601                 pforms.append(None)
1602                 indices.append(i)
1603             elif term.is_Number and term < 0:
1604                 pform = self._print(-term)
1605                 pforms.append(pretty_negative(pform, i))
1606             elif term.is_Relational:
1607                 pforms.append(prettyForm(*self._print(term).parens()))
1608             else:
1609                 pforms.append(self._print(term))
1610 
1611         if indices:
1612             large = True
1613 
1614             for pform in pforms:
1615                 if pform is not None and pform.height() > 1:
1616                     break
1617             else:
1618                 large = False
1619 
1620             for i in indices:
1621                 term, negative = terms[i], False
1622 
1623                 if term < 0:
1624                     term, negative = -term, True
1625 
1626                 if large:
1627                     pform = prettyForm(str(term.p))/prettyForm(str(term.q))
1628                 else:
1629                     pform = self._print(term)
1630 
1631                 if negative:

1638     def _print_Mul(self, product):
1639         from sympy.physics.units import Quantity
1640         a = []  # items in the numerator
1641         b = []  # items that are in the denominator (if any)
1642 
1643         if self.order not in ('old', 'none'):
1644             args = product.as_ordered_factors()
1645         else:
1646             args = list(product.args)
1647 
1648         # If quantities are present append them at the back
1649         args = sorted(args, key=lambda x: isinstance(x, Quantity) or
1650                      (isinstance(x, Pow) and isinstance(x.base, Quantity)))
1651 
1652         # Gather terms for numerator/denominator
1653         for item in args:
1654             if item.is_commutative and item.is_Pow and item.exp.is_Rational and item.exp.is_negative:
1655                 if item.exp != -1:
1656                     b.append(Pow(item.base, -item.exp, evaluate=False))
1657                 else:
1658                     b.append(Pow(item.base, -item.exp))
1659             elif item.is_Rational and item is not S.Infinity:
1660                 if item.p != 1:
1661                     a.append( Rational(item.p) )
1662                 if item.q != 1:
1663                     b.append( Rational(item.q) )
1664             else:
1665                 a.append(item)
1666 
1667         from sympy import Integral, Piecewise, Product, Sum
1668 
1669         # Convert to pretty forms. Add parens to Add instances if there
1670         # is more than one term in the numer/denom
1671         for i in range(0, len(a)):
1672             if (a[i].is_Add and len(a) > 1) or (i != len(a) - 1 and
1673                     isinstance(a[i], (Integral, Piecewise, Product, Sum))):
1674                 a[i] = prettyForm(*self._print(a[i]).parens())
1675             elif a[i].is_Relational:
1676                 a[i] = prettyForm(*self._print(a[i]).parens())
1677             else:
1678                 a[i] = self._print(a[i])
1679 
1680         for i in range(0, len(b)):
1681             if (b[i].is_Add and len(b) > 1) or (i != len(b) - 1 and
1682                     isinstance(b[i], (Integral, Piecewise, Product, Sum))):
1683                 b[i] = prettyForm(*self._print(b[i]).parens())
1684             else:
1685                 b[i] = self._print(b[i])
1686 
1687         # Construct a pretty form
1688         if len(b) == 0:
1689             return prettyForm.__mul__(*a)
1690         else:
1691             if len(a) == 0:
1692                 a.append( self._print(S.One) )
1693             return prettyForm.__mul__(*a)/prettyForm.__mul__(*b)

1695     # A helper function for _print_Pow to print x**(1/n)
1696     def _print_nth_root(self, base, expt):
1697         bpretty = self._print(base)
1698 
1699         # In very simple cases, use a single-char root sign
1700         if (self._settings['use_unicode_sqrt_char'] and self._use_unicode
1701             and expt is S.Half and bpretty.height() == 1
1702             and (bpretty.width() == 1
1703                  or (base.is_Integer and base.is_nonnegative))):
1704             return prettyForm(*bpretty.left(u'\N{SQUARE ROOT}'))
1705 
1706         # Construct root sign, start with the \/ shape
1707         _zZ = xobj('/', 1)
1708         rootsign = xobj('\\', 1) + _zZ
1709         # Make exponent number to put above it
1710         if isinstance(expt, Rational):
1711             exp = str(expt.q)
1712             if exp == '2':
1713                 exp = ''
1714         else:
1715             exp = str(expt.args[0])
1716         exp = exp.ljust(2)
1717         if len(exp) > 2:
1718             rootsign = ' '*(len(exp) - 2) + rootsign
1719         # Stack the exponent
1720         rootsign = stringPict(exp + '\n' + rootsign)
1721         rootsign.baseline = 0
1722         # Diagonal: length is one less than height of base
1723         linelength = bpretty.height() - 1
1724         diagonal = stringPict('\n'.join(
1725             ' '*(linelength - i - 1) + _zZ + ' '*i
1726             for i in range(linelength)
1727         ))
1728         # Put baseline just below lowest line: next to exp
1729         diagonal.baseline = linelength - 1
1730         # Make the root symbol
1731         rootsign = prettyForm(*rootsign.right(diagonal))
1732         # Det the baseline to match contents to fix the height
1733         # but if the height of bpretty is one, the rootsign must be one higher
1734         rootsign.baseline = max(1, bpretty.baseline)
1735         #build result
1736         s = prettyForm(hobj('_', 2 + bpretty.width()))
1737         s = prettyForm(*bpretty.above(s))
1738         s = prettyForm(*s.left(rootsign))
1739         return s

1741     def _print_Pow(self, power):

Product pretty print could be improved
This is what the pretty printing for `Product` looks like:

```
>>> pprint(Product(1, (n, 1, oo)))
  ∞
┬───┬
│   │ 1
│   │
n = 1
>>> pprint(Product(1/n, (n, 1, oo)))
   ∞
┬──────┬
│      │ 1
│      │ ─
│      │ n
│      │
 n = 1
>>> pprint(Product(1/n**2, (n, 1, oo)))
    ∞
┬────────┬
│        │ 1
│        │ ──
│        │  2
│        │ n
│        │
  n = 1
>>> pprint(Product(1, (n, 1, oo)), use_unicode=False)
  oo
_____
|   | 1
|   |
n = 1
>>> pprint(Product(1/n, (n, 1, oo)), use_unicode=False)
   oo
________
|      | 1
|      | -
|      | n
|      |
 n = 1
>>> pprint(Product(1/n**2, (n, 1, oo)), use_unicode=False)
    oo
__________
|        | 1
|        | --
|        |  2
|        | n
|        |
  n = 1
```

(if those don't look good in your browser copy paste them into the terminal)

This could be improved:

- Why is there always an empty line at the bottom of the ∏? Keeping everything below the horizontal line is good, but the bottom looks asymmetric, and it makes the ∏ bigger than it needs to be.

- The ∏ is too fat IMO. 

- It might look better if we extended the top bar. I'm unsure about this. 

Compare this

```
    ∞
─┬─────┬─
 │     │  1
 │     │  ──
 │     │   2
 │     │  n
  n = 1
```

That's still almost twice as wide as the equivalent Sum, but if you make it much skinnier it starts to look bad.

```
  ∞
 ____
 ╲
  ╲   1
   ╲  ──
   ╱   2
  ╱   n
 ╱
 ‾‾‾‾
n = 1
```

The `mathematica.py` file goes thru a table of known functions (of which neither Mathematica `Max` or `Min` functions are in) that are specified with lowercase capitalization, so it might be that doing `mathematica_code(Max(x,2))` is just yielding the unevaluated expression of `mathematica_code`. 382             for message in messages:
383                 if (isinstance(message, ValidationError) and
384                         message.code in error_messages):
385                     message.message = error_messages[message.code]
386 
387         self.add_error(None, errors)
388 
389     def _post_clean(self):
390         opts = self._meta
391 
392         exclude = self._get_validation_exclusions()
393 
394         # Foreign Keys being used to represent inline relationships
395         # are excluded from basic field value validation. This is for two
396         # reasons: firstly, the value may not be supplied (#12507; the
397         # case of providing new values to the admin); secondly the
398         # object being referred to may not yet fully exist (#12749).
399         # However, these fields *must* be included in uniqueness checks,
400         # so this can't be part of _get_validation_exclusions().
401         for name, field in self.fields.items():
402             if isinstance(field, InlineForeignKeyField):
403                 exclude.append(name)
404 
405         try:
406             self.instance = construct_instance(self, self.instance, opts.fields, opts.exclude)
407         except ValidationError as e:
408             self._update_errors(e)
409 
410         try:
411             self.instance.full_clean(exclude=exclude, validate_unique=False)
412         except ValidationError as e:
413             self._update_errors(e)
414 
415         # Validate uniqueness if needed.
416         if self._validate_unique:
417             self.validate_unique()
418 
419     def validate_unique(self):
420         """
421         Call the instance's validate_unique() method and update the form's
422         validation errors if any were raised.
423         """
424         exclude = self._get_validation_exclusions()
425         try:
426             self.instance.validate_unique(exclude=exclude)
427         except ValidationError as e:
428             self._update_errors(e)
429 
430     def _save_m2m(self):
431         """
432         Save the many-to-many fields and generic relations for this form.
433         """
434         cleaned_data = self.cleaned_data
435         exclude = self._meta.exclude
436         fields = self._meta.fields
437         opts = self.instance._meta
438         # Note that for historical reasons we want to include also
439         # private_fields here. (GenericRelation was previously a fake
440         # m2m field).
441         for f in chain(opts.many_to_many, opts.private_fields):
442             if not hasattr(f, 'save_form_data'):
443                 continue
444             if fields and f.name not in fields:
445                 continue
446             if exclude and f.name in exclude:
447                 continue
448             if f.name in cleaned_data:
449                 f.save_form_data(self.instance, cleaned_data[f.name])
450 
451     def save(self, commit=True):
452         """
453         Save this form's self.instance object if commit=True. Otherwise, add
454         a save_m2m() method to the form which can be called after the instance
455         is saved manually at a later time. Return the model instance.
456         """
457         if self.errors:
458             raise ValueError(
459                 "The %s could not be %s because the data didn't validate." % (
460                     self.instance._meta.object_name,
461                     'created' if self.instance._state.adding else 'changed',
462                 )
463             )
464         if commit:
465             # If committing, save the instance and the m2m data immediately.
466             self.instance.save()
467             self._save_m2m()
468         else:
469             # If not committing, add a method to the form to allow deferred
470             # saving of m2m data.
471             self.save_m2m = self._save_m2m
472         return self.instance
473 
474     save.alters_data = True

481 def modelform_factory(model, form=ModelForm, fields=None, exclude=None,
482                       formfield_callback=None, widgets=None, localized_fields=None,
483                       labels=None, help_texts=None, error_messages=None,
484                       field_classes=None):
485     """
486     Return a ModelForm containing form fields for the given model. You can
487     optionally pass a `form` argument to use as a starting point for
488     constructing the ModelForm.
489 
490     ``fields`` is an optional list of field names. If provided, include only
491     the named fields in the returned fields. If omitted or '__all__', use all
492     fields.
493 
494     ``exclude`` is an optional list of field names. If provided, exclude the
495     named fields from the returned fields, even if they are listed in the
496     ``fields`` argument.
497 
498     ``widgets`` is a dictionary of model field names mapped to a widget.
499 
500     ``localized_fields`` is a list of names of fields which should be localized.
501 
502     ``formfield_callback`` is a callable that takes a model field and returns
503     a form field.
504 
505     ``labels`` is a dictionary of model field names mapped to a label.
506 
507     ``help_texts`` is a dictionary of model field names mapped to a help text.
508 
509     ``error_messages`` is a dictionary of model field names mapped to a
510     dictionary of error messages.
511 
512     ``field_classes`` is a dictionary of model field names mapped to a form
513     field class.
514     """
515     # Create the inner Meta class. FIXME: ideally, we should be able to
516     # construct a ModelForm without creating and passing in a temporary
517     # inner class.
518 
519     # Build up a list of attributes that the Meta object will have.
520     attrs = {'model': model}
521     if fields is not None:
522         attrs['fields'] = fields
523     if exclude is not None:
524         attrs['exclude'] = exclude
525     if widgets is not None:
526         attrs['widgets'] = widgets
527     if localized_fields is not None:
528         attrs['localized_fields'] = localized_fields
529     if labels is not None:
530         attrs['labels'] = labels
531     if help_texts is not None:
532         attrs['help_texts'] = help_texts
533     if error_messages is not None:
534         attrs['error_messages'] = error_messages
535     if field_classes is not None:
536         attrs['field_classes'] = field_classes
537 
538     # If parent form class already has an inner Meta, the Meta we're
539     # creating needs to inherit from the parent's inner meta.
540     bases = (form.Meta,) if hasattr(form, 'Meta') else ()
541     Meta = type('Meta', bases, attrs)
542     if formfield_callback:
543         Meta.formfield_callback = staticmethod(formfield_callback)
544     # Give this new form class a reasonable name.
545     class_name = model.__name__ + 'Form'
546 
547     # Class attributes for the new form class.
548     form_class_attrs = {
549         'Meta': Meta,
550         'formfield_callback': formfield_callback
551     }
552 
553     if (getattr(Meta, 'fields', None) is None and
554             getattr(Meta, 'exclude', None) is None):
555         raise ImproperlyConfigured(
556             "Calling modelform_factory without defining 'fields' or "
557             "'exclude' explicitly is prohibited."
558         )
559 
560     # Instantiate type(form) in order to use the same metaclass as form.
561     return type(form)(class_name, (form,), form_class_attrs)
