464 class Permutation(Basic):
465     """
466     A permutation, alternatively known as an 'arrangement number' or 'ordering'
467     is an arrangement of the elements of an ordered list into a one-to-one
468     mapping with itself. The permutation of a given arrangement is given by
469     indicating the positions of the elements after re-arrangement [2]_. For
470     example, if one started with elements [x, y, a, b] (in that order) and
471     they were reordered as [x, y, b, a] then the permutation would be
472     [0, 1, 3, 2]. Notice that (in SymPy) the first element is always referred
473     to as 0 and the permutation uses the indices of the elements in the
474     original ordering, not the elements (a, b, etc...) themselves.
475 
476     >>> from sympy.combinatorics import Permutation
477     >>> Permutation.print_cyclic = False
478 
479     Permutations Notation
480     =====================
481 
482     Permutations are commonly represented in disjoint cycle or array forms.
483 
484     Array Notation and 2-line Form
485     ------------------------------------
486 
487     In the 2-line form, the elements and their final positions are shown
488     as a matrix with 2 rows:
489 
490     [0    1    2     ... n-1]
491     [p(0) p(1) p(2)  ... p(n-1)]
492 
493     Since the first line is always range(n), where n is the size of p,
494     it is sufficient to represent the permutation by the second line,
495     referred to as the "array form" of the permutation. This is entered
496     in brackets as the argument to the Permutation class:
497 
498     >>> p = Permutation([0, 2, 1]); p
499     Permutation([0, 2, 1])
500 
501     Given i in range(p.size), the permutation maps i to i^p
502 
503     >>> [i^p for i in range(p.size)]
504     [0, 2, 1]
505 
506     The composite of two permutations p*q means first apply p, then q, so
507     i^(p*q) = (i^p)^q which is i^p^q according to Python precedence rules:
508 
509     >>> q = Permutation([2, 1, 0])
510     >>> [i^p^q for i in range(3)]
511     [2, 0, 1]
512     >>> [i^(p*q) for i in range(3)]
513     [2, 0, 1]
514 
515     One can use also the notation p(i) = i^p, but then the composition
516     rule is (p*q)(i) = q(p(i)), not p(q(i)):
517 
518     >>> [(p*q)(i) for i in range(p.size)]
519     [2, 0, 1]
520     >>> [q(p(i)) for i in range(p.size)]
521     [2, 0, 1]
522     >>> [p(q(i)) for i in range(p.size)]
523     [1, 2, 0]
524 
525     Disjoint Cycle Notation
526     -----------------------
527 
528     In disjoint cycle notation, only the elements that have shifted are
529     indicated. In the above case, the 2 and 1 switched places. This can
530     be entered in two ways:
531 
532     >>> Permutation(1, 2) == Permutation([[1, 2]]) == p
533     True
534 
535     Only the relative ordering of elements in a cycle matter:
536 
537     >>> Permutation(1,2,3) == Permutation(2,3,1) == Permutation(3,1,2)
538     True
539 
540     The disjoint cycle notation is convenient when representing permutations
541     that have several cycles in them:
542 
543     >>> Permutation(1, 2)(3, 5) == Permutation([[1, 2], [3, 5]])
544     True
545 
546     It also provides some economy in entry when computing products of
547     permutations that are written in disjoint cycle notation:
548 
549     >>> Permutation(1, 2)(1, 3)(2, 3)
550     Permutation([0, 3, 2, 1])
551     >>> _ == Permutation([[1, 2]])*Permutation([[1, 3]])*Permutation([[2, 3]])
552     True
553 
554     Entering a singleton in a permutation is a way to indicate the size of the
555     permutation. The ``size`` keyword can also be used.
556 
557     Array-form entry:
558 
559     >>> Permutation([[1, 2], [9]])
560     Permutation([0, 2, 1], size=10)
561     >>> Permutation([[1, 2]], size=10)
562     Permutation([0, 2, 1], size=10)
563 
564     Cyclic-form entry:
565 
566     >>> Permutation(1, 2, size=10)
567     Permutation([0, 2, 1], size=10)
568     >>> Permutation(9)(1, 2)
569     Permutation([0, 2, 1], size=10)
570 
571     Caution: no singleton containing an element larger than the largest
572     in any previous cycle can be entered. This is an important difference
573     in how Permutation and Cycle handle the __call__ syntax. A singleton
574     argument at the start of a Permutation performs instantiation of the
575     Permutation and is permitted:
576 
577     >>> Permutation(5)
578     Permutation([], size=6)
579 
580     A singleton entered after instantiation is a call to the permutation
581     -- a function call -- and if the argument is out of range it will
582     trigger an error. For this reason, it is better to start the cycle
583     with the singleton:
584 
585     The following fails because there is is no element 3:
586 
587     >>> Permutation(1, 2)(3)
588     Traceback (most recent call last):
589     ...
590     IndexError: list index out of range
591 
592     This is ok: only the call to an out of range singleton is prohibited;
593     otherwise the permutation autosizes:
594 
595     >>> Permutation(3)(1, 2)
596     Permutation([0, 2, 1, 3])
597     >>> Permutation(1, 2)(3, 4) == Permutation(3, 4)(1, 2)
598     True
599 
600 
601     Equality testing
602     ----------------
603 
604     The array forms must be the same in order for permutations to be equal:
605 
606     >>> Permutation([1, 0, 2, 3]) == Permutation([1, 0])
607     False
608 
609 
610     Identity Permutation
611     --------------------
612 
613     The identity permutation is a permutation in which no element is out of
614     place. It can be entered in a variety of ways. All the following create
615     an identity permutation of size 4:
616 
617     >>> I = Permutation([0, 1, 2, 3])
618     >>> all(p == I for p in [
619     ... Permutation(3),
620     ... Permutation(range(4)),
621     ... Permutation([], size=4),
622     ... Permutation(size=4)])
623     True
624 
625     Watch out for entering the range *inside* a set of brackets (which is
626     cycle notation):
627 
628     >>> I == Permutation([range(4)])
629     False
630 
631 
632     Permutation Printing
633     ====================
634 
635     There are a few things to note about how Permutations are printed.
636 
637     1) If you prefer one form (array or cycle) over another, you can set that
638     with the print_cyclic flag.
639 
640     >>> Permutation(1, 2)(4, 5)(3, 4)
641     Permutation([0, 2, 1, 4, 5, 3])
642     >>> p = _
643 
644     >>> Permutation.print_cyclic = True
645     >>> p
646     (1 2)(3 4 5)
647     >>> Permutation.print_cyclic = False
648 
649     2) Regardless of the setting, a list of elements in the array for cyclic
650     form can be obtained and either of those can be copied and supplied as
651     the argument to Permutation:
652 
653     >>> p.array_form
654     [0, 2, 1, 4, 5, 3]
655     >>> p.cyclic_form
656     [[1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]
657     >>> Permutation(_) == p
658     True
659 
660     3) Printing is economical in that as little as possible is printed while
661     retaining all information about the size of the permutation:
662 
663     >>> Permutation([1, 0, 2, 3])
664     Permutation([1, 0, 2, 3])
665     >>> Permutation([1, 0, 2, 3], size=20)
666     Permutation([1, 0], size=20)
667     >>> Permutation([1, 0, 2, 4, 3, 5, 6], size=20)
668     Permutation([1, 0, 2, 4, 3], size=20)
669 
670     >>> p = Permutation([1, 0, 2, 3])
671     >>> Permutation.print_cyclic = True
672     >>> p
673     (3)(0 1)
674     >>> Permutation.print_cyclic = False
675 
676     The 2 was not printed but it is still there as can be seen with the
677     array_form and size methods:
678 
679     >>> p.array_form
680     [1, 0, 2, 3]
681     >>> p.size
682     4
683 
684     Short introduction to other methods
685     ===================================
686 
687     The permutation can act as a bijective function, telling what element is
688     located at a given position
689 
690     >>> q = Permutation([5, 2, 3, 4, 1, 0])
691     >>> q.array_form[1] # the hard way
692     2
693     >>> q(1) # the easy way
694     2
695     >>> {i: q(i) for i in range(q.size)} # showing the bijection
696     {0: 5, 1: 2, 2: 3, 3: 4, 4: 1, 5: 0}
697 
698     The full cyclic form (including singletons) can be obtained:
699 
700     >>> p.full_cyclic_form
701     [[0, 1], [2], [3]]
702 
703     Any permutation can be factored into transpositions of pairs of elements:
704 
705     >>> Permutation([[1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]).transpositions()
706     [(1, 2), (3, 5), (3, 4)]
707     >>> Permutation.rmul(*[Permutation([ti], size=6) for ti in _]).cyclic_form
708     [[1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]
709 
710     The number of permutations on a set of n elements is given by n! and is
711     called the cardinality.
712 
713     >>> p.size
714     4
715     >>> p.cardinality
716     24
717 
718     A given permutation has a rank among all the possible permutations of the
719     same elements, but what that rank is depends on how the permutations are
720     enumerated. (There are a number of different methods of doing so.) The
721     lexicographic rank is given by the rank method and this rank is used to
722     increment a permutation with addition/subtraction:
723 
724     >>> p.rank()
725     6
726     >>> p + 1
727     Permutation([1, 0, 3, 2])
728     >>> p.next_lex()
729     Permutation([1, 0, 3, 2])
730     >>> _.rank()
731     7
732     >>> p.unrank_lex(p.size, rank=7)
733     Permutation([1, 0, 3, 2])
734 
735     The product of two permutations p and q is defined as their composition as
736     functions, (p*q)(i) = q(p(i)) [6]_.
737 
738     >>> p = Permutation([1, 0, 2, 3])
739     >>> q = Permutation([2, 3, 1, 0])
740     >>> list(q*p)
741     [2, 3, 0, 1]
742     >>> list(p*q)
743     [3, 2, 1, 0]
744     >>> [q(p(i)) for i in range(p.size)]
745     [3, 2, 1, 0]
746 
747     The permutation can be 'applied' to any list-like object, not only
748     Permutations:
749 
750     >>> p(['zero', 'one', 'four', 'two'])
751      ['one', 'zero', 'four', 'two']
752     >>> p('zo42')
753     ['o', 'z', '4', '2']
754 
755     If you have a list of arbitrary elements, the corresponding permutation
756     can be found with the from_sequence method:
757 
758     >>> Permutation.from_sequence('SymPy')
759     Permutation([1, 3, 2, 0, 4])
760

801     def __new__(cls, *args, **kwargs):
802         """
803         Constructor for the Permutation object from a list or a
804         list of lists in which all elements of the permutation may
805         appear only once.
806 
807         Examples
808         ========
809 
810         >>> from sympy.combinatorics.permutations import Permutation
811         >>> Permutation.print_cyclic = False
812 
813         Permutations entered in array-form are left unaltered:
814 
815         >>> Permutation([0, 2, 1])
816         Permutation([0, 2, 1])
817 
818         Permutations entered in cyclic form are converted to array form;
819         singletons need not be entered, but can be entered to indicate the
820         largest element:
821 
822         >>> Permutation([[4, 5, 6], [0, 1]])
823         Permutation([1, 0, 2, 3, 5, 6, 4])
824         >>> Permutation([[4, 5, 6], [0, 1], [19]])
825         Permutation([1, 0, 2, 3, 5, 6, 4], size=20)
826 
827         All manipulation of permutations assumes that the smallest element
828         is 0 (in keeping with 0-based indexing in Python) so if the 0 is
829         missing when entering a permutation in array form, an error will be
830         raised:
831 
832         >>> Permutation([2, 1])
833         Traceback (most recent call last):
834         ...
835         ValueError: Integers 0 through 2 must be present.
836 
837         If a permutation is entered in cyclic form, it can be entered without
838         singletons and the ``size`` specified so those values can be filled
839         in, otherwise the array form will only extend to the maximum value
840         in the cycles:
841 
842         >>> Permutation([[1, 4], [3, 5, 2]], size=10)
843         Permutation([0, 4, 3, 5, 1, 2], size=10)
844         >>> _.array_form
845         [0, 4, 3, 5, 1, 2, 6, 7, 8, 9]
846         """
847         size = kwargs.pop('size', None)
848         if size is not None:
849             size = int(size)
850 
851         #a) ()
852         #b) (1) = identity
853         #c) (1, 2) = cycle
854         #d) ([1, 2, 3]) = array form
855         #e) ([[1, 2]]) = cyclic form
856         #f) (Cycle) = conversion to permutation
857         #g) (Permutation) = adjust size or return copy
858         ok = True
859         if not args:  # a
860             return _af_new(list(range(size or 0)))
861         elif len(args) > 1:  # c
862             return _af_new(Cycle(*args).list(size))
863         if len(args) == 1:
864             a = args[0]
865             if isinstance(a, Perm):  # g
866                 if size is None or size == a.size:
867                     return a
868                 return Perm(a.array_form, size=size)
869             if isinstance(a, Cycle):  # f
870                 return _af_new(a.list(size))
871             if not is_sequence(a):  # b
872                 return _af_new(list(range(a + 1)))
873             if has_variety(is_sequence(ai) for ai in a):
874                 ok = False
875         else:
876             ok = False
877         if not ok:
878             raise ValueError("Permutation argument must be a list of ints, "
879                              "a list of lists, Permutation or Cycle.")
880 
881 
882         # safe to assume args are valid; this also makes a copy
883         # of the args
884         args = list(args[0])
885 
886         is_cycle = args and is_sequence(args[0])
887         if is_cycle:  # e
888             args = [[int(i) for i in c] for c in args]
889         else:  # d
890             args = [int(i) for i in args]
891 
892         # if there are n elements present, 0, 1, ..., n-1 should be present
893         # unless a cycle notation has been provided. A 0 will be added
894         # for convenience in case one wants to enter permutations where
895         # counting starts from 1.
896 
897         temp = flatten(args)
898         if has_dups(temp):
899             if is_cycle:
900                 raise ValueError('there were repeated elements; to resolve '
901                 'cycles use Cycle%s.' % ''.join([str(tuple(c)) for c in args]))
902             else:
903                 raise ValueError('there were repeated elements.')
904         temp = set(temp)
905 
906         if not is_cycle and \
907                 any(i not in temp for i in range(len(temp))):
908             raise ValueError("Integers 0 through %s must be present." %
909                              max(temp))
910 
911         if is_cycle:
912             # it's not necessarily canonical so we won't store
913             # it -- use the array form instead
914             c = Cycle()
915             for ci in args:
916                 c = c(*ci)
917             aform = c.list()
918         else:
919             aform = list(args)
920         if size and size > len(aform):
921             # don't allow for truncation of permutation which
922             # might split a cycle and lead to an invalid aform
923             # but do allow the permutation size to be increased
924             aform.extend(list(range(len(aform), size)))
925         size = len(aform)
926         obj = Basic.__new__(cls, aform)
927         obj._array_form = aform
928         obj._size = size
929         return obj
930

932     def _af_new(perm):
933         """A method to produce a Permutation object from a list;
934         the list is bound to the _array_form attribute, so it must
935         not be modified; this method is meant for internal use only;
936         the list ``a`` is supposed to be generated as a temporary value
937         in a method, so p = Perm._af_new(a) is the only object
938         to hold a reference to ``a``::
939 
940         Examples
941         ========
942 
943         >>> from sympy.combinatorics.permutations import Perm
944         >>> Perm.print_cyclic = False
945         >>> a = [2,1,3,0]
946         >>> p = Perm._af_new(a)
947         >>> p
948         Permutation([2, 1, 3, 0])
949 
950         """
951         p = Basic.__new__(Perm, perm)
952         p._array_form = perm
953         p._size = len(perm)
954         return p

961     @property
962     def array_form(self):

964         Return a copy of the attribute _array_form
965         Examples
966         ========
967 
968         >>> from sympy.combinatorics.permutations import Permutation
969         >>> Permutation.print_cyclic = False
970         >>> p = Permutation([[2, 0], [3, 1]])
971         >>> p.array_form
972         [2, 3, 0, 1]
973         >>> Permutation([[2, 0, 3, 1]]).array_form

976         [2, 0, 3, 1]

978         [0, 2, 1, 3, 5, 4]

982     def __repr__(self):
983         from sympy.combinatorics.permutations import Permutation, Cycle
984         if Permutation.print_cyclic:
985             if not self.size:
986                 return 'Permutation()'
987             # before taking Cycle notation, see if the last element is
988             # a singleton and move it to the head of the string
989             s = Cycle(self)(self.size - 1).__repr__()[len('Cycle'):]
990             last = s.rfind('(')
991             if not last == 0 and ',' not in s[last:]:
992                 s = s[last:] + s[:last]
993             return 'Permutation%s' %s
994         else:
995             s = self.support()
996             if not s:
997                 if self.size < 5:
998                     return 'Permutation(%s)' % str(self.array_form)
999                 return 'Permutation([], size=%s)' % self.size
1000             trim = str(self.array_form[:s[-1] + 1]) + ', size=%s' % self.size
1001             use = full = str(self.array_form)
1002             if len(trim) < len(full):
1003                 use = trim
1004             return 'Permutation(%s)' % use

1006     def list(self, size=None):
1007         """Return the permutation as an explicit list, possibly
1008         trimming unmoved elements if size is less than the maximum
1009         element in the permutation; if this is desired, setting
1010         ``size=-1`` will guarantee such trimming.
1011 
1012         Examples
1013         ========
1014 
1015         >>> from sympy.combinatorics.permutations import Permutation
1016         >>> Permutation.print_cyclic = False
1017         >>> p = Permutation(2, 3)(4, 5)
1018         >>> p.list()
1019         [0, 1, 3, 2, 5, 4]
1020         >>> p.list(10)
1021         [0, 1, 3, 2, 5, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9]
1022 
1023         Passing a length too small will trim trailing, unchanged elements
1024         in the permutation:
1025 
1026         >>> Permutation(2, 4)(1, 2, 4).list(-1)
1027         [0, 2, 1]
1028         >>> Permutation(3).list(-1)
1029         []
1030         """
1031         if not self and size is None:
1032             raise ValueError('must give size for empty Cycle')
1033         rv = self.array_form
1034         if size is not None:
1035             if size > self.size:
1036                 rv.extend(list(range(self.size, size)))
1037             else:
1038                 # find first value from rhs where rv[i] != i
1039                 i = self.size - 1
1040                 while rv:
1041                     if rv[-1] != i:
1042                         break
1043                     rv.pop()
1044                     i -= 1
1045         return rv

1047     @property
1048     def cyclic_form(self):
1049         """
1050         This is used to convert to the cyclic notation
1051         from the canonical notation. Singletons are omitted.
1052 
1053         Examples
1054         ========
1055 
1056         >>> from sympy.combinatorics.permutations import Permutation
1057         >>> Permutation.print_cyclic = False
1058         >>> p = Permutation([0, 3, 1, 2])
1059         >>> p.cyclic_form
1060         [[1, 3, 2]]
1061         >>> Permutation([1, 0, 2, 4, 3, 5]).cyclic_form
1062         [[0, 1], [3, 4]]
1063 
1064         See Also
1065         ========
1066 
1067         array_form, full_cyclic_form
1068         """
1069         if self._cyclic_form is not None:
1070             return list(self._cyclic_form)
1071         array_form = self.array_form
1072         unchecked = [True] * len(array_form)
1073         cyclic_form = []
1074         for i in range(len(array_form)):
1075             if unchecked[i]:
1076                 cycle = []
1077                 cycle.append(i)
1078                 unchecked[i] = False
1079                 j = i
1080                 while unchecked[array_form[j]]:
1081                     j = array_form[j]
1082                     cycle.append(j)
1083                     unchecked[j] = False
1084                 if len(cycle) > 1:
1085                     cyclic_form.append(cycle)
1086                     assert cycle == list(minlex(cycle, is_set=True))
1087         cyclic_form.sort()
1088         self._cyclic_form = cyclic_form[:]
1089         return cyclic_form

1091     @property
1092     def full_cyclic_form(self):
1093         """Return permutation in cyclic form including singletons.
1094 
1095         Examples
1096         ========
1097 
1098         >>> from sympy.combinatorics.permutations import Permutation
1099         >>> Permutation([0, 2, 1]).full_cyclic_form
1100         [[0], [1, 2]]
1101         """
1102         need = set(range(self.size)) - set(flatten(self.cyclic_form))

1192         >>> Permutation.print_cyclic = False

1195         >>> a = Permutation(a); b = Permutation(b)

1216         True

1248     def __mul__(self, other):
1249         """
1250         Return the product a*b as a Permutation; the ith value is b(a(i)).
1251 
1252         Examples
1253         ========
1254 
1255         >>> from sympy.combinatorics.permutations import _af_rmul, Permutation
1256         >>> Permutation.print_cyclic = False
1257 
1258         >>> a, b = [1, 0, 2], [0, 2, 1]
1259         >>> a = Permutation(a); b = Permutation(b)
1260         >>> list(a*b)
1261         [2, 0, 1]
1262         >>> [b(a(i)) for i in range(3)]
1263         [2, 0, 1]
1264 
1265         This handles operands in reverse order compared to _af_rmul and rmul:
1266 
1267         >>> al = list(a); bl = list(b)
1268         >>> _af_rmul(al, bl)
1269         [1, 2, 0]
1270         >>> [al[bl[i]] for i in range(3)]
1271         [1, 2, 0]
1272 
1273         It is acceptable for the arrays to have different lengths; the shorter
1274         one will be padded to match the longer one:
1275 
1276         >>> b*Permutation([1, 0])
1277         Permutation([1, 2, 0])
1278         >>> Permutation([1, 0])*b
1279         Permutation([2, 0, 1])
1280 
1281         It is also acceptable to allow coercion to handle conversion of a
1282         single list to the left of a Permutation:
1283 
1284         >>> [0, 1]*a # no change: 2-element identity
1285         Permutation([1, 0, 2])
1286         >>> [[0, 1]]*a # exchange first two elements
1287         Permutation([0, 1, 2])
1288 
1289         You cannot use more than 1 cycle notation in a product of cycles
1290         since coercion can only handle one argument to the left. To handle
1291         multiple cycles it is convenient to use Cycle instead of Permutation:
1292 
1293         >>> [[1, 2]]*[[2, 3]]*Permutation([]) # doctest: +SKIP
1294         >>> from sympy.combinatorics.permutations import Cycle
1295         >>> Cycle(1, 2)(2, 3)
1296         (1 3 2)
1297 
1298         """
1299         a = self.array_form
1300         # __rmul__ makes sure the other is a Permutation
1301         b = other.array_form
1302         if not b:
1303             perm = a
1304         else:
1305             b.extend(list(range(len(b), len(a))))
1306             perm = [b[i] for i in a] + b[len(a):]
1307         return _af_new(perm)

1367     def __xor__(self, h):
1368         """Return the conjugate permutation ``~h*self*h` `.
1369 
1370         If ``a`` and ``b`` are conjugates, ``a = h*b*~h`` and
1371         ``b = ~h*a*h`` and both have the same cycle structure.
1372 
1373         Examples
1374         ========
1375 
1376         >>> from sympy.combinatorics.permutations import Permutation
1377         >>> Permutation.print_cyclic = True
1378         >>> p = Permutation(1, 2, 9)
1379         >>> q = Permutation(6, 9, 8)
1380         >>> p*q != q*p
1381         True
1382 
1383         Calculate and check properties of the conjugate:
1384 
1385         >>> c = p^q
1386         >>> c == ~q*p*q and p == q*c*~q
1387         True
1388 
1389         The expression q^p^r is equivalent to q^(p*r):
1390 
1391         >>> r = Permutation(9)(4, 6, 8)
1392         >>> q^p^r == q^(p*r)
1393         True
1394 
1395         If the term to the left of the conjugate operator, i, is an integer
1396         then this is interpreted as selecting the ith element from the
1397         permutation to the right:
1398 
1399         >>> all(i^p == p(i) for i in range(p.size))
1400         True
1401 
1402         Note that the * operator as higher precedence than the ^ operator:
1403 
1404         >>> q^r*p^r == q^(r*p)^r == Permutation(9)(1, 6, 4)
1405         True
1406 
1407         Notes
1408         =====
1409 
1410         In Python the precedence rule is p^q^r = (p^q)^r which differs
1411         in general from p^(q^r)
1412 
1413         >>> q^p^r
1414         (9)(1 4 8)
1415         >>> q^(p^r)
1416         (9)(1 8 6)
1417 
1418         For a given r and p, both of the following are conjugates of p:
1419         ~r*p*r and r*p*~r. But these are not necessarily the same:
1420 
1421         >>> ~r*p*r == r*p*~r
1422         True
1423 
1424         >>> p = Permutation(1, 2, 9)(5, 6)
1425         >>> ~r*p*r == r*p*~r
1426         False
1427 
1428         The conjugate ~r*p*r was chosen so that ``p^q^r`` would be equivalent
1429         to ``p^(q*r)`` rather than ``p^(r*q)``. To obtain r*p*~r, pass ~r to
1430         this method:
1431 
1432         >>> p^~r == r*p*~r
1433         True
1434         """
1435 
1436         if self.size != h.size:
1437             raise ValueError("The permutations must be of equal size.")
1438         a = [None]*self.size
1439         h = h._array_form
1440         p = self._array_form
1441         for i in range(self.size):
1442             a[h[i]] = h[p[i]]
1443         return _af_new(a)
1444 
1445     def transpositions(self):
1446         """
1447         Return the permutation decomposed into a list of transpositions.
1448 
1449         It is always possible to express a permutation as the product of
1450         transpositions, see [1]
1451 
1452         Examples
1453         ========
1454 
1455         >>> from sympy.combinatorics.permutations import Permutation
1456         >>> p = Permutation([[1, 2, 3], [0, 4, 5, 6, 7]])
1457         >>> t = p.transpositions()
1458         >>> t
1459         [(0, 7), (0, 6), (0, 5), (0, 4), (1, 3), (1, 2)]
1460         >>> print(''.join(str(c) for c in t))
1461         (0, 7)(0, 6)(0, 5)(0, 4)(1, 3)(1, 2)
1462         >>> Permutation.rmul(*[Permutation([ti], size=p.size) for ti in t]) == p
1463         True
1464 
1465         References
1466         ==========
1467 
1468         1. http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transposition_%28mathematics%29#Properties
1469 
1470         """
1471         a = self.cyclic_form
1472         res = []
1473         for x in a:
1474             nx = len(x)
1475             if nx == 2:
1476                 res.append(tuple(x))
1477             elif nx > 2:
1478                 first = x[0]
1479                 for y in x[nx - 1:0:-1]:
1480                     res.append((first, y))
1481         return res

1595     def next_lex(self):
1596         """
1597         Returns the next permutation in lexicographical order.
1598         If self is the last permutation in lexicographical order
1599         it returns None.
1600         See [4] section 2.4.
1601 
1602 
1603         Examples
1604         ========
1605 
1606         >>> from sympy.combinatorics.permutations import Permutation
1607         >>> p = Permutation([2, 3, 1, 0])
1608         >>> p = Permutation([2, 3, 1, 0]); p.rank()
1609         17
1610         >>> p = p.next_lex(); p.rank()
1611         18
1612 
1613         See Also
1614         ========
1615 
1616         rank, unrank_lex
1617         """
1618         perm = self.array_form[:]
1619         n = len(perm)
1620         i = n - 2
1621         while perm[i + 1] < perm[i]:
1622             i -= 1
1623         if i == -1:
1624             return None
1625         else:
1626             j = n - 1
1627             while perm[j] < perm[i]:
1628                 j -= 1
1629             perm[j], perm[i] = perm[i], perm[j]
1630             i += 1
1631             j = n - 1
1632             while i < j:
1633                 perm[j], perm[i] = perm[i], perm[j]
1634                 i += 1
1635                 j -= 1
1636         return _af_new(perm)

1638     @classmethod
1639     def unrank_nonlex(self, n, r):
1640         """
1641         This is a linear time unranking algorithm that does not
1642         respect lexicographic order [3].
1643 
1644         Examples
1645         ========
1646 
1647         >>> from sympy.combinatorics.permutations import Permutation
1648         >>> Permutation.print_cyclic = False
1649         >>> Permutation.unrank_nonlex(4, 5)
1650         Permutation([2, 0, 3, 1])
1651         >>> Permutation.unrank_nonlex(4, -1)
1652         Permutation([0, 1, 2, 3])
1653 
1654         See Also
1655         ========
1656 
1657         next_nonlex, rank_nonlex
1658         """
1659         def _unrank1(n, r, a):
1660             if n > 0:
1661                 a[n - 1], a[r % n] = a[r % n], a[n - 1]
1662                 _unrank1(n - 1, r//n, a)
1663 
1664         id_perm = list(range(n))
1665         n = int(n)
1666         r = r % ifac(n)
1667         _unrank1(n, r, id_perm)
1668         return _af_new(id_perm)

1670     def rank_nonlex(self, inv_perm=None):
1671         """
1672         This is a linear time ranking algorithm that does not
1673         enforce lexicographic order [3].
1674 
1675 
1676         Examples
1677         ========
1678 
1679         >>> from sympy.combinatorics.permutations import Permutation
1680         >>> p = Permutation([0, 1, 2, 3])
1681         >>> p.rank_nonlex()
1682         23
1683 
1684         See Also
1685         ========
1686 
1687         next_nonlex, unrank_nonlex
1688         """
1689         def _rank1(n, perm, inv_perm):
1690             if n == 1:
1691                 return 0
1692             s = perm[n - 1]
1693             t = inv_perm[n - 1]
1694             perm[n - 1], perm[t] = perm[t], s
1695             inv_perm[n - 1], inv_perm[s] = inv_perm[s], t
1696             return s + n*_rank1(n - 1, perm, inv_perm)
1697 
1698         if inv_perm is None:
1699             inv_perm = (~self).array_form
1700         if not inv_perm:
1701             return 0
1702         perm = self.array_form[:]
1703         r = _rank1(len(perm), perm, inv_perm)
1704         return r
1705 
1706     def next_nonlex(self):
1707         """
1708         Returns the next permutation in nonlex order [3].
1709         If self is the last permutation in this order it returns None.
1710 
1711         Examples
1712         ========
1713 
1714         >>> from sympy.combinatorics.permutations import Permutation
1715         >>> Permutation.print_cyclic = False
1716         >>> p = Permutation([2, 0, 3, 1]); p.rank_nonlex()
1717         5
1718         >>> p = p.next_nonlex(); p

1720         >>> p.rank_nonlex()
1721         6

1724         ========
1725 
1726         rank_nonlex, unrank_nonlex

1733     def rank(self):
1734         """
1735         Returns the lexicographic rank of the permutation.
1736 
1737         Examples
1738         ========
1739 
1740         >>> from sympy.combinatorics.permutations import Permutation
1741         >>> p = Permutation([0, 1, 2, 3])
1742         >>> p.rank()
1743         0
1744         >>> p = Permutation([3, 2, 1, 0])
1745         >>> p.rank()
1746         23
1747 
1748         See Also
1749         ========
1750 
1751         next_lex, unrank_lex, cardinality, length, order, size
1752         """
1753         if not self._rank is None:
1754             return self._rank
1755         rank = 0
1756         rho = self.array_form[:]
1757         n = self.size - 1
1758         size = n + 1
1759         psize = int(ifac(n))
1760         for j in range(size - 1):
1761             rank += rho[j]*psize
1762             for i in range(j + 1, size):
1763                 if rho[i] > rho[j]:
1764                     rho[i] -= 1
1765             psize //= n
1766             n -= 1
1767         self._rank = rank
1768         return rank

2030     def inversions(self):
2031         """
2032         Computes the number of inversions of a permutation.
2033 
2034         An inversion is where i > j but p[i] < p[j].
2035 
2036         For small length of p, it iterates over all i and j
2037         values and calculates the number of inversions.
2038         For large length of p, it uses a variation of merge
2039         sort to calculate the number of inversions.
2040 
2041         References
2042         ==========
2043 
2044         [1] http://www.cp.eng.chula.ac.th/~piak/teaching/algo/algo2008/count-inv.htm
2045 
2046         Examples
2047         ========
2048 
2049         >>> from sympy.combinatorics.permutations import Permutation
2050         >>> p = Permutation([0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5])
2051         >>> p.inversions()
2052         0
2053         >>> Permutation([3, 2, 1, 0]).inversions()
2054         6
2055 
2056         See Also
2057         ========
2058 
2059         descents, ascents, min, max
2060         """
2061         inversions = 0
2062         a = self.array_form
2063         n = len(a)
2064         if n < 130:
2065             for i in range(n - 1):
2066                 b = a[i]
2067                 for c in a[i + 1:]:
2068                     if b > c:
2069                         inversions += 1
2070         else:
2071             k = 1
2072             right = 0
2073             arr = a[:]
2074             temp = a[:]
2075             while k < n:
2076                 i = 0
2077                 while i + k < n:
2078                     right = i + k * 2 - 1
2079                     if right >= n:
2080                         right = n - 1
2081                     inversions += _merge(arr, temp, i, i + k, right)
2082                     i = i + k * 2
2083                 k = k * 2
2084         return inversions

2086     def commutator(self, x):
2087         """Return the commutator of self and x: ``~x*~self*x*self``
2088 
2089         If f and g are part of a group, G, then the commutator of f and g
2090         is the group identity iff f and g commute, i.e. fg == gf.
2091 
2092         Examples
2093         ========
2094 
2095         >>> from sympy.combinatorics.permutations import Permutation
2096         >>> Permutation.print_cyclic = False
2097         >>> p = Permutation([0, 2, 3, 1])
2098         >>> x = Permutation([2, 0, 3, 1])
2099         >>> c = p.commutator(x); c
2100         Permutation([2, 1, 3, 0])
2101         >>> c == ~x*~p*x*p
2102         True
2103 
2104         >>> I = Permutation(3)
2105         >>> p = [I + i for i in range(6)]
2106         >>> for i in range(len(p)):
2107         ...     for j in range(len(p)):
2108         ...         c = p[i].commutator(p[j])
2109         ...         if p[i]*p[j] == p[j]*p[i]:
2110         ...             assert c == I
2111         ...         else:
2112         ...             assert c != I
2113         ...
2114 
2115         References
2116         ==========
2117 
2118         http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commutator
2119         """
2120 
2121         a = self.array_form
2122         b = x.array_form
2123         n = len(a)
2124         if len(b) != n:
2125             raise ValueError("The permutations must be of equal size.")
2126         inva = [None]*n
2127         for i in range(n):
2128             inva[a[i]] = i
2129         invb = [None]*n
2130         for i in range(n):
2131             invb[b[i]] = i
2132         return _af_new([a[b[inva[i]]] for i in invb])

2302     def inversion_vector(self):
2303         """Return the inversion vector of the permutation.

2305         The inversion vector consists of elements whose value
2306         indicates the number of elements in the permutation
2307         that are lesser than it and lie on its right hand side.

2313         ========

2315         >>> from sympy.combinatorics.permutations import Permutation
2316         >>> p = Permutation([4, 8, 0, 7, 1, 5, 3, 6, 2])
2317         >>> p.inversion_vector()
2318         [4, 7, 0, 5, 0, 2, 1, 1]
2319         >>> p = Permutation([3, 2, 1, 0])
2320         >>> p.inversion_vector()
2321         [3, 2, 1]
2322 
2323         The inversion vector increases lexicographically with the rank
2324         of the permutation, the -ith element cycling through 0..i.
2325 
2326         >>> p = Permutation(2)
2327         >>> while p:
2328         ...     print('%s %s %s' % (p, p.inversion_vector(), p.rank()))
2329         ...     p = p.next_lex()
2330         ...
2331         Permutation([0, 1, 2]) [0, 0] 0
2332         Permutation([0, 2, 1]) [0, 1] 1
2333         Permutation([1, 0, 2]) [1, 0] 2
2334         Permutation([1, 2, 0]) [1, 1] 3
2335         Permutation([2, 0, 1]) [2, 0] 4
2336         Permutation([2, 1, 0]) [2, 1] 5
2337

2339         ========

2345 
2346         for i in range(n - 1):
2347             val = 0
2348             for j in range(i + 1, n):
2349                 if self_array_form[j] < self_array_form[i]:
2350                     val += 1
2351             inversion_vector[i] = val
2352         return inversion_vector

2354     def rank_trotterjohnson(self):
2355         """
2356         Returns the Trotter Johnson rank, which we get from the minimal
2357         change algorithm. See [4] section 2.4.
2358 
2359         Examples
2360         ========
2361 
2362         >>> from sympy.combinatorics.permutations import Permutation
2363         >>> p = Permutation([0, 1, 2, 3])
2364         >>> p.rank_trotterjohnson()
2365         0
2366         >>> p = Permutation([0, 2, 1, 3])
2367         >>> p.rank_trotterjohnson()
2368         7
2369 
2370         See Also
2371         ========
2372 
2373         unrank_trotterjohnson, next_trotterjohnson
2374         """
2375         if self.array_form == [] or self.is_Identity:
2376             return 0
2377         if self.array_form == [1, 0]:
2378             return 1
2379         perm = self.array_form
2380         n = self.size
2381         rank = 0
2382         for j in range(1, n):
2383             k = 1
2384             i = 0
2385             while perm[i] != j:
2386                 if perm[i] < j:
2387                     k += 1
2388                 i += 1
2389             j1 = j + 1
2390             if rank % 2 == 0:
2391                 rank = j1*rank + j1 - k
2392             else:
2393                 rank = j1*rank + k - 1
2394         return rank
2395 
2396     @classmethod
2397     def unrank_trotterjohnson(self, size, rank):
2398         """
2399         Trotter Johnson permutation unranking. See [4] section 2.4.
2400 
2401         Examples
2402         ========
2403 
2404         >>> from sympy.combinatorics.permutations import Permutation
2405         >>> Permutation.unrank_trotterjohnson(5, 10)
2406         Permutation([0, 3, 1, 2, 4])
2407 
2408         See Also
2409         ========
2410 
2411         rank_trotterjohnson, next_trotterjohnson
2412         """
2413         perm = [0]*size
2414         r2 = 0
2415         n = ifac(size)
2416         pj = 1
2417         for j in range(2, size + 1):
2418             pj *= j
2419             r1 = (rank * pj) // n
2420             k = r1 - j*r2
2421             if r2 % 2 == 0:
2422                 for i in range(j - 1, j - k - 1, -1):
2423                     perm[i] = perm[i - 1]
2424                 perm[j - k - 1] = j - 1
2425             else:
2426                 for i in range(j - 1, k, -1):
2427                     perm[i] = perm[i - 1]
2428                 perm[k] = j - 1
2429             r2 = r1
2430         return _af_new(perm)
2431 
2432     def next_trotterjohnson(self):
2433         """
2434         Returns the next permutation in Trotter-Johnson order.
2435         If self is the last permutation it returns None.
2436         See [4] section 2.4. If it is desired to generate all such
2437         permutations, they can be generated in order more quickly
2438         with the ``generate_bell`` function.
2439 
2440         Examples
2441         ========
2442 
2443         >>> from sympy.combinatorics.permutations import Permutation
2444         >>> Permutation.print_cyclic = False
2445         >>> p = Permutation([3, 0, 2, 1])
2446         >>> p.rank_trotterjohnson()
2447         4
2448         >>> p = p.next_trotterjohnson(); p
2449         Permutation([0, 3, 2, 1])
2450         >>> p.rank_trotterjohnson()
2451         5
2452 
2453         See Also
2454         ========
2455 
2456         rank_trotterjohnson, unrank_trotterjohnson, sympy.utilities.iterables.generate_bell
2457         """
2458         pi = self.array_form[:]
2459         n = len(pi)
2460         st = 0
2461         rho = pi[:]
2462         done = False
2463         m = n-1
2464         while m > 0 and not done:
2465             d = rho.index(m)
2466             for i in range(d, m):
2467                 rho[i] = rho[i + 1]
2468             par = _af_parity(rho[:m])
2469             if par == 1:
2470                 if d == m:
2471                     m -= 1
2472                 else:
2473                     pi[st + d], pi[st + d + 1] = pi[st + d + 1], pi[st + d]
2474                     done = True
2475             else:
2476                 if d == 0:
2477                     m -= 1
2478                     st += 1
2479                 else:
2480                     pi[st + d], pi[st + d - 1] = pi[st + d - 1], pi[st + d]
2481                     done = True
2482         if m == 0:
2483             return None
2484         return _af_new(pi)
2485

2500         [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0],
2501         [1, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0],

2510         get_precedence_distance, get_adjacency_matrix, get_adjacency_distance
2511         """

2519     def get_precedence_distance(self, other):
2520         """
2521         Computes the precedence distance between two permutations.
2522 
2523         Suppose p and p' represent n jobs. The precedence metric
2524         counts the number of times a job j is preceded by job i
2525         in both p and p'. This metric is commutative.
2526 
2527         Examples
2528         ========
2529 
2530         >>> from sympy.combinatorics.permutations import Permutation
2531         >>> p = Permutation([2, 0, 4, 3, 1])
2532         >>> q = Permutation([3, 1, 2, 4, 0])
2533         >>> p.get_precedence_distance(q)
2534         7
2535         >>> q.get_precedence_distance(p)
2536         7
2537 
2538         See Also
2539         ========
2540 
2541         get_precedence_matrix, get_adjacency_matrix, get_adjacency_distance
2542         """
2543         if self.size != other.size:
2544             raise ValueError("The permutations must be of equal size.")
2545         self_prec_mat = self.get_precedence_matrix()
2546         other_prec_mat = other.get_precedence_matrix()
2547         n_prec = 0
2548         for i in range(self.size):
2549             for j in range(self.size):
2550                 if i == j:
2551                     continue
2552                 if self_prec_mat[i, j] * other_prec_mat[i, j] == 1:
2553                     n_prec += 1
2554         d = self.size * (self.size - 1)//2 - n_prec
2555         return d

2668     def josephus(self, m, n, s=1):
2669         """Return as a permutation the shuffling of range(n) using the Josephus
2670         scheme in which every m-th item is selected until all have been chosen.
2671         The returned permutation has elements listed by the order in which they
2672         were selected.
2673 
2674         The parameter ``s`` stops the selection process when there are ``s``
2675         items remaining and these are selected by continuing the selection,
2676         counting by 1 rather than by ``m``.
2677 
2678         Consider selecting every 3rd item from 6 until only 2 remain::
2679 
2680             choices    chosen
2681             ========   ======
2682               012345
2683               01 345   2
2684               01 34    25
2685               01  4    253
2686               0   4    2531
2687               0        25314
2688                        253140
2689 
2690         Examples
2691         ========
2692 
2693         >>> from sympy.combinatorics import Permutation
2694         >>> Permutation.josephus(3, 6, 2).array_form
2695         [2, 5, 3, 1, 4, 0]

2698         ==========

2701         2. http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josephus_problem
2702         3. http://www.wou.edu/~burtonl/josephus.html

2704         """
2705         from collections import deque
2706         m -= 1
2707         Q = deque(list(range(n)))
2708         perm = []
2709         while len(Q) > max(s, 1):
2710             for dp in range(m):
2711                 Q.append(Q.popleft())
2712             perm.append(Q.popleft())
2713         perm.extend(list(Q))
2714         return Perm(perm)

244     def _check_choices(self):

417     def deconstruct(self):
418         """
419         Return enough information to recreate the field as a 4-tuple:
420 
421          * The name of the field on the model, if contribute_to_class() has
422            been run.
423          * The import path of the field, including the class, e.g.
424            django.db.models.IntegerField. This should be the most portable
425            version, so less specific may be better.
426          * A list of positional arguments.
427          * A dict of keyword arguments.
428 
429         Note that the positional or keyword arguments must contain values of
430         the following types (including inner values of collection types):
431 
432          * None, bool, str, int, float, complex, set, frozenset, list, tuple,
433            dict
434          * UUID
435          * datetime.datetime (naive), datetime.date
436          * top-level classes, top-level functions - will be referenced by their
437            full import path
438          * Storage instances - these have their own deconstruct() method
439 
440         This is because the values here must be serialized into a text format
441         (possibly new Python code, possibly JSON) and these are the only types
442         with encoding handlers defined.
443 
444         There's no need to return the exact way the field was instantiated this
445         time, just ensure that the resulting field is the same - prefer keyword
446         arguments over positional ones, and omit parameters with their default
447         values.
448         """
449         # Short-form way of fetching all the default parameters
450         keywords = {}
451         possibles = {
452             "verbose_name": None,
453             "primary_key": False,
454             "max_length": None,
455             "unique": False,
456             "blank": False,
457             "null": False,
458             "db_index": False,
459             "default": NOT_PROVIDED,
460             "editable": True,
461             "serialize": True,
462             "unique_for_date": None,
463             "unique_for_month": None,
464             "unique_for_year": None,
465             "choices": None,
466             "help_text": '',
467             "db_column": None,
468             "db_tablespace": None,
469             "auto_created": False,
470             "validators": [],
471             "error_messages": None,
472         }
473         attr_overrides = {
474             "unique": "_unique",
475             "error_messages": "_error_messages",
476             "validators": "_validators",
477             "verbose_name": "_verbose_name",
478             "db_tablespace": "_db_tablespace",
479         }
480         equals_comparison = {"choices", "validators"}
481         for name, default in possibles.items():
482             value = getattr(self, attr_overrides.get(name, name))
483             # Unroll anything iterable for choices into a concrete list
484             if name == "choices" and isinstance(value, collections.abc.Iterable):
485                 value = list(value)
486             # Do correct kind of comparison
487             if name in equals_comparison:
488                 if value != default:
489                     keywords[name] = value
490             else:
491                 if value is not default:
492                     keywords[name] = value
493         # Work out path - we shorten it for known Django core fields
494         path = "%s.%s" % (self.__class__.__module__, self.__class__.__qualname__)
495         if path.startswith("django.db.models.fields.related"):
496             path = path.replace("django.db.models.fields.related", "django.db.models")
497         elif path.startswith("django.db.models.fields.files"):
498             path = path.replace("django.db.models.fields.files", "django.db.models")
499         elif path.startswith('django.db.models.fields.json'):
500             path = path.replace('django.db.models.fields.json', 'django.db.models')
501         elif path.startswith("django.db.models.fields.proxy"):
502             path = path.replace("django.db.models.fields.proxy", "django.db.models")
503         elif path.startswith("django.db.models.fields"):
504             path = path.replace("django.db.models.fields", "django.db.models")
505         # Return basic info - other fields should override this.
506         return (self.name, path, [], keywords)
507

530                 self.creation_counter != other.creation_counter or
531                 not hasattr(self, 'model') and not hasattr(other, 'model')

534             elif hasattr(self, 'model') != hasattr(other, 'model'):
535                 return not hasattr(self, 'model')  # Order no-model fields first
536             else:
537                 # creation_counter's are equal, compare only models.
538                 return (
539                     (self.model._meta.app_label, self.model._meta.model_name) <
540                     (other.model._meta.app_label, other.model._meta.model_name)
541                 )

570     def __reduce__(self):

572         Pickling should return the model._meta.fields instance of the field,
573         not a new copy of that field. So, use the app registry to load the
574         model and then the field back.

576         if not hasattr(self, 'model'):
577             # Fields are sometimes used without attaching them to models (for
578             # example in aggregation). In this case give back a plain field
579             # instance. The code below will create a new empty instance of
580             # class self.__class__, then update its dict with self.__dict__

617     def run_validators(self, value):
618         if value in self.empty_values:
619             return
620 
621         errors = []
622         for v in self.validators:
623             try:
624                 v(value)
625             except exceptions.ValidationError as e:
626                 if hasattr(e, 'code') and e.code in self.error_messages:
627                     e.message = self.error_messages[e.code]
628                 errors.extend(e.error_list)
629 
630         if errors:

633     def validate(self, value, model_instance):
634         """
635         Validate value and raise ValidationError if necessary. Subclasses
636         should override this to provide validation logic.
637         """
638         if not self.editable:
639             # Skip validation for non-editable fields.
640             return
641 
642         if self.choices is not None and value not in self.empty_values:
643             for option_key, option_value in self.choices:
644                 if isinstance(option_value, (list, tuple)):
645                     # This is an optgroup, so look inside the group for
646                     # options.
647                     for optgroup_key, optgroup_value in option_value:
648                         if value == optgroup_key:
649                             return
650                 elif value == option_key:
651                     return
652             raise exceptions.ValidationError(
653                 self.error_messages['invalid_choice'],
654                 code='invalid_choice',
655                 params={'value': value},
656             )
657 
658         if value is None and not self.null:
659             raise exceptions.ValidationError(self.error_messages['null'], code='null')
660 
661         if not self.blank and value in self.empty_values:
662             raise exceptions.ValidationError(self.error_messages['blank'], code='blank')

671         self.validate(value, model_instance)
672         self.run_validators(value)
673         return value

690     def db_type(self, connection):
691         """
692         Return the database column data type for this field, for the provided
693         connection.
694         """
695         # The default implementation of this method looks at the
696         # backend-specific data_types dictionary, looking up the field by its
697         # "internal type".
698         #
699         # A Field class can implement the get_internal_type() method to specify
700         # which *preexisting* Django Field class it's most similar to -- i.e.,
701         # a custom field might be represented by a TEXT column type, which is
702         # the same as the TextField Django field type, which means the custom
703         # field's get_internal_type() returns 'TextField'.
704         #
705         # But the limitation of the get_internal_type() / data_types approach
706         # is that it cannot handle database column types that aren't already
707         # mapped to one of the built-in Django field types. In this case, you
708         # can implement db_type() instead of get_internal_type() to specify
709         # exactly which wacky database column type you want to use.
710         data = self.db_type_parameters(connection)
711         try:
712             return connection.data_types[self.get_internal_type()] % data
713         except KeyError:
714             return None

1176                         'as default, use `django.utils.timezone.now`'

problem_statement:
Please support header rows in RestructuredText output
### Description

It would be great if the following would work:

```Python
>>> from astropy.table import QTable
>>> import astropy.units as u
>>> import sys
>>> tbl = QTable({'wave': [350,950]*u.nm, 'response': [0.7, 1.2]*u.count})
>>> tbl.write(sys.stdout,  format="ascii.rst")
===== ========
 wave response
===== ========
350.0      0.7
950.0      1.2
===== ========
>>> tbl.write(sys.stdout,  format="ascii.fixed_width", header_rows=["name", "unit"])
|  wave | response |
|    nm |       ct |
| 350.0 |      0.7 |
| 950.0 |      1.2 |
>>> tbl.write(sys.stdout,  format="ascii.rst", header_rows=["name", "unit"])
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
  File "/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/astropy/table/connect.py", line 129, in __call__
    self.registry.write(instance, *args, **kwargs)
  File "/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/astropy/io/registry/core.py", line 369, in write
    return writer(data, *args, **kwargs)
  File "/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/astropy/io/ascii/connect.py", line 26, in io_write
    return write(table, filename, **kwargs)
  File "/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/astropy/io/ascii/ui.py", line 856, in write
    writer = get_writer(Writer=Writer, fast_writer=fast_writer, **kwargs)
  File "/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/astropy/io/ascii/ui.py", line 800, in get_writer
    writer = core._get_writer(Writer, fast_writer, **kwargs)
  File "/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/astropy/io/ascii/core.py", line 1719, in _get_writer
    writer = Writer(**writer_kwargs)
TypeError: RST.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'header_rows'
```


### Additional context

RestructuredText output is a great way to fill autogenerated documentation with content, so having this flexible makes the life easier `:-)`

LaTeX printing for Matrix Expression
```py
>>> A = MatrixSymbol("A", n, n)
>>> latex(trace(A**2))
'Trace(A**2)'
```

The bad part is not only is Trace not recognized, but whatever printer is being used doesn't fallback to the LaTeX printer for the inner expression (it should be `A^2`).

180     def parenthesize(self, item, level, strict=False):
181         prec_val = precedence_traditional(item)
182         if (prec_val < level) or ((not strict) and prec_val <= level):
183             return r"\left(%s\right)" % self._print(item)
184         else:
185             return self._print(item)

193             return r"$%s$" % tex

200     def _needs_brackets(self, expr):
201         """
202         Returns True if the expression needs to be wrapped in brackets when
203         printed, False otherwise. For example: a + b => True; a => False;
204         10 => False; -10 => True.
205         """
206         return not ((expr.is_Integer and expr.is_nonnegative)
207                     or (expr.is_Atom and (expr is not S.NegativeOne
208                                           and expr.is_Rational is False)))
209 
210     def _needs_function_brackets(self, expr):
211         """
212         Returns True if the expression needs to be wrapped in brackets when
213         passed as an argument to a function, False otherwise. This is a more
214         liberal version of _needs_brackets, in that many expressions which need
215         to be wrapped in brackets when added/subtracted/raised to a power do
216         not need them when passed to a function. Such an example is a*b.
217         """
218         if not self._needs_brackets(expr):
219             return False
220         else:
221             # Muls of the form a*b*c... can be folded
222             if expr.is_Mul and not self._mul_is_clean(expr):
223                 return True
224             # Pows which don't need brackets can be folded
225             elif expr.is_Pow and not self._pow_is_clean(expr):
226                 return True
227             # Add and Function always need brackets
228             elif expr.is_Add or expr.is_Function:
229                 return True
230             else:
231                 return False
232 
233     def _needs_mul_brackets(self, expr, first=False, last=False):
234         """
235         Returns True if the expression needs to be wrapped in brackets when
236         printed as part of a Mul, False otherwise. This is True for Add,
237         but also for some container objects that would not need brackets
238         when appearing last in a Mul, e.g. an Integral. ``last=True``
239         specifies that this expr is the last to appear in a Mul.
240         ``first=True`` specifies that this expr is the first to appear in a Mul.
241         """
242         from sympy import Integral, Piecewise, Product, Sum
243 
244         if expr.is_Mul:
245             if not first and _coeff_isneg(expr):
246                 return True
247         elif precedence_traditional(expr) < PRECEDENCE["Mul"]:
248             return True
249         elif expr.is_Relational:
250             return True
251         if expr.is_Piecewise:
252             return True
253         if any([expr.has(x) for x in (Mod,)]):
254             return True
255         if (not last and
256             any([expr.has(x) for x in (Integral, Product, Sum)])):
257             return True
258 
259         return False
260

262     def _needs_add_brackets(self, expr):
263         """
264         Returns True if the expression needs to be wrapped in brackets when
265         printed as part of an Add, False otherwise.  This is False for most
266         things.
267         """
268         if expr.is_Relational:
269             return True
270         if any([expr.has(x) for x in (Mod,)]):
271             return True
272         if expr.is_Add:
273             return True
274         return False

302     def _print_Add(self, expr, order=None):
303         if self.order == 'none':
304             terms = list(expr.args)

306             terms = self._as_ordered_terms(expr, order=order)

313                 tex += " - "
314                 term = -term

316                 tex += " + "

318             if self._needs_add_brackets(term):
319                 term_tex = r"\left(%s\right)" % term_tex
320             tex += term_tex

324     def _print_Cycle(self, expr):
325         from sympy.combinatorics.permutations import Permutation
326         if expr.size == 0:
327             return r"\left( \right)"
328         expr = Permutation(expr)
329         expr_perm = expr.cyclic_form
330         siz = expr.size
331         if expr.array_form[-1] == siz - 1:
332             expr_perm = expr_perm + [[siz - 1]]
333         term_tex = ''
334         for i in expr_perm:
335             term_tex += str(i).replace(',', r"\;")
336         term_tex = term_tex.replace('[', r"\left( ")
337         term_tex = term_tex.replace(']', r"\right)")
338         return term_tex

389     def _print_Mul(self, expr):
390         from sympy.core.power import Pow
391         from sympy.physics.units import Quantity
392         include_parens = False
393         if _coeff_isneg(expr):
394             expr = -expr
395             tex = "- "
396             if expr.is_Add:
397                 tex += "("
398                 include_parens = True
399         else:
400             tex = ""
401 
402         from sympy.simplify import fraction
403         numer, denom = fraction(expr, exact=True)
404         separator = self._settings['mul_symbol_latex']
405         numbersep = self._settings['mul_symbol_latex_numbers']
406 
407         def convert(expr):
408             if not expr.is_Mul:
409                 return str(self._print(expr))
410             else:
411                 _tex = last_term_tex = ""
412 
413                 if self.order not in ('old', 'none'):
414                     args = expr.as_ordered_factors()
415                 else:
416                     args = list(expr.args)
417 
418                 # If quantities are present append them at the back
419                 args = sorted(args, key=lambda x: isinstance(x, Quantity) or
420                              (isinstance(x, Pow) and isinstance(x.base, Quantity)))
421 
422                 for i, term in enumerate(args):
423                     term_tex = self._print(term)
424 
425                     if self._needs_mul_brackets(term, first=(i == 0),
426                                                 last=(i == len(args) - 1)):
427                         term_tex = r"\left(%s\right)" % term_tex
428 
429                     if _between_two_numbers_p[0].search(last_term_tex) and \
430                             _between_two_numbers_p[1].match(term_tex):
431                         # between two numbers
432                         _tex += numbersep
433                     elif _tex:
434                         _tex += separator
435 
436                     _tex += term_tex
437                     last_term_tex = term_tex
438                 return _tex
439 
440         if denom is S.One and Pow(1, -1, evaluate=False) not in expr.args:
441             # use the original expression here, since fraction() may have
442             # altered it when producing numer and denom
443             tex += convert(expr)
444 
445         else:
446             snumer = convert(numer)
447             sdenom = convert(denom)
448             ldenom = len(sdenom.split())
449             ratio = self._settings['long_frac_ratio']
450             if self._settings['fold_short_frac'] \
451                    and ldenom <= 2 and not "^" in sdenom:
452                 # handle short fractions
453                 if self._needs_mul_brackets(numer, last=False):
454                     tex += r"\left(%s\right) / %s" % (snumer, sdenom)
455                 else:
456                     tex += r"%s / %s" % (snumer, sdenom)
457             elif ratio is not None and \
458                     len(snumer.split()) > ratio*ldenom:
459                 # handle long fractions
460                 if self._needs_mul_brackets(numer, last=True):
461                     tex += r"\frac{1}{%s}%s\left(%s\right)" \
462                         % (sdenom, separator, snumer)
463                 elif numer.is_Mul:
464                     # split a long numerator
465                     a = S.One
466                     b = S.One
467                     for x in numer.args:
468                         if self._needs_mul_brackets(x, last=False) or \
469                                 len(convert(a*x).split()) > ratio*ldenom or \
470                                 (b.is_commutative is x.is_commutative is False):
471                             b *= x
472                         else:
473                             a *= x
474                     if self._needs_mul_brackets(b, last=True):
475                         tex += r"\frac{%s}{%s}%s\left(%s\right)" \
476                             % (convert(a), sdenom, separator, convert(b))
477                     else:
478                         tex += r"\frac{%s}{%s}%s%s" \
479                             % (convert(a), sdenom, separator, convert(b))
480                 else:
481                     tex += r"\frac{1}{%s}%s%s" % (sdenom, separator, snumer)
482             else:
483                 tex += r"\frac{%s}{%s}" % (snumer, sdenom)
484 
485         if include_parens:
486             tex += ")"
487         return tex
488 
489     def _print_Pow(self, expr):
490         # Treat x**Rational(1,n) as special case
491         if expr.exp.is_Rational and abs(expr.exp.p) == 1 and expr.exp.q != 1:
492             base = self._print(expr.base)
493             expq = expr.exp.q
494 
495             if expq == 2:
496                 tex = r"\sqrt{%s}" % base
497             elif self._settings['itex']:
498                 tex = r"\root{%d}{%s}" % (expq, base)
499             else:
500                 tex = r"\sqrt[%d]{%s}" % (expq, base)
501 
502             if expr.exp.is_negative:
503                 return r"\frac{1}{%s}" % tex
504             else:
505                 return tex
506         elif self._settings['fold_frac_powers'] \
507             and expr.exp.is_Rational \
508                 and expr.exp.q != 1:
509             base, p, q = self.parenthesize(expr.base, PRECEDENCE['Pow']), expr.exp.p, expr.exp.q
510             # issue #12886: add parentheses for superscripts raised to powers
511             if '^' in base and expr.base.is_Symbol:
512                 base = r"\left(%s\right)" % base
513             if expr.base.is_Function:
514                 return self._print(expr.base, exp="%s/%s" % (p, q))
515             return r"%s^{%s/%s}" % (base, p, q)
516         elif expr.exp.is_Rational and expr.exp.is_negative and expr.base.is_commutative:
517             # special case for 1^(-x), issue 9216
518             if expr.base == 1:
519                 return r"%s^{%s}" % (expr.base, expr.exp)
520             # things like 1/x
521             return self._print_Mul(expr)
522         else:
523             if expr.base.is_Function:
524                 return self._print(expr.base, exp=self._print(expr.exp))
525             else:
526                 tex = r"%s^{%s}"
527                 exp = self._print(expr.exp)
528                 # issue #12886: add parentheses around superscripts raised to powers
529                 base = self.parenthesize(expr.base, PRECEDENCE['Pow'])
530                 if '^' in base and expr.base.is_Symbol:
531                     base = r"\left(%s\right)" % base
532                 elif isinstance(expr.base, Derivative
533                         ) and base.startswith(r'\left('
534                         ) and re.match(r'\\left\(\\d?d?dot', base
535                         ) and base.endswith(r'\right)'):
536                     # don't use parentheses around dotted derivative
537                     base = base[6: -7]  # remove outermost added parens
538 
539                 return tex % (base, exp)
540

660             symbols = [r"\, d%s" % self._print(symbol[0])
661                        for symbol in expr.limits]

663         else:
664             for lim in reversed(expr.limits):
665                 symbol = lim[0]
666                 tex += r"\int"
667 
668                 if len(lim) > 1:
669                     if self._settings['mode'] in ['equation', 'equation*'] \
670                             and not self._settings['itex']:
671                         tex += r"\limits"
672 
673                     if len(lim) == 3:
674                         tex += "_{%s}^{%s}" % (self._print(lim[1]),
675                                                self._print(lim[2]))
676                     if len(lim) == 2:
677                         tex += "^{%s}" % (self._print(lim[1]))
678 
679                 symbols.insert(0, r"\, d%s" % self._print(symbol))

682             self.parenthesize(expr.function, PRECEDENCE["Mul"], strict=True), "".join(symbols))

698     def _hprint_Function(self, func):
699         r'''
700         Logic to decide how to render a function to latex
701           - if it is a recognized latex name, use the appropriate latex command
702           - if it is a single letter, just use that letter
703           - if it is a longer name, then put \operatorname{} around it and be
704             mindful of undercores in the name
705         '''
706         func = self._deal_with_super_sub(func)
707         if func in accepted_latex_functions:
708             name = r"\%s" % func
709         elif len(func) == 1 or func.startswith('\\'):
710             name = func
711         else:
712             name = r"\operatorname{%s}" % func
713         return name
714 
715     def _print_Function(self, expr, exp=None):
716         r'''
717         Render functions to LaTeX, handling functions that LaTeX knows about
718         e.g., sin, cos, ... by using the proper LaTeX command (\sin, \cos, ...).
719         For single-letter function names, render them as regular LaTeX math
720         symbols. For multi-letter function names that LaTeX does not know
721         about, (e.g., Li, sech) use \operatorname{} so that the function name
722         is rendered in Roman font and LaTeX handles spacing properly.
723 
724         expr is the expression involving the function
725         exp is an exponent
726         '''
727         func = expr.func.__name__
728         if hasattr(self, '_print_' + func) and \
729             not isinstance(expr.func, UndefinedFunction):
730             return getattr(self, '_print_' + func)(expr, exp)
731         else:
732             args = [ str(self._print(arg)) for arg in expr.args ]
733             # How inverse trig functions should be displayed, formats are:
734             # abbreviated: asin, full: arcsin, power: sin^-1
735             inv_trig_style = self._settings['inv_trig_style']
736             # If we are dealing with a power-style inverse trig function
737             inv_trig_power_case = False
738             # If it is applicable to fold the argument brackets
739             can_fold_brackets = self._settings['fold_func_brackets'] and \
740                 len(args) == 1 and \
741                 not self._needs_function_brackets(expr.args[0])
742 
743             inv_trig_table = ["asin", "acos", "atan", "acsc", "asec", "acot"]
744 
745             # If the function is an inverse trig function, handle the style
746             if func in inv_trig_table:
747                 if inv_trig_style == "abbreviated":
748                     func = func
749                 elif inv_trig_style == "full":
750                     func = "arc" + func[1:]
751                 elif inv_trig_style == "power":
752                     func = func[1:]
753                     inv_trig_power_case = True
754 
755                     # Can never fold brackets if we're raised to a power
756                     if exp is not None:
757                         can_fold_brackets = False
758 
759             if inv_trig_power_case:
760                 if func in accepted_latex_functions:
761                     name = r"\%s^{-1}" % func
762                 else:
763                     name = r"\operatorname{%s}^{-1}" % func
764             elif exp is not None:
765                 name = r'%s^{%s}' % (self._hprint_Function(func), exp)
766             else:
767                 name = self._hprint_Function(func)
768 
769             if can_fold_brackets:
770                 if func in accepted_latex_functions:
771                     # Wrap argument safely to avoid parse-time conflicts
772                     # with the function name itself
773                     name += r" {%s}"
774                 else:
775                     name += r"%s"
776             else:
777                 name += r"{\left (%s \right )}"
778 
779             if inv_trig_power_case and exp is not None:
780                 name += r"^{%s}" % exp
781 
782             return name % ",".join(args)
783

1541     def _print_NDimArray(self, expr):
1542 
1543         if expr.rank() == 0:
1544             return self._print(expr[()])
1545 
1546         mat_str = self._settings['mat_str']
1547         if mat_str is None:
1548             if self._settings['mode'] == 'inline':
1549                 mat_str = 'smallmatrix'
1550             else:
1551                 if (expr.rank() == 0) or (expr.shape[-1] <= 10):
1552                     mat_str = 'matrix'
1553                 else:
1554                     mat_str = 'array'
1555         block_str = r'\begin{%MATSTR%}%s\end{%MATSTR%}'
1556         block_str = block_str.replace('%MATSTR%', mat_str)
1557         if self._settings['mat_delim']:
1558             left_delim = self._settings['mat_delim']
1559             right_delim = self._delim_dict[left_delim]
1560             block_str = r'\left' + left_delim + block_str + \
1561                       r'\right' + right_delim
1562 
1563         if expr.rank() == 0:
1564             return block_str % ""
1565 
1566         level_str = [[]] + [[] for i in range(expr.rank())]
1567         shape_ranges = [list(range(i)) for i in expr.shape]
1568         for outer_i in itertools.product(*shape_ranges):
1569             level_str[-1].append(self._print(expr[outer_i]))
1570             even = True
1571             for back_outer_i in range(expr.rank()-1, -1, -1):
1572                 if len(level_str[back_outer_i+1]) < expr.shape[back_outer_i]:
1573                     break
1574                 if even:
1575                     level_str[back_outer_i].append(r" & ".join(level_str[back_outer_i+1]))
1576                 else:
1577                     level_str[back_outer_i].append(block_str % (r"\\".join(level_str[back_outer_i+1])))
1578                     if len(level_str[back_outer_i+1]) == 1:
1579                         level_str[back_outer_i][-1] = r"\left[" + level_str[back_outer_i][-1] + r"\right]"
1580                 even = not even
1581                 level_str[back_outer_i+1] = []
1582 
1583         out_str = level_str[0][0]
1584 
1585         if expr.rank() % 2 == 1:
1586             out_str = block_str % out_str
1587 
1588         return out_str

1595     def _printer_tensor_indices(self, name, indices, index_map={}):

1598         prev_map = None

1600             new_valence = index.is_up
1601             if ((index in index_map) or prev_map) and last_valence == new_valence:
1602                 out_str += ","
1603             if last_valence != new_valence:
1604                 if last_valence is not None:
1605                     out_str += "}"
1606                 if index.is_up:
1607                     out_str += "{}^{"
1608                 else:
1609                     out_str += "{}_{"
1610             out_str += self._print(index.args[0])
1611             if index in index_map:

1613                 out_str += self._print(index_map[index])
1614                 prev_map = True
1615             else:
1616                 prev_map = False
1617             last_valence = new_valence
1618         if last_valence is not None:
1619             out_str += "}"
1620         return out_str

1916     def _print_Poly(self, poly):
1917         cls = poly.__class__.__name__
1918         terms = []
1919         for monom, coeff in poly.terms():
1920             s_monom = ''
1921             for i, exp in enumerate(monom):
1922                 if exp > 0:
1923                     if exp == 1:
1924                         s_monom += self._print(poly.gens[i])
1925                     else:
1926                         s_monom += self._print(pow(poly.gens[i], exp))
1927 
1928             if coeff.is_Add:
1929                 if s_monom:
1930                     s_coeff = r"\left(%s\right)" % self._print(coeff)
1931                 else:
1932                     s_coeff = self._print(coeff)
1933             else:
1934                 if s_monom:
1935                     if coeff is S.One:
1936                         terms.extend(['+', s_monom])
1937                         continue
1938 
1939                     if coeff is S.NegativeOne:
1940                         terms.extend(['-', s_monom])
1941                         continue
1942 
1943                 s_coeff = self._print(coeff)
1944 
1945             if not s_monom:
1946                 s_term = s_coeff
1947             else:
1948                 s_term = s_coeff + " " + s_monom
1949 
1950             if s_term.startswith('-'):
1951                 terms.extend(['-', s_term[1:]])
1952             else:
1953                 terms.extend(['+', s_term])
1954 
1955         if terms[0] in ['-', '+']:
1956             modifier = terms.pop(0)
1957 
1958             if modifier == '-':
1959                 terms[0] = '-' + terms[0]
1960 
1961         expr = ' '.join(terms)
1962         gens = list(map(self._print, poly.gens))
1963         domain = "domain=%s" % self._print(poly.get_domain())
1964 
1965         args = ", ".join([expr] + gens + [domain])
1966         if cls in accepted_latex_functions:
1967             tex = r"\%s {\left (%s \right )}" % (cls, args)
1968         else:
1969             tex = r"\operatorname{%s}{\left( %s \right)}" % (cls, args)
1970 
1971         return tex

2238 def translate(s):
2239     r'''
2240     Check for a modifier ending the string.  If present, convert the
2241     modifier to latex and translate the rest recursively.
2242 
2243     Given a description of a Greek letter or other special character,
2244     return the appropriate latex.
2245 
2246     Let everything else pass as given.
2247 
2248     >>> from sympy.printing.latex import translate
2249     >>> translate('alphahatdotprime')
2250     "{\\dot{\\hat{\\alpha}}}'"
2251     '''
2252     # Process the rest
2253     tex = tex_greek_dictionary.get(s)
2254     if tex:
2255         return tex
2256     elif s.lower() in greek_letters_set:
2257         return "\\" + s.lower()
2258     elif s in other_symbols:
2259         return "\\" + s
2260     else:
2261         # Process modifiers, if any, and recurse
2262         for key in sorted(modifier_dict.keys(), key=lambda k:len(k), reverse=True):
2263             if s.lower().endswith(key) and len(s)>len(key):
2264                 return modifier_dict[key](translate(s[:-len(key)]))
2265         return s
