187 Brief History
188 -------------
189 
190 SymPy was started by Ondřej Čertík in 2005, he wrote some code during the
191 summer, then he wrote some more code during summer 2006. In February 2007,
192 Fabian Pedregosa joined the project and helped fixed many things, contributed
193 documentation and made it alive again. 5 students (Mateusz Paprocki, Brian
194 Jorgensen, Jason Gedge, Robert Schwarz, and Chris Wu) improved SymPy incredibly
195 during summer 2007 as part of the Google Summer of Code. Pearu Peterson
196 joined the development during the summer 2007 and he has made SymPy much more
197 competitive by rewriting the core from scratch, that has made it from 10x to
198 100x faster. Jurjen N.E. Bos has contributed pretty printing and other patches.
199 Fredrik Johansson has written mpmath and contributed a lot of patches.
200 
201 SymPy has participated in every Google Summer of Code since 2007. You can see
202 https://github.com/sympy/sympy/wiki#google-summer-of-code for full details.
203 Each year has improved SymPy by bounds. Most of SymPy's development has come
204 from Google Summer of Code students.
205 
206 In 2011, Ondřej Čertík stepped down as lead developer, with Aaron Meurer, who
207 also started as a Google Summer of Code student, taking his place. Ondřej
208 Čertík is still active in the community but is too busy with work and family
209 to play a lead development role.
210 
211 Since then, a lot more people have joined the development and some people have
212 also left. You can see the full list in doc/src/aboutus.rst, or online at:
213 
214 https://docs.sympy.org/dev/aboutus.html#sympy-development-team
215 
216 The git history goes back to 2007 when development moved from svn to hg.  To
217 see the history before that point, look at https://github.com/sympy/sympy-old.
218 
219 You can use git to see the biggest developers.  The command::
220 
221      $ git shortlog -ns
222 
223 will show each developer, sorted by commits to the project.  The command::
224 
225      $ git shortlog -ns --since="1 year"
226 
227 will show the top developers from the last year.

340         for sym, num in reversed(deriv.variable_count):
341             s = self._print(sym)
342             ds = prettyForm(*s.left(deriv_symbol))
343             count_total_deriv += num
344

346                 ds = ds**prettyForm(str(num))

355             binding=prettyForm.FUNC, *self._print(deriv.expr).parens())

405     def _print_Integral(self, integral):

408         # Add parentheses if arg involves addition of terms and
409         # create a pretty form for the argument
410         prettyF = self._print(f)
411         # XXX generalize parens
412         if f.is_Add:
413             prettyF = prettyForm(*prettyF.parens())
414 
415         # dx dy dz ...
416         arg = prettyF
417         for x in integral.limits:
418             prettyArg = self._print(x[0])
419             # XXX qparens (parens if needs-parens)
420             if prettyArg.width() > 1:
421                 prettyArg = prettyForm(*prettyArg.parens())
422 
423             arg = prettyForm(*arg.right(' d', prettyArg))
424 
425         # \int \int \int ...
426         firstterm = True
427         s = None
428         for lim in integral.limits:
429             x = lim[0]
430             # Create bar based on the height of the argument
431             h = arg.height()
432             H = h + 2
433 
434             # XXX hack!
435             ascii_mode = not self._use_unicode
436             if ascii_mode:
437                 H += 2
438 
439             vint = vobj('int', H)
440 
441             # Construct the pretty form with the integral sign and the argument

444                 H - h)//2    # covering the whole argument

446             if len(lim) > 1:
447                 # Create pretty forms for endpoints, if definite integral.
448                 # Do not print empty endpoints.
449                 if len(lim) == 2:

451                     prettyB = self._print(lim[1])
452                 if len(lim) == 3:
453                     prettyA = self._print(lim[1])

456                 if ascii_mode:  # XXX hack

458                     # identified with the correct integral sign

460                     prettyB = prettyForm(*prettyB.left(' ' * spc))
461 
462                     spc = max(1, 4 - prettyA.width())

465                 pform = prettyForm(*pform.above(prettyB))

470 
471             if firstterm:
472                 s = pform   # first term
473                 firstterm = False
474             else:
475                 s = prettyForm(*s.left(pform))

477         pform = prettyForm(*arg.left(s))

535     def _print_Sum(self, expr):
536         ascii_mode = not self._use_unicode
537 
538         def asum(hrequired, lower, upper, use_ascii):
539             def adjust(s, wid=None, how='<^>'):
540                 if not wid or len(s) > wid:
541                     return s
542                 need = wid - len(s)
543                 if how == '<^>' or how == "<" or how not in list('<^>'):
544                     return s + ' '*need
545                 half = need//2
546                 lead = ' '*half
547                 if how == ">":
548                     return " "*need + s
549                 return lead + s + ' '*(need - len(lead))
550 
551             h = max(hrequired, 2)
552             d = h//2
553             w = d + 1
554             more = hrequired % 2
555 
556             lines = []
557             if use_ascii:
558                 lines.append("_"*(w) + ' ')
559                 lines.append(r"\%s`" % (' '*(w - 1)))
560                 for i in range(1, d):
561                     lines.append('%s\\%s' % (' '*i, ' '*(w - i)))
562                 if more:
563                     lines.append('%s)%s' % (' '*(d), ' '*(w - d)))
564                 for i in reversed(range(1, d)):
565                     lines.append('%s/%s' % (' '*i, ' '*(w - i)))
566                 lines.append("/" + "_"*(w - 1) + ',')
567                 return d, h + more, lines, 0
568             else:
569                 w = w + more
570                 d = d + more
571                 vsum = vobj('sum', 4)
572                 lines.append("_"*(w))
573                 for i in range(0, d):
574                     lines.append('%s%s%s' % (' '*i, vsum[2], ' '*(w - i - 1)))
575                 for i in reversed(range(0, d)):
576                     lines.append('%s%s%s' % (' '*i, vsum[4], ' '*(w - i - 1)))
577                 lines.append(vsum[8]*(w))
578                 return d, h + 2*more, lines, more
579 
580         f = expr.function
581 
582         prettyF = self._print(f)
583 
584         if f.is_Add:  # add parens
585             prettyF = prettyForm(*prettyF.parens())
586 
587         H = prettyF.height() + 2
588 
589         # \sum \sum \sum ...
590         first = True
591         max_upper = 0
592         sign_height = 0
593 
594         for lim in expr.limits:
595             if len(lim) == 3:
596                 prettyUpper = self._print(lim[2])
597                 prettyLower = self._print(Equality(lim[0], lim[1]))
598             elif len(lim) == 2:
599                 prettyUpper = self._print("")
600                 prettyLower = self._print(Equality(lim[0], lim[1]))
601             elif len(lim) == 1:
602                 prettyUpper = self._print("")
603                 prettyLower = self._print(lim[0])
604 
605             max_upper = max(max_upper, prettyUpper.height())
606 
607             # Create sum sign based on the height of the argument
608             d, h, slines, adjustment = asum(
609                 H, prettyLower.width(), prettyUpper.width(), ascii_mode)
610             prettySign = stringPict('')
611             prettySign = prettyForm(*prettySign.stack(*slines))
612 
613             if first:
614                 sign_height = prettySign.height()
615 
616             prettySign = prettyForm(*prettySign.above(prettyUpper))
617             prettySign = prettyForm(*prettySign.below(prettyLower))
618 
619             if first:
620                 # change F baseline so it centers on the sign
621                 prettyF.baseline -= d - (prettyF.height()//2 -
622                                          prettyF.baseline) - adjustment
623                 first = False
624 
625             # put padding to the right
626             pad = stringPict('')
627             pad = prettyForm(*pad.stack(*[' ']*h))
628             prettySign = prettyForm(*prettySign.right(pad))
629             # put the present prettyF to the right
630             prettyF = prettyForm(*prettySign.right(prettyF))
631 
632         prettyF.baseline = max_upper + sign_height//2
633         prettyF.binding = prettyForm.MUL
634         return prettyF

664     def _print_matrix_contents(self, e):
665         """
666         This method factors out what is essentially grid printing.
667         """
668         M = e   # matrix
669         Ms = {}  # i,j -> pretty(M[i,j])
670         for i in range(M.rows):
671             for j in range(M.cols):
672                 Ms[i, j] = self._print(M[i, j])
673 
674         # h- and v- spacers
675         hsep = 2
676         vsep = 1
677 
678         # max width for columns
679         maxw = [-1] * M.cols
680 
681         for j in range(M.cols):
682             maxw[j] = max([Ms[i, j].width() for i in range(M.rows)] or [0])
683 
684         # drawing result
685         D = None
686 
687         for i in range(M.rows):
688 
689             D_row = None
690             for j in range(M.cols):
691                 s = Ms[i, j]
692 
693                 # reshape s to maxw
694                 # XXX this should be generalized, and go to stringPict.reshape ?
695                 assert s.width() <= maxw[j]
696 
697                 # hcenter it, +0.5 to the right                        2
698                 # ( it's better to align formula starts for say 0 and r )
699                 # XXX this is not good in all cases -- maybe introduce vbaseline?
700                 wdelta = maxw[j] - s.width()
701                 wleft = wdelta // 2
702                 wright = wdelta - wleft
703 
704                 s = prettyForm(*s.right(' '*wright))
705                 s = prettyForm(*s.left(' '*wleft))
706 
707                 # we don't need vcenter cells -- this is automatically done in
708                 # a pretty way because when their baselines are taking into
709                 # account in .right()
710 
711                 if D_row is None:
712                     D_row = s   # first box in a row
713                     continue
714 
715                 D_row = prettyForm(*D_row.right(' '*hsep))  # h-spacer
716                 D_row = prettyForm(*D_row.right(s))
717 
718             if D is None:
719                 D = D_row       # first row in a picture
720                 continue
721 
722             # v-spacer
723             for _ in range(vsep):
724                 D = prettyForm(*D.below(' '))
725 
726             D = prettyForm(*D.below(D_row))
727 
728         if D is None:
729             D = prettyForm('')  # Empty Matrix
730 
731         return D

899     def _print_BasisDependent(self, expr):

901 
902         if not self._use_unicode:
903             raise NotImplementedError("ASCII pretty printing of BasisDependent is not implemented")
904 
905         if expr == expr.zero:
906             return prettyForm(expr.zero._pretty_form)
907         o1 = []
908         vectstrs = []
909         if isinstance(expr, Vector):
910             items = expr.separate().items()
911         else:
912             items = [(0, expr)]
913         for system, vect in items:
914             inneritems = list(vect.components.items())
915             inneritems.sort(key = lambda x: x[0].__str__())
916             for k, v in inneritems:
917                 #if the coef of the basis vector is 1
918                 #we skip the 1
919                 if v == 1:
920                     o1.append(u"" +
921                               k._pretty_form)
922                 #Same for -1
923                 elif v == -1:
924                     o1.append(u"(-1) " +
925                               k._pretty_form)
926                 #For a general expr
927                 else:
928                     #We always wrap the measure numbers in
929                     #parentheses
930                     arg_str = self._print(
931                         v).parens()[0]
932 
933                     o1.append(arg_str + ' ' + k._pretty_form)
934                 vectstrs.append(k._pretty_form)
935 
936         #outstr = u("").join(o1)
937         if o1[0].startswith(u" + "):
938             o1[0] = o1[0][3:]
939         elif o1[0].startswith(" "):
940             o1[0] = o1[0][1:]
941         #Fixing the newlines
942         lengths = []
943         strs = ['']
944         flag = []
945         for i, partstr in enumerate(o1):
946             flag.append(0)
947             # XXX: What is this hack?
948             if '\n' in partstr:
949                 tempstr = partstr
950                 tempstr = tempstr.replace(vectstrs[i], '')
951                 if u'\N{right parenthesis extension}' in tempstr:   # If scalar is a fraction
952                     for paren in range(len(tempstr)):
953                         flag[i] = 1
954                         if tempstr[paren] == u'\N{right parenthesis extension}':
955                             tempstr = tempstr[:paren] + u'\N{right parenthesis extension}'\
956                                          + ' '  + vectstrs[i] + tempstr[paren + 1:]
957                             break
958                 elif u'\N{RIGHT PARENTHESIS LOWER HOOK}' in tempstr:
959                     flag[i] = 1
960                     tempstr = tempstr.replace(u'\N{RIGHT PARENTHESIS LOWER HOOK}',
961                                         u'\N{RIGHT PARENTHESIS LOWER HOOK}'
962                                         + ' ' + vectstrs[i])
963                 else:
964                     tempstr = tempstr.replace(u'\N{RIGHT PARENTHESIS UPPER HOOK}',
965                                         u'\N{RIGHT PARENTHESIS UPPER HOOK}'
966                                         + ' ' + vectstrs[i])
967                 o1[i] = tempstr
968 
969         o1 = [x.split('\n') for x in o1]
970         n_newlines = max([len(x) for x in o1])  # Width of part in its pretty form
971 
972         if 1 in flag:                           # If there was a fractional scalar
973             for i, parts in enumerate(o1):
974                 if len(parts) == 1:             # If part has no newline
975                     parts.insert(0, ' ' * (len(parts[0])))
976                     flag[i] = 1
977 
978         for i, parts in enumerate(o1):
979             lengths.append(len(parts[flag[i]]))
980             for j in range(n_newlines):
981                 if j+1 <= len(parts):
982                     if j >= len(strs):
983                         strs.append(' ' * (sum(lengths[:-1]) +
984                                            3*(len(lengths)-1)))
985                     if j == flag[i]:
986                         strs[flag[i]] += parts[flag[i]] + ' + '
987                     else:
988                         strs[j] += parts[j] + ' '*(lengths[-1] -
989                                                    len(parts[j])+
990                                                    3)
991                 else:
992                     if j >= len(strs):
993                         strs.append(' ' * (sum(lengths[:-1]) +
994                                            3*(len(lengths)-1)))
995                     strs[j] += ' '*(lengths[-1]+3)
996 
997         return prettyForm(u'\n'.join([s[:-3] for s in strs]))

999     def _print_NDimArray(self, expr):
1000         from sympy import ImmutableMatrix
1001 
1002         if expr.rank() == 0:
1003             return self._print(expr[()])
1004 
1005         level_str = [[]] + [[] for i in range(expr.rank())]
1006         shape_ranges = [list(range(i)) for i in expr.shape]
1007         for outer_i in itertools.product(*shape_ranges):
1008             level_str[-1].append(expr[outer_i])
1009             even = True
1010             for back_outer_i in range(expr.rank()-1, -1, -1):
1011                 if len(level_str[back_outer_i+1]) < expr.shape[back_outer_i]:
1012                     break
1013                 if even:
1014                     level_str[back_outer_i].append(level_str[back_outer_i+1])
1015                 else:
1016                     level_str[back_outer_i].append(ImmutableMatrix(level_str[back_outer_i+1]))
1017                     if len(level_str[back_outer_i + 1]) == 1:
1018                         level_str[back_outer_i][-1] = ImmutableMatrix([[level_str[back_outer_i][-1]]])
1019                 even = not even
1020                 level_str[back_outer_i+1] = []
1021 
1022         out_expr = level_str[0][0]
1023         if expr.rank() % 2 == 1:
1024             out_expr = ImmutableMatrix([out_expr])
1025 
1026         return self._print(out_expr)

1033     def _printer_tensor_indices(self, name, indices, index_map={}):
1034         center = stringPict(name)
1035         top = stringPict(" "*center.width())
1036         bot = stringPict(" "*center.width())
1037 
1038         last_valence = None
1039         prev_map = None
1040 
1041         for i, index in enumerate(indices):
1042             indpic = self._print(index.args[0])
1043             if ((index in index_map) or prev_map) and last_valence == index.is_up:
1044                 if index.is_up:
1045                     top = prettyForm(*stringPict.next(top, ","))
1046                 else:
1047                     bot = prettyForm(*stringPict.next(bot, ","))
1048             if index in index_map:
1049                 indpic = prettyForm(*stringPict.next(indpic, "="))
1050                 indpic = prettyForm(*stringPict.next(indpic, self._print(index_map[index])))
1051                 prev_map = True
1052             else:
1053                 prev_map = False
1054             if index.is_up:
1055                 top = stringPict(*top.right(indpic))
1056                 center = stringPict(*center.right(" "*indpic.width()))
1057                 bot = stringPict(*bot.right(" "*indpic.width()))
1058             else:
1059                 bot = stringPict(*bot.right(indpic))
1060                 center = stringPict(*center.right(" "*indpic.width()))
1061                 top = stringPict(*top.right(" "*indpic.width()))
1062             last_valence = index.is_up
1063 
1064         pict = prettyForm(*center.above(top))
1065         pict = prettyForm(*pict.below(bot))
1066         return pict

1263     def _print_meijerg(self, e):
1264         # FIXME refactor Matrix, Piecewise, and this into a tabular environment
1265 
1266         v = {}
1267         v[(0, 0)] = [self._print(a) for a in e.an]
1268         v[(0, 1)] = [self._print(a) for a in e.aother]
1269         v[(1, 0)] = [self._print(b) for b in e.bm]
1270         v[(1, 1)] = [self._print(b) for b in e.bother]
1271 
1272         P = self._print(e.argument)
1273         P.baseline = P.height()//2
1274 
1275         vp = {}
1276         for idx in v:
1277             vp[idx] = self._hprint_vec(v[idx])
1278 
1279         for i in range(2):
1280             maxw = max(vp[(0, i)].width(), vp[(1, i)].width())
1281             for j in range(2):
1282                 s = vp[(j, i)]
1283                 left = (maxw - s.width()) // 2
1284                 right = maxw - left - s.width()
1285                 s = prettyForm(*s.left(' ' * left))
1286                 s = prettyForm(*s.right(' ' * right))
1287                 vp[(j, i)] = s
1288 
1289         D1 = prettyForm(*vp[(0, 0)].right('  ', vp[(0, 1)]))
1290         D1 = prettyForm(*D1.below(' '))
1291         D2 = prettyForm(*vp[(1, 0)].right('  ', vp[(1, 1)]))
1292         D = prettyForm(*D1.below(D2))
1293 
1294         # make sure that the argument `z' is centred vertically
1295         D.baseline = D.height()//2
1296 
1297         # insert horizontal separator
1298         P = prettyForm(*P.left(' '))
1299         D = prettyForm(*D.right(' '))
1300 
1301         # insert separating `|`
1302         D = self._hprint_vseparator(D, P)
1303 
1304         # add parens
1305         D = prettyForm(*D.parens('(', ')'))
1306 
1307         # create the G symbol
1308         above = D.height()//2 - 1
1309         below = D.height() - above - 1
1310 
1311         sz, t, b, add, img = annotated('G')
1312         F = prettyForm('\n' * (above - t) + img + '\n' * (below - b),
1313                        baseline=above + sz)
1314 
1315         pp = self._print(len(e.ap))
1316         pq = self._print(len(e.bq))
1317         pm = self._print(len(e.bm))
1318         pn = self._print(len(e.an))
1319 
1320         def adjust(p1, p2):
1321             diff = p1.width() - p2.width()
1322             if diff == 0:
1323                 return p1, p2
1324             elif diff > 0:
1325                 return p1, prettyForm(*p2.left(' '*diff))
1326             else:
1327                 return prettyForm(*p1.left(' '*-diff)), p2
1328         pp, pm = adjust(pp, pm)
1329         pq, pn = adjust(pq, pn)
1330         pu = prettyForm(*pm.right(', ', pn))
1331         pl = prettyForm(*pp.right(', ', pq))
1332 
1333         ht = F.baseline - above - 2
1334         if ht > 0:
1335             pu = prettyForm(*pu.below('\n'*ht))
1336         p = prettyForm(*pu.below(pl))
1337 
1338         F.baseline = above
1339         F = prettyForm(*F.right(p))
1340 
1341         F.baseline = above + add
1342 
1343         D = prettyForm(*F.right(' ', D))
1344 
1345         return D

1645     def _print_Mul(self, product):
1646         from sympy.physics.units import Quantity
1647         a = []  # items in the numerator
1648         b = []  # items that are in the denominator (if any)
1649 
1650         if self.order not in ('old', 'none'):
1651             args = product.as_ordered_factors()
1652         else:
1653             args = list(product.args)
1654 
1655         # If quantities are present append them at the back
1656         args = sorted(args, key=lambda x: isinstance(x, Quantity) or
1657                      (isinstance(x, Pow) and isinstance(x.base, Quantity)))
1658 
1659         # Gather terms for numerator/denominator
1660         for item in args:
1661             if item.is_commutative and item.is_Pow and item.exp.is_Rational and item.exp.is_negative:
1662                 if item.exp != -1:
1663                     b.append(Pow(item.base, -item.exp, evaluate=False))
1664                 else:
1665                     b.append(Pow(item.base, -item.exp))
1666             elif item.is_Rational and item is not S.Infinity:
1667                 if item.p != 1:
1668                     a.append( Rational(item.p) )
1669                 if item.q != 1:
1670                     b.append( Rational(item.q) )
1671             else:
1672                 a.append(item)
1673 
1674         from sympy import Integral, Piecewise, Product, Sum
1675 
1676         # Convert to pretty forms. Add parens to Add instances if there
1677         # is more than one term in the numer/denom
1678         for i in range(0, len(a)):
1679             if (a[i].is_Add and len(a) > 1) or (i != len(a) - 1 and
1680                     isinstance(a[i], (Integral, Piecewise, Product, Sum))):
1681                 a[i] = prettyForm(*self._print(a[i]).parens())
1682             elif a[i].is_Relational:
1683                 a[i] = prettyForm(*self._print(a[i]).parens())
1684             else:
1685                 a[i] = self._print(a[i])
1686 
1687         for i in range(0, len(b)):
1688             if (b[i].is_Add and len(b) > 1) or (i != len(b) - 1 and
1689                     isinstance(b[i], (Integral, Piecewise, Product, Sum))):
1690                 b[i] = prettyForm(*self._print(b[i]).parens())
1691             else:
1692                 b[i] = self._print(b[i])
1693 
1694         # Construct a pretty form
1695         if len(b) == 0:
1696             return prettyForm.__mul__(*a)
1697         else:
1698             if len(a) == 0:
1699                 a.append( self._print(S.One) )
1700             return prettyForm.__mul__(*a)/prettyForm.__mul__(*b)

1702     # A helper function for _print_Pow to print x**(1/n)
1703     def _print_nth_root(self, base, expt):
1704         bpretty = self._print(base)
1705 
1706         # In very simple cases, use a single-char root sign
1707         if (self._settings['use_unicode_sqrt_char'] and self._use_unicode
1708             and expt is S.Half and bpretty.height() == 1
1709             and (bpretty.width() == 1
1710                  or (base.is_Integer and base.is_nonnegative))):
1711             return prettyForm(*bpretty.left(u'\N{SQUARE ROOT}'))
1712 
1713         # Construct root sign, start with the \/ shape
1714         _zZ = xobj('/', 1)
1715         rootsign = xobj('\\', 1) + _zZ
1716         # Make exponent number to put above it
1717         if isinstance(expt, Rational):
1718             exp = str(expt.q)
1719             if exp == '2':
1720                 exp = ''
1721         else:
1722             exp = str(expt.args[0])
1723         exp = exp.ljust(2)
1724         if len(exp) > 2:
1725             rootsign = ' '*(len(exp) - 2) + rootsign
1726         # Stack the exponent
1727         rootsign = stringPict(exp + '\n' + rootsign)
1728         rootsign.baseline = 0
1729         # Diagonal: length is one less than height of base
1730         linelength = bpretty.height() - 1
1731         diagonal = stringPict('\n'.join(
1732             ' '*(linelength - i - 1) + _zZ + ' '*i
1733             for i in range(linelength)
1734         ))
1735         # Put baseline just below lowest line: next to exp
1736         diagonal.baseline = linelength - 1
1737         # Make the root symbol
1738         rootsign = prettyForm(*rootsign.right(diagonal))
1739         # Det the baseline to match contents to fix the height
1740         # but if the height of bpretty is one, the rootsign must be one higher
1741         rootsign.baseline = max(1, bpretty.baseline)
1742         #build result
1743         s = prettyForm(hobj('_', 2 + bpretty.width()))
1744         s = prettyForm(*bpretty.above(s))
1745         s = prettyForm(*s.left(rootsign))
1746         return s

1748     def _print_Pow(self, power):

1754             n, d = fraction(e)

1759 
1760         if b.is_Relational:
1761             return prettyForm(*self._print(b).parens()).__pow__(self._print(e))
1762 
1763         return self._print(b)**self._print(e)

problem_statement:
"TypeError: cannot pickle" when applying | operator to a Q object
Description
	 
		(last modified by Daniel Izquierdo)
	 
Using a reference to a non-pickleable type of object such as dict_keys in a Q object makes the | operator fail:
>>> from django.db.models import Q
>>> Q(x__in={}.keys())
<Q: (AND: ('x__in', dict_keys([])))>
>>> Q() | Q(x__in={}.keys())
Traceback (most recent call last):
...
TypeError: cannot pickle 'dict_keys' object
Even though this particular example could be solved by doing Q() | Q(x__in={}) it still feels like using .keys() should work.
I can work on a patch if there's agreement that this should not crash.

model = SVR(C=316.227766017, cache_size=200, coef0=0.0, degree=3, epsilon=0.1,

35 
36     # XXX we could do preallocation of coef but
37     # would have to take care in the sparse case
38     coef = []
39     sv_locs = np.cumsum(np.hstack([[0], n_support]))
40     for class1 in range(n_class):
41         # SVs for class1:
42         sv1 = support_vectors[sv_locs[class1]:sv_locs[class1 + 1], :]
43         for class2 in range(class1 + 1, n_class):
44             # SVs for class1:
45             sv2 = support_vectors[sv_locs[class2]:sv_locs[class2 + 1], :]
46 
47             # dual coef for class1 SVs:
48             alpha1 = dual_coef[class2 - 1, sv_locs[class1]:sv_locs[class1 + 1]]
49             # dual coef for class2 SVs:
50             alpha2 = dual_coef[class1, sv_locs[class2]:sv_locs[class2 + 1]]
51             # build weight for class1 vs class2
52 
53             coef.append(safe_sparse_dot(alpha1, sv1)
54                         + safe_sparse_dot(alpha2, sv2))
55     return coef
56

58 class BaseLibSVM(BaseEstimator, metaclass=ABCMeta):
59     """Base class for estimators that use libsvm as backing library
60 
61     This implements support vector machine classification and regression.
62 
63     Parameter documentation is in the derived `SVC` class.
64     """
65 
66     # The order of these must match the integer values in LibSVM.
67     # XXX These are actually the same in the dense case. Need to factor
68     # this out.
69     _sparse_kernels = ["linear", "poly", "rbf", "sigmoid", "precomputed"]
70 
71     @abstractmethod
72     def __init__(self, kernel, degree, gamma, coef0,
73                  tol, C, nu, epsilon, shrinking, probability, cache_size,
74                  class_weight, verbose, max_iter, random_state):
75 
76         if self._impl not in LIBSVM_IMPL:  # pragma: no cover
77             raise ValueError("impl should be one of %s, %s was given" % (
78                 LIBSVM_IMPL, self._impl))
79 
80         if gamma == 0:
81             msg = ("The gamma value of 0.0 is invalid. Use 'auto' to set"
82                    " gamma to a value of 1 / n_features.")
83             raise ValueError(msg)
84 
85         self.kernel = kernel
86         self.degree = degree
87         self.gamma = gamma
88         self.coef0 = coef0
89         self.tol = tol
90         self.C = C
91         self.nu = nu
92         self.epsilon = epsilon
93         self.shrinking = shrinking
94         self.probability = probability
95         self.cache_size = cache_size
96         self.class_weight = class_weight
97         self.verbose = verbose
98         self.max_iter = max_iter
99         self.random_state = random_state
100 
101     @property
102     def _pairwise(self):
103         # Used by cross_val_score.
104         return self.kernel == "precomputed"
105 
106     def fit(self, X, y, sample_weight=None):
107         """Fit the SVM model according to the given training data.
108 
109         Parameters
110         ----------
111         X : {array-like, sparse matrix}, shape (n_samples, n_features)
112             Training vectors, where n_samples is the number of samples
113             and n_features is the number of features.
114             For kernel="precomputed", the expected shape of X is
115             (n_samples, n_samples).
116 
117         y : array-like, shape (n_samples,)
118             Target values (class labels in classification, real numbers in
119             regression)
120 
121         sample_weight : array-like, shape (n_samples,)
122             Per-sample weights. Rescale C per sample. Higher weights
123             force the classifier to put more emphasis on these points.
124 
125         Returns
126         -------
127         self : object
128 
129         Notes
130         -----
131         If X and y are not C-ordered and contiguous arrays of np.float64 and
132         X is not a scipy.sparse.csr_matrix, X and/or y may be copied.
133 
134         If X is a dense array, then the other methods will not support sparse
135         matrices as input.
136         """
137 
138         rnd = check_random_state(self.random_state)
139 
140         sparse = sp.isspmatrix(X)
141         if sparse and self.kernel == "precomputed":
142             raise TypeError("Sparse precomputed kernels are not supported.")
143         self._sparse = sparse and not callable(self.kernel)
144 
145         X, y = check_X_y(X, y, dtype=np.float64,
146                          order='C', accept_sparse='csr',
147                          accept_large_sparse=False)
148         y = self._validate_targets(y)
149 
150         sample_weight = np.asarray([]
151                                    if sample_weight is None
152                                    else sample_weight, dtype=np.float64)
153         solver_type = LIBSVM_IMPL.index(self._impl)
154 
155         # input validation
156         if solver_type != 2 and X.shape[0] != y.shape[0]:
157             raise ValueError("X and y have incompatible shapes.\n" +
158                              "X has %s samples, but y has %s." %
159                              (X.shape[0], y.shape[0]))
160 
161         if self.kernel == "precomputed" and X.shape[0] != X.shape[1]:
162             raise ValueError("Precomputed matrix must be a square matrix."
163                              " Input is a {}x{} matrix."
164                              .format(X.shape[0], X.shape[1]))
165 
166         if sample_weight.shape[0] > 0 and sample_weight.shape[0] != X.shape[0]:
167             raise ValueError("sample_weight and X have incompatible shapes: "
168                              "%r vs %r\n"
169                              "Note: Sparse matrices cannot be indexed w/"
170                              "boolean masks (use `indices=True` in CV)."
171                              % (sample_weight.shape, X.shape))
172 
173         if isinstance(self.gamma, str):
174             if self.gamma == 'scale':
175                 # var = E[X^2] - E[X]^2 if sparse
176                 X_var = ((X.multiply(X)).mean() - (X.mean()) ** 2
177                          if sparse else X.var())
178                 self._gamma = 1.0 / (X.shape[1] * X_var) if X_var != 0 else 1.0
179             elif self.gamma == 'auto':
180                 self._gamma = 1.0 / X.shape[1]
181             else:
182                 raise ValueError(
183                     "When 'gamma' is a string, it should be either 'scale' or "
184                     "'auto'. Got '{}' instead.".format(self.gamma)
185                 )
186         else:
187             self._gamma = self.gamma
188 
189         kernel = self.kernel
190         if callable(kernel):
191             kernel = 'precomputed'
192 
193         fit = self._sparse_fit if self._sparse else self._dense_fit
194         if self.verbose:  # pragma: no cover
195             print('[LibSVM]', end='')
196 
197         seed = rnd.randint(np.iinfo('i').max)
198         fit(X, y, sample_weight, solver_type, kernel, random_seed=seed)
199         # see comment on the other call to np.iinfo in this file
200 
201         self.shape_fit_ = X.shape
202 
203         # In binary case, we need to flip the sign of coef, intercept and
204         # decision function. Use self._intercept_ and self._dual_coef_
205         # internally.
206         self._intercept_ = self.intercept_.copy()
207         self._dual_coef_ = self.dual_coef_
208         if self._impl in ['c_svc', 'nu_svc'] and len(self.classes_) == 2:
209             self.intercept_ *= -1
210             self.dual_coef_ = -self.dual_coef_
211 
212         return self
213 
214     def _validate_targets(self, y):
215         """Validation of y and class_weight.
216 
217         Default implementation for SVR and one-class; overridden in BaseSVC.
218         """
219         # XXX this is ugly.
220         # Regression models should not have a class_weight_ attribute.
221         self.class_weight_ = np.empty(0)
222         return column_or_1d(y, warn=True).astype(np.float64, copy=False)
223 
224     def _warn_from_fit_status(self):
225         assert self.fit_status_ in (0, 1)
226         if self.fit_status_ == 1:
227             warnings.warn('Solver terminated early (max_iter=%i).'
228                           '  Consider pre-processing your data with'
229                           ' StandardScaler or MinMaxScaler.'
230                           % self.max_iter, ConvergenceWarning)
231 
232     def _dense_fit(self, X, y, sample_weight, solver_type, kernel,
233                    random_seed):
234         if callable(self.kernel):
235             # you must store a reference to X to compute the kernel in predict
236             # TODO: add keyword copy to copy on demand
237             self.__Xfit = X
238             X = self._compute_kernel(X)
239 
240             if X.shape[0] != X.shape[1]:
241                 raise ValueError("X.shape[0] should be equal to X.shape[1]")
242 
243         libsvm.set_verbosity_wrap(self.verbose)
244 
245         # we don't pass **self.get_params() to allow subclasses to
246         # add other parameters to __init__
247         self.support_, self.support_vectors_, self._n_support, \
248             self.dual_coef_, self.intercept_, self.probA_, \
249             self.probB_, self.fit_status_ = libsvm.fit(
250                 X, y,
251                 svm_type=solver_type, sample_weight=sample_weight,
252                 class_weight=self.class_weight_, kernel=kernel, C=self.C,
253                 nu=self.nu, probability=self.probability, degree=self.degree,
254                 shrinking=self.shrinking, tol=self.tol,
255                 cache_size=self.cache_size, coef0=self.coef0,
256                 gamma=self._gamma, epsilon=self.epsilon,
257                 max_iter=self.max_iter, random_seed=random_seed)
258 
259         self._warn_from_fit_status()
260 
261     def _sparse_fit(self, X, y, sample_weight, solver_type, kernel,
262                     random_seed):
263         X.data = np.asarray(X.data, dtype=np.float64, order='C')
264         X.sort_indices()
265 
266         kernel_type = self._sparse_kernels.index(kernel)
267 
268         libsvm_sparse.set_verbosity_wrap(self.verbose)
269 
270         self.support_, self.support_vectors_, dual_coef_data, \
271             self.intercept_, self._n_support, \
272             self.probA_, self.probB_, self.fit_status_ = \
273             libsvm_sparse.libsvm_sparse_train(
274                 X.shape[1], X.data, X.indices, X.indptr, y, solver_type,
275                 kernel_type, self.degree, self._gamma, self.coef0, self.tol,
276                 self.C, self.class_weight_,
277                 sample_weight, self.nu, self.cache_size, self.epsilon,
278                 int(self.shrinking), int(self.probability), self.max_iter,
279                 random_seed)
280 
281         self._warn_from_fit_status()
282 
283         if hasattr(self, "classes_"):
284             n_class = len(self.classes_) - 1
285         else:  # regression
286             n_class = 1
287         n_SV = self.support_vectors_.shape[0]
288 
289         dual_coef_indices = np.tile(np.arange(n_SV), n_class)
290         dual_coef_indptr = np.arange(0, dual_coef_indices.size + 1,
291                                      dual_coef_indices.size / n_class)
292         self.dual_coef_ = sp.csr_matrix(
293             (dual_coef_data, dual_coef_indices, dual_coef_indptr),
294             (n_class, n_SV))
295 
296     def predict(self, X):
297         """Perform regression on samples in X.
298 
299         For an one-class model, +1 (inlier) or -1 (outlier) is returned.
300 
301         Parameters
302         ----------
303         X : {array-like, sparse matrix}, shape (n_samples, n_features)
304             For kernel="precomputed", the expected shape of X is
305             (n_samples_test, n_samples_train).
306 
307         Returns
308         -------
309         y_pred : array, shape (n_samples,)
310         """
311         X = self._validate_for_predict(X)
312         predict = self._sparse_predict if self._sparse else self._dense_predict
313         return predict(X)
314 
315     def _dense_predict(self, X):
316         X = self._compute_kernel(X)
317         if X.ndim == 1:
318             X = check_array(X, order='C', accept_large_sparse=False)
319 
320         kernel = self.kernel
321         if callable(self.kernel):
322             kernel = 'precomputed'
323             if X.shape[1] != self.shape_fit_[0]:
324                 raise ValueError("X.shape[1] = %d should be equal to %d, "
325                                  "the number of samples at training time" %
326                                  (X.shape[1], self.shape_fit_[0]))
327 
328         svm_type = LIBSVM_IMPL.index(self._impl)
329 
330         return libsvm.predict(
331             X, self.support_, self.support_vectors_, self._n_support,
332             self._dual_coef_, self._intercept_,
333             self.probA_, self.probB_, svm_type=svm_type, kernel=kernel,
334             degree=self.degree, coef0=self.coef0, gamma=self._gamma,
335             cache_size=self.cache_size)
336 
337     def _sparse_predict(self, X):
338         # Precondition: X is a csr_matrix of dtype np.float64.
339         kernel = self.kernel
340         if callable(kernel):
341             kernel = 'precomputed'
342 
343         kernel_type = self._sparse_kernels.index(kernel)
344 
345         C = 0.0  # C is not useful here
346 
347         return libsvm_sparse.libsvm_sparse_predict(
348             X.data, X.indices, X.indptr,
349             self.support_vectors_.data,
350             self.support_vectors_.indices,
351             self.support_vectors_.indptr,
352             self._dual_coef_.data, self._intercept_,
353             LIBSVM_IMPL.index(self._impl), kernel_type,
354             self.degree, self._gamma, self.coef0, self.tol,
355             C, self.class_weight_,
356             self.nu, self.epsilon, self.shrinking,
357             self.probability, self._n_support,
358             self.probA_, self.probB_)
359 
360     def _compute_kernel(self, X):
361         """Return the data transformed by a callable kernel"""
362         if callable(self.kernel):
363             # in the case of precomputed kernel given as a function, we
364             # have to compute explicitly the kernel matrix
365             kernel = self.kernel(X, self.__Xfit)
366             if sp.issparse(kernel):
367                 kernel = kernel.toarray()
368             X = np.asarray(kernel, dtype=np.float64, order='C')
369         return X
370 
371     def _decision_function(self, X):
372         """Evaluates the decision function for the samples in X.
373 
374         Parameters
375         ----------
376         X : array-like, shape (n_samples, n_features)
377 
378         Returns
379         -------
380         X : array-like, shape (n_samples, n_class * (n_class-1) / 2)
381             Returns the decision function of the sample for each class
382             in the model.
383         """
384         # NOTE: _validate_for_predict contains check for is_fitted
385         # hence must be placed before any other attributes are used.
386         X = self._validate_for_predict(X)
387         X = self._compute_kernel(X)
388 
389         if self._sparse:
390             dec_func = self._sparse_decision_function(X)
391         else:
392             dec_func = self._dense_decision_function(X)
393 
394         # In binary case, we need to flip the sign of coef, intercept and
395         # decision function.
396         if self._impl in ['c_svc', 'nu_svc'] and len(self.classes_) == 2:
397             return -dec_func.ravel()
398 
399         return dec_func
400 
401     def _dense_decision_function(self, X):
402         X = check_array(X, dtype=np.float64, order="C",
403                         accept_large_sparse=False)
404 
405         kernel = self.kernel
406         if callable(kernel):
407             kernel = 'precomputed'
408 
409         return libsvm.decision_function(
410             X, self.support_, self.support_vectors_, self._n_support,
411             self._dual_coef_, self._intercept_,
412             self.probA_, self.probB_,
413             svm_type=LIBSVM_IMPL.index(self._impl),
414             kernel=kernel, degree=self.degree, cache_size=self.cache_size,
415             coef0=self.coef0, gamma=self._gamma)
416 
417     def _sparse_decision_function(self, X):
418         X.data = np.asarray(X.data, dtype=np.float64, order='C')
419 
420         kernel = self.kernel
421         if hasattr(kernel, '__call__'):
422             kernel = 'precomputed'
423 
424         kernel_type = self._sparse_kernels.index(kernel)
425 
426         return libsvm_sparse.libsvm_sparse_decision_function(
427             X.data, X.indices, X.indptr,
428             self.support_vectors_.data,
429             self.support_vectors_.indices,
430             self.support_vectors_.indptr,
431             self._dual_coef_.data, self._intercept_,
432             LIBSVM_IMPL.index(self._impl), kernel_type,
433             self.degree, self._gamma, self.coef0, self.tol,
434             self.C, self.class_weight_,
435             self.nu, self.epsilon, self.shrinking,
436             self.probability, self._n_support,
437             self.probA_, self.probB_)
438 
439     def _validate_for_predict(self, X):
440         check_is_fitted(self)
441 
442         X = check_array(X, accept_sparse='csr', dtype=np.float64, order="C",
443                         accept_large_sparse=False)
444         if self._sparse and not sp.isspmatrix(X):
445             X = sp.csr_matrix(X)
446         if self._sparse:
447             X.sort_indices()
448 
449         if sp.issparse(X) and not self._sparse and not callable(self.kernel):
450             raise ValueError(
451                 "cannot use sparse input in %r trained on dense data"
452                 % type(self).__name__)
453         n_samples, n_features = X.shape
454 
455         if self.kernel == "precomputed":
456             if X.shape[1] != self.shape_fit_[0]:
457                 raise ValueError("X.shape[1] = %d should be equal to %d, "
458                                  "the number of samples at training time" %
459                                  (X.shape[1], self.shape_fit_[0]))
460         elif n_features != self.shape_fit_[1]:
461             raise ValueError("X.shape[1] = %d should be equal to %d, "
462                              "the number of features at training time" %
463                              (n_features, self.shape_fit_[1]))
464         return X
465 
466     @property
467     def coef_(self):
468         if self.kernel != 'linear':
469             raise AttributeError('coef_ is only available when using a '
470                                  'linear kernel')
471 
472         coef = self._get_coef()
473 
474         # coef_ being a read-only property, it's better to mark the value as
475         # immutable to avoid hiding potential bugs for the unsuspecting user.
476         if sp.issparse(coef):
477             # sparse matrix do not have global flags
478             coef.data.flags.writeable = False
479         else:
480             # regular dense array
481             coef.flags.writeable = False
482         return coef
483 
484     def _get_coef(self):
485         return safe_sparse_dot(self._dual_coef_, self.support_vectors_)
486 
487     @property
488     def n_support_(self):
489         try:
490             check_is_fitted(self)
491         except NotFittedError:
492             raise AttributeError
493 
494         svm_type = LIBSVM_IMPL.index(self._impl)
495         if svm_type in (0, 1):
496             return self._n_support
497         else:
498             # SVR and OneClass
499             # _n_support has size 2, we make it size 1
500             return np.array([self._n_support[0]])
501

503 class BaseSVC(ClassifierMixin, BaseLibSVM, metaclass=ABCMeta):
504     """ABC for LibSVM-based classifiers."""
505     @abstractmethod
506     def __init__(self, kernel, degree, gamma, coef0, tol, C, nu,
507                  shrinking, probability, cache_size, class_weight, verbose,
508                  max_iter, decision_function_shape, random_state,
509                  break_ties):
510         self.decision_function_shape = decision_function_shape
511         self.break_ties = break_ties
512         super().__init__(
513             kernel=kernel, degree=degree, gamma=gamma,
514             coef0=coef0, tol=tol, C=C, nu=nu, epsilon=0., shrinking=shrinking,
515             probability=probability, cache_size=cache_size,
516             class_weight=class_weight, verbose=verbose, max_iter=max_iter,
517             random_state=random_state)
518 
519     def _validate_targets(self, y):
520         y_ = column_or_1d(y, warn=True)
521         check_classification_targets(y)
522         cls, y = np.unique(y_, return_inverse=True)
523         self.class_weight_ = compute_class_weight(self.class_weight, cls, y_)
524         if len(cls) < 2:
525             raise ValueError(
526                 "The number of classes has to be greater than one; got %d"
527                 " class" % len(cls))
528 
529         self.classes_ = cls
530 
531         return np.asarray(y, dtype=np.float64, order='C')
532 
533     def decision_function(self, X):
534         """Evaluates the decision function for the samples in X.
535 
536         Parameters
537         ----------
538         X : array-like, shape (n_samples, n_features)
539 
540         Returns
541         -------
542         X : array-like, shape (n_samples, n_classes * (n_classes-1) / 2)
543             Returns the decision function of the sample for each class
544             in the model.
545             If decision_function_shape='ovr', the shape is (n_samples,
546             n_classes).
547 
548         Notes
549         -----
550         If decision_function_shape='ovo', the function values are proportional
551         to the distance of the samples X to the separating hyperplane. If the
552         exact distances are required, divide the function values by the norm of
553         the weight vector (``coef_``). See also `this question
554         <https://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/14876/
555         interpreting-distance-from-hyperplane-in-svm>`_ for further details.
556         If decision_function_shape='ovr', the decision function is a monotonic
557         transformation of ovo decision function.
558         """
559         dec = self._decision_function(X)
560         if self.decision_function_shape == 'ovr' and len(self.classes_) > 2:
561             return _ovr_decision_function(dec < 0, -dec, len(self.classes_))
562         return dec
563 
564     def predict(self, X):
565         """Perform classification on samples in X.
566 
567         For an one-class model, +1 or -1 is returned.
568 
569         Parameters
570         ----------
571         X : {array-like, sparse matrix}, shape (n_samples, n_features)
572             For kernel="precomputed", the expected shape of X is
573             [n_samples_test, n_samples_train]
574 
575         Returns
576         -------
577         y_pred : array, shape (n_samples,)
578             Class labels for samples in X.
579         """
580         check_is_fitted(self)
581         if self.break_ties and self.decision_function_shape == 'ovo':
582             raise ValueError("break_ties must be False when "
583                              "decision_function_shape is 'ovo'")
584 
585         if (self.break_ties
586                 and self.decision_function_shape == 'ovr'
587                 and len(self.classes_) > 2):
588             y = np.argmax(self.decision_function(X), axis=1)
589         else:
590             y = super().predict(X)
591         return self.classes_.take(np.asarray(y, dtype=np.intp))
592 
593     # Hacky way of getting predict_proba to raise an AttributeError when
594     # probability=False using properties. Do not use this in new code; when
595     # probabilities are not available depending on a setting, introduce two
596     # estimators.
597     def _check_proba(self):
598         if not self.probability:
599             raise AttributeError("predict_proba is not available when "
600                                  " probability=False")
601         if self._impl not in ('c_svc', 'nu_svc'):
602             raise AttributeError("predict_proba only implemented for SVC"
603                                  " and NuSVC")
604 
605     @property
606     def predict_proba(self):
607         """Compute probabilities of possible outcomes for samples in X.
608 
609         The model need to have probability information computed at training
610         time: fit with attribute `probability` set to True.
611 
612         Parameters
613         ----------
614         X : array-like, shape (n_samples, n_features)
615             For kernel="precomputed", the expected shape of X is
616             [n_samples_test, n_samples_train]
617 
618         Returns
619         -------
620         T : array-like, shape (n_samples, n_classes)
621             Returns the probability of the sample for each class in
622             the model. The columns correspond to the classes in sorted
623             order, as they appear in the attribute :term:`classes_`.
624 
625         Notes
626         -----
627         The probability model is created using cross validation, so
628         the results can be slightly different than those obtained by
629         predict. Also, it will produce meaningless results on very small
630         datasets.
631         """
632         self._check_proba()
633         return self._predict_proba
634 
635     def _predict_proba(self, X):
636         X = self._validate_for_predict(X)
637         if self.probA_.size == 0 or self.probB_.size == 0:
638             raise NotFittedError("predict_proba is not available when fitted "
639                                  "with probability=False")
640         pred_proba = (self._sparse_predict_proba
641                       if self._sparse else self._dense_predict_proba)
642         return pred_proba(X)
643 
644     @property
645     def predict_log_proba(self):
646         """Compute log probabilities of possible outcomes for samples in X.
647 
648         The model need to have probability information computed at training
649         time: fit with attribute `probability` set to True.
650

<issue>
Sum of the elements of an identity matrix is zero
I think this is a bug.

I created a matrix by M.T * M under an assumption that M is orthogonal.  SymPy successfully recognized that the result is an identity matrix.  I tested its identity-ness by element-wise, queries, and sum of the diagonal elements and received expected results.

However, when I attempt to evaluate the total sum of the elements the result was 0 while 'n' is expected.

```
from sympy import *
from sympy import Q as Query

n = Symbol('n', integer=True, positive=True)
i, j = symbols('i j', integer=True)
M = MatrixSymbol('M', n, n)

e = None
with assuming(Query.orthogonal(M)):
    e = refine((M.T * M).doit())

# Correct: M.T * M is an identity matrix.
print(e, e[0, 0], e[0, 1], e[1, 0], e[1, 1])

# Correct: The output is True True
print(ask(Query.diagonal(e)), ask(Query.integer_elements(e)))

# Correct: The sum of the diagonal elements is n
print(Sum(e[i, i], (i, 0, n-1)).doit())

# So far so good
# Total sum of the elements is expected to be 'n' but the answer is 0!
print(Sum(Sum(e[i, j], (i, 0, n-1)), (j, 0, n-1)).doit())
```

</issue>

179 Brief History

182 SymPy was started by Ondřej Čertík in 2005, he wrote some code during the
183 summer, then he wrote some more code during the summer 2006. In February 2007,
184 Fabian Pedregosa joined the project and helped fixed many things, contributed
185 documentation and made it alive again. 5 students (Mateusz Paprocki, Brian
186 Jorgensen, Jason Gedge, Robert Schwarz and Chris Wu) improved SymPy incredibly
187 during the summer 2007 as part of the Google Summer of Code. Pearu Peterson
188 joined the development during the summer 2007 and he has made SymPy much more
189 competitive by rewriting the core from scratch, that has made it from 10x to
190 100x faster. Jurjen N.E. Bos has contributed pretty printing and other patches.
191 Fredrik Johansson has written mpmath and contributed a lot of patches.

193 SymPy has participated in every Google Summer of Code since 2007. You can see

195 Each year has improved SymPy by bounds. Most of SymPy's development has come
196 from Google Summer of Code students.

198 In 2011, Ondřej Čertík stepped down as lead developer, with Aaron Meurer, who

problem_statement:
Sum of the elements of an identity matrix is zero
I think this is a bug.

I created a matrix by M.T * M under an assumption that M is orthogonal.  SymPy successfully recognized that the result is an identity matrix.  I tested its identity-ness by element-wise, queries, and sum of the diagonal elements and received expected results.

However, when I attempt to evaluate the total sum of the elements the result was 0 while 'n' is expected.

```
from sympy import *
from sympy import Q as Query

n = Symbol('n', integer=True, positive=True)
i, j = symbols('i j', integer=True)
M = MatrixSymbol('M', n, n)

e = None
with assuming(Query.orthogonal(M)):
    e = refine((M.T * M).doit())

# Correct: M.T * M is an identity matrix.
print(e, e[0, 0], e[0, 1], e[1, 0], e[1, 1])

# Correct: The output is True True
print(ask(Query.diagonal(e)), ask(Query.integer_elements(e)))

# Correct: The sum of the diagonal elements is n
print(Sum(e[i, i], (i, 0, n-1)).doit())

# So far so good
# Total sum of the elements is expected to be 'n' but the answer is 0!
print(Sum(Sum(e[i, j], (i, 0, n-1)), (j, 0, n-1)).doit())
```

[Bug]: get_backend() clears figures from Gcf.figs if they were created under rc_context
### Bug summary

calling `matplotlib.get_backend()` removes all figures from `Gcf` if the *first* figure in `Gcf.figs` was created in an `rc_context`.

### Code for reproduction

```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib import get_backend, rc_context

# fig1 = plt.figure()  # <- UNCOMMENT THIS LINE AND IT WILL WORK
# plt.ion()            # <- ALTERNATIVELY, UNCOMMENT THIS LINE AND IT WILL ALSO WORK
with rc_context():
    fig2 = plt.figure()
before = f'{id(plt._pylab_helpers.Gcf)} {plt._pylab_helpers.Gcf.figs!r}'
get_backend()
after = f'{id(plt._pylab_helpers.Gcf)} {plt._pylab_helpers.Gcf.figs!r}'

assert before == after, '\n' + before + '\n' + after
```


### Actual outcome

```
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
AssertionError                            Traceback (most recent call last)
<ipython-input-1-fa4d099aa289> in <cell line: 11>()
      9 after = f'{id(plt._pylab_helpers.Gcf)} {plt._pylab_helpers.Gcf.figs!r}'
     10 
---> 11 assert before == after, '\n' + before + '\n' + after

94453354309744 OrderedDict([(1, <matplotlib.backends.backend_qt.FigureManagerQT object at 0x7fb33e26c220>)])
94453354309744 OrderedDict()
```

### Expected outcome

The figure should not be missing from `Gcf`.  Consequences of this are, e.g, `plt.close(fig2)` doesn't work because `Gcf.destroy_fig()` can't find it.

### Additional information

_No response_

Xubuntu

QtAgg

Python 3.10.4

n/a

conda

141 def _parse_to_version_info(version_str):
142     """
143     Parse a version string to a namedtuple analogous to sys.version_info.
144 
145     See:
146     https://packaging.pypa.io/en/latest/version.html#packaging.version.parse
147     https://docs.python.org/3/library/sys.html#sys.version_info
148     """
149     v = parse_version(version_str)
150     if v.pre is None and v.post is None and v.dev is None:
151         return _VersionInfo(v.major, v.minor, v.micro, 'final', 0)
152     elif v.dev is not None:
153         return _VersionInfo(v.major, v.minor, v.micro, 'alpha', v.dev)
154     elif v.pre is not None:
155         releaselevel = {
156             'a': 'alpha',
157             'b': 'beta',
158             'rc': 'candidate'}.get(v.pre[0], 'alpha')
159         return _VersionInfo(v.major, v.minor, v.micro, releaselevel, v.pre[1])
160     else:
161         # fallback for v.post: guess-next-dev scheme from setuptools_scm
162         return _VersionInfo(v.major, v.minor, v.micro + 1, 'alpha', v.post)

165 def _get_version():
166     """Return the version string used for __version__."""
167     # Only shell out to a git subprocess if really needed, i.e. when we are in
168     # a matplotlib git repo but not in a shallow clone, such as those used by
169     # CI, as the latter would trigger a warning from setuptools_scm.
170     root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
171     if ((root / ".matplotlib-repo").exists()
172             and (root / ".git").exists()
173             and not (root / ".git/shallow").exists()):
174         import setuptools_scm
175         return setuptools_scm.get_version(
176             root=root,
177             version_scheme="release-branch-semver",
178             local_scheme="node-and-date",
179             fallback_version=_version.version,
180         )
181     else:  # Get the version from the _version.py setuptools_scm file.
182         return _version.version

256 def _logged_cached(fmt, func=None):
257     """
258     Decorator that logs a function's return value, and memoizes that value.
259 
260     After ::
261 
262         @_logged_cached(fmt)
263         def func(): ...
264 
265     the first call to *func* will log its return value at the DEBUG level using
266     %-format string *fmt*, and memoize it; later calls to *func* will directly
267     return that value.
268     """
269     if func is None:  # Return the actual decorator.
270         return functools.partial(_logged_cached, fmt)
271 
272     called = False
273     ret = None
274 
275     @functools.wraps(func)
276     def wrapper(**kwargs):
277         nonlocal called, ret
278         if not called:
279             ret = func(**kwargs)
280             called = True
281             _log.debug(fmt, ret)
282         return ret
283 
284     return wrapper

298 @functools.lru_cache()
299 def _get_executable_info(name):
300     """
301     Get the version of some executable that Matplotlib optionally depends on.
302 
303     .. warning::
304        The list of executables that this function supports is set according to
305        Matplotlib's internal needs, and may change without notice.
306 
307     Parameters
308     ----------
309     name : str
310         The executable to query.  The following values are currently supported:
311         "dvipng", "gs", "inkscape", "magick", "pdftocairo", "pdftops".  This
312         list is subject to change without notice.
313 
314     Returns
315     -------
316     tuple
317         A namedtuple with fields ``executable`` (`str`) and ``version``
318         (`packaging.Version`, or ``None`` if the version cannot be determined).
319 
320     Raises
321     ------
322     ExecutableNotFoundError
323         If the executable is not found or older than the oldest version
324         supported by Matplotlib.  For debugging purposes, it is also
325         possible to "hide" an executable from Matplotlib by adding it to the
326         :envvar:`_MPLHIDEEXECUTABLES` environment variable (a comma-separated
327         list), which must be set prior to any calls to this function.
328     ValueError
329         If the executable is not one that we know how to query.
330     """
331 
332     def impl(args, regex, min_ver=None, ignore_exit_code=False):
333         # Execute the subprocess specified by args; capture stdout and stderr.
334         # Search for a regex match in the output; if the match succeeds, the
335         # first group of the match is the version.
336         # Return an _ExecInfo if the executable exists, and has a version of
337         # at least min_ver (if set); else, raise ExecutableNotFoundError.
338         try:
339             output = subprocess.check_output(
340                 args, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
341                 universal_newlines=True, errors="replace")
342         except subprocess.CalledProcessError as _cpe:
343             if ignore_exit_code:
344                 output = _cpe.output
345             else:
346                 raise ExecutableNotFoundError(str(_cpe)) from _cpe
347         except OSError as _ose:
348             raise ExecutableNotFoundError(str(_ose)) from _ose
349         match = re.search(regex, output)
350         if match:
351             raw_version = match.group(1)
352             version = parse_version(raw_version)
353             if min_ver is not None and version < parse_version(min_ver):
354                 raise ExecutableNotFoundError(
355                     f"You have {args[0]} version {version} but the minimum "
356                     f"version supported by Matplotlib is {min_ver}")
357             return _ExecInfo(args[0], raw_version, version)
358         else:
359             raise ExecutableNotFoundError(
360                 f"Failed to determine the version of {args[0]} from "
361                 f"{' '.join(args)}, which output {output}")
362 
363     if name in os.environ.get("_MPLHIDEEXECUTABLES", "").split(","):
364         raise ExecutableNotFoundError(f"{name} was hidden")
365 
366     if name == "dvipng":
367         return impl(["dvipng", "-version"], "(?m)^dvipng(?: .*)? (.+)", "1.6")
368     elif name == "gs":
369         execs = (["gswin32c", "gswin64c", "mgs", "gs"]  # "mgs" for miktex.
370                  if sys.platform == "win32" else
371                  ["gs"])
372         for e in execs:
373             try:
374                 return impl([e, "--version"], "(.*)", "9")
375             except ExecutableNotFoundError:
376                 pass
377         message = "Failed to find a Ghostscript installation"
378         raise ExecutableNotFoundError(message)
379     elif name == "inkscape":
380         try:
381             # Try headless option first (needed for Inkscape version < 1.0):
382             return impl(["inkscape", "--without-gui", "-V"],
383                         "Inkscape ([^ ]*)")
384         except ExecutableNotFoundError:
385             pass  # Suppress exception chaining.
386         # If --without-gui is not accepted, we may be using Inkscape >= 1.0 so
387         # try without it:
388         return impl(["inkscape", "-V"], "Inkscape ([^ ]*)")
389     elif name == "magick":
390         if sys.platform == "win32":
391             # Check the registry to avoid confusing ImageMagick's convert with
392             # Windows's builtin convert.exe.
393             import winreg
394             binpath = ""
395             for flag in [0, winreg.KEY_WOW64_32KEY, winreg.KEY_WOW64_64KEY]:
396                 try:
397                     with winreg.OpenKeyEx(
398                             winreg.HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE,
399                             r"Software\Imagemagick\Current",
400                             0, winreg.KEY_QUERY_VALUE | flag) as hkey:
401                         binpath = winreg.QueryValueEx(hkey, "BinPath")[0]
402                 except OSError:
403                     pass
404             path = None
405             if binpath:
406                 for name in ["convert.exe", "magick.exe"]:
407                     candidate = Path(binpath, name)
408                     if candidate.exists():
409                         path = str(candidate)
410                         break
411             if path is None:
412                 raise ExecutableNotFoundError(
413                     "Failed to find an ImageMagick installation")
414         else:
415             path = "convert"
416         info = impl([path, "--version"], r"^Version: ImageMagick (\S*)")
417         if info.raw_version == "7.0.10-34":
418             # https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick/issues/2720
419             raise ExecutableNotFoundError(
420                 f"You have ImageMagick {info.version}, which is unsupported")
421         return info
422     elif name == "pdftocairo":
423         return impl(["pdftocairo", "-v"], "pdftocairo version (.*)")
424     elif name == "pdftops":
425         info = impl(["pdftops", "-v"], "^pdftops version (.*)",
426                     ignore_exit_code=True)
427         if info and not (
428                 3 <= info.version.major or
429                 # poppler version numbers.
430                 parse_version("0.9") <= info.version < parse_version("1.0")):
431             raise ExecutableNotFoundError(
432                 f"You have pdftops version {info.version} but the minimum "
433                 f"version supported by Matplotlib is 3.0")
434         return info
435     else:
436         raise ValueError("Unknown executable: {!r}".format(name))

478 def _get_config_or_cache_dir(xdg_base_getter):
479     configdir = os.environ.get('MPLCONFIGDIR')
480     if configdir:
481         configdir = Path(configdir).resolve()
482     elif sys.platform.startswith(('linux', 'freebsd')):
483         # Only call _xdg_base_getter here so that MPLCONFIGDIR is tried first,
484         # as _xdg_base_getter can throw.
485         configdir = Path(xdg_base_getter(), "matplotlib")
486     else:
487         configdir = Path.home() / ".matplotlib"
488     try:
489         configdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
490     except OSError:
491         pass
492     else:
493         if os.access(str(configdir), os.W_OK) and configdir.is_dir():
494             return str(configdir)
495     # If the config or cache directory cannot be created or is not a writable
496     # directory, create a temporary one.
497     tmpdir = os.environ["MPLCONFIGDIR"] = \
498         tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="matplotlib-")
499     atexit.register(shutil.rmtree, tmpdir)
500     _log.warning(
501         "Matplotlib created a temporary config/cache directory at %s because "
502         "the default path (%s) is not a writable directory; it is highly "
503         "recommended to set the MPLCONFIGDIR environment variable to a "
504         "writable directory, in particular to speed up the import of "
505         "Matplotlib and to better support multiprocessing.",
506         tmpdir, configdir)
507     return tmpdir

546 def matplotlib_fname():
547     """
548     Get the location of the config file.
549 
550     The file location is determined in the following order
551 
552     - ``$PWD/matplotlibrc``
553     - ``$MATPLOTLIBRC`` if it is not a directory
554     - ``$MATPLOTLIBRC/matplotlibrc``
555     - ``$MPLCONFIGDIR/matplotlibrc``
556     - On Linux,
557         - ``$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/matplotlib/matplotlibrc`` (if ``$XDG_CONFIG_HOME``
558           is defined)
559         - or ``$HOME/.config/matplotlib/matplotlibrc`` (if ``$XDG_CONFIG_HOME``
560           is not defined)
561     - On other platforms,
562       - ``$HOME/.matplotlib/matplotlibrc`` if ``$HOME`` is defined
563     - Lastly, it looks in ``$MATPLOTLIBDATA/matplotlibrc``, which should always
564       exist.
565     """
566 
567     def gen_candidates():
568         # rely on down-stream code to make absolute.  This protects us
569         # from having to directly get the current working directory
570         # which can fail if the user has ended up with a cwd that is
571         # non-existent.
572         yield 'matplotlibrc'
573         try:
574             matplotlibrc = os.environ['MATPLOTLIBRC']
575         except KeyError:
576             pass
577         else:
578             yield matplotlibrc
579             yield os.path.join(matplotlibrc, 'matplotlibrc')
580         yield os.path.join(get_configdir(), 'matplotlibrc')
581         yield os.path.join(get_data_path(), 'matplotlibrc')
582 
583     for fname in gen_candidates():
584         if os.path.exists(fname) and not os.path.isdir(fname):
585             return fname
586 
587     raise RuntimeError("Could not find matplotlibrc file; your Matplotlib "
588                        "install is broken")

591 # rcParams deprecated and automatically mapped to another key.
592 # Values are tuples of (version, new_name, f_old2new, f_new2old).
593 _deprecated_map = {}
594 # rcParams deprecated; some can manually be mapped to another key.
595 # Values are tuples of (version, new_name_or_None).
596 _deprecated_ignore_map = {}
597 # rcParams deprecated; can use None to suppress warnings; remain actually
598 # listed in the rcParams.
599 # Values are tuples of (version,)
600 _deprecated_remain_as_none = {}
601 
602 
603 @_docstring.Substitution(
604     "\n".join(map("- {}".format, sorted(rcsetup._validators, key=str.lower)))
605 )
606 class RcParams(MutableMapping, dict):
607     """
608     A dictionary object including validation.
609 
610     Validating functions are defined and associated with rc parameters in
611     :mod:`matplotlib.rcsetup`.
612 
613     The list of rcParams is:
614 
615     %s
616 
617     See Also
618     --------
619     :ref:`customizing-with-matplotlibrc-files`
620     """
621 
622     validate = rcsetup._validators
623 
624     # validate values on the way in
625     def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
626         self.update(*args, **kwargs)
627 
628     def __setitem__(self, key, val):
629         try:
630             if key in _deprecated_map:
631                 version, alt_key, alt_val, inverse_alt = _deprecated_map[key]
632                 _api.warn_deprecated(
633                     version, name=key, obj_type="rcparam", alternative=alt_key)
634                 key = alt_key
635                 val = alt_val(val)
636             elif key in _deprecated_remain_as_none and val is not None:
637                 version, = _deprecated_remain_as_none[key]
638                 _api.warn_deprecated(version, name=key, obj_type="rcparam")
639             elif key in _deprecated_ignore_map:
640                 version, alt_key = _deprecated_ignore_map[key]
641                 _api.warn_deprecated(
642                     version, name=key, obj_type="rcparam", alternative=alt_key)
643                 return
644             elif key == 'backend':
645                 if val is rcsetup._auto_backend_sentinel:
646                     if 'backend' in self:
647                         return
648             try:
649                 cval = self.validate[key](val)
650             except ValueError as ve:
651                 raise ValueError(f"Key {key}: {ve}") from None
652             dict.__setitem__(self, key, cval)
653         except KeyError as err:
654             raise KeyError(
655                 f"{key} is not a valid rc parameter (see rcParams.keys() for "
656                 f"a list of valid parameters)") from err
657 
658     def __getitem__(self, key):
659         if key in _deprecated_map:
660             version, alt_key, alt_val, inverse_alt = _deprecated_map[key]
661             _api.warn_deprecated(
662                 version, name=key, obj_type="rcparam", alternative=alt_key)
663             return inverse_alt(dict.__getitem__(self, alt_key))
664 
665         elif key in _deprecated_ignore_map:
666             version, alt_key = _deprecated_ignore_map[key]
667             _api.warn_deprecated(
668                 version, name=key, obj_type="rcparam", alternative=alt_key)
669             return dict.__getitem__(self, alt_key) if alt_key else None
670 
671         # In theory, this should only ever be used after the global rcParams
672         # has been set up, but better be safe e.g. in presence of breakpoints.
673         elif key == "backend" and self is globals().get("rcParams"):
674             val = dict.__getitem__(self, key)
675             if val is rcsetup._auto_backend_sentinel:
676                 from matplotlib import pyplot as plt
677                 plt.switch_backend(rcsetup._auto_backend_sentinel)
678 
679         return dict.__getitem__(self, key)
680 
681     def _get_backend_or_none(self):
682         """Get the requested backend, if any, without triggering resolution."""
683         backend = dict.__getitem__(self, "backend")
684         return None if backend is rcsetup._auto_backend_sentinel else backend
685 
686     def __repr__(self):
687         class_name = self.__class__.__name__
688         indent = len(class_name) + 1
689         with _api.suppress_matplotlib_deprecation_warning():
690             repr_split = pprint.pformat(dict(self), indent=1,
691                                         width=80 - indent).split('\n')
692         repr_indented = ('\n' + ' ' * indent).join(repr_split)
693         return '{}({})'.format(class_name, repr_indented)
694 
695     def __str__(self):
696         return '\n'.join(map('{0[0]}: {0[1]}'.format, sorted(self.items())))
697 
698     def __iter__(self):
699         """Yield sorted list of keys."""
700         with _api.suppress_matplotlib_deprecation_warning():
701             yield from sorted(dict.__iter__(self))
702 
703     def __len__(self):
704         return dict.__len__(self)
705 
706     def find_all(self, pattern):
707         """
708         Return the subset of this RcParams dictionary whose keys match,
709         using :func:`re.search`, the given ``pattern``.
710 
711         .. note::
712 
713             Changes to the returned dictionary are *not* propagated to
714             the parent RcParams dictionary.
715 
716         """
717         pattern_re = re.compile(pattern)
718         return RcParams((key, value)
719                         for key, value in self.items()
720                         if pattern_re.search(key))
721 
722     def copy(self):
723         rccopy = RcParams()
724         for k in self:  # Skip deprecations and revalidation.
725             dict.__setitem__(rccopy, k, dict.__getitem__(self, k))
726         return rccopy

753     if (isinstance(fname, str)
754             and fname.startswith(('http://', 'https://', 'ftp://', 'file:'))):
755         import urllib.request
756         ssl_ctx = _get_ssl_context()
757         if ssl_ctx is None:
758             _log.debug(
759                 "Could not get certifi ssl context, https may not work."
760             )
761         with urllib.request.urlopen(fname, context=ssl_ctx) as f:
762             yield (line.decode('utf-8') for line in f)
763     else:
764         fname = os.path.expanduser(fname)
765         with open(fname, encoding='utf-8') as f:
766             yield f
