1970     def split_exclude(self, filter_expr, can_reuse, names_with_path):
1971         """
1972         When doing an exclude against any kind of N-to-many relation, we need
1973         to use a subquery. This method constructs the nested query, given the
1974         original exclude filter (filter_expr) and the portion up to the first
1975         N-to-many relation field.
1976 
1977         For example, if the origin filter is ~Q(child__name='foo'), filter_expr
1978         is ('child__name', 'foo') and can_reuse is a set of joins usable for
1979         filters in the original query.
1980 
1981         We will turn this into equivalent of:
1982             WHERE NOT EXISTS(
1983                 SELECT 1
1984                 FROM child
1985                 WHERE name = 'foo' AND child.parent_id = parent.id
1986                 LIMIT 1
1987             )
1988         """
1989         # Generate the inner query.
1990         query = self.__class__(self.model)
1991         query._filtered_relations = self._filtered_relations
1992         filter_lhs, filter_rhs = filter_expr
1993         if isinstance(filter_rhs, OuterRef):
1994             filter_rhs = OuterRef(filter_rhs)
1995         elif isinstance(filter_rhs, F):
1996             filter_rhs = OuterRef(filter_rhs.name)
1997         query.add_filter(filter_lhs, filter_rhs)
1998         query.clear_ordering(force=True)
1999         # Try to have as simple as possible subquery -> trim leading joins from
2000         # the subquery.
2001         trimmed_prefix, contains_louter = query.trim_start(names_with_path)
2002 
2003         col = query.select[0]
2004         select_field = col.target
2005         alias = col.alias
2006         if alias in can_reuse:
2007             pk = select_field.model._meta.pk
2008             # Need to add a restriction so that outer query's filters are in effect for
2009             # the subquery, too.
2010             query.bump_prefix(self)
2011             lookup_class = select_field.get_lookup("exact")
2012             # Note that the query.select[0].alias is different from alias
2013             # due to bump_prefix above.
2014             lookup = lookup_class(pk.get_col(query.select[0].alias), pk.get_col(alias))
2015             query.where.add(lookup, AND)
2016             query.external_aliases[alias] = True
2017 
2018         lookup_class = select_field.get_lookup("exact")
2019         lookup = lookup_class(col, ResolvedOuterRef(trimmed_prefix))
2020         query.where.add(lookup, AND)
2021         condition, needed_inner = self.build_filter(Exists(query))
2022 
2023         if contains_louter:
2024             or_null_condition, _ = self.build_filter(
2025                 ("%s__isnull" % trimmed_prefix, True),
2026                 current_negated=True,
2027                 branch_negated=True,
2028                 can_reuse=can_reuse,
2029             )
2030             condition.add(or_null_condition, OR)
2031             # Note that the end result will be:
2032             # (outercol NOT IN innerq AND outercol IS NOT NULL) OR outercol IS NULL.
2033             # This might look crazy but due to how IN works, this seems to be
2034             # correct. If the IS NOT NULL check is removed then outercol NOT
2035             # IN will return UNKNOWN. If the IS NULL check is removed, then if
2036             # outercol IS NULL we will not match the row.
2037         return condition, needed_inner

2473     def trim_start(self, names_with_path):
2474         """
2475         Trim joins from the start of the join path. The candidates for trim
2476         are the PathInfos in names_with_path structure that are m2m joins.
2477 
2478         Also set the select column so the start matches the join.
2479 
2480         This method is meant to be used for generating the subquery joins &
2481         cols in split_exclude().
2482 
2483         Return a lookup usable for doing outerq.filter(lookup=self) and a
2484         boolean indicating if the joins in the prefix contain a LEFT OUTER join.
2485         _"""
2486         all_paths = []
2487         for _, paths in names_with_path:
2488             all_paths.extend(paths)
2489         contains_louter = False
2490         # Trim and operate only on tables that were generated for
2491         # the lookup part of the query. That is, avoid trimming
2492         # joins generated for F() expressions.
2493         lookup_tables = [
2494             t for t in self.alias_map if t in self._lookup_joins or t == self.base_table
2495         ]
2496         for trimmed_paths, path in enumerate(all_paths):
2497             if path.m2m:
2498                 break
2499             if self.alias_map[lookup_tables[trimmed_paths + 1]].join_type == LOUTER:
2500                 contains_louter = True
2501             alias = lookup_tables[trimmed_paths]
2502             self.unref_alias(alias)
2503         # The path.join_field is a Rel, lets get the other side's field
2504         join_field = path.join_field.field
2505         # Build the filter prefix.
2506         paths_in_prefix = trimmed_paths
2507         trimmed_prefix = []
2508         for name, path in names_with_path:
2509             if paths_in_prefix - len(path) < 0:
2510                 break
2511             trimmed_prefix.append(name)
2512             paths_in_prefix -= len(path)
2513         trimmed_prefix.append(join_field.foreign_related_fields[0].name)
2514         trimmed_prefix = LOOKUP_SEP.join(trimmed_prefix)
2515         # Lets still see if we can trim the first join from the inner query
2516         # (that is, self). We can't do this for:
2517         # - LEFT JOINs because we would miss those rows that have nothing on
2518         #   the outer side,
2519         # - INNER JOINs from filtered relations because we would miss their
2520         #   filters.
2521         first_join = self.alias_map[lookup_tables[trimmed_paths + 1]]
2522         if first_join.join_type != LOUTER and not first_join.filtered_relation:
2523             select_fields = [r[0] for r in join_field.related_fields]
2524             select_alias = lookup_tables[trimmed_paths + 1]
2525             self.unref_alias(lookup_tables[trimmed_paths])
2526             extra_restriction = join_field.get_extra_restriction(
2527                 None, lookup_tables[trimmed_paths + 1]
2528             )
2529             if extra_restriction:
2530                 self.where.add(extra_restriction, AND)
2531         else:
2532             # TODO: It might be possible to trim more joins from the start of the
2533             # inner query if it happens to have a longer join chain containing the
2534             # values in select_fields. Lets punt this one for now.
2535             select_fields = [r[1] for r in join_field.related_fields]
2536             select_alias = lookup_tables[trimmed_paths]
2537         # The found starting point is likely a join_class instead of a
2538         # base_table_class reference. But the first entry in the query's FROM
2539         # clause must not be a JOIN.
2540         for table in self.alias_map:
2541             if self.alias_refcount[table] > 0:
2542                 self.alias_map[table] = self.base_table_class(
2543                     self.alias_map[table].table_name,
2544                     table,
2545                 )
2546                 break
2547         self.set_select([f.get_col(select_alias) for f in select_fields])
2548         return trimmed_prefix, contains_louter

2618         """

2622         results from the query.
2623         """
2624         to_promote = set()

2627         # similarly to (a OR b) for join promotion.

2629             # We must use outer joins in OR case when the join isn't contained

2632             # rel_b relations is queried with rel_a__col=1 | rel_b__col=2. Now,
2633             # if rel_a join doesn't produce any results is null (for example
2634             # reverse foreign key or null value in direct foreign key), and
2635             # there is a matching row in rel_b with col=2, then an INNER join
2636             # to rel_a would remove a valid match from the query. So, we need
2637             # to promote any existing INNER to LOUTER (it is possible this
2638             # promotion in turn will be demoted later on).
2639             if self.effective_connector == OR and votes < self.num_children:

2642             # when there is a joinable row, then use INNER. For example, in
2643             # rel_a__col=1 & rel_b__col=2, if either of the rels produce NULL
2644             # as join output, then the col=1 or col=2 can't match (as
2645             # NULL=anything is always false).
2646             # For the OR case, if all children voted for a join to be inner,
2647             # then we can use INNER for the join. For example:
2648             #     (rel_a__col__icontains=Alex | rel_a__col__icontains=Russell)
2649             # then if rel_a doesn't produce any rows, the whole condition
2650             # can't match. Hence we can safely use INNER join.
2651             if self.effective_connector == AND or (
2652                 self.effective_connector == OR and votes == self.num_children
2653             ):
2654                 to_demote.add(table)
2655             # Finally, what happens in cases where we have:
2656             #    (rel_a__col=1|rel_b__col=2) & rel_a__col__gte=0
2657             # Now, we first generate the OR clause, and promote joins for it
2658             # in the first if branch above. Both rel_a and rel_b are promoted
2659             # to LOUTER joins. After that we do the AND case. The OR case
2660             # voted no inner joins but the rel_a__col__gte=0 votes inner join
2661             # for rel_a. We demote it back to INNER join (in AND case a single
2662             # vote is enough). The demotion is OK, if rel_a doesn't produce
2663             # rows, then the rel_a__col__gte=0 clause can't be true, and thus
2664             # the whole clause must be false. So, it is safe to use INNER
2665             # join.
2666             # Note that in this example we could just as well have the __gte
2667             # clause and the OR clause swapped. Or we could replace the __gte
2668             # clause with an OR clause containing rel_a__col=1|rel_a__col=2,
2669             # and again we could safely demote to INNER.
2670         query.promote_joins(to_promote)
2671         query.demote_joins(to_demote)

problem_statement:
QuerySet.only() doesn't work with select_related() on a reverse OneToOneField relation.
Description
	
On Django 4.2 calling only() with select_related() on a query using the reverse lookup for a OneToOne relation does not generate the correct query.
All the fields from the related model are still included in the generated SQL.
Sample models:
class Main(models.Model):
	main_field_1 = models.CharField(blank=True, max_length=45)
	main_field_2 = models.CharField(blank=True, max_length=45)
	main_field_3 = models.CharField(blank=True, max_length=45)
class Secondary(models.Model):
	main = models.OneToOneField(Main, primary_key=True, related_name='secondary', on_delete=models.CASCADE)
	secondary_field_1 = models.CharField(blank=True, max_length=45)
	secondary_field_2 = models.CharField(blank=True, max_length=45)
	secondary_field_3 = models.CharField(blank=True, max_length=45)
Sample code:
Main.objects.select_related('secondary').only('main_field_1', 'secondary__secondary_field_1')
Generated query on Django 4.2.1:
SELECT "bugtest_main"."id", "bugtest_main"."main_field_1", "bugtest_secondary"."main_id", "bugtest_secondary"."secondary_field_1", "bugtest_secondary"."secondary_field_2", "bugtest_secondary"."secondary_field_3" FROM "bugtest_main" LEFT OUTER JOIN "bugtest_secondary" ON ("bugtest_main"."id" = "bugtest_secondary"."main_id")
Generated query on Django 4.1.9:
SELECT "bugtest_main"."id", "bugtest_main"."main_field_1", "bugtest_secondary"."main_id", "bugtest_secondary"."secondary_field_1" FROM "bugtest_main" LEFT OUTER JOIN "bugtest_secondary" ON ("bugtest_main"."id" = "bugtest_secondary"."main_id")

44 def _splitnode(nodeid):
45     """Split a nodeid into constituent 'parts'.

47     Node IDs are strings, and can be things like:
48         ''

61         return ()

63     # Replace single last element 'test_foo.py::Bar' with multiple elements 'test_foo.py', 'Bar'

#### Description

```python
from sklearn.utils.validation import check_array
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame([[1, 2, 3], [2, 3, 4]], dtype=object)

DataConversionWarning: Data with input dtype object was converted to float64.

No warning is thrown

154 
155     Under Windows 64 bit (and Python 2), the `long` type is used by default
156     in numpy shapes even when the integer dimensions are well below 32 bit.
157     The platform specific type causes string messages or doctests to change
158     from one platform to another which is not desirable.
159 
160     Under Python 3, there is no more `long` type so the `L` suffix is never
161     introduced in string representation.
162 
163     >>> _shape_repr((1, 2))
164     '(1, 2)'
165     >>> one = 2 ** 64 / 2 ** 64  # force an upcast to `long` under Python 2
166     >>> _shape_repr((one, 2 * one))
167     '(1, 2)'
168     >>> _shape_repr((1,))
169     '(1,)'
170     >>> _shape_repr(())
171     '()'
172     """
173     if len(shape) == 0:
174         return "()"
175     joined = ", ".join("%d" % e for e in shape)
176     if len(shape) == 1:
177         # special notation for singleton tuples
178         joined += ','
179     return "(%s)" % joined
180

256 def _ensure_sparse_format(spmatrix, accept_sparse, dtype, copy,
257                           force_all_finite, accept_large_sparse):
258     """Convert a sparse matrix to a given format.
259 
260     Checks the sparse format of spmatrix and converts if necessary.
261 
262     Parameters
263     ----------
264     spmatrix : scipy sparse matrix
265         Input to validate and convert.
266 
267     accept_sparse : string, boolean or list/tuple of strings
268         String[s] representing allowed sparse matrix formats ('csc',
269         'csr', 'coo', 'dok', 'bsr', 'lil', 'dia'). If the input is sparse but
270         not in the allowed format, it will be converted to the first listed
271         format. True allows the input to be any format. False means
272         that a sparse matrix input will raise an error.
273 
274     dtype : string, type or None
275         Data type of result. If None, the dtype of the input is preserved.
276 
277     copy : boolean
278         Whether a forced copy will be triggered. If copy=False, a copy might
279         be triggered by a conversion.
280 
281     force_all_finite : boolean or 'allow-nan', (default=True)
282         Whether to raise an error on np.inf and np.nan in X. The possibilities
283         are:
284 
285         - True: Force all values of X to be finite.
286         - False: accept both np.inf and np.nan in X.
287         - 'allow-nan':  accept  only  np.nan  values in  X.  Values  cannot  be
288           infinite.
289 
290         .. versionadded:: 0.20
291            ``force_all_finite`` accepts the string ``'allow-nan'``.
292 
293     Returns
294     -------
295     spmatrix_converted : scipy sparse matrix.
296         Matrix that is ensured to have an allowed type.
297     """
298     if dtype is None:
299         dtype = spmatrix.dtype
300 
301     changed_format = False
302 
303     if isinstance(accept_sparse, six.string_types):
304         accept_sparse = [accept_sparse]
305 
306     # Indices dtype validation
307     _check_large_sparse(spmatrix, accept_large_sparse)
308 
309     if accept_sparse is False:
310         raise TypeError('A sparse matrix was passed, but dense '
311                         'data is required. Use X.toarray() to '
312                         'convert to a dense numpy array.')
313     elif isinstance(accept_sparse, (list, tuple)):
314         if len(accept_sparse) == 0:
315             raise ValueError("When providing 'accept_sparse' "
316                              "as a tuple or list, it must contain at "
317                              "least one string value.")
318         # ensure correct sparse format
319         if spmatrix.format not in accept_sparse:
320             # create new with correct sparse
321             spmatrix = spmatrix.asformat(accept_sparse[0])
322             changed_format = True
323     elif accept_sparse is not True:
324         # any other type
325         raise ValueError("Parameter 'accept_sparse' should be a string, "
326                          "boolean or list of strings. You provided "
327                          "'accept_sparse={}'.".format(accept_sparse))
328 
329     if dtype != spmatrix.dtype:
330         # convert dtype
331         spmatrix = spmatrix.astype(dtype)
332     elif copy and not changed_format:
333         # force copy
334         spmatrix = spmatrix.copy()
335 
336     if force_all_finite:
337         if not hasattr(spmatrix, "data"):
338             warnings.warn("Can't check %s sparse matrix for nan or inf."
339                           % spmatrix.format)
340         else:
341             _assert_all_finite(spmatrix.data,
342                                allow_nan=force_all_finite == 'allow-nan')
343 
344     return spmatrix
345

350         raise ValueError("Complex data not supported\n"

354 def check_array(array, accept_sparse=False, accept_large_sparse=True,
355                 dtype="numeric", order=None, copy=False, force_all_finite=True,
356                 ensure_2d=True, allow_nd=False, ensure_min_samples=1,
357                 ensure_min_features=1, warn_on_dtype=False, estimator=None):
358 
359     """Input validation on an array, list, sparse matrix or similar.
360 
361     By default, the input is converted to an at least 2D numpy array.
362     If the dtype of the array is object, attempt converting to float,
363     raising on failure.
364 
365     Parameters
366     ----------
367     array : object
368         Input object to check / convert.
369 
370     accept_sparse : string, boolean or list/tuple of strings (default=False)
371         String[s] representing allowed sparse matrix formats, such as 'csc',
372         'csr', etc. If the input is sparse but not in the allowed format,
373         it will be converted to the first listed format. True allows the input
374         to be any format. False means that a sparse matrix input will
375         raise an error.
376 
377         .. deprecated:: 0.19
378            Passing 'None' to parameter ``accept_sparse`` in methods is
379            deprecated in version 0.19 "and will be removed in 0.21. Use
380            ``accept_sparse=False`` instead.
381 
382     accept_large_sparse : bool (default=True)
383         If a CSR, CSC, COO or BSR sparse matrix is supplied and accepted by
384         accept_sparse, accept_large_sparse=False will cause it to be accepted
385         only if its indices are stored with a 32-bit dtype.
386 
387         .. versionadded:: 0.20
388 
389     dtype : string, type, list of types or None (default="numeric")
390         Data type of result. If None, the dtype of the input is preserved.
391         If "numeric", dtype is preserved unless array.dtype is object.
392         If dtype is a list of types, conversion on the first type is only
393         performed if the dtype of the input is not in the list.
394 
395     order : 'F', 'C' or None (default=None)
396         Whether an array will be forced to be fortran or c-style.
397         When order is None (default), then if copy=False, nothing is ensured
398         about the memory layout of the output array; otherwise (copy=True)
399         the memory layout of the returned array is kept as close as possible
400         to the original array.
401 
402     copy : boolean (default=False)
403         Whether a forced copy will be triggered. If copy=False, a copy might
404         be triggered by a conversion.
405 
406     force_all_finite : boolean or 'allow-nan', (default=True)
407         Whether to raise an error on np.inf and np.nan in X. The possibilities
408         are:
409 
410         - True: Force all values of X to be finite.
411         - False: accept both np.inf and np.nan in X.
412         - 'allow-nan':  accept  only  np.nan  values in  X.  Values  cannot  be
413           infinite.
414 
415         .. versionadded:: 0.20
416            ``force_all_finite`` accepts the string ``'allow-nan'``.
417 
418     ensure_2d : boolean (default=True)
419         Whether to raise a value error if X is not 2d.
420 
421     allow_nd : boolean (default=False)
422         Whether to allow X.ndim > 2.
423 
424     ensure_min_samples : int (default=1)
425         Make sure that the array has a minimum number of samples in its first
426         axis (rows for a 2D array). Setting to 0 disables this check.
427 
428     ensure_min_features : int (default=1)
429         Make sure that the 2D array has some minimum number of features
430         (columns). The default value of 1 rejects empty datasets.
431         This check is only enforced when the input data has effectively 2
432         dimensions or is originally 1D and ``ensure_2d`` is True. Setting to 0
433         disables this check.
434 
435     warn_on_dtype : boolean (default=False)
436         Raise DataConversionWarning if the dtype of the input data structure
437         does not match the requested dtype, causing a memory copy.
438 
439     estimator : str or estimator instance (default=None)
440         If passed, include the name of the estimator in warning messages.
441 
442     Returns
443     -------
444     X_converted : object
445         The converted and validated X.
446 
447     """
448     # accept_sparse 'None' deprecation check
449     if accept_sparse is None:
450         warnings.warn(
451             "Passing 'None' to parameter 'accept_sparse' in methods "
452             "check_array and check_X_y is deprecated in version 0.19 "
453             "and will be removed in 0.21. Use 'accept_sparse=False' "
454             " instead.", DeprecationWarning)
455         accept_sparse = False
456 
457     # store reference to original array to check if copy is needed when
458     # function returns
459     array_orig = array
460 
461     # store whether originally we wanted numeric dtype
462     dtype_numeric = isinstance(dtype, six.string_types) and dtype == "numeric"
463 
464     dtype_orig = getattr(array, "dtype", None)
465     if not hasattr(dtype_orig, 'kind'):
466         # not a data type (e.g. a column named dtype in a pandas DataFrame)
467         dtype_orig = None
468 
469     if dtype_numeric:
470         if dtype_orig is not None and dtype_orig.kind == "O":
471             # if input is object, convert to float.
472             dtype = np.float64
473         else:
474             dtype = None
475 
476     if isinstance(dtype, (list, tuple)):
477         if dtype_orig is not None and dtype_orig in dtype:
478             # no dtype conversion required
479             dtype = None
480         else:
481             # dtype conversion required. Let's select the first element of the
482             # list of accepted types.
483             dtype = dtype[0]
484 
485     if force_all_finite not in (True, False, 'allow-nan'):
486         raise ValueError('force_all_finite should be a bool or "allow-nan"'
487                          '. Got {!r} instead'.format(force_all_finite))
488 
489     if estimator is not None:
490         if isinstance(estimator, six.string_types):
491             estimator_name = estimator
492         else:
493             estimator_name = estimator.__class__.__name__
494     else:
495         estimator_name = "Estimator"
496     context = " by %s" % estimator_name if estimator is not None else ""
497 
498     if sp.issparse(array):
499         _ensure_no_complex_data(array)
500         array = _ensure_sparse_format(array, accept_sparse=accept_sparse,
501                                       dtype=dtype, copy=copy,
502                                       force_all_finite=force_all_finite,
503                                       accept_large_sparse=accept_large_sparse)
504     else:
505         # If np.array(..) gives ComplexWarning, then we convert the warning
506         # to an error. This is needed because specifying a non complex
507         # dtype to the function converts complex to real dtype,
508         # thereby passing the test made in the lines following the scope
509         # of warnings context manager.
510         with warnings.catch_warnings():
511             try:
512                 warnings.simplefilter('error', ComplexWarning)
513                 array = np.asarray(array, dtype=dtype, order=order)
514             except ComplexWarning:
515                 raise ValueError("Complex data not supported\n"
516                                  "{}\n".format(array))
517 
518         # It is possible that the np.array(..) gave no warning. This happens
519         # when no dtype conversion happened, for example dtype = None. The
520         # result is that np.array(..) produces an array of complex dtype
521         # and we need to catch and raise exception for such cases.
522         _ensure_no_complex_data(array)
523 
524         if ensure_2d:
525             # If input is scalar raise error
526             if array.ndim == 0:
527                 raise ValueError(
528                     "Expected 2D array, got scalar array instead:\narray={}.\n"
529                     "Reshape your data either using array.reshape(-1, 1) if "
530                     "your data has a single feature or array.reshape(1, -1) "
531                     "if it contains a single sample.".format(array))
532             # If input is 1D raise error
533             if array.ndim == 1:
534                 raise ValueError(
535                     "Expected 2D array, got 1D array instead:\narray={}.\n"
536                     "Reshape your data either using array.reshape(-1, 1) if "
537                     "your data has a single feature or array.reshape(1, -1) "
538                     "if it contains a single sample.".format(array))
539 
540         # in the future np.flexible dtypes will be handled like object dtypes
541         if dtype_numeric and np.issubdtype(array.dtype, np.flexible):
542             warnings.warn(
543                 "Beginning in version 0.22, arrays of strings will be "
544                 "interpreted as decimal numbers if parameter 'dtype' is "
545                 "'numeric'. It is recommended that you convert the array to "
546                 "type np.float64 before passing it to check_array.",
547                 FutureWarning)
548 
549         # make sure we actually converted to numeric:
550         if dtype_numeric and array.dtype.kind == "O":
551             array = array.astype(np.float64)
552         if not allow_nd and array.ndim >= 3:
553             raise ValueError("Found array with dim %d. %s expected <= 2."
554                              % (array.ndim, estimator_name))
555         if force_all_finite:
556             _assert_all_finite(array,
557                                allow_nan=force_all_finite == 'allow-nan')
558 
559     shape_repr = _shape_repr(array.shape)
560     if ensure_min_samples > 0:
561         n_samples = _num_samples(array)
562         if n_samples < ensure_min_samples:
563             raise ValueError("Found array with %d sample(s) (shape=%s) while a"
564                              " minimum of %d is required%s."
565                              % (n_samples, shape_repr, ensure_min_samples,
566                                 context))
567 
568     if ensure_min_features > 0 and array.ndim == 2:
569         n_features = array.shape[1]
570         if n_features < ensure_min_features:
571             raise ValueError("Found array with %d feature(s) (shape=%s) while"
572                              " a minimum of %d is required%s."
573                              % (n_features, shape_repr, ensure_min_features,
574                                 context))
575 
576     if warn_on_dtype and dtype_orig is not None and array.dtype != dtype_orig:
577         msg = ("Data with input dtype %s was converted to %s%s."
578                % (dtype_orig, array.dtype, context))
579         warnings.warn(msg, DataConversionWarning)
580 
581     if copy and np.may_share_memory(array, array_orig):
582         array = np.array(array, dtype=dtype, order=order)
583 
584     return array
585

587 def _check_large_sparse(X, accept_large_sparse=False):
588     """Raise a ValueError if X has 64bit indices and accept_large_sparse=False
589     """
590     if not (accept_large_sparse and LARGE_SPARSE_SUPPORTED):
591         supported_indices = ["int32"]
592         if X.getformat() == "coo":
593             index_keys = ['col', 'row']
594         elif X.getformat() in ["csr", "csc", "bsr"]:
595             index_keys = ['indices', 'indptr']
596         else:
597             return
598         for key in index_keys:
599             indices_datatype = getattr(X, key).dtype
600             if (indices_datatype not in supported_indices):
601                 if not LARGE_SPARSE_SUPPORTED:
602                     raise ValueError("Scipy version %s does not support large"
603                                      " indices, please upgrade your scipy"
604                                      " to 0.14.0 or above" % scipy_version)
605                 raise ValueError("Only sparse matrices with 32-bit integer"
606                                  " indices are accepted. Got %s indices."
607                                  % indices_datatype)
608

610 def check_X_y(X, y, accept_sparse=False, accept_large_sparse=True,
611               dtype="numeric", order=None, copy=False, force_all_finite=True,
612               ensure_2d=True, allow_nd=False, multi_output=False,
613               ensure_min_samples=1, ensure_min_features=1, y_numeric=False,
614               warn_on_dtype=False, estimator=None):
615     """Input validation for standard estimators.
616 
617     Checks X and y for consistent length, enforces X 2d and y 1d.
618     Standard input checks are only applied to y, such as checking that y
619     does not have np.nan or np.inf targets. For multi-label y, set
620     multi_output=True to allow 2d and sparse y.  If the dtype of X is
621     object, attempt converting to float, raising on failure.
622 
623     Parameters
624     ----------
625     X : nd-array, list or sparse matrix
626         Input data.
627 
628     y : nd-array, list or sparse matrix
629         Labels.
630 
631     accept_sparse : string, boolean or list of string (default=False)
632         String[s] representing allowed sparse matrix formats, such as 'csc',
633         'csr', etc. If the input is sparse but not in the allowed format,
634         it will be converted to the first listed format. True allows the input
635         to be any format. False means that a sparse matrix input will
636         raise an error.
637 
638         .. deprecated:: 0.19
639            Passing 'None' to parameter ``accept_sparse`` in methods is
640            deprecated in version 0.19 "and will be removed in 0.21. Use
641            ``accept_sparse=False`` instead.
642 
643     accept_large_sparse : bool (default=True)
644         If a CSR, CSC, COO or BSR sparse matrix is supplied and accepted by
645         accept_sparse, accept_large_sparse will cause it to be accepted only
646         if its indices are stored with a 32-bit dtype.
647 
648         .. versionadded:: 0.20
649 
650     dtype : string, type, list of types or None (default="numeric")
651         Data type of result. If None, the dtype of the input is preserved.
652         If "numeric", dtype is preserved unless array.dtype is object.
653         If dtype is a list of types, conversion on the first type is only
654         performed if the dtype of the input is not in the list.
655 
656     order : 'F', 'C' or None (default=None)
657         Whether an array will be forced to be fortran or c-style.
658 
659     copy : boolean (default=False)
660         Whether a forced copy will be triggered. If copy=False, a copy might
661         be triggered by a conversion.
662 
663     force_all_finite : boolean or 'allow-nan', (default=True)
664         Whether to raise an error on np.inf and np.nan in X. This parameter
665         does not influence whether y can have np.inf or np.nan values.
666         The possibilities are:
667 
668         - True: Force all values of X to be finite.
669         - False: accept both np.inf and np.nan in X.
670         - 'allow-nan':  accept  only  np.nan  values in  X.  Values  cannot  be
671           infinite.
672 
673         .. versionadded:: 0.20
674            ``force_all_finite`` accepts the string ``'allow-nan'``.
675 
676     ensure_2d : boolean (default=True)
677         Whether to make X at least 2d.
678 
679     allow_nd : boolean (default=False)
680         Whether to allow X.ndim > 2.
681 
682     multi_output : boolean (default=False)
683         Whether to allow 2-d y (array or sparse matrix). If false, y will be
684         validated as a vector. y cannot have np.nan or np.inf values if
685         multi_output=True.
686 
687     ensure_min_samples : int (default=1)
688         Make sure that X has a minimum number of samples in its first
689         axis (rows for a 2D array).
690 
691     ensure_min_features : int (default=1)
692         Make sure that the 2D array has some minimum number of features
693         (columns). The default value of 1 rejects empty datasets.
694         This check is only enforced when X has effectively 2 dimensions or
695         is originally 1D and ``ensure_2d`` is True. Setting to 0 disables
696         this check.
697 
698     y_numeric : boolean (default=False)
699         Whether to ensure that y has a numeric type. If dtype of y is object,
700         it is converted to float64. Should only be used for regression
701         algorithms.
702 
703     warn_on_dtype : boolean (default=False)
704         Raise DataConversionWarning if the dtype of the input data structure
705         does not match the requested dtype, causing a memory copy.
706 
707     estimator : str or estimator instance (default=None)
708         If passed, include the name of the estimator in warning messages.
709 
710     Returns
711     -------
712     X_converted : object
713         The converted and validated X.
714 
715     y_converted : object
716         The converted and validated y.
717     """
718     X = check_array(X, accept_sparse=accept_sparse,
719                     accept_large_sparse=accept_large_sparse,
720                     dtype=dtype, order=order, copy=copy,
721                     force_all_finite=force_all_finite,
722                     ensure_2d=ensure_2d, allow_nd=allow_nd,
723                     ensure_min_samples=ensure_min_samples,
724                     ensure_min_features=ensure_min_features,
725                     warn_on_dtype=warn_on_dtype,
726                     estimator=estimator)

728         y = check_array(y, 'csr', force_all_finite=True, ensure_2d=False,
729                         dtype=None)
730     else:
731         y = column_or_1d(y, warn=True)
732         _assert_all_finite(y)
733     if y_numeric and y.dtype.kind == 'O':
734         y = y.astype(np.float64)
735 
736     check_consistent_length(X, y)
737 
738     return X, y

741 def column_or_1d(y, warn=False):
742     """ Ravel column or 1d numpy array, else raises an error
743 
744     Parameters
745     ----------
746     y : array-like
747 
748     warn : boolean, default False
749        To control display of warnings.
750 
751     Returns
752     -------
753     y : array
754 
755     """
756     shape = np.shape(y)
757     if len(shape) == 1:
758         return np.ravel(y)
759     if len(shape) == 2 and shape[1] == 1:
760         if warn:
761             warnings.warn("A column-vector y was passed when a 1d array was"
762                           " expected. Please change the shape of y to "
763                           "(n_samples, ), for example using ravel().",
764                           DataConversionWarning, stacklevel=2)
765         return np.ravel(y)
766 
767     raise ValueError("bad input shape {0}".format(shape))

770 def check_random_state(seed):
771     """Turn seed into a np.random.RandomState instance
772 
773     Parameters
774     ----------
775     seed : None | int | instance of RandomState
776         If seed is None, return the RandomState singleton used by np.random.
777         If seed is an int, return a new RandomState instance seeded with seed.
778         If seed is already a RandomState instance, return it.
779         Otherwise raise ValueError.
780     """
781     if seed is None or seed is np.random:
782         return np.random.mtrand._rand
783     if isinstance(seed, (numbers.Integral, np.integer)):
784         return np.random.RandomState(seed)
785     if isinstance(seed, np.random.RandomState):
786         return seed
787     raise ValueError('%r cannot be used to seed a numpy.random.RandomState'
788                      ' instance' % seed)

169     def fit(self, X, y=None):
170         """Estimate model parameters with the EM algorithm.
171 
172         The method fits the model ``n_init`` times and sets the parameters with
173         which the model has the largest likelihood or lower bound. Within each
174         trial, the method iterates between E-step and M-step for ``max_iter``
175         times until the change of likelihood or lower bound is less than
176         ``tol``, otherwise, a ``ConvergenceWarning`` is raised.
177         If ``warm_start`` is ``True``, then ``n_init`` is ignored and a single
178         initialization is performed upon the first call. Upon consecutive
179         calls, training starts where it left off.
180 
181         Parameters
182         ----------
183         X : array-like, shape (n_samples, n_features)
184             List of n_features-dimensional data points. Each row
185             corresponds to a single data point.
186 
187         Returns
188         -------
189         self
190         """
191         self.fit_predict(X, y)
192         return self
193 
194     def fit_predict(self, X, y=None):
195         """Estimate model parameters using X and predict the labels for X.
196 
197         The method fits the model n_init times and sets the parameters with
198         which the model has the largest likelihood or lower bound. Within each
199         trial, the method iterates between E-step and M-step for `max_iter`
200         times until the change of likelihood or lower bound is less than
201         `tol`, otherwise, a `ConvergenceWarning` is raised. After fitting, it
202         predicts the most probable label for the input data points.
203 
204         .. versionadded:: 0.20
205 
206         Parameters
207         ----------
208         X : array-like, shape (n_samples, n_features)
209             List of n_features-dimensional data points. Each row
210             corresponds to a single data point.
211 
212         Returns
213         -------
214         labels : array, shape (n_samples,)
215             Component labels.
216         """
217         X = _check_X(X, self.n_components, ensure_min_samples=2)
218         self._check_initial_parameters(X)
219 
220         # if we enable warm_start, we will have a unique initialisation
221         do_init = not(self.warm_start and hasattr(self, 'converged_'))
222         n_init = self.n_init if do_init else 1
223 
224         max_lower_bound = -np.infty
225         self.converged_ = False
226 
227         random_state = check_random_state(self.random_state)
228 
229         n_samples, _ = X.shape
230         for init in range(n_init):
231             self._print_verbose_msg_init_beg(init)
232 
233             if do_init:
234                 self._initialize_parameters(X, random_state)
235 
236             lower_bound = (-np.infty if do_init else self.lower_bound_)
237 
238             for n_iter in range(1, self.max_iter + 1):
239                 prev_lower_bound = lower_bound
240 
241                 log_prob_norm, log_resp = self._e_step(X)
242                 self._m_step(X, log_resp)
243                 lower_bound = self._compute_lower_bound(
244                     log_resp, log_prob_norm)
245 
246                 change = lower_bound - prev_lower_bound
247                 self._print_verbose_msg_iter_end(n_iter, change)
248 
249                 if abs(change) < self.tol:
250                     self.converged_ = True
251                     break
252 
253             self._print_verbose_msg_init_end(lower_bound)
254 
255             if lower_bound > max_lower_bound:
256                 max_lower_bound = lower_bound
257                 best_params = self._get_parameters()
258                 best_n_iter = n_iter
259 
260         # Always do a final e-step to guarantee that the labels returned by
261         # fit_predict(X) are always consistent with fit(X).predict(X)
262         # for any value of max_iter and tol (and any random_state).
263         _, log_resp = self._e_step(X)
264 
265         if not self.converged_:
266             warnings.warn('Initialization %d did not converge. '
267                           'Try different init parameters, '
268                           'or increase max_iter, tol '
269                           'or check for degenerate data.'
270                           % (init + 1), ConvergenceWarning)
271 
272         self._set_parameters(best_params)
273         self.n_iter_ = best_n_iter
274         self.lower_bound_ = max_lower_bound
275 
276         return log_resp.argmax(axis=1)

I don't think the math is wrong or inconsistent.  I think it's a matter of `fit_predict` returning the fit from the last of `n_iter` iterations, when it should be returning the fit from the _best_ of the iterations. Seems good indeed. When looking quickly you can miss the fact that `_e_step` uses the parameters even if not passed as arguments because they are attributes of the estimator. That's what happened to me :)

64 def _generalized_average(U, V, average_method):
65     """Return a particular mean of two numbers."""
66     if average_method == "min":
67         return min(U, V)
68     elif average_method == "geometric":
69         return np.sqrt(U * V)
70     elif average_method == "arithmetic":

72     elif average_method == "max":

79 def contingency_matrix(labels_true, labels_pred, eps=None, sparse=False):
80     """Build a contingency matrix describing the relationship between labels.
81 
82     Parameters
83     ----------
84     labels_true : int array, shape = [n_samples]
85         Ground truth class labels to be used as a reference
86 
87     labels_pred : array-like of shape (n_samples,)
88         Cluster labels to evaluate
89 
90     eps : None or float, optional.
91         If a float, that value is added to all values in the contingency
92         matrix. This helps to stop NaN propagation.
93         If ``None``, nothing is adjusted.
94 
95     sparse : boolean, optional.
96         If True, return a sparse CSR continency matrix. If ``eps is not None``,
97         and ``sparse is True``, will throw ValueError.
98 
99         .. versionadded:: 0.18
100 
101     Returns
102     -------
103     contingency : {array-like, sparse}, shape=[n_classes_true, n_classes_pred]
104         Matrix :math:`C` such that :math:`C_{i, j}` is the number of samples in
105         true class :math:`i` and in predicted class :math:`j`. If
106         ``eps is None``, the dtype of this array will be integer. If ``eps`` is
107         given, the dtype will be float.
108         Will be a ``scipy.sparse.csr_matrix`` if ``sparse=True``.
109     """
110 
111     if eps is not None and sparse:
112         raise ValueError("Cannot set 'eps' when sparse=True")
113 
114     classes, class_idx = np.unique(labels_true, return_inverse=True)
115     clusters, cluster_idx = np.unique(labels_pred, return_inverse=True)
116     n_classes = classes.shape[0]
117     n_clusters = clusters.shape[0]
118     # Using coo_matrix to accelerate simple histogram calculation,
119     # i.e. bins are consecutive integers
120     # Currently, coo_matrix is faster than histogram2d for simple cases
121     contingency = sp.coo_matrix((np.ones(class_idx.shape[0]),
122                                  (class_idx, cluster_idx)),
123                                 shape=(n_classes, n_clusters),
124                                 dtype=np.int)
125     if sparse:
126         contingency = contingency.tocsr()
127         contingency.sum_duplicates()
128     else:
129         contingency = contingency.toarray()
130         if eps is not None:
131             # don't use += as contingency is integer
132             contingency = contingency + eps
133     return contingency

138 def adjusted_rand_score(labels_true, labels_pred):
139     """Rand index adjusted for chance.
140 
141     The Rand Index computes a similarity measure between two clusterings
142     by considering all pairs of samples and counting pairs that are
143     assigned in the same or different clusters in the predicted and
144     true clusterings.
145 
146     The raw RI score is then "adjusted for chance" into the ARI score
147     using the following scheme::
148 
149         ARI = (RI - Expected_RI) / (max(RI) - Expected_RI)
150 
151     The adjusted Rand index is thus ensured to have a value close to
152     0.0 for random labeling independently of the number of clusters and
153     samples and exactly 1.0 when the clusterings are identical (up to
154     a permutation).
155 
156     ARI is a symmetric measure::
157 
158         adjusted_rand_score(a, b) == adjusted_rand_score(b, a)
159 
160     Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <adjusted_rand_score>`.
161 
162     Parameters
163     ----------
164     labels_true : int array, shape = [n_samples]
165         Ground truth class labels to be used as a reference
166 
167     labels_pred : array-like of shape (n_samples,)
168         Cluster labels to evaluate
169 
170     Returns
171     -------
172     ari : float
173        Similarity score between -1.0 and 1.0. Random labelings have an ARI
174        close to 0.0. 1.0 stands for perfect match.
175 
176     Examples
177     --------
178 
179     Perfectly matching labelings have a score of 1 even
180 
181       >>> from sklearn.metrics.cluster import adjusted_rand_score
182       >>> adjusted_rand_score([0, 0, 1, 1], [0, 0, 1, 1])
183       1.0
184       >>> adjusted_rand_score([0, 0, 1, 1], [1, 1, 0, 0])
185       1.0
186 
187     Labelings that assign all classes members to the same clusters
188     are complete be not always pure, hence penalized::
189 
190       >>> adjusted_rand_score([0, 0, 1, 2], [0, 0, 1, 1])
191       0.57...
192 
193     ARI is symmetric, so labelings that have pure clusters with members
194     coming from the same classes but unnecessary splits are penalized::
195 
196       >>> adjusted_rand_score([0, 0, 1, 1], [0, 0, 1, 2])
197       0.57...
198 
199     If classes members are completely split across different clusters, the
200     assignment is totally incomplete, hence the ARI is very low::
201 
202       >>> adjusted_rand_score([0, 0, 0, 0], [0, 1, 2, 3])
203       0.0
204 
205     References
206     ----------
207 
208     .. [Hubert1985] L. Hubert and P. Arabie, Comparing Partitions,
209       Journal of Classification 1985
210       https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007%2FBF01908075
211 
212     .. [wk] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rand_index#Adjusted_Rand_index
213 
214     See also
215     --------
216     adjusted_mutual_info_score: Adjusted Mutual Information
217 
218     """
219     labels_true, labels_pred = check_clusterings(labels_true, labels_pred)
220     n_samples = labels_true.shape[0]
221     n_classes = np.unique(labels_true).shape[0]
222     n_clusters = np.unique(labels_pred).shape[0]
223 
224     # Special limit cases: no clustering since the data is not split;
225     # or trivial clustering where each document is assigned a unique cluster.
226     # These are perfect matches hence return 1.0.
227     if (n_classes == n_clusters == 1 or
228             n_classes == n_clusters == 0 or
229             n_classes == n_clusters == n_samples):
230         return 1.0
231 
232     # Compute the ARI using the contingency data
233     contingency = contingency_matrix(labels_true, labels_pred, sparse=True)
234     sum_comb_c = sum(_comb2(n_c) for n_c in np.ravel(contingency.sum(axis=1)))
235     sum_comb_k = sum(_comb2(n_k) for n_k in np.ravel(contingency.sum(axis=0)))
236     sum_comb = sum(_comb2(n_ij) for n_ij in contingency.data)
237 
238     prod_comb = (sum_comb_c * sum_comb_k) / _comb2(n_samples)
239     mean_comb = (sum_comb_k + sum_comb_c) / 2.
240     return (sum_comb - prod_comb) / (mean_comb - prod_comb)

243 def homogeneity_completeness_v_measure(labels_true, labels_pred, beta=1.0):
244     """Compute the homogeneity and completeness and V-Measure scores at once.
245 
246     Those metrics are based on normalized conditional entropy measures of
247     the clustering labeling to evaluate given the knowledge of a Ground
248     Truth class labels of the same samples.
249 
250     A clustering result satisfies homogeneity if all of its clusters
251     contain only data points which are members of a single class.
252 
253     A clustering result satisfies completeness if all the data points
254     that are members of a given class are elements of the same cluster.
255 
256     Both scores have positive values between 0.0 and 1.0, larger values
257     being desirable.
258 
259     Those 3 metrics are independent of the absolute values of the labels:
260     a permutation of the class or cluster label values won't change the
261     score values in any way.
262 
263     V-Measure is furthermore symmetric: swapping ``labels_true`` and
264     ``label_pred`` will give the same score. This does not hold for
265     homogeneity and completeness. V-Measure is identical to
266     :func:`normalized_mutual_info_score` with the arithmetic averaging
267     method.
268 
269     Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <homogeneity_completeness>`.
270 
271     Parameters
272     ----------
273     labels_true : int array, shape = [n_samples]
274         ground truth class labels to be used as a reference
275 
276     labels_pred : array-like of shape (n_samples,)
277         cluster labels to evaluate
278 
279     beta : float
280         Ratio of weight attributed to ``homogeneity`` vs ``completeness``.
281         If ``beta`` is greater than 1, ``completeness`` is weighted more
282         strongly in the calculation. If ``beta`` is less than 1,
283         ``homogeneity`` is weighted more strongly.
284 
285     Returns
286     -------
287     homogeneity : float
288        score between 0.0 and 1.0. 1.0 stands for perfectly homogeneous labeling
289 
290     completeness : float
291        score between 0.0 and 1.0. 1.0 stands for perfectly complete labeling
292 
293     v_measure : float
294         harmonic mean of the first two
295 
296     See also
297     --------
298     homogeneity_score
299     completeness_score
300     v_measure_score
301     """
302     labels_true, labels_pred = check_clusterings(labels_true, labels_pred)
303 
304     if len(labels_true) == 0:
305         return 1.0, 1.0, 1.0
306 
307     entropy_C = entropy(labels_true)
308     entropy_K = entropy(labels_pred)
309 
310     contingency = contingency_matrix(labels_true, labels_pred, sparse=True)
311     MI = mutual_info_score(None, None, contingency=contingency)
312 
313     homogeneity = MI / (entropy_C) if entropy_C else 1.0
314     completeness = MI / (entropy_K) if entropy_K else 1.0
315 
316     if homogeneity + completeness == 0.0:
317         v_measure_score = 0.0
318     else:
319         v_measure_score = ((1 + beta) * homogeneity * completeness
320                            / (beta * homogeneity + completeness))
321 
322     return homogeneity, completeness, v_measure_score

325 def homogeneity_score(labels_true, labels_pred):
326     """Homogeneity metric of a cluster labeling given a ground truth.
327 
328     A clustering result satisfies homogeneity if all of its clusters
329     contain only data points which are members of a single class.

565 def mutual_info_score(labels_true, labels_pred, contingency=None):
566     """Mutual Information between two clusterings.
567 
568     The Mutual Information is a measure of the similarity between two labels of
569     the same data. Where :math:`|U_i|` is the number of the samples
570     in cluster :math:`U_i` and :math:`|V_j|` is the number of the
571     samples in cluster :math:`V_j`, the Mutual Information
572     between clusterings :math:`U` and :math:`V` is given as:
573 
574     .. math::
575 
576         MI(U,V)=\\sum_{i=1}^{|U|} \\sum_{j=1}^{|V|} \\frac{|U_i\\cap V_j|}{N}
577         \\log\\frac{N|U_i \\cap V_j|}{|U_i||V_j|}
578 
579     This metric is independent of the absolute values of the labels:
580     a permutation of the class or cluster label values won't change the
581     score value in any way.
582 
583     This metric is furthermore symmetric: switching ``label_true`` with
584     ``label_pred`` will return the same score value. This can be useful to
585     measure the agreement of two independent label assignments strategies
586     on the same dataset when the real ground truth is not known.
587 
588     Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <mutual_info_score>`.
589 
590     Parameters
591     ----------
592     labels_true : int array, shape = [n_samples]
593         A clustering of the data into disjoint subsets.
594 
595     labels_pred : int array-like of shape (n_samples,)
596         A clustering of the data into disjoint subsets.
597 
598     contingency : {None, array, sparse matrix}, \
599                   shape = [n_classes_true, n_classes_pred]
600         A contingency matrix given by the :func:`contingency_matrix` function.
601         If value is ``None``, it will be computed, otherwise the given value is
602         used, with ``labels_true`` and ``labels_pred`` ignored.
603 
604     Returns
605     -------
606     mi : float
607        Mutual information, a non-negative value
608 
609     Notes
610     -----
611     The logarithm used is the natural logarithm (base-e).
612 
613     See also
614     --------
615     adjusted_mutual_info_score: Adjusted against chance Mutual Information
616     normalized_mutual_info_score: Normalized Mutual Information
617     """
618     if contingency is None:
619         labels_true, labels_pred = check_clusterings(labels_true, labels_pred)
620         contingency = contingency_matrix(labels_true, labels_pred, sparse=True)
621     else:
622         contingency = check_array(contingency,
623                                   accept_sparse=['csr', 'csc', 'coo'],
624                                   dtype=[int, np.int32, np.int64])
625 
626     if isinstance(contingency, np.ndarray):
627         # For an array
628         nzx, nzy = np.nonzero(contingency)
629         nz_val = contingency[nzx, nzy]
630     elif sp.issparse(contingency):
631         # For a sparse matrix
632         nzx, nzy, nz_val = sp.find(contingency)
633     else:
634         raise ValueError("Unsupported type for 'contingency': %s" %
635                          type(contingency))
636 
637     contingency_sum = contingency.sum()
638     pi = np.ravel(contingency.sum(axis=1))
639     pj = np.ravel(contingency.sum(axis=0))
640     log_contingency_nm = np.log(nz_val)
641     contingency_nm = nz_val / contingency_sum
642     # Don't need to calculate the full outer product, just for non-zeroes
643     outer = (pi.take(nzx).astype(np.int64, copy=False)
644              * pj.take(nzy).astype(np.int64, copy=False))
645     log_outer = -np.log(outer) + log(pi.sum()) + log(pj.sum())
646     mi = (contingency_nm * (log_contingency_nm - log(contingency_sum)) +
647           contingency_nm * log_outer)
648     return mi.sum()
649

651 def adjusted_mutual_info_score(labels_true, labels_pred,
652                                average_method='arithmetic'):
653     """Adjusted Mutual Information between two clusterings.
654 
655     Adjusted Mutual Information (AMI) is an adjustment of the Mutual
656     Information (MI) score to account for chance. It accounts for the fact that
657     the MI is generally higher for two clusterings with a larger number of
658     clusters, regardless of whether there is actually more information shared.
659     For two clusterings :math:`U` and :math:`V`, the AMI is given as::
660 
661         AMI(U, V) = [MI(U, V) - E(MI(U, V))] / [avg(H(U), H(V)) - E(MI(U, V))]
662 
663     This metric is independent of the absolute values of the labels:
664     a permutation of the class or cluster label values won't change the
665     score value in any way.
666 
667     This metric is furthermore symmetric: switching ``label_true`` with
668     ``label_pred`` will return the same score value. This can be useful to
669     measure the agreement of two independent label assignments strategies
670     on the same dataset when the real ground truth is not known.
671 
672     Be mindful that this function is an order of magnitude slower than other
673     metrics, such as the Adjusted Rand Index.
674 
675     Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <mutual_info_score>`.
676 
677     Parameters
678     ----------
679     labels_true : int array, shape = [n_samples]
680         A clustering of the data into disjoint subsets.
681 
682     labels_pred : int array-like of shape (n_samples,)
683         A clustering of the data into disjoint subsets.
684 
685     average_method : string, optional (default: 'arithmetic')
686         How to compute the normalizer in the denominator. Possible options
687         are 'min', 'geometric', 'arithmetic', and 'max'.
688 
689         .. versionadded:: 0.20
690 
691         .. versionchanged:: 0.22
692            The default value of ``average_method`` changed from 'max' to
693            'arithmetic'.
694 
695     Returns
696     -------
697     ami: float (upperlimited by 1.0)
698        The AMI returns a value of 1 when the two partitions are identical
699        (ie perfectly matched). Random partitions (independent labellings) have
700        an expected AMI around 0 on average hence can be negative.
701 
702     See also
703     --------
704     adjusted_rand_score: Adjusted Rand Index
705     mutual_info_score: Mutual Information (not adjusted for chance)
706 
707     Examples
708     --------
709 
710     Perfect labelings are both homogeneous and complete, hence have
711     score 1.0::
712 
713       >>> from sklearn.metrics.cluster import adjusted_mutual_info_score
714       >>> adjusted_mutual_info_score([0, 0, 1, 1], [0, 0, 1, 1])
715       ... # doctest: +SKIP
716       1.0
717       >>> adjusted_mutual_info_score([0, 0, 1, 1], [1, 1, 0, 0])
718       ... # doctest: +SKIP
719       1.0
720 
721     If classes members are completely split across different clusters,
722     the assignment is totally in-complete, hence the AMI is null::
723 
724       >>> adjusted_mutual_info_score([0, 0, 0, 0], [0, 1, 2, 3])
725       ... # doctest: +SKIP
726       0.0
727 
728     References
729     ----------
730     .. [1] `Vinh, Epps, and Bailey, (2010). Information Theoretic Measures for
731        Clusterings Comparison: Variants, Properties, Normalization and
732        Correction for Chance, JMLR
733        <http://jmlr.csail.mit.edu/papers/volume11/vinh10a/vinh10a.pdf>`_
734 
735     .. [2] `Wikipedia entry for the Adjusted Mutual Information
736        <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adjusted_Mutual_Information>`_
737 
738     """
739     labels_true, labels_pred = check_clusterings(labels_true, labels_pred)
740     n_samples = labels_true.shape[0]
741     classes = np.unique(labels_true)
742     clusters = np.unique(labels_pred)
743     # Special limit cases: no clustering since the data is not split.
744     # This is a perfect match hence return 1.0.
745     if (classes.shape[0] == clusters.shape[0] == 1 or
746             classes.shape[0] == clusters.shape[0] == 0):
747         return 1.0
748     contingency = contingency_matrix(labels_true, labels_pred, sparse=True)
749     contingency = contingency.astype(np.float64,
750                                      **_astype_copy_false(contingency))
751     # Calculate the MI for the two clusterings
752     mi = mutual_info_score(labels_true, labels_pred,
753                            contingency=contingency)
754     # Calculate the expected value for the mutual information
755     emi = expected_mutual_information(contingency, n_samples)
756     # Calculate entropy for each labeling
757     h_true, h_pred = entropy(labels_true), entropy(labels_pred)
758     normalizer = _generalized_average(h_true, h_pred, average_method)
759     denominator = normalizer - emi
760     # Avoid 0.0 / 0.0 when expectation equals maximum, i.e a perfect match.
761     # normalizer should always be >= emi, but because of floating-point
762     # representation, sometimes emi is slightly larger. Correct this
763     # by preserving the sign.
764     if denominator < 0:
765         denominator = min(denominator, -np.finfo('float64').eps)
766     else:
767         denominator = max(denominator, np.finfo('float64').eps)
768     ami = (mi - emi) / denominator
769     return ami

872 def fowlkes_mallows_score(labels_true, labels_pred, sparse=False):

876     the precision and recall::

881     points that belongs in the same clusters in both ``labels_true`` and
882     ``labels_pred``), ``FP`` is the number of **False Positive** (i.e. the
883     number of pair of points that belongs in the same clusters in
884     ``labels_true`` and not in ``labels_pred``) and ``FN`` is the number of
885     **False Negative** (i.e the number of pair of points that belongs in the
886     same clusters in ``labels_pred`` and not in ``labels_True``).
887 
888     The score ranges from 0 to 1. A high value indicates a good similarity
889     between two clusters.
890 
891     Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <fowlkes_mallows_scores>`.
892 
893     Parameters
894     ----------
895     labels_true : int array, shape = (``n_samples``,)
896         A clustering of the data into disjoint subsets.
897 
898     labels_pred : array, shape = (``n_samples``, )
899         A clustering of the data into disjoint subsets.
900 
901     sparse : bool
902         Compute contingency matrix internally with sparse matrix.
903 
904     Returns
905     -------
906     score : float
907        The resulting Fowlkes-Mallows score.
908 
909     Examples
910     --------
911 
912     Perfect labelings are both homogeneous and complete, hence have
913     score 1.0::
914 
915       >>> from sklearn.metrics.cluster import fowlkes_mallows_score
916       >>> fowlkes_mallows_score([0, 0, 1, 1], [0, 0, 1, 1])
917       1.0
918       >>> fowlkes_mallows_score([0, 0, 1, 1], [1, 1, 0, 0])
919       1.0
920 
921     If classes members are completely split across different clusters,
922     the assignment is totally random, hence the FMI is null::
923 
924       >>> fowlkes_mallows_score([0, 0, 0, 0], [0, 1, 2, 3])
925       0.0
926 
927     References
928     ----------
929     .. [1] `E. B. Fowkles and C. L. Mallows, 1983. "A method for comparing two
930        hierarchical clusterings". Journal of the American Statistical
931        Association
932        <http://wildfire.stat.ucla.edu/pdflibrary/fowlkes.pdf>`_
933 
934     .. [2] `Wikipedia entry for the Fowlkes-Mallows Index
935            <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fowlkes-Mallows_index>`_
936     """
937     labels_true, labels_pred = check_clusterings(labels_true, labels_pred)
938     n_samples, = labels_true.shape
939 
940     c = contingency_matrix(labels_true, labels_pred,
941                            sparse=True)
942     c = c.astype(np.int64, **_astype_copy_false(c))
943     tk = np.dot(c.data, c.data) - n_samples
944     pk = np.sum(np.asarray(c.sum(axis=0)).ravel() ** 2) - n_samples
945     qk = np.sum(np.asarray(c.sum(axis=1)).ravel() ** 2) - n_samples
946     return np.sqrt(tk / pk) * np.sqrt(tk / qk) if tk != 0. else 0.

950     """Calculates the entropy for a labeling.
951 
952     Parameters
953     ----------
954     labels : int array, shape = [n_samples]
955         The labels
956 
957     Notes
958     -----
959     The logarithm used is the natural logarithm (base-e).

961     if len(labels) == 0:
962         return 1.0
963     label_idx = np.unique(labels, return_inverse=True)[1]

965     pi = pi[pi > 0]

967     # log(a / b) should be calculated as log(a) - log(b) for
968     # possible loss of precision
969     return -np.sum((pi / pi_sum) * (np.log(pi) - log(pi_sum)))

problem_statement:
Cannot parse Greek characters (and possibly others) in parse_mathematica
The old Mathematica parser `mathematica` in the package `sympy.parsing.mathematica` was able to parse e.g. Greek characters. Hence the following example works fine:
```
from sympy.parsing.mathematica import mathematica
mathematica('λ')
Out[]: 
λ
```

As of SymPy v. 1.11, the `mathematica` function is deprecated, and is replaced by `parse_mathematica`. This function, however, seems unable to handle the simple example above:
```
from sympy.parsing.mathematica import parse_mathematica
parse_mathematica('λ')
Traceback (most recent call last):
...
File "<string>", line unknown
SyntaxError: unable to create a single AST for the expression
```

This appears to be due to a bug in `parse_mathematica`, which is why I have opened this issue.

Thanks in advance!

problem_statement:
convert_to seems to combine orthogonal units
Tested in sympy 1.4, not presently in a position to install 1.5+.
Simple example. Consider `J = kg*m**2/s**2 => J*s = kg*m**2/s`. The convert_to behavior is odd:
```
>>>convert_to(joule*second,joule)
    joule**(7/9)
```
I would expect the unchanged original expression back, an expression in terms of base units, or an error. It appears that convert_to can only readily handle conversions where the full unit expression is valid.

Note that the following three related examples give sensible results:
```
>>>convert_to(joule*second,joule*second)
    joule*second
```
```
>>>convert_to(J*s, kg*m**2/s)
    kg*m**2/s
```
```
>>>convert_to(J*s,mins)
    J*mins/60
```
hints_text:
Yes, this is a problem. When trying to convert into a unit that is not compatible, it should either do nothing (no conversion), or raise an exception. I personally don't see how the following makes sense:
```
>>> convert_to(meter, second) 
meter

```
I often do calculations with units as a failsafe check. When The operation checks out and delivers reasonable units, I take it as a sign that it went well. When it "silently" converts an expression into non-sensible units, this cannot be used as a failsafe check.
I am glad someone agrees this is a problem. I suggest that the physics.units package be disabled for now as it has serious flaws.

My solution is simply to use positive, real symbolic variables for units. I worry about the conversions myself. For example: `var('J m kg s Pa', positive=True, real=True)`. These behave as proper units and don't do anything mysterious. For unit conversions, I usually just use things like `.subs({J:kg*m**2/s**2})`. You could also use substitution using `.evalf()`.
> I suggest that the physics.units package be disabled for now

That seems a little drastic.

I don't use the units module but the docstring for `convert_to` says:
```
    Convert ``expr`` to the same expression with all of its units and quantities
    represented as factors of ``target_units``, whenever the dimension is compatible.
```
There are examples in the docstring showing that the `target_units` parameter can be a list and is intended to apply only to the relevant dimensions e.g.:
```

It's curious that this conversation has taken so long, when just 5 minutes of debugging have revealed this simple error:
https://github.com/sympy/sympy/blob/702bceaa0dde32193bfa9456df89eb63153a7538/sympy/physics/units/util.py#L33

`solve_least_squares` finds the solution to the matrix equation. In case no solution is found (like in `convert_to(joule*second, joule)`), it approximates to an inexact solution to the matrix system instead of raising an exception.

Simply changing it to `.solve_least_squares` to `.solve` should fix this issue.

445 class CombinedExpression(SQLiteNumericMixin, Expression):
446 
447     def __init__(self, lhs, connector, rhs, output_field=None):
448         super().__init__(output_field=output_field)
449         self.connector = connector
450         self.lhs = lhs
451         self.rhs = rhs
452 
453     def __repr__(self):
454         return "<{}: {}>".format(self.__class__.__name__, self)
455 
456     def __str__(self):
457         return "{} {} {}".format(self.lhs, self.connector, self.rhs)
458 
459     def get_source_expressions(self):
460         return [self.lhs, self.rhs]
461 
462     def set_source_expressions(self, exprs):
463         self.lhs, self.rhs = exprs
464 
465     def _resolve_output_field(self):
466         try:
467             return super()._resolve_output_field()
468         except FieldError:
469             combined_type = _resolve_combined_type(
470                 self.connector,
471                 type(self.lhs.output_field),
472                 type(self.rhs.output_field),
473             )
474             if combined_type is None:
475                 raise
476             return combined_type()
477 
478     def as_sql(self, compiler, connection):
479         expressions = []
480         expression_params = []
481         sql, params = compiler.compile(self.lhs)
482         expressions.append(sql)
483         expression_params.extend(params)
484         sql, params = compiler.compile(self.rhs)
485         expressions.append(sql)
486         expression_params.extend(params)
487         # order of precedence
488         expression_wrapper = '(%s)'
489         sql = connection.ops.combine_expression(self.connector, expressions)
490         return expression_wrapper % sql, expression_params
491 
492     def resolve_expression(self, query=None, allow_joins=True, reuse=None, summarize=False, for_save=False):
493         lhs = self.lhs.resolve_expression(query, allow_joins, reuse, summarize, for_save)
494         rhs = self.rhs.resolve_expression(query, allow_joins, reuse, summarize, for_save)
495         if not isinstance(self, (DurationExpression, TemporalSubtraction)):
496             try:
497                 lhs_type = lhs.output_field.get_internal_type()
498             except (AttributeError, FieldError):
499                 lhs_type = None
500             try:
501                 rhs_type = rhs.output_field.get_internal_type()
502             except (AttributeError, FieldError):
503                 rhs_type = None
504             if 'DurationField' in {lhs_type, rhs_type} and lhs_type != rhs_type:
505                 return DurationExpression(self.lhs, self.connector, self.rhs).resolve_expression(
506                     query, allow_joins, reuse, summarize, for_save,
507                 )
508             datetime_fields = {'DateField', 'DateTimeField', 'TimeField'}
509             if self.connector == self.SUB and lhs_type in datetime_fields and lhs_type == rhs_type:
510                 return TemporalSubtraction(self.lhs, self.rhs).resolve_expression(
511                     query, allow_joins, reuse, summarize, for_save,
512                 )
513         c = self.copy()
514         c.is_summary = summarize
515         c.lhs = lhs
516         c.rhs = rhs
517         return c

520 class DurationExpression(CombinedExpression):
521     def compile(self, side, compiler, connection):
522         try:
523             output = side.output_field
524         except FieldError:
525             pass
526         else:
527             if output.get_internal_type() == 'DurationField':
528                 sql, params = compiler.compile(side)
529                 return connection.ops.format_for_duration_arithmetic(sql), params
530         return compiler.compile(side)

532     def as_sql(self, compiler, connection):
533         if connection.features.has_native_duration_field:
534             return super().as_sql(compiler, connection)
535         connection.ops.check_expression_support(self)
536         expressions = []
537         expression_params = []
538         sql, params = self.compile(self.lhs, compiler, connection)
539         expressions.append(sql)
540         expression_params.extend(params)
541         sql, params = self.compile(self.rhs, compiler, connection)
542         expressions.append(sql)
543         expression_params.extend(params)
544         # order of precedence
545         expression_wrapper = '(%s)'
546         sql = connection.ops.combine_duration_expression(self.connector, expressions)
547         return expression_wrapper % sql, expression_params

549     def as_sqlite(self, compiler, connection, **extra_context):
550         sql, params = self.as_sql(compiler, connection, **extra_context)

552             try:

554                 rhs_type = self.rhs.output_field.get_internal_type()
555             except (AttributeError, FieldError):
556                 pass
557             else:
558                 allowed_fields = {
559                     'DecimalField', 'DurationField', 'FloatField', 'IntegerField',
560                 }
561                 if lhs_type not in allowed_fields or rhs_type not in allowed_fields:
562                     raise DatabaseError(
563                         f'Invalid arguments for operator {self.connector}.'
564                     )

654 @deconstructible(path='django.db.models.Func')
655 class Func(SQLiteNumericMixin, Expression):
656     """An SQL function call."""
657     function = None
658     template = '%(function)s(%(expressions)s)'
659     arg_joiner = ', '
660     arity = None  # The number of arguments the function accepts.
661 
662     def __init__(self, *expressions, output_field=None, **extra):
663         if self.arity is not None and len(expressions) != self.arity:
664             raise TypeError(
665                 "'%s' takes exactly %s %s (%s given)" % (
666                     self.__class__.__name__,
667                     self.arity,
668                     "argument" if self.arity == 1 else "arguments",
669                     len(expressions),
670                 )
671             )
672         super().__init__(output_field=output_field)
673         self.source_expressions = self._parse_expressions(*expressions)
674         self.extra = extra
675 
676     def __repr__(self):
677         args = self.arg_joiner.join(str(arg) for arg in self.source_expressions)
678         extra = {**self.extra, **self._get_repr_options()}
679         if extra:
680             extra = ', '.join(str(key) + '=' + str(val) for key, val in sorted(extra.items()))
681             return "{}({}, {})".format(self.__class__.__name__, args, extra)
682         return "{}({})".format(self.__class__.__name__, args)
683 
684     def _get_repr_options(self):
685         """Return a dict of extra __init__() options to include in the repr."""
686         return {}
687 
688     def get_source_expressions(self):
689         return self.source_expressions
690 
691     def set_source_expressions(self, exprs):
692         self.source_expressions = exprs
693 
694     def resolve_expression(self, query=None, allow_joins=True, reuse=None, summarize=False, for_save=False):
695         c = self.copy()
696         c.is_summary = summarize
697         for pos, arg in enumerate(c.source_expressions):
698             c.source_expressions[pos] = arg.resolve_expression(query, allow_joins, reuse, summarize, for_save)
699         return c
700 
701     def as_sql(self, compiler, connection, function=None, template=None, arg_joiner=None, **extra_context):
702         connection.ops.check_expression_support(self)
703         sql_parts = []
704         params = []
705         for arg in self.source_expressions:
706             try:
707                 arg_sql, arg_params = compiler.compile(arg)
708             except EmptyResultSet:
709                 empty_result_set_value = getattr(arg, 'empty_result_set_value', NotImplemented)
710                 if empty_result_set_value is NotImplemented:
711                     raise
712                 arg_sql, arg_params = compiler.compile(Value(empty_result_set_value))
713             sql_parts.append(arg_sql)
714             params.extend(arg_params)
715         data = {**self.extra, **extra_context}
716         # Use the first supplied value in this order: the parameter to this
717         # method, a value supplied in __init__()'s **extra (the value in
718         # `data`), or the value defined on the class.
719         if function is not None:
720             data['function'] = function
721         else:
722             data.setdefault('function', self.function)
723         template = template or data.get('template', self.template)
724         arg_joiner = arg_joiner or data.get('arg_joiner', self.arg_joiner)
725         data['expressions'] = data['field'] = arg_joiner.join(sql_parts)
726         return template % data, params
727 
728     def copy(self):
729         copy = super().copy()
730         copy.source_expressions = self.source_expressions[:]
731         copy.extra = self.extra.copy()
732         return copy

problem_statement:
Subquery.as_sql() generates invalid SQL.
Description
	 
		(last modified by M1ha Shvn)
	 
Since ​this commit Subquery.as_sql(...) method returns incorrect SQL removing first and last symbols instead of absent breakets. Adding Subquery().query.subquery = True attribute fixes the problem. From my point of view, it should be set in Subquery constructor.
from django.db import connection
from apps.models import App
q = Subquery(App.objects.all())
print(str(q.query))
# Output SQL is valid:
# 'SELECT "apps_app"."id", "apps_app"."name" FROM "apps_app"'
print(q.as_sql(q.query.get_compiler('default'), connection))
# Outptut SQL is invalid (no S letter at the beggining and " symbol at the end):
# ('(ELECT "apps_app"."id", "apps_app"."name" FROM "apps_app)', ())
q.query.subquery = True
print(q.as_sql(q.query.get_compiler('default'), connection))
# Outputs correct result
('(SELECT "apps_app"."id", "apps_app"."name" FROM "apps_app")', ())

UsernameValidator allows trailing newline in usernames
Description
	
ASCIIUsernameValidator and UnicodeUsernameValidator use the regex 
r'^[\w.@+-]+$'
The intent is to only allow alphanumeric characters as well as ., @, +, and -. However, a little known quirk of Python regexes is that $ will also match a trailing newline. Therefore, the user name validators will accept usernames which end with a newline. You can avoid this behavior by instead using \A and \Z to terminate regexes. For example, the validator regex could be changed to
r'\A[\w.@+-]+\Z'
in order to reject usernames that end with a newline.
I am not sure how to officially post a patch, but the required change is trivial - using the regex above in the two validators in contrib.auth.validators.
