655     def matchnodes(self, matching, names):
656         self.trace("matchnodes", matching, names)
657         self.trace.root.indent += 1
658         nodes = self._matchnodes(matching, names)
659         num = len(nodes)
660         self.trace("matchnodes finished -> ", num, "nodes")
661         self.trace.root.indent -= 1
662         if num == 0:
663             raise NoMatch(matching, names[:1])
664         return nodes

666     def _matchnodes(self, matching, names):
667         if not matching or not names:
668             return matching
669         name = names[0]
670         assert name
671         nextnames = names[1:]
672         resultnodes = []
673         for node in matching:
674             if isinstance(node, nodes.Item):
675                 if not names:
676                     resultnodes.append(node)
677                 continue

FeatureUnion not working when aggregating data and pandas transform output selected
### Describe the bug

I would like to use `pandas` transform output and use a custom transformer in a feature union which aggregates data. When I'm using this combination I got an error. When I use default `numpy` output it works fine.

### Steps/Code to Reproduce

```python
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.base import BaseEstimator, TransformerMixin
from sklearn import set_config
from sklearn.pipeline import make_union

index = pd.date_range(start="2020-01-01", end="2020-01-05", inclusive="left", freq="H")
data = pd.DataFrame(index=index, data=[10] * len(index), columns=["value"])
data["date"] = index.date


class MyTransformer(BaseEstimator, TransformerMixin):
    def fit(self, X: pd.DataFrame, y: pd.Series | None = None, **kwargs):
        return self

    def transform(self, X: pd.DataFrame, y: pd.Series | None = None) -> pd.DataFrame:
        return X["value"].groupby(X["date"]).sum()


# This works.
set_config(transform_output="default")
print(make_union(MyTransformer()).fit_transform(data))

# This does not work.
set_config(transform_output="pandas")
print(make_union(MyTransformer()).fit_transform(data))
```

159     is manually disabled.

168 class _SetOutputMixin:
169     """Mixin that dynamically wraps methods to return container based on config.
170 
171     Currently `_SetOutputMixin` wraps `transform` and `fit_transform` and configures
172     it based on `set_output` of the global configuration.
173 
174     `set_output` is only defined if `get_feature_names_out` is defined and
175     `auto_wrap_output_keys` is the default value.
176     """
177 
178     def __init_subclass__(cls, auto_wrap_output_keys=("transform",), **kwargs):
179         super().__init_subclass__(**kwargs)
180 
181         # Dynamically wraps `transform` and `fit_transform` and configure it's
182         # output based on `set_output`.

201                 continue
202             cls._sklearn_auto_wrap_output_keys.add(key)
203 
204             # Only wrap methods defined by cls itself
205             if method not in cls.__dict__:
206                 continue

208             setattr(cls, method, wrapped_method)

As noted in the [glossery](https://scikit-learn.org/dev/glossary.html#term-transform), Scikit-learn transformers expects that `transform`'s output have the same number of samples as the input. This exception is held in `FeatureUnion` when processing data and tries to make sure that the output index is the same as the input index. In principle, we can have a less restrictive requirement and only set the index if it is not defined.

To better understand your use case, how do you intend to use the `FeatureUnion` in the overall pipeline?


> Scikit-learn transformers expects that transform's output have the same number of samples as the input

I haven't known that. Good to know. What is the correct way to aggregate or drop rows in a pipeline? Isn't that supported?

> To better understand your use case, how do you intend to use the FeatureUnion in the overall pipeline?

The actual use case: I have a time series (`price`) with hourly frequency. It is a single series with a datetime index. I have built a dataframe with pipeline and custom transformers (by also violating the rule to have same number of inputs and outputs) which aggregates the data (calculates daily mean, and some moving average of daily means) then I have transformed back to hourly frequency (using same values for all the hours of a day). So the dataframe has (`date`, `price`, `mean`, `moving_avg`) columns at that point with hourly frequency ("same number input/output" rule violated again). After that I have added the problematic `FeatureUnion`. One part of the union simply drops `price` and "collapses" the remaining part to daily data (as I said all the remaining columns has the same values on the same day). On the other part of the feature union I calculate a standard devition between `price` and `moving_avg` on daily basis. So I have the (`date`, `mean`, `moving_avg`) on the left side of the feature union and an `std` on the right side. Both have daily frequency. I would like to have a dataframe with (`date`, `mean`, `moving_avg`, `std`) at the end of the transformation.
As I see there is the same "problem" in `ColumnTransfromer`.
I have a look at how `scikit-learn` encapsulates output into a `DataFrame` and found this code block:

https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/blob/main/sklearn/utils/_set_output.py#L55-L62

Is there any reason to set index here? If transformer returned a `DataFrame` this already has some kind of index. Why should we restore the original input index? What is the use case when a transformer changes the `DataFrame`'s index and `scikit-learn` has to restore it automatically to the input index?

With index restoration it is also expected for transformers that index should not be changed (or if it is changed by transformer then `scikit-learn` restores the original one which could be a bit unintuitive). Is this an intended behaviour?

What is the design decision to not allow changing index and row count in data by transformers? In time series problems I think it is very common to aggregate raw data and modify original index.

2 Module to implement integration of uni/bivariate polynomials over
3 2D Polytopes(Polygons).
4 
5 Uses evaluation techniques as described in Chin et al(2015)[1]
6 
7 References
8 ===========
9 [1] : http://dilbert.engr.ucdavis.edu/~suku/quadrature/cls-integration.pdf
10 """
11

13

15

24 def polytope_integrate(poly, expr, **kwargs):
25     """Integrates homogeneous functions over polytopes.
26 
27     This function accepts the polytope in `poly` (currently only polygons are
28     implemented) and the function in `expr` (currently only
29     univariate/bivariate polynomials are implemented) and returns the exact
30     integral of `expr` over `poly`.
31     Parameters
32     ==========
33     poly : The input Polygon.
34     expr : The input polynomial.
35 
36     Optional Parameters:
37     clockwise : Binary value to sort input points of the polygon clockwise.
38     max_degree : The maximum degree of any monomial of the input polynomial.
39     Examples
40     ========
41     >>> from sympy.abc import x, y
42     >>> from sympy.geometry.polygon import Polygon
43     >>> from sympy.geometry.point import Point
44     >>> from sympy.integrals.intpoly import polytope_integrate
45     >>> polygon = Polygon(Point(0,0), Point(0,1), Point(1,1), Point(1,0))
46     >>> polys = [1, x, y, x*y, x**2*y, x*y**2]
47     >>> expr = x*y
48     >>> polytope_integrate(polygon, expr)
49     1/4
50     >>> polytope_integrate(polygon, polys, max_degree=3)
51     {1: 1, x: 1/2, y: 1/2, x*y: 1/4, x*y**2: 1/6, x**2*y: 1/6}
52     """
53     clockwise = kwargs.get('clockwise', False)
54     max_degree = kwargs.get('max_degree', None)
55 
56     if clockwise is True and isinstance(poly, Polygon):
57         poly = clockwise_sort(poly)
58 
59     expr = S(expr)
60 
61     if isinstance(poly, Polygon):
62         # For Vertex Representation
63         hp_params = hyperplane_parameters(poly)
64         facets = poly.sides
65     else:
66         # For Hyperplane Representation
67         plen = len(poly)
68         intersections = [intersection(poly[(i - 1) % plen], poly[i])
69                          for i in range(0, plen)]
70         hp_params = poly
71         lints = len(intersections)
72         facets = [Segment2D(intersections[i], intersections[(i + 1) % lints])
73                   for i in range(0, lints)]
74 
75     if max_degree is not None:
76         result = {}
77         if not isinstance(expr, list):
78             raise TypeError('Input polynomials must be list of expressions')
79         result_dict = main_integrate(0, facets, hp_params, max_degree)
80         for polys in expr:
81             if polys not in result:
82                 if polys is S.Zero:
83                     result[S.Zero] = S.Zero
84                     continue
85                 integral_value = S.Zero
86                 monoms = decompose(polys, separate=True)
87                 for monom in monoms:
88                     if monom.is_number:
89                         integral_value += result_dict[1] * monom
90                     else:
91                         coeff = LC(monom)
92                         integral_value += result_dict[monom / coeff] * coeff
93                 result[polys] = integral_value
94         return result
95 
96     return main_integrate(expr, facets, hp_params)
97

99 def main_integrate(expr, facets, hp_params, max_degree=None):
100     """Function to translate the problem of integrating univariate/bivariate
101     polynomials over a 2-Polytope to integrating over it's boundary facets.
102     This is done using Generalized Stokes Theorem and Euler Theorem.
103 
104     Parameters
105     ===========
106     expr : The input polynomial
107     facets : Facets(Line Segments) of the 2-Polytope
108     hp_params : Hyperplane Parameters of the facets
109 
110     Optional Parameters:
111     max_degree : The maximum degree of any monomial of the input polynomial.
112 
113     >>> from sympy.abc import x, y
114     >>> from sympy.integrals.intpoly import main_integrate,\
115     hyperplane_parameters
116     >>> from sympy.geometry.polygon import Polygon
117     >>> from sympy.geometry.point import Point
118     >>> triangle = Polygon(Point(0, 3), Point(5, 3), Point(1, 1))
119     >>> facets = triangle.sides
120     >>> hp_params = hyperplane_parameters(triangle)
121     >>> main_integrate(x**2 + y**2, facets, hp_params)
122     325/6
123     """
124     dims = (x, y)
125     dim_length = len(dims)
126     result = {}
127     integral_value = S.Zero
128 
129     if max_degree:
130         y_degree = max_degree
131         grad_terms = [[0, 0, 0, 0]] + \
132             gradient_terms(max_degree)
133 
134         for facet_count, hp in enumerate(hp_params):
135             a, b = hp[0], hp[1]
136             x0 = facets[facet_count].points[0]
137 
138             for i, monom in enumerate(grad_terms):
139                 #  Every monomial is a tuple :
140                 #  (term, x_degree, y_degree, value over boundary)
141                 m, x_d, y_d, _ = monom
142                 value = result.get(m, None)
143                 if b is S.Zero:
144                     value_over_boundary = S.Zero
145                 else:
146                     value_over_boundary = \
147                         integration_reduction_dynamic(facets, facet_count, a,
148                                                       b, m, dims, x_d, y_d,
149                                                       y_degree, x0,
150                                                       grad_terms, i)
151                 monom[3] = value_over_boundary
152                 degree = x_d + y_d
153                 if value is not None:
154                     result[m] += value_over_boundary * \
155                                         (b / norm(a)) / (dim_length + degree)
156                 else:
157                     result[m] = value_over_boundary * \
158                                 (b / norm(a)) / (dim_length + degree)
159         return result
160     else:
161         polynomials = decompose(expr)
162         for deg in polynomials:
163             poly_contribute = S.Zero
164             facet_count = 0
165             for hp in hp_params:
166                 value_over_boundary = integration_reduction(facets,
167                                                             facet_count,
168                                                             hp[0], hp[1],
169                                                             polynomials[deg],
170                                                             dims, deg)
171                 poly_contribute += value_over_boundary * (hp[1] / norm(hp[0]))
172                 facet_count += 1
173             poly_contribute /= (dim_length + deg)
174             integral_value += poly_contribute
175     return integral_value
176

178 def integration_reduction(facets, index, a, b, expr, dims, degree):
179     """Helper method for main_integrate. Returns the value of the input
180     expression evaluated over the polytope facet referenced by a given index.
181 
182     Parameters
183     ===========
184     facets : List of facets of the polytope.
185     index : Index referencing the facet to integrate the expression over.
186     a : Hyperplane parameter denoting direction.
187     b : Hyperplane parameter denoting distance.
188     expr : The expression to integrate over the facet.
189     dims : List of symbols denoting axes.
190     degree : Degree of the homogeneous polynomial.
191 
192     >>> from sympy.abc import x, y
193     >>> from sympy.integrals.intpoly import integration_reduction,\
194     hyperplane_parameters
195     >>> from sympy.geometry.point import Point
196     >>> from sympy.geometry.polygon import Polygon
197     >>> triangle = Polygon(Point(0, 3), Point(5, 3), Point(1, 1))
198     >>> facets = triangle.sides
199     >>> a, b = hyperplane_parameters(triangle)[0]
200     >>> integration_reduction(facets, 0, a, b, 1, (x, y), 0)
201     5
202     """
203     if expr == S.Zero:
204         return expr
205 
206     a, b = (S(a[0]), S(a[1])), S(b)
207 
208     value = S.Zero
209     x0 = facets[index].points[0]
210     m = len(facets)
211     gens = (x, y)
212 
213     inner_product = diff(expr, gens[0]) * x0[0] + diff(expr, gens[1]) * x0[1]
214 
215     if inner_product != 0:
216         value += integration_reduction(facets, index, a, b,
217                                        inner_product, dims, degree - 1)
218 
219     value += left_integral(m, index, facets, x0, expr, gens)
220 
221     return value/(len(dims) + degree - 1)
222 
223 
224 def left_integral(m, index, facets, x0, expr, gens):
225     """Computes the left integral of Eq 10 in Chin et al.
226     For the 2D case, the integral is just an evaluation of the polynomial
227     at the intersection of two facets which is multiplied by the distance
228     between the first point of facet and that intersection.
229 
230     Parameters
231     ===========
232     m : No. of hyperplanes.
233     index : Index of facet to find intersections with.
234     facets : List of facets(Line Segments in 2D case).
235     x0 : First point on facet referenced by index.
236     expr : Input polynomial
237     gens : Generators which generate the polynomial
238 
239     >>> from sympy.abc import x, y
240     >>> from sympy.integrals.intpoly import left_integral
241     >>> from sympy.geometry.point import Point
242     >>> from sympy.geometry.polygon import Polygon
243     >>> triangle = Polygon(Point(0, 3), Point(5, 3), Point(1, 1))
244     >>> facets = triangle.sides
245     >>> left_integral(3, 0, facets, facets[0].points[0], 1, (x, y))
246     5
247     """
248     value = S.Zero
249     for j in range(0, m):
250         intersect = ()
251         if j == (index - 1) % m or j == (index + 1) % m:
252             intersect = intersection(facets[index], facets[j])
253         if intersect:
254             distance_origin = norm(tuple(map(lambda x, y: x - y,
255                                              intersect, x0)))
256             if is_vertex(intersect):
257                 if isinstance(expr, Expr):
258                     if len(gens) == 3:
259                         expr_dict = {gens[0]: intersect[0],
260                                      gens[1]: intersect[1],
261                                      gens[2]: intersect[2]}
262                     else:
263                         expr_dict = {gens[0]: intersect[0],
264                                      gens[1]: intersect[1]}
265                     value += distance_origin * expr.subs(expr_dict)
266                 else:
267                     value += distance_origin * expr
268     return value
269

271 def integration_reduction_dynamic(facets, index, a, b, expr,
272                                   dims, x_degree, y_degree, max_y_degree,
273                                   x0, monomial_values, monom_index):
274     """The same integration_reduction function which uses a dynamic
275     programming approach to compute terms by using the values of the integral
276     the gradient of previous terms.
277 
278     Parameters
279     ===========
280     facets : Facets of 2-Polytope
281     index : Index of facet to find intersections with.(Used in left_integral())
282     a, b : Hyperplane parameters
283     expr : Input monomial
284     dims : Tuple denoting axes variables
285     x_degree : Exponent of 'x' in expr
286     y_degree : Exponent of 'y' in expr
287     max_y_degree : Maximum y-exponent of any monomial in monomial_values
288     x0 : First point on facets[index]
289     monomial_values : List of monomial values constituting the polynomial
290     monom_index : Index of monomial whose integration is being found.
291 
292     >>> from sympy.abc import x, y
293     >>> from sympy.integrals.intpoly import integration_reduction_dynamic,\
294     hyperplane_parameters, gradient_terms
295     >>> from sympy.geometry.point import Point
296     >>> from sympy.geometry.polygon import Polygon
297     >>> triangle = Polygon(Point(0, 3), Point(5, 3), Point(1, 1))
298     >>> facets = triangle.sides
299     >>> a, b = hyperplane_parameters(triangle)[0]
300     >>> x0 = facets[0].points[0]
301     >>> monomial_values = [[0, 0, 0, 0], [1, 0, 0, 5],\
302                            [y, 0, 1, 15], [x, 1, 0, None]]
303     >>> integration_reduction_dynamic(facets, 0, a, b, x, (x, y), 1, 0, 1, x0,\
304                                       monomial_values, 3)
305     25/2
306     """
307     expr = S(expr)
308     value = S.Zero
309     degree = x_degree + y_degree
310     m = len(facets)
311     gens = (x, y)
312     if expr == S.Zero:
313         return expr
314 
315     if not expr.is_number:
316         a, b = (S(a[0]), S(a[1])), S(b)
317 
318         x_index = monom_index - max_y_degree + \
319             x_degree - 2 if x_degree >= 1 else 0
320         y_index = monom_index - 1 if y_degree >= 1 else 0
321 
322         x_value, y_value =\
323             monomial_values[x_index][3], monomial_values[y_index][3]
324 
325         value += x_degree * x_value * x0[0] + y_degree * y_value * x0[1]
326 
327     value += left_integral(m, index, facets, x0, expr, gens)
328 
329     return value/(len(dims) + degree - 1)
330

332 def gradient_terms(binomial_power=0):
333     """Returns a list of all the possible
334     monomials between 0 and y**binomial_power
335 
336     Parameters
337     ===========
338     binomial_power : Power upto which terms are generated.
339 
340     Examples
341     ========
342     >>> from sympy.abc import x, y
343     >>> from sympy.integrals.intpoly import gradient_terms
344     >>> gradient_terms(2)
345     [[1, 0, 0, None], [y, 0, 1, None], [y**2, 0, 2, None], [x, 1, 0, None],\
346     [x*y, 1, 1, None], [x**2, 2, 0, None]]
347 
348     """
349     terms = []
350     for x_count in range(0, binomial_power + 1):
351         for y_count in range(0, binomial_power - x_count + 1):
352             terms.append([x**x_count*y**y_count,
353                           x_count, y_count, None])
354     return terms

357 def hyperplane_parameters(poly):
358     """A helper function to return the hyperplane parameters
359     of which the facets of the polygon are a part of.
360     Currently works for only 2-Polytopes.
361     Parameters
362     ==========
363     poly : The input Polygon
364 
365     Examples
366     ========
367     >>> from sympy.geometry.point import Point
368     >>> from sympy.geometry.polygon import Polygon
369     >>> from sympy.integrals.intpoly import hyperplane_parameters
370     >>> hyperplane_parameters(Polygon(Point(0, 3), Point(5, 3), Point(1, 1)))
371     [((0, 1), 3), ((1, -2), -1), ((-2, -1), -3)]
372     """
373     vertices = list(poly.vertices) + [poly.vertices[0]]  # Close the polygon.
374     params = [None] * (len(vertices) - 1)
375     for i in range(len(vertices) - 1):
376         v1 = vertices[i]
377         v2 = vertices[i + 1]
378 
379         a1 = v1[1] - v2[1]
380         a2 = v2[0] - v1[0]
381         b = v2[0] * v1[1] - v2[1] * v1[0]
382 
383         factor = gcd_list([a1, a2, b])
384 
385         b = S(b)/factor
386         a = (S(a1)/factor, S(a2)/factor)
387         params[i] = (a, b)
388 
389     return params

392 def best_origin(a, b, lineseg, expr):
393     """Helper method for polytope_integrate.
394     Returns a point on the lineseg whose vector inner product with the
395     divergence of `expr` yields an expression with the least maximum
396     total power.
397     Parameters
398     ==========
399     a : Hyperplane parameter denoting direction.
400     b : Hyperplane parameter denoting distance.
401     lineseg : Line segment on which to find the origin.
402     expr : The expression which determines the best point.
403     Algorithm(currently works only for 2D use case)
404     ===============================================
405     1 > Firstly, check for edge cases. Here that would refer to vertical
406         or horizontal lines.
407 
408     2 > If input expression is a polynomial containing more than one generator
409         then find out the total power of each of the generators.
410 
411         x**2 + 3 + x*y + x**4*y**5 ---> {x: 7, y: 6}
412 
413         If expression is a constant value then pick the first boundary point
414         of the line segment.
415 
416     3 > First check if a point exists on the line segment where the value of
417         the highest power generator becomes 0. If not check if the value of
418         the next highest becomes 0. If none becomes 0 within line segment
419         constraints then pick the first boundary point of the line segement.
420         Actually, any point lying on the segment can be picked as best origin
421         in the last case.
422     Examples
423     ========
424     >>> from sympy.integrals.intpoly import best_origin
425     >>> from sympy.abc import x, y
426     >>> from sympy.geometry.line import Segment2D
427     >>> from sympy.geometry.point import Point
428     >>> l = Segment2D(Point(0, 3), Point(1, 1))
429     >>> expr = x**3*y**7
430     >>> best_origin((2, 1), 3, l, expr)

538 def decompose(expr, separate=False):
539     """Decomposes an input polynomial into homogeneous ones of
540     smaller or equal degree.
541     Returns a dictionary with keys as the degree of the smaller
542     constituting polynomials. Values are the constituting polynomials.
543     Parameters
544     ==========
545     expr : Polynomial(SymPy expression)
546 
547     Optional Parameters :
548 
549     separate : If True then simply return a list of the constituent monomials
550                If not then break up the polynomial into constituent homogeneous
551                polynomials.
552     Examples
553     ========
554     >>> from sympy.abc import x, y
555     >>> from sympy.integrals.intpoly import decompose
556     >>> decompose(x**2 + x*y + x + y + x**3*y**2 + y**5)
557     {1: x + y, 2: x**2 + x*y, 5: x**3*y**2 + y**5}
558     >>> decompose(x**2 + x*y + x + y + x**3*y**2 + y**5, True)
559     [x, y, x**2, y**5, x*y, x**3*y**2]
560     """
561     expr = S(expr)
562     poly_dict = {}
563 
564     if isinstance(expr, Expr) and not expr.is_number:
565         if expr.is_Symbol:
566             poly_dict[1] = expr
567         elif expr.is_Add:
568             symbols = expr.atoms(Symbol)
569             degrees = [(sum(degree_list(monom, *symbols)), monom)
570                        for monom in expr.args]
571             if separate:
572                 return [monom[1] for monom in degrees]
573             else:
574                 for monom in degrees:
575                     degree, term = monom
576                     if poly_dict.get(degree):
577                         poly_dict[degree] += term
578                     else:
579                         poly_dict[degree] = term
580         elif expr.is_Pow:
581             _, degree = expr.args
582             poly_dict[degree] = expr
583         else:  # Now expr can only be of `Mul` type
584             degree = 0
585             for term in expr.args:
586                 term_type = len(term.args)
587                 if term_type == 0 and term.is_Symbol:
588                     degree += 1
589                 elif term_type == 2:
590                     degree += term.args[1]
591             poly_dict[degree] = expr
592     else:
593         poly_dict[0] = expr
594 
595     if separate:
596         return list(poly_dict.values())

600 def clockwise_sort(poly):
601     """Returns the same polygon with points sorted in clockwise order.
602 
603     Note that it's necessary for input points to be sorted in some order
604     (clockwise or anti-clockwise) for the algorithm to work. As a convention
605     algorithm has been implemented keeping clockwise orientation in mind.
606 
607     Parameters
608     ==========
609     poly: 2-Polytope
610 
611     Examples
612     ========
613     >>> from sympy.integrals.intpoly import clockwise_sort
614     >>> from sympy.geometry.point import Point
615     >>> from sympy.geometry.polygon import Polygon
616     >>> clockwise_sort(Polygon(Point(0, 0), Point(1, 0), Point(1, 1)))
617     Triangle(Point2D(1, 1), Point2D(1, 0), Point2D(0, 0))
618 
619     """
620     n = len(poly.vertices)
621     vertices = list(poly.vertices)
622     center = Point(sum(map(lambda vertex: vertex.x, poly.vertices)) / n,
623                    sum(map(lambda vertex: vertex.y, poly.vertices)) / n)
624 
625     def compareTo(a, b):
626         if a.x - center.x >= S.Zero and b.x - center.x < S.Zero:
627             return S(-1)
628         elif a.x - center.x < S.Zero and b.x - center.x >= S.Zero:
629             return S(1)
630         elif a.x - center.x == S.Zero and b.x - center.x == S.Zero:
631             if a.y - center.y >= S.Zero or b.y - center.y >= S.Zero:
632                 return S(-1) if a.y > b.y else S(1)
633             return S(-1) if b.y > a.y else S(1)
634 
635         det = (a.x - center.x) * (b.y - center.y) -\
636               (b.x - center.x) * (a.y - center.y)
637         if det < S.Zero:
638             return S(-1)
639         elif det > S.Zero:
640             return S(1)
641 
642         first = (a.x - center.x) * (a.x - center.x) +\
643                 (a.y - center.y) * (a.y - center.y)
644         second = (b.x - center.x) * (b.x - center.x) +\
645                  (b.y - center.y) * (b.y - center.y)
646         return S(-1) if first > second else S(1)
647 
648     return Polygon(*sorted(vertices, key=cmp_to_key(compareTo)))

problem_statement:
Symbol instances have __dict__ since 1.7?
In version 1.6.2 Symbol instances had no `__dict__` attribute
```python
>>> sympy.Symbol('s').__dict__
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
AttributeError                            Traceback (most recent call last)
<ipython-input-3-e2060d5eec73> in <module>
----> 1 sympy.Symbol('s').__dict__

AttributeError: 'Symbol' object has no attribute '__dict__'
>>> sympy.Symbol('s').__slots__
('name',)
```

This changes in 1.7 where `sympy.Symbol('s').__dict__` now exists (and returns an empty dict)
I may misinterpret this, but given the purpose of `__slots__`, I assume this is a bug, introduced because some parent class accidentally stopped defining `__slots__`.
hints_text:
I've bisected the change to 5644df199fdac0b7a44e85c97faff58dfd462a5a from #19425
It seems that Basic now inherits `DefaultPrinting` which I guess doesn't have slots. I'm not sure if it's a good idea to add `__slots__` to that class as it would then affect all subclasses.

@eric-wieser 
I'm not sure if this should count as a regression but it's certainly not an intended change.
Maybe we should just get rid of `__slots__`. The benchmark results from #19425 don't show any regression from not using `__slots__`.
Adding `__slots__` won't affect subclasses - if a subclass does not specify `__slots__`, then the default is to add a `__dict__` anyway.

I think adding it should be fine.
Using slots can break multiple inheritance but only if the slots are non-empty I guess. Maybe this means that any mixin should always declare empty slots or it won't work properly with subclasses that have slots...

I see that `EvalfMixin` has `__slots__ = ()`.
I guess we should add empty slots to DefaultPrinting then. Probably the intention of using slots with Basic classes is to enforce immutability so this could be considered a regression in that sense so it should go into 1.7.1 I think.

Display of SeqFormula()
```
import sympy as sp
k, m, n = sp.symbols('k m n', integer=True)
sp.init_printing()

sp.SeqFormula(n**2, (n,0,sp.oo))
```

The Jupyter rendering of this command backslash-escapes the brackets producing:

`\left\[0, 1, 4, 9, \ldots\right\]`

Copying this output to a markdown cell this does not render properly.  Whereas:

`[0, 1, 4, 9, \ldots ]`

does render just fine.  

So - sequence output should not backslash-escape square brackets, or, `\]` should instead render?

387     def _print_Mul(self, expr):
388         from sympy.core.power import Pow
389         include_parens = False
390         if _coeff_isneg(expr):
391             expr = -expr
392             tex = "- "
393             if expr.is_Add:
394                 tex += "("
395                 include_parens = True
396         else:
397             tex = ""
398 
399         from sympy.simplify import fraction
400         numer, denom = fraction(expr, exact=True)
401         separator = self._settings['mul_symbol_latex']
402         numbersep = self._settings['mul_symbol_latex_numbers']
403 
404         def convert(expr):
405             if not expr.is_Mul:
406                 return str(self._print(expr))
407             else:
408                 _tex = last_term_tex = ""
409 
410                 if self.order not in ('old', 'none'):
411                     args = expr.as_ordered_factors()
412                 else:
413                     args = expr.args
414 
415                 for i, term in enumerate(args):
416                     term_tex = self._print(term)
417 
418                     if self._needs_mul_brackets(term, first=(i == 0),
419                                                 last=(i == len(args) - 1)):
420                         term_tex = r"\left(%s\right)" % term_tex
421 
422                     if _between_two_numbers_p[0].search(last_term_tex) and \
423                             _between_two_numbers_p[1].match(term_tex):
424                         # between two numbers
425                         _tex += numbersep
426                     elif _tex:
427                         _tex += separator
428 
429                     _tex += term_tex
430                     last_term_tex = term_tex
431                 return _tex
432 
433         if denom is S.One and Pow(1, -1, evaluate=False) not in expr.args:
434             # use the original expression here, since fraction() may have
435             # altered it when producing numer and denom
436             tex += convert(expr)
437 
438         else:
439             snumer = convert(numer)
440             sdenom = convert(denom)
441             ldenom = len(sdenom.split())
442             ratio = self._settings['long_frac_ratio']
443             if self._settings['fold_short_frac'] \
444                     and ldenom <= 2 and not "^" in sdenom:
445                 # handle short fractions
446                 if self._needs_mul_brackets(numer, last=False):
447                     tex += r"\left(%s\right) / %s" % (snumer, sdenom)
448                 else:
449                     tex += r"%s / %s" % (snumer, sdenom)
450             elif len(snumer.split()) > ratio*ldenom:
451                 # handle long fractions
452                 if self._needs_mul_brackets(numer, last=True):
453                     tex += r"\frac{1}{%s}%s\left(%s\right)" \
454                         % (sdenom, separator, snumer)
455                 elif numer.is_Mul:
456                     # split a long numerator
457                     a = S.One
458                     b = S.One
459                     for x in numer.args:
460                         if self._needs_mul_brackets(x, last=False) or \
461                                 len(convert(a*x).split()) > ratio*ldenom or \
462                                 (b.is_commutative is x.is_commutative is False):
463                             b *= x
464                         else:
465                             a *= x
466                     if self._needs_mul_brackets(b, last=True):
467                         tex += r"\frac{%s}{%s}%s\left(%s\right)" \
468                             % (convert(a), sdenom, separator, convert(b))
469                     else:
470                         tex += r"\frac{%s}{%s}%s%s" \
471                             % (convert(a), sdenom, separator, convert(b))
472                 else:
473                     tex += r"\frac{1}{%s}%s%s" % (sdenom, separator, snumer)
474             else:
475                 tex += r"\frac{%s}{%s}" % (snumer, sdenom)
476 
477         if include_parens:
478             tex += ")"
479         return tex
480 
481     def _print_Pow(self, expr):
482         # Treat x**Rational(1,n) as special case
483         if expr.exp.is_Rational and abs(expr.exp.p) == 1 and expr.exp.q != 1:
484             base = self._print(expr.base)
485             expq = expr.exp.q
486 
487             if expq == 2:
488                 tex = r"\sqrt{%s}" % base
489             elif self._settings['itex']:
490                 tex = r"\root{%d}{%s}" % (expq, base)
491             else:
492                 tex = r"\sqrt[%d]{%s}" % (expq, base)
493 
494             if expr.exp.is_negative:
495                 return r"\frac{1}{%s}" % tex
496             else:
497                 return tex
498         elif self._settings['fold_frac_powers'] \
499             and expr.exp.is_Rational \
500                 and expr.exp.q != 1:
501             base, p, q = self.parenthesize(expr.base, PRECEDENCE['Pow']), expr.exp.p, expr.exp.q
502             #fixes issue #12886, adds parentheses before superscripts raised to powers
503             if '^' in base and expr.base.is_Symbol:
504                 base = r"\left(%s\right)" % base
505             if expr.base.is_Function:
506                 return self._print(expr.base, "%s/%s" % (p, q))
507             return r"%s^{%s/%s}" % (base, p, q)
508         elif expr.exp.is_Rational and expr.exp.is_negative and expr.base.is_commutative:
509             # Things like 1/x
510             return self._print_Mul(expr)
511         else:
512             if expr.base.is_Function:
513                 return self._print(expr.base, self._print(expr.exp))
514             else:
515                 if expr.is_commutative and expr.exp == -1:
516                     #solves issue 4129
517                     #As Mul always simplify 1/x to x**-1
518                     #The objective is achieved with this hack
519                     #first we get the latex for -1 * expr,
520                     #which is a Mul expression
521                     tex = self._print(S.NegativeOne * expr).strip()
522                     #the result comes with a minus and a space, so we remove
523                     if tex[:1] == "-":
524                         return tex[1:].strip()
525                 tex = r"%s^{%s}"
526                 #fixes issue #12886, adds parentheses before superscripts raised to powers
527                 base = self.parenthesize(expr.base, PRECEDENCE['Pow'])
528                 if '^' in base and expr.base.is_Symbol:
529                     base = r"\left(%s\right)" % base
530                 exp = self._print(expr.exp)
531 
532                 return tex % (base, exp)
533

690     def _hprint_Function(self, func):
691         r'''
692         Logic to decide how to render a function to latex
693           - if it is a recognized latex name, use the appropriate latex command
694           - if it is a single letter, just use that letter
695           - if it is a longer name, then put \operatorname{} around it and be
696             mindful of undercores in the name
697         '''
698         func = self._deal_with_super_sub(func)
699 
700         if func in accepted_latex_functions:
701             name = r"\%s" % func
702         elif len(func) == 1 or func.startswith('\\'):
703             name = func
704         else:
705             name = r"\operatorname{%s}" % func
706         return name

708     def _print_Function(self, expr, exp=None):
709         r'''
710         Render functions to LaTeX, handling functions that LaTeX knows about
711         e.g., sin, cos, ... by using the proper LaTeX command (\sin, \cos, ...).
712         For single-letter function names, render them as regular LaTeX math
713         symbols. For multi-letter function names that LaTeX does not know
714         about, (e.g., Li, sech) use \operatorname{} so that the function name
715         is rendered in Roman font and LaTeX handles spacing properly.
716 
717         expr is the expression involving the function
718         exp is an exponent
719         '''
720         func = expr.func.__name__
721 
722         if hasattr(self, '_print_' + func):
723             return getattr(self, '_print_' + func)(expr, exp)
724         else:
725             args = [ str(self._print(arg)) for arg in expr.args ]
726             # How inverse trig functions should be displayed, formats are:
727             # abbreviated: asin, full: arcsin, power: sin^-1
728             inv_trig_style = self._settings['inv_trig_style']
729             # If we are dealing with a power-style inverse trig function
730             inv_trig_power_case = False
731             # If it is applicable to fold the argument brackets
732             can_fold_brackets = self._settings['fold_func_brackets'] and \
733                 len(args) == 1 and \
734                 not self._needs_function_brackets(expr.args[0])
735 
736             inv_trig_table = ["asin", "acos", "atan", "acot"]
737 
738             # If the function is an inverse trig function, handle the style
739             if func in inv_trig_table:
740                 if inv_trig_style == "abbreviated":
741                     func = func
742                 elif inv_trig_style == "full":
743                     func = "arc" + func[1:]
744                 elif inv_trig_style == "power":
745                     func = func[1:]
746                     inv_trig_power_case = True
747 
748                     # Can never fold brackets if we're raised to a power
749                     if exp is not None:
750                         can_fold_brackets = False
751 
752             if inv_trig_power_case:
753                 if func in accepted_latex_functions:
754                     name = r"\%s^{-1}" % func
755                 else:
756                     name = r"\operatorname{%s}^{-1}" % func
757             elif exp is not None:
758                 name = r'%s^{%s}' % (self._hprint_Function(func), exp)
759             else:
760                 name = self._hprint_Function(func)
761 
762             if can_fold_brackets:
763                 if func in accepted_latex_functions:
764                     # Wrap argument safely to avoid parse-time conflicts
765                     # with the function name itself
766                     name += r" {%s}"
767                 else:
768                     name += r"%s"
769             else:
770                 name += r"{\left (%s \right )}"
771 
772             if inv_trig_power_case and exp is not None:
773                 name += r"^{%s}" % exp
774 
775             return name % ",".join(args)
776

1313     def _deal_with_super_sub(self, string):
1314         if '{' in string:
1315             return string
1316 
1317         name, supers, subs = split_super_sub(string)
1318 
1319         name = translate(name)
1320         supers = [translate(sup) for sup in supers]
1321         subs = [translate(sub) for sub in subs]
1322 
1323         # glue all items together:

1325             name += "^{%s}" % " ".join(supers)

1475     def _print_NDimArray(self, expr):
1476 
1477         if expr.rank() == 0:
1478             return self._print(expr[()])
1479 
1480         mat_str = self._settings['mat_str']
1481         if mat_str is None:
1482             if self._settings['mode'] == 'inline':
1483                 mat_str = 'smallmatrix'
1484             else:
1485                 if (expr.rank() == 0) or (expr.shape[-1] <= 10):
1486                     mat_str = 'matrix'
1487                 else:
1488                     mat_str = 'array'
1489         block_str = r'\begin{%MATSTR%}%s\end{%MATSTR%}'
1490         block_str = block_str.replace('%MATSTR%', mat_str)
1491         if self._settings['mat_delim']:
1492             left_delim = self._settings['mat_delim']
1493             right_delim = self._delim_dict[left_delim]
1494             block_str = r'\left' + left_delim + block_str + \
1495                       r'\right' + right_delim
1496 
1497         if expr.rank() == 0:
1498             return block_str % ""
1499 
1500         level_str = [[]] + [[] for i in range(expr.rank())]
1501         shape_ranges = [list(range(i)) for i in expr.shape]
1502         for outer_i in itertools.product(*shape_ranges):
1503             level_str[-1].append(self._print(expr[outer_i]))
1504             even = True
1505             for back_outer_i in range(expr.rank()-1, -1, -1):
1506                 if len(level_str[back_outer_i+1]) < expr.shape[back_outer_i]:
1507                     break
1508                 if even:
1509                     level_str[back_outer_i].append(r" & ".join(level_str[back_outer_i+1]))
1510                 else:
1511                     level_str[back_outer_i].append(block_str % (r"\\".join(level_str[back_outer_i+1])))
1512                     if len(level_str[back_outer_i+1]) == 1:
1513                         level_str[back_outer_i][-1] = r"\left[" + level_str[back_outer_i][-1] + r"\right]"
1514                 even = not even
1515                 level_str[back_outer_i+1] = []
1516 
1517         out_str = level_str[0][0]
1518 
1519         if expr.rank() % 2 == 1:
1520             out_str = block_str % out_str
1521 
1522         return out_str
1523

Is it intentional that creating a Dataset with a DataArray and dimension names for a single variable causes computation of that variable?  In other words, why does ```xr.Dataset(dict(a=('d0', xr.DataArray(da.random.random(10)))))``` cause the dask array to compute?

86 def as_variable(obj, name=None) -> "Union[Variable, IndexVariable]":
87     """Convert an object into a Variable.
88 
89     Parameters
90     ----------
91     obj : object
92         Object to convert into a Variable.
93 
94         - If the object is already a Variable, return a shallow copy.
95         - Otherwise, if the object has 'dims' and 'data' attributes, convert
96           it into a new Variable.
97         - If all else fails, attempt to convert the object into a Variable by
98           unpacking it into the arguments for creating a new Variable.
99     name : str, optional
100         If provided:
101 
102         - `obj` can be a 1D array, which is assumed to label coordinate values
103           along a dimension of this given name.
104         - Variables with name matching one of their dimensions are converted
105           into `IndexVariable` objects.
106 
107     Returns
108     -------
109     var : Variable
110         The newly created variable.
111 
112     """
113     from .dataarray import DataArray
114 
115     # TODO: consider extending this method to automatically handle Iris and
116     if isinstance(obj, DataArray):
117         # extract the primary Variable from DataArrays
118         obj = obj.variable
119 
120     if isinstance(obj, Variable):
121         obj = obj.copy(deep=False)
122     elif isinstance(obj, tuple):
123         try:
124             obj = Variable(*obj)
125         except (TypeError, ValueError) as error:
126             # use .format() instead of % because it handles tuples consistently
127             raise error.__class__(
128                 "Could not convert tuple of form "
129                 "(dims, data[, attrs, encoding]): "
130                 "{} to Variable.".format(obj)
131             )
132     elif utils.is_scalar(obj):
133         obj = Variable([], obj)
134     elif isinstance(obj, (pd.Index, IndexVariable)) and obj.name is not None:
135         obj = Variable(obj.name, obj)
136     elif isinstance(obj, (set, dict)):
137         raise TypeError("variable {!r} has invalid type {!r}".format(name, type(obj)))
138     elif name is not None:
139         data = as_compatible_data(obj)
140         if data.ndim != 1:
141             raise MissingDimensionsError(
142                 "cannot set variable %r with %r-dimensional data "
143                 "without explicit dimension names. Pass a tuple of "
144                 "(dims, data) instead." % (name, data.ndim)
145             )
146         obj = Variable(name, data, fastpath=True)
147     else:
148         raise TypeError(
149             "unable to convert object into a variable without an "
150             "explicit list of dimensions: %r" % obj
151         )
152 
153     if name is not None and name in obj.dims:
154         # convert the Variable into an Index
155         if obj.ndim != 1:
156             raise MissingDimensionsError(
157                 "%r has more than 1-dimension and the same name as one of its "
158                 "dimensions %r. xarray disallows such variables because they "
159                 "conflict with the coordinates used to label "
160                 "dimensions." % (name, obj.dims)
161             )
162         obj = obj.to_index_variable()
163 
164     return obj

180 def _possibly_convert_objects(values):
181     """Convert arrays of datetime.datetime and datetime.timedelta objects into
182     datetime64 and timedelta64, according to the pandas convention. Also used for
183     validating that datetime64 and timedelta64 objects are within the valid date

189 def as_compatible_data(data, fastpath=False):
190     """Prepare and wrap data to put in a Variable.
191 
192     - If data does not have the necessary attributes, convert it to ndarray.
193     - If data has dtype=datetime64, ensure that it has ns precision. If it's a
194       pandas.Timestamp, convert it to datetime64.
195     - If data is already a pandas or xarray object (other than an Index), just
196       use the values.
197 
198     Finally, wrap it up with an adapter if necessary.
199     """
200     if fastpath and getattr(data, "ndim", 0) > 0:
201         # can't use fastpath (yet) for scalars
202         return _maybe_wrap_data(data)
203 
204     if isinstance(data, Variable):
205         return data.data
206 
207     if isinstance(data, NON_NUMPY_SUPPORTED_ARRAY_TYPES):
208         return _maybe_wrap_data(data)
209 
210     if isinstance(data, tuple):
211         data = utils.to_0d_object_array(data)
212 
213     if isinstance(data, pd.Timestamp):
214         # TODO: convert, handle datetime objects, too
215         data = np.datetime64(data.value, "ns")
216 
217     if isinstance(data, timedelta):
218         data = np.timedelta64(getattr(data, "value", data), "ns")
219 
220     # we don't want nested self-described arrays
221     data = getattr(data, "values", data)
222 
223     if isinstance(data, np.ma.MaskedArray):
224         mask = np.ma.getmaskarray(data)
225         if mask.any():
226             dtype, fill_value = dtypes.maybe_promote(data.dtype)
227             data = np.asarray(data, dtype=dtype)
228             data[mask] = fill_value
229         else:
230             data = np.asarray(data)
231 
232     if not isinstance(data, np.ndarray):
233         if hasattr(data, "__array_function__"):
234             if IS_NEP18_ACTIVE:
235                 return data
236             else:
237                 raise TypeError(
238                     "Got an NumPy-like array type providing the "
239                     "__array_function__ protocol but NEP18 is not enabled. "
240                     "Check that numpy >= v1.16 and that the environment "
241                     'variable "NUMPY_EXPERIMENTAL_ARRAY_FUNCTION" is set to '
242                     '"1"'
243                 )
244 
245     # validate whether the data is valid data types.
246     data = np.asarray(data)
247 
248     if isinstance(data, np.ndarray):
249         if data.dtype.kind == "O":
250             data = _possibly_convert_objects(data)
251         elif data.dtype.kind == "M":
252             data = _possibly_convert_objects(data)
253         elif data.dtype.kind == "m":
254             data = _possibly_convert_objects(data)
255 
256     return _maybe_wrap_data(data)
257

259 def _as_array_or_item(data):
260     """Return the given values as a numpy array, or as an individual item if
261     it's a 0d datetime64 or timedelta64 array.
262 
263     Importantly, this function does not copy data if it is already an ndarray -
264     otherwise, it will not be possible to update Variable values in place.
265 
266     This function mostly exists because 0-dimensional ndarrays with
267     dtype=datetime64 are broken :(
268     https://github.com/numpy/numpy/issues/4337
269     https://github.com/numpy/numpy/issues/7619
270 
271     TODO: remove this (replace with np.asarray) once these issues are fixed
272     """
273     if isinstance(data, cupy_array_type):
274         data = data.get()
275     else:
276         data = np.asarray(data)
277     if data.ndim == 0:
278         if data.dtype.kind == "M":
279             data = np.datetime64(data, "ns")
280         elif data.dtype.kind == "m":
281             data = np.timedelta64(data, "ns")
282     return data

285 class Variable(
286     common.AbstractArray, arithmetic.SupportsArithmetic, utils.NdimSizeLenMixin
287 ):
288     """A netcdf-like variable consisting of dimensions, data and attributes
289     which describe a single Array. A single Variable object is not fully
290     described outside the context of its parent Dataset (if you want such a
291     fully described object, use a DataArray instead).
292 
293     The main functional difference between Variables and numpy arrays is that
294     numerical operations on Variables implement array broadcasting by dimension
295     name. For example, adding an Variable with dimensions `('time',)` to
296     another Variable with dimensions `('space',)` results in a new Variable
297     with dimensions `('time', 'space')`. Furthermore, numpy reduce operations
298     like ``mean`` or ``sum`` are overwritten to take a "dimension" argument
299     instead of an "axis".
300 
301     Variables are light-weight objects used as the building block for datasets.
302     They are more primitive objects, so operations with them provide marginally
303     higher performance than using DataArrays. However, manipulating data in the
304     form of a Dataset or DataArray should almost always be preferred, because
305     they can use more complete metadata in context of coordinate labels.
306     """
307 
308     __slots__ = ("_dims", "_data", "_attrs", "_encoding")
309 
310     def __init__(self, dims, data, attrs=None, encoding=None, fastpath=False):
311         """
312         Parameters
313         ----------
314         dims : str or sequence of str
315             Name(s) of the the data dimension(s). Must be either a string (only
316             for 1D data) or a sequence of strings with length equal to the
317             number of dimensions.
318         data : array_like
319             Data array which supports numpy-like data access.
320         attrs : dict_like or None, optional
321             Attributes to assign to the new variable. If None (default), an
322             empty attribute dictionary is initialized.
323         encoding : dict_like or None, optional
324             Dictionary specifying how to encode this array's data into a
325             serialized format like netCDF4. Currently used keys (for netCDF)
326             include '_FillValue', 'scale_factor', 'add_offset' and 'dtype'.
327             Well-behaved code to serialize a Variable should ignore
328             unrecognized encoding items.
329         """
330         self._data = as_compatible_data(data, fastpath=fastpath)
331         self._dims = self._parse_dimensions(dims)
332         self._attrs = None
333         self._encoding = None
334         if attrs is not None:
335             self.attrs = attrs
336         if encoding is not None:
337             self.encoding = encoding

375     def astype(
376         self: VariableType,
377         dtype,
378         *,
379         order=None,
380         casting=None,
381         subok=None,
382         copy=None,
383         keep_attrs=True,
384     ) -> VariableType:
385         """
386         Copy of the Variable object, with data cast to a specified type.
387 
388         Parameters
389         ----------
390         dtype : str or dtype
391             Typecode or data-type to which the array is cast.
392         order : {'C', 'F', 'A', 'K'}, optional
393             Controls the memory layout order of the result. ‘C’ means C order,
394             ‘F’ means Fortran order, ‘A’ means ‘F’ order if all the arrays are
395             Fortran contiguous, ‘C’ order otherwise, and ‘K’ means as close to
396             the order the array elements appear in memory as possible.
397         casting : {'no', 'equiv', 'safe', 'same_kind', 'unsafe'}, optional
398             Controls what kind of data casting may occur.
399 
400             * 'no' means the data types should not be cast at all.
401             * 'equiv' means only byte-order changes are allowed.
402             * 'safe' means only casts which can preserve values are allowed.
403             * 'same_kind' means only safe casts or casts within a kind,
404               like float64 to float32, are allowed.
405             * 'unsafe' means any data conversions may be done.
406 
407         subok : bool, optional
408             If True, then sub-classes will be passed-through, otherwise the
409             returned array will be forced to be a base-class array.
410         copy : bool, optional
411             By default, astype always returns a newly allocated array. If this
412             is set to False and the `dtype` requirement is satisfied, the input
413             array is returned instead of a copy.
414         keep_attrs : bool, optional
415             By default, astype keeps attributes. Set to False to remove
416             attributes in the returned object.
417 
418         Returns
419         -------
420         out : same as object
421             New object with data cast to the specified type.
422 
423         Notes
424         -----
425         The ``order``, ``casting``, ``subok`` and ``copy`` arguments are only passed
426         through to the ``astype`` method of the underlying array when a value
427         different than ``None`` is supplied.
428         Make sure to only supply these arguments if the underlying array class
429         supports them.
430 
431         See also
432         --------
433         numpy.ndarray.astype
434         dask.array.Array.astype
435         sparse.COO.astype
436         """
437         from .computation import apply_ufunc
438 
439         kwargs = dict(order=order, casting=casting, subok=subok, copy=copy)
440         kwargs = {k: v for k, v in kwargs.items() if v is not None}
441 
442         return apply_ufunc(
443             duck_array_ops.astype,
444             self,
445             dtype,
446             kwargs=kwargs,
447             keep_attrs=keep_attrs,
448             dask="allowed",
449         )

605     def _broadcast_indexes(self, key):
606         """Prepare an indexing key for an indexing operation.
607 
608         Parameters
609         -----------
610         key: int, slice, array-like, dict or tuple of integer, slice and array-like
611             Any valid input for indexing.
612 
613         Returns
614         -------
615         dims : tuple
616             Dimension of the resultant variable.
617         indexers : IndexingTuple subclass
618             Tuple of integer, array-like, or slices to use when indexing
619             self._data. The type of this argument indicates the type of
620             indexing to perform, either basic, outer or vectorized.
621         new_order : Optional[Sequence[int]]
622             Optional reordering to do on the result of indexing. If not None,
623             the first len(new_order) indexing should be moved to these
624             positions.
625         """
626         key = self._item_key_to_tuple(key)  # key is a tuple
627         # key is a tuple of full size
628         key = indexing.expanded_indexer(key, self.ndim)
629         # Convert a scalar Variable to an integer
630         key = tuple(
631             k.data.item() if isinstance(k, Variable) and k.ndim == 0 else k for k in key
632         )
633         # Convert a 0d-array to an integer
634         key = tuple(
635             k.item() if isinstance(k, np.ndarray) and k.ndim == 0 else k for k in key
636         )
637 
638         if all(isinstance(k, BASIC_INDEXING_TYPES) for k in key):
639             return self._broadcast_indexes_basic(key)
640 
641         self._validate_indexers(key)
642         # Detect it can be mapped as an outer indexer
643         # If all key is unlabeled, or
644         # key can be mapped as an OuterIndexer.
645         if all(not isinstance(k, Variable) for k in key):
646             return self._broadcast_indexes_outer(key)
647 
648         # If all key is 1-dimensional and there are no duplicate labels,
649         # key can be mapped as an OuterIndexer.
650         dims = []
651         for k, d in zip(key, self.dims):
652             if isinstance(k, Variable):
653                 if len(k.dims) > 1:
654                     return self._broadcast_indexes_vectorized(key)
655                 dims.append(k.dims[0])
656             elif not isinstance(k, integer_types):
657                 dims.append(d)
658         if len(set(dims)) == len(dims):
659             return self._broadcast_indexes_outer(key)
660 
661         return self._broadcast_indexes_vectorized(key)
662 
663     def _broadcast_indexes_basic(self, key):
664         dims = tuple(
665             dim for k, dim in zip(key, self.dims) if not isinstance(k, integer_types)
666         )
667         return dims, BasicIndexer(key), None

669     def _validate_indexers(self, key):
670         """ Make sanity checks """
671         for dim, k in zip(self.dims, key):

673                 pass

675                 if not isinstance(k, Variable):
676                     k = np.asarray(k)

678                         raise IndexError(
679                             "Unlabeled multi-dimensional array cannot be "
680                             "used for indexing: {}".format(k)

684                         raise IndexError(

696                             "same dimension to the indexed array. Indexer is "
697                             "on {:s} but the target dimension is {:s}.".format(

702     def _broadcast_indexes_outer(self, key):
703         dims = tuple(
704             k.dims[0] if isinstance(k, Variable) else dim
705             for k, dim in zip(key, self.dims)
706             if not isinstance(k, integer_types)
707         )
708 
709         new_key = []
710         for k in key:
711             if isinstance(k, Variable):
712                 k = k.data
713             if not isinstance(k, BASIC_INDEXING_TYPES):
714                 k = np.asarray(k)
715                 if k.size == 0:
716                     # Slice by empty list; numpy could not infer the dtype
717                     k = k.astype(int)
718                 elif k.dtype.kind == "b":
719                     (k,) = np.nonzero(k)
720             new_key.append(k)
721 
722         return dims, OuterIndexer(tuple(new_key)), None

731     def _broadcast_indexes_vectorized(self, key):
732         variables = []
733         out_dims_set = OrderedSet()
734         for dim, value in zip(self.dims, key):
735             if isinstance(value, slice):
736                 out_dims_set.add(dim)
737             else:
738                 variable = (
739                     value
740                     if isinstance(value, Variable)
741                     else as_variable(value, name=dim)
742                 )
743                 if variable.dtype.kind == "b":  # boolean indexing case
744                     (variable,) = variable._nonzero()
745 
746                 variables.append(variable)
747                 out_dims_set.update(variable.dims)
748 
749         variable_dims = set()
750         for variable in variables:
751             variable_dims.update(variable.dims)
752 
753         slices = []
754         for i, (dim, value) in enumerate(zip(self.dims, key)):
755             if isinstance(value, slice):
756                 if dim in variable_dims:
757                     # We only convert slice objects to variables if they share
758                     # a dimension with at least one other variable. Otherwise,
759                     # we can equivalently leave them as slices aknd transpose
760                     # the result. This is significantly faster/more efficient
761                     # for most array backends.
762                     values = np.arange(*value.indices(self.sizes[dim]))
763                     variables.insert(i - len(slices), Variable((dim,), values))
764                 else:
765                     slices.append((i, value))
766 
767         try:
768             variables = _broadcast_compat_variables(*variables)
769         except ValueError:
770             raise IndexError(f"Dimensions of indexers mismatch: {key}")
771 
772         out_key = [variable.data for variable in variables]
773         out_dims = tuple(out_dims_set)
774         slice_positions = set()
775         for i, value in slices:
776             out_key.insert(i, value)
777             new_position = out_dims.index(self.dims[i])
778             slice_positions.add(new_position)
779 
780         if slice_positions:
781             new_order = [i for i in range(len(out_dims)) if i not in slice_positions]
782         else:
783             new_order = None
784 
785         return out_dims, VectorizedIndexer(tuple(out_key)), new_order

787     def __getitem__(self: VariableType, key) -> VariableType:
788         """Return a new Variable object whose contents are consistent with
789         getting the provided key from the underlying data.
790 
791         NB. __getitem__ and __setitem__ implement xarray-style indexing,
792         where if keys are unlabeled arrays, we index the array orthogonally
793         with them. If keys are labeled array (such as Variables), they are
794         broadcasted with our usual scheme and then the array is indexed with
795         the broadcasted key, like numpy's fancy indexing.
796 
797         If you really want to do indexing like `x[x > 0]`, manipulate the numpy
798         array `x.values` directly.
799         """
800         dims, indexer, new_order = self._broadcast_indexes(key)
801         data = as_indexable(self._data)[indexer]
802         if new_order:
803             data = duck_array_ops.moveaxis(data, range(len(new_order)), new_order)
804         return self._finalize_indexing_result(dims, data)
805

810     def _getitem_with_mask(self, key, fill_value=dtypes.NA):
811         """Index this Variable with -1 remapped to fill_value."""
812         # TODO(shoyer): expose this method in public API somewhere (isel?) and
813         # use it for reindex.
814         # TODO(shoyer): add a sanity check that all other integers are
815         # non-negative
816         # TODO(shoyer): add an optimization, remapping -1 to an adjacent value
817         # that is actually indexed rather than mapping it to the last value
818         # along each axis.
819 
820         if fill_value is dtypes.NA:
821             fill_value = dtypes.get_fill_value(self.dtype)
822 
823         dims, indexer, new_order = self._broadcast_indexes(key)
824 
825         if self.size:
826             if is_duck_dask_array(self._data):
827                 # dask's indexing is faster this way; also vindex does not
828                 # support negative indices yet:
829                 # https://github.com/dask/dask/pull/2967
830                 actual_indexer = indexing.posify_mask_indexer(indexer)
831             else:
832                 actual_indexer = indexer
833 
834             data = as_indexable(self._data)[actual_indexer]
835             mask = indexing.create_mask(indexer, self.shape, data)
836             # we need to invert the mask in order to pass data first. This helps
837             # pint to choose the correct unit
838             # TODO: revert after https://github.com/hgrecco/pint/issues/1019 is fixed
839             data = duck_array_ops.where(np.logical_not(mask), data, fill_value)
840         else:
841             # array cannot be indexed along dimensions of size 0, so just
842             # build the mask directly instead.
843             mask = indexing.create_mask(indexer, self.shape)
844             data = np.broadcast_to(fill_value, getattr(mask, "shape", ()))
845 
846         if new_order:
847             data = duck_array_ops.moveaxis(data, range(len(new_order)), new_order)
848         return self._finalize_indexing_result(dims, data)

850     def __setitem__(self, key, value):
851         """__setitem__ is overloaded to access the underlying numpy values with
852         orthogonal indexing.
853 
854         See __getitem__ for more details.
855         """
856         dims, index_tuple, new_order = self._broadcast_indexes(key)
857 
858         if not isinstance(value, Variable):
859             value = as_compatible_data(value)
860             if value.ndim > len(dims):
861                 raise ValueError(
862                     "shape mismatch: value array of shape %s could not be "
863                     "broadcast to indexing result with %s dimensions"
864                     % (value.shape, len(dims))
865                 )
866             if value.ndim == 0:
867                 value = Variable((), value)
868             else:
869                 value = Variable(dims[-value.ndim :], value)
870         # broadcast to become assignable
871         value = value.set_dims(dims).data
872 
873         if new_order:
874             value = duck_array_ops.asarray(value)
875             value = value[(len(dims) - value.ndim) * (np.newaxis,) + (Ellipsis,)]
876             value = duck_array_ops.moveaxis(value, new_order, range(len(new_order)))
877 
878         indexable = as_indexable(self._data)
879         indexable[index_tuple] = value

906     def copy(self, deep=True, data=None):
907         """Returns a copy of this object.
908 
909         If `deep=True`, the data array is loaded into memory and copied onto
910         the new object. Dimensions, attributes and encodings are always copied.
911 
912         Use `data` to create a new object with the same structure as
913         original but entirely new data.
914 
915         Parameters
916         ----------
917         deep : bool, optional
918             Whether the data array is loaded into memory and copied onto
919             the new object. Default is True.
920         data : array_like, optional
921             Data to use in the new object. Must have same shape as original.
922             When `data` is used, `deep` is ignored.
923 
924         Returns
925         -------
926         object : Variable
927             New object with dimensions, attributes, encodings, and optionally
928             data copied from original.
929 
930         Examples
931         --------
932 
933         Shallow copy versus deep copy
934 
935         >>> var = xr.Variable(data=[1, 2, 3], dims="x")
936         >>> var.copy()
937         <xarray.Variable (x: 3)>
938         array([1, 2, 3])
939         >>> var_0 = var.copy(deep=False)
940         >>> var_0[0] = 7
941         >>> var_0
942         <xarray.Variable (x: 3)>
943         array([7, 2, 3])
944         >>> var
945         <xarray.Variable (x: 3)>
946         array([7, 2, 3])
947 
948         Changing the data using the ``data`` argument maintains the
949         structure of the original object, but with the new data. Original
950         object is unaffected.
951 
952         >>> var.copy(data=[0.1, 0.2, 0.3])
953         <xarray.Variable (x: 3)>
954         array([0.1, 0.2, 0.3])
955         >>> var
956         <xarray.Variable (x: 3)>
957         array([7, 2, 3])
958 
959         See Also
960         --------
961         pandas.DataFrame.copy
962         """
963         if data is None:
964             data = self._data
965 
966             if isinstance(data, indexing.MemoryCachedArray):
967                 # don't share caching between copies
968                 data = indexing.MemoryCachedArray(data.array)
969 
970             if deep:
971                 data = copy.deepcopy(data)
972 
973         else:
974             data = as_compatible_data(data)
975             if self.shape != data.shape:
976                 raise ValueError(
977                     "Data shape {} must match shape of object {}".format(
978                         data.shape, self.shape
979                     )
980                 )
981 
982         # note:
983         # dims is already an immutable tuple
984         # attributes and encoding will be copied when the new Array is created
985         return self._replace(data=data)
986 
987     def _replace(
988         self, dims=_default, data=_default, attrs=_default, encoding=_default
989     ) -> "Variable":
990         if dims is _default:
991             dims = copy.copy(self._dims)
992         if data is _default:
993             data = copy.copy(self.data)
994         if attrs is _default:
995             attrs = copy.copy(self._attrs)
996         if encoding is _default:
997             encoding = copy.copy(self._encoding)
998         return type(self)(dims, data, attrs, encoding, fastpath=True)

1021     def chunk(self, chunks={}, name=None, lock=False):
1022         """Coerce this array's data into a dask arrays with the given chunks.
1023 
1024         If this variable is a non-dask array, it will be converted to dask
1025         array. If it's a dask array, it will be rechunked to the given chunk
1026         sizes.
1027 
1028         If neither chunks is not provided for one or more dimensions, chunk
1029         sizes along that dimension will not be updated; non-dask arrays will be
1030         converted into dask arrays with a single block.
1031 
1032         Parameters
1033         ----------
1034         chunks : int, tuple or dict, optional
1035             Chunk sizes along each dimension, e.g., ``5``, ``(5, 5)`` or
1036             ``{'x': 5, 'y': 5}``.
1037         name : str, optional
1038             Used to generate the name for this array in the internal dask
1039             graph. Does not need not be unique.
1040         lock : optional
1041             Passed on to :py:func:`dask.array.from_array`, if the array is not
1042             already as dask array.
1043 
1044         Returns
1045         -------
1046         chunked : xarray.Variable
1047         """
1048         import dask
1049         import dask.array as da
1050 
1051         if chunks is None:
1052             warnings.warn(
1053                 "None value for 'chunks' is deprecated. "
1054                 "It will raise an error in the future. Use instead '{}'",
1055                 category=FutureWarning,
1056             )
1057             chunks = {}
1058 
1059         if utils.is_dict_like(chunks):
1060             chunks = {self.get_axis_num(dim): chunk for dim, chunk in chunks.items()}
1061 
1062         data = self._data
1063         if is_duck_dask_array(data):
1064             data = data.rechunk(chunks)
1065         else:
1066             if isinstance(data, indexing.ExplicitlyIndexed):
1067                 # Unambiguously handle array storage backends (like NetCDF4 and h5py)
1068                 # that can't handle general array indexing. For example, in netCDF4 you
1069                 # can do "outer" indexing along two dimensions independent, which works
1070                 # differently from how NumPy handles it.
1071                 # da.from_array works by using lazy indexing with a tuple of slices.
1072                 # Using OuterIndexer is a pragmatic choice: dask does not yet handle
1073                 # different indexing types in an explicit way:
1074                 # https://github.com/dask/dask/issues/2883
1075                 data = indexing.ImplicitToExplicitIndexingAdapter(
1076                     data, indexing.OuterIndexer
1077                 )
1078                 if LooseVersion(dask.__version__) < "2.0.0":
1079                     kwargs = {}
1080                 else:
1081                     # All of our lazily loaded backend array classes should use NumPy
1082                     # array operations.
1083                     kwargs = {"meta": np.ndarray}
1084             else:
1085                 kwargs = {}
1086 
1087             if utils.is_dict_like(chunks):
1088                 chunks = tuple(chunks.get(n, s) for n, s in enumerate(self.shape))
1089 
1090             data = da.from_array(data, chunks, name=name, lock=lock, **kwargs)
1091 
1092         return type(self)(self.dims, data, self._attrs, self._encoding, fastpath=True)
1093

1182     def _shift_one_dim(self, dim, count, fill_value=dtypes.NA):
1183         axis = self.get_axis_num(dim)
1184 
1185         if count > 0:
1186             keep = slice(None, -count)
1187         elif count < 0:
1188             keep = slice(-count, None)
1189         else:
1190             keep = slice(None)
1191 
1192         trimmed_data = self[(slice(None),) * axis + (keep,)].data
1193 
1194         if fill_value is dtypes.NA:
1195             dtype, fill_value = dtypes.maybe_promote(self.dtype)
1196         else:
1197             dtype = self.dtype
1198 
1199         width = min(abs(count), self.shape[axis])
1200         dim_pad = (width, 0) if count >= 0 else (0, width)
1201         pads = [(0, 0) if d != dim else dim_pad for d in self.dims]
1202 
1203         data = duck_array_ops.pad(
1204             trimmed_data.astype(dtype),
1205             pads,
1206             mode="constant",
1207             constant_values=fill_value,
1208         )
1209 
1210         if is_duck_dask_array(data):
1211             # chunked data should come out with the same chunks; this makes
1212             # it feasible to combine shifted and unshifted data
1213             # TODO: remove this once dask.array automatically aligns chunks
1214             data = data.rechunk(self.data.chunks)
1215 
1216         return type(self)(self.dims, data, self._attrs, fastpath=True)

1299             One of pad_width or pad_width_kwargs must be provided.
1300 
1301         Returns
1302         -------
1303         padded : Variable
1304             Variable with the same dimensions and attributes but padded data.
1305         """
1306         pad_width = either_dict_or_kwargs(pad_width, pad_width_kwargs, "pad")
1307 
1308         # change default behaviour of pad with mode constant
1309         if mode == "constant" and (
1310             constant_values is None or constant_values is dtypes.NA
1311         ):
1312             dtype, constant_values = dtypes.maybe_promote(self.dtype)
1313         else:
1314             dtype = self.dtype
1315 
1316         # create pad_options_kwargs, numpy requires only relevant kwargs to be nonempty
1317         if isinstance(stat_length, dict):
1318             stat_length = self._pad_options_dim_to_index(
1319                 stat_length, fill_with_shape=True
1320             )
1321         if isinstance(constant_values, dict):
1322             constant_values = self._pad_options_dim_to_index(constant_values)
1323         if isinstance(end_values, dict):
1324             end_values = self._pad_options_dim_to_index(end_values)
1325 
1326         # workaround for bug in Dask's default value of stat_length https://github.com/dask/dask/issues/5303
1327         if stat_length is None and mode in ["maximum", "mean", "median", "minimum"]:
1328             stat_length = [(n, n) for n in self.data.shape]  # type: ignore
1329 
1330         # change integer values to a tuple of two of those values and change pad_width to index
1331         for k, v in pad_width.items():
1332             if isinstance(v, numbers.Number):
1333                 pad_width[k] = (v, v)
1334         pad_width_by_index = self._pad_options_dim_to_index(pad_width)
1335 
1336         # create pad_options_kwargs, numpy/dask requires only relevant kwargs to be nonempty
1337         pad_option_kwargs = {}
1338         if stat_length is not None:
1339             pad_option_kwargs["stat_length"] = stat_length
1340         if constant_values is not None:
1341             pad_option_kwargs["constant_values"] = constant_values
1342         if end_values is not None:
1343             pad_option_kwargs["end_values"] = end_values
1344         if reflect_type is not None:
1345             pad_option_kwargs["reflect_type"] = reflect_type  # type: ignore
1346 
1347         array = duck_array_ops.pad(
1348             self.data.astype(dtype, copy=False),
1349             pad_width_by_index,
1350             mode=mode,
1351             **pad_option_kwargs,
1352         )
1353 
1354         return type(self)(self.dims, array)
