1356     def _roll_one_dim(self, dim, count):
1357         axis = self.get_axis_num(dim)
1358 
1359         count %= self.shape[axis]
1360         if count != 0:
1361             indices = [slice(-count, None), slice(None, -count)]
1362         else:
1363             indices = [slice(None)]
1364 
1365         arrays = [self[(slice(None),) * axis + (idx,)].data for idx in indices]
1366 
1367         data = duck_array_ops.concatenate(arrays, axis)
1368 
1369         if is_duck_dask_array(data):
1370             # chunked data should come out with the same chunks; this makes
1371             # it feasible to combine shifted and unshifted data
1372             # TODO: remove this once dask.array automatically aligns chunks
1373             data = data.rechunk(self.data.chunks)
1374 
1375         return type(self)(self.dims, data, self._attrs, fastpath=True)

1403     def transpose(self, *dims) -> "Variable":
1404         """Return a new Variable object with transposed dimensions.
1405 
1406         Parameters
1407         ----------
1408         *dims : str, optional
1409             By default, reverse the dimensions. Otherwise, reorder the
1410             dimensions to this order.

1412         Returns
1413         -------
1414         transposed : Variable
1415             The returned object has transposed data and dimensions with the
1416             same attributes as the original.
1417 
1418         Notes
1419         -----
1420         This operation returns a view of this variable's data. It is
1421         lazy for dask-backed Variables but not for numpy-backed Variables.
1422 
1423         See Also
1424         --------
1425         numpy.transpose
1426         """
1427         if len(dims) == 0:
1428             dims = self.dims[::-1]

1430         axes = self.get_axis_num(dims)
1431         if len(dims) < 2 or dims == self.dims:
1432             # no need to transpose if only one dimension
1433             # or dims are in same order
1434             return self.copy(deep=False)

1436         data = as_indexable(self._data).transpose(axes)
1437         return type(self)(dims, data, self._attrs, self._encoding, fastpath=True)

1443     def set_dims(self, dims, shape=None):
1444         """Return a new variable with given set of dimensions.
1445         This method might be used to attach new dimension(s) to variable.
1446 
1447         When possible, this operation does not copy this variable's data.
1448 
1449         Parameters
1450         ----------
1451         dims : str or sequence of str or dict
1452             Dimensions to include on the new variable. If a dict, values are
1453             used to provide the sizes of new dimensions; otherwise, new
1454             dimensions are inserted with length 1.
1455 
1456         Returns
1457         -------
1458         Variable
1459         """
1460         if isinstance(dims, str):
1461             dims = [dims]
1462 
1463         if shape is None and utils.is_dict_like(dims):
1464             shape = dims.values()
1465 
1466         missing_dims = set(self.dims) - set(dims)
1467         if missing_dims:
1468             raise ValueError(
1469                 "new dimensions %r must be a superset of "
1470                 "existing dimensions %r" % (dims, self.dims)
1471             )
1472 
1473         self_dims = set(self.dims)
1474         expanded_dims = tuple(d for d in dims if d not in self_dims) + self.dims
1475 
1476         if self.dims == expanded_dims:
1477             # don't use broadcast_to unless necessary so the result remains
1478             # writeable if possible
1479             expanded_data = self.data
1480         elif shape is not None:
1481             dims_map = dict(zip(dims, shape))
1482             tmp_shape = tuple(dims_map[d] for d in expanded_dims)
1483             expanded_data = duck_array_ops.broadcast_to(self.data, tmp_shape)
1484         else:
1485             expanded_data = self.data[(None,) * (len(expanded_dims) - self.ndim)]
1486 
1487         expanded_var = Variable(
1488             expanded_dims, expanded_data, self._attrs, self._encoding, fastpath=True
1489         )
1490         return expanded_var.transpose(*dims)

1492     def _stack_once(self, dims: List[Hashable], new_dim: Hashable):
1493         if not set(dims) <= set(self.dims):
1494             raise ValueError("invalid existing dimensions: %s" % dims)
1495 
1496         if new_dim in self.dims:
1497             raise ValueError(
1498                 "cannot create a new dimension with the same "
1499                 "name as an existing dimension"
1500             )
1501 
1502         if len(dims) == 0:
1503             # don't stack
1504             return self.copy(deep=False)
1505 
1506         other_dims = [d for d in self.dims if d not in dims]
1507         dim_order = other_dims + list(dims)
1508         reordered = self.transpose(*dim_order)
1509 
1510         new_shape = reordered.shape[: len(other_dims)] + (-1,)
1511         new_data = reordered.data.reshape(new_shape)
1512         new_dims = reordered.dims[: len(other_dims)] + (new_dim,)
1513 
1514         return Variable(new_dims, new_data, self._attrs, self._encoding, fastpath=True)

1516     def stack(self, dimensions=None, **dimensions_kwargs):
1517         """
1518         Stack any number of existing dimensions into a single new dimension.
1519 
1520         New dimensions will be added at the end, and the order of the data
1521         along each new dimension will be in contiguous (C) order.
1522 
1523         Parameters
1524         ----------
1525         dimensions : mapping of hashable to tuple of hashable
1526             Mapping of form new_name=(dim1, dim2, ...) describing the
1527             names of new dimensions, and the existing dimensions that
1528             they replace.
1529         **dimensions_kwargs
1530             The keyword arguments form of ``dimensions``.
1531             One of dimensions or dimensions_kwargs must be provided.
1532 
1533         Returns
1534         -------
1535         stacked : Variable
1536             Variable with the same attributes but stacked data.
1537 
1538         See also
1539         --------
1540         Variable.unstack
1541         """
1542         dimensions = either_dict_or_kwargs(dimensions, dimensions_kwargs, "stack")
1543         result = self
1544         for new_dim, dims in dimensions.items():
1545             result = result._stack_once(dims, new_dim)
1546         return result

1548     def _unstack_once_full(
1549         self, dims: Mapping[Hashable, int], old_dim: Hashable
1550     ) -> "Variable":
1551         """
1552         Unstacks the variable without needing an index.
1553 
1554         Unlike `_unstack_once`, this function requires the existing dimension to
1555         contain the full product of the new dimensions.
1556         """
1557         new_dim_names = tuple(dims.keys())
1558         new_dim_sizes = tuple(dims.values())
1559 
1560         if old_dim not in self.dims:
1561             raise ValueError("invalid existing dimension: %s" % old_dim)
1562 
1563         if set(new_dim_names).intersection(self.dims):
1564             raise ValueError(
1565                 "cannot create a new dimension with the same "
1566                 "name as an existing dimension"
1567             )
1568 
1569         if np.prod(new_dim_sizes) != self.sizes[old_dim]:
1570             raise ValueError(
1571                 "the product of the new dimension sizes must "
1572                 "equal the size of the old dimension"
1573             )
1574 
1575         other_dims = [d for d in self.dims if d != old_dim]
1576         dim_order = other_dims + [old_dim]
1577         reordered = self.transpose(*dim_order)
1578 
1579         new_shape = reordered.shape[: len(other_dims)] + new_dim_sizes
1580         new_data = reordered.data.reshape(new_shape)
1581         new_dims = reordered.dims[: len(other_dims)] + new_dim_names
1582 
1583         return Variable(new_dims, new_data, self._attrs, self._encoding, fastpath=True)
1584 
1585     def _unstack_once(
1586         self,
1587         index: pd.MultiIndex,
1588         dim: Hashable,
1589         fill_value=dtypes.NA,
1590     ) -> "Variable":
1591         """
1592         Unstacks this variable given an index to unstack and the name of the
1593         dimension to which the index refers.
1594         """
1595 
1596         reordered = self.transpose(..., dim)
1597 
1598         new_dim_sizes = [lev.size for lev in index.levels]
1599         new_dim_names = index.names
1600         indexer = index.codes
1601 
1602         # Potentially we could replace `len(other_dims)` with just `-1`
1603         other_dims = [d for d in self.dims if d != dim]
1604         new_shape = list(reordered.shape[: len(other_dims)]) + new_dim_sizes
1605         new_dims = reordered.dims[: len(other_dims)] + new_dim_names
1606 
1607         if fill_value is dtypes.NA:
1608             is_missing_values = np.prod(new_shape) > np.prod(self.shape)
1609             if is_missing_values:
1610                 dtype, fill_value = dtypes.maybe_promote(self.dtype)
1611             else:
1612                 dtype = self.dtype
1613                 fill_value = dtypes.get_fill_value(dtype)
1614         else:
1615             dtype = self.dtype
1616 
1617         # Currently fails on sparse due to https://github.com/pydata/sparse/issues/422
1618         data = np.full_like(
1619             self.data,
1620             fill_value=fill_value,
1621             shape=new_shape,
1622             dtype=dtype,
1623         )
1624 
1625         # Indexer is a list of lists of locations. Each list is the locations
1626         # on the new dimension. This is robust to the data being sparse; in that
1627         # case the destinations will be NaN / zero.
1628         data[(..., *indexer)] = reordered
1629 
1630         return self._replace(dims=new_dims, data=data)
1631 
1632     def unstack(self, dimensions=None, **dimensions_kwargs):
1633         """
1634         Unstack an existing dimension into multiple new dimensions.
1635 
1636         New dimensions will be added at the end, and the order of the data
1637         along each new dimension will be in contiguous (C) order.
1638 
1639         Note that unlike ``DataArray.unstack`` and ``Dataset.unstack``, this
1640         method requires the existing dimension to contain the full product of
1641         the new dimensions.
1642 
1643         Parameters
1644         ----------
1645         dimensions : mapping of hashable to mapping of hashable to int
1646             Mapping of the form old_dim={dim1: size1, ...} describing the
1647             names of existing dimensions, and the new dimensions and sizes
1648             that they map to.
1649         **dimensions_kwargs
1650             The keyword arguments form of ``dimensions``.
1651             One of dimensions or dimensions_kwargs must be provided.
1652 
1653         Returns
1654         -------
1655         unstacked : Variable
1656             Variable with the same attributes but unstacked data.
1657 
1658         See also
1659         --------
1660         Variable.stack
1661         DataArray.unstack
1662         Dataset.unstack
1663         """
1664         dimensions = either_dict_or_kwargs(dimensions, dimensions_kwargs, "unstack")
1665         result = self
1666         for old_dim, dims in dimensions.items():
1667             result = result._unstack_once_full(dims, old_dim)
1668         return result

1676     def reduce(
1677         self,
1678         func,
1679         dim=None,
1680         axis=None,
1681         keep_attrs=None,
1682         keepdims=False,
1683         **kwargs,
1684     ):
1685         """Reduce this array by applying `func` along some dimension(s).
1686 
1687         Parameters
1688         ----------
1689         func : callable
1690             Function which can be called in the form
1691             `func(x, axis=axis, **kwargs)` to return the result of reducing an
1692             np.ndarray over an integer valued axis.
1693         dim : str or sequence of str, optional
1694             Dimension(s) over which to apply `func`.
1695         axis : int or sequence of int, optional
1696             Axis(es) over which to apply `func`. Only one of the 'dim'
1697             and 'axis' arguments can be supplied. If neither are supplied, then
1698             the reduction is calculated over the flattened array (by calling
1699             `func(x)` without an axis argument).
1700         keep_attrs : bool, optional
1701             If True, the variable's attributes (`attrs`) will be copied from
1702             the original object to the new one.  If False (default), the new
1703             object will be returned without attributes.
1704         keepdims : bool, default: False
1705             If True, the dimensions which are reduced are left in the result
1706             as dimensions of size one
1707         **kwargs : dict
1708             Additional keyword arguments passed on to `func`.
1709 
1710         Returns
1711         -------
1712         reduced : Array
1713             Array with summarized data and the indicated dimension(s)
1714             removed.
1715         """
1716         if dim == ...:
1717             dim = None
1718         if dim is not None and axis is not None:
1719             raise ValueError("cannot supply both 'axis' and 'dim' arguments")
1720 
1721         if dim is not None:
1722             axis = self.get_axis_num(dim)
1723 
1724         with warnings.catch_warnings():
1725             warnings.filterwarnings(
1726                 "ignore", r"Mean of empty slice", category=RuntimeWarning
1727             )
1728             if axis is not None:
1729                 data = func(self.data, axis=axis, **kwargs)
1730             else:
1731                 data = func(self.data, **kwargs)
1732 
1733         if getattr(data, "shape", ()) == self.shape:
1734             dims = self.dims
1735         else:
1736             removed_axes = (
1737                 range(self.ndim) if axis is None else np.atleast_1d(axis) % self.ndim
1738             )
1739             if keepdims:
1740                 # Insert np.newaxis for removed dims
1741                 slices = tuple(
1742                     np.newaxis if i in removed_axes else slice(None, None)
1743                     for i in range(self.ndim)
1744                 )
1745                 if getattr(data, "shape", None) is None:
1746                     # Reduce has produced a scalar value, not an array-like
1747                     data = np.asanyarray(data)[slices]
1748                 else:
1749                     data = data[slices]
1750                 dims = self.dims
1751             else:
1752                 dims = [
1753                     adim for n, adim in enumerate(self.dims) if n not in removed_axes
1754                 ]
1755 
1756         if keep_attrs is None:
1757             keep_attrs = _get_keep_attrs(default=False)
1758         attrs = self._attrs if keep_attrs else None
1759 
1760         return Variable(dims, data, attrs=attrs)

1762     @classmethod
1763     def concat(cls, variables, dim="concat_dim", positions=None, shortcut=False):
1764         """Concatenate variables along a new or existing dimension.
1765 
1766         Parameters
1767         ----------
1768         variables : iterable of Variable
1769             Arrays to stack together. Each variable is expected to have
1770             matching dimensions and shape except for along the stacked
1771             dimension.
1772         dim : str or DataArray, optional
1773             Name of the dimension to stack along. This can either be a new
1774             dimension name, in which case it is added along axis=0, or an
1775             existing dimension name, in which case the location of the
1776             dimension is unchanged. Where to insert the new dimension is
1777             determined by the first variable.
1778         positions : None or list of array-like, optional
1779             List of integer arrays which specifies the integer positions to
1780             which to assign each dataset along the concatenated dimension.
1781             If not supplied, objects are concatenated in the provided order.
1782         shortcut : bool, optional
1783             This option is used internally to speed-up groupby operations.
1784             If `shortcut` is True, some checks of internal consistency between
1785             arrays to concatenate are skipped.
1786 
1787         Returns
1788         -------
1789         stacked : Variable
1790             Concatenated Variable formed by stacking all the supplied variables
1791             along the given dimension.
1792         """
1793         if not isinstance(dim, str):
1794             (dim,) = dim.dims
1795 
1796         # can't do this lazily: we need to loop through variables at least
1797         # twice
1798         variables = list(variables)
1799         first_var = variables[0]
1800 
1801         arrays = [v.data for v in variables]
1802 
1803         if dim in first_var.dims:
1804             axis = first_var.get_axis_num(dim)
1805             dims = first_var.dims
1806             data = duck_array_ops.concatenate(arrays, axis=axis)
1807             if positions is not None:
1808                 # TODO: deprecate this option -- we don't need it for groupby
1809                 # any more.
1810                 indices = nputils.inverse_permutation(np.concatenate(positions))
1811                 data = duck_array_ops.take(data, indices, axis=axis)
1812         else:
1813             axis = 0
1814             dims = (dim,) + first_var.dims
1815             data = duck_array_ops.stack(arrays, axis=axis)
1816 
1817         attrs = dict(first_var.attrs)
1818         encoding = dict(first_var.encoding)
1819         if not shortcut:
1820             for var in variables:
1821                 if var.dims != first_var.dims:
1822                     raise ValueError(
1823                         f"Variable has dimensions {list(var.dims)} but first Variable has dimensions {list(first_var.dims)}"
1824                     )
1825 
1826         return cls(dims, data, attrs, encoding)

1828     def equals(self, other, equiv=duck_array_ops.array_equiv):
1829         """True if two Variables have the same dimensions and values;
1830         otherwise False.
1831 
1832         Variables can still be equal (like pandas objects) if they have NaN
1833         values in the same locations.
1834 
1835         This method is necessary because `v1 == v2` for Variables
1836         does element-wise comparisons (like numpy.ndarrays).
1837         """
1838         other = getattr(other, "variable", other)
1839         try:
1840             return self.dims == other.dims and (
1841                 self._data is other._data or equiv(self.data, other.data)
1842             )
1843         except (TypeError, AttributeError):
1844             return False
1845 
1846     def broadcast_equals(self, other, equiv=duck_array_ops.array_equiv):
1847         """True if two Variables have the values after being broadcast against
1848         each other; otherwise False.
1849 
1850         Variables can still be equal (like pandas objects) if they have NaN
1851         values in the same locations.
1852         """
1853         try:
1854             self, other = broadcast_variables(self, other)
1855         except (ValueError, AttributeError):
1856             return False
1857         return self.equals(other, equiv=equiv)

1859     def identical(self, other, equiv=duck_array_ops.array_equiv):
1860         """Like equals, but also checks attributes."""
1861         try:
1862             return utils.dict_equiv(self.attrs, other.attrs) and self.equals(
1863                 other, equiv=equiv
1864             )
1865         except (TypeError, AttributeError):
1866             return False

1868     def no_conflicts(self, other, equiv=duck_array_ops.array_notnull_equiv):
1869         """True if the intersection of two Variable's non-null data is
1870         equal; otherwise false.
1871 
1872         Variables can thus still be equal if there are locations where either,
1873         or both, contain NaN values.
1874         """
1875         return self.broadcast_equals(other, equiv=equiv)

1877     def quantile(
1878         self, q, dim=None, interpolation="linear", keep_attrs=None, skipna=True
1879     ):
1880         """Compute the qth quantile of the data along the specified dimension.
1881 
1882         Returns the qth quantiles(s) of the array elements.
1883 
1884         Parameters
1885         ----------
1886         q : float or sequence of float
1887             Quantile to compute, which must be between 0 and 1
1888             inclusive.
1889         dim : str or sequence of str, optional
1890             Dimension(s) over which to apply quantile.
1891         interpolation : {"linear", "lower", "higher", "midpoint", "nearest"}, default: "linear"
1892             This optional parameter specifies the interpolation method to
1893             use when the desired quantile lies between two data points
1894             ``i < j``:
1895 
1896                 * linear: ``i + (j - i) * fraction``, where ``fraction`` is
1897                   the fractional part of the index surrounded by ``i`` and
1898                   ``j``.
1899                 * lower: ``i``.
1900                 * higher: ``j``.
1901                 * nearest: ``i`` or ``j``, whichever is nearest.
1902                 * midpoint: ``(i + j) / 2``.
1903 
1904         keep_attrs : bool, optional
1905             If True, the variable's attributes (`attrs`) will be copied from
1906             the original object to the new one.  If False (default), the new
1907             object will be returned without attributes.
1908 
1909         Returns
1910         -------
1911         quantiles : Variable
1912             If `q` is a single quantile, then the result
1913             is a scalar. If multiple percentiles are given, first axis of
1914             the result corresponds to the quantile and a quantile dimension
1915             is added to the return array. The other dimensions are the
1916             dimensions that remain after the reduction of the array.
1917 
1918         See Also
1919         --------
1920         numpy.nanquantile, pandas.Series.quantile, Dataset.quantile,
1921         DataArray.quantile
1922         """
1923 
1924         from .computation import apply_ufunc
1925 
1926         _quantile_func = np.nanquantile if skipna else np.quantile
1927 
1928         if keep_attrs is None:
1929             keep_attrs = _get_keep_attrs(default=False)
1930 
1931         scalar = utils.is_scalar(q)
1932         q = np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(q, dtype=np.float64))
1933 
1934         if dim is None:
1935             dim = self.dims
1936

1969         would have been otherwise assigned to all of the values within that
1970         set.  Ranks begin at 1, not 0. If `pct`, computes percentage ranks.

1977         ----------

1985         ranked : Variable

2014     def rolling_window(
2015         self, dim, window, window_dim, center=False, fill_value=dtypes.NA

2018         Make a rolling_window along dim and add a new_dim to the last place.
2019 
2020         Parameters
2021         ----------
2022         dim : str
2023             Dimension over which to compute rolling_window.
2024             For nd-rolling, should be list of dimensions.

2033             of the axis.

2038         -------

2040         size w.

2042         The return shape: self.shape + (window, )

2044         Examples
2045         --------
2046         >>> v = Variable(("a", "b"), np.arange(8).reshape((2, 4)))
2047         >>> v.rolling_window("b", 3, "window_dim")
2048         <xarray.Variable (a: 2, b: 4, window_dim: 3)>
2049         array([[[nan, nan,  0.],
2050                 [nan,  0.,  1.],
2051                 [ 0.,  1.,  2.],
2052                 [ 1.,  2.,  3.]],
2053         <BLANKLINE>
2054                [[nan, nan,  4.],
2055                 [nan,  4.,  5.],
2056                 [ 4.,  5.,  6.],
2057                 [ 5.,  6.,  7.]]])
2058 
2059         >>> v.rolling_window("b", 3, "window_dim", center=True)
2060         <xarray.Variable (a: 2, b: 4, window_dim: 3)>
2061         array([[[nan,  0.,  1.],
2062                 [ 0.,  1.,  2.],
2063                 [ 1.,  2.,  3.],
2064                 [ 2.,  3., nan]],
2065         <BLANKLINE>
2066                [[nan,  4.,  5.],
2067                 [ 4.,  5.,  6.],
2068                 [ 5.,  6.,  7.],
2069                 [ 6.,  7., nan]]])
2070         """
2071         if fill_value is dtypes.NA:  # np.nan is passed
2072             dtype, fill_value = dtypes.maybe_promote(self.dtype)
2073             array = self.astype(dtype, copy=False).data
2074         else:
2075             dtype = self.dtype
2076             array = self.data
2077 
2078         if isinstance(dim, list):
2079             assert len(dim) == len(window)
2080             assert len(dim) == len(window_dim)
2081             assert len(dim) == len(center)

2083             dim = [dim]
2084             window = [window]
2085             window_dim = [window_dim]
2086             center = [center]

2088         new_dims = self.dims + tuple(window_dim)

2090             new_dims,
2091             duck_array_ops.rolling_window(

2097         self, windows, func, boundary="exact", side="left", keep_attrs=None, **kwargs
2098     ):

2100         Apply reduction function.
2101         """
2102         windows = {k: v for k, v in windows.items() if k in self.dims}
2103         if not windows:
2104             return self.copy()
2105 
2106         if keep_attrs is None:
2107             keep_attrs = _get_keep_attrs(default=False)
2108 
2109         if keep_attrs:
2110             _attrs = self.attrs
2111         else:
2112             _attrs = None
2113 
2114         reshaped, axes = self._coarsen_reshape(windows, boundary, side)
2115         if isinstance(func, str):
2116             name = func
2117             func = getattr(duck_array_ops, name, None)

2123     def _coarsen_reshape(self, windows, boundary, side):
2124         """
2125         Construct a reshaped-array for coarsen
2126         """
2127         if not utils.is_dict_like(boundary):
2128             boundary = {d: boundary for d in windows.keys()}
2129 
2130         if not utils.is_dict_like(side):
2131             side = {d: side for d in windows.keys()}
2132 
2133         # remove unrelated dimensions
2134         boundary = {k: v for k, v in boundary.items() if k in windows}
2135         side = {k: v for k, v in side.items() if k in windows}
2136 
2137         for d, window in windows.items():
2138             if window <= 0:
2139                 raise ValueError(f"window must be > 0. Given {window}")
2140 
2141         variable = self
2142         for d, window in windows.items():
2143             # trim or pad the object
2144             size = variable.shape[self._get_axis_num(d)]
2145             n = int(size / window)
2146             if boundary[d] == "exact":
2147                 if n * window != size:
2148                     raise ValueError(
2149                         "Could not coarsen a dimension of size {} with "
2150                         "window {}".format(size, window)
2151                     )
2152             elif boundary[d] == "trim":
2153                 if side[d] == "left":
2154                     variable = variable.isel({d: slice(0, window * n)})
2155                 else:
2156                     excess = size - window * n
2157                     variable = variable.isel({d: slice(excess, None)})
2158             elif boundary[d] == "pad":  # pad
2159                 pad = window * n - size
2160                 if pad < 0:
2161                     pad += window
2162                 if side[d] == "left":
2163                     pad_width = {d: (0, pad)}
2164                 else:
2165                     pad_width = {d: (pad, 0)}
2166                 variable = variable.pad(pad_width, mode="constant")
2167             else:
2168                 raise TypeError(
2169                     "{} is invalid for boundary. Valid option is 'exact', "
2170                     "'trim' and 'pad'".format(boundary[d])
2171                 )
2172 
2173         shape = []
2174         axes = []
2175         axis_count = 0
2176         for i, d in enumerate(variable.dims):
2177             if d in windows:
2178                 size = variable.shape[i]
2179                 shape.append(int(size / windows[d]))
2180                 shape.append(windows[d])
2181                 axis_count += 1
2182                 axes.append(i + axis_count)
2183             else:
2184                 shape.append(variable.shape[i])
2185 
2186         return variable.data.reshape(shape), tuple(axes)

2326     def _unravel_argminmax(
2327         self,
2328         argminmax: str,
2329         dim: Union[Hashable, Sequence[Hashable], None],
2330         axis: Union[int, None],
2331         keep_attrs: Optional[bool],
2332         skipna: Optional[bool],
2333     ) -> Union["Variable", Dict[Hashable, "Variable"]]:
2334         """Apply argmin or argmax over one or more dimensions, returning the result as a
2335         dict of DataArray that can be passed directly to isel.
2336         """
2337         if dim is None and axis is None:
2338             warnings.warn(
2339                 "Behaviour of argmin/argmax with neither dim nor axis argument will "
2340                 "change to return a dict of indices of each dimension. To get a "
2341                 "single, flat index, please use np.argmin(da.data) or "
2342                 "np.argmax(da.data) instead of da.argmin() or da.argmax().",
2343                 DeprecationWarning,
2344                 stacklevel=3,
2345             )
2346 
2347         argminmax_func = getattr(duck_array_ops, argminmax)
2348 
2349         if dim is ...:
2350             # In future, should do this also when (dim is None and axis is None)
2351             dim = self.dims
2352         if (
2353             dim is None
2354             or axis is not None
2355             or not isinstance(dim, Sequence)
2356             or isinstance(dim, str)
2357         ):
2358             # Return int index if single dimension is passed, and is not part of a
2359             # sequence
2360             return self.reduce(
2361                 argminmax_func, dim=dim, axis=axis, keep_attrs=keep_attrs, skipna=skipna
2362             )
2363 
2364         # Get a name for the new dimension that does not conflict with any existing
2365         # dimension
2366         newdimname = "_unravel_argminmax_dim_0"
2367         count = 1
2368         while newdimname in self.dims:
2369             newdimname = f"_unravel_argminmax_dim_{count}"
2370             count += 1
2371 
2372         stacked = self.stack({newdimname: dim})
2373 
2374         result_dims = stacked.dims[:-1]
2375         reduce_shape = tuple(self.sizes[d] for d in dim)
2376 
2377         result_flat_indices = stacked.reduce(argminmax_func, axis=-1, skipna=skipna)
2378 
2379         result_unravelled_indices = duck_array_ops.unravel_index(
2380             result_flat_indices.data, reduce_shape
2381         )
2382 
2383         result = {
2384             d: Variable(dims=result_dims, data=i)
2385             for d, i in zip(dim, result_unravelled_indices)
2386         }
2387 
2388         if keep_attrs is None:
2389             keep_attrs = _get_keep_attrs(default=False)
2390         if keep_attrs:
2391             for v in result.values():
2392                 v.attrs = self.attrs
2393 
2394         return result

DataSet.update causes chunked dask DataArray to evalute its values eagerly 
**What happened**:
Used `DataSet.update` to update a chunked dask DataArray, but the DataArray is no longer chunked after the update.

**What you expected to happen**:
The chunked DataArray should still be chunked after the update

**Minimal Complete Verifiable Example**:

```python
foo = xr.DataArray(np.random.randn(3, 3), dims=("x", "y")).chunk()  # foo is chunked
ds = xr.Dataset({"foo": foo, "bar": ("x", [1, 2, 3])})  # foo is still chunked here
ds  # you can verify that foo is chunked
```

```python
update_dict = {"foo": (("x", "y"), ds.foo[1:, :]), "bar": ("x", ds.bar[1:])}
update_dict["foo"][1]  # foo is still chunked
```
```python
ds.update(update_dict)
ds  # now foo is no longer chunked
```

```python
    if isinstance(data, (DataArray, Variable)):

```
but I didn't check if that would break anything. Are you up for sending in a PR?

> xarray.core.variable.as_compatible_data doesn't consider DataArray objects:

I don't think DataArrays are expected at that level though. BUT I'm probably wrong.

> {"foo": (("x", "y"), ds.foo[1:, :]), "bar": ("x", ds.bar[1:])}

This syntax is weird. You should be able to do `update_dict = {"foo": ds.foo[1:, :], "bar": ds.bar[1:]}` . 

For the simple example,  `ds.update(update_dict)` and `ds.assign(update_dict)` both fail because you can't align dimensions without labels when the dimension size is different between variables (I find this confusing).

> when the dimension size is different between variables (I find this confusing).

I guess the issue is that the dataset has `x` at a certain size and by reassigning we're trying to set `x` to a different size. I *think* the failure is expected in this case, and it could be solved by assigning labels to `x`.

```python
ds2 = ds.isel(x=slice(1, None))
ds2
```

should do the same, but without having to worry about manually reconstructing a valid dataset.

[Bug]: scalar mappable format_cursor_data crashes on BoundarNorm
### Bug summary

In 3.5.0 if you do:

```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import matplotlib as mpl

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
norm = mpl.colors.BoundaryNorm(np.linspace(-4, 4, 5), 256)
X = np.random.randn(10, 10)
pc = ax.imshow(X, cmap='RdBu_r', norm=norm)
```

and mouse over the image, it crashes with

```
File "/Users/jklymak/matplotlib/lib/matplotlib/artist.py", line 1282, in format_cursor_data
    neighbors = self.norm.inverse(
  File "/Users/jklymak/matplotlib/lib/matplotlib/colors.py", line 1829, in inverse
    raise ValueError("BoundaryNorm is not invertible")
ValueError: BoundaryNorm is not invertible
```

and interaction stops.  

Not sure if we should have a special check here, a try-except, or actually just make BoundaryNorm approximately invertible.  


### Matplotlib Version

main 3.5.0

23 def allow_rasterization(draw):
24     """
25     Decorator for Artist.draw method. Provides routines
26     that run before and after the draw call. The before and after functions
27     are useful for changing artist-dependent renderer attributes or making
28     other setup function calls, such as starting and flushing a mixed-mode
29     renderer.
30     """
31 
32     @wraps(draw)
33     def draw_wrapper(artist, renderer):
34         try:
35             if artist.get_rasterized():
36                 if renderer._raster_depth == 0 and not renderer._rasterizing:
37                     renderer.start_rasterizing()
38                     renderer._rasterizing = True
39                 renderer._raster_depth += 1
40             else:
41                 if renderer._raster_depth == 0 and renderer._rasterizing:
42                     # Only stop when we are not in a rasterized parent
43                     # and something has be rasterized since last stop
44                     renderer.stop_rasterizing()
45                     renderer._rasterizing = False
46 
47             if artist.get_agg_filter() is not None:
48                 renderer.start_filter()
49 
50             return draw(artist, renderer)
51         finally:
52             if artist.get_agg_filter() is not None:
53                 renderer.stop_filter(artist.get_agg_filter())
54             if artist.get_rasterized():
55                 renderer._raster_depth -= 1
56             if (renderer._rasterizing and artist.figure and
57                     artist.figure.suppressComposite):
58                 # restart rasterizing to prevent merging
59                 renderer.stop_rasterizing()
60                 renderer.start_rasterizing()
61 
62     draw_wrapper._supports_rasterization = True
63     return draw_wrapper

74         if renderer._rasterizing:

489     def pick(self, mouseevent):
490         """
491         Process a pick event.
492 
493         Each child artist will fire a pick event if *mouseevent* is over
494         the artist and the artist has picker set.
495 
496         See Also
497         --------
498         set_picker, get_picker, pickable
499         """
500         # Pick self
501         if self.pickable():
502             picker = self.get_picker()
503             if callable(picker):
504                 inside, prop = picker(self, mouseevent)
505             else:
506                 inside, prop = self.contains(mouseevent)
507             if inside:
508                 self.figure.canvas.pick_event(mouseevent, self, **prop)
509 
510         # Pick children
511         for a in self.get_children():
512             # make sure the event happened in the same Axes
513             ax = getattr(a, 'axes', None)
514             if (mouseevent.inaxes is None or ax is None
515                     or mouseevent.inaxes == ax):
516                 # we need to check if mouseevent.inaxes is None
517                 # because some objects associated with an Axes (e.g., a
518                 # tick label) can be outside the bounding box of the
519                 # Axes and inaxes will be None
520                 # also check that ax is None so that it traverse objects
521                 # which do no have an axes property but children might
522                 a.pick(mouseevent)
523

740     def set_clip_path(self, path, transform=None):
741         """
742         Set the artist's clip path.
743 
744         Parameters
745         ----------
746         path : `.Patch` or `.Path` or `.TransformedPath` or None
747             The clip path. If given a `.Path`, *transform* must be provided as
748             well. If *None*, a previously set clip path is removed.
749         transform : `~matplotlib.transforms.Transform`, optional
750             Only used if *path* is a `.Path`, in which case the given `.Path`
751             is converted to a `.TransformedPath` using *transform*.
752 
753         Notes
754         -----
755         For efficiency, if *path* is a `.Rectangle` this method will set the
756         clipping box to the corresponding rectangle and set the clipping path
757         to ``None``.
758 
759         For technical reasons (support of `~.Artist.set`), a tuple
760         (*path*, *transform*) is also accepted as a single positional
761         parameter.
762 
763         .. ACCEPTS: Patch or (Path, Transform) or None
764         """
765         from matplotlib.patches import Patch, Rectangle
766 
767         success = False
768         if transform is None:
769             if isinstance(path, Rectangle):
770                 self.clipbox = TransformedBbox(Bbox.unit(),
771                                                path.get_transform())
772                 self._clippath = None
773                 success = True
774             elif isinstance(path, Patch):
775                 self._clippath = TransformedPatchPath(path)
776                 success = True
777             elif isinstance(path, tuple):
778                 path, transform = path
779 
780         if path is None:
781             self._clippath = None
782             success = True
783         elif isinstance(path, Path):
784             self._clippath = TransformedPath(path, transform)
785             success = True
786         elif isinstance(path, TransformedPatchPath):
787             self._clippath = path
788             success = True
789         elif isinstance(path, TransformedPath):
790             self._clippath = path
791             success = True
792 
793         if not success:
794             raise TypeError(
795                 "Invalid arguments to set_clip_path, of type {} and {}"
796                 .format(type(path).__name__, type(transform).__name__))
797         # This may result in the callbacks being hit twice, but guarantees they
798         # will be hit at least once.
799         self.pchanged()
800         self.stale = True

828     def _fully_clipped_to_axes(self):

831         and can thus be skipped in layout calculations. Requires `get_clip_on`
832         is True, one of `clip_box` or `clip_path` is set, ``clip_box.extents``

834         is equivalent to ``ax.patch`` (if set).

844                 and self.get_clip_on()
845                 and (clip_box is not None or clip_path is not None)
846                 and (clip_box is None
847                      or np.all(clip_box.extents == self.axes.bbox.extents))
848                 and (clip_path is None
849                      or isinstance(clip_path, TransformedPatchPath)
850                      and clip_path._patch is self.axes.patch))

@@ -1303,10 +1304,20 @@ def format_cursor_data(self, data):
                 return "[]"
             normed = self.norm(data)
             if np.isfinite(normed):
-                # Midpoints of neighboring color intervals.

-                    (int(self.norm(data) * n) + np.array([0, 1])) / n)
-                delta = abs(neighbors - data).max()
+                if isinstance(self.norm, BoundaryNorm):
+                    # not an invertible normalization mapping
+                    cur_idx = np.argmin(np.abs(self.norm.boundaries - data))
+                    neigh_idx = max(0, cur_idx - 1)
+                    # use max diff to prevent delta == 0
+                    delta = np.diff(
+                        self.norm.boundaries[neigh_idx:cur_idx + 2]
+                    ).max()
+
+                else:
+                    # Midpoints of neighboring color intervals.
+                    neighbors = self.norm.inverse(
+                        (int(normed * n) + np.array([0, 1])) / n)
+                    delta = abs(neighbors - data).max()
                 g_sig_digits = cbook._g_sig_digits(data, delta)
             else:

745                 "    {exc_type}: {exc_msg}\n"

Two sections called Symbols in index
When using index entries with the following leading characters: _@_, _£_, and _←_ I get two sections called _Symbols_ in the HTML output, the first containing all _@_ entries before ”normal” words and the second containing _£_ and _←_ entries after the ”normal” words. problem_statement:
Allow ValidationErrors to equal each other when created identically
Description
	 
		(last modified by kamni)
	 
Currently ValidationErrors (django.core.exceptions.ValidationError) that have identical messages don't equal each other, which is counter-intuitive, and can make certain kinds of testing more complicated. Please add an __eq__ method that allows two ValidationErrors to be compared. 
Ideally, this would be more than just a simple self.messages == other.messages. It would be most helpful if the comparison were independent of the order in which errors were raised in a field or in non_field_errors.
hints_text:
I probably wouldn't want to limit the comparison to an error's message but rather to its full set of attributes (message, code, params). While params is always pushed into message when iterating over the errors in an ValidationError, I believe it can be beneficial to know if the params that were put inside are the same.
​PR
patch:
<patch>
diff --git a/django/core/exceptions.py b/django/core/exceptions.py
--- a/django/core/exceptions.py
+++ b/django/core/exceptions.py
@@ -1,6 +1,9 @@
 """
 Global Django exception and warning classes.
 """
+import operator
+
+from django.utils.hashable import make_hashable
 
 
 class FieldDoesNotExist(Exception):
@@ -182,6 +185,23 @@ def __str__(self):
     def __repr__(self):
         return 'ValidationError(%s)' % self
 
+    def __eq__(self, other):
+        if not isinstance(other, ValidationError):
+            return NotImplemented
+        return hash(self) == hash(other)
+
+    def __hash__(self):
+        # Ignore params and messages ordering.
+        if hasattr(self, 'message'):
+            return hash((
+                self.message,
+                self.code,
+                tuple(sorted(make_hashable(self.params))) if self.params else None,
+            ))
+        if hasattr(self, 'error_dict'):
+            return hash(tuple(sorted(make_hashable(self.error_dict))))
+        return hash(tuple(sorted(self.error_list, key=operator.attrgetter('message'))))
+
 
 class EmptyResultSet(Exception):
     """A database query predicate is impossible."""

</patch>

255         :meth:`~astropy.wcs.Wcsprm.sub`.  If a header is provided, and
256         *naxis* is not ``None``, *naxis* will be passed to
257         :meth:`~astropy.wcs.Wcsprm.sub` in order to select specific
258         axes from the header.  See :meth:`~astropy.wcs.Wcsprm.sub` for
259         more details about this parameter.
260 
261     keysel : sequence of flags, optional
262         A sequence of flags used to select the keyword types
263         considered by wcslib.  When ``None``, only the standard image
264         header keywords are considered (and the underlying wcspih() C
265         function is called).  To use binary table image array or pixel
266         list keywords, *keysel* must be set.
267 
268         Each element in the list should be one of the following
269         strings:
270 
271         - 'image': Image header keywords
272 
273         - 'binary': Binary table image array keywords
274 
275         - 'pixel': Pixel list keywords
276 
277         Keywords such as ``EQUIna`` or ``RFRQna`` that are common to
278         binary table image arrays and pixel lists (including
279         ``WCSNna`` and ``TWCSna``) are selected by both 'binary' and
280         'pixel'.
281 
282     colsel : sequence of int, optional
283         A sequence of table column numbers used to restrict the WCS
284         transformations considered to only those pertaining to the
285         specified columns.  If `None`, there is no restriction.
286 
287     fix : bool, optional
288         When `True` (default), call `~astropy.wcs.Wcsprm.fix` on
289         the resulting object to fix any non-standard uses in the
290         header.  `FITSFixedWarning` Warnings will be emitted if any
291         changes were made.
292 
293     translate_units : str, optional
294         Specify which potentially unsafe translations of non-standard
295         unit strings to perform.  By default, performs none.  See
296         `WCS.fix` for more information about this parameter.  Only
297         effective when ``fix`` is `True`.
298 
299     Raises
300     ------
301     MemoryError
302          Memory allocation failed.
303 
304     ValueError
305          Invalid key.
306 
307     KeyError
308          Key not found in FITS header.
309 
310     ValueError
311          Lookup table distortion present in the header but *fobj* was
312          not provided.
313 
314     Notes
315     -----
316 
317     1. astropy.wcs supports arbitrary *n* dimensions for the core WCS
318        (the transformations handled by WCSLIB).  However, the
319        `distortion paper`_ lookup table and `SIP`_ distortions must be
320        two dimensional.  Therefore, if you try to create a WCS object
321        where the core WCS has a different number of dimensions than 2
322        and that object also contains a `distortion paper`_ lookup
323        table or `SIP`_ distortion, a `ValueError`
324        exception will be raised.  To avoid this, consider using the
325        *naxis* kwarg to select two dimensions from the core WCS.
326 
327     2. The number of coordinate axes in the transformation is not
328        determined directly from the ``NAXIS`` keyword but instead from
329        the highest of:
330 
331            - ``NAXIS`` keyword
332 
333            - ``WCSAXESa`` keyword
334 
335            - The highest axis number in any parameterized WCS keyword.
336              The keyvalue, as well as the keyword, must be
337              syntactically valid otherwise it will not be considered.
338 
339        If none of these keyword types is present, i.e. if the header
340        only contains auxiliary WCS keywords for a particular
341        coordinate representation, then no coordinate description is
342        constructed for it.
343 
344        The number of axes, which is set as the ``naxis`` member, may
345        differ for different coordinate representations of the same
346        image.
347 
348     3. When the header includes duplicate keywords, in most cases the
349        last encountered is used.
350 
351     4. `~astropy.wcs.Wcsprm.set` is called immediately after
352        construction, so any invalid keywords or transformations will
353        be raised by the constructor, not when subsequently calling a
354        transformation method.
355 
356     """
357 
358     def __init__(self, header=None, fobj=None, key=' ', minerr=0.0,
359                  relax=True, naxis=None, keysel=None, colsel=None,
360                  fix=True, translate_units='', _do_set=True):
361         close_fds = []
362 
363         if header is None:
364             if naxis is None:
365                 naxis = 2
366             wcsprm = _wcs.Wcsprm(header=None, key=key,
367                                  relax=relax, naxis=naxis)
368             self.naxis = wcsprm.naxis
369             # Set some reasonable defaults.
370             det2im = (None, None)
371             cpdis = (None, None)
372             sip = None
373         else:
374             keysel_flags = _parse_keysel(keysel)
375 
376             if isinstance(header, (str, bytes)):
377                 try:
378                     is_path = (possible_filename(header) and
379                                os.path.exists(header))
380                 except (OSError, ValueError):
381                     is_path = False
382 
383                 if is_path:
384                     if fobj is not None:
385                         raise ValueError(
386                             "Can not provide both a FITS filename to "
387                             "argument 1 and a FITS file object to argument 2")
388                     fobj = fits.open(header)
389                     close_fds.append(fobj)
390                     header = fobj[0].header
391             elif isinstance(header, fits.hdu.image._ImageBaseHDU):
392                 header = header.header
393             elif not isinstance(header, fits.Header):
394                 try:
395                     # Accept any dict-like object
396                     orig_header = header
397                     header = fits.Header()
398                     for dict_key in orig_header.keys():
399                         header[dict_key] = orig_header[dict_key]
400                 except TypeError:
401                     raise TypeError(
402                         "header must be a string, an astropy.io.fits.Header "
403                         "object, or a dict-like object")
404 
405             if isinstance(header, fits.Header):
406                 header_string = header.tostring().rstrip()
407             else:
408                 header_string = header
409 
410             # Importantly, header is a *copy* of the passed-in header
411             # because we will be modifying it
412             if isinstance(header_string, str):
413                 header_bytes = header_string.encode('ascii')
414                 header_string = header_string
415             else:
416                 header_bytes = header_string
417                 header_string = header_string.decode('ascii')
418 
419             try:
420                 tmp_header = fits.Header.fromstring(header_string)
421                 self._remove_sip_kw(tmp_header)
422                 tmp_header_bytes = tmp_header.tostring().rstrip()
423                 if isinstance(tmp_header_bytes, str):
424                     tmp_header_bytes = tmp_header_bytes.encode('ascii')
425                 tmp_wcsprm = _wcs.Wcsprm(header=tmp_header_bytes, key=key,
426                                          relax=relax, keysel=keysel_flags,
427                                          colsel=colsel, warnings=False)
428             except _wcs.NoWcsKeywordsFoundError:
429                 est_naxis = 0
430             else:
431                 if naxis is not None:
432                     try:
433                         tmp_wcsprm.sub(naxis)
434                     except ValueError:
435                         pass
436                     est_naxis = tmp_wcsprm.naxis
437                 else:
438                     est_naxis = 2
439 
440             header = fits.Header.fromstring(header_string)
441 
442             if est_naxis == 0:
443                 est_naxis = 2
444             self.naxis = est_naxis
445 
446             det2im = self._read_det2im_kw(header, fobj, err=minerr)
447             cpdis = self._read_distortion_kw(
448                 header, fobj, dist='CPDIS', err=minerr)
449             sip = self._read_sip_kw(header, wcskey=key)
450             self._remove_sip_kw(header)
451 
452             header_string = header.tostring()
453             header_string = header_string.replace('END' + ' ' * 77, '')
454 
455             if isinstance(header_string, str):
456                 header_bytes = header_string.encode('ascii')
457                 header_string = header_string
458             else:
459                 header_bytes = header_string
460                 header_string = header_string.decode('ascii')
461 
462             try:
463                 wcsprm = _wcs.Wcsprm(header=header_bytes, key=key,
464                                      relax=relax, keysel=keysel_flags,
465                                      colsel=colsel)
466             except _wcs.NoWcsKeywordsFoundError:
467                 # The header may have SIP or distortions, but no core
468                 # WCS.  That isn't an error -- we want a "default"
469                 # (identity) core Wcs transformation in that case.
470                 if colsel is None:
471                     wcsprm = _wcs.Wcsprm(header=None, key=key,
472                                          relax=relax, keysel=keysel_flags,
473                                          colsel=colsel)
474                 else:
475                     raise
476 
477             if naxis is not None:
478                 wcsprm = wcsprm.sub(naxis)
479             self.naxis = wcsprm.naxis
480 
481             if (wcsprm.naxis != 2 and
482                 (det2im[0] or det2im[1] or cpdis[0] or cpdis[1] or sip)):
483                 raise ValueError(
484                     """
485 FITS WCS distortion paper lookup tables and SIP distortions only work
486 in 2 dimensions.  However, WCSLIB has detected {0} dimensions in the
487 core WCS keywords.  To use core WCS in conjunction with FITS WCS
488 distortion paper lookup tables or SIP distortion, you must select or
489 reduce these to 2 dimensions using the naxis kwarg.
490 """.format(wcsprm.naxis))
491 
492             header_naxis = header.get('NAXIS', None)
493             if header_naxis is not None and header_naxis < wcsprm.naxis:
494                 warnings.warn(
495                     "The WCS transformation has more axes ({0:d}) than the "
496                     "image it is associated with ({1:d})".format(
497                         wcsprm.naxis, header_naxis), FITSFixedWarning)
498 
499         self._get_naxis(header)
500         WCSBase.__init__(self, sip, cpdis, wcsprm, det2im)
501 
502         if fix:
503             self.fix(translate_units=translate_units)
504 
505         if _do_set:
506             self.wcs.set()
507 
508         for fd in close_fds:
509             fd.close()
510

514                          (self.cpdis1, self.cpdis2),
515                          self.wcs,
516                          (self.det2im1, self.det2im2))
517         new_copy.__dict__.update(self.__dict__)

521         from copy import deepcopy
522 
523         new_copy = self.__class__()
524         new_copy.naxis = deepcopy(self.naxis, memo)

531         for key, val in self.__dict__.items():
532             new_copy.__dict__[key] = deepcopy(val, memo)

565     def _fix_scamp(self):
566         """
567         Remove SCAMP's PVi_m distortion parameters if SIP distortion parameters
568         are also present. Some projects (e.g., Palomar Transient Factory)
569         convert SCAMP's distortion parameters (which abuse the PVi_m cards) to
570         SIP. However, wcslib gets confused by the presence of both SCAMP and
571         SIP distortion parameters.
572 
573         See https://github.com/astropy/astropy/issues/299.
574         """
575         # Nothing to be done if no WCS attached
576         if self.wcs is None:
577             return
578 
579         # Nothing to be done if no PV parameters attached
580         pv = self.wcs.get_pv()
581         if not pv:
582             return
583 
584         # Nothing to be done if axes don't use SIP distortion parameters
585         if self.sip is None:
586             return
587 
588         # Nothing to be done if any radial terms are present...
589         # Loop over list to find any radial terms.
590         # Certain values of the `j' index are used for storing
591         # radial terms; refer to Equation (1) in
592         # <http://web.ipac.caltech.edu/staff/shupe/reprints/SIP_to_PV_SPIE2012.pdf>.
593         pv = np.asarray(pv)
594         # Loop over distinct values of `i' index
595         for i in set(pv[:, 0]):
596             # Get all values of `j' index for this value of `i' index
597             js = set(pv[:, 1][pv[:, 0] == i])
598             # Find max value of `j' index
599             max_j = max(js)
600             for j in (3, 11, 23, 39):
601                 if j < max_j and j in js:
602                     return
603 
604         self.wcs.set_pv([])
605         warnings.warn("Removed redundant SCAMP distortion parameters " +
606             "because SIP parameters are also present", FITSFixedWarning)
607 
608     def fix(self, translate_units='', naxis=None):
609         """
610         Perform the fix operations from wcslib, and warn about any
611         changes it has made.
612 
613         Parameters
614         ----------
615         translate_units : str, optional
616             Specify which potentially unsafe translations of
617             non-standard unit strings to perform.  By default,
618             performs none.
619 
620             Although ``"S"`` is commonly used to represent seconds,
621             its translation to ``"s"`` is potentially unsafe since the
622             standard recognizes ``"S"`` formally as Siemens, however
623             rarely that may be used.  The same applies to ``"H"`` for
624             hours (Henry), and ``"D"`` for days (Debye).
625 
626             This string controls what to do in such cases, and is
627             case-insensitive.
628 
629             - If the string contains ``"s"``, translate ``"S"`` to
630               ``"s"``.
631 
632             - If the string contains ``"h"``, translate ``"H"`` to
633               ``"h"``.
634 
635             - If the string contains ``"d"``, translate ``"D"`` to
636               ``"d"``.
637 
638             Thus ``''`` doesn't do any unsafe translations, whereas
639             ``'shd'`` does all of them.
640 
641         naxis : int array[naxis], optional
642             Image axis lengths.  If this array is set to zero or
643             ``None``, then `~astropy.wcs.Wcsprm.cylfix` will not be
644             invoked.
645         """
646         if self.wcs is not None:
647             self._fix_scamp()
648             fixes = self.wcs.fix(translate_units, naxis)
649             for key, val in fixes.items():
650                 if val != "No change":
651                     warnings.warn(
652                         ("'{0}' made the change '{1}'.").
653                         format(key, val),
654                         FITSFixedWarning)
655 
656     def calc_footprint(self, header=None, undistort=True, axes=None, center=True):
657         """
658         Calculates the footprint of the image on the sky.
659 
660         A footprint is defined as the positions of the corners of the
661         image on the sky after all available distortions have been
662         applied.
663 
664         Parameters
665         ----------
666         header : `~astropy.io.fits.Header` object, optional
667             Used to get ``NAXIS1`` and ``NAXIS2``
668             header and axes are mutually exclusive, alternative ways
669             to provide the same information.
670 
671         undistort : bool, optional
672             If `True`, take SIP and distortion lookup table into
673             account
674 
675         axes : length 2 sequence ints, optional
676             If provided, use the given sequence as the shape of the
677             image.  Otherwise, use the ``NAXIS1`` and ``NAXIS2``
678             keywords from the header that was used to create this
679             `WCS` object.
680 
681         center : bool, optional
682             If `True` use the center of the pixel, otherwise use the corner.
683 
684         Returns
685         -------
686         coord : (4, 2) array of (*x*, *y*) coordinates.
687             The order is clockwise starting with the bottom left corner.
688         """
689         if axes is not None:
690             naxis1, naxis2 = axes
691         else:
692             if header is None:
693                 try:
694                     # classes that inherit from WCS and define naxis1/2
695                     # do not require a header parameter
696                     naxis1 = self._naxis1
697                     naxis2 = self._naxis2
698                 except AttributeError:
699                     warnings.warn("Need a valid header in order to calculate footprint\n", AstropyUserWarning)
700                     return None
701             else:
702                 naxis1 = header.get('NAXIS1', None)
703                 naxis2 = header.get('NAXIS2', None)
704 
705         if naxis1 is None or naxis2 is None:
706             raise ValueError(
707                     "Image size could not be determined.")
708 
709         if center:
710             corners = np.array([[1, 1],
711                                 [1, naxis2],
712                                 [naxis1, naxis2],
713                                 [naxis1, 1]], dtype=np.float64)
714         else:
715             corners = np.array([[0.5, 0.5],
716                                 [0.5, naxis2 + 0.5],
717                                 [naxis1 + 0.5, naxis2 + 0.5],
718                                 [naxis1 + 0.5, 0.5]], dtype=np.float64)
719 
720         if undistort:
721             return self.all_pix2world(corners, 1)
722         else:
723             return self.wcs_pix2world(corners, 1)
724 
725     def _read_det2im_kw(self, header, fobj, err=0.0):
726         """
727         Create a `distortion paper`_ type lookup table for detector to
728         image plane correction.
729         """
730         if fobj is None:
731             return (None, None)
732 
733         if not isinstance(fobj, fits.HDUList):
734             return (None, None)
735 
736         try:
737             axiscorr = header[str('AXISCORR')]
738             d2imdis = self._read_d2im_old_format(header, fobj, axiscorr)
739             return d2imdis
740         except KeyError:
741             pass
742 
743         dist = 'D2IMDIS'
744         d_kw = 'D2IM'
745         err_kw = 'D2IMERR'
746         tables = {}
747         for i in range(1, self.naxis + 1):
748             d_error = header.get(err_kw + str(i), 0.0)
749             if d_error < err:
750                 tables[i] = None
751                 continue
752             distortion = dist + str(i)
753             if distortion in header:
754                 dis = header[distortion].lower()
755                 if dis == 'lookup':
756                     del header[distortion]
757                     assert isinstance(fobj, fits.HDUList), ('An astropy.io.fits.HDUList'
758                                 'is required for Lookup table distortion.')
759                     dp = (d_kw + str(i)).strip()
760                     dp_extver_key = dp + str('.EXTVER')
761                     if dp_extver_key in header:
762                         d_extver = header[dp_extver_key]
763                         del header[dp_extver_key]
764                     else:
765                         d_extver = 1
766                     dp_axis_key = dp + str('.AXIS.{0:d}').format(i)
767                     if i == header[dp_axis_key]:
768                         d_data = fobj[str('D2IMARR'), d_extver].data
769                     else:
770                         d_data = (fobj[str('D2IMARR'), d_extver].data).transpose()
771                     del header[dp_axis_key]
772                     d_header = fobj[str('D2IMARR'), d_extver].header
773                     d_crpix = (d_header.get(str('CRPIX1'), 0.0), d_header.get(str('CRPIX2'), 0.0))
774                     d_crval = (d_header.get(str('CRVAL1'), 0.0), d_header.get(str('CRVAL2'), 0.0))
775                     d_cdelt = (d_header.get(str('CDELT1'), 1.0), d_header.get(str('CDELT2'), 1.0))
776                     d_lookup = DistortionLookupTable(d_data, d_crpix,
777                                                      d_crval, d_cdelt)
778                     tables[i] = d_lookup
779                 else:
780                     warnings.warn('Polynomial distortion is not implemented.\n', AstropyUserWarning)
781                 for key in list(header):
782                     if key.startswith(dp + str('.')):
783                         del header[key]
784             else:
785                 tables[i] = None
786         if not tables:
787             return (None, None)
788         else:
789             return (tables.get(1), tables.get(2))
790 
791     def _read_d2im_old_format(self, header, fobj, axiscorr):
792         warnings.warn("The use of ``AXISCORR`` for D2IM correction has been deprecated."
793                       "`~astropy.wcs` will read in files with ``AXISCORR`` but ``to_fits()`` will write "
794                       "out files without it.",
795                       AstropyDeprecationWarning)
796         cpdis = [None, None]
797         crpix = [0., 0.]
798         crval = [0., 0.]
799         cdelt = [1., 1.]
800         try:
801             d2im_data = fobj[(str('D2IMARR'), 1)].data
802         except KeyError:
803             return (None, None)
804         except AttributeError:
805             return (None, None)
806 
807         d2im_data = np.array([d2im_data])
808         d2im_hdr = fobj[(str('D2IMARR'), 1)].header
809         naxis = d2im_hdr[str('NAXIS')]
810 
811         for i in range(1, naxis + 1):
812             crpix[i - 1] = d2im_hdr.get(str('CRPIX') + str(i), 0.0)
813             crval[i - 1] = d2im_hdr.get(str('CRVAL') + str(i), 0.0)
814             cdelt[i - 1] = d2im_hdr.get(str('CDELT') + str(i), 1.0)
815 
816         cpdis = DistortionLookupTable(d2im_data, crpix, crval, cdelt)
817 
818         if axiscorr == 1:
819             return (cpdis, None)
820         elif axiscorr == 2:
821             return (None, cpdis)
822         else:
823             warnings.warn("Expected AXISCORR to be 1 or 2", AstropyUserWarning)
824             return (None, None)
825 
826     def _write_det2im(self, hdulist):
827         """
828         Writes a `distortion paper`_ type lookup table to the given
829         `astropy.io.fits.HDUList`.
830         """
831 
832         if self.det2im1 is None and self.det2im2 is None:
833             return
834         dist = 'D2IMDIS'
835         d_kw = 'D2IM'
836         err_kw = 'D2IMERR'
837 
838         def write_d2i(num, det2im):
839             if det2im is None:
840                 return
841             str('{0}{1:d}').format(dist, num),
842             hdulist[0].header[str('{0}{1:d}').format(dist, num)] = (
843                 'LOOKUP', 'Detector to image correction type')
844             hdulist[0].header[str('{0}{1:d}.EXTVER').format(d_kw, num)] = (
845                 num, 'Version number of WCSDVARR extension')
846             hdulist[0].header[str('{0}{1:d}.NAXES').format(d_kw, num)] = (
847                 len(det2im.data.shape), 'Number of independent variables in d2im function')
848             for i in range(det2im.data.ndim):
849                 hdulist[0].header[str('{0}{1:d}.AXIS.{2:d}').format(d_kw, num, i + 1)] = (
850                     i + 1, 'Axis number of the jth independent variable in a d2im function')
851 
852             image = fits.ImageHDU(det2im.data, name=str('D2IMARR'))
853             header = image.header
854 
855             header[str('CRPIX1')] = (det2im.crpix[0],
856                                      'Coordinate system reference pixel')
857             header[str('CRPIX2')] = (det2im.crpix[1],
858                                      'Coordinate system reference pixel')
859             header[str('CRVAL1')] = (det2im.crval[0],
860                                      'Coordinate system value at reference pixel')
861             header[str('CRVAL2')] = (det2im.crval[1],
862                                      'Coordinate system value at reference pixel')
863             header[str('CDELT1')] = (det2im.cdelt[0],
864                                      'Coordinate increment along axis')
865             header[str('CDELT2')] = (det2im.cdelt[1],
866                                      'Coordinate increment along axis')
867             image.ver = int(hdulist[0].header[str('{0}{1:d}.EXTVER').format(d_kw, num)])
868             hdulist.append(image)
869         write_d2i(1, self.det2im1)
870         write_d2i(2, self.det2im2)
871 
872     def _read_distortion_kw(self, header, fobj, dist='CPDIS', err=0.0):
873         """
874         Reads `distortion paper`_ table-lookup keywords and data, and
875         returns a 2-tuple of `~astropy.wcs.DistortionLookupTable`
876         objects.
877 
878         If no `distortion paper`_ keywords are found, ``(None, None)``
879         is returned.
880         """
881         if isinstance(header, (str, bytes)):
882             return (None, None)
883 
884         if dist == 'CPDIS':
885             d_kw = str('DP')
886             err_kw = str('CPERR')
887         else:
888             d_kw = str('DQ')
889             err_kw = str('CQERR')
890 
891         tables = {}
892         for i in range(1, self.naxis + 1):
893             d_error_key = err_kw + str(i)
894             if d_error_key in header:
895                 d_error = header[d_error_key]
896                 del header[d_error_key]
897             else:
898                 d_error = 0.0
899             if d_error < err:
900                 tables[i] = None
901                 continue
902             distortion = dist + str(i)
903             if distortion in header:
904                 dis = header[distortion].lower()
905                 del header[distortion]
906                 if dis == 'lookup':
907                     if not isinstance(fobj, fits.HDUList):
908                         raise ValueError('an astropy.io.fits.HDUList is '
909                                 'required for Lookup table distortion.')
910                     dp = (d_kw + str(i)).strip()
911                     dp_extver_key = dp + str('.EXTVER')
912                     if dp_extver_key in header:
913                         d_extver = header[dp_extver_key]
914                         del header[dp_extver_key]
915                     else:
916                         d_extver = 1
917                     dp_axis_key = dp + str('.AXIS.{0:d}'.format(i))
918                     if i == header[dp_axis_key]:
919                         d_data = fobj[str('WCSDVARR'), d_extver].data
920                     else:
921                         d_data = (fobj[str('WCSDVARR'), d_extver].data).transpose()
922                     del header[dp_axis_key]
923                     d_header = fobj[str('WCSDVARR'), d_extver].header
924                     d_crpix = (d_header.get(str('CRPIX1'), 0.0),
925                                d_header.get(str('CRPIX2'), 0.0))
926                     d_crval = (d_header.get(str('CRVAL1'), 0.0),
927                                d_header.get(str('CRVAL2'), 0.0))
928                     d_cdelt = (d_header.get(str('CDELT1'), 1.0),
929                                d_header.get(str('CDELT2'), 1.0))
930                     d_lookup = DistortionLookupTable(d_data, d_crpix, d_crval, d_cdelt)
931                     tables[i] = d_lookup
932 
933                     for key in list(header):
934                         if key.startswith(dp + str('.')):
935                             del header[key]
936                 else:
937                     warnings.warn('Polynomial distortion is not implemented.\n', AstropyUserWarning)
938             else:
939                 tables[i] = None
940 
941         if not tables:
942             return (None, None)
943         else:
944             return (tables.get(1), tables.get(2))

1002     def _read_sip_kw(self, header, wcskey=""):
1003         """
1004         Reads `SIP`_ header keywords and returns a `~astropy.wcs.Sip`
1005         object.
1006 
1007         If no `SIP`_ header keywords are found, ``None`` is returned.
1008         """
1009         if isinstance(header, (str, bytes)):
1010             # TODO: Parse SIP from a string without pyfits around
1011             return None
1012 
1013         if str("A_ORDER") in header and header[str('A_ORDER')] > 1:
1014             if str("B_ORDER") not in header:
1015                 raise ValueError(
1016                     "A_ORDER provided without corresponding B_ORDER "
1017                     "keyword for SIP distortion")
1018 
1019             m = int(header[str("A_ORDER")])
1020             a = np.zeros((m + 1, m + 1), np.double)
1021             for i in range(m + 1):
1022                 for j in range(m - i + 1):
1023                     key = str("A_{0}_{1}").format(i, j)
1024                     if key in header:
1025                         a[i, j] = header[key]
1026                         del header[key]
1027 
1028             m = int(header[str("B_ORDER")])
1029             if m > 1:
1030                 b = np.zeros((m + 1, m + 1), np.double)
1031                 for i in range(m + 1):
1032                     for j in range(m - i + 1):
1033                         key = str("B_{0}_{1}").format(i, j)
1034                         if key in header:
1035                             b[i, j] = header[key]
1036                             del header[key]
1037             else:
1038                 a = None
1039                 b = None
1040 
1041             del header[str('A_ORDER')]
1042             del header[str('B_ORDER')]
1043 
1044             ctype = [header['CTYPE{0}{1}'.format(nax, wcskey)] for nax in range(1, self.naxis + 1)]
1045             if any(not ctyp.endswith('-SIP') for ctyp in ctype):
1046                 message = """
1047                 Inconsistent SIP distortion information is present in the FITS header and the WCS object:
1048                 SIP coefficients were detected, but CTYPE is missing a "-SIP" suffix.
1049                 astropy.wcs is using the SIP distortion coefficients,
1050                 therefore the coordinates calculated here might be incorrect.
1051 
1052                 If you do not want to apply the SIP distortion coefficients,
1053                 please remove the SIP coefficients from the FITS header or the
1054                 WCS object.  As an example, if the image is already distortion-corrected
1055                 (e.g., drizzled) then distortion components should not apply and the SIP
1056                 coefficients should be removed.
1057 
1058                 While the SIP distortion coefficients are being applied here, if that was indeed the intent,
1059                 for consistency please append "-SIP" to the CTYPE in the FITS header or the WCS object.
1060 
1061                 """
1062                 log.info(message)
1063         elif str("B_ORDER") in header and header[str('B_ORDER')] > 1:
1064             raise ValueError(
1065                 "B_ORDER provided without corresponding A_ORDER " +
1066                 "keyword for SIP distortion")
1067         else:
1068             a = None
1069             b = None
1070 
1071         if str("AP_ORDER") in header and header[str('AP_ORDER')] > 1:
1072             if str("BP_ORDER") not in header:
1073                 raise ValueError(
1074                     "AP_ORDER provided without corresponding BP_ORDER "
1075                     "keyword for SIP distortion")
1076 
1077             m = int(header[str("AP_ORDER")])
1078             ap = np.zeros((m + 1, m + 1), np.double)
1079             for i in range(m + 1):
1080                 for j in range(m - i + 1):
1081                     key = str("AP_{0}_{1}").format(i, j)
1082                     if key in header:
1083                         ap[i, j] = header[key]
1084                         del header[key]
1085 
1086             m = int(header[str("BP_ORDER")])
1087             if m > 1:
1088                 bp = np.zeros((m + 1, m + 1), np.double)
1089                 for i in range(m + 1):
1090                     for j in range(m - i + 1):
1091                         key = str("BP_{0}_{1}").format(i, j)
1092                         if key in header:
1093                             bp[i, j] = header[key]
1094                             del header[key]
1095             else:
1096                 ap = None
1097                 bp = None
1098 
1099             del header[str('AP_ORDER')]
1100             del header[str('BP_ORDER')]
1101         elif str("BP_ORDER") in header and header[str('BP_ORDER')] > 1:
1102             raise ValueError(
1103                 "BP_ORDER provided without corresponding AP_ORDER "
1104                 "keyword for SIP distortion")
1105         else:
1106             ap = None
1107             bp = None
1108 
1109         if a is None and b is None and ap is None and bp is None:
1110             return None
1111 
1112         if str("CRPIX1{0}".format(wcskey)) not in header or str("CRPIX2{0}".format(wcskey)) not in header:
1113             raise ValueError(
1114                 "Header has SIP keywords without CRPIX keywords")
1115 
1116         crpix1 = header.get("CRPIX1{0}".format(wcskey))
1117         crpix2 = header.get("CRPIX2{0}".format(wcskey))
1118 
1119         return Sip(a, b, ap, bp, (crpix1, crpix2))
