63     def __getitem__(self, key):
64         if isinstance(key, str):
65             indx = _get_index(self.array.names, key)
66 
67             if indx < self.start or indx > self.end - 1:
68                 raise KeyError("Key '{}' does not exist.".format(key))

146     FITS record array class.

148     `FITS_rec` is the data part of a table HDU's data part.  This is a layer
149     over the `~numpy.recarray`, so we can deal with scaled columns.

151     It inherits all of the standard methods from `numpy.ndarray`.

157     def __new__(subtype, input):
158         """
159         Construct a FITS record array from a recarray.
160         """
161 
162         # input should be a record array
163         if input.dtype.subdtype is None:
164             self = np.recarray.__new__(subtype, input.shape, input.dtype,
165                                        buf=input.data)
166         else:
167             self = np.recarray.__new__(subtype, input.shape, input.dtype,
168                                        buf=input.data, strides=input.strides)
169 
170         self._init()
171         if self.dtype.fields:
172             self._nfields = len(self.dtype.fields)
173 
174         return self

176     def __setstate__(self, state):
177         meta = state[-1]
178         column_state = state[-2]
179         state = state[:-2]
180 
181         super().__setstate__(state)
182 
183         self._col_weakrefs = weakref.WeakSet()
184 
185         for attr, value in zip(meta, column_state):
186             setattr(self, attr, value)

188     def __reduce__(self):
189         """
190         Return a 3-tuple for pickling a FITS_rec. Use the super-class
191         functionality but then add in a tuple of FITS_rec-specific
192         values that get used in __setstate__.
193         """
194 
195         reconst_func, reconst_func_args, state = super().__reduce__()
196 
197         # Define FITS_rec-specific attrs that get added to state
198         column_state = []
199         meta = []
200 
201         for attrs in ['_converted', '_heapoffset', '_heapsize', '_nfields',
202                       '_gap', '_uint', 'parnames', '_coldefs']:
203 
204             with suppress(AttributeError):
205                 # _coldefs can be Delayed, and file objects cannot be
206                 # picked, it needs to be deepcopied first
207                 if attrs == '_coldefs':
208                     column_state.append(self._coldefs.__deepcopy__(None))
209                 else:
210                     column_state.append(getattr(self, attrs))

214

233         elif self.dtype.fields is not None:

235             # just other FITS_rec objects

244             self._col_weakrefs = weakref.WeakSet()

247             # Work around chicken-egg problem.  Column.array relies on the
248             # _coldefs attribute to set up ref back to parent FITS_rec; however
249             # in the above line the self._coldefs has not been assigned yet so

257     def _init(self):
258         """Initializes internal attributes specific to FITS-isms."""

261         self._converted = {}
262         self._heapoffset = 0
263         self._heapsize = 0
264         self._col_weakrefs = weakref.WeakSet()
265         self._coldefs = None

269     @classmethod
270     def from_columns(cls, columns, nrows=0, fill=False, character_as_bytes=False):
271         """
272         Given a `ColDefs` object of unknown origin, initialize a new `FITS_rec`
273         object.
274 
275         .. note::
276 
277             This was originally part of the ``new_table`` function in the table
278             module but was moved into a class method since most of its
279             functionality always had more to do with initializing a `FITS_rec`
280             object than anything else, and much of it also overlapped with
281             ``FITS_rec._scale_back``.
282 
283         Parameters
284         ----------
285         columns : sequence of `Column` or a `ColDefs`
286             The columns from which to create the table data.  If these
287             columns have data arrays attached that data may be used in
288             initializing the new table.  Otherwise the input columns
289             will be used as a template for a new table with the requested
290             number of rows.
291 
292         nrows : int
293             Number of rows in the new table.  If the input columns have data
294             associated with them, the size of the largest input column is used.
295             Otherwise the default is 0.
296 
297         fill : bool
298             If `True`, will fill all cells with zeros or blanks.  If
299             `False`, copy the data from input, undefined cells will still
300             be filled with zeros/blanks.
301         """
302 
303         if not isinstance(columns, ColDefs):
304             columns = ColDefs(columns)
305 
306         # read the delayed data
307         for column in columns:
308             arr = column.array
309             if isinstance(arr, Delayed):
310                 if arr.hdu.data is None:
311                     column.array = None
312                 else:
313                     column.array = _get_recarray_field(arr.hdu.data,
314                                                        arr.field)
315         # Reset columns._arrays (which we may want to just do away with
316         # altogether
317         del columns._arrays
318 
319         # use the largest column shape as the shape of the record
320         if nrows == 0:
321             for arr in columns._arrays:
322                 if arr is not None:
323                     dim = arr.shape[0]
324                 else:
325                     dim = 0
326                 if dim > nrows:
327                     nrows = dim
328 
329         raw_data = np.empty(columns.dtype.itemsize * nrows, dtype=np.uint8)
330         raw_data.fill(ord(columns._padding_byte))
331         data = np.recarray(nrows, dtype=columns.dtype, buf=raw_data).view(cls)
332         data._character_as_bytes = character_as_bytes
333 
334         # Make sure the data is a listener for changes to the columns
335         columns._add_listener(data)
336 
337         # Previously this assignment was made from hdu.columns, but that's a
338         # bug since if a _TableBaseHDU has a FITS_rec in its .data attribute
339         # the _TableBaseHDU.columns property is actually returned from
340         # .data._coldefs, so this assignment was circular!  Don't make that
341         # mistake again.
342         # All of this is an artifact of the fragility of the FITS_rec class,
343         # and that it can't just be initialized by columns...
344         data._coldefs = columns
345 
346         # If fill is True we don't copy anything from the column arrays.  We're
347         # just using them as a template, and returning a table filled with
348         # zeros/blanks
349         if fill:
350             return data
351 
352         # Otherwise we have to fill the recarray with data from the input
353         # columns
354         for idx, column in enumerate(columns):
355             # For each column in the ColDef object, determine the number of
356             # rows in that column.  This will be either the number of rows in
357             # the ndarray associated with the column, or the number of rows
358             # given in the call to this function, which ever is smaller.  If
359             # the input FILL argument is true, the number of rows is set to
360             # zero so that no data is copied from the original input data.
361             arr = column.array
362 
363             if arr is None:
364                 array_size = 0
365             else:
366                 array_size = len(arr)
367 
368             n = min(array_size, nrows)
369 
370             # TODO: At least *some* of this logic is mostly redundant with the
371             # _convert_foo methods in this class; see if we can eliminate some
372             # of that duplication.
373 
374             if not n:
375                 # The input column had an empty array, so just use the fill
376                 # value
377                 continue
378 
379             field = _get_recarray_field(data, idx)
380             name = column.name
381             fitsformat = column.format
382             recformat = fitsformat.recformat
383 
384             outarr = field[:n]
385             inarr = arr[:n]
386 
387             if isinstance(recformat, _FormatX):
388                 # Data is a bit array
389                 if inarr.shape[-1] == recformat.repeat:
390                     _wrapx(inarr, outarr, recformat.repeat)
391                     continue
392             elif isinstance(recformat, _FormatP):
393                 data._cache_field(name, _makep(inarr, field, recformat,
394                                                nrows=nrows))
395                 continue
396             # TODO: Find a better way of determining that the column is meant
397             # to be FITS L formatted
398             elif recformat[-2:] == FITS2NUMPY['L'] and inarr.dtype == bool:
399                 # column is boolean
400                 # The raw data field should be filled with either 'T' or 'F'
401                 # (not 0).  Use 'F' as a default
402                 field[:] = ord('F')
403                 # Also save the original boolean array in data._converted so
404                 # that it doesn't have to be re-converted
405                 converted = np.zeros(field.shape, dtype=bool)
406                 converted[:n] = inarr
407                 data._cache_field(name, converted)
408                 # TODO: Maybe this step isn't necessary at all if _scale_back
409                 # will handle it?
410                 inarr = np.where(inarr == np.False_, ord('F'), ord('T'))
411             elif (columns[idx]._physical_values and
412                     columns[idx]._pseudo_unsigned_ints):
413                 # Temporary hack...
414                 bzero = column.bzero
415                 converted = np.zeros(field.shape, dtype=inarr.dtype)
416                 converted[:n] = inarr
417                 data._cache_field(name, converted)
418                 if n < nrows:
419                     # Pre-scale rows below the input data
420                     field[n:] = -bzero
421 
422                 inarr = inarr - bzero
423             elif isinstance(columns, _AsciiColDefs):
424                 # Regardless whether the format is character or numeric, if the
425                 # input array contains characters then it's already in the raw
426                 # format for ASCII tables
427                 if fitsformat._pseudo_logical:
428                     # Hack to support converting from 8-bit T/F characters
429                     # Normally the column array is a chararray of 1 character
430                     # strings, but we need to view it as a normal ndarray of
431                     # 8-bit ints to fill it with ASCII codes for 'T' and 'F'
432                     outarr = field.view(np.uint8, np.ndarray)[:n]
433                 elif arr.dtype.kind not in ('S', 'U'):
434                     # Set up views of numeric columns with the appropriate
435                     # numeric dtype
436                     # Fill with the appropriate blanks for the column format
437                     data._cache_field(name, np.zeros(nrows, dtype=arr.dtype))
438                     outarr = data._converted[name][:n]
439 
440                 outarr[:] = inarr
441                 continue
442 
443             if inarr.shape != outarr.shape:
444                 if (inarr.dtype.kind == outarr.dtype.kind and
445                         inarr.dtype.kind in ('U', 'S') and
446                         inarr.dtype != outarr.dtype):
447 
448                     inarr_rowsize = inarr[0].size
449                     inarr = inarr.flatten().view(outarr.dtype)
450 
451                 # This is a special case to handle input arrays with
452                 # non-trivial TDIMn.
453                 # By design each row of the outarray is 1-D, while each row of
454                 # the input array may be n-D
455                 if outarr.ndim > 1:
456                     # The normal case where the first dimension is the rows
457                     inarr_rowsize = inarr[0].size
458                     inarr = inarr.reshape(n, inarr_rowsize)
459                     outarr[:, :inarr_rowsize] = inarr
460                 else:
461                     # Special case for strings where the out array only has one
462                     # dimension (the second dimension is rolled up into the
463                     # strings
464                     outarr[:n] = inarr.ravel()
465             else:
466                 outarr[:] = inarr
467 
468         # Now replace the original column array references with the new
469         # fields
470         # This is required to prevent the issue reported in
471         # https://github.com/spacetelescope/PyFITS/issues/99
472         for idx in range(len(columns)):
473             columns._arrays[idx] = data.field(idx)
474 
475         return data
476 
477     def __repr__(self):
478         # Force use of the normal ndarray repr (rather than the new
479         # one added for recarray in Numpy 1.10) for backwards compat
480         return np.ndarray.__repr__(self)

482     def __getitem__(self, key):
483         if self._coldefs is None:
484             return super().__getitem__(key)
485 
486         if isinstance(key, str):
487             return self.field(key)
488 
489         # Have to view as a recarray then back as a FITS_rec, otherwise the
490         # circular reference fix/hack in FITS_rec.field() won't preserve
491         # the slice.
492         out = self.view(np.recarray)[key]
493         if type(out) is not np.recarray:
494             # Oops, we got a single element rather than a view. In that case,
495             # return a Record, which has no __getstate__ and is more efficient.
496             return self._record_type(self, key)
497 
498         # We got a view; change it back to our class, and add stuff
499         out = out.view(type(self))
500         out._coldefs = ColDefs(self._coldefs)
501         arrays = []
502         out._converted = {}
503         for idx, name in enumerate(self._coldefs.names):
504             #
505             # Store the new arrays for the _coldefs object
506             #
507             arrays.append(self._coldefs._arrays[idx][key])
508 
509             # Ensure that the sliced FITS_rec will view the same scaled
510             # columns as the original; this is one of the few cases where
511             # it is not necessary to use _cache_field()
512             if name in self._converted:
513                 dummy = self._converted[name]
514                 field = np.ndarray.__getitem__(dummy, key)
515                 out._converted[name] = field
516 
517         out._coldefs._arrays = arrays
518         return out
519 
520     def __setitem__(self, key, value):
521         if self._coldefs is None:
522             return super().__setitem__(key, value)
523 
524         if isinstance(key, str):
525             self[key][:] = value
526             return
527 
528         if isinstance(key, slice):
529             end = min(len(self), key.stop or len(self))
530             end = max(0, end)
531             start = max(0, key.start or 0)
532             end = min(end, start + len(value))
533 
534             for idx in range(start, end):
535                 self.__setitem__(idx, value[idx - start])
536             return
537 
538         if isinstance(value, FITS_record):
539             for idx in range(self._nfields):
540                 self.field(self.names[idx])[key] = value.field(self.names[idx])
541         elif isinstance(value, (tuple, list, np.void)):
542             if self._nfields == len(value):
543                 for idx in range(self._nfields):
544                     self.field(idx)[key] = value[idx]
545             else:
546                 raise ValueError('Input tuple or list required to have {} '
547                                  'elements.'.format(self._nfields))
548         else:
549             raise TypeError('Assignment requires a FITS_record, tuple, or '
550                             'list as input.')

552     def copy(self, order='C'):
553         """
554         The Numpy documentation lies; `numpy.ndarray.copy` is not equivalent to
555         `numpy.copy`.  Differences include that it re-views the copied array as
556         self's ndarray subclass, as though it were taking a slice; this means
557         ``__array_finalize__`` is called and the copy shares all the array
558         attributes (including ``._converted``!).  So we need to make a deep
559         copy of all those attributes so that the two arrays truly do not share
560         any data.
561         """
562 
563         new = super().copy(order=order)
564 
565         new.__dict__ = copy.deepcopy(self.__dict__)
566         return new

578     @property
579     def _coldefs(self):
580         # This used to be a normal internal attribute, but it was changed to a
581         # property as a quick and transparent way to work around the reference
582         # leak bug fixed in https://github.com/astropy/astropy/pull/4539
583         #
584         # See the long comment in the Column.array property for more details
585         # on this.  But in short, FITS_rec now has a ._col_weakrefs attribute
586         # which is a WeakSet of weakrefs to each Column in _coldefs.
587         #
588         # So whenever ._coldefs is set we also add each Column in the ColDefs
589         # to the weakrefs set.  This is an easy way to find out if a Column has
590         # any references to it external to the FITS_rec (i.e. a user assigned a
591         # column to a variable).  If the column is still in _col_weakrefs then
592         # there are other references to it external to this FITS_rec.  We use
593         # that information in __del__ to save off copies of the array data
594         # for those columns to their Column.array property before our memory
595         # is freed.
596         return self.__dict__.get('_coldefs')

645     @property
646     def _raw_itemsize(self):
647         """
648         Returns the size of row items that would be written to the raw FITS
649         file, taking into account the possibility of unicode columns being
650         compactified.

652         Currently for internal use only.

667     def field(self, key):
668         """
669         A view of a `Column`'s data as an array.
670         """
671 
672         # NOTE: The *column* index may not be the same as the field index in
673         # the recarray, if the column is a phantom column
674         column = self.columns[key]
675         name = column.name
676         format = column.format
677 
678         if format.dtype.itemsize == 0:
679             warnings.warn(
680                 'Field {!r} has a repeat count of 0 in its format code, '
681                 'indicating an empty field.'.format(key))
682             return np.array([], dtype=format.dtype)
683 
684         # If field's base is a FITS_rec, we can run into trouble because it
685         # contains a reference to the ._coldefs object of the original data;
686         # this can lead to a circular reference; see ticket #49
687         base = self
688         while (isinstance(base, FITS_rec) and
689                 isinstance(base.base, np.recarray)):
690             base = base.base
691         # base could still be a FITS_rec in some cases, so take care to
692         # use rec.recarray.field to avoid a potential infinite
693         # recursion
694         field = _get_recarray_field(base, name)
695 
696         if name not in self._converted:
697             recformat = format.recformat
698             # TODO: If we're now passing the column to these subroutines, do we
699             # really need to pass them the recformat?
700             if isinstance(recformat, _FormatP):
701                 # for P format
702                 converted = self._convert_p(column, field, recformat)
703             else:
704                 # Handle all other column data types which are fixed-width
705                 # fields
706                 converted = self._convert_other(column, field, recformat)
707 
708             # Note: Never assign values directly into the self._converted dict;
709             # always go through self._cache_field; this way self._converted is
710             # only used to store arrays that are not already direct views of
711             # our own data.
712             self._cache_field(name, converted)
713             return converted
714 
715         return self._converted[name]
716 
717     def _cache_field(self, name, field):
718         """
719         Do not store fields in _converted if one of its bases is self,
720         or if it has a common base with self.
721 
722         This results in a reference cycle that cannot be broken since
723         ndarrays do not participate in cyclic garbage collection.
724         """
725 
726         base = field
727         while True:
728             self_base = self
729             while True:
730                 if self_base is base:
731                     return
732 
733                 if getattr(self_base, 'base', None) is not None:
734                     self_base = self_base.base
735                 else:
736                     break
737 
738             if getattr(base, 'base', None) is not None:
739                 base = base.base
740             else:
741                 break
742 
743         self._converted[name] = field
744

768     def _convert_x(self, field, recformat):

770         FITS X format.

772 
773         dummy = np.zeros(self.shape + (recformat.repeat,), dtype=np.bool_)

777     def _convert_p(self, column, field, recformat):
778         """Convert a raw table column of FITS P or Q format descriptors
779         to a VLA column with the array data returned from the heap.
780         """
781 
782         dummy = _VLF([None] * len(self), dtype=recformat.dtype)
783         raw_data = self._get_raw_data()
784 
785         if raw_data is None:
786             raise OSError(
787                 "Could not find heap data for the {!r} variable-length "
788                 "array column.".format(column.name))
789 
790         for idx in range(len(self)):
791             offset = field[idx, 1] + self._heapoffset
792             count = field[idx, 0]
793 
794             if recformat.dtype == 'a':
795                 dt = np.dtype(recformat.dtype + str(1))
796                 arr_len = count * dt.itemsize
797                 da = raw_data[offset:offset + arr_len].view(dt)
798                 da = np.char.array(da.view(dtype=dt), itemsize=count)
799                 dummy[idx] = decode_ascii(da)
800             else:
801                 dt = np.dtype(recformat.dtype)
802                 arr_len = count * dt.itemsize
803                 dummy[idx] = raw_data[offset:offset + arr_len].view(dt)
804                 dummy[idx].dtype = dummy[idx].dtype.newbyteorder('>')
805                 # Each array in the field may now require additional
806                 # scaling depending on the other scaling parameters
807                 # TODO: The same scaling parameters apply to every
808                 # array in the column so this is currently very slow; we
809                 # really only need to check once whether any scaling will
810                 # be necessary and skip this step if not
811                 # TODO: Test that this works for X format; I don't think
812                 # that it does--the recformat variable only applies to the P
813                 # format not the X format
814                 dummy[idx] = self._convert_other(column, dummy[idx],
815                                                  recformat)
816 
817         return dummy
818 
819     def _convert_ascii(self, column, field):
820         """
821         Special handling for ASCII table columns to convert columns containing
822         numeric types to actual numeric arrays from the string representation.
823         """
824 
825         format = column.format
826         recformat = ASCII2NUMPY[format[0]]
827         # if the string = TNULL, return ASCIITNULL
828         nullval = str(column.null).strip().encode('ascii')
829         if len(nullval) > format.width:
830             nullval = nullval[:format.width]
831 
832         # Before using .replace make sure that any trailing bytes in each
833         # column are filled with spaces, and *not*, say, nulls; this causes
834         # functions like replace to potentially leave gibberish bytes in the
835         # array buffer.
836         dummy = np.char.ljust(field, format.width)
837         dummy = np.char.replace(dummy, encode_ascii('D'), encode_ascii('E'))
838         null_fill = encode_ascii(str(ASCIITNULL).rjust(format.width))
839 
840         # Convert all fields equal to the TNULL value (nullval) to empty fields.
841         # TODO: These fields really should be conerted to NaN or something else undefined.
842         # Currently they are converted to empty fields, which are then set to zero.
843         dummy = np.where(np.char.strip(dummy) == nullval, null_fill, dummy)
844 
845         # always replace empty fields, see https://github.com/astropy/astropy/pull/5394
846         if nullval != b'':
847             dummy = np.where(np.char.strip(dummy) == b'', null_fill, dummy)
848 
849         try:
850             dummy = np.array(dummy, dtype=recformat)
851         except ValueError as exc:
852             indx = self.names.index(column.name)
853             raise ValueError(
854                 '{}; the header may be missing the necessary TNULL{} '
855                 'keyword or the table contains invalid data'.format(
856                     exc, indx + 1))
857 
858         return dummy
859 
860     def _convert_other(self, column, field, recformat):
861         """Perform conversions on any other fixed-width column data types.
862 
863         This may not perform any conversion at all if it's not necessary, in
864         which case the original column array is returned.
865         """
866 
867         if isinstance(recformat, _FormatX):
868             # special handling for the X format
869             return self._convert_x(field, recformat)
870 
871         (_str, _bool, _number, _scale, _zero, bscale, bzero, dim) = \
872             self._get_scale_factors(column)
873 
874         indx = self.names.index(column.name)
875 
876         # ASCII table, convert strings to numbers
877         # TODO:
878         # For now, check that these are ASCII columns by checking the coldefs
879         # type; in the future all columns (for binary tables, ASCII tables, or
880         # otherwise) should "know" what type they are already and how to handle
881         # converting their data from FITS format to native format and vice
882         # versa...
883         if not _str and isinstance(self._coldefs, _AsciiColDefs):
884             field = self._convert_ascii(column, field)
885 
886         # Test that the dimensions given in dim are sensible; otherwise
887         # display a warning and ignore them
888         if dim:
889             # See if the dimensions already match, if not, make sure the
890             # number items will fit in the specified dimensions
891             if field.ndim > 1:
892                 actual_shape = field.shape[1:]
893                 if _str:
894                     actual_shape = actual_shape + (field.itemsize,)
895             else:
896                 actual_shape = field.shape[0]
897 
898             if dim == actual_shape:
899                 # The array already has the correct dimensions, so we
900                 # ignore dim and don't convert
901                 dim = None
902             else:
903                 nitems = reduce(operator.mul, dim)
904                 if _str:
905                     actual_nitems = field.itemsize
906                 elif len(field.shape) == 1:  # No repeat count in TFORMn, equivalent to 1
907                     actual_nitems = 1
908                 else:
909                     actual_nitems = field.shape[1]
910                 if nitems > actual_nitems:
911                     warnings.warn(
912                         'TDIM{} value {:d} does not fit with the size of '
913                         'the array items ({:d}).  TDIM{:d} will be ignored.'

        # Replace exponent separator in floating point numbers

<issue>
Using __isnull=True on a KeyTransform should not match JSON null on SQLite and Oracle
Description
	
The KeyTransformIsNull lookup borrows the logic from HasKey for isnull=False, which is correct. If isnull=True, the query should only match objects that do not have the key. The query is correct for MariaDB, MySQL, and PostgreSQL. However, on SQLite and Oracle, the query also matches objects that have the key with the value null, which is incorrect.
To confirm, edit tests.model_fields.test_jsonfield.TestQuerying.test_isnull_key. For the first assertion, change
		self.assertSequenceEqual(
			NullableJSONModel.objects.filter(value__a__isnull=True),
			self.objs[:3] + self.objs[5:],
		)
to
		self.assertSequenceEqual(
			NullableJSONModel.objects.filter(value__j__isnull=True),
			self.objs[:4] + self.objs[5:],
		)
The test previously only checks with value__a which could not catch this behavior because the value is not JSON null.

271 class KeyTransform(Transform):
272     postgres_operator = '->'
273     postgres_nested_operator = '#>'
274 
275     def __init__(self, key_name, *args, **kwargs):
276         super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
277         self.key_name = str(key_name)
278 
279     def preprocess_lhs(self, compiler, connection):
280         key_transforms = [self.key_name]
281         previous = self.lhs
282         while isinstance(previous, KeyTransform):
283             key_transforms.insert(0, previous.key_name)
284             previous = previous.lhs
285         lhs, params = compiler.compile(previous)
286         if connection.vendor == 'oracle':
287             # Escape string-formatting.
288             key_transforms = [key.replace('%', '%%') for key in key_transforms]
289         return lhs, params, key_transforms
290 
291     def as_mysql(self, compiler, connection):
292         lhs, params, key_transforms = self.preprocess_lhs(compiler, connection)
293         json_path = compile_json_path(key_transforms)
294         return 'JSON_EXTRACT(%s, %%s)' % lhs, tuple(params) + (json_path,)
295 
296     def as_oracle(self, compiler, connection):
297         lhs, params, key_transforms = self.preprocess_lhs(compiler, connection)
298         json_path = compile_json_path(key_transforms)
299         return (
300             "COALESCE(JSON_QUERY(%s, '%s'), JSON_VALUE(%s, '%s'))" %
301             ((lhs, json_path) * 2)
302         ), tuple(params) * 2
303 
304     def as_postgresql(self, compiler, connection):
305         lhs, params, key_transforms = self.preprocess_lhs(compiler, connection)
306         if len(key_transforms) > 1:
307             sql = '(%s %s %%s)' % (lhs, self.postgres_nested_operator)
308             return sql, tuple(params) + (key_transforms,)
309         try:
310             lookup = int(self.key_name)
311         except ValueError:
312             lookup = self.key_name
313         return '(%s %s %%s)' % (lhs, self.postgres_operator), tuple(params) + (lookup,)
314 
315     def as_sqlite(self, compiler, connection):
316         lhs, params, key_transforms = self.preprocess_lhs(compiler, connection)
317         json_path = compile_json_path(key_transforms)
318         return 'JSON_EXTRACT(%s, %%s)' % lhs, tuple(params) + (json_path,)

problem_statement:
Using __isnull=True on a KeyTransform should not match JSON null on SQLite and Oracle
Description
	
The KeyTransformIsNull lookup borrows the logic from HasKey for isnull=False, which is correct. If isnull=True, the query should only match objects that do not have the key. The query is correct for MariaDB, MySQL, and PostgreSQL. However, on SQLite and Oracle, the query also matches objects that have the key with the value null, which is incorrect.
To confirm, edit tests.model_fields.test_jsonfield.TestQuerying.test_isnull_key. For the first assertion, change
		self.assertSequenceEqual(
			NullableJSONModel.objects.filter(value__a__isnull=True),
			self.objs[:3] + self.objs[5:],
		)
to
		self.assertSequenceEqual(
			NullableJSONModel.objects.filter(value__j__isnull=True),
			self.objs[:4] + self.objs[5:],
		)
The test previously only checks with value__a which could not catch this behavior because the value is not JSON null.

462             args = "(%s)" % self.args
463             retann = self.retann
464         else:
465             # try to introspect the signature
466             try:
467                 retann = None
468                 args = self._call_format_args(**kwargs)
469                 if args:
470                     matched = re.match(r'^(\(.*\))\s+->\s+(.*)$', args)
471                     if matched:
472                         args = matched.group(1)
473                         retann = matched.group(2)
474             except Exception as exc:
475                 logger.warning(__('error while formatting arguments for %s: %s'),
476                                self.fullname, exc, type='autodoc')
477                 args = None
478 
479         result = self.env.events.emit_firstresult('autodoc-process-signature',
480                                                   self.objtype, self.fullname,
481                                                   self.object, self.options, args, retann)
482         if result:
483             args, retann = result
484 
485         if args is not None:
486             return args + ((' -> %s' % retann) if retann else '')
487         else:
488             return ''
489 
490     def add_directive_header(self, sig: str) -> None:
491         """Add the directive header and options to the generated content."""
492         domain = getattr(self, 'domain', 'py')
493         directive = getattr(self, 'directivetype', self.objtype)
494         name = self.format_name()
495         sourcename = self.get_sourcename()
496 
497         # one signature per line, indented by column
498         prefix = '.. %s:%s:: ' % (domain, directive)
499         for i, sig_line in enumerate(sig.split("\n")):
500             self.add_line('%s%s%s' % (prefix, name, sig_line),
501                           sourcename)
502             if i == 0:
503                 prefix = " " * len(prefix)
504 
505         if self.options.noindex:
506             self.add_line('   :noindex:', sourcename)
507         if self.objpath:
508             # Be explicit about the module, this is necessary since .. class::
509             # etc. don't support a prepended module name
510             self.add_line('   :module: %s' % self.modname, sourcename)
511 
512     def get_doc(self, encoding: str = None, ignore: int = None) -> List[List[str]]:
513         """Decode and return lines of the docstring(s) for the object."""
514         if encoding is not None:
515             warnings.warn("The 'encoding' argument to autodoc.%s.get_doc() is deprecated."
516                           % self.__class__.__name__,
517                           RemovedInSphinx40Warning, stacklevel=2)
518         if ignore is not None:
519             warnings.warn("The 'ignore' argument to autodoc.%s.get_doc() is deprecated."
520                           % self.__class__.__name__,
521                           RemovedInSphinx50Warning, stacklevel=2)
522         docstring = getdoc(self.object, self.get_attr,
523                            self.env.config.autodoc_inherit_docstrings,
524                            self.parent, self.object_name)
525         if docstring:
526             tab_width = self.directive.state.document.settings.tab_width
527             return [prepare_docstring(docstring, ignore, tab_width)]
528         return []
529 
530     def process_doc(self, docstrings: List[List[str]]) -> Iterator[str]:
531         """Let the user process the docstrings before adding them."""
532         for docstringlines in docstrings:
533             if self.env.app:
534                 # let extensions preprocess docstrings
535                 self.env.app.emit('autodoc-process-docstring',
536                                   self.objtype, self.fullname, self.object,
537                                   self.options, docstringlines)
538 
539                 if docstringlines and docstringlines[-1] != '':
540                     # append a blank line to the end of the docstring
541                     docstringlines.append('')
542 
543             yield from docstringlines
544 
545     def get_sourcename(self) -> str:
546         if self.analyzer:
547             return '%s:docstring of %s' % (self.analyzer.srcname, self.fullname)
548         return 'docstring of %s' % self.fullname
549 
550     def add_content(self, more_content: Any, no_docstring: bool = False) -> None:
551         """Add content from docstrings, attribute documentation and user."""
552         # set sourcename and add content from attribute documentation
553         sourcename = self.get_sourcename()
554         if self.analyzer:
555             attr_docs = self.analyzer.find_attr_docs()
556             if self.objpath:
557                 key = ('.'.join(self.objpath[:-1]), self.objpath[-1])
558                 if key in attr_docs:
559                     no_docstring = True
560                     # make a copy of docstring for attributes to avoid cache
561                     # the change of autodoc-process-docstring event.
562                     docstrings = [list(attr_docs[key])]
563 
564                     for i, line in enumerate(self.process_doc(docstrings)):
565                         self.add_line(line, sourcename, i)
566 
567         # add content from docstrings
568         if not no_docstring:
569             docstrings = self.get_doc()
570             if not docstrings:
571                 # append at least a dummy docstring, so that the event
572                 # autodoc-process-docstring is fired and can add some
573                 # content if desired
574                 docstrings.append([])
575             for i, line in enumerate(self.process_doc(docstrings)):
576                 self.add_line(line, sourcename, i)
577 
578         # add additional content (e.g. from document), if present
579         if more_content:
580             for line, src in zip(more_content.data, more_content.items):
581                 self.add_line(line, src[0], src[1])

583     def get_object_members(self, want_all: bool) -> Tuple[bool, List[Tuple[str, Any]]]:
584         """Return `(members_check_module, members)` where `members` is a
585         list of `(membername, member)` pairs of the members of *self.object*.
586 
587         If *want_all* is True, return all members.  Else, only return those
588         members given by *self.options.members* (which may also be none).
589         """
590         members = get_object_members(self.object, self.objpath, self.get_attr, self.analyzer)
591         if not want_all:
592             if not self.options.members:
593                 return False, []
594             # specific members given
595             selected = []
596             for name in self.options.members:
597                 if name in members:
598                     selected.append((name, members[name].value))
599                 else:
600                     logger.warning(__('missing attribute %s in object %s') %
601                                    (name, self.fullname), type='autodoc')
602             return False, selected
603         elif self.options.inherited_members:
604             return False, [(m.name, m.value) for m in members.values()]
605         else:
606             return False, [(m.name, m.value) for m in members.values()
607                            if m.directly_defined]
608 
609     def filter_members(self, members: List[Tuple[str, Any]], want_all: bool
610                        ) -> List[Tuple[str, Any, bool]]:
611         """Filter the given member list.
612 
613         Members are skipped if
614 
615         - they are private (except if given explicitly or the private-members
616           option is set)
617         - they are special methods (except if given explicitly or the
618           special-members option is set)
619         - they are undocumented (except if the undoc-members option is set)
620 
621         The user can override the skipping decision by connecting to the
622         ``autodoc-skip-member`` event.
623         """
624         def is_filtered_inherited_member(name: str) -> bool:
625             if inspect.isclass(self.object):
626                 for cls in self.object.__mro__:
627                     if cls.__name__ == self.options.inherited_members and cls != self.object:
628                         # given member is a member of specified *super class*
629                         return True
630                     elif name in cls.__dict__:
631                         return False
632                     elif name in self.get_attr(cls, '__annotations__', {}):
633                         return False
634 
635             return False
636 
637         ret = []
638 
639         # search for members in source code too
640         namespace = '.'.join(self.objpath)  # will be empty for modules
641 
642         if self.analyzer:
643             attr_docs = self.analyzer.find_attr_docs()
644         else:
645             attr_docs = {}
646 
647         # process members and determine which to skip
648         for (membername, member) in members:
649             # if isattr is True, the member is documented as an attribute
650             if member is INSTANCEATTR:
651                 isattr = True
652             else:
653                 isattr = False
654 
655             doc = getdoc(member, self.get_attr, self.env.config.autodoc_inherit_docstrings,
656                          self.parent, self.object_name)
657             if not isinstance(doc, str):
658                 # Ignore non-string __doc__
659                 doc = None
660 
661             # if the member __doc__ is the same as self's __doc__, it's just
662             # inherited and therefore not the member's doc
663             cls = self.get_attr(member, '__class__', None)
664             if cls:
665                 cls_doc = self.get_attr(cls, '__doc__', None)
666                 if cls_doc == doc:
667                     doc = None
668             has_doc = bool(doc)
669 
670             metadata = extract_metadata(doc)
671             if 'private' in metadata:
672                 # consider a member private if docstring has "private" metadata
673                 isprivate = True
674             elif 'public' in metadata:
675                 # consider a member public if docstring has "public" metadata
676                 isprivate = False
677             else:
678                 isprivate = membername.startswith('_')
679 
680             keep = False
681             if safe_getattr(member, '__sphinx_mock__', False):
682                 # mocked module or object
683                 pass
684             elif self.options.exclude_members and membername in self.options.exclude_members:
685                 # remove members given by exclude-members
686                 keep = False
687             elif want_all and special_member_re.match(membername):
688                 # special __methods__
689                 if self.options.special_members and membername in self.options.special_members:
690                     if membername == '__doc__':
691                         keep = False
692                     elif is_filtered_inherited_member(membername):
693                         keep = False
694                     else:
695                         keep = has_doc or self.options.undoc_members
696                 else:
697                     keep = False
698             elif (namespace, membername) in attr_docs:
699                 if want_all and isprivate:
700                     if self.options.private_members is None:
701                         keep = False
702                     else:
703                         keep = membername in self.options.private_members
704                 else:
705                     # keep documented attributes
706                     keep = True
707                 isattr = True
708             elif want_all and isprivate:
709                 if has_doc or self.options.undoc_members:
710                     if self.options.private_members is None:
711                         keep = False
712                     elif is_filtered_inherited_member(membername):
713                         keep = False
714                     else:
715                         keep = membername in self.options.private_members
716                 else:
717                     keep = False
718             else:
719                 if self.options.members is ALL and is_filtered_inherited_member(membername):
720                     keep = False
721                 else:
722                     # ignore undocumented members if :undoc-members: is not given
723                     keep = has_doc or self.options.undoc_members
724 
725             # give the user a chance to decide whether this member
726             # should be skipped
727             if self.env.app:
728                 # let extensions preprocess docstrings
729                 try:
730                     skip_user = self.env.app.emit_firstresult(
731                         'autodoc-skip-member', self.objtype, membername, member,
732                         not keep, self.options)
733                     if skip_user is not None:
734                         keep = not skip_user
735                 except Exception as exc:
736                     logger.warning(__('autodoc: failed to determine %r to be documented, '
737                                       'the following exception was raised:\n%s'),
738                                    member, exc, type='autodoc')
739                     keep = False
740 
741             if keep:
742                 ret.append((membername, member, isattr))
743 
744         return ret
745 
746     def document_members(self, all_members: bool = False) -> None:
747         """Generate reST for member documentation.
748 
749         If *all_members* is True, do all members, else those given by
750         *self.options.members*.
751         """
752         # set current namespace for finding members
753         self.env.temp_data['autodoc:module'] = self.modname
754         if self.objpath:
755             self.env.temp_data['autodoc:class'] = self.objpath[0]
756 
757         want_all = all_members or self.options.inherited_members or \
758             self.options.members is ALL
759         # find out which members are documentable
760         members_check_module, members = self.get_object_members(want_all)
761 
762         # document non-skipped members
763         memberdocumenters = []  # type: List[Tuple[Documenter, bool]]
764         for (mname, member, isattr) in self.filter_members(members, want_all):
765             classes = [cls for cls in self.documenters.values()
766                        if cls.can_document_member(member, mname, isattr, self)]
767             if not classes:
768                 # don't know how to document this member
769                 continue
770             # prefer the documenter with the highest priority
771             classes.sort(key=lambda cls: cls.priority)
772             # give explicitly separated module name, so that members
773             # of inner classes can be documented
774             full_mname = self.modname + '::' + \
775                 '.'.join(self.objpath + [mname])
776             documenter = classes[-1](self.directive, full_mname, self.indent)
777             memberdocumenters.append((documenter, isattr))
778 
779         member_order = self.options.member_order or self.env.config.autodoc_member_order
780         memberdocumenters = self.sort_members(memberdocumenters, member_order)
781 
782         for documenter, isattr in memberdocumenters:
783             documenter.generate(
784                 all_members=True, real_modname=self.real_modname,
785                 check_module=members_check_module and not isattr)
786 
787         # reset current objects
788         self.env.temp_data['autodoc:module'] = None
789         self.env.temp_data['autodoc:class'] = None
790 
791     def sort_members(self, documenters: List[Tuple["Documenter", bool]],
792                      order: str) -> List[Tuple["Documenter", bool]]:
793         """Sort the given member list."""
794         if order == 'groupwise':
795             # sort by group; alphabetically within groups
796             documenters.sort(key=lambda e: (e[0].member_order, e[0].name))
797         elif order == 'bysource':
798             if self.analyzer:
799                 # sort by source order, by virtue of the module analyzer
800                 tagorder = self.analyzer.tagorder
801 
802                 def keyfunc(entry: Tuple[Documenter, bool]) -> int:
803                     fullname = entry[0].name.split('::')[1]
804                     return tagorder.get(fullname, len(tagorder))
805                 documenters.sort(key=keyfunc)
806             else:
807                 # Assume that member discovery order matches source order.
808                 # This is a reasonable assumption in Python 3.6 and up, where
809                 # module.__dict__ is insertion-ordered.
810                 pass
811         else:  # alphabetical
812             documenters.sort(key=lambda e: e[0].name)
813 
814         return documenters
815 
816     def generate(self, more_content: Any = None, real_modname: str = None,
817                  check_module: bool = False, all_members: bool = False) -> None:
818         """Generate reST for the object given by *self.name*, and possibly for
819         its members.
820 
821         If *more_content* is given, include that content. If *real_modname* is
822         given, use that module name to find attribute docs. If *check_module* is
823         True, only generate if the object is defined in the module name it is
824         imported from. If *all_members* is True, document all members.
825         """
826         if not self.parse_name():
827             # need a module to import
828             logger.warning(
829                 __('don\'t know which module to import for autodocumenting '
830                    '%r (try placing a "module" or "currentmodule" directive '
831                    'in the document, or giving an explicit module name)') %
832                 self.name, type='autodoc')
833             return
834 
835         # now, import the module and get object to document
836         if not self.import_object():
837             return
838 
839         # If there is no real module defined, figure out which to use.
840         # The real module is used in the module analyzer to look up the module
841         # where the attribute documentation would actually be found in.
842         # This is used for situations where you have a module that collects the
843         # functions and classes of internal submodules.
844         guess_modname = self.get_real_modname()
845         self.real_modname = real_modname or guess_modname
846 
847         # try to also get a source code analyzer for attribute docs
848         try:
849             self.analyzer = ModuleAnalyzer.for_module(self.real_modname)
850             # parse right now, to get PycodeErrors on parsing (results will
851             # be cached anyway)
852             self.analyzer.find_attr_docs()
853         except PycodeError as exc:
854             logger.debug('[autodoc] module analyzer failed: %s', exc)
855             # no source file -- e.g. for builtin and C modules
856             self.analyzer = None
857             # at least add the module.__file__ as a dependency
858             if hasattr(self.module, '__file__') and self.module.__file__:
859                 self.directive.filename_set.add(self.module.__file__)
860         else:
861             self.directive.filename_set.add(self.analyzer.srcname)
862 
863         if self.real_modname != guess_modname:
864             # Add module to dependency list if target object is defined in other module.
865             try:
866                 analyzer = ModuleAnalyzer.for_module(guess_modname)
867                 self.directive.filename_set.add(analyzer.srcname)
868             except PycodeError:
869                 pass
870 
871         # check __module__ of object (for members not given explicitly)
872         if check_module:
873             if not self.check_module():
874                 return
875 
876         sourcename = self.get_sourcename()
877 
878         # make sure that the result starts with an empty line.  This is
879         # necessary for some situations where another directive preprocesses
880         # reST and no starting newline is present
881         self.add_line('', sourcename)
882 
883         # format the object's signature, if any
884         try:
885             sig = self.format_signature()
886         except Exception as exc:
887             logger.warning(__('error while formatting signature for %s: %s'),
888                            self.fullname, exc, type='autodoc')
889             return
890 
891         # generate the directive header and options, if applicable
892         self.add_directive_header(sig)
893         self.add_line('', sourcename)
894 
895         # e.g. the module directive doesn't have content
896         self.indent += self.content_indent
897 
898         # add all content (from docstrings, attribute docs etc.)
899         self.add_content(more_content)
900 
901         # document members, if possible
902         self.document_members(all_members)
903

905 class ModuleDocumenter(Documenter):
906     """
907     Specialized Documenter subclass for modules.
908     """
909     objtype = 'module'
910     content_indent = ''
911     titles_allowed = True
912 
913     option_spec = {
914         'members': members_option, 'undoc-members': bool_option,
915         'noindex': bool_option, 'inherited-members': inherited_members_option,
916         'show-inheritance': bool_option, 'synopsis': identity,
917         'platform': identity, 'deprecated': bool_option,
918         'member-order': member_order_option, 'exclude-members': exclude_members_option,
919         'private-members': members_option, 'special-members': members_option,
920         'imported-members': bool_option, 'ignore-module-all': bool_option
921     }  # type: Dict[str, Callable]

923     def __init__(self, *args: Any) -> None:
924         super().__init__(*args)

928     @classmethod

930                             ) -> bool:

935                      ) -> Tuple[str, List[str]]:

937             logger.warning(__('"::" in automodule name doesn\'t make sense'),

941     def parse_name(self) -> bool:
942         ret = super().parse_name()

944             logger.warning(__('signature arguments or return annotation '
945                               'given for automodule %s') % self.fullname,
946                            type='autodoc')

949     def import_object(self, raiseerror: bool = False) -> bool:
950         def is_valid_module_all(__all__: Any) -> bool:
951             """Check the given *__all__* is valid for a module."""
952             if (isinstance(__all__, (list, tuple)) and
953                     all(isinstance(e, str) for e in __all__)):
954                 return True
955             else:
956                 return False
957 
958         ret = super().import_object(raiseerror)
959 
960         if not self.options.ignore_module_all:
961             __all__ = getattr(self.object, '__all__', None)
962             if is_valid_module_all(__all__):
963                 # valid __all__ found. copy it to self.__all__
964                 self.__all__ = __all__
965             elif __all__:
966                 # invalid __all__ found.
967                 logger.warning(__('__all__ should be a list of strings, not %r '
968                                   '(in module %s) -- ignoring __all__') %
969                                (__all__, self.fullname), type='autodoc')
970 
971         return ret

973     def add_directive_header(self, sig: str) -> None:
974         Documenter.add_directive_header(self, sig)
975 
976         sourcename = self.get_sourcename()
977 
978         # add some module-specific options
979         if self.options.synopsis:
980             self.add_line('   :synopsis: ' + self.options.synopsis, sourcename)
981         if self.options.platform:
982             self.add_line('   :platform: ' + self.options.platform, sourcename)
983         if self.options.deprecated:
984             self.add_line('   :deprecated:', sourcename)

986     def get_object_members(self, want_all: bool) -> Tuple[bool, List[Tuple[str, Any]]]:
987         if want_all:
988             if self.__all__:
989                 memberlist = self.__all__
990             else:
991                 # for implicit module members, check __module__ to avoid
992                 # documenting imported objects
993                 return True, get_module_members(self.object)
994         else:
995             memberlist = self.options.members or []
996         ret = []
997         for mname in memberlist:
998             try:
999                 ret.append((mname, safe_getattr(self.object, mname)))
1000             except AttributeError:
1001                 logger.warning(
1002                     __('missing attribute mentioned in :members: or __all__: '
1003                        'module %s, attribute %s') %
1004                     (safe_getattr(self.object, '__name__', '???'), mname),
1005                     type='autodoc'
1006                 )
1007         return False, ret

1009     def sort_members(self, documenters: List[Tuple["Documenter", bool]],
1010                      order: str) -> List[Tuple["Documenter", bool]]:
1011         if order == 'bysource' and self.__all__:
1012             # Sort alphabetically first (for members not listed on the __all__)
1013             documenters.sort(key=lambda e: e[0].name)
1014 
1015             # Sort by __all__
1016             def keyfunc(entry: Tuple[Documenter, bool]) -> int:
1017                 name = entry[0].name.split('::')[1]
1018                 if name in self.__all__:
1019                     return self.__all__.index(name)
1020                 else:
1021                     return len(self.__all__)
1022             documenters.sort(key=keyfunc)
1023 
1024             return documenters
1025         else:
1026             return super().sort_members(documenters, order)

1029 class ModuleLevelDocumenter(Documenter):

1031     Specialized Documenter subclass for objects on module level (functions,
1032     classes, data/constants).

1034     def resolve_name(self, modname: str, parents: Any, path: str, base: Any
1035                      ) -> Tuple[str, List[str]]:
1036         if modname is None:
1037             if path:
1038                 modname = path.rstrip('.')
1039             else:
1040                 # if documenting a toplevel object without explicit module,
1041                 # it can be contained in another auto directive ...
1042                 modname = self.env.temp_data.get('autodoc:module')
1043                 # ... or in the scope of a module directive
1044                 if not modname:
1045                     modname = self.env.ref_context.get('py:module')
1046                 # ... else, it stays None, which means invalid
1047         return modname, parents + [base]

1050 class ClassLevelDocumenter(Documenter):
1051     """
1052     Specialized Documenter subclass for objects on class level (methods,
1053     attributes).
1054     """
1055     def resolve_name(self, modname: str, parents: Any, path: str, base: Any
1056                      ) -> Tuple[str, List[str]]:
1057         if modname is None:
1058             if path:
1059                 mod_cls = path.rstrip('.')
1060             else:
1061                 mod_cls = None
1062                 # if documenting a class-level object without path,
1063                 # there must be a current class, either from a parent
1064                 # auto directive ...
1065                 mod_cls = self.env.temp_data.get('autodoc:class')
1066                 # ... or from a class directive
1067                 if mod_cls is None:
1068                     mod_cls = self.env.ref_context.get('py:class')
1069                 # ... if still None, there's no way to know
1070                 if mod_cls is None:
1071                     return None, []
1072             modname, sep, cls = mod_cls.rpartition('.')

1083 class DocstringSignatureMixin:
1084     """
1085     Mixin for FunctionDocumenter and MethodDocumenter to provide the
1086     feature of reading the signature from the docstring.
1087     """
1088     _new_docstrings = None  # type: List[List[str]]
1089     _signatures = None      # type: List[str]
1090 
1091     def _find_signature(self, encoding: str = None) -> Tuple[str, str]:
1092         if encoding is not None:
1093             warnings.warn("The 'encoding' argument to autodoc.%s._find_signature() is "
1094                           "deprecated." % self.__class__.__name__,
1095                           RemovedInSphinx40Warning, stacklevel=2)
1096 
1097         # candidates of the object name
1098         valid_names = [self.objpath[-1]]  # type: ignore
1099         if isinstance(self, ClassDocumenter):
1100             valid_names.append('__init__')
1101             if hasattr(self.object, '__mro__'):
1102                 valid_names.extend(cls.__name__ for cls in self.object.__mro__)
1103 
1104         docstrings = self.get_doc()
1105         self._new_docstrings = docstrings[:]
1106         self._signatures = []
1107         result = None
1108         for i, doclines in enumerate(docstrings):
1109             for j, line in enumerate(doclines):
1110                 if not line:
1111                     # no lines in docstring, no match
1112                     break
1113 
1114                 if line.endswith('\\'):
1115                     multiline = True
1116                     line = line.rstrip('\\').rstrip()
1117                 else:
1118                     multiline = False
1119 
1120                 # match first line of docstring against signature RE
1121                 match = py_ext_sig_re.match(line)
1122                 if not match:
1123                     continue
1124                 exmod, path, base, args, retann = match.groups()
1125 
1126                 # the base name must match ours
1127                 if base not in valid_names:
1128                     continue
1129 
1130                 # re-prepare docstring to ignore more leading indentation
1131                 tab_width = self.directive.state.document.settings.tab_width  # type: ignore
1132                 self._new_docstrings[i] = prepare_docstring('\n'.join(doclines[j + 1:]),
1133                                                             tabsize=tab_width)
1134 
1135                 if result is None:
1136                     # first signature
1137                     result = args, retann
1138                 else:
1139                     # subsequent signatures
1140                     self._signatures.append("(%s) -> %s" % (args, retann))
1141 
1142                 if multiline:
1143                     # the signature have multiple signatures on docstring
1144                     continue
1145                 else:
1146                     # don't look any further
1147                     break
1148 
1149             if result:
1150                 # finish the loop when signature found
1151                 break
1152 
1153         return result
1154 
1155     def get_doc(self, encoding: str = None, ignore: int = None) -> List[List[str]]:
1156         if encoding is not None:
1157             warnings.warn("The 'encoding' argument to autodoc.%s.get_doc() is deprecated."
1158                           % self.__class__.__name__,
1159                           RemovedInSphinx40Warning, stacklevel=2)
1160         if self._new_docstrings is not None:
1161             return self._new_docstrings
1162         return super().get_doc(None, ignore)  # type: ignore
1163 
1164     def format_signature(self, **kwargs: Any) -> str:
1165         if self.args is None and self.env.config.autodoc_docstring_signature:  # type: ignore
1166             # only act if a signature is not explicitly given already, and if
1167             # the feature is enabled
1168             result = self._find_signature()
1169             if result is not None:
1170                 self.args, self.retann = result
1171         sig = super().format_signature(**kwargs)  # type: ignore
1172         if self._signatures:
1173             return "\n".join([sig] + self._signatures)
1174         else:
1175             return sig

1379     def _get_signature(self) -> Tuple[Optional[Any], Optional[str], Optional[Signature]]:

1392         # First, let's see if it has an overloaded __call__ defined
1393         # in its metaclass
1394         call = get_user_defined_function_or_method(type(self.object), '__call__')
1395 
1396         if call is not None:
1397             if "{0.__module__}.{0.__qualname__}".format(call) in _METACLASS_CALL_BLACKLIST:

1404                                         type_aliases=self.env.config.autodoc_type_aliases)

1415 
1416         if new is not None:

1419                 sig = inspect.signature(new, bound_method=True,
1420                                         type_aliases=self.env.config.autodoc_type_aliases)
1421                 return self.object, '__new__', sig
1422             except ValueError:
1423                 pass

1426         init = get_user_defined_function_or_method(self.object, '__init__')
1427         if init is not None:

1431                                         type_aliases=self.env.config.autodoc_type_aliases)

1449         # with __init__ in C and no `__text_signature__`.
1450         return None, None, None

11 class AssocOp(Basic):
12     """ Associative operations, can separate noncommutative and
13     commutative parts.
14 
15     (a op b) op c == a op (b op c) == a op b op c.
16 
17     Base class for Add and Mul.
18 
19     This is an abstract base class, concrete derived classes must define
20     the attribute `identity`.
21     """
22 
23     # for performance reason, we don't let is_commutative go to assumptions,
24     # and keep it right here
25     __slots__ = ['is_commutative']
26 
27     @cacheit
28     def __new__(cls, *args, **options):
29         from sympy import Order
30         args = list(map(_sympify, args))
31         args = [a for a in args if a is not cls.identity]
32 
33         if not options.pop('evaluate', global_evaluate[0]):
34             return cls._from_args(args)
35 
36         if len(args) == 0:
37             return cls.identity
38         if len(args) == 1:
39             return args[0]
40 
41         c_part, nc_part, order_symbols = cls.flatten(args)
42         is_commutative = not nc_part
43         obj = cls._from_args(c_part + nc_part, is_commutative)
44         obj = cls._exec_constructor_postprocessors(obj)
45 
46         if order_symbols is not None:
47             return Order(obj, *order_symbols)
48         return obj
49 
50     @classmethod
51     def _from_args(cls, args, is_commutative=None):
52         """Create new instance with already-processed args"""
53         if len(args) == 0:
54             return cls.identity
55         elif len(args) == 1:
56             return args[0]
57 
58         obj = super(AssocOp, cls).__new__(cls, *args)
59         if is_commutative is None:
60             is_commutative = fuzzy_and(a.is_commutative for a in args)
61         obj.is_commutative = is_commutative
62         return obj

64     def _new_rawargs(self, *args, **kwargs):
65         """Create new instance of own class with args exactly as provided by
66         caller but returning the self class identity if args is empty.
67 
68            This is handy when we want to optimize things, e.g.
69 
70                >>> from sympy import Mul, S
71                >>> from sympy.abc import x, y
72                >>> e = Mul(3, x, y)
73                >>> e.args
74                (3, x, y)
75                >>> Mul(*e.args[1:])
76                x*y
77                >>> e._new_rawargs(*e.args[1:])  # the same as above, but faster
78                x*y
79 
80            Note: use this with caution. There is no checking of arguments at
81            all. This is best used when you are rebuilding an Add or Mul after
82            simply removing one or more terms. If modification which result,
83            for example, in extra 1s being inserted (as when collecting an
84            expression's numerators and denominators) they will not show up in
85            the result but a Mul will be returned nonetheless:

87                >>> m = (x*y)._new_rawargs(S.One, x); m
88                x
89                >>> m == x

94            Another issue to be aware of is that the commutativity of the result
95            is based on the commutativity of self. If you are rebuilding the
96            terms that came from a commutative object then there will be no
97            problem, but if self was non-commutative then what you are
98            rebuilding may now be commutative.

100            Although this routine tries to do as little as possible with the
101            input, getting the commutativity right is important, so this level
102            of safety is enforced: commutativity will always be recomputed if
103            self is non-commutative and kwarg `reeval=False` has not been
104            passed.

297         """
298         Evaluate the parts of self that are numbers; if the whole thing
299         was a number with no functions it would have been evaluated, but
300         it wasn't so we must judiciously extract the numbers and reconstruct
301         the object. This is *not* simply replacing numbers with evaluated
302         numbers. Nunmbers should be handled in the largest pure-number
303         expression as possible. So the code below separates ``self`` into
304         number and non-number parts and evaluates the number parts and
305         walks the args of the non-number part recursively (doing the same
306         thing).
307         """
308         from .add import Add
309         from .mul import Mul
310         from .symbol import Symbol
311         from .function import AppliedUndef
312         if isinstance(self, (Mul, Add)):
313             x, tail = self.as_independent(Symbol, AppliedUndef)
314             # if x is an AssocOp Function then the _evalf below will
315             # call _eval_evalf (here) so we must break the recursion
316             if not (tail is self.identity or
317                     isinstance(x, AssocOp) and x.is_Function or
318                     x is self.identity and isinstance(tail, AssocOp)):
319                 # here, we have a number so we just call to _evalf with prec;
320                 # prec is not the same as n, it is the binary precision so
321                 # that's why we don't call to evalf.
322                 x = x._evalf(prec) if x is not self.identity else self.identity
323                 args = []
324                 tail_args = tuple(self.func.make_args(tail))
325                 for a in tail_args:
326                     # here we call to _eval_evalf since we don't know what we
327                     # are dealing with and all other _eval_evalf routines should
328                     # be doing the same thing (i.e. taking binary prec and
329                     # finding the evalf-able args)
330                     newa = a._eval_evalf(prec)
331                     if newa is None:
332                         args.append(a)
333                     else:
334                         args.append(newa)
335                 if not _aresame(tuple(args), tail_args):
336                     tail = self.func(*args)
337                 return self.func(x, tail)
338 
339         # this is the same as above, but there were no pure-number args to
340         # deal with
341         args = []
342         for a in self.args:
343             newa = a._eval_evalf(prec)
344             if newa is None:
345                 args.append(a)
346             else:
347                 args.append(newa)
348         if not _aresame(tuple(args), self.args):
349             return self.func(*args)

problem_statement:
`refine()` does not understand how to simplify complex arguments
Just learned about the refine-function, which would come in handy frequently for me.  But
`refine()` does not recognize that argument functions simplify for real numbers.

```
>>> from sympy import *                                                     
>>> var('a,x')                                                              
>>> J = Integral(sin(x)*exp(-a*x),(x,0,oo))                                     
>>> J.doit()
	Piecewise((1/(a**2 + 1), 2*Abs(arg(a)) < pi), (Integral(exp(-a*x)*sin(x), (x, 0, oo)), True))
>>> refine(J.doit(),Q.positive(a))                                                 
        Piecewise((1/(a**2 + 1), 2*Abs(arg(a)) < pi), (Integral(exp(-a*x)*sin(x), (x, 0, oo)), True))
>>> refine(abs(a),Q.positive(a))                                            
	a
>>> refine(arg(a),Q.positive(a))                                            
	arg(a)
```
I cann't find any open issues identifying this.  Easy to fix, though.

@@ -297,6 +297,28 @@ def refine_im(expr, assumptions):
         return - S.ImaginaryUnit * arg
     return _refine_reim(expr, assumptions)
 
+def refine_arg(expr, assumptions):
+    """
+    Handler for complex argument
+
+    Explanation
+    ===========
+
+    >>> from sympy.assumptions.refine import refine_arg
+    >>> from sympy import Q, arg
+    >>> from sympy.abc import x
+    >>> refine_arg(arg(x), Q.positive(x))
+    0
+    >>> refine_arg(arg(x), Q.negative(x))
+    pi
+    """
+    rg = expr.args[0]
+    if ask(Q.positive(rg), assumptions):
+        return S.Zero
+    if ask(Q.negative(rg), assumptions):
+        return S.Pi
+    return None
+
 
 def _refine_reim(expr, assumptions):
     # Helper function for refine_re & refine_im
@@ -379,6 +401,7 @@ def refine_matrixelement(expr, assumptions):
     'atan2': refine_atan2,
     're': refine_re,
     'im': refine_im,
+    'arg': refine_arg,
     'sign': refine_sign,
     'MatrixElement': refine_matrixelement
 }  # type: Dict[str, Callable[[Expr, Boolean], Expr]]

<issue>
Missing parameter validation in Neighbors estimator for float n_neighbors
```python
from sklearn.neighbors import NearestNeighbors
from sklearn.datasets import make_blobs
X, y = make_blobs()
neighbors = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=3.)
neighbors.fit(X)
neighbors.kneighbors(X)
```
```
~/checkout/scikit-learn/sklearn/neighbors/binary_tree.pxi in sklearn.neighbors.kd_tree.NeighborsHeap.__init__()

TypeError: 'float' object cannot be interpreted as an integer
```
This should be caught earlier and a more helpful error message should be raised (or we could be lenient and cast to integer, but I think a better error might be better).

We need to make sure that 
```python
neighbors.kneighbors(X, n_neighbors=3.)
```
also works.

</issue>

47 def _check_weights(weights):
48     """Check to make sure weights are valid"""
49     if weights in (None, 'uniform', 'distance'):
50         return weights
51     elif callable(weights):
52         return weights
53     else:
54         raise ValueError("weights not recognized: should be 'uniform', "
55                          "'distance', or a callable function")

58 def _get_weights(dist, weights):
59     """Get the weights from an array of distances and a parameter ``weights``
60 
61     Parameters
62     ===========
63     dist : ndarray
64         The input distances
65     weights : {'uniform', 'distance' or a callable}
66         The kind of weighting used
67 
68     Returns
69     ========
70     weights_arr : array of the same shape as ``dist``
71         if ``weights == 'uniform'``, then returns None
72     """
73     if weights in (None, 'uniform'):
74         return None
75     elif weights == 'distance':
76         # if user attempts to classify a point that was zero distance from one
77         # or more training points, those training points are weighted as 1.0
78         # and the other points as 0.0
79         if dist.dtype is np.dtype(object):
80             for point_dist_i, point_dist in enumerate(dist):
81                 # check if point_dist is iterable
82                 # (ex: RadiusNeighborClassifier.predict may set an element of
83                 # dist to 1e-6 to represent an 'outlier')
84                 if hasattr(point_dist, '__contains__') and 0. in point_dist:
85                     dist[point_dist_i] = point_dist == 0.
86                 else:
87                     dist[point_dist_i] = 1. / point_dist
88         else:
89             with np.errstate(divide='ignore'):
90                 dist = 1. / dist
91             inf_mask = np.isinf(dist)
92             inf_row = np.any(inf_mask, axis=1)
93             dist[inf_row] = inf_mask[inf_row]
94         return dist
95     elif callable(weights):
96         return weights(dist)
97     else:
98         raise ValueError("weights not recognized: should be 'uniform', "
99                          "'distance', or a callable function")
