105     @abstractmethod
106     def __init__(self, n_neighbors=None, radius=None,
107                  algorithm='auto', leaf_size=30, metric='minkowski',
108                  p=2, metric_params=None, n_jobs=1):
109 
110         self.n_neighbors = n_neighbors
111         self.radius = radius
112         self.algorithm = algorithm
113         self.leaf_size = leaf_size
114         self.metric = metric
115         self.metric_params = metric_params
116         self.p = p
117         self.n_jobs = n_jobs
118         self._check_algorithm_metric()
119 
120     def _check_algorithm_metric(self):
121         if self.algorithm not in ['auto', 'brute',
122                                   'kd_tree', 'ball_tree']:
123             raise ValueError("unrecognized algorithm: '%s'" % self.algorithm)
124 
125         if self.algorithm == 'auto':
126             if self.metric == 'precomputed':
127                 alg_check = 'brute'
128             elif (callable(self.metric) or
129                   self.metric in VALID_METRICS['ball_tree']):
130                 alg_check = 'ball_tree'
131             else:
132                 alg_check = 'brute'
133         else:
134             alg_check = self.algorithm
135 
136         if callable(self.metric):
137             if self.algorithm == 'kd_tree':
138                 # callable metric is only valid for brute force and ball_tree
139                 raise ValueError(
140                     "kd_tree algorithm does not support callable metric '%s'"
141                     % self.metric)
142         elif self.metric not in VALID_METRICS[alg_check]:
143             raise ValueError("Metric '%s' not valid for algorithm '%s'"
144                              % (self.metric, self.algorithm))
145 
146         if self.metric_params is not None and 'p' in self.metric_params:
147             warnings.warn("Parameter p is found in metric_params. "
148                           "The corresponding parameter from __init__ "
149                           "is ignored.", SyntaxWarning, stacklevel=3)
150             effective_p = self.metric_params['p']
151         else:
152             effective_p = self.p
153 
154         if self.metric in ['wminkowski', 'minkowski'] and effective_p < 1:
155             raise ValueError("p must be greater than one for minkowski metric")
156 
157     def _fit(self, X):
158         self._check_algorithm_metric()
159         if self.metric_params is None:
160             self.effective_metric_params_ = {}
161         else:
162             self.effective_metric_params_ = self.metric_params.copy()
163 
164         effective_p = self.effective_metric_params_.get('p', self.p)
165         if self.metric in ['wminkowski', 'minkowski']:
166             self.effective_metric_params_['p'] = effective_p
167 
168         self.effective_metric_ = self.metric
169         # For minkowski distance, use more efficient methods where available
170         if self.metric == 'minkowski':
171             p = self.effective_metric_params_.pop('p', 2)
172             if p < 1:
173                 raise ValueError("p must be greater than one "
174                                  "for minkowski metric")
175             elif p == 1:
176                 self.effective_metric_ = 'manhattan'
177             elif p == 2:
178                 self.effective_metric_ = 'euclidean'
179             elif p == np.inf:
180                 self.effective_metric_ = 'chebyshev'
181             else:
182                 self.effective_metric_params_['p'] = p
183 
184         if isinstance(X, NeighborsBase):
185             self._fit_X = X._fit_X
186             self._tree = X._tree
187             self._fit_method = X._fit_method
188             return self
189 
190         elif isinstance(X, BallTree):
191             self._fit_X = X.data
192             self._tree = X
193             self._fit_method = 'ball_tree'
194             return self
195 
196         elif isinstance(X, KDTree):
197             self._fit_X = X.data
198             self._tree = X
199             self._fit_method = 'kd_tree'
200             return self
201 
202         X = check_array(X, accept_sparse='csr')
203 
204         n_samples = X.shape[0]
205         if n_samples == 0:
206             raise ValueError("n_samples must be greater than 0")
207 
208         if issparse(X):
209             if self.algorithm not in ('auto', 'brute'):
210                 warnings.warn("cannot use tree with sparse input: "
211                               "using brute force")
212             if self.effective_metric_ not in VALID_METRICS_SPARSE['brute'] \
213                     and not callable(self.effective_metric_):
214 
215                 raise ValueError("metric '%s' not valid for sparse input"
216                                  % self.effective_metric_)
217             self._fit_X = X.copy()
218             self._tree = None
219             self._fit_method = 'brute'
220             return self
221 
222         self._fit_method = self.algorithm
223         self._fit_X = X
224 
225         if self._fit_method == 'auto':
226             # A tree approach is better for small number of neighbors,
227             # and KDTree is generally faster when available
228             if ((self.n_neighbors is None or
229                  self.n_neighbors < self._fit_X.shape[0] // 2) and
230                     self.metric != 'precomputed'):
231                 if self.effective_metric_ in VALID_METRICS['kd_tree']:
232                     self._fit_method = 'kd_tree'
233                 elif (callable(self.effective_metric_) or
234                         self.effective_metric_ in VALID_METRICS['ball_tree']):
235                     self._fit_method = 'ball_tree'
236                 else:
237                     self._fit_method = 'brute'
238             else:
239                 self._fit_method = 'brute'
240 
241         if self._fit_method == 'ball_tree':
242             self._tree = BallTree(X, self.leaf_size,
243                                   metric=self.effective_metric_,
244                                   **self.effective_metric_params_)
245         elif self._fit_method == 'kd_tree':
246             self._tree = KDTree(X, self.leaf_size,
247                                 metric=self.effective_metric_,
248                                 **self.effective_metric_params_)
249         elif self._fit_method == 'brute':
250             self._tree = None
251         else:
252             raise ValueError("algorithm = '%s' not recognized"
253                              % self.algorithm)
254 
255         if self.n_neighbors is not None:
256             if self.n_neighbors <= 0:
257                 raise ValueError(
258                     "Expected n_neighbors > 0. Got %d" %
259                     self.n_neighbors
260                 )
261 
262         return self
263

270 class KNeighborsMixin(object):
271     """Mixin for k-neighbors searches"""
272 
273     def kneighbors(self, X=None, n_neighbors=None, return_distance=True):
274         """Finds the K-neighbors of a point.
275 
276         Returns indices of and distances to the neighbors of each point.
277 
278         Parameters
279         ----------
280         X : array-like, shape (n_query, n_features), \
281                 or (n_query, n_indexed) if metric == 'precomputed'
282             The query point or points.
283             If not provided, neighbors of each indexed point are returned.
284             In this case, the query point is not considered its own neighbor.
285 
286         n_neighbors : int
287             Number of neighbors to get (default is the value
288             passed to the constructor).
289 
290         return_distance : boolean, optional. Defaults to True.
291             If False, distances will not be returned
292 
293         Returns
294         -------
295         dist : array
296             Array representing the lengths to points, only present if
297             return_distance=True
298 
299         ind : array
300             Indices of the nearest points in the population matrix.
301 
302         Examples
303         --------
304         In the following example, we construct a NeighborsClassifier
305         class from an array representing our data set and ask who's
306         the closest point to [1,1,1]
307 
308         >>> samples = [[0., 0., 0.], [0., .5, 0.], [1., 1., .5]]
309         >>> from sklearn.neighbors import NearestNeighbors
310         >>> neigh = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=1)
311         >>> neigh.fit(samples) # doctest: +ELLIPSIS
312         NearestNeighbors(algorithm='auto', leaf_size=30, ...)
313         >>> print(neigh.kneighbors([[1., 1., 1.]])) # doctest: +ELLIPSIS
314         (array([[0.5]]), array([[2]]))
315 
316         As you can see, it returns [[0.5]], and [[2]], which means that the
317         element is at distance 0.5 and is the third element of samples
318         (indexes start at 0). You can also query for multiple points:
319 
320         >>> X = [[0., 1., 0.], [1., 0., 1.]]
321         >>> neigh.kneighbors(X, return_distance=False) # doctest: +ELLIPSIS
322         array([[1],
323                [2]]...)
324 
325         """
326         check_is_fitted(self, "_fit_method")
327 
328         if n_neighbors is None:
329             n_neighbors = self.n_neighbors
330 
331         if X is not None:
332             query_is_train = False
333             X = check_array(X, accept_sparse='csr')
334         else:
335             query_is_train = True
336             X = self._fit_X
337             # Include an extra neighbor to account for the sample itself being
338             # returned, which is removed later
339             n_neighbors += 1
340 
341         train_size = self._fit_X.shape[0]
342         if n_neighbors > train_size:
343             raise ValueError(
344                 "Expected n_neighbors <= n_samples, "
345                 " but n_samples = %d, n_neighbors = %d" %
346                 (train_size, n_neighbors)
347             )
348         n_samples, _ = X.shape
349         sample_range = np.arange(n_samples)[:, None]
350 
351         n_jobs = _get_n_jobs(self.n_jobs)
352         if self._fit_method == 'brute':
353             # for efficiency, use squared euclidean distances
354             if self.effective_metric_ == 'euclidean':
355                 dist = pairwise_distances(X, self._fit_X, 'euclidean',
356                                           n_jobs=n_jobs, squared=True)
357             else:
358                 dist = pairwise_distances(
359                     X, self._fit_X, self.effective_metric_, n_jobs=n_jobs,
360                     **self.effective_metric_params_)
361 
362             neigh_ind = np.argpartition(dist, n_neighbors - 1, axis=1)
363             neigh_ind = neigh_ind[:, :n_neighbors]
364             # argpartition doesn't guarantee sorted order, so we sort again
365             neigh_ind = neigh_ind[
366                 sample_range, np.argsort(dist[sample_range, neigh_ind])]
367 
368             if return_distance:
369                 if self.effective_metric_ == 'euclidean':
370                     result = np.sqrt(dist[sample_range, neigh_ind]), neigh_ind
371                 else:
372                     result = dist[sample_range, neigh_ind], neigh_ind
373             else:
374                 result = neigh_ind
375 
376         elif self._fit_method in ['ball_tree', 'kd_tree']:
377             if issparse(X):
378                 raise ValueError(
379                     "%s does not work with sparse matrices. Densify the data, "
380                     "or set algorithm='brute'" % self._fit_method)
381             result = Parallel(n_jobs, backend='threading')(
382                 delayed(self._tree.query, check_pickle=False)(
383                     X[s], n_neighbors, return_distance)
384                 for s in gen_even_slices(X.shape[0], n_jobs)
385             )
386             if return_distance:
387                 dist, neigh_ind = tuple(zip(*result))
388                 result = np.vstack(dist), np.vstack(neigh_ind)
389             else:
390                 result = np.vstack(result)
391         else:
392             raise ValueError("internal: _fit_method not recognized")
393 
394         if not query_is_train:
395             return result
396         else:
397             # If the query data is the same as the indexed data, we would like
398             # to ignore the first nearest neighbor of every sample, i.e
399             # the sample itself.
400             if return_distance:
401                 dist, neigh_ind = result
402             else:
403                 neigh_ind = result
404 
405             sample_mask = neigh_ind != sample_range
406 
407             # Corner case: When the number of duplicates are more
408             # than the number of neighbors, the first NN will not
409             # be the sample, but a duplicate.
410             # In that case mask the first duplicate.
411             dup_gr_nbrs = np.all(sample_mask, axis=1)
412             sample_mask[:, 0][dup_gr_nbrs] = False
413 
414             neigh_ind = np.reshape(
415                 neigh_ind[sample_mask], (n_samples, n_neighbors - 1))
416 
417             if return_distance:
418                 dist = np.reshape(
419                     dist[sample_mask], (n_samples, n_neighbors - 1))
420                 return dist, neigh_ind
421             return neigh_ind
422 
423     def kneighbors_graph(self, X=None, n_neighbors=None,
424                          mode='connectivity'):
425         """Computes the (weighted) graph of k-Neighbors for points in X
426 
427         Parameters
428         ----------
429         X : array-like, shape (n_query, n_features), \
430                 or (n_query, n_indexed) if metric == 'precomputed'
431             The query point or points.
432             If not provided, neighbors of each indexed point are returned.
433             In this case, the query point is not considered its own neighbor.
434 
435         n_neighbors : int
436             Number of neighbors for each sample.
437             (default is value passed to the constructor).
438 
439         mode : {'connectivity', 'distance'}, optional
440             Type of returned matrix: 'connectivity' will return the
441             connectivity matrix with ones and zeros, in 'distance' the
442             edges are Euclidean distance between points.
443 
444         Returns
445         -------
446         A : sparse matrix in CSR format, shape = [n_samples, n_samples_fit]
447             n_samples_fit is the number of samples in the fitted data
448             A[i, j] is assigned the weight of edge that connects i to j.
449 
450         Examples
451         --------
452         >>> X = [[0], [3], [1]]
453         >>> from sklearn.neighbors import NearestNeighbors
454         >>> neigh = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=2)
455         >>> neigh.fit(X) # doctest: +ELLIPSIS
456         NearestNeighbors(algorithm='auto', leaf_size=30, ...)
457         >>> A = neigh.kneighbors_graph(X)
458         >>> A.toarray()
459         array([[1., 0., 1.],
460                [0., 1., 1.],
461                [1., 0., 1.]])
462 
463         See also
464         --------
465         NearestNeighbors.radius_neighbors_graph
466         """
467         if n_neighbors is None:
468             n_neighbors = self.n_neighbors
469 
470         # kneighbors does the None handling.
471         if X is not None:
472             X = check_array(X, accept_sparse='csr')
473             n_samples1 = X.shape[0]
474         else:
475             n_samples1 = self._fit_X.shape[0]
476 
477         n_samples2 = self._fit_X.shape[0]
478         n_nonzero = n_samples1 * n_neighbors
479         A_indptr = np.arange(0, n_nonzero + 1, n_neighbors)
480 
481         # construct CSR matrix representation of the k-NN graph
482         if mode == 'connectivity':
483             A_data = np.ones(n_samples1 * n_neighbors)
484             A_ind = self.kneighbors(X, n_neighbors, return_distance=False)
485 
486         elif mode == 'distance':
487             A_data, A_ind = self.kneighbors(
488                 X, n_neighbors, return_distance=True)
489             A_data = np.ravel(A_data)
490 
491         else:
492             raise ValueError(
493                 'Unsupported mode, must be one of "connectivity" '
494                 'or "distance" but got "%s" instead' % mode)
495 
496         kneighbors_graph = csr_matrix((A_data, A_ind.ravel(), A_indptr),
497                                       shape=(n_samples1, n_samples2))
498 
499         return kneighbors_graph

502 class RadiusNeighborsMixin(object):
503     """Mixin for radius-based neighbors searches"""

505     def radius_neighbors(self, X=None, radius=None, return_distance=True):
506         """Finds the neighbors within a given radius of a point or points.
507 
508         Return the indices and distances of each point from the dataset
509         lying in a ball with size ``radius`` around the points of the query
510         array. Points lying on the boundary are included in the results.
511 
512         The result points are *not* necessarily sorted by distance to their
513         query point.
514 
515         Parameters
516         ----------
517         X : array-like, (n_samples, n_features), optional
518             The query point or points.
519             If not provided, neighbors of each indexed point are returned.
520             In this case, the query point is not considered its own neighbor.
521 
522         radius : float
523             Limiting distance of neighbors to return.
524             (default is the value passed to the constructor).
525 
526         return_distance : boolean, optional. Defaults to True.
527             If False, distances will not be returned
528 
529         Returns
530         -------
531         dist : array, shape (n_samples,) of arrays
532             Array representing the distances to each point, only present if
533             return_distance=True. The distance values are computed according
534             to the ``metric`` constructor parameter.
535 
536         ind : array, shape (n_samples,) of arrays
537             An array of arrays of indices of the approximate nearest points
538             from the population matrix that lie within a ball of size
539             ``radius`` around the query points.
540 
541         Examples
542         --------
543         In the following example, we construct a NeighborsClassifier
544         class from an array representing our data set and ask who's
545         the closest point to [1, 1, 1]:
546 
547         >>> import numpy as np
548         >>> samples = [[0., 0., 0.], [0., .5, 0.], [1., 1., .5]]
549         >>> from sklearn.neighbors import NearestNeighbors
550         >>> neigh = NearestNeighbors(radius=1.6)
551         >>> neigh.fit(samples) # doctest: +ELLIPSIS
552         NearestNeighbors(algorithm='auto', leaf_size=30, ...)
553         >>> rng = neigh.radius_neighbors([[1., 1., 1.]])
554         >>> print(np.asarray(rng[0][0])) # doctest: +ELLIPSIS
555         [1.5 0.5]
556         >>> print(np.asarray(rng[1][0])) # doctest: +ELLIPSIS
557         [1 2]
558 
559         The first array returned contains the distances to all points which
560         are closer than 1.6, while the second array returned contains their
561         indices.  In general, multiple points can be queried at the same time.
562 
563         Notes
564         -----
565         Because the number of neighbors of each point is not necessarily
566         equal, the results for multiple query points cannot be fit in a
567         standard data array.
568         For efficiency, `radius_neighbors` returns arrays of objects, where
569         each object is a 1D array of indices or distances.
570         """
571         check_is_fitted(self, "_fit_method")
572 
573         if X is not None:
574             query_is_train = False
575             X = check_array(X, accept_sparse='csr')
576         else:
577             query_is_train = True
578             X = self._fit_X
579 
580         if radius is None:
581             radius = self.radius
582 
583         n_samples = X.shape[0]
584         if self._fit_method == 'brute':
585             # for efficiency, use squared euclidean distances
586             if self.effective_metric_ == 'euclidean':
587                 dist = pairwise_distances(X, self._fit_X, 'euclidean',
588                                           n_jobs=self.n_jobs, squared=True)
589                 radius *= radius
590             else:
591                 dist = pairwise_distances(X, self._fit_X,
592                                           self.effective_metric_,
593                                           n_jobs=self.n_jobs,
594                                           **self.effective_metric_params_)
595 
596             neigh_ind_list = [np.where(d <= radius)[0] for d in dist]
597 
598             # See https://github.com/numpy/numpy/issues/5456
599             # if you want to understand why this is initialized this way.
600             neigh_ind = np.empty(n_samples, dtype='object')
601             neigh_ind[:] = neigh_ind_list
602 
603             if return_distance:
604                 dist_array = np.empty(n_samples, dtype='object')
605                 if self.effective_metric_ == 'euclidean':
606                     dist_list = [np.sqrt(d[neigh_ind[i]])
607                                  for i, d in enumerate(dist)]
608                 else:
609                     dist_list = [d[neigh_ind[i]]
610                                  for i, d in enumerate(dist)]
611                 dist_array[:] = dist_list
612 
613                 results = dist_array, neigh_ind
614             else:
615                 results = neigh_ind
616 
617         elif self._fit_method in ['ball_tree', 'kd_tree']:
618             if issparse(X):
619                 raise ValueError(
620                     "%s does not work with sparse matrices. Densify the data, "
621                     "or set algorithm='brute'" % self._fit_method)
622 
623             n_jobs = _get_n_jobs(self.n_jobs)
624             results = Parallel(n_jobs, backend='threading')(
625                 delayed(self._tree.query_radius, check_pickle=False)(
626                     X[s], radius, return_distance)
627                 for s in gen_even_slices(X.shape[0], n_jobs)
628             )
629             if return_distance:
630                 neigh_ind, dist = tuple(zip(*results))
631                 results = np.hstack(dist), np.hstack(neigh_ind)
632             else:
633                 results = np.hstack(results)
634         else:
635             raise ValueError("internal: _fit_method not recognized")
636 
637         if not query_is_train:
638             return results
639         else:

659     def radius_neighbors_graph(self, X=None, radius=None, mode='connectivity'):
660         """Computes the (weighted) graph of Neighbors for points in X
661 
662         Neighborhoods are restricted the points at a distance lower than
663         radius.
664 
665         Parameters
666         ----------
667         X : array-like, shape = [n_samples, n_features], optional
668             The query point or points.
669             If not provided, neighbors of each indexed point are returned.
670             In this case, the query point is not considered its own neighbor.
671 
672         radius : float
673             Radius of neighborhoods.
674             (default is the value passed to the constructor).
675 
676         mode : {'connectivity', 'distance'}, optional
677             Type of returned matrix: 'connectivity' will return the
678             connectivity matrix with ones and zeros, in 'distance' the
679             edges are Euclidean distance between points.
680 
681         Returns
682         -------
683         A : sparse matrix in CSR format, shape = [n_samples, n_samples]
684             A[i, j] is assigned the weight of edge that connects i to j.
685 
686         Examples
687         --------
688         >>> X = [[0], [3], [1]]
689         >>> from sklearn.neighbors import NearestNeighbors
690         >>> neigh = NearestNeighbors(radius=1.5)
691         >>> neigh.fit(X) # doctest: +ELLIPSIS
692         NearestNeighbors(algorithm='auto', leaf_size=30, ...)
693         >>> A = neigh.radius_neighbors_graph(X)
694         >>> A.toarray()
695         array([[1., 0., 1.],
696                [0., 1., 0.],
697                [1., 0., 1.]])
698 
699         See also
700         --------
701         kneighbors_graph
702         """
703         if X is not None:
704             X = check_array(X, accept_sparse=['csr', 'csc', 'coo'])
705 
706         n_samples2 = self._fit_X.shape[0]
707         if radius is None:
708             radius = self.radius
709 
710         # construct CSR matrix representation of the NN graph
711         if mode == 'connectivity':
712             A_ind = self.radius_neighbors(X, radius,
713                                           return_distance=False)
714             A_data = None
715         elif mode == 'distance':
716             dist, A_ind = self.radius_neighbors(X, radius,
717                                                 return_distance=True)
718             A_data = np.concatenate(list(dist))
719         else:
720             raise ValueError(
721                 'Unsupported mode, must be one of "connectivity", '
722                 'or "distance" but got %s instead' % mode)
723 
724         n_samples1 = A_ind.shape[0]
725         n_neighbors = np.array([len(a) for a in A_ind])
726         A_ind = np.concatenate(list(A_ind))
727         if A_data is None:
728             A_data = np.ones(len(A_ind))
729         A_indptr = np.concatenate((np.zeros(1, dtype=int),
730                                    np.cumsum(n_neighbors)))
731 
732         return csr_matrix((A_data, A_ind, A_indptr),
733                           shape=(n_samples1, n_samples2))

problem_statement:
Missing parameter validation in Neighbors estimator for float n_neighbors
```python
from sklearn.neighbors import NearestNeighbors
from sklearn.datasets import make_blobs
X, y = make_blobs()
neighbors = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=3.)
neighbors.fit(X)
neighbors.kneighbors(X)
```
```
~/checkout/scikit-learn/sklearn/neighbors/binary_tree.pxi in sklearn.neighbors.kd_tree.NeighborsHeap.__init__()

TypeError: 'float' object cannot be interpreted as an integer
```
This should be caught earlier and a more helpful error message should be raised (or we could be lenient and cast to integer, but I think a better error might be better).

We need to make sure that 
```python
neighbors.kneighbors(X, n_neighbors=3.)
```
also works.

@amueller I think there is a lot of other estimators and Python functions in general where dtype isn't explicitely checked and wrong dtype just raises an exception later on.

Take for instance,
```py
import numpy as np

x = np.array([1])
np.sum(x, axis=1.)
```
which produces,
```py
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
  File "lib/python3.6/site-packages/numpy/core/fromnumeric.py", line 1882, in sum
    out=out, **kwargs)
  File "lib/python3.6/site-packages/numpy/core/_methods.py", line 32, in _sum
    return umr_sum(a, axis, dtype, out, keepdims)
TypeError: 'float' object cannot be interpreted as an integer
```
so pretty much the same exception as in the original post, with no indications of what is wrong exactly. Here it's straightforward because we only provided one parameter, but the same is true for more complex constructions. 

So I'm not sure that starting to enforce int/float dtype of parameters, estimator by estimator is a solution here. In general don't think there is a need to do more parameter validation than what is done e.g. in numpy or pandas. If we want to do it, some generic type validation based on annotaitons (e.g. https://github.com/agronholm/typeguard) might be easier but also require more maintenance time and probably harder to implement while Python 2.7 is supported.

Intersection should remove duplicates
```python
>>> Intersection({1},{1},{x})
EmptySet()
>>> Intersection({1},{x})
{1}
```

The answer should be `Piecewise(({1}, Eq(x, 1)), (S.EmptySet, True))` or remain unevaluated.

The routine should give the same answer if duplicates are present; my initial guess is that duplicates should just be removed at the outset of instantiation. Ordering them will produce canonical processing.

170     def _complement(self, other):
171         # this behaves as other - self
172         if isinstance(other, ProductSet):
173             # For each set consider it or it's complement
174             # We need at least one of the sets to be complemented
175             # Consider all 2^n combinations.
176             # We can conveniently represent these options easily using a
177             # ProductSet
178 
179             # XXX: this doesn't work if the dimensions of the sets isn't same.
180             # A - B is essentially same as A if B has a different
181             # dimensionality than A
182             switch_sets = ProductSet(FiniteSet(o, o - s) for s, o in
183                                      zip(self.sets, other.sets))
184             product_sets = (ProductSet(*set) for set in switch_sets)
185             # Union of all combinations but this one
186             return Union(*(p for p in product_sets if p != other))
187 
188         elif isinstance(other, Interval):
189             if isinstance(self, Interval) or isinstance(self, FiniteSet):
190                 return Intersection(other, self.complement(S.Reals))
191 
192         elif isinstance(other, Union):
193             return Union(*(o - self for o in other.args))
194 
195         elif isinstance(other, Complement):
196             return Complement(other.args[0], Union(other.args[1], self), evaluate=False)
197 
198         elif isinstance(other, EmptySet):
199             return S.EmptySet
200 
201         elif isinstance(other, FiniteSet):
202             from sympy.utilities.iterables import sift
203 
204             sifted = sift(other, lambda x: fuzzy_bool(self.contains(x)))
205             # ignore those that are contained in self
206             return Union(FiniteSet(*(sifted[False])),
207                 Complement(FiniteSet(*(sifted[None])), self, evaluate=False)

607     """
608     Represents a Cartesian Product of Sets.
609 
610     Returns a Cartesian product given several sets as either an iterable
611     or individual arguments.
612 
613     Can use '*' operator on any sets for convenient shorthand.
614 
615     Examples
616     ========
617 
618     >>> from sympy import Interval, FiniteSet, ProductSet
619     >>> I = Interval(0, 5); S = FiniteSet(1, 2, 3)
620     >>> ProductSet(I, S)
621     Interval(0, 5) x {1, 2, 3}
622 
623     >>> (2, 2) in ProductSet(I, S)
624     True
625 
626     >>> Interval(0, 1) * Interval(0, 1) # The unit square
627     Interval(0, 1) x Interval(0, 1)
628 
629     >>> coin = FiniteSet('H', 'T')
630     >>> set(coin**2)
631     {(H, H), (H, T), (T, H), (T, T)}
632 
633 
634     Notes
635     =====
636 
637     - Passes most operations down to the argument sets
638     - Flattens Products of ProductSets
639 
640     References
641     ==========
642 
643     .. [1] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cartesian_product
644     """
645     is_ProductSet = True
646 
647     def __new__(cls, *sets, **assumptions):
648         def flatten(arg):
649             if isinstance(arg, Set):
650                 if arg.is_ProductSet:
651                     return sum(map(flatten, arg.args), [])
652                 else:
653                     return [arg]
654             elif iterable(arg):
655                 return sum(map(flatten, arg), [])
656             raise TypeError("Input must be Sets or iterables of Sets")
657         sets = flatten(list(sets))
658 
659         if EmptySet() in sets or len(sets) == 0:
660             return EmptySet()
661 
662         if len(sets) == 1:
663             return sets[0]
664 
665         return Basic.__new__(cls, *sets, **assumptions)

667     def _eval_Eq(self, other):
668         if not other.is_ProductSet:
669             return
670 
671         if len(self.args) != len(other.args):
672             return false
673 
674         return And(*(Eq(x, y) for x, y in zip(self.args, other.args)))

677         """
678         'in' operator for ProductSets

680         Examples
681         ========

683         >>> from sympy import Interval
684         >>> (2, 3) in Interval(0, 5) * Interval(0, 5)
685         True
686 
687         >>> (10, 10) in Interval(0, 5) * Interval(0, 5)
688         False
689 
690         Passes operation on to constituent sets
691         """
692         if is_sequence(element):
693             if len(element) != len(self.args):
694                 return False
695         elif len(self.args) > 1:
696             return False
697         d = [Dummy() for i in element]
698         reps = dict(zip(d, element))
699         return tfn[self.as_relational(*d).xreplace(reps)]

706         return And(*[s.contains(i) for s, i in zip(self.args, symbols)])

1105     @property
1106     def _measure(self):
1107         # Measure of a union is the sum of the measures of the sets minus
1108         # the sum of their pairwise intersections plus the sum of their
1109         # triple-wise intersections minus ... etc...
1110 
1111         # Sets is a collection of intersections and a set of elementary
1112         # sets which made up those intersections (called "sos" for set of sets)
1113         # An example element might of this list might be:
1114         #    ( {A,B,C}, A.intersect(B).intersect(C) )
1115 
1116         # Start with just elementary sets (  ({A}, A), ({B}, B), ... )
1117         # Then get and subtract (  ({A,B}, (A int B), ... ) while non-zero
1118         sets = [(FiniteSet(s), s) for s in self.args]
1119         measure = 0
1120         parity = 1
1121         while sets:
1122             # Add up the measure of these sets and add or subtract it to total
1123             measure += parity * sum(inter.measure for sos, inter in sets)
1124 
1125             # For each intersection in sets, compute the intersection with every
1126             # other set not already part of the intersection.
1127             sets = ((sos + FiniteSet(newset), newset.intersect(intersection))
1128                     for sos, intersection in sets for newset in self.args
1129                     if newset not in sos)
1130 
1131             # Clear out sets with no measure
1132             sets = [(sos, inter) for sos, inter in sets if inter.measure != 0]
1133 
1134             # Clear out duplicates
1135             sos_list = []
1136             sets_list = []
1137             for set in sets:
1138                 if set[0] in sos_list:
1139                     continue
1140                 else:
1141                     sos_list.append(set[0])
1142                     sets_list.append(set)
1143             sets = sets_list
1144 
1145             # Flip Parity - next time subtract/add if we added/subtracted here
1146             parity *= -1
1147         return measure

1155                 if j != i:

1157             return b
1158         return Union(*map(boundary_of_set, range(len(self.args))))

1196     def __iter__(self):
1197         import itertools
1198 
1199         # roundrobin recipe taken from itertools documentation:
1200         # https://docs.python.org/2/library/itertools.html#recipes
1201         def roundrobin(*iterables):
1202             "roundrobin('ABC', 'D', 'EF') --> A D E B F C"
1203             # Recipe credited to George Sakkis
1204             pending = len(iterables)
1205             if PY3:
1206                 nexts = itertools.cycle(iter(it).__next__ for it in iterables)
1207             else:
1208                 nexts = itertools.cycle(iter(it).next for it in iterables)
1209             while pending:
1210                 try:
1211                     for next in nexts:
1212                         yield next()
1213                 except StopIteration:
1214                     pending -= 1
1215                     nexts = itertools.cycle(itertools.islice(nexts, pending))
1216 
1217         if all(set.is_iterable for set in self.args):
1218             return roundrobin(*(iter(arg) for arg in self.args))
1219         else:
1220             raise TypeError("Not all constituent sets are iterable")

1315     @staticmethod
1316     def _handle_finite_sets(args):
1317         from sympy.core.logic import fuzzy_and, fuzzy_bool
1318         from sympy.core.compatibility import zip_longest
1319 
1320         fs_args, other = sift(args, lambda x: x.is_FiniteSet,
1321             binary=True)
1322         if not fs_args:
1323             return
1324         fs_args.sort(key=len)
1325         s = fs_args[0]
1326         fs_args = fs_args[1:]
1327 
1328         res = []
1329         unk = []
1330         for x in s:
1331             c = fuzzy_and(fuzzy_bool(o.contains(x))
1332                 for o in fs_args + other)
1333             if c:
1334                 res.append(x)
1335             elif c is None:
1336                 unk.append(x)
1337             else:
1338                 pass  # drop arg
1339 
1340         res = FiniteSet(
1341             *res, evaluate=False) if res else S.EmptySet
1342         if unk:
1343             symbolic_s_list = [x for x in s if x.has(Symbol)]
1344             non_symbolic_s = s - FiniteSet(
1345                 *symbolic_s_list, evaluate=False)
1346             while fs_args:
1347                 v = fs_args.pop()
1348                 if all(i == j for i, j in zip_longest(
1349                         symbolic_s_list,
1350                         (x for x in v if x.has(Symbol)))):
1351                     # all the symbolic elements of `v` are the same
1352                     # as in `s` so remove the non-symbol containing
1353                     # expressions from `unk`, since they cannot be
1354                     # contained
1355                     for x in non_symbolic_s:
1356                         if x in unk:
1357                             unk.remove(x)
1358                 else:
1359                     # if only a subset of elements in `s` are
1360                     # contained in `v` then remove them from `v`
1361                     # and add this as a new arg
1362                     contained = [x for x in symbolic_s_list
1363                         if sympify(v.contains(x)) is S.true]
1364                     if contained != symbolic_s_list:
1365                         other.append(
1366                             v - FiniteSet(
1367                             *contained, evaluate=False))
1368                     else:
1369                         pass  # for coverage
1370 
1371             other_sets = Intersection(*other)
1372             if not other_sets:
1373                 return S.EmptySet  # b/c we use evaluate=False below
1374             elif other_sets == S.UniversalSet:
1375                 res += FiniteSet(*unk)
1376             else:
1377                 res += Intersection(
1378                     FiniteSet(*unk),
1379                     other_sets, evaluate=False)
1380         return res
1381

1383         """Rewrite an Intersection in terms of equalities and logic operators"""
1384         return And(*[set.as_relational(symbol) for set in self.args])

+import copy

+

+
+

problem_statement:
Generate man page section directories
**Current man page generation does not conform to `MANPATH` search functionality**
Currently, all generated man pages are placed in to a single-level directory: `<build-dir>/man`. Unfortunately, this cannot be used in combination with the unix `MANPATH` environment variable. The `man` program explicitly looks for man pages in section directories (such as `man/man1`, etc.). 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
It would be great if sphinx would automatically create the section directories (e.g., `man/man1/`, `man/man3/`, etc.) and place each generated man page within appropriate section.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
This problem can be over come within our project’s build system, ensuring the built man pages are installed in a correct location, but it would be nice if the build directory had the proper layout.

I’m happy to take a crack at implementing a fix, though this change in behavior may break some people who expect everything to appear in a `man/` directory.
hints_text:
I think that users should copy the generated man file to the appropriate directory. The build directory is not an appropriate directory to manage man pages. So no section directory is needed, AFAIK. I don't know why do you want to set `MANPATH` to the output directory. To check the output, you can give the path to the man file for man command like `man _build/man/sphinx-build.1`. Please let me know your purpose in detail.
From a [separate github thread](https://github.com/flux-framework/flux-core/pull/3033#issuecomment-662515605) that describes the specific use case in some more detail:
> When run in a builddir, `src/cmd/flux` sets `MANPATH` such that `man flux` will display the current builddir version of `flux.1`. This is done so that documentation matches the version of Flux being run.

Essentially, we are trying to make running in-tree look as similar to running an installed version as possible.

---

> I think that users should copy the generated man file to the appropriate directory.

On `make install`, we do have the automake setup to copy the manpages to `$prefix/man/man1`, `$prefix/man/man3`, etc.  This did require some extra work though, since each source file and its destination has to be explicitly enumerated in the automake file.  If the man pages were built into their respective sections, a recursive copy would work too.  Not a huge deal, but just another factor I wanted to bring up.
Understandable. +1 to change the structure of output directory. As commented, it causes a breaking change for users. So I propose you to add a configuration `man_make_section_directory = (True | False)` for migration. During 3.x, it defaults to False, and it will default to True on 4.0 release. What do you think?

>I’m happy to take a crack at implementing a fix, though this change in behavior may break some people who expect everything to appear in a man/ directory.

It would be very nice if you send us a PR :-)

135     def __init__(self, verbose_name=None, name=None, primary_key=False,
136                  max_length=None, unique=False, blank=False, null=False,
137                  db_index=False, rel=None, default=NOT_PROVIDED, editable=True,
138                  serialize=True, unique_for_date=None, unique_for_month=None,
139                  unique_for_year=None, choices=None, help_text='', db_column=None,
140                  db_tablespace=None, auto_created=False, validators=(),
141                  error_messages=None):

143         self.verbose_name = verbose_name  # May be set by set_attributes_from_name
144         self._verbose_name = verbose_name  # Store original for deconstruction
145         self.primary_key = primary_key

147         self.blank, self.null = blank, null
148         self.remote_field = rel

154         self.unique_for_month = unique_for_month

156         if isinstance(choices, collections.abc.Iterator):
157             choices = list(choices)

161         self.db_column = db_column

165         # Adjust the appropriate creation counter, and save our local copy.
166         if auto_created:
167             self.creation_counter = Field.auto_creation_counter

169         else:
170             self.creation_counter = Field.creation_counter
171             Field.creation_counter += 1

173         self._validators = list(validators)  # Store for deconstruction later
174 
175         messages = {}

177             messages.update(getattr(c, 'default_error_messages', {}))

212     def _check_field_name(self):
213         """
214         Check if field name is valid, i.e. 1) does not end with an
215         underscore, 2) does not contain "__" and 3) is not "pk".
216         """
217         if self.name.endswith('_'):
218             return [
219                 checks.Error(
220                     'Field names must not end with an underscore.',
221                     obj=self,
222                     id='fields.E001',
223                 )
224             ]
225         elif LOOKUP_SEP in self.name:
226             return [
227                 checks.Error(
228                     'Field names must not contain "%s".' % (LOOKUP_SEP,),
229                     obj=self,
230                     id='fields.E002',
231                 )
232             ]
233         elif self.name == 'pk':
234             return [
235                 checks.Error(
236                     "'pk' is a reserved word that cannot be used as a field name.",
237                     obj=self,
238                     id='fields.E003',
239                 )
240             ]
241         else:
242             return []
243 
244     def _check_choices(self):
245         if not self.choices:
246             return []
247 
248         def is_value(value, accept_promise=True):
249             return isinstance(value, (str, Promise) if accept_promise else str) or not is_iterable(value)
250 
251         if is_value(self.choices, accept_promise=False):
252             return [
253                 checks.Error(
254                     "'choices' must be an iterable (e.g., a list or tuple).",
255                     obj=self,
256                     id='fields.E004',
257                 )
258             ]
259 
260         # Expect [group_name, [value, display]]
261         for choices_group in self.choices:
262             try:
263                 group_name, group_choices = choices_group
264             except (TypeError, ValueError):
265                 # Containing non-pairs
266                 break
267             try:
268                 if not all(
269                     is_value(value) and is_value(human_name)
270                     for value, human_name in group_choices
271                 ):
272                     break
273             except (TypeError, ValueError):
274                 # No groups, choices in the form [value, display]
275                 value, human_name = group_name, group_choices
276                 if not is_value(value) or not is_value(human_name):
277                     break
278 
279             # Special case: choices=['ab']
280             if isinstance(choices_group, str):
281                 break
282         else:
283             return []
284 
285         return [
286             checks.Error(
287                 "'choices' must be an iterable containing "
288                 "(actual value, human readable name) tuples.",
289                 obj=self,
290                 id='fields.E005',
291             )
292         ]
293

298                     "'db_index' must be None, True or False.",
299                     obj=self,
300                     id='fields.E006',
301                 )
302             ]
303         else:
304             return []

400     def deconstruct(self):
401         """
402         Return enough information to recreate the field as a 4-tuple:
403 
404          * The name of the field on the model, if contribute_to_class() has
405            been run.
406          * The import path of the field, including the class:e.g.
407            django.db.models.IntegerField This should be the most portable
408            version, so less specific may be better.
409          * A list of positional arguments.
410          * A dict of keyword arguments.
411 
412         Note that the positional or keyword arguments must contain values of
413         the following types (including inner values of collection types):
414 
415          * None, bool, str, int, float, complex, set, frozenset, list, tuple,
416            dict
417          * UUID
418          * datetime.datetime (naive), datetime.date
419          * top-level classes, top-level functions - will be referenced by their
420            full import path
421          * Storage instances - these have their own deconstruct() method
422 
423         This is because the values here must be serialized into a text format
424         (possibly new Python code, possibly JSON) and these are the only types
425         with encoding handlers defined.
426 
427         There's no need to return the exact way the field was instantiated this
428         time, just ensure that the resulting field is the same - prefer keyword
429         arguments over positional ones, and omit parameters with their default
430         values.
431         """
432         # Short-form way of fetching all the default parameters
433         keywords = {}
434         possibles = {
435             "verbose_name": None,
436             "primary_key": False,
437             "max_length": None,
438             "unique": False,
439             "blank": False,
440             "null": False,
441             "db_index": False,
442             "default": NOT_PROVIDED,
443             "editable": True,
444             "serialize": True,
445             "unique_for_date": None,
446             "unique_for_month": None,
447             "unique_for_year": None,
448             "choices": None,
449             "help_text": '',
450             "db_column": None,
451             "db_tablespace": None,
452             "auto_created": False,
453             "validators": [],
454             "error_messages": None,
455         }
456         attr_overrides = {
457             "unique": "_unique",
458             "error_messages": "_error_messages",
459             "validators": "_validators",
460             "verbose_name": "_verbose_name",
461             "db_tablespace": "_db_tablespace",
462         }
463         equals_comparison = {"choices", "validators"}
464         for name, default in possibles.items():
465             value = getattr(self, attr_overrides.get(name, name))
466             # Unroll anything iterable for choices into a concrete list
467             if name == "choices" and isinstance(value, collections.abc.Iterable):
468                 value = list(value)
469             # Do correct kind of comparison
470             if name in equals_comparison:
471                 if value != default:
472                     keywords[name] = value
473             else:
474                 if value is not default:
475                     keywords[name] = value
476         # Work out path - we shorten it for known Django core fields
477         path = "%s.%s" % (self.__class__.__module__, self.__class__.__qualname__)
478         if path.startswith("django.db.models.fields.related"):
479             path = path.replace("django.db.models.fields.related", "django.db.models")
480         elif path.startswith("django.db.models.fields.files"):
481             path = path.replace("django.db.models.fields.files", "django.db.models")
482         elif path.startswith("django.db.models.fields.proxy"):
483             path = path.replace("django.db.models.fields.proxy", "django.db.models")
484         elif path.startswith("django.db.models.fields"):
485             path = path.replace("django.db.models.fields", "django.db.models")
486         # Return basic info - other fields should override this.
487         return (self.name, path, [], keywords)
488 
489     def clone(self):

491         Uses deconstruct() to clone a new copy of this Field.
492         Will not preserve any class attachments/attribute names.
493         """
494         name, path, args, kwargs = self.deconstruct()
495         return self.__class__(*args, **kwargs)

512     def __deepcopy__(self, memodict):
513         # We don't have to deepcopy very much here, since most things are not
514         # intended to be altered after initial creation.
515         obj = copy.copy(self)
516         if self.remote_field:
517             obj.remote_field = copy.copy(self.remote_field)
518             if hasattr(self.remote_field, 'field') and self.remote_field.field is self:
519                 obj.remote_field.field = obj

531     def __reduce__(self):
532         """
533         Pickling should return the model._meta.fields instance of the field,
534         not a new copy of that field. So, use the app registry to load the
535         model and then the field back.
536         """
537         if not hasattr(self, 'model'):
538             # Fields are sometimes used without attaching them to models (for
539             # example in aggregation). In this case give back a plain field
540             # instance. The code below will create a new empty instance of
541             # class self.__class__, then update its dict with self.__dict__
542             # values - so, this is very close to normal pickle.
543             state = self.__dict__.copy()
544             # The _get_default cached_property can't be pickled due to lambda
545             # usage.
546             state.pop('_get_default', None)
547             return _empty, (self.__class__,), state
548         return _load_field, (self.model._meta.app_label, self.model._meta.object_name,
549                              self.name)

562     def to_python(self, value):
563         """
564         Convert the input value into the expected Python data type, raising
565         django.core.exceptions.ValidationError if the data can't be converted.
566         Return the converted value. Subclasses should override this.

570     @cached_property
571     def validators(self):
572         """
573         Some validators can't be created at field initialization time.
574         This method provides a way to delay their creation until required.
575         """
576         return [*self.default_validators, *self._validators]

578     def run_validators(self, value):
579         if value in self.empty_values:
580             return
581 
582         errors = []
583         for v in self.validators:
584             try:
585                 v(value)
586             except exceptions.ValidationError as e:
587                 if hasattr(e, 'code') and e.code in self.error_messages:
588                     e.message = self.error_messages[e.code]
589                 errors.extend(e.error_list)
590 
591         if errors:
592             raise exceptions.ValidationError(errors)
593 
594     def validate(self, value, model_instance):
595         """
596         Validate value and raise ValidationError if necessary. Subclasses
597         should override this to provide validation logic.
598         """
599         if not self.editable:
600             # Skip validation for non-editable fields.
601             return
602 
603         if self.choices is not None and value not in self.empty_values:
604             for option_key, option_value in self.choices:
605                 if isinstance(option_value, (list, tuple)):
606                     # This is an optgroup, so look inside the group for
607                     # options.
608                     for optgroup_key, optgroup_value in option_value:
609                         if value == optgroup_key:
610                             return
611                 elif value == option_key:
612                     return
613             raise exceptions.ValidationError(
614                 self.error_messages['invalid_choice'],
615                 code='invalid_choice',
616                 params={'value': value},
617             )
618 
619         if value is None and not self.null:
620             raise exceptions.ValidationError(self.error_messages['null'], code='null')
621 
622         if not self.blank and value in self.empty_values:
623             raise exceptions.ValidationError(self.error_messages['blank'], code='blank')
624 
625     def clean(self, value, model_instance):
626         """
627         Convert the value's type and run validation. Validation errors
628         from to_python() and validate() are propagated. Return the correct
629         value if no error is raised.
630         """
631         value = self.to_python(value)
632         self.validate(value, model_instance)
633         self.run_validators(value)
634         return value

639     def db_check(self, connection):
640         """
641         Return the database column check constraint for this field, for the
642         provided connection. Works the same way as db_type() for the case that
643         get_internal_type() does not map to a preexisting model field.
644         """
645         data = self.db_type_parameters(connection)
646         try:
647             return connection.data_type_check_constraints[self.get_internal_type()] % data
648         except KeyError:
649             return None

651     def db_type(self, connection):
652         """
653         Return the database column data type for this field, for the provided
654         connection.
655         """
656         # The default implementation of this method looks at the
657         # backend-specific data_types dictionary, looking up the field by its
658         # "internal type".
659         #
660         # A Field class can implement the get_internal_type() method to specify
661         # which *preexisting* Django Field class it's most similar to -- i.e.,
662         # a custom field might be represented by a TEXT column type, which is
663         # the same as the TextField Django field type, which means the custom
664         # field's get_internal_type() returns 'TextField'.
665         #
666         # But the limitation of the get_internal_type() / data_types approach
667         # is that it cannot handle database column types that aren't already
668         # mapped to one of the built-in Django field types. In this case, you
669         # can implement db_type() instead of get_internal_type() to specify
670         # exactly which wacky database column type you want to use.
671         data = self.db_type_parameters(connection)
672         try:
673             return connection.data_types[self.get_internal_type()] % data
674         except KeyError:
675             return None
676 
677     def rel_db_type(self, connection):
678         """
679         Return the data type that a related field pointing to this field should
680         use. For example, this method is called by ForeignKey and OneToOneField
681         to determine its data type.
682         """
683         return self.db_type(connection)

685     def cast_db_type(self, connection):
686         """Return the data type to use in the Cast() function."""
687         db_type = connection.ops.cast_data_types.get(self.get_internal_type())
688         if db_type:
689             return db_type % self.db_type_parameters(connection)
690         return self.db_type(connection)

692     def db_parameters(self, connection):
693         """
694         Extension of db_type(), providing a range of different return values
695         (type, checks). This will look at db_type(), allowing custom model
696         fields to override it.
697         """
698         type_string = self.db_type(connection)
699         check_string = self.db_check(connection)
700         return {
701             "type": type_string,
702             "check": check_string,
703         }

728     def contribute_to_class(self, cls, name, private_only=False):
729         """
730         Register the field with the model class it belongs to.
731 
732         If private_only is True, create a separate instance of this field
733         for every subclass of cls, even if cls is not an abstract model.
734         """
735         self.set_attributes_from_name(name)
736         self.model = cls
737         cls._meta.add_field(self, private=private_only)
738         if self.column:
739             # Don't override classmethods with the descriptor. This means that
740             # if you have a classmethod and a field with the same name, then
741             # such fields can't be deferred (we don't have a check for this).
742             if not getattr(cls, self.attname, None):
743                 setattr(cls, self.attname, self.descriptor_class(self))
744         if self.choices is not None:
745             setattr(cls, 'get_%s_display' % self.name,
746                     partialmethod(cls._get_FIELD_display, field=self))

753         return {self.name: getattr(obj, self.attname)}

Add check to ensure max_length fits longest choice.
Description
	
There is currently no check to ensure that Field.max_length is large enough to fit the longest value in Field.choices.
This would be very helpful as often this mistake is not noticed until an attempt is made to save a record with those values that are too long.

+                if self.max_length is not None and group_choices:

                 # No groups, choices in the form [value, display]

+                if self.max_length is not None and isinstance(value, str):

You will be provided with a partial code base and an issue statement explaining a problem to resolve.
<issue>
NCA fails in GridSearch due to too strict parameter checks
NCA checks its parameters to have a specific type, which can easily fail in a GridSearch due to how param grid is made.

Here is an example:
```python
import numpy as np

from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.model_selection import GridSearchCV
from sklearn.neighbors import NeighborhoodComponentsAnalysis
from sklearn.neighbors import KNeighborsClassifier

X = np.random.random_sample((100, 10))
y = np.random.randint(2, size=100)

nca = NeighborhoodComponentsAnalysis()
knn = KNeighborsClassifier()

pipe = Pipeline([('nca', nca),
                 ('knn', knn)])
                
params = {'nca__tol': [0.1, 0.5, 1],
          'nca__n_components': np.arange(1, 10)}
          
gs = GridSearchCV(estimator=pipe, param_grid=params, error_score='raise')
gs.fit(X,y)
```

The issue is that for `tol`: 1 is not a float, and for  `n_components`: np.int64 is not int

Before proposing a fix for this specific situation, I'd like to have your general opinion about parameter checking.  
I like this idea of common parameter checking tool introduced with the NCA PR. What do you think about extending it across the code-base (or at least for new or recent estimators) ?

Currently parameter checking is not always done or often partially done, and is quite redundant. For instance, here is the input validation of lda:
```python
def _check_params(self):
        """Check model parameters."""
        if self.n_components <= 0:
            raise ValueError("Invalid 'n_components' parameter: %r"
                             % self.n_components)

        if self.total_samples <= 0:
            raise ValueError("Invalid 'total_samples' parameter: %r"
                             % self.total_samples)

        if self.learning_offset < 0:
            raise ValueError("Invalid 'learning_offset' parameter: %r"
                             % self.learning_offset)

        if self.learning_method not in ("batch", "online"):
            raise ValueError("Invalid 'learning_method' parameter: %r"
                             % self.learning_method)
```
most params aren't checked and for those who are there's a lot of duplicated code.

A propose to be upgrade the new tool to be able to check open/closed intervals (currently only closed) and list membership.

The api would be something like that:
```
check_param(param, name, valid_options)
```
where valid_options would be a dict of `type: constraint`. e.g for the `beta_loss` param of `NMF`, it can be either a float or a string in a list, which would give
```
valid_options = {numbers.Real: None,  # None for no constraint
                 str: ['frobenius', 'kullback-leibler', 'itakura-saito']}
```
Sometimes a parameter can only be positive or within a given interval, e.g. `l1_ratio` of `LogisticRegression` must be between 0 and 1, which would give
```
valid_options = {numbers.Real: Interval(0, 1, closed='both')}
```
positivity of e.g. `max_iter` would be `numbers.Integral: Interval(left=1)`.

</issue>

12 from warnings import warn
13 import numpy as np
14 import sys
15 import time
16 from scipy.optimize import minimize
17 from ..utils.extmath import softmax
18 from ..metrics import pairwise_distances
19 from ..base import BaseEstimator, TransformerMixin
20 from ..preprocessing import LabelEncoder
21 from ..decomposition import PCA
22 from ..utils.multiclass import check_classification_targets
23 from ..utils.random import check_random_state
24 from ..utils.validation import (check_is_fitted, check_array, check_X_y,

29 class NeighborhoodComponentsAnalysis(BaseEstimator, TransformerMixin):
30     """Neighborhood Components Analysis
31 
32     Neighborhood Component Analysis (NCA) is a machine learning algorithm for
33     metric learning. It learns a linear transformation in a supervised fashion
34     to improve the classification accuracy of a stochastic nearest neighbors
35     rule in the transformed space.
36 
37     Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <nca>`.
38 
39     Parameters
40     ----------
41     n_components : int, optional (default=None)
42         Preferred dimensionality of the projected space.
43         If None it will be set to ``n_features``.
44 
45     init : string or numpy array, optional (default='auto')
46         Initialization of the linear transformation. Possible options are
47         'auto', 'pca', 'lda', 'identity', 'random', and a numpy array of shape
48         (n_features_a, n_features_b).
49 
50         'auto'
51             Depending on ``n_components``, the most reasonable initialization
52             will be chosen. If ``n_components <= n_classes`` we use 'lda', as
53             it uses labels information. If not, but
54             ``n_components < min(n_features, n_samples)``, we use 'pca', as
55             it projects data in meaningful directions (those of higher
56             variance). Otherwise, we just use 'identity'.
57 
58         'pca'
59             ``n_components`` principal components of the inputs passed
60             to :meth:`fit` will be used to initialize the transformation.
61             (See `decomposition.PCA`)
62 
63         'lda'
64             ``min(n_components, n_classes)`` most discriminative
65             components of the inputs passed to :meth:`fit` will be used to
66             initialize the transformation. (If ``n_components > n_classes``,
67             the rest of the components will be zero.) (See
68             `discriminant_analysis.LinearDiscriminantAnalysis`)
69 
70         'identity'
71             If ``n_components`` is strictly smaller than the
72             dimensionality of the inputs passed to :meth:`fit`, the identity
73             matrix will be truncated to the first ``n_components`` rows.
74 
75         'random'
76             The initial transformation will be a random array of shape
77             `(n_components, n_features)`. Each value is sampled from the
78             standard normal distribution.
79 
80         numpy array
81             n_features_b must match the dimensionality of the inputs passed to
82             :meth:`fit` and n_features_a must be less than or equal to that.
83             If ``n_components`` is not None, n_features_a must match it.
84 
85     warm_start : bool, optional, (default=False)
86         If True and :meth:`fit` has been called before, the solution of the
87         previous call to :meth:`fit` is used as the initial linear
88         transformation (``n_components`` and ``init`` will be ignored).
89 
90     max_iter : int, optional (default=50)
91         Maximum number of iterations in the optimization.
92 
93     tol : float, optional (default=1e-5)
94         Convergence tolerance for the optimization.
95 
96     callback : callable, optional (default=None)
97         If not None, this function is called after every iteration of the
98         optimizer, taking as arguments the current solution (flattened
99         transformation matrix) and the number of iterations. This might be
100         useful in case one wants to examine or store the transformation
101         found after each iteration.
102 
103     verbose : int, optional (default=0)
104         If 0, no progress messages will be printed.
105         If 1, progress messages will be printed to stdout.
106         If > 1, progress messages will be printed and the ``disp``
107         parameter of :func:`scipy.optimize.minimize` will be set to
108         ``verbose - 2``.
109 
110     random_state : int or numpy.RandomState or None, optional (default=None)
111         A pseudo random number generator object or a seed for it if int. If
112         ``init='random'``, ``random_state`` is used to initialize the random
113         transformation. If ``init='pca'``, ``random_state`` is passed as an
114         argument to PCA when initializing the transformation.
115 
116     Attributes
117     ----------
118     components_ : array, shape (n_components, n_features)
119         The linear transformation learned during fitting.
120 
121     n_iter_ : int
122         Counts the number of iterations performed by the optimizer.
123 
124     Examples
125     --------
126     >>> from sklearn.neighbors.nca import NeighborhoodComponentsAnalysis
127     >>> from sklearn.neighbors import KNeighborsClassifier
128     >>> from sklearn.datasets import load_iris
129     >>> from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
130     >>> X, y = load_iris(return_X_y=True)
131     >>> X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y,
132     ... stratify=y, test_size=0.7, random_state=42)
133     >>> nca = NeighborhoodComponentsAnalysis(random_state=42)
134     >>> nca.fit(X_train, y_train)
135     NeighborhoodComponentsAnalysis(...)
136     >>> knn = KNeighborsClassifier(n_neighbors=3)
137     >>> knn.fit(X_train, y_train)
138     KNeighborsClassifier(...)
139     >>> print(knn.score(X_test, y_test))
140     0.933333...
141     >>> knn.fit(nca.transform(X_train), y_train)
142     KNeighborsClassifier(...)
143     >>> print(knn.score(nca.transform(X_test), y_test))
144     0.961904...
145 
146     References
147     ----------
148     .. [1] J. Goldberger, G. Hinton, S. Roweis, R. Salakhutdinov.
149            "Neighbourhood Components Analysis". Advances in Neural Information
150            Processing Systems. 17, 513-520, 2005.
151            http://www.cs.nyu.edu/~roweis/papers/ncanips.pdf
152 
153     .. [2] Wikipedia entry on Neighborhood Components Analysis
154            https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neighbourhood_components_analysis
155 
156     """
157 
158     def __init__(self, n_components=None, init='auto', warm_start=False,
159                  max_iter=50, tol=1e-5, callback=None, verbose=0,
160                  random_state=None):
161         self.n_components = n_components
162         self.init = init
163         self.warm_start = warm_start
164         self.max_iter = max_iter
165         self.tol = tol
166         self.callback = callback
167         self.verbose = verbose
168         self.random_state = random_state
169 
170     def fit(self, X, y):
171         """Fit the model according to the given training data.
172 
173         Parameters
174         ----------
175         X : array-like, shape (n_samples, n_features)
176             The training samples.
177 
178         y : array-like, shape (n_samples,)
179             The corresponding training labels.
180 
181         Returns
182         -------
183         self : object
184             returns a trained NeighborhoodComponentsAnalysis model.
185         """
186 
187         # Verify inputs X and y and NCA parameters, and transform a copy if
188         # needed
189         X, y, init = self._validate_params(X, y)
190 
191         # Initialize the random generator
192         self.random_state_ = check_random_state(self.random_state)
193 
194         # Measure the total training time
195         t_train = time.time()
196 
197         # Compute a mask that stays fixed during optimization:
198         same_class_mask = y[:, np.newaxis] == y[np.newaxis, :]
199         # (n_samples, n_samples)
200 
201         # Initialize the transformation
202         transformation = self._initialize(X, y, init)
203 
204         # Create a dictionary of parameters to be passed to the optimizer
205         disp = self.verbose - 2 if self.verbose > 1 else -1
206         optimizer_params = {'method': 'L-BFGS-B',
207                             'fun': self._loss_grad_lbfgs,
208                             'args': (X, same_class_mask, -1.0),
209                             'jac': True,
210                             'x0': transformation,
211                             'tol': self.tol,
212                             'options': dict(maxiter=self.max_iter, disp=disp),
213                             'callback': self._callback
214                             }
215 
216         # Call the optimizer
217         self.n_iter_ = 0
218         opt_result = minimize(**optimizer_params)
219 
220         # Reshape the solution found by the optimizer
221         self.components_ = opt_result.x.reshape(-1, X.shape[1])
222 
223         # Stop timer
224         t_train = time.time() - t_train
225         if self.verbose:
226             cls_name = self.__class__.__name__
227 
228             # Warn the user if the algorithm did not converge
229             if not opt_result.success:
230                 warn('[{}] NCA did not converge: {}'.format(
231                     cls_name, opt_result.message),
232                      ConvergenceWarning)
233 
234             print('[{}] Training took {:8.2f}s.'.format(cls_name, t_train))
235 
236         return self
237 
238     def transform(self, X):
239         """Applies the learned transformation to the given data.
240 
241         Parameters
242         ----------
243         X : array-like, shape (n_samples, n_features)
244             Data samples.
245 
246         Returns
247         -------
248         X_embedded: array, shape (n_samples, n_components)
249             The data samples transformed.
250 
251         Raises
252         ------
253         NotFittedError
254             If :meth:`fit` has not been called before.
255         """
256 
257         check_is_fitted(self, ['components_'])
258         X = check_array(X)
259 
260         return np.dot(X, self.components_.T)
261 
262     def _validate_params(self, X, y):
263         """Validate parameters as soon as :meth:`fit` is called.
264 
265         Parameters
266         ----------
267         X : array-like, shape (n_samples, n_features)
268             The training samples.
269 
270         y : array-like, shape (n_samples,)
271             The corresponding training labels.
272 
273         Returns
274         -------
275         X : array, shape (n_samples, n_features)
276             The validated training samples.
277 
278         y : array, shape (n_samples,)
279             The validated training labels, encoded to be integers in
280             the range(0, n_classes).
281 
282         init : string or numpy array of shape (n_features_a, n_features_b)
283             The validated initialization of the linear transformation.
284 
285         Raises
286         -------
287         TypeError
288             If a parameter is not an instance of the desired type.
289 
290         ValueError
291             If a parameter's value violates its legal value range or if the
292             combination of two or more given parameters is incompatible.
293         """
294 
295         # Validate the inputs X and y, and converts y to numerical classes.
296         X, y = check_X_y(X, y, ensure_min_samples=2)
297         check_classification_targets(y)
298         y = LabelEncoder().fit_transform(y)
299 
300         # Check the preferred dimensionality of the projected space
301         if self.n_components is not None:
302             check_scalar(self.n_components, 'n_components', int, 1)
303 
304             if self.n_components > X.shape[1]:
305                 raise ValueError('The preferred dimensionality of the '
306                                  'projected space `n_components` ({}) cannot '
307                                  'be greater than the given data '
308                                  'dimensionality ({})!'
309                                  .format(self.n_components, X.shape[1]))
310 
311         # If warm_start is enabled, check that the inputs are consistent
312         check_scalar(self.warm_start, 'warm_start', bool)
313         if self.warm_start and hasattr(self, 'components_'):
314             if self.components_.shape[1] != X.shape[1]:
315                 raise ValueError('The new inputs dimensionality ({}) does not '
316                                  'match the input dimensionality of the '
317                                  'previously learned transformation ({}).'
318                                  .format(X.shape[1],
319                                          self.components_.shape[1]))
320 
321         check_scalar(self.max_iter, 'max_iter', int, 1)
322         check_scalar(self.tol, 'tol', float, 0.)

422                 elif init == 'lda':

442             The solution computed by the optimizer in this iteration.
