Thanks for the report! Unfortunately I can't reproduce this. What version of numpy are you using when the warning appears?
Sorry, forgot to mention that you need to enable the warnings during normal execution, e.g., `python -W always <file>.py`. In my case, the warnings are issued during `pytest` run which seems to activate these warnings by default.

As for the NumPy version, I'm running
```console
$ python -c 'import numpy; print(numpy.__version__)'
1.24.0
```
Thanks, I can now reproduce 😄 
The problem is that there are three more values, that are by default out of range in this case, to note specific cases:
https://github.com/matplotlib/matplotlib/blob/8d2329ad89120410d7ef04faddba2c51db743b06/lib/matplotlib/colors.py#L673-L675
(N = 256 by default)

These are then assigned to out-of-range and masked/bad values here:
https://github.com/matplotlib/matplotlib/blob/8d2329ad89120410d7ef04faddba2c51db743b06/lib/matplotlib/colors.py#L730-L732
which now raises a deprecation warning.

I think that one way forward would be to check the type of `xa` for int/uint and in that case take modulo the maximum value for `self._i_over` etc. This is basically what happens now anyway, but we need to do it explicitly rather than relying on numpy doing it. (I cannot really see how this makes sense from a color perspective, but we will at least keep the current behavior.)
I think this is exposing a real bug that we need to promote the input data to be bigger than uint8.  What we are doing here is buildin a lookup up table, the first N entries are for for values into the actually color map and then the next 3 entries are the special cases for over/under/bad so `xa` needs to be big enough to hold `self.N + 2` as values.
I don't know if this is a bigger bug or not, but I would like us to have fixed any deprecation warnings from dependencies before 3.7 is out (or if necessary a quick 3.7.1.)

179 Brief History
180 -------------
181 
182 SymPy was started by Ondřej Čertík in 2005, he wrote some code during the
183 summer, then he wrote some more code during the summer 2006. In February 2007,
184 Fabian Pedregosa joined the project and helped fixed many things, contributed
185 documentation and made it alive again. 5 students (Mateusz Paprocki, Brian
186 Jorgensen, Jason Gedge, Robert Schwarz and Chris Wu) improved SymPy incredibly
187 during the summer 2007 as part of the Google Summer of Code. Pearu Peterson
188 joined the development during the summer 2007 and he has made SymPy much more
189 competitive by rewriting the core from scratch, that has made it from 10x to
190 100x faster. Jurjen N.E. Bos has contributed pretty printing and other patches.
191 Fredrik Johansson has written mpmath and contributed a lot of patches.
192 
193 SymPy has participated in every Google Summer of Code since 2007. You can see
194 https://github.com/sympy/sympy/wiki#google-summer-of-code for full details.
195 Each year has improved SymPy by bounds. Most of SymPy's development has come
196 from Google Summer of Code students.
197 
198 In 2011, Ondřej Čertík stepped down as lead developer, with Aaron Meurer, who
199 also started as a Google Summer of Code student, taking his place. Ondřej
200 Čertík is still active in the community, but is too busy with work and family
201 to play a lead development role.
202 
203 Since then, a lot more people have joined the development and some people have
204 also left. You can see the full list in doc/src/aboutus.rst, or online at:
205 
206 http://docs.sympy.org/dev/aboutus.html#sympy-development-team
207 
208 The git history goes back to 2007, when development moved from svn to hg.  To

38 def comp(z1, z2, tol=None):
39     """Return a bool indicating whether the error between z1 and z2 is <= tol.
40 
41     If ``tol`` is None then True will be returned if there is a significant
42     difference between the numbers: ``abs(z1 - z2)*10**p <= 1/2`` where ``p``
43     is the lower of the precisions of the values. A comparison of strings will
44     be made if ``z1`` is a Number and a) ``z2`` is a string or b) ``tol`` is ''
45     and ``z2`` is a Number.
46 
47     When ``tol`` is a nonzero value, if z2 is non-zero and ``|z1| > 1``
48     the error is normalized by ``|z1|``, so if you want to see if the
49     absolute error between ``z1`` and ``z2`` is <= ``tol`` then call this
50     as ``comp(z1 - z2, 0, tol)``.
51     """
52     if type(z2) is str:
53         if not isinstance(z1, Number):
54             raise ValueError('when z2 is a str z1 must be a Number')
55         return str(z1) == z2
56     if not z1:
57         z1, z2 = z2, z1
58     if not z1:
59         return True
60     if not tol:
61         if tol is None:
62             if type(z2) is str and getattr(z1, 'is_Number', False):
63                 return str(z1) == z2
64             a, b = Float(z1), Float(z2)
65             return int(abs(a - b)*10**prec_to_dps(
66                 min(a._prec, b._prec)))*2 <= 1
67         elif all(getattr(i, 'is_Number', False) for i in (z1, z2)):
68             return z1._prec == z2._prec and str(z1) == str(z2)
69         raise ValueError('exact comparison requires two Numbers')
70     diff = abs(z1 - z2)
71     az1 = abs(z1)
72     if z2 and az1 > 1:
73         return diff/az1 <= tol
74     else:
75         return diff <= tol

79     """Return the mpf tuple normalized appropriately for the indicated
80     precision after doing a check to see if zero should be returned or
81     not when the mantissa is 0. ``mpf_normlize`` always assumes that this
82     is zero, but it may not be since the mantissa for mpf's values "+inf",

87     is only a wrapper to ``mpf_normalize`` which provides the check for non-
88     zero mpfs that have a 0 for the mantissa.

171     2
172     >>> igcd(5, 10, 15)

177         raise TypeError(
178             'igcd() takes at least 2 arguments (%s given)' % len(args))
179     if 1 in args:
180         a = 1
181         k = 0
182     else:
183         a = abs(as_int(args[0]))
184         k = 1
185     if a != 1:
186         while k < len(args):

194                     continue

224 # Use Lehmer's algorithm only for very large numbers.
225 # The limit could be different on Python 2.7 and 3.x.
226 # If so, then this could be defined in compatibility.py.
227 BIGBITS = 5000
228 def igcd_lehmer(a, b):
229     """Computes greatest common divisor of two integers.
230 
231     Euclid's algorithm for the computation of the greatest
232     common divisor  gcd(a, b)  of two (positive) integers
233     a and b is based on the division identity
234         a = q*b + r,
235     where the quotient  q  and the remainder  r  are integers
236     and  0 <= r < b. Then each common divisor of  a  and  b
237     divides  r, and it follows that  gcd(a, b) == gcd(b, r).
238     The algorithm works by constructing the sequence
239     r0, r1, r2, ..., where  r0 = a, r1 = b,  and each  rn
240     is the remainder from the division of the two preceding
241     elements.
242 
243     In Python, q = a // b  and  r = a % b  are obtained by the
244     floor division and the remainder operations, respectively.
245     These are the most expensive arithmetic operations, especially
246     for large  a  and  b.
247 
248     Lehmer's algorithm is based on the observation that the quotients
249     qn = r(n-1) // rn  are in general small integers even
250     when  a  and  b  are very large. Hence the quotients can be
251     usually determined from a relatively small number of most
252     significant bits.
253 
254     The efficiency of the algorithm is further enhanced by not
255     computing each long remainder in Euclid's sequence. The remainders
256     are linear combinations of  a  and  b  with integer coefficients
257     derived from the quotients. The coefficients can be computed
258     as far as the quotients can be determined from the chosen
259     most significant parts of  a  and  b. Only then a new pair of
260     consecutive remainders is computed and the algorithm starts
261     anew with this pair.
262 
263     References
264     ==========
265 
266     .. [1] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lehmer%27s_GCD_algorithm
267 
268     """
269     a, b = abs(as_int(a)), abs(as_int(b))
270     if a < b:
271         a, b = b, a
272 
273     # The algorithm works by using one or two digit division
274     # whenever possible. The outer loop will replace the
275     # pair (a, b) with a pair of shorter consecutive elements
276     # of the Euclidean gcd sequence until a and b
277     # fit into two Python (long) int digits.
278     nbits = 2*int_info.bits_per_digit
279 
280     while a.bit_length() > nbits and b != 0:
281         # Quotients are mostly small integers that can
282         # be determined from most significant bits.
283         n = a.bit_length() - nbits
284         x, y = int(a >> n), int(b >> n)  # most significant bits
285 
286         # Elements of the Euclidean gcd sequence are linear
287         # combinations of a and b with integer coefficients.
288         # Compute the coefficients of consequtive pairs
289         #     a' = A*a + B*b, b' = C*a + D*b
290         # using small integer arithmetic as far as possible.
291         A, B, C, D = 1, 0, 0, 1  # initial values
292 
293         while True:
294             # The coefficients alternate in sign while looping.
295             # The inner loop combines two steps to keep track
296             # of the signs.
297 
298             # At this point we have
299             #   A > 0, B <= 0, C <= 0, D > 0,
300             #   x' = x + B <= x < x" = x + A,
301             #   y' = y + C <= y < y" = y + D,
302             # and
303             #   x'*N <= a' < x"*N, y'*N <= b' < y"*N,
304             # where N = 2**n.
305 
306             # Now, if y' > 0, and x"//y' and x'//y" agree,
307             # then their common value is equal to  q = a'//b'.
308             # In addition,
309             #   x'%y" = x' - q*y" < x" - q*y' = x"%y',
310             # and
311             #   (x'%y")*N < a'%b' < (x"%y')*N.
312 
313             # On the other hand, we also have  x//y == q,
314             # and therefore
315             #   x'%y" = x + B - q*(y + D) = x%y + B',
316             #   x"%y' = x + A - q*(y + C) = x%y + A',
317             # where
318             #    B' = B - q*D < 0, A' = A - q*C > 0.
319 
320             if y + C <= 0:
321                 break
322             q = (x + A) // (y + C)
323 
324             # Now  x'//y" <= q, and equality holds if
325             #   x' - q*y" = (x - q*y) + (B - q*D) >= 0.
326             # This is a minor optimization to avoid division.
327             x_qy, B_qD = x - q*y, B - q*D
328             if x_qy + B_qD < 0:
329                 break
330 
331             # Next step in the Euclidean sequence.
332             x, y = y, x_qy
333             A, B, C, D = C, D, A - q*C, B_qD
334 
335             # At this point the signs of the coefficients
336             # change and their roles are interchanged.
337             #   A <= 0, B > 0, C > 0, D < 0,
338             #   x' = x + A <= x < x" = x + B,
339             #   y' = y + D < y < y" = y + C.
340 
341             if y + D <= 0:
342                 break
343             q = (x + B) // (y + D)
344             x_qy, A_qC = x - q*y, A - q*C
345             if x_qy + A_qC < 0:
346                 break
347 
348             x, y = y, x_qy
349             A, B, C, D = C, D, A_qC, B - q*D
350             # Now the conditions on top of the loop
351             # are again satisfied.
352             #   A > 0, B < 0, C < 0, D > 0.
353 
354         if B == 0:
355             # This can only happen when y == 0 in the beginning
356             # and the inner loop does nothing.
357             # Long division is forced.
358             a, b = b, a % b
359             continue
360 
361         # Compute new long arguments using the coefficients.
362         a, b = A*a + B*b, C*a + D*b
363 
364     # Small divisors. Finish with the standard algorithm.
365     while b:
366         a, b = b, a % b
367 
368     return a

382     >>> ilcm(5, 10, 15)
383     30
384 
385     """
386     if len(args) < 2:
387         raise TypeError(
388             'ilcm() takes at least 2 arguments (%s given)' % len(args))
389     if 0 in args:
390         return 0
391     a = args[0]
392     for b in args[1:]:
393         a = a*b // igcd(a, b)

397 def igcdex(a, b):
398     """Returns x, y, g such that g = x*a + y*b = gcd(a, b).
399 
400        >>> from sympy.core.numbers import igcdex
401        >>> igcdex(2, 3)
402        (-1, 1, 1)
403        >>> igcdex(10, 12)
404        (-1, 1, 2)
405 
406        >>> x, y, g = igcdex(100, 2004)
407        >>> x, y, g
408        (-20, 1, 4)
409        >>> x*100 + y*2004
410        4
411 
412     """
413     if (not a) and (not b):
414         return (0, 1, 0)
415 
416     if not a:
417         return (0, b//abs(b), abs(b))
418     if not b:
419         return (a//abs(a), 0, abs(a))
420 
421     if a < 0:
422         a, x_sign = -a, -1
423     else:
424         x_sign = 1
425 
426     if b < 0:
427         b, y_sign = -b, -1
428     else:
429         y_sign = 1
430 
431     x, y, r, s = 1, 0, 0, 1
432 
433     while b:
434         (c, q) = (a % b, a // b)
435         (a, b, r, s, x, y) = (b, c, x - q*r, y - q*s, r, s)
436 
437     return (x*x_sign, y*y_sign, a)
438

440 def mod_inverse(a, m):
441     """
442     Return the number c such that, ( a * c ) % m == 1 where
443     c has the same sign as a. If no such value exists, a
444     ValueError is raised.
445 
446     Examples
447     ========
448 
449     >>> from sympy import S
450     >>> from sympy.core.numbers import mod_inverse
451 
452     Suppose we wish to find multiplicative inverse x of
453     3 modulo 11. This is the same as finding x such
454     that 3 * x = 1 (mod 11). One value of x that satisfies
455     this congruence is 4. Because 3 * 4 = 12 and 12 = 1 mod(11).
456     This is the value return by mod_inverse:
457 
458     >>> mod_inverse(3, 11)
459     4
460     >>> mod_inverse(-3, 11)
461     -4
462 
463     When there is a common factor between the numerators of
464     ``a`` and ``m`` the inverse does not exist:
465 
466     >>> mod_inverse(2, 4)
467     Traceback (most recent call last):
468     ...
469     ValueError: inverse of 2 mod 4 does not exist
470 
471     >>> mod_inverse(S(2)/7, S(5)/2)
472     7/2
473 
474     References
475     ==========
476     - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modular_multiplicative_inverse
477     - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extended_Euclidean_algorithm
478     """
479     c = None
480     try:
481         a, m = as_int(a), as_int(m)
482         if m > 1:
483             x, y, g = igcdex(a, m)
484             if g == 1:
485                 c = x % m
486             if a < 0:
487                 c -= m
488     except ValueError:
489         a, m = sympify(a), sympify(m)
490         if not (a.is_number and m.is_number):
491             raise TypeError(filldedent('''
492                 Expected numbers for arguments; symbolic `mod_inverse`
493                 is not implemented
494                 but symbolic expressions can be handled with the
495                 similar function,
496                 sympy.polys.polytools.invert'''))
497         big = (m > 1)
498         if not (big is S.true or big is S.false):
499             raise ValueError('m > 1 did not evaluate; try to simplify %s' % m)
500         elif big:
501             c = 1/a
502     if c is None:
503         raise ValueError('inverse of %s (mod %s) does not exist' % (a, m))
504     return c
505

774 class Float(Number):
775     """Represent a floating-point number of arbitrary precision.
776 
777     Examples
778     ========
779 
780     >>> from sympy import Float
781     >>> Float(3.5)
782     3.50000000000000
783     >>> Float(3)
784     3.00000000000000
785 
786     Creating Floats from strings (and Python ``int`` and ``long``
787     types) will give a minimum precision of 15 digits, but the
788     precision will automatically increase to capture all digits
789     entered.
790 
791     >>> Float(1)
792     1.00000000000000
793     >>> Float(10**20)
794     100000000000000000000.
795     >>> Float('1e20')
796     100000000000000000000.
797 
798     However, *floating-point* numbers (Python ``float`` types) retain
799     only 15 digits of precision:
800 
801     >>> Float(1e20)
802     1.00000000000000e+20
803     >>> Float(1.23456789123456789)
804     1.23456789123457
805 
806     It may be preferable to enter high-precision decimal numbers
807     as strings:
808 
809     Float('1.23456789123456789')
810     1.23456789123456789
811 
812     The desired number of digits can also be specified:
813 
814     >>> Float('1e-3', 3)
815     0.00100
816     >>> Float(100, 4)
817     100.0
818 
819     Float can automatically count significant figures if a null string
820     is sent for the precision; space are also allowed in the string. (Auto-
821     counting is only allowed for strings, ints and longs).
822 
823     >>> Float('123 456 789 . 123 456', '')
824     123456789.123456
825     >>> Float('12e-3', '')
826     0.012
827     >>> Float(3, '')
828     3.
829 
830     If a number is written in scientific notation, only the digits before the
831     exponent are considered significant if a decimal appears, otherwise the
832     "e" signifies only how to move the decimal:
833 
834     >>> Float('60.e2', '')  # 2 digits significant
835     6.0e+3
836     >>> Float('60e2', '')  # 4 digits significant
837     6000.
838     >>> Float('600e-2', '')  # 3 digits significant
839     6.00
840 
841     Notes
842     =====
843 
844     Floats are inexact by their nature unless their value is a binary-exact
845     value.
846 
847     >>> approx, exact = Float(.1, 1), Float(.125, 1)
848 
849     For calculation purposes, evalf needs to be able to change the precision
850     but this will not increase the accuracy of the inexact value. The
851     following is the most accurate 5-digit approximation of a value of 0.1
852     that had only 1 digit of precision:
853 
854     >>> approx.evalf(5)
855     0.099609
856 
857     By contrast, 0.125 is exact in binary (as it is in base 10) and so it
858     can be passed to Float or evalf to obtain an arbitrary precision with
859     matching accuracy:
860 
861     >>> Float(exact, 5)
862     0.12500
863     >>> exact.evalf(20)
864     0.12500000000000000000
865 
866     Trying to make a high-precision Float from a float is not disallowed,
867     but one must keep in mind that the *underlying float* (not the apparent
868     decimal value) is being obtained with high precision. For example, 0.3
869     does not have a finite binary representation. The closest rational is
870     the fraction 5404319552844595/2**54. So if you try to obtain a Float of
871     0.3 to 20 digits of precision you will not see the same thing as 0.3
872     followed by 19 zeros:
873 
874     >>> Float(0.3, 20)
875     0.29999999999999998890
876 
877     If you want a 20-digit value of the decimal 0.3 (not the floating point
878     approximation of 0.3) you should send the 0.3 as a string. The underlying
879     representation is still binary but a higher precision than Python's float
880     is used:
881 
882     >>> Float('0.3', 20)
883     0.30000000000000000000
884 
885     Although you can increase the precision of an existing Float using Float
886     it will not increase the accuracy -- the underlying value is not changed:
887 
888     >>> def show(f): # binary rep of Float
889     ...     from sympy import Mul, Pow
890     ...     s, m, e, b = f._mpf_
891     ...     v = Mul(int(m), Pow(2, int(e), evaluate=False), evaluate=False)
892     ...     print('%s at prec=%s' % (v, f._prec))
893     ...
894     >>> t = Float('0.3', 3)
895     >>> show(t)
896     4915/2**14 at prec=13
897     >>> show(Float(t, 20)) # higher prec, not higher accuracy
898     4915/2**14 at prec=70
899     >>> show(Float(t, 2)) # lower prec
900     307/2**10 at prec=10
901 
902     The same thing happens when evalf is used on a Float:
903 
904     >>> show(t.evalf(20))
905     4915/2**14 at prec=70
906     >>> show(t.evalf(2))
907     307/2**10 at prec=10
908 
909     Finally, Floats can be instantiated with an mpf tuple (n, c, p) to
910     produce the number (-1)**n*c*2**p:
911 
912     >>> n, c, p = 1, 5, 0
913     >>> (-1)**n*c*2**p
914     -5
915     >>> Float((1, 5, 0))
916     -5.00000000000000
917 
918     An actual mpf tuple also contains the number of bits in c as the last
919     element of the tuple:
920 
921     >>> _._mpf_
922     (1, 5, 0, 3)
923 
924     This is not needed for instantiation and is not the same thing as the
925     precision. The mpf tuple and the precision are two separate quantities
926     that Float tracks.
927 
928     """

934     is_irrational = None

1358 class Rational(Number):
1359     """Represents integers and rational numbers (p/q) of any size.
1360 
1361     Examples
1362     ========
1363 
1364     >>> from sympy import Rational, nsimplify, S, pi
1365     >>> Rational(3)
1366     3
1367     >>> Rational(1, 2)
1368     1/2
1369 
1370     Rational is unprejudiced in accepting input. If a float is passed, the
1371     underlying value of the binary representation will be returned:
1372 
1373     >>> Rational(.5)
1374     1/2
1375     >>> Rational(.2)
1376     3602879701896397/18014398509481984
1377 
1378     If the simpler representation of the float is desired then consider
1379     limiting the denominator to the desired value or convert the float to
1380     a string (which is roughly equivalent to limiting the denominator to
1381     10**12):
1382 
1383     >>> Rational(str(.2))
1384     1/5
1385     >>> Rational(.2).limit_denominator(10**12)
1386     1/5
1387 
1388     An arbitrarily precise Rational is obtained when a string literal is
1389     passed:
1390 
1391     >>> Rational("1.23")
1392     123/100
1393     >>> Rational('1e-2')
1394     1/100
1395     >>> Rational(".1")
1396     1/10
1397     >>> Rational('1e-2/3.2')
1398     1/320
1399 
1400     The conversion of other types of strings can be handled by
1401     the sympify() function, and conversion of floats to expressions
1402     or simple fractions can be handled with nsimplify:
1403 
1404     >>> S('.[3]')  # repeating digits in brackets
1405     1/3
1406     >>> S('3**2/10')  # general expressions
1407     9/10
1408     >>> nsimplify(.3)  # numbers that have a simple form
1409     3/10
1410 
1411     But if the input does not reduce to a literal Rational, an error will
1412     be raised:
1413 
1414     >>> Rational(pi)
1415     Traceback (most recent call last):
1416     ...
1417     TypeError: invalid input: pi
1418 
1419 
1420     Low-level
1421     ---------
1422 
1423     Access numerator and denominator as .p and .q:
1424 
1425     >>> r = Rational(3, 4)
1426     >>> r
1427     3/4
1428     >>> r.p
1429     3
1430     >>> r.q
1431     4
1432 
1433     Note that p and q return integers (not SymPy Integers) so some care
1434     is needed when using them in expressions:
1435 
1436     >>> r.p/r.q
1437     0.75
1438 
1439     See Also
1440     ========
1441     sympify, sympy.simplify.simplify.nsimplify
1442     """

2164     def _eval_power(self, expt):
2165         """
2166         Tries to do some simplifications on self**expt
2167 
2168         Returns None if no further simplifications can be done
2169 
2170         When exponent is a fraction (so we have for example a square root),
2171         we try to find a simpler representation by factoring the argument
2172         up to factors of 2**15, e.g.
2173 
2174           - sqrt(4) becomes 2
2175           - sqrt(-4) becomes 2*I
2176           - (2**(3+7)*3**(6+7))**Rational(1,7) becomes 6*18**(3/7)
2177 
2178         Further simplification would require a special call to factorint on
2179         the argument which is not done here for sake of speed.
2180 
2181         """
2182         from sympy import perfect_power
2183 
2184         if expt is S.Infinity:
2185             if self.p > S.One:
2186                 return S.Infinity
2187             # cases -1, 0, 1 are done in their respective classes
2188             return S.Infinity + S.ImaginaryUnit*S.Infinity
2189         if expt is S.NegativeInfinity:
2190             return Rational(1, self)**S.Infinity
2191         if not isinstance(expt, Number):
2192             # simplify when expt is even
2193             # (-2)**k --> 2**k
2194             if self.is_negative and expt.is_even:
2195                 return (-self)**expt
2196         if isinstance(expt, Float):
2197             # Rational knows how to exponentiate by a Float
2198             return super(Integer, self)._eval_power(expt)
2199         if not isinstance(expt, Rational):
2200             return
2201         if expt is S.Half and self.is_negative:
2202             # we extract I for this special case since everyone is doing so
2203             return S.ImaginaryUnit*Pow(-self, expt)
2204         if expt.is_negative:
2205             # invert base and change sign on exponent
2206             ne = -expt
2207             if self.is_negative:
2208                 if expt.q != 1:
2209                     return -(S.NegativeOne)**((expt.p % expt.q) /
2210                             S(expt.q))*Rational(1, -self)**ne
2211                 else:
2212                     return (S.NegativeOne)**ne*Rational(1, -self)**ne
2213             else:
2214                 return Rational(1, self.p)**ne
2215         # see if base is a perfect root, sqrt(4) --> 2
2216         x, xexact = integer_nthroot(abs(self.p), expt.q)
2217         if xexact:
2218             # if it's a perfect root we've finished
2219             result = Integer(x**abs(expt.p))
2220             if self.is_negative:
2221                 result *= S.NegativeOne**expt
2222             return result
2223 
2224         # The following is an algorithm where we collect perfect roots
2225         # from the factors of base.
2226 
2227         # if it's not an nth root, it still might be a perfect power
2228         b_pos = int(abs(self.p))
2229         p = perfect_power(b_pos)
2230         if p is not False:
2231             dict = {p[0]: p[1]}
2232         else:
2233             dict = Integer(self).factors(limit=2**15)
2234 
2235         # now process the dict of factors
2236         if self.is_negative:
2237             dict[-1] = 1
2238         out_int = 1  # integer part
2239         out_rad = 1  # extracted radicals
2240         sqr_int = 1
2241         sqr_gcd = 0
2242         sqr_dict = {}
2243         for prime, exponent in dict.items():
2244             exponent *= expt.p
2245             # remove multiples of expt.q: (2**12)**(1/10) -> 2*(2**2)**(1/10)
2246             div_e, div_m = divmod(exponent, expt.q)
2247             if div_e > 0:
2248                 out_int *= prime**div_e
2249             if div_m > 0:
2250                 # see if the reduced exponent shares a gcd with e.q
2251                 # (2**2)**(1/10) -> 2**(1/5)
2252                 g = igcd(div_m, expt.q)
2253                 if g != 1:
2254                     out_rad *= Pow(prime, Rational(div_m//g, expt.q//g))
2255                 else:
2256                     sqr_dict[prime] = div_m
2257         # identify gcd of remaining powers
2258         for p, ex in sqr_dict.items():
2259             if sqr_gcd == 0:
2260                 sqr_gcd = ex
2261             else:
2262                 sqr_gcd = igcd(sqr_gcd, ex)
2263                 if sqr_gcd == 1:
2264                     break
2265         for k, v in sqr_dict.items():
2266             sqr_int *= k**(v//sqr_gcd)
2267         if sqr_int == self and out_int == 1 and out_rad == 1:
2268             result = None
2269         else:
2270             result = out_int*out_rad*Pow(sqr_int, Rational(sqr_gcd, expt.q))
2271         return result

<issue>
Hostname and timestamp properties in generated JUnit XML reports
Pytest enables generating JUnit XML reports of the tests.

However, there are some properties missing, specifically `hostname` and `timestamp` from the `testsuite` XML element. Is there an option to include them?

Example of a pytest XML report:
```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<testsuite errors="0" failures="2" name="check" skipped="0" tests="4" time="0.049">
	<testcase classname="test_sample.TestClass" file="test_sample.py" line="3" name="test_addOne_normal" time="0.001"></testcase>
	<testcase classname="test_sample.TestClass" file="test_sample.py" line="6" name="test_addOne_edge" time="0.001"></testcase>
</testsuite>
```

Example of a junit XML report:
```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<testsuite name="location.GeoLocationTest" tests="2" skipped="0" failures="0" errors="0" timestamp="2019-04-22T10:32:27" hostname="Anass-MacBook-Pro.local" time="0.048">
  <properties/>
  <testcase name="testIoException()" classname="location.GeoLocationTest" time="0.044"/>
  <testcase name="testJsonDeserialization()" classname="location.GeoLocationTest" time="0.003"/>
  <system-out><![CDATA[]]></system-out>
  <system-err><![CDATA[]]></system-err>
</testsuite>
```

28 # We need to get the subset of the invalid unicode ranges according to
29 # XML 1.0 which are valid in this python build.  Hence we calculate
30 # this dynamically instead of hardcoding it.  The spec range of valid
31 # chars is: Char ::= #x9 | #xA | #xD | [#x20-#xD7FF] | [#xE000-#xFFFD]
32 #                    | [#x10000-#x10FFFF]
33 _legal_chars = (0x09, 0x0A, 0x0D)
34 _legal_ranges = ((0x20, 0x7E), (0x80, 0xD7FF), (0xE000, 0xFFFD), (0x10000, 0x10FFFF))
35 _legal_xml_re = [
36     "{}-{}".format(chr(low), chr(high))
37     for (low, high) in _legal_ranges
38     if low < sys.maxunicode
39 ]
40 _legal_xml_re = [chr(x) for x in _legal_chars] + _legal_xml_re
41 illegal_xml_re = re.compile("[^%s]" % "".join(_legal_xml_re))
42 del _legal_chars
43 del _legal_ranges
44 del _legal_xml_re
45 
46 _py_ext_re = re.compile(r"\.py$")

49 def bin_xml_escape(arg):
50     def repl(matchobj):
51         i = ord(matchobj.group())
52         if i <= 0xFF:
53             return "#x%02X" % i
54         else:
55             return "#x%04X" % i
56 
57     return py.xml.raw(illegal_xml_re.sub(repl, py.xml.escape(arg)))

104     def make_properties_node(self):
105         """Return a Junit node containing custom properties, if any.
106         """
107         if self.properties:
108             return Junit.properties(
109                 [
110                     Junit.property(name=name, value=value)
111                     for name, value in self.properties
112                 ]
113             )
114         return ""

116     def record_testreport(self, testreport):
117         assert not self.testcase
118         names = mangle_test_address(testreport.nodeid)
119         existing_attrs = self.attrs
120         classnames = names[:-1]
121         if self.xml.prefix:
122             classnames.insert(0, self.xml.prefix)
123         attrs = {
124             "classname": ".".join(classnames),
125             "name": bin_xml_escape(names[-1]),
126             "file": testreport.location[0],
127         }
128         if testreport.location[1] is not None:
129             attrs["line"] = testreport.location[1]
130         if hasattr(testreport, "url"):
131             attrs["url"] = testreport.url
132         self.attrs = attrs
133         self.attrs.update(existing_attrs)  # restore any user-defined attributes
134 
135         # Preserve legacy testcase behavior
136         if self.family == "xunit1":
137             return
138 
139         # Filter out attributes not permitted by this test family.
140         # Including custom attributes because they are not valid here.
141         temp_attrs = {}
142         for key in self.attrs.keys():
143             if key in families[self.family]["testcase"]:
144                 temp_attrs[key] = self.attrs[key]
145         self.attrs = temp_attrs
146 
147     def to_xml(self):
148         testcase = Junit.testcase(time="%.3f" % self.duration, **self.attrs)
149         testcase.append(self.make_properties_node())
150         for node in self.nodes:
151             testcase.append(node)
152         return testcase

154     def _add_simple(self, kind, message, data=None):
155         data = bin_xml_escape(data)

159     def write_captured_output(self, report):
160         if not self.xml.log_passing_tests and report.passed:
161             return
162 
163         content_out = report.capstdout
164         content_log = report.caplog
165         content_err = report.capstderr
166 
167         if content_log or content_out:
168             if content_log and self.xml.logging == "system-out":

177                             "",
178                             " Captured Log ".center(80, "-"),

182                 else:

186

451 def mangle_test_address(address):
452     path, possible_open_bracket, params = address.partition("[")
453     names = path.split("::")
454     try:
455         names.remove("()")
456     except ValueError:
457         pass
458     # convert file path to dotted path
459     names[0] = names[0].replace(nodes.SEP, ".")

Behavior of Matrix hstack and vstack changed in sympy 1.1
In sympy 1.0:
```
import sympy as sy
M1 = sy.Matrix.zeros(0, 0)
M2 = sy.Matrix.zeros(0, 1)

returns 
`(0, 6)`

Now, same in sympy 1.1:
```
import sympy as sy
M1 = sy.Matrix.zeros(0, 0)
M2 = sy.Matrix.zeros(0, 1)
M3 = sy.Matrix.zeros(0, 2)
M4 = sy.Matrix.zeros(0, 3)
sy.Matrix.hstack(M1, M2, M3, M4).shape
```
returns
`(0, 3)

whereas:
```
import sympy as sy
M1 = sy.Matrix.zeros(1, 0)

```
returns
`(1, 6)
`

30     [0, 1],
31     [2, 3]])

42     def __new__(cls, *args, **kwargs):
43         self = object.__new__(cls)
44         if len(args) == 1 and isinstance(args[0], SparseMatrix):
45             self.rows = args[0].rows
46             self.cols = args[0].cols
47             self._smat = dict(args[0]._smat)
48             return self
49 
50         self._smat = {}
51 
52         if len(args) == 3:
53             self.rows = as_int(args[0])
54             self.cols = as_int(args[1])
55 
56             if isinstance(args[2], collections.Callable):
57                 op = args[2]
58                 for i in range(self.rows):
59                     for j in range(self.cols):
60                         value = self._sympify(
61                             op(self._sympify(i), self._sympify(j)))
62                         if value:
63                             self._smat[(i, j)] = value
64             elif isinstance(args[2], (dict, Dict)):
65                 # manual copy, copy.deepcopy() doesn't work
66                 for key in args[2].keys():
67                     v = args[2][key]
68                     if v:
69                         self._smat[key] = self._sympify(v)
70             elif is_sequence(args[2]):
71                 if len(args[2]) != self.rows*self.cols:
72                     raise ValueError(
73                         'List length (%s) != rows*columns (%s)' %
74                         (len(args[2]), self.rows*self.cols))
75                 flat_list = args[2]
76                 for i in range(self.rows):
77                     for j in range(self.cols):
78                         value = self._sympify(flat_list[i*self.cols + j])
79                         if value:
80                             self._smat[(i, j)] = value
81         else:
82             # handle full matrix forms with _handle_creation_inputs
83             r, c, _list = Matrix._handle_creation_inputs(*args)
84             self.rows = r
85             self.cols = c
86             for i in range(self.rows):
87                 for j in range(self.cols):
88                     value = _list[self.cols*i + j]
89                     if value:
90                         self._smat[(i, j)] = value

154         # for speed reasons, this is not uncommented, but if you are
155         # having difficulties, try uncommenting to make sure that the
156         # input matrix is symmetric
157 
158         #assert self.is_symmetric()

164     def _cholesky_sparse(self):
165         """Algorithm for numeric Cholesky factorization of a sparse matrix."""
166         Crowstruc = self.row_structure_symbolic_cholesky()
167         C = self.zeros(self.rows)
168         for i in range(len(Crowstruc)):
169             for j in Crowstruc[i]:
170                 if i != j:
171                     C[i, j] = self[i, j]
172                     summ = 0
173                     for p1 in Crowstruc[i]:
174                         if p1 < j:
175                             for p2 in Crowstruc[j]:
176                                 if p2 < j:
177                                     if p1 == p2:
178                                         summ += C[i, p1]*C[j, p1]
179                                 else:
180                                     break
181                             else:
182                                 break
183                     C[i, j] -= summ
184                     C[i, j] /= C[j, j]
185                 else:
186                     C[j, j] = self[j, j]
187                     summ = 0
188                     for k in Crowstruc[j]:
189                         if k < j:
190                             summ += C[j, k]**2
191                         else:
192                             break
193                     C[j, j] -= summ
194                     C[j, j] = sqrt(C[j, j])
195 
196         return C

202     def _eval_inverse(self, **kwargs):
203         """Return the matrix inverse using Cholesky or LDL (default)
204         decomposition as selected with the ``method`` keyword: 'CH' or 'LDL',
205         respectively.
206 
207         Examples
208         ========
209 
210         >>> from sympy import SparseMatrix, Matrix
211         >>> A = SparseMatrix([
212         ... [ 2, -1,  0],
213         ... [-1,  2, -1],
214         ... [ 0,  0,  2]])
215         >>> A.inv('CH')
216         Matrix([
217         [2/3, 1/3, 1/6],
218         [1/3, 2/3, 1/3],
219         [  0,   0, 1/2]])
220         >>> A.inv(method='LDL') # use of 'method=' is optional
221         Matrix([
222         [2/3, 1/3, 1/6],
223         [1/3, 2/3, 1/3],
224         [  0,   0, 1/2]])
225         >>> A * _
226         Matrix([
227         [1, 0, 0],
228         [0, 1, 0],
229         [0, 0, 1]])
230 
231         """
232         sym = self.is_symmetric()
233         M = self.as_mutable()
234         I = M.eye(M.rows)
235         if not sym:
236             t = M.T
237             r1 = M[0, :]
238             M = t*M
239             I = t*I
240         method = kwargs.get('method', 'LDL')
241         if method in "LDL":
242             solve = M._LDL_solve
243         elif method == "CH":
244             solve = M._cholesky_solve
245         else:
246             raise NotImplementedError(
247                 'Method may be "CH" or "LDL", not %s.' % method)
248         rv = M.hstack(*[solve(I[:, i]) for i in range(I.cols)])
249         if not sym:
250             scale = (r1*rv[:, 0])[0, 0]
251             rv /= scale
252         return self._new(rv)

257     def _eval_add(self, other):
258         """If `other` is a SparseMatrix, add efficiently. Otherwise,
259         do standard addition."""
260         if not isinstance(other, SparseMatrix):
261             return self + self._new(other)
262 
263         smat = {}
264         zero = self._sympify(0)
265         for key in set().union(self._smat.keys(), other._smat.keys()):
266             sum = self._smat.get(key, zero) + other._smat.get(key, zero)
267             if sum != 0:
268                 smat[key] = sum
269         return self._new(self.rows, self.cols, smat)

291     def _eval_extract(self, rowsList, colsList):
292         urow = list(uniq(rowsList))
293         ucol = list(uniq(colsList))
294         smat = {}
295         if len(urow)*len(ucol) < len(self._smat):
296             # there are fewer elements requested than there are elements in the matrix
297             for i, r in enumerate(urow):
298                 for j, c in enumerate(ucol):
299                     smat[i, j] = self._smat.get((r, c), 0)
300         else:
301             # most of the request will be zeros so check all of self's entries,
302             # keeping only the ones that are desired
303             for rk, ck in self._smat:
304                 if rk in urow and ck in ucol:
305                     smat[(urow.index(rk), ucol.index(ck))] = self._smat[(rk, ck)]
306 
307         rv = self._new(len(urow), len(ucol), smat)
308         # rv is nominally correct but there might be rows/cols
309         # which require duplication
310         if len(rowsList) != len(urow):
311             for i, r in enumerate(rowsList):
312                 i_previous = rowsList.index(r)
313                 if i_previous != i:
314                     rv = rv.row_insert(i, rv.row(i_previous))
315         if len(colsList) != len(ucol):
316             for i, c in enumerate(colsList):
317                 i_previous = colsList.index(c)
318                 if i_previous != i:
319                     rv = rv.col_insert(i, rv.col(i_previous))
320         return rv

345     def _eval_matrix_mul(self, other):
346         """Fast multiplication exploiting the sparsity of the matrix."""
347         if not isinstance(other, SparseMatrix):
348             return self*self._new(other)
349 
350         # if we made it here, we're both sparse matrices
351         # create quick lookups for rows and cols
352         row_lookup = defaultdict(dict)
353         for (i,j), val in self._smat.items():
354             row_lookup[i][j] = val
355         col_lookup = defaultdict(dict)
356         for (i,j), val in other._smat.items():
357             col_lookup[j][i] = val
358 
359         smat = {}
360         for row in row_lookup.keys():
361             for col in col_lookup.keys():
362                 # find the common indices of non-zero entries.
363                 # these are the only things that need to be multiplied.
364                 indices = set(col_lookup[col].keys()) & set(row_lookup[row].keys())
365                 if indices:
366                     val = sum(row_lookup[row][k]*col_lookup[col][k] for k in indices)
367                     smat[(row, col)] = val
368         return self._new(self.rows, other.cols, smat)

430     def _LDL_sparse(self):
431         """Algorithm for numeric LDL factization, exploiting sparse structure.
432         """
433         Lrowstruc = self.row_structure_symbolic_cholesky()
434         L = self.eye(self.rows)
435         D = self.zeros(self.rows, self.cols)
436 
437         for i in range(len(Lrowstruc)):
438             for j in Lrowstruc[i]:
439                 if i != j:
440                     L[i, j] = self[i, j]
441                     summ = 0
442                     for p1 in Lrowstruc[i]:
443                         if p1 < j:
444                             for p2 in Lrowstruc[j]:
445                                 if p2 < j:
446                                     if p1 == p2:
447                                         summ += L[i, p1]*L[j, p1]*D[p1, p1]
448                                 else:
449                                     break
450                         else:
451                             break
452                     L[i, j] -= summ
453                     L[i, j] /= D[j, j]
454                 elif i == j:
455                     D[i, i] = self[i, i]
456                     summ = 0
457                     for k in Lrowstruc[i]:
458                         if k < i:
459                             summ += L[i, k]**2*D[k, k]
460                         else:
461                             break
462                     D[i, i] -= summ
463 
464         return L, D

466     def _lower_triangular_solve(self, rhs):
467         """Fast algorithm for solving a lower-triangular system,
468         exploiting the sparsity of the given matrix.
469         """
470         rows = [[] for i in range(self.rows)]
471         for i, j, v in self.row_list():
472             if i > j:
473                 rows[i].append((j, v))
474         X = rhs.copy()
475         for i in range(self.rows):
476             for j, v in rows[i]:
477                 X[i, 0] -= v*X[j, 0]
478             X[i, 0] /= self[i, i]
479         return self._new(X)

487     def _upper_triangular_solve(self, rhs):
488         """Fast algorithm for solving an upper-triangular system,
489         exploiting the sparsity of the given matrix.
490         """
491         rows = [[] for i in range(self.rows)]
492         for i, j, v in self.row_list():
493             if i < j:
494                 rows[i].append((j, v))
495         X = rhs.copy()
496         for i in range(self.rows - 1, -1, -1):
497             rows[i].reverse()
498             for j, v in rows[i]:
499                 X[i, 0] -= v*X[j, 0]
500             X[i, 0] /= self[i, i]
501         return self._new(X)

613     def LDLdecomposition(self):
614         """
615         Returns the LDL Decomposition (matrices ``L`` and ``D``) of matrix
616         ``A``, such that ``L * D * L.T == A``. ``A`` must be a square,
617         symmetric, positive-definite and non-singular.
618 
619         This method eliminates the use of square root and ensures that all
620         the diagonal entries of L are 1.
621 
622         Examples
623         ========
624 
625         >>> from sympy.matrices import SparseMatrix
626         >>> A = SparseMatrix(((25, 15, -5), (15, 18, 0), (-5, 0, 11)))
627         >>> L, D = A.LDLdecomposition()
628         >>> L
629         Matrix([
630         [   1,   0, 0],
631         [ 3/5,   1, 0],
632         [-1/5, 1/3, 1]])
633         >>> D
634         Matrix([
635         [25, 0, 0],
636         [ 0, 9, 0],
637         [ 0, 0, 9]])
638         >>> L * D * L.T == A
639         True
640 
641         """
642         from sympy.core.numbers import nan, oo
643         if not self.is_symmetric():
644             raise ValueError('LDL decomposition applies only to '
645                 'symmetric matrices.')
646         L, D = self.as_mutable()._LDL_sparse()
647         if L.has(nan) or L.has(oo) or D.has(nan) or D.has(oo):
648             raise ValueError('LDL decomposition applies only to '
649                 'positive-definite matrices')
650 
651         return self._new(L), self._new(D)

690                     t = virtual[c]
691                     virtual[c] = r

838                     'more rows than columns, try M.solve_least_squares(rhs).')

problem_statement:
Behavior of Matrix hstack and vstack changed in sympy 1.1
In sympy 1.0:
```
import sympy as sy
M1 = sy.Matrix.zeros(0, 0)
M2 = sy.Matrix.zeros(0, 1)
M3 = sy.Matrix.zeros(0, 2)
M4 = sy.Matrix.zeros(0, 3)
sy.Matrix.hstack(M1, M2, M3, M4).shape
```
returns 
`(0, 6)`

Now, same in sympy 1.1:
```
import sympy as sy
M1 = sy.Matrix.zeros(0, 0)
M2 = sy.Matrix.zeros(0, 1)
M3 = sy.Matrix.zeros(0, 2)
M4 = sy.Matrix.zeros(0, 3)
sy.Matrix.hstack(M1, M2, M3, M4).shape
```
returns
`(0, 3)
`
whereas:
```
import sympy as sy
M1 = sy.Matrix.zeros(1, 0)

51 Documentation and usage

53 
54 Everything is at:

56 http://docs.sympy.org/

58 You can generate everything at the above site in your local copy of SymPy by::
59 
60     $ cd doc
61     $ make html

63 Then the docs will be in `_build/html`. If you don't want to read that, here
64 is a short usage:
65 
66 From this directory, start python and::
67 
68     >>> from sympy import Symbol, cos
69     >>> x = Symbol('x')
70     >>> e = 1/cos(x)
71     >>> print e.series(x, 0, 10)
72     1 + x**2/2 + 5*x**4/24 + 61*x**6/720 + 277*x**8/8064 + O(x**10)

91 SymPy has a hard dependency on the `mpmath <http://mpmath.org/>`

193 Brief History
194 -------------
195 
196 SymPy was started by Ondřej Čertík in 2005, he wrote some code during the
197 summer, then he wrote some more code during the summer 2006. In February 2007,
198 Fabian Pedregosa joined the project and helped fixed many things, contributed
199 documentation and made it alive again. 5 students (Mateusz Paprocki, Brian
200 Jorgensen, Jason Gedge, Robert Schwarz and Chris Wu) improved SymPy incredibly
201 during the summer 2007 as part of the Google Summer of Code. Pearu Peterson
202 joined the development during the summer 2007 and he has made SymPy much more
203 competitive by rewriting the core from scratch, that has made it from 10x to
204 100x faster. Jurjen N.E. Bos has contributed pretty printing and other patches.
205 Fredrik Johansson has written mpmath and contributed a lot of patches.
206 
207 SymPy has participated in every Google Summer of Code since 2007. You can see
208 https://github.com/sympy/sympy/wiki#google-summer-of-code for full details.
209 Each year has improved SymPy by bounds. Most of SymPy's development has come
210 from Google Summer of Code students.
211 
212 In 2011, Ondřej Čertík stepped down as lead developer, with Aaron Meurer, who
213 also started as a Google Summer of Code student, taking his place. Ondřej
214 Čertík is still active in the community, but is too busy with work and family
215 to play a lead development role.
216 
217 Since then, a lot more people have joined the development and some people have
218 also left. You can see the full list in doc/src/aboutus.rst, or online at:
219 
220 http://docs.sympy.org/dev/aboutus.html#sympy-development-team
221 
222 The git history goes back to 2007, when development moved from svn to hg.  To
223 see the history before that point, look at http://github.com/sympy/sympy-old.
224 
225 You can use git to see the biggest developers.  The command::
226 
227      $ git shortlog -ns
228 
229 will show each developer, sorted by commits to the project.  The command::
230 
231      $ git shortlog -ns --since="1 year"
232 
233 will show the top developers from the last year.

75 @public
76 class Options(dict):
77     """
78     Options manager for polynomial manipulation module.
79 
80     Examples
81     ========
82 
83     >>> from sympy.polys.polyoptions import Options
84     >>> from sympy.polys.polyoptions import build_options
85 
86     >>> from sympy.abc import x, y, z
87 
88     >>> Options((x, y, z), {'domain': 'ZZ'})
89     {'auto': False, 'domain': ZZ, 'gens': (x, y, z)}
90 
91     >>> build_options((x, y, z), {'domain': 'ZZ'})
92     {'auto': False, 'domain': ZZ, 'gens': (x, y, z)}
93 
94     **Options**
95 
96     * Expand --- boolean option
97     * Gens --- option
98     * Wrt --- option
99     * Sort --- option
100     * Order --- option
101     * Field --- boolean option
102     * Greedy --- boolean option
103     * Domain --- option
104     * Split --- boolean option
105     * Gaussian --- boolean option
106     * Extension --- option
107     * Modulus --- option
108     * Symmetric --- boolean option
109     * Strict --- boolean option
110 
111     **Flags**
112 
113     * Auto --- boolean flag
114     * Frac --- boolean flag
115     * Formal --- boolean flag
116     * Polys --- boolean flag
117     * Include --- boolean flag
118     * All --- boolean flag
119     * Gen --- flag
120     * Series --- boolean flag
121 
122     """
123 
124     __order__ = None
125     __options__ = {}
126 
127     def __init__(self, gens, args, flags=None, strict=False):
128         dict.__init__(self)
129 
130         if gens and args.get('gens', ()):
131             raise OptionError(
132                 "both '*gens' and keyword argument 'gens' supplied")
133         elif gens:
134             args = dict(args)
135             args['gens'] = gens
136 
137         defaults = args.pop('defaults', {})
138 
139         def preprocess_options(args):
140             for option, value in args.items():
141                 try:
142                     cls = self.__options__[option]
143                 except KeyError:
144                     raise OptionError("'%s' is not a valid option" % option)
145 
146                 if issubclass(cls, Flag):
147                     if flags is None or option not in flags:
148                         if strict:
149                             raise OptionError("'%s' flag is not allowed in this context" % option)
150 
151                 if value is not None:
152                     self[option] = cls.preprocess(value)
153 
154         preprocess_options(args)
155 
156         for key, value in dict(defaults).items():
157             if key in self:
158                 del defaults[key]
159             else:
160                 for option in self.keys():
161                     cls = self.__options__[option]
162 
163                     if key in cls.excludes:
164                         del defaults[key]
165                         break
166 
167         preprocess_options(defaults)
168 
169         for option in self.keys():
170             cls = self.__options__[option]
171 
172             for require_option in cls.requires:
173                 if self.get(require_option) is None:
174                     raise OptionError("'%s' option is only allowed together with '%s'" % (option, require_option))
175 
176             for exclude_option in cls.excludes:
177                 if self.get(exclude_option) is not None:
178                     raise OptionError("'%s' option is not allowed together with '%s'" % (option, exclude_option))
179 
180         for option in self.__order__:
181             self.__options__[option].postprocess(self)
182 
183     @classmethod
184     def _init_dependencies_order(cls):
185         """Resolve the order of options' processing. """
186         if cls.__order__ is None:
187             vertices, edges = [], set([])
188 
189             for name, option in cls.__options__.items():
190                 vertices.append(name)
191 
192                 for _name in option.after:
193                     edges.add((_name, name))
194 
195                 for _name in option.before:
196                     edges.add((name, _name))
197 
198             try:
199                 cls.__order__ = topological_sort((vertices, list(edges)))
200             except ValueError:
201                 raise RuntimeError(
202                     "cycle detected in sympy.polys options framework")
203 
204     def clone(self, updates={}):
205         """Clone ``self`` and update specified options. """
206         obj = dict.__new__(self.__class__)
207 
208         for option, value in self.items():
209             obj[option] = value
210 
211         for option, value in updates.items():
212             obj[option] = value
213 
214         return obj
215 
216     def __setattr__(self, attr, value):
217         if attr in self.__options__:
218             self[attr] = value
219         else:
220             super(Options, self).__setattr__(attr, value)
221 
222     @property
223     def args(self):
224         args = {}
225 
226         for option, value in self.items():
227             if value is not None and option != 'gens':
228                 cls = self.__options__[option]
229 
230                 if not issubclass(cls, Flag):
231                     args[option] = value
232 
233         return args
234 
235     @property
236     def options(self):
237         options = {}
238 
239         for option, cls in self.__options__.items():
240             if not issubclass(cls, Flag):
241                 options[option] = getattr(self, option)
242 
243         return options
244 
245     @property
246     def flags(self):
247         flags = {}
248 
249         for option, cls in self.__options__.items():
250             if issubclass(cls, Flag):
251                 flags[option] = getattr(self, option)
252 
253         return flags

269 class Gens(with_metaclass(OptionType, Option)):
270     """``gens`` option to polynomial manipulation functions. """
271 
272     option = 'gens'
273 
274     requires = []
275     excludes = []
276 
277     @classmethod
278     def default(cls):
279         return ()
280 
281     @classmethod
282     def preprocess(cls, gens):
283         if isinstance(gens, Basic):
284             gens = (gens,)
285         elif len(gens) == 1 and hasattr(gens[0], '__iter__'):
286             gens = gens[0]
287 
288         if gens == (None,):
289             gens = ()
290         elif has_dups(gens):
291             raise GeneratorsError("duplicated generators: %s" % str(gens))
292         elif any(gen.is_commutative is False for gen in gens):
293             raise GeneratorsError("non-commutative generators: %s" % str(gens))
294 
295         return tuple(gens)
296

298 class Wrt(with_metaclass(OptionType, Option)):
299     """``wrt`` option to polynomial manipulation functions. """

301     option = 'wrt'

303     requires = []
304     excludes = []
305 
306     _re_split = re.compile(r"\s*,\s*|\s+")

308     @classmethod
309     def preprocess(cls, wrt):
310         if isinstance(wrt, Basic):
311             return [str(wrt)]
312         elif isinstance(wrt, str):
313             wrt = wrt.strip()
314             if wrt.endswith(','):
315                 raise OptionError('Bad input: missing parameter.')
316             if not wrt:
317                 return []
318             return [ gen for gen in cls._re_split.split(wrt) ]
319         elif hasattr(wrt, '__getitem__'):
320             return list(map(str, wrt))
321         else:
322             raise OptionError("invalid argument for 'wrt' option")

395 class Domain(with_metaclass(OptionType, Option)):
396     """``domain`` option to polynomial manipulation functions. """
397 
398     option = 'domain'
399 
400     requires = []
401     excludes = ['field', 'greedy', 'split', 'gaussian', 'extension']
402 
403     after = ['gens']
404 
405     _re_realfield = re.compile(r"^(R|RR)(_(\d+))?$")
406     _re_complexfield = re.compile(r"^(C|CC)(_(\d+))?$")
407     _re_finitefield = re.compile(r"^(FF|GF)\((\d+)\)$")
408     _re_polynomial = re.compile(r"^(Z|ZZ|Q|QQ)\[(.+)\]$")
409     _re_fraction = re.compile(r"^(Z|ZZ|Q|QQ)\((.+)\)$")
410     _re_algebraic = re.compile(r"^(Q|QQ)\<(.+)\>$")
411 
412     @classmethod
413     def preprocess(cls, domain):
414         if isinstance(domain, sympy.polys.domains.Domain):
415             return domain
416         elif hasattr(domain, 'to_domain'):
417             return domain.to_domain()
418         elif isinstance(domain, string_types):
419             if domain in ['Z', 'ZZ']:
420                 return sympy.polys.domains.ZZ
421 
422             if domain in ['Q', 'QQ']:
423                 return sympy.polys.domains.QQ
424 
425             if domain == 'EX':
426                 return sympy.polys.domains.EX
427 
428             r = cls._re_realfield.match(domain)
429 
430             if r is not None:
431                 _, _, prec = r.groups()
432 
433                 if prec is None:
434                     return sympy.polys.domains.RR
435                 else:
436                     return sympy.polys.domains.RealField(int(prec))
437 
438             r = cls._re_complexfield.match(domain)
439 
440             if r is not None:
441                 _, _, prec = r.groups()
442 
443                 if prec is None:
444                     return sympy.polys.domains.CC
445                 else:
446                     return sympy.polys.domains.ComplexField(int(prec))
447 
448             r = cls._re_finitefield.match(domain)
449 
450             if r is not None:
451                 return sympy.polys.domains.FF(int(r.groups()[1]))
452 
453             r = cls._re_polynomial.match(domain)
454 
455             if r is not None:
456                 ground, gens = r.groups()
457 
458                 gens = list(map(sympify, gens.split(',')))
459 
460                 if ground in ['Z', 'ZZ']:
461                     return sympy.polys.domains.ZZ.poly_ring(*gens)
462                 else:
463                     return sympy.polys.domains.QQ.poly_ring(*gens)
464 
465             r = cls._re_fraction.match(domain)
466 
467             if r is not None:
468                 ground, gens = r.groups()
469 
470                 gens = list(map(sympify, gens.split(',')))
471

You will be provided with a partial code base and an issue statement explaining a problem to resolve.
<issue>
Merging 3 or more media objects can throw unnecessary MediaOrderConflictWarnings
Description
	
Consider the following form definition, where text-editor-extras.js depends on text-editor.js but all other JS files are independent:
from django import forms
class ColorPicker(forms.Widget):
	class Media:
		js = ['color-picker.js']
class SimpleTextWidget(forms.Widget):
	class Media:
		js = ['text-editor.js']
class FancyTextWidget(forms.Widget):
	class Media:
		js = ['text-editor.js', 'text-editor-extras.js', 'color-picker.js']
class MyForm(forms.Form):
	background_color = forms.CharField(widget=ColorPicker())
	intro = forms.CharField(widget=SimpleTextWidget())
	body = forms.CharField(widget=FancyTextWidget())
Django should be able to resolve the JS files for the final form into the order text-editor.js, text-editor-extras.js, color-picker.js. However, accessing MyForm().media results in:
/projects/django/django/forms/widgets.py:145: MediaOrderConflictWarning: Detected duplicate Media files in an opposite order:
text-editor-extras.js
text-editor.js
 MediaOrderConflictWarning,
Media(css={}, js=['text-editor-extras.js', 'color-picker.js', 'text-editor.js'])
The MediaOrderConflictWarning is a result of the order that the additions happen in: ColorPicker().media + SimpleTextWidget().media produces Media(css={}, js=['color-picker.js', 'text-editor.js']), which (wrongly) imposes the constraint that color-picker.js must appear before text-editor.js.
The final result is particularly unintuitive here, as it's worse than the "naïve" result produced by Django 1.11 before order-checking was added (color-picker.js, text-editor.js, text-editor-extras.js), and the pair of files reported in the warning message seems wrong too (aren't color-picker.js and text-editor.js the wrong-ordered ones?)

</issue>

122         order.
123 
124         For static assets it can be important to have them included in the DOM
125         in a certain order. In JavaScript you may not be able to reference a
126         global or in CSS you might want to override a style.
127         """
128         # Start with a copy of list_1.
129         combined_list = list(list_1)
130         last_insert_index = len(list_1)
131         # Walk list_2 in reverse, inserting each element into combined_list if
132         # it doesn't already exist.
133         for path in reversed(list_2):
134             try:
135                 # Does path already exist in the list?
136                 index = combined_list.index(path)
137             except ValueError:
138                 # Add path to combined_list since it doesn't exist.
139                 combined_list.insert(last_insert_index, path)
140             else:
141                 if index > last_insert_index:
142                     warnings.warn(
143                         'Detected duplicate Media files in an opposite order:\n'
144                         '%s\n%s' % (combined_list[last_insert_index], combined_list[index]),
145                         MediaOrderConflictWarning,
146                     )
147                 # path already exists in the list. Update last_insert_index so
148                 # that the following elements are inserted in front of this one.
149                 last_insert_index = index
150         return combined_list
151 
152     def __add__(self, other):
153         combined = Media()
154         combined._css_lists = self._css_lists + other._css_lists
155         combined._js_lists = self._js_lists + other._js_lists
156         return combined

159 def media_property(cls):
160     def _media(self):
161         # Get the media property of the superclass, if it exists
162         sup_cls = super(cls, self)
163         try:
164             base = sup_cls.media
165         except AttributeError:
166             base = Media()
167 
168         # Get the media definition for this class
169         definition = getattr(cls, 'Media', None)
170         if definition:
171             extend = getattr(definition, 'extend', True)
172             if extend:
173                 if extend is True:
174                     m = base
175                 else:
176                     m = Media()
177                     for medium in extend:
178                         m = m + base[medium]
179                 return m + Media(definition)
180             return Media(definition)
181         return base
182     return property(_media)
183

185 class MediaDefiningClass(type):
186     """
187     Metaclass for classes that can have media definitions.
188     """
189     def __new__(mcs, name, bases, attrs):
190         new_class = super(MediaDefiningClass, mcs).__new__(mcs, name, bases, attrs)
191 
192         if 'media' not in attrs:
193             new_class.media = media_property(new_class)
194 
195         return new_class

555     template_name = None
556     option_template_name = None
557     add_id_index = True
558     checked_attribute = {'checked': True}
559     option_inherits_attrs = True

561     def __init__(self, attrs=None, choices=()):
562         super().__init__(attrs)
563         # choices can be any iterable, but we may need to render this widget
564         # multiple times. Thus, collapse it into a list so it can be consumed
565         # more than once.
566         self.choices = list(choices)
567 
568     def __deepcopy__(self, memo):
569         obj = copy.copy(self)
570         obj.attrs = self.attrs.copy()
571         obj.choices = copy.copy(self.choices)
572         memo[id(self)] = obj
573         return obj

575     def subwidgets(self, name, value, attrs=None):
576         """
577         Yield all "subwidgets" of this widget. Used to enable iterating
578         options from a BoundField for choice widgets.
579         """
580         value = self.format_value(value)
581         yield from self.options(name, value, attrs)
582 
583     def options(self, name, value, attrs=None):
584         """Yield a flat list of options for this widgets."""
585         for group in self.optgroups(name, value, attrs):
586             yield from group[1]
587 
588     def optgroups(self, name, value, attrs=None):
589         """Return a list of optgroups for this widget."""
590         groups = []
591         has_selected = False
592 
593         for index, (option_value, option_label) in enumerate(self.choices):
594             if option_value is None:
595                 option_value = ''
596 
597             subgroup = []
598             if isinstance(option_label, (list, tuple)):
599                 group_name = option_value
600                 subindex = 0
601                 choices = option_label
602             else:
603                 group_name = None
604                 subindex = None
605                 choices = [(option_value, option_label)]
606             groups.append((group_name, subgroup, index))
607 
608             for subvalue, sublabel in choices:
609                 selected = (
610                     str(subvalue) in value and
611                     (not has_selected or self.allow_multiple_selected)
612                 )
613                 has_selected |= selected
614                 subgroup.append(self.create_option(
615                     name, subvalue, sublabel, selected, index,
616                     subindex=subindex, attrs=attrs,
617                 ))
618                 if subindex is not None:
619                     subindex += 1
620         return groups
621 
622     def create_option(self, name, value, label, selected, index, subindex=None, attrs=None):
623         index = str(index) if subindex is None else "%s_%s" % (index, subindex)
624         if attrs is None:
625             attrs = {}
626         option_attrs = self.build_attrs(self.attrs, attrs) if self.option_inherits_attrs else {}
627         if selected:
628             option_attrs.update(self.checked_attribute)
629         if 'id' in option_attrs:
630             option_attrs['id'] = self.id_for_label(option_attrs['id'], index)
631         return {
632             'name': name,
633             'value': value,
634             'label': label,
635             'selected': selected,
636             'index': index,
637             'attrs': option_attrs,
638             'type': self.input_type,
639             'template_name': self.option_template_name,
640             'wrap_label': True,
641         }
642 
643     def get_context(self, name, value, attrs):
644         context = super().get_context(name, value, attrs)
645         context['widget']['optgroups'] = self.optgroups(name, context['widget']['value'], attrs)
646         return context
647 
648     def id_for_label(self, id_, index='0'):
649         """
650         Use an incremented id for each option where the main widget
651         references the zero index.
652         """
653         if id_ and self.add_id_index:
654             id_ = '%s_%s' % (id_, index)
655         return id_
656 
657     def value_from_datadict(self, data, files, name):
658         getter = data.get
659         if self.allow_multiple_selected:
660             try:
661                 getter = data.getlist
662             except AttributeError:
663                 pass
664         return getter(name)
665 
666     def format_value(self, value):
667         """Return selected values as a list."""
668         if value is None and self.allow_multiple_selected:
669             return []
670         if not isinstance(value, (tuple, list)):
671             value = [value]
672         return [str(v) if v is not None else '' for v in value]

797     A widget that is composed of multiple widgets.
798 
799     In addition to the values added by Widget.get_context(), this widget
800     adds a list of subwidgets to the context as widget['subwidgets'].
801     These can be looped over and rendered like normal widgets.
802 
803     You'll probably want to use this class with MultiValueField.
804     """
805     template_name = 'django/forms/widgets/multiwidget.html'
806 
807     def __init__(self, widgets, attrs=None):
808         self.widgets = [w() if isinstance(w, type) else w for w in widgets]
809         super().__init__(attrs)
810 
811     @property
812     def is_hidden(self):
813         return all(w.is_hidden for w in self.widgets)
814 
815     def get_context(self, name, value, attrs):
816         context = super().get_context(name, value, attrs)
817         if self.is_localized:
818             for widget in self.widgets:
819                 widget.is_localized = self.is_localized
820         # value is a list of values, each corresponding to a widget
821         # in self.widgets.
822         if not isinstance(value, list):
823             value = self.decompress(value)
824 
825         final_attrs = context['widget']['attrs']
826         input_type = final_attrs.pop('type', None)
827         id_ = final_attrs.get('id')
828         subwidgets = []
829         for i, widget in enumerate(self.widgets):
830             if input_type is not None:
831                 widget.input_type = input_type
832             widget_name = '%s_%s' % (name, i)
833             try:
834                 widget_value = value[i]
835             except IndexError:
836                 widget_value = None

problem_statement:
Merging 3 or more media objects can throw unnecessary MediaOrderConflictWarnings
Description
	
Consider the following form definition, where text-editor-extras.js depends on text-editor.js but all other JS files are independent:
from django import forms
class ColorPicker(forms.Widget):
	class Media:
		js = ['color-picker.js']
class SimpleTextWidget(forms.Widget):
	class Media:
		js = ['text-editor.js']
class FancyTextWidget(forms.Widget):
	class Media:
		js = ['text-editor.js', 'text-editor-extras.js', 'color-picker.js']
class MyForm(forms.Form):
	background_color = forms.CharField(widget=ColorPicker())
	intro = forms.CharField(widget=SimpleTextWidget())
	body = forms.CharField(widget=FancyTextWidget())
Django should be able to resolve the JS files for the final form into the order text-editor.js, text-editor-extras.js, color-picker.js. However, accessing MyForm().media results in:
/projects/django/django/forms/widgets.py:145: MediaOrderConflictWarning: Detected duplicate Media files in an opposite order:
text-editor-extras.js
text-editor.js
 MediaOrderConflictWarning,
Media(css={}, js=['text-editor-extras.js', 'color-picker.js', 'text-editor.js'])
The MediaOrderConflictWarning is a result of the order that the additions happen in: ColorPicker().media + SimpleTextWidget().media produces Media(css={}, js=['color-picker.js', 'text-editor.js']), which (wrongly) imposes the constraint that color-picker.js must appear before text-editor.js.
The final result is particularly unintuitive here, as it's worse than the "naïve" result produced by Django 1.11 before order-checking was added (color-picker.js, text-editor.js, text-editor-extras.js), and the pair of files reported in the warning message seems wrong too (aren't color-picker.js and text-editor.js the wrong-ordered ones?)
hints_text:
As a tentative fix, I propose that media objects should explicitly distinguish between cases where we do / don't care about ordering, notionally something like: class FancyTextWidget(forms.Widget): class Media: js = { ('text-editor.js', 'text-editor-extras.js'), # tuple = order is important 'color-picker.js' # set = order is unimportant } (although using a set for this is problematic due to the need for contents to be hashable), and the result of adding two media objects should be a "don't care" so that we aren't introducing dependencies where the original objects didn't have them. We would then defer assembling them into a flat list until the final render call. I haven't worked out the rest of the algorithm yet, but I'm willing to dig further if this sounds like a sensible plan of attack...

I can (reluctantly) accept an implementation that produces false warnings, and I can accept that a genuine dependency loop might produce undefined behaviour, but the combination of the two - breaking the ordering as a result of seeing a loop that isn't there - is definitely a bug. (To be clear, I'm not suggesting that the 2.x implementation is a step backwards from not doing order checking at all - but it does introduce a new failure case, and that's what I'm keen to fix.)
To summarise: Even with the new strategy in #30153 of holding on to the un-merged lists as long as possible, the final merging is still done by adding one list at a time. The intermediate results are lists, which are assumed to be order-critical; this means the intermediate results have additional constraints that are not present in the original lists, causing it to see conflicts where there aren't any. Additionally, we should try to preserve the original sequence of files as much as possible, to avoid unnecessarily breaking user code that hasn't fully specified its dependencies and is relying on the 1.x behaviour. I think we need to approach this as a graph problem (which I realise might sound like overkill, but I'd rather start with something formally correct and optimise later as necessary): a conflict occurs whenever the dependency graph is cyclic. #30153 is a useful step towards this, as it ensures we have the accurate dependency graph up until the point where we need to assemble the final list. I suggest we replace Media.merge with a new method that accepts any number of lists (using *args if we want to preserve the existing method signature for backwards compatibility). This would work as follows: Iterate over all items in all sub-lists, building a dependency graph (where a dependency is any item that immediately precedes it within a sub-list) and a de-duplicated list containing all items indexed in the order they are first encountered Starting from the first item in the de-duplicated list, backtrack through the dependency graph, following the lowest-indexed dependency each time until we reach an item with no dependencies. While backtracking, maintain a stack of visited items. If we encounter an item already on the stack, this is a dependency loop; throw a MediaOrderConflictWarning and break out of the backtracking loop Output the resulting item, then remove it from the dependency graph and the de-duplicated list If the 'visited items' stack is non-empty, pop the last item off it and repeat the backtracking step from there. Otherwise, repeat the backtracking step starting from the next item in the de-duplicated list Repeat until no items remain

Django 3.0: "GROUP BY" clauses error with tricky field annotation
Description
	
Let's pretend that we have next model structure with next model's relations:
class A(models.Model):
	bs = models.ManyToManyField('B',
								related_name="a",
								through="AB")
class B(models.Model):
	pass
class AB(models.Model):
	a = models.ForeignKey(A, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name="ab_a")
	b = models.ForeignKey(B, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name="ab_b")
	status = models.IntegerField()
class C(models.Model):
	a = models.ForeignKey(
		A,
		null=True,
		blank=True,
		on_delete=models.SET_NULL,
		related_name="c",
		verbose_name=_("a")
	)
	status = models.IntegerField()
Let's try to evaluate next query
ab_query = AB.objects.filter(a=OuterRef("pk"), b=1)
filter_conditions = Q(pk=1) | Q(ab_a__b=1)
query = A.objects.\
	filter(filter_conditions).\
	annotate(
		status=Subquery(ab_query.values("status")),
		c_count=Count("c"),
)
answer = query.values("status").annotate(total_count=Count("status"))
print(answer.query)
print(answer)
On Django 3.0.4 we have an error
