879 _idn = lambda x: x
880 _midn = lambda x: -x
881 _one = lambda x: S.One

883 def _match_div_rewrite(expr, i):
884     """helper for __trigsimp"""
885     if i == 0:
886         expr = _replace_mul_fpowxgpow(expr, sin, cos,
887             _midn, tan, _idn)
888     elif i == 1:
889         expr = _replace_mul_fpowxgpow(expr, tan, cos,
890             _idn, sin, _idn)
891     elif i == 2:
892         expr = _replace_mul_fpowxgpow(expr, cot, sin,
893             _idn, cos, _idn)
894     elif i == 3:
895         expr = _replace_mul_fpowxgpow(expr, tan, sin,
896             _midn, cos, _midn)
897     elif i == 4:
898         expr = _replace_mul_fpowxgpow(expr, cot, cos,
899             _midn, sin, _midn)
900     elif i == 5:
901         expr = _replace_mul_fpowxgpow(expr, cot, tan,
902             _idn, _one, _idn)
903     # i in (6, 7) is skipped
904     elif i == 8:
905         expr = _replace_mul_fpowxgpow(expr, sinh, cosh,
906             _midn, tanh, _idn)
907     elif i == 9:
908         expr = _replace_mul_fpowxgpow(expr, tanh, cosh,
909             _idn, sinh, _idn)
910     elif i == 10:
911         expr = _replace_mul_fpowxgpow(expr, coth, sinh,
912             _idn, cosh, _idn)
913     elif i == 11:
914         expr = _replace_mul_fpowxgpow(expr, tanh, sinh,
915             _midn, cosh, _midn)
916     elif i == 12:
917         expr = _replace_mul_fpowxgpow(expr, coth, cosh,
918             _midn, sinh, _midn)
919     elif i == 13:
920         expr = _replace_mul_fpowxgpow(expr, coth, tanh,
921             _idn, _one, _idn)
922     else:
923         return None
924     return expr

935 @cacheit
936 def __trigsimp(expr, deep=False):
937     """recursive helper for trigsimp"""
938     from sympy.simplify.fu import TR10i
939 
940     if _trigpat is None:
941         _trigpats()
942     a, b, c, d, matchers_division, matchers_add, \
943     matchers_identity, artifacts = _trigpat
944 
945     if expr.is_Mul:
946         # do some simplifications like sin/cos -> tan:
947         if not expr.is_commutative:
948             com, nc = expr.args_cnc()
949             expr = _trigsimp(Mul._from_args(com), deep)*Mul._from_args(nc)
950         else:
951             for i, (pattern, simp, ok1, ok2) in enumerate(matchers_division):
952                 if not _dotrig(expr, pattern):
953                     continue
954 
955                 newexpr = _match_div_rewrite(expr, i)
956                 if newexpr is not None:
957                     if newexpr != expr:
958                         expr = newexpr
959                         break
960                     else:
961                         continue
962 
963                 # use SymPy matching instead
964                 res = expr.match(pattern)
965                 if res and res.get(c, 0):
966                     if not res[c].is_integer:
967                         ok = ok1.subs(res)
968                         if not ok.is_positive:
969                             continue
970                         ok = ok2.subs(res)
971                         if not ok.is_positive:
972                             continue
973                     # if "a" contains any of trig or hyperbolic funcs with
974                     # argument "b" then skip the simplification
975                     if any(w.args[0] == res[b] for w in res[a].atoms(
976                             TrigonometricFunction, HyperbolicFunction)):
977                         continue
978                     # simplify and finish:
979                     expr = simp.subs(res)
980                     break  # process below
981 
982     if expr.is_Add:
983         args = []
984         for term in expr.args:
985             if not term.is_commutative:
986                 com, nc = term.args_cnc()
987                 nc = Mul._from_args(nc)
988                 term = Mul._from_args(com)
989             else:
990                 nc = S.One
991             term = _trigsimp(term, deep)
992             for pattern, result in matchers_identity:
993                 res = term.match(pattern)
994                 if res is not None:
995                     term = result.subs(res)
996                     break
997             args.append(term*nc)
998         if args != expr.args:
999             expr = Add(*args)
1000             expr = min(expr, expand(expr), key=count_ops)
1001         if expr.is_Add:
1002             for pattern, result in matchers_add:
1003                 if not _dotrig(expr, pattern):
1004                     continue
1005                 expr = TR10i(expr)
1006                 if expr.has(HyperbolicFunction):
1007                     res = expr.match(pattern)
1008                     # if "d" contains any trig or hyperbolic funcs with
1009                     # argument "a" or "b" then skip the simplification;
1010                     # this isn't perfect -- see tests
1011                     if res is None or not (a in res and b in res) or any(
1012                         w.args[0] in (res[a], res[b]) for w in res[d].atoms(
1013                             TrigonometricFunction, HyperbolicFunction)):
1014                         continue
1015                     expr = result.subs(res)
1016                     break
1017 
1018         # Reduce any lingering artifacts, such as sin(x)**2 changing
1019         # to 1 - cos(x)**2 when sin(x)**2 was "simpler"
1020         for pattern, result, ex in artifacts:
1021             if not _dotrig(expr, pattern):
1022                 continue
1023             # Substitute a new wild that excludes some function(s)
1024             # to help influence a better match. This is because
1025             # sometimes, for example, 'a' would match sec(x)**2
1026             a_t = Wild('a', exclude=[ex])
1027             pattern = pattern.subs(a, a_t)
1028             result = result.subs(a, a_t)
1029 
1030             m = expr.match(pattern)
1031             was = None
1032             while m and was != expr:
1033                 was = expr
1034                 if m[a_t] == 0 or \
1035                         -m[a_t] in m[c].args or m[a_t] + m[c] == 0:
1036                     break
1037                 if d in m and m[a_t]*m[d] + m[c] == 0:
1038                     break
1039                 expr = result.subs(m)
1040                 m = expr.match(pattern)
1041                 m.setdefault(c, S.Zero)
1042 
1043     elif expr.is_Mul or expr.is_Pow or deep and expr.args:
1044         expr = expr.func(*[_trigsimp(a, deep) for a in expr.args])
1045 
1046     try:

```
sin(1/25)*sin(3/50) + cos(1/25)*cos(3/50)
cos(1/50)
```
Trigonometric simplifications are performed by `trigsimp`. It works by calling sequentially functions defined in the `fu` module. This particular simplification is carried out by `TR10i` which comes right after `TRmorrie` in the [list of methods](https://github.com/sympy/sympy/blob/master/sympy/simplify/trigsimp.py#L1131-L1164).

`TRmorrie` does a very special type of transformation:
 
    Returns cos(x)*cos(2*x)*...*cos(2**(k-1)*x) -> sin(2**k*x)/(2**k*sin(x))

In this example, it will transform the expression into a form that `TR10i` can no more recognize.
```
>>> from sympy.simplify.fu import TRmorrie
>>> x = S(1)/50
>>> e = sin(x)*sin(2*x) + cos(x)*cos(2*x)
>>> TRmorrie(e)
sin(1/50)*sin(1/25) + sin(2/25)/(4*sin(1/50))
```
I cannot think of any reason why `TRmorrie` should come before `TR10i`. This issue could probably be fixed by changing the order of these two functions.
So, if the user-input expression varies, there is no way to simplify the expression to a very simple formation, isn't it?
I think that this issue could be fixed by changing the order of `TRmorrie` and `TR10i`. (But, of course, there may be other issues in simplification that this will not resolve.)
That should be easy to fix, assuming it works. If it doesn't work then the actual fix may be more complicated.

problem_statement:
Modeling's `separability_matrix` does not compute separability correctly for nested CompoundModels
Consider the following model:

```python
from astropy.modeling import models as m
from astropy.modeling.separable import separability_matrix

cm = m.Linear1D(10) & m.Linear1D(5)
```

It's separability matrix as you might expect is a diagonal:

```python
>>> separability_matrix(cm)
array([[ True, False],
       [False,  True]])
```

If I make the model more complex:
```python
>>> separability_matrix(m.Pix2Sky_TAN() & m.Linear1D(10) & m.Linear1D(5))
array([[ True,  True, False, False],
       [ True,  True, False, False],
       [False, False,  True, False],
       [False, False, False,  True]])
```

The output matrix is again, as expected, the outputs and inputs to the linear models are separable and independent of each other.

If however, I nest these compound models:
```python
>>> separability_matrix(m.Pix2Sky_TAN() & cm)
array([[ True,  True, False, False],
       [ True,  True, False, False],
       [False, False,  True,  True],
       [False, False,  True,  True]])
```
Suddenly the inputs and outputs are no longer separable?

This feels like a bug to me, but I might be missing something?

diff --git a/astropy/modeling/separable.py b/astropy/modeling/separable.py
--- a/astropy/modeling/separable.py
+++ b/astropy/modeling/separable.py
@@ -242,7 +242,7 @@ def _cstack(left, right):
         cright = _coord_matrix(right, 'right', noutp)
     else:
         cright = np.zeros((noutp, right.shape[1]))
-        cright[-right.shape[0]:, -right.shape[1]:] = 1
+        cright[-right.shape[0]:, -right.shape[1]:] = right
 
     return np.hstack([cleft, cright])
 

</patch>

ColumnTransformer with pandas output can't handle transformers with no features
### Describe the bug

Hi,

ColumnTransformer doesn't deal well with transformers that apply to 0 features (categorical_features in the example below) when using "pandas" as output. It seems steps with 0 features are not fitted, hence don't appear in `self._iter(fitted=True)` (_column_transformer.py l.856) and hence break the input to the `_add_prefix_for_feature_names_out` function (l.859).


### Steps/Code to Reproduce

Here is some code to reproduce the error. If you remove .set_output(transform="pandas") on the line before last, all works fine. If you remove the ("categorical", ...) step, it works fine too.

```python
import numpy as np

from sklearn.compose import ColumnTransformer

pipeline = Pipeline([model_preprocessing, ("classifier", LGBMClassifier())]).set_output(transform="pandas")
pipeline.fit(X, y)
```

41 class ColumnTransformer(TransformerMixin, _BaseComposition):
42     """Applies transformers to columns of an array or pandas DataFrame.
43 
44     This estimator allows different columns or column subsets of the input
45     to be transformed separately and the features generated by each transformer
46     will be concatenated to form a single feature space.
47     This is useful for heterogeneous or columnar data, to combine several
48     feature extraction mechanisms or transformations into a single transformer.
49 
50     Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <column_transformer>`.
51 
52     .. versionadded:: 0.20
53 
54     Parameters
55     ----------
56     transformers : list of tuples
57         List of (name, transformer, columns) tuples specifying the
58         transformer objects to be applied to subsets of the data.
59 
60         name : str
61             Like in Pipeline and FeatureUnion, this allows the transformer and
62             its parameters to be set using ``set_params`` and searched in grid
63             search.
64         transformer : {'drop', 'passthrough'} or estimator
65             Estimator must support :term:`fit` and :term:`transform`.
66             Special-cased strings 'drop' and 'passthrough' are accepted as
67             well, to indicate to drop the columns or to pass them through
68             untransformed, respectively.
69         columns :  str, array-like of str, int, array-like of int, \
70                 array-like of bool, slice or callable
71             Indexes the data on its second axis. Integers are interpreted as
72             positional columns, while strings can reference DataFrame columns
73             by name.  A scalar string or int should be used where
74             ``transformer`` expects X to be a 1d array-like (vector),
75             otherwise a 2d array will be passed to the transformer.
76             A callable is passed the input data `X` and can return any of the
77             above. To select multiple columns by name or dtype, you can use
78             :obj:`make_column_selector`.
79 
80     remainder : {'drop', 'passthrough'} or estimator, default='drop'
81         By default, only the specified columns in `transformers` are
82         transformed and combined in the output, and the non-specified
83         columns are dropped. (default of ``'drop'``).
84         By specifying ``remainder='passthrough'``, all remaining columns that
85         were not specified in `transformers`, but present in the data passed
86         to `fit` will be automatically passed through. This subset of columns
87         is concatenated with the output of the transformers. For dataframes,
88         extra columns not seen during `fit` will be excluded from the output
89         of `transform`.
90         By setting ``remainder`` to be an estimator, the remaining
91         non-specified columns will use the ``remainder`` estimator. The
92         estimator must support :term:`fit` and :term:`transform`.
93         Note that using this feature requires that the DataFrame columns
94         input at :term:`fit` and :term:`transform` have identical order.
95 
96     sparse_threshold : float, default=0.3
97         If the output of the different transformers contains sparse matrices,
98         these will be stacked as a sparse matrix if the overall density is
99         lower than this value. Use ``sparse_threshold=0`` to always return
100         dense.  When the transformed output consists of all dense data, the
101         stacked result will be dense, and this keyword will be ignored.
102 
103     n_jobs : int, default=None
104         Number of jobs to run in parallel.
105         ``None`` means 1 unless in a :obj:`joblib.parallel_backend` context.
106         ``-1`` means using all processors. See :term:`Glossary <n_jobs>`
107         for more details.
108 
109     transformer_weights : dict, default=None
110         Multiplicative weights for features per transformer. The output of the
111         transformer is multiplied by these weights. Keys are transformer names,
112         values the weights.
113 
114     verbose : bool, default=False
115         If True, the time elapsed while fitting each transformer will be
116         printed as it is completed.
117 
118     verbose_feature_names_out : bool, default=True
119         If True, :meth:`get_feature_names_out` will prefix all feature names
120         with the name of the transformer that generated that feature.
121         If False, :meth:`get_feature_names_out` will not prefix any feature
122         names and will error if feature names are not unique.
123 
124         .. versionadded:: 1.0
125 
126     Attributes
127     ----------
128     transformers_ : list
129         The collection of fitted transformers as tuples of
130         (name, fitted_transformer, column). `fitted_transformer` can be an
131         estimator, 'drop', or 'passthrough'. In case there were no columns
132         selected, this will be the unfitted transformer.
133         If there are remaining columns, the final element is a tuple of the
134         form:
135         ('remainder', transformer, remaining_columns) corresponding to the
136         ``remainder`` parameter. If there are remaining columns, then
137         ``len(transformers_)==len(transformers)+1``, otherwise
138         ``len(transformers_)==len(transformers)``.
139 
140     named_transformers_ : :class:`~sklearn.utils.Bunch`
141         Read-only attribute to access any transformer by given name.
142         Keys are transformer names and values are the fitted transformer
143         objects.
144 
145     sparse_output_ : bool
146         Boolean flag indicating whether the output of ``transform`` is a
147         sparse matrix or a dense numpy array, which depends on the output
148         of the individual transformers and the `sparse_threshold` keyword.
149 
150     output_indices_ : dict
151         A dictionary from each transformer name to a slice, where the slice
152         corresponds to indices in the transformed output. This is useful to
153         inspect which transformer is responsible for which transformed
154         feature(s).
155 
156         .. versionadded:: 1.0
157 
158     n_features_in_ : int
159         Number of features seen during :term:`fit`. Only defined if the
160         underlying transformers expose such an attribute when fit.
161 
162         .. versionadded:: 0.24
163 
164     See Also
165     --------
166     make_column_transformer : Convenience function for
167         combining the outputs of multiple transformer objects applied to
168         column subsets of the original feature space.
169     make_column_selector : Convenience function for selecting
170         columns based on datatype or the columns name with a regex pattern.
171 
172     Notes
173     -----
174     The order of the columns in the transformed feature matrix follows the
175     order of how the columns are specified in the `transformers` list.
176     Columns of the original feature matrix that are not specified are
177     dropped from the resulting transformed feature matrix, unless specified
178     in the `passthrough` keyword. Those columns specified with `passthrough`
179     are added at the right to the output of the transformers.
180 
181     Examples
182     --------
183     >>> import numpy as np
184     >>> from sklearn.compose import ColumnTransformer
185     >>> from sklearn.preprocessing import Normalizer
186     >>> ct = ColumnTransformer(
187     ...     [("norm1", Normalizer(norm='l1'), [0, 1]),
188     ...      ("norm2", Normalizer(norm='l1'), slice(2, 4))])
189     >>> X = np.array([[0., 1., 2., 2.],
190     ...               [1., 1., 0., 1.]])
191     >>> # Normalizer scales each row of X to unit norm. A separate scaling
192     >>> # is applied for the two first and two last elements of each
193     >>> # row independently.
194     >>> ct.fit_transform(X)
195     array([[0. , 1. , 0.5, 0.5],
196            [0.5, 0.5, 0. , 1. ]])
197 
198     :class:`ColumnTransformer` can be configured with a transformer that requires
199     a 1d array by setting the column to a string:
200 
201     >>> from sklearn.feature_extraction import FeatureHasher
202     >>> from sklearn.preprocessing import MinMaxScaler
203     >>> import pandas as pd   # doctest: +SKIP
204     >>> X = pd.DataFrame({
205     ...     "documents": ["First item", "second one here", "Is this the last?"],
206     ...     "width": [3, 4, 5],
207     ... })  # doctest: +SKIP
208     >>> # "documents" is a string which configures ColumnTransformer to
209     >>> # pass the documents column as a 1d array to the FeatureHasher
210     >>> ct = ColumnTransformer(
211     ...     [("text_preprocess", FeatureHasher(input_type="string"), "documents"),
212     ...      ("num_preprocess", MinMaxScaler(), ["width"])])
213     >>> X_trans = ct.fit_transform(X)  # doctest: +SKIP
214     """
215 
216     _required_parameters = ["transformers"]
217 
218     _parameter_constraints: dict = {
219         "transformers": [list, Hidden(tuple)],
220         "remainder": [
221             StrOptions({"drop", "passthrough"}),
222             HasMethods(["fit", "transform"]),
223             HasMethods(["fit_transform", "transform"]),
224         ],
225         "sparse_threshold": [Interval(Real, 0, 1, closed="both")],
226         "n_jobs": [Integral, None],
227         "transformer_weights": [dict, None],
228         "verbose": ["verbose"],
229         "verbose_feature_names_out": ["boolean"],
230     }

232     def __init__(
233         self,
234         transformers,
235         *,
236         remainder="drop",
237         sparse_threshold=0.3,
238         n_jobs=None,
239         transformer_weights=None,
240         verbose=False,
241         verbose_feature_names_out=True,
242     ):
243         self.transformers = transformers
244         self.remainder = remainder
245         self.sparse_threshold = sparse_threshold
246         self.n_jobs = n_jobs
247         self.transformer_weights = transformer_weights
248         self.verbose = verbose
249         self.verbose_feature_names_out = verbose_feature_names_out

251     @property
252     def _transformers(self):
253         """
254         Internal list of transformer only containing the name and
255         transformers, dropping the columns. This is for the implementation
256         of get_params via BaseComposition._get_params which expects lists
257         of tuples of len 2.
258         """
259         try:
260             return [(name, trans) for name, trans, _ in self.transformers]
261         except (TypeError, ValueError):
262             return self.transformers
263 
264     @_transformers.setter
265     def _transformers(self, value):
266         try:
267             self.transformers = [
268                 (name, trans, col)
269                 for ((name, trans), (_, _, col)) in zip(value, self.transformers)
270             ]
271         except (TypeError, ValueError):
272             self.transformers = value

274     def set_output(self, *, transform=None):
275         """Set the output container when `"transform"` and `"fit_transform"` are called.
276 
277         Calling `set_output` will set the output of all estimators in `transformers`
278         and `transformers_`.
279 
280         Parameters
281         ----------
282         transform : {"default", "pandas"}, default=None
283             Configure output of `transform` and `fit_transform`.
284 
285             - `"default"`: Default output format of a transformer
286             - `"pandas"`: DataFrame output
287             - `None`: Transform configuration is unchanged
288 
289         Returns
290         -------
291         self : estimator instance
292             Estimator instance.
293         """
294         super().set_output(transform=transform)
295         transformers = (
296             trans
297             for _, trans, _ in chain(
298                 self.transformers, getattr(self, "transformers_", [])
299             )
300             if trans not in {"passthrough", "drop"}
301         )
302         for trans in transformers:
303             _safe_set_output(trans, transform=transform)
304 
305         return self

347     def _iter(self, fitted=False, replace_strings=False, column_as_strings=False):
348         """
349         Generate (name, trans, column, weight) tuples.
350 
351         If fitted=True, use the fitted transformers, else use the
352         user specified transformers updated with converted column names
353         and potentially appended with transformer for remainder.
354 
355         """
356         if fitted:
357             if replace_strings:
358                 # Replace "passthrough" with the fitted version in
359                 # _name_to_fitted_passthrough
360                 def replace_passthrough(name, trans, columns):
361                     if name not in self._name_to_fitted_passthrough:
362                         return name, trans, columns
363                     return name, self._name_to_fitted_passthrough[name], columns
364 
365                 transformers = [
366                     replace_passthrough(*trans) for trans in self.transformers_
367                 ]
368             else:
369                 transformers = self.transformers_
370         else:
371             # interleave the validated column specifiers
372             transformers = [
373                 (name, trans, column)
374                 for (name, trans, _), column in zip(self.transformers, self._columns)
375             ]
376             # add transformer tuple for remainder
377             if self._remainder[2]:
378                 transformers = chain(transformers, [self._remainder])
379         get_weight = (self.transformer_weights or {}).get
380 
381         output_config = _get_output_config("transform", self)
382         for name, trans, columns in transformers:
383             if replace_strings:
384                 # replace 'passthrough' with identity transformer and
385                 # skip in case of 'drop'
386                 if trans == "passthrough":
387                     trans = FunctionTransformer(
388                         accept_sparse=True,
389                         check_inverse=False,
390                         feature_names_out="one-to-one",
391                     ).set_output(transform=output_config["dense"])
392                 elif trans == "drop":
393                     continue
394                 elif _is_empty_column_selection(columns):
395                     continue
396 
397             if column_as_strings:
398                 # Convert all columns to using their string labels
399                 columns_is_scalar = np.isscalar(columns)
400 
401                 indices = self._transformer_to_input_indices[name]
402                 columns = self.feature_names_in_[indices]
403 
404                 if columns_is_scalar:
405                     # selection is done with one dimension
406                     columns = columns[0]
407 
408             yield (name, trans, columns, get_weight(name))
409 
410     def _validate_transformers(self):
411         if not self.transformers:
412             return
413 
414         names, transformers, _ = zip(*self.transformers)
415 
416         # validate names
417         self._validate_names(names)
418 
419         # validate estimators
420         for t in transformers:
421             if t in ("drop", "passthrough"):
422                 continue
423             if not (hasattr(t, "fit") or hasattr(t, "fit_transform")) or not hasattr(
424                 t, "transform"
425             ):
426                 # Used to validate the transformers in the `transformers` list
427                 raise TypeError(
428                     "All estimators should implement fit and "
429                     "transform, or can be 'drop' or 'passthrough' "
430                     "specifiers. '%s' (type %s) doesn't." % (t, type(t))
431                 )
432 
433     def _validate_column_callables(self, X):
434         """
435         Converts callable column specifications.
436         """
437         all_columns = []
438         transformer_to_input_indices = {}
439         for name, _, columns in self.transformers:
440             if callable(columns):
441                 columns = columns(X)
442             all_columns.append(columns)
443             transformer_to_input_indices[name] = _get_column_indices(X, columns)
444 
445         self._columns = all_columns
446         self._transformer_to_input_indices = transformer_to_input_indices
447 
448     def _validate_remainder(self, X):
449         """
450         Validates ``remainder`` and defines ``_remainder`` targeting
451         the remaining columns.
452         """
453         self._n_features = X.shape[1]
454         cols = set(chain(*self._transformer_to_input_indices.values()))
455         remaining = sorted(set(range(self._n_features)) - cols)
456         self._remainder = ("remainder", self.remainder, remaining)
457         self._transformer_to_input_indices["remainder"] = remaining
458 
459     @property
460     def named_transformers_(self):
461         """Access the fitted transformer by name.
462 
463         Read-only attribute to access any transformer by given name.
464         Keys are transformer names and values are the fitted transformer
465         objects.
466         """
467         # Use Bunch object to improve autocomplete
468         return Bunch(**{name: trans for name, trans, _ in self.transformers_})

470     def _get_feature_name_out_for_transformer(
471         self, name, trans, column, feature_names_in
472     ):
473         """Gets feature names of transformer.
474 
475         Used in conjunction with self._iter(fitted=True) in get_feature_names_out.
476         """
477         column_indices = self._transformer_to_input_indices[name]
478         names = feature_names_in[column_indices]
479         if trans == "drop" or _is_empty_column_selection(column):
480             return
481         elif trans == "passthrough":
482             return names
483 
484         # An actual transformer
485         if not hasattr(trans, "get_feature_names_out"):
486             raise AttributeError(
487                 f"Transformer {name} (type {type(trans).__name__}) does "
488                 "not provide get_feature_names_out."
489             )
490         return trans.get_feature_names_out(names)
491 
492     def get_feature_names_out(self, input_features=None):
493         """Get output feature names for transformation.
494 
495         Parameters
496         ----------
497         input_features : array-like of str or None, default=None
498             Input features.
499 
500             - If `input_features` is `None`, then `feature_names_in_` is
501               used as feature names in. If `feature_names_in_` is not defined,
502               then the following input feature names are generated:
503               `["x0", "x1", ..., "x(n_features_in_ - 1)"]`.
504             - If `input_features` is an array-like, then `input_features` must
505               match `feature_names_in_` if `feature_names_in_` is defined.
506 
507         Returns
508         -------
509         feature_names_out : ndarray of str objects
510             Transformed feature names.
511         """
512         check_is_fitted(self)
513         input_features = _check_feature_names_in(self, input_features)
514 
515         # List of tuples (name, feature_names_out)
516         transformer_with_feature_names_out = []
517         for name, trans, column, _ in self._iter(fitted=True):
518             feature_names_out = self._get_feature_name_out_for_transformer(
519                 name, trans, column, input_features
520             )
521             if feature_names_out is None:
522                 continue
523             transformer_with_feature_names_out.append((name, feature_names_out))
524 
525         if not transformer_with_feature_names_out:
526             # No feature names
527             return np.array([], dtype=object)
528 
529         return self._add_prefix_for_feature_names_out(
530             transformer_with_feature_names_out
531         )
532 
533     def _add_prefix_for_feature_names_out(self, transformer_with_feature_names_out):
534         """Add prefix for feature names out that includes the transformer names.
535 
536         Parameters
537         ----------
538         transformer_with_feature_names_out : list of tuples of (str, array-like of str)
539             The tuple consistent of the transformer's name and its feature names out.
540 
541         Returns
542         -------
543         feature_names_out : ndarray of shape (n_features,), dtype=str
544             Transformed feature names.
545         """
546         if self.verbose_feature_names_out:
547             # Prefix the feature names out with the transformers name
548             names = list(
549                 chain.from_iterable(
550                     (f"{name}__{i}" for i in feature_names_out)
551                     for name, feature_names_out in transformer_with_feature_names_out
552                 )
553             )
554             return np.asarray(names, dtype=object)
555 
556         # verbose_feature_names_out is False
557         # Check that names are all unique without a prefix
558         feature_names_count = Counter(
559             chain.from_iterable(s for _, s in transformer_with_feature_names_out)
560         )
561         top_6_overlap = [
562             name for name, count in feature_names_count.most_common(6) if count > 1
563         ]
564         top_6_overlap.sort()
565         if top_6_overlap:
566             if len(top_6_overlap) == 6:
567                 # There are more than 5 overlapping names, we only show the 5
568                 # of the feature names
569                 names_repr = str(top_6_overlap[:5])[:-1] + ", ...]"
570             else:
571                 names_repr = str(top_6_overlap)
572             raise ValueError(
573                 f"Output feature names: {names_repr} are not unique. Please set "
574                 "verbose_feature_names_out=True to add prefixes to feature names"
575             )
576 
577         return np.concatenate(
578             [name for _, name in transformer_with_feature_names_out],
579         )
580 
581     def _update_fitted_transformers(self, transformers):
582         # transformers are fitted; excludes 'drop' cases
583         fitted_transformers = iter(transformers)
584         transformers_ = []
585         self._name_to_fitted_passthrough = {}
586 
587         for name, old, column, _ in self._iter():
588             if old == "drop":
589                 trans = "drop"
590             elif old == "passthrough":
591                 # FunctionTransformer is present in list of transformers,
592                 # so get next transformer, but save original string
593                 func_transformer = next(fitted_transformers)
594                 trans = "passthrough"
595 
596                 # The fitted FunctionTransformer is saved in another attribute,
597                 # so it can be used during transform for set_output.
598                 self._name_to_fitted_passthrough[name] = func_transformer
599             elif _is_empty_column_selection(column):
600                 trans = old
601             else:
602                 trans = next(fitted_transformers)
603             transformers_.append((name, trans, column))
604 
605         # sanity check that transformers is exhausted
606         assert not list(fitted_transformers)
607         self.transformers_ = transformers_
608 
609     def _validate_output(self, result):
610         """
611         Ensure that the output of each transformer is 2D. Otherwise
612         hstack can raise an error or produce incorrect results.
613         """
614         names = [
615             name for name, _, _, _ in self._iter(fitted=True, replace_strings=True)
616         ]
617         for Xs, name in zip(result, names):
618             if not getattr(Xs, "ndim", 0) == 2:
619                 raise ValueError(
620                     "The output of the '{0}' transformer should be 2D (scipy "
621                     "matrix, array, or pandas DataFrame).".format(name)
622                 )
623 
624     def _record_output_indices(self, Xs):
625         """
626         Record which transformer produced which column.
627         """
628         idx = 0
629         self.output_indices_ = {}
630 
631         for transformer_idx, (name, _, _, _) in enumerate(
632             self._iter(fitted=True, replace_strings=True)
633         ):
634             n_columns = Xs[transformer_idx].shape[1]
635             self.output_indices_[name] = slice(idx, idx + n_columns)
636             idx += n_columns
637 
638         # `_iter` only generates transformers that have a non empty
639         # selection. Here we set empty slices for transformers that
640         # generate no output, which are safe for indexing
641         all_names = [t[0] for t in self.transformers] + ["remainder"]
642         for name in all_names:
643             if name not in self.output_indices_:
644                 self.output_indices_[name] = slice(0, 0)
645 
646     def _log_message(self, name, idx, total):
647         if not self.verbose:
648             return None
649         return "(%d of %d) Processing %s" % (idx, total, name)
650 
651     def _fit_transform(self, X, y, func, fitted=False, column_as_strings=False):
652         """
653         Private function to fit and/or transform on demand.
654 
655         Return value (transformers and/or transformed X data) depends
656         on the passed function.
657         ``fitted=True`` ensures the fitted transformers are used.
658         """
659         transformers = list(
660             self._iter(
661                 fitted=fitted, replace_strings=True, column_as_strings=column_as_strings
662             )
663         )
664         try:
665             return Parallel(n_jobs=self.n_jobs)(
666                 delayed(func)(
667                     transformer=clone(trans) if not fitted else trans,
668                     X=_safe_indexing(X, column, axis=1),
669                     y=y,
670                     weight=weight,
671                     message_clsname="ColumnTransformer",
672                     message=self._log_message(name, idx, len(transformers)),
673                 )
674                 for idx, (name, trans, column, weight) in enumerate(transformers, 1)
675             )
676         except ValueError as e:
677             if "Expected 2D array, got 1D array instead" in str(e):
678                 raise ValueError(_ERR_MSG_1DCOLUMN) from e
679             else:
680                 raise
681 
682     def fit(self, X, y=None):
683         """Fit all transformers using X.
684 
685         Parameters
686         ----------
687         X : {array-like, dataframe} of shape (n_samples, n_features)
688             Input data, of which specified subsets are used to fit the
689             transformers.
690 
691         y : array-like of shape (n_samples,...), default=None
692             Targets for supervised learning.
693 
694         Returns
695         -------
696         self : ColumnTransformer
697             This estimator.
698         """
699         self._validate_params()
700         # we use fit_transform to make sure to set sparse_output_ (for which we
701         # need the transformed data) to have consistent output type in predict
702         self.fit_transform(X, y=y)
703         return self
704 
705     def fit_transform(self, X, y=None):
706         """Fit all transformers, transform the data and concatenate results.
707 
708         Parameters
709         ----------
710         X : {array-like, dataframe} of shape (n_samples, n_features)
711             Input data, of which specified subsets are used to fit the
712             transformers.
713

ColumnTransformer with pandas output can't handle transformers with no features
### Describe the bug

Hi,

ColumnTransformer doesn't deal well with transformers that apply to 0 features (categorical_features in the example below) when using "pandas" as output. It seems steps with 0 features are not fitted, hence don't appear in `self._iter(fitted=True)` (_column_transformer.py l.856) and hence break the input to the `_add_prefix_for_feature_names_out` function (l.859).

Here is some code to reproduce the error. If you remove .set_output(transform="pandas") on the line before last, all works fine. If you remove the ("categorical", ...) step, it works fine too.

```python

pipeline = Pipeline([model_preprocessing, ("classifier", LGBMClassifier())]).set_output(transform="pandas")
```

<issue>
Self referencing foreign key doesn't correctly order by a relation "_id" field.
Description
	
Initially discovered on 2.2.10 but verified still happens on 3.0.6. Given the following models:
class OneModel(models.Model):
	class Meta:
		ordering = ("-id",)
	id = models.BigAutoField(primary_key=True)
	root = models.ForeignKey("OneModel", on_delete=models.CASCADE, null=True)
	oneval = models.BigIntegerField(null=True)
class TwoModel(models.Model):
	id = models.BigAutoField(primary_key=True)
	record = models.ForeignKey(OneModel, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
	twoval = models.BigIntegerField(null=True)
The following queryset gives unexpected results and appears to be an incorrect SQL query:
qs = TwoModel.objects.filter(record__oneval__in=[1,2,3])
qs = qs.order_by("record__root_id")
print(qs.query)
SELECT "orion_twomodel"."id", "orion_twomodel"."record_id", "orion_twomodel"."twoval" FROM "orion_twomodel" INNER JOIN "orion_onemodel" ON ("orion_twomodel"."record_id" = "orion_onemodel"."id") LEFT OUTER JOIN "orion_onemodel" T3 ON ("orion_onemodel"."root_id" = T3."id") WHERE "orion_onemodel"."oneval" IN (1, 2, 3) ORDER BY T3."id" DESC
The query has an unexpected DESCENDING sort. That appears to come from the default sort order on the OneModel class, but I would expect the order_by() to take prececence. The the query has two JOINS, which is unnecessary. It appears that, since OneModel.root is a foreign key to itself, that is causing it to do the unnecessary extra join. In fact, testing a model where root is a foreign key to a third model doesn't show the problem behavior.
Note also that the queryset with order_by("record__root") gives the exact same SQL.
This queryset gives correct results and what looks like a pretty optimal SQL:
qs = TwoModel.objects.filter(record__oneval__in=[1,2,3])
qs = qs.order_by("record__root__id")
print(qs.query)
SELECT "orion_twomodel"."id", "orion_twomodel"."record_id", "orion_twomodel"."twoval" FROM "orion_twomodel" INNER JOIN "orion_onemodel" ON ("orion_twomodel"."record_id" = "orion_onemodel"."id") WHERE "orion_onemodel"."oneval" IN (1, 2, 3) ORDER BY "orion_onemodel"."root_id" ASC
So is this a potential bug or a misunderstanding on my part?
Another queryset that works around the issue and gives a reasonable SQL query and expected results:
qs = TwoModel.objects.filter(record__oneval__in=[1,2,3])
qs = qs.annotate(root_id=F("record__root_id"))
qs = qs.order_by("root_id")
print(qs.query)
SELECT "orion_twomodel"."id", "orion_twomodel"."record_id", "orion_twomodel"."twoval" FROM "orion_twomodel" INNER JOIN "orion_onemodel" ON ("orion_twomodel"."record_id" = "orion_onemodel"."id") WHERE "orion_onemodel"."oneval" IN (1, 2, 3) ORDER BY "orion_onemodel"."zero_id" ASC
ASCENDING sort, and a single INNER JOIN, as I'd expect. That actually works for my use because I need that output column anyway.
One final oddity; with the original queryset but the inverted sort order_by():
qs = TwoModel.objects.filter(record__oneval__in=[1,2,3])
qs = qs.order_by("-record__root_id")
print(qs.query)
SELECT "orion_twomodel"."id", "orion_twomodel"."record_id", "orion_twomodel"."twoval" FROM "orion_twomodel" INNER JOIN "orion_onemodel" ON ("orion_twomodel"."record_id" = "orion_onemodel"."id") LEFT OUTER JOIN "orion_onemodel" T3 ON ("orion_onemodel"."root_id" = T3."id") WHERE "orion_onemodel"."oneval" IN (1, 2, 3) ORDER BY T3."id" ASC
One gets the query with the two JOINs but an ASCENDING sort order. I was not under the impression that sort orders are somehow relative to the class level sort order, eg: does specifing order_by("-record__root_id") invert the class sort order? Testing that on a simple case doesn't show that behavior at all.
Thanks for any assistance and clarification.

409         """
410         A wrapper around connection.ops.quote_name that doesn't quote aliases
411         for table names. This avoids problems with some SQL dialects that treat
412         quoted strings specially (e.g. PostgreSQL).
413         """
414         if name in self.quote_cache:
415             return self.quote_cache[name]
416         if ((name in self.query.alias_map and name not in self.query.table_map) or
417                 name in self.query.extra_select or (
418                     self.query.external_aliases.get(name) and name not in self.query.table_map)):
419             self.quote_cache[name] = name
420             return name
421         r = self.connection.ops.quote_name(name)
422         self.quote_cache[name] = r
423         return r
424 
425     def compile(self, node):
426         vendor_impl = getattr(node, 'as_' + self.connection.vendor, None)
427         if vendor_impl:
428             sql, params = vendor_impl(self, self.connection)
429         else:
430             sql, params = node.as_sql(self, self.connection)
431         return sql, params
432 
433     def get_combinator_sql(self, combinator, all):
434         features = self.connection.features
435         compilers = [
436             query.get_compiler(self.using, self.connection)
437             for query in self.query.combined_queries if not query.is_empty()
438         ]
439         if not features.supports_slicing_ordering_in_compound:
440             for query, compiler in zip(self.query.combined_queries, compilers):
441                 if query.low_mark or query.high_mark:
442                     raise DatabaseError('LIMIT/OFFSET not allowed in subqueries of compound statements.')
443                 if compiler.get_order_by():
444                     raise DatabaseError('ORDER BY not allowed in subqueries of compound statements.')
445         parts = ()
446         for compiler in compilers:
447             try:
448                 # If the columns list is limited, then all combined queries
449                 # must have the same columns list. Set the selects defined on
450                 # the query on all combined queries, if not already set.
451                 if not compiler.query.values_select and self.query.values_select:
452                     compiler.query = compiler.query.clone()
453                     compiler.query.set_values((
454                         *self.query.extra_select,
455                         *self.query.values_select,
456                         *self.query.annotation_select,
457                     ))
458                 part_sql, part_args = compiler.as_sql()
459                 if compiler.query.combinator:
460                     # Wrap in a subquery if wrapping in parentheses isn't
461                     # supported.
462                     if not features.supports_parentheses_in_compound:
463                         part_sql = 'SELECT * FROM ({})'.format(part_sql)
464                     # Add parentheses when combining with compound query if not
465                     # already added for all compound queries.
466                     elif not features.supports_slicing_ordering_in_compound:
467                         part_sql = '({})'.format(part_sql)
468                 parts += ((part_sql, part_args),)
469             except EmptyResultSet:
470                 # Omit the empty queryset with UNION and with DIFFERENCE if the
471                 # first queryset is nonempty.
472                 if combinator == 'union' or (combinator == 'difference' and parts):
473                     continue
474                 raise
475         if not parts:
476             raise EmptyResultSet
477         combinator_sql = self.connection.ops.set_operators[combinator]
478         if all and combinator == 'union':
479             combinator_sql += ' ALL'
480         braces = '({})' if features.supports_slicing_ordering_in_compound else '{}'
481         sql_parts, args_parts = zip(*((braces.format(sql), args) for sql, args in parts))
482         result = [' {} '.format(combinator_sql).join(sql_parts)]
483         params = []
484         for part in args_parts:
485             params.extend(part)
486         return result, params
487 
488     def as_sql(self, with_limits=True, with_col_aliases=False):
489         """
490         Create the SQL for this query. Return the SQL string and list of
491         parameters.
492 
493         If 'with_limits' is False, any limit/offset information is not included
494         in the query.
495         """
496         refcounts_before = self.query.alias_refcount.copy()
497         try:
498             extra_select, order_by, group_by = self.pre_sql_setup()
499             for_update_part = None
500             # Is a LIMIT/OFFSET clause needed?
501             with_limit_offset = with_limits and (self.query.high_mark is not None or self.query.low_mark)
502             combinator = self.query.combinator
503             features = self.connection.features
504             if combinator:
505                 if not getattr(features, 'supports_select_{}'.format(combinator)):
506                     raise NotSupportedError('{} is not supported on this database backend.'.format(combinator))
507                 result, params = self.get_combinator_sql(combinator, self.query.combinator_all)
508             else:
509                 distinct_fields, distinct_params = self.get_distinct()
510                 # This must come after 'select', 'ordering', and 'distinct'
511                 # (see docstring of get_from_clause() for details).
512                 from_, f_params = self.get_from_clause()
513                 where, w_params = self.compile(self.where) if self.where is not None else ("", [])
514                 having, h_params = self.compile(self.having) if self.having is not None else ("", [])
515                 result = ['SELECT']
516                 params = []
517 
518                 if self.query.distinct:
519                     distinct_result, distinct_params = self.connection.ops.distinct_sql(
520                         distinct_fields,
521                         distinct_params,
522                     )
523                     result += distinct_result
524                     params += distinct_params
525 
526                 out_cols = []
527                 col_idx = 1
528                 for _, (s_sql, s_params), alias in self.select + extra_select:
529                     if alias:
530                         s_sql = '%s AS %s' % (s_sql, self.connection.ops.quote_name(alias))
531                     elif with_col_aliases:
532                         s_sql = '%s AS %s' % (s_sql, 'Col%d' % col_idx)
533                         col_idx += 1
534                     params.extend(s_params)
535                     out_cols.append(s_sql)
536 
537                 result += [', '.join(out_cols), 'FROM', *from_]
538                 params.extend(f_params)
539 
540                 if self.query.select_for_update and self.connection.features.has_select_for_update:
541                     if self.connection.get_autocommit():
542                         raise TransactionManagementError('select_for_update cannot be used outside of a transaction.')
543 
544                     if with_limit_offset and not self.connection.features.supports_select_for_update_with_limit:
545                         raise NotSupportedError(
546                             'LIMIT/OFFSET is not supported with '
547                             'select_for_update on this database backend.'
548                         )
549                     nowait = self.query.select_for_update_nowait
550                     skip_locked = self.query.select_for_update_skip_locked
551                     of = self.query.select_for_update_of
552                     no_key = self.query.select_for_no_key_update
553                     # If it's a NOWAIT/SKIP LOCKED/OF/NO KEY query but the
554                     # backend doesn't support it, raise NotSupportedError to
555                     # prevent a possible deadlock.
556                     if nowait and not self.connection.features.has_select_for_update_nowait:
557                         raise NotSupportedError('NOWAIT is not supported on this database backend.')
558                     elif skip_locked and not self.connection.features.has_select_for_update_skip_locked:
559                         raise NotSupportedError('SKIP LOCKED is not supported on this database backend.')
560                     elif of and not self.connection.features.has_select_for_update_of:
561                         raise NotSupportedError('FOR UPDATE OF is not supported on this database backend.')
562                     elif no_key and not self.connection.features.has_select_for_no_key_update:
563                         raise NotSupportedError(
564                             'FOR NO KEY UPDATE is not supported on this '
565                             'database backend.'
566                         )
567                     for_update_part = self.connection.ops.for_update_sql(
568                         nowait=nowait,
569                         skip_locked=skip_locked,
570                         of=self.get_select_for_update_of_arguments(),
571                         no_key=no_key,
572                     )
573 
574                 if for_update_part and self.connection.features.for_update_after_from:
575                     result.append(for_update_part)
576 
577                 if where:
578                     result.append('WHERE %s' % where)
579                     params.extend(w_params)
580 
581                 grouping = []
582                 for g_sql, g_params in group_by:
583                     grouping.append(g_sql)
584                     params.extend(g_params)
585                 if grouping:
586                     if distinct_fields:
587                         raise NotImplementedError('annotate() + distinct(fields) is not implemented.')
588                     order_by = order_by or self.connection.ops.force_no_ordering()
589                     result.append('GROUP BY %s' % ', '.join(grouping))
590                     if self._meta_ordering:
591                         order_by = None
592                 if having:
593                     result.append('HAVING %s' % having)
594                     params.extend(h_params)
595 
596             if self.query.explain_query:
597                 result.insert(0, self.connection.ops.explain_query_prefix(
598                     self.query.explain_format,
599                     **self.query.explain_options
600                 ))
601 
602             if order_by:
603                 ordering = []
604                 for _, (o_sql, o_params, _) in order_by:
605                     ordering.append(o_sql)
606                     params.extend(o_params)
607                 result.append('ORDER BY %s' % ', '.join(ordering))
608 
609             if with_limit_offset:
610                 result.append(self.connection.ops.limit_offset_sql(self.query.low_mark, self.query.high_mark))
611 
612             if for_update_part and not self.connection.features.for_update_after_from:
613                 result.append(for_update_part)
614 
615             if self.query.subquery and extra_select:
616                 # If the query is used as a subquery, the extra selects would
617                 # result in more columns than the left-hand side expression is
618                 # expecting. This can happen when a subquery uses a combination
619                 # of order_by() and distinct(), forcing the ordering expressions
620                 # to be selected as well. Wrap the query in another subquery
621                 # to exclude extraneous selects.
622                 sub_selects = []
623                 sub_params = []
624                 for index, (select, _, alias) in enumerate(self.select, start=1):
625                     if not alias and with_col_aliases:
626                         alias = 'col%d' % index
627                     if alias:
628                         sub_selects.append("%s.%s" % (
629                             self.connection.ops.quote_name('subquery'),
630                             self.connection.ops.quote_name(alias),
631                         ))
632                     else:
633                         select_clone = select.relabeled_clone({select.alias: 'subquery'})
634                         subselect, subparams = select_clone.as_sql(self, self.connection)
635                         sub_selects.append(subselect)
636                         sub_params.extend(subparams)
637                 return 'SELECT %s FROM (%s) subquery' % (
638                     ', '.join(sub_selects),
639                     ' '.join(result),
640                 ), tuple(sub_params + params)
641 
642             return ' '.join(result), tuple(params)
643         finally:
644             # Finally do cleanup - get rid of the joins we created above.
645             self.query.reset_refcounts(refcounts_before)
646 
647     def get_default_columns(self, start_alias=None, opts=None, from_parent=None):
648         """
649         Compute the default columns for selecting every field in the base
650         model. Will sometimes be called to pull in related models (e.g. via
651         select_related), in which case "opts" and "start_alias" will be given
652         to provide a starting point for the traversal.
653 
654         Return a list of strings, quoted appropriately for use in SQL
655         directly, as well as a set of aliases used in the select statement (if
656         'as_pairs' is True, return a list of (alias, col_name) pairs instead
657         of strings as the first component and None as the second component).
658         """
659         result = []
660         if opts is None:
661             opts = self.query.get_meta()
662         only_load = self.deferred_to_columns()
663         start_alias = start_alias or self.query.get_initial_alias()
664         # The 'seen_models' is used to optimize checking the needed parent
665         # alias for a given field. This also includes None -> start_alias to
666         # be used by local fields.
667         seen_models = {None: start_alias}
668 
669         for field in opts.concrete_fields:
670             model = field.model._meta.concrete_model
671             # A proxy model will have a different model and concrete_model. We
672             # will assign None if the field belongs to this model.
673             if model == opts.model:
674                 model = None
675             if from_parent and model is not None and issubclass(
676                     from_parent._meta.concrete_model, model._meta.concrete_model):
677                 # Avoid loading data for already loaded parents.
678                 # We end up here in the case select_related() resolution
679                 # proceeds from parent model to child model. In that case the
680                 # parent model data is already present in the SELECT clause,
681                 # and we want to avoid reloading the same data again.
682                 continue
683             if field.model in only_load and field.attname not in only_load[field.model]:
684                 continue
685             alias = self.query.join_parent_model(opts, model, start_alias,
686                                                  seen_models)
687             column = field.get_col(alias)
688             result.append(column)
689         return result
690 
691     def get_distinct(self):
692         """
693         Return a quoted list of fields to use in DISTINCT ON part of the query.
694 
695         This method can alter the tables in the query, and thus it must be
696         called before get_from_clause().
697         """
698         result = []
699         params = []
700         opts = self.query.get_meta()
701 
702         for name in self.query.distinct_fields:
703             parts = name.split(LOOKUP_SEP)
704             _, targets, alias, joins, path, _, transform_function = self._setup_joins(parts, opts, None)
705             targets, alias, _ = self.query.trim_joins(targets, joins, path)
706             for target in targets:
707                 if name in self.query.annotation_select:
708                     result.append(name)
709                 else:
710                     r, p = self.compile(transform_function(target, alias))
711                     result.append(r)
712                     params.append(p)
713         return result, params
714 
715     def find_ordering_name(self, name, opts, alias=None, default_order='ASC',
716                            already_seen=None):
717         """
718         Return the table alias (the name might be ambiguous, the alias will
719         not be) and column name for ordering by the given 'name' parameter.
720         The 'name' is of the form 'field1__field2__...__fieldN'.
721         """
722         name, order = get_order_dir(name, default_order)
723         descending = order == 'DESC'
724         pieces = name.split(LOOKUP_SEP)
725         field, targets, alias, joins, path, opts, transform_function = self._setup_joins(pieces, opts, alias)
726 
727         # If we get to this point and the field is a relation to another model,
728         # append the default ordering for that model unless it is the pk
729         # shortcut or the attribute name of the field that is specified.
730         if field.is_relation and opts.ordering and getattr(field, 'attname', None) != name and name != 'pk':
731             # Firstly, avoid infinite loops.
732             already_seen = already_seen or set()
733             join_tuple = tuple(getattr(self.query.alias_map[j], 'join_cols', None) for j in joins)
734             if join_tuple in already_seen:
735                 raise FieldError('Infinite loop caused by ordering.')
736             already_seen.add(join_tuple)
737 
738             results = []
739             for item in opts.ordering:
740                 if hasattr(item, 'resolve_expression') and not isinstance(item, OrderBy):
741                     item = item.desc() if descending else item.asc()
742                 if isinstance(item, OrderBy):
743                     results.append((item, False))
744                     continue
745                 results.extend(self.find_ordering_name(item, opts, alias,
746                                                        order, already_seen))
747             return results
748         targets, alias, _ = self.query.trim_joins(targets, joins, path)
749         return [(OrderBy(transform_function(t, alias), descending=descending), False) for t in targets]
750 
751     def _setup_joins(self, pieces, opts, alias):
752         """
753         Helper method for get_order_by() and get_distinct().
754 
755         get_ordering() and get_distinct() must produce same target columns on
756         same input, as the prefixes of get_ordering() and get_distinct() must
757         match. Executing SQL where this is not true is an error.
758         """
759         alias = alias or self.query.get_initial_alias()
760         field, targets, opts, joins, path, transform_function = self.query.setup_joins(pieces, opts, alias)
761         alias = joins[-1]
762         return field, targets, alias, joins, path, opts, transform_function
763 
764     def get_from_clause(self):
765         """
766         Return a list of strings that are joined together to go after the
767         "FROM" part of the query, as well as a list any extra parameters that
768         need to be included. Subclasses, can override this to create a
769         from-clause via a "select".
770 
771         This should only be called after any SQL construction methods that
772         might change the tables that are needed. This means the select columns,
773         ordering, and distinct must be done first.
774         """
775         result = []
776         params = []
777         for alias in tuple(self.query.alias_map):
778             if not self.query.alias_refcount[alias]:
779                 continue
780             try:
781                 from_clause = self.query.alias_map[alias]
782             except KeyError:
783                 # Extra tables can end up in self.tables, but not in the
784                 # alias_map if they aren't in a join. That's OK. We skip them.
785                 continue
786             clause_sql, clause_params = self.compile(from_clause)
787             result.append(clause_sql)
788             params.extend(clause_params)
789         for t in self.query.extra_tables:
790             alias, _ = self.query.table_alias(t)
791             # Only add the alias if it's not already present (the table_alias()
792             # call increments the refcount, so an alias refcount of one means
793             # this is the only reference).
794             if alias not in self.query.alias_map or self.query.alias_refcount[alias] == 1:
795                 result.append(', %s' % self.quote_name_unless_alias(alias))
796         return result, params
797 
798     def get_related_selections(self, select, opts=None, root_alias=None, cur_depth=1,
799                                requested=None, restricted=None):
800         """
801         Fill in the information needed for a select_related query. The current
802         depth is measured as the number of connections away from the root model
803         (for example, cur_depth=1 means we are looking at models with direct
804         connections to the root model).
805         """
806         def _get_field_choices():
807             direct_choices = (f.name for f in opts.fields if f.is_relation)
808             reverse_choices = (
809                 f.field.related_query_name()
810                 for f in opts.related_objects if f.field.unique
811             )
812             return chain(direct_choices, reverse_choices, self.query._filtered_relations)
813 
814         related_klass_infos = []
815         if not restricted and cur_depth > self.query.max_depth:
816             # We've recursed far enough; bail out.
817             return related_klass_infos
818 
819         if not opts:
820             opts = self.query.get_meta()
821             root_alias = self.query.get_initial_alias()
822         only_load = self.query.get_loaded_field_names()
823 
824         # Setup for the case when only particular related fields should be
825         # included in the related selection.
826         fields_found = set()
827         if requested is None:
828             restricted = isinstance(self.query.select_related, dict)
829             if restricted:
830                 requested = self.query.select_related
831 
832         def get_related_klass_infos(klass_info, related_klass_infos):
833             klass_info['related_klass_infos'] = related_klass_infos
834 
835         for f in opts.fields:
836             field_model = f.model._meta.concrete_model
837             fields_found.add(f.name)
838 
839             if restricted:
840                 next = requested.get(f.name, {})
841                 if not f.is_relation:
842                     # If a non-related field is used like a relation,
843                     # or if a single non-relational field is given.
844                     if next or f.name in requested:
845                         raise FieldError(
846                             "Non-relational field given in select_related: '%s'. "
847                             "Choices are: %s" % (
848                                 f.name,
849                                 ", ".join(_get_field_choices()) or '(none)',
850                             )
851                         )
852             else:
853                 next = False
854 
855             if not select_related_descend(f, restricted, requested,
856                                           only_load.get(field_model)):
857                 continue
858             klass_info = {
859                 'model': f.remote_field.model,
860                 'field': f,
861                 'reverse': False,
862                 'local_setter': f.set_cached_value,
863                 'remote_setter': f.remote_field.set_cached_value if f.unique else lambda x, y: None,
864                 'from_parent': False,
865             }
866             related_klass_infos.append(klass_info)
867             select_fields = []
868             _, _, _, joins, _, _ = self.query.setup_joins(
869                 [f.name], opts, root_alias)
870             alias = joins[-1]
871             columns = self.get_default_columns(start_alias=alias, opts=f.remote_field.model._meta)
872             for col in columns:
873                 select_fields.append(len(select))
874                 select.append((col, None))
875             klass_info['select_fields'] = select_fields
876             next_klass_infos = self.get_related_selections(
877                 select, f.remote_field.model._meta, alias, cur_depth + 1, next, restricted)
878             get_related_klass_infos(klass_info, next_klass_infos)
879 
880         if restricted:
881             related_fields = [
882                 (o.field, o.related_model)
883                 for o in opts.related_objects
884                 if o.field.unique and not o.many_to_many
885             ]
886             for f, model in related_fields:
887                 if not select_related_descend(f, restricted, requested,
888                                               only_load.get(model), reverse=True):
889                     continue
890 
891                 related_field_name = f.related_query_name()
892                 fields_found.add(related_field_name)
893 
894                 join_info = self.query.setup_joins([related_field_name], opts, root_alias)
895                 alias = join_info.joins[-1]
896                 from_parent = issubclass(model, opts.model) and model is not opts.model
897                 klass_info = {
898                     'model': model,
899                     'field': f,
900                     'reverse': True,
901                     'local_setter': f.remote_field.set_cached_value,
902                     'remote_setter': f.set_cached_value,
903                     'from_parent': from_parent,
904                 }
905                 related_klass_infos.append(klass_info)
906                 select_fields = []
907                 columns = self.get_default_columns(
908                     start_alias=alias, opts=model._meta, from_parent=opts.model)
909                 for col in columns:
910                     select_fields.append(len(select))
911                     select.append((col, None))
912                 klass_info['select_fields'] = select_fields
913                 next = requested.get(f.related_query_name(), {})
914                 next_klass_infos = self.get_related_selections(
915                     select, model._meta, alias, cur_depth + 1,
916                     next, restricted)
917                 get_related_klass_infos(klass_info, next_klass_infos)
918 
919             def local_setter(obj, from_obj):
920                 # Set a reverse fk object when relation is non-empty.
921                 if from_obj:
922                     f.remote_field.set_cached_value(from_obj, obj)
923 
924             def remote_setter(name, obj, from_obj):
925                 setattr(from_obj, name, obj)
926 
927             for name in list(requested):
928                 # Filtered relations work only on the topmost level.
929                 if cur_depth > 1:
930                     break
931                 if name in self.query._filtered_relations:
932                     fields_found.add(name)
933                     f, _, join_opts, joins, _, _ = self.query.setup_joins([name], opts, root_alias)
934                     model = join_opts.model
935                     alias = joins[-1]
936                     from_parent = issubclass(model, opts.model) and model is not opts.model
937                     klass_info = {
938                         'model': model,
939                         'field': f,
940                         'reverse': True,
941                         'local_setter': local_setter,
942                         'remote_setter': partial(remote_setter, name),
943                         'from_parent': from_parent,
944                     }
945                     related_klass_infos.append(klass_info)
946                     select_fields = []
947                     columns = self.get_default_columns(
948                         start_alias=alias, opts=model._meta,
949                         from_parent=opts.model,
950                     )
951                     for col in columns:
952                         select_fields.append(len(select))
953                         select.append((col, None))
954                     klass_info['select_fields'] = select_fields
955                     next_requested = requested.get(name, {})
956                     next_klass_infos = self.get_related_selections(
957                         select, opts=model._meta, root_alias=alias,
958                         cur_depth=cur_depth + 1, requested=next_requested,
959                         restricted=restricted,
960                     )
961                     get_related_klass_infos(klass_info, next_klass_infos)
962             fields_not_found = set(requested).difference(fields_found)
963             if fields_not_found:
964                 invalid_fields = ("'%s'" % s for s in fields_not_found)
965                 raise FieldError(
966                     'Invalid field name(s) given in select_related: %s. '
967                     'Choices are: %s' % (
968                         ', '.join(invalid_fields),
969                         ', '.join(_get_field_choices()) or '(none)',
970                     )
971                 )
972         return related_klass_infos

974     def get_select_for_update_of_arguments(self):
975         """
976         Return a quoted list of arguments for the SELECT FOR UPDATE OF part of
977         the query.
978         """
979         def _get_parent_klass_info(klass_info):
980             for parent_model, parent_link in klass_info['model']._meta.parents.items():
981                 parent_list = parent_model._meta.get_parent_list()
982                 yield {
983                     'model': parent_model,
984                     'field': parent_link,
985                     'reverse': False,
986                     'select_fields': [
987                         select_index
988                         for select_index in klass_info['select_fields']
989                         # Selected columns from a model or its parents.
990                         if (
991                             self.select[select_index][0].target.model == parent_model or
992                             self.select[select_index][0].target.model in parent_list
993                         )
994                     ],
995                 }
996 
997         def _get_first_selected_col_from_model(klass_info):
998             """
999             Find the first selected column from a model. If it doesn't exist,
1000             don't lock a model.
1001 
1002             select_fields is filled recursively, so it also contains fields
1003             from the parent models.
1004             """
1005             for select_index in klass_info['select_fields']:
1006                 if self.select[select_index][0].target.model == klass_info['model']:
1007                     return self.select[select_index][0]
1008 
1009         def _get_field_choices():
1010             """Yield all allowed field paths in breadth-first search order."""
1011             queue = collections.deque([(None, self.klass_info)])
1012             while queue:
1013                 parent_path, klass_info = queue.popleft()
1014                 if parent_path is None:
1015                     path = []
1016                     yield 'self'
1017                 else:
1018                     field = klass_info['field']
1019                     if klass_info['reverse']:
1020                         field = field.remote_field
1021                     path = parent_path + [field.name]
1022                     yield LOOKUP_SEP.join(path)
1023                 queue.extend(
1024                     (path, klass_info)
1025                     for klass_info in _get_parent_klass_info(klass_info)
1026                 )
1027                 queue.extend(
1028                     (path, klass_info)
1029                     for klass_info in klass_info.get('related_klass_infos', [])
1030                 )
1031         result = []
1032         invalid_names = []
1033         for name in self.query.select_for_update_of:
1034             klass_info = self.klass_info
1035             if name == 'self':
1036                 col = _get_first_selected_col_from_model(klass_info)
1037             else:
1038                 for part in name.split(LOOKUP_SEP):
1039                     klass_infos = (
1040                         *klass_info.get('related_klass_infos', []),
1041                         *_get_parent_klass_info(klass_info),
1042                     )
1043                     for related_klass_info in klass_infos:
1044                         field = related_klass_info['field']
1045                         if related_klass_info['reverse']:
1046                             field = field.remote_field
1047                         if field.name == part:
1048                             klass_info = related_klass_info
1049                             break
1050                     else:
1051                         klass_info = None
1052                         break
1053                 if klass_info is None:
1054                     invalid_names.append(name)
1055                     continue
1056                 col = _get_first_selected_col_from_model(klass_info)
1057             if col is not None:
1058                 if self.connection.features.select_for_update_of_column:
1059                     result.append(self.compile(col)[0])
1060                 else:
1061                     result.append(self.quote_name_unless_alias(col.alias))
1062         if invalid_names:
1063             raise FieldError(
1064                 'Invalid field name(s) given in select_for_update(of=(...)): %s. '
1065                 'Only relational fields followed in the query are allowed. '
1066                 'Choices are: %s.' % (
1067                     ', '.join(invalid_names),
1068                     ', '.join(_get_field_choices()),
1069                 )
1070             )
1071         return result
1072

1076         names to sets of column names which are to be loaded. Return the
1077         dictionary.

1083     def get_converters(self, expressions):
1084         converters = {}
1085         for i, expression in enumerate(expressions):
1086             if expression:
1087                 backend_converters = self.connection.ops.get_db_converters(expression)
1088                 field_converters = expression.get_db_converters(self.connection)
1089                 if backend_converters or field_converters:
1090                     converters[i] = (backend_converters + field_converters, expression)
1091         return converters

1093     def apply_converters(self, rows, converters):
1094         connection = self.connection
1095         converters = list(converters.items())
1096         for row in map(list, rows):
1097             for pos, (convs, expression) in converters:
1098                 value = row[pos]
1099                 for converter in convs:
1100                     value = converter(value, expression, connection)
1101                 row[pos] = value
1102             yield row

1104     def results_iter(self, results=None, tuple_expected=False, chunked_fetch=False,
1105                      chunk_size=GET_ITERATOR_CHUNK_SIZE):
1106         """Return an iterator over the results from executing this query."""
1107         if results is None:
1108             results = self.execute_sql(MULTI, chunked_fetch=chunked_fetch, chunk_size=chunk_size)
1109         fields = [s[0] for s in self.select[0:self.col_count]]
1110         converters = self.get_converters(fields)
1111         rows = chain.from_iterable(results)
1112         if converters:
1113             rows = self.apply_converters(rows, converters)
1114             if tuple_expected:
1115                 rows = map(tuple, rows)
1116         return rows
