524     def _print_Sum(self, expr):
525         ascii_mode = not self._use_unicode
526 
527         def asum(hrequired, lower, upper, use_ascii):
528             def adjust(s, wid=None, how='<^>'):
529                 if not wid or len(s) > wid:
530                     return s
531                 need = wid - len(s)
532                 if how == '<^>' or how == "<" or how not in list('<^>'):
533                     return s + ' '*need
534                 half = need//2
535                 lead = ' '*half
536                 if how == ">":
537                     return " "*need + s
538                 return lead + s + ' '*(need - len(lead))
539 
540             h = max(hrequired, 2)
541             d = h//2
542             w = d + 1
543             more = hrequired % 2
544 
545             lines = []
546             if use_ascii:
547                 lines.append("_"*(w) + ' ')

1440         def pretty_negative(pform, index):
1441             """Prepend a minus sign to a pretty form. """
1442             #TODO: Move this code to prettyForm
1443             if index == 0:
1444                 if pform.height() > 1:
1445                     pform_neg = '- '

1454             else:
1455                 p = pform

1458             # will print as a + ( - (b)), instead of a - (b).
1459             return prettyForm(binding=prettyForm.NEG, *p)
1460 
1461         for i, term in enumerate(terms):
1462             if term.is_Mul and _coeff_isneg(term):
1463                 coeff, other = term.as_coeff_mul(rational=False)

1471                 pforms.append(pretty_negative(pform, i))
1472             elif term.is_Relational:

1474             else:
1475                 pforms.append(self._print(term))
1476 
1477         if indices:
1478             large = True
1479 
1480             for pform in pforms:
1481                 if pform is not None and pform.height() > 1:
1482                     break
1483             else:
1484                 large = False
1485 
1486             for i in indices:
1487                 term, negative = terms[i], False
1488 
1489                 if term < 0:
1490                     term, negative = -term, True
1491 
1492                 if large:
1493                     pform = prettyForm(str(term.p))/prettyForm(str(term.q))
1494                 else:
1495                     pform = self._print(term)
1496 
1497                 if negative:

1500                 pforms[i] = pform

1504     def _print_Mul(self, product):
1505         from sympy.physics.units import Quantity
1506         a = []  # items in the numerator
1507         b = []  # items that are in the denominator (if any)
1508 
1509         if self.order not in ('old', 'none'):
1510             args = product.as_ordered_factors()
1511         else:
1512             args = list(product.args)
1513 
1514         # If quantities are present append them at the back
1515         args = sorted(args, key=lambda x: isinstance(x, Quantity) or
1516                      (isinstance(x, Pow) and isinstance(x.base, Quantity)))
1517 
1518         # Gather terms for numerator/denominator
1519         for item in args:
1520             if item.is_commutative and item.is_Pow and item.exp.is_Rational and item.exp.is_negative:
1521                 if item.exp != -1:
1522                     b.append(Pow(item.base, -item.exp, evaluate=False))
1523                 else:
1524                     b.append(Pow(item.base, -item.exp))
1525             elif item.is_Rational and item is not S.Infinity:
1526                 if item.p != 1:
1527                     a.append( Rational(item.p) )
1528                 if item.q != 1:
1529                     b.append( Rational(item.q) )
1530             else:
1531                 a.append(item)
1532 
1533         from sympy import Integral, Piecewise, Product, Sum
1534 
1535         # Convert to pretty forms. Add parens to Add instances if there
1536         # is more than one term in the numer/denom
1537         for i in range(0, len(a)):
1538             if (a[i].is_Add and len(a) > 1) or (i != len(a) - 1 and
1539                     isinstance(a[i], (Integral, Piecewise, Product, Sum))):
1540                 a[i] = prettyForm(*self._print(a[i]).parens())
1541             elif a[i].is_Relational:
1542                 a[i] = prettyForm(*self._print(a[i]).parens())
1543             else:
1544                 a[i] = self._print(a[i])
1545 
1546         for i in range(0, len(b)):
1547             if (b[i].is_Add and len(b) > 1) or (i != len(b) - 1 and
1548                     isinstance(b[i], (Integral, Piecewise, Product, Sum))):
1549                 b[i] = prettyForm(*self._print(b[i]).parens())
1550             else:
1551                 b[i] = self._print(b[i])
1552 
1553         # Construct a pretty form
1554         if len(b) == 0:
1555             return prettyForm.__mul__(*a)
1556         else:
1557             if len(a) == 0:
1558                 a.append( self._print(S.One) )
1559             return prettyForm.__mul__(*a)/prettyForm.__mul__(*b)

1561     # A helper function for _print_Pow to print x**(1/n)
1562     def _print_nth_root(self, base, expt):
1563         bpretty = self._print(base)
1564 
1565         # In very simple cases, use a single-char root sign
1566         if (self._settings['use_unicode_sqrt_char'] and self._use_unicode
1567             and expt is S.Half and bpretty.height() == 1
1568             and (bpretty.width() == 1
1569                  or (base.is_Integer and base.is_nonnegative))):
1570             return prettyForm(*bpretty.left(u'\N{SQUARE ROOT}'))
1571 
1572         # Construct root sign, start with the \/ shape
1573         _zZ = xobj('/', 1)
1574         rootsign = xobj('\\', 1) + _zZ
1575         # Make exponent number to put above it
1576         if isinstance(expt, Rational):
1577             exp = str(expt.q)
1578             if exp == '2':
1579                 exp = ''
1580         else:
1581             exp = str(expt.args[0])
1582         exp = exp.ljust(2)
1583         if len(exp) > 2:
1584             rootsign = ' '*(len(exp) - 2) + rootsign
1585         # Stack the exponent
1586         rootsign = stringPict(exp + '\n' + rootsign)
1587         rootsign.baseline = 0
1588         # Diagonal: length is one less than height of base
1589         linelength = bpretty.height() - 1
1590         diagonal = stringPict('\n'.join(
1591             ' '*(linelength - i - 1) + _zZ + ' '*i
1592             for i in range(linelength)
1593         ))
1594         # Put baseline just below lowest line: next to exp
1595         diagonal.baseline = linelength - 1
1596         # Make the root symbol
1597         rootsign = prettyForm(*rootsign.right(diagonal))
1598         # Det the baseline to match contents to fix the height
1599         # but if the height of bpretty is one, the rootsign must be one higher
1600         rootsign.baseline = max(1, bpretty.baseline)
1601         #build result
1602         s = prettyForm(hobj('_', 2 + bpretty.width()))
1603         s = prettyForm(*bpretty.above(s))
1604         s = prettyForm(*s.left(rootsign))
1605         return s

2353     This invokes a pager command using pydoc. Lines are not wrapped
2354     automatically. This routine is meant to be used with a pager that allows

You will be provided with a partial code base and an issue statement explaining a problem to resolve.
<issue>
Allow lists in the dict values of the hooks argument
Currently the Request class has a .register_hook() method but it parses the dictionary it expects from it's hooks argument weirdly: the argument can only specify one hook function per hook.  If you pass in a list of hook functions per hook the code in Request.**init**() will wrap the list in a list which then fails when the hooks are consumed (since a list is not callable).  This is especially annoying since you can not use multiple hooks from a session.  The only way to get multiple hooks now is to create the request object without sending it, then call .register_hook() multiple times and then finally call .send().

This would all be much easier if Request.**init**() parsed the hooks parameter in a way that it accepts lists as it's values.


</issue>

problem_statement:
Allow lists in the dict values of the hooks argument
Currently the Request class has a .register_hook() method but it parses the dictionary it expects from it's hooks argument weirdly: the argument can only specify one hook function per hook.  If you pass in a list of hook functions per hook the code in Request.**init**() will wrap the list in a list which then fails when the hooks are consumed (since a list is not callable).  This is especially annoying since you can not use multiple hooks from a session.  The only way to get multiple hooks now is to create the request object without sending it, then call .register_hook() multiple times and then finally call .send().

This would all be much easier if Request.**init**() parsed the hooks parameter in a way that it accepts lists as it's values.

inherited-members should support more than one class
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I have two situations:
- A class inherits from multiple other classes. I want to document members from some of the base classes but ignore some of the base classes
- A module contains several class definitions that inherit from different classes that should all be ignored (e.g., classes that inherit from list or set or tuple). I want to ignore members from list, set, and tuple while documenting all other inherited members in classes in the module.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
The :inherited-members: option to automodule should accept a list of classes. If any of these classes are encountered as base classes when instantiating autoclass documentation, they should be ignored.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
The alternative is to not use automodule, but instead manually enumerate several autoclass blocks for a module. This only addresses the second bullet in the problem description and not the first. It is also tedious for modules containing many class definitions.

187 def cut_lines(pre: int, post: int = 0, what: str = None) -> Callable:
188     """Return a listener that removes the first *pre* and last *post*
189     lines of every docstring.  If *what* is a sequence of strings,
190     only docstrings of a type in *what* will be processed.
191 
192     Use like this (e.g. in the ``setup()`` function of :file:`conf.py`)::
193 
194        from sphinx.ext.autodoc import cut_lines
195        app.connect('autodoc-process-docstring', cut_lines(4, what=['module']))
196 
197     This can (and should) be used in place of :confval:`automodule_skip_lines`.
198     """
199     def process(app: Sphinx, what_: str, name: str, obj: Any, options: Any, lines: List[str]
200                 ) -> None:
201         if what and what_ not in what:
202             return
203         del lines[:pre]
204         if post:
205             # remove one trailing blank line.
206             if lines and not lines[-1]:
207                 lines.pop(-1)
208             del lines[-post:]
209         # make sure there is a blank line at the end
210         if lines and lines[-1]:
211             lines.append('')
212     return process

215 def between(marker: str, what: Sequence[str] = None, keepempty: bool = False,
216             exclude: bool = False) -> Callable:
217     """Return a listener that either keeps, or if *exclude* is True excludes,
218     lines between lines that match the *marker* regular expression.  If no line
219     matches, the resulting docstring would be empty, so no change will be made
220     unless *keepempty* is true.
221 
222     If *what* is a sequence of strings, only docstrings of a type in *what* will
223     be processed.
224     """
225     marker_re = re.compile(marker)
226 
227     def process(app: Sphinx, what_: str, name: str, obj: Any, options: Any, lines: List[str]
228                 ) -> None:
229         if what and what_ not in what:
230             return
231         deleted = 0
232         delete = not exclude
233         orig_lines = lines[:]
234         for i, line in enumerate(orig_lines):
235             if delete:
236                 lines.pop(i - deleted)
237                 deleted += 1
238             if marker_re.match(line):
239                 delete = not delete
240                 if delete:
241                     lines.pop(i - deleted)
242                     deleted += 1
243         if not lines and not keepempty:
244             lines[:] = orig_lines
245         # make sure there is a blank line at the end
246         if lines and lines[-1]:
247             lines.append('')
248     return process

383     def parse_name(self) -> bool:

386         Returns True and sets *self.modname*, *self.objpath*, *self.fullname*,
387         *self.args* and *self.retann* if parsing and resolving was successful.

389         # first, parse the definition -- auto directives for classes and
390         # functions can contain a signature which is then used instead of
391         # an autogenerated one
392         try:
393             matched = py_ext_sig_re.match(self.name)
394             explicit_modname, path, base, args, retann = matched.groups()
395         except AttributeError:
396             logger.warning(__('invalid signature for auto%s (%r)') % (self.objtype, self.name),
397                            type='autodoc')

400         # support explicit module and class name separation via ::
401         if explicit_modname is not None:
402             modname = explicit_modname[:-2]
403             parents = path.rstrip('.').split('.') if path else []
404         else:
405             modname = None
406             parents = []

408         with mock(self.config.autodoc_mock_imports):
409             self.modname, self.objpath = self.resolve_name(modname, parents, path, base)
410 
411         if not self.modname:
412             return False
413 
414         self.args = args
415         self.retann = retann
416         self.fullname = ((self.modname or '') +
417                          ('.' + '.'.join(self.objpath) if self.objpath else ''))
418         return True

493     def format_signature(self, **kwargs: Any) -> str:
494         """Format the signature (arguments and return annotation) of the object.

496         Let the user process it via the ``autodoc-process-signature`` event.

503             # try to introspect the signature
504             try:
505                 retann = None
506                 args = self._call_format_args(**kwargs)
507                 if args:
508                     matched = re.match(r'^(\(.*\))\s+->\s+(.*)$', args)
509                     if matched:
510                         args = matched.group(1)

518                                                   self.objtype, self.fullname,
519                                                   self.object, self.options, args, retann)
520         if result:

523         if args is not None:

612                     # make a copy of docstring for attributes to avoid cache
613                     # the change of autodoc-process-docstring event.
614                     docstrings = [list(attr_docs[key])]
615 
616                     for i, line in enumerate(self.process_doc(docstrings)):
617                         self.add_line(line, sourcename, i)
618 
619         # add content from docstrings
620         if not no_docstring:
621             docstrings = self.get_doc()
622             if docstrings is None:
623                 # Do not call autodoc-process-docstring on get_doc() returns None.
624                 pass
625             else:
626                 if not docstrings:
627                     # append at least a dummy docstring, so that the event
628                     # autodoc-process-docstring is fired and can add some
629                     # content if desired
630                     docstrings.append([])
631                 for i, line in enumerate(self.process_doc(docstrings)):
632                     self.add_line(line, sourcename, i)
633 
634         # add additional content (e.g. from document), if present
635         if more_content:
636             for line, src in zip(more_content.data, more_content.items):
637                 self.add_line(line, src[0], src[1])

639     def get_object_members(self, want_all: bool) -> Tuple[bool, ObjectMembers]:
640         """Return `(members_check_module, members)` where `members` is a
641         list of `(membername, member)` pairs of the members of *self.object*.
642 
643         If *want_all* is True, return all members.  Else, only return those
644         members given by *self.options.members* (which may also be None).
645         """
646         warnings.warn('The implementation of Documenter.get_object_members() will be '
647                       'removed from Sphinx-6.0.', RemovedInSphinx60Warning)
648         members = get_object_members(self.object, self.objpath, self.get_attr, self.analyzer)
649         if not want_all:
650             if not self.options.members:
651                 return False, []  # type: ignore
652             # specific members given
653             selected = []
654             for name in self.options.members:  # type: str
655                 if name in members:
656                     selected.append((name, members[name].value))
657                 else:
658                     logger.warning(__('missing attribute %s in object %s') %
659                                    (name, self.fullname), type='autodoc')
660             return False, selected
661         elif self.options.inherited_members:
662             return False, [(m.name, m.value) for m in members.values()]
663         else:
664             return False, [(m.name, m.value) for m in members.values()
665                            if m.directly_defined]
666 
667     def filter_members(self, members: ObjectMembers, want_all: bool
668                        ) -> List[Tuple[str, Any, bool]]:
669         """Filter the given member list.
670 
671         Members are skipped if
672 
673         - they are private (except if given explicitly or the private-members
674           option is set)
675         - they are special methods (except if given explicitly or the
676           special-members option is set)
677         - they are undocumented (except if the undoc-members option is set)
678 
679         The user can override the skipping decision by connecting to the
680         ``autodoc-skip-member`` event.
681         """
682         def is_filtered_inherited_member(name: str, obj: Any) -> bool:
683             if inspect.isclass(self.object):
684                 for cls in self.object.__mro__:
685                     if cls.__name__ == self.options.inherited_members and cls != self.object:
686                         # given member is a member of specified *super class*
687                         return True
688                     elif name in cls.__dict__:
689                         return False
690                     elif name in self.get_attr(cls, '__annotations__', {}):
691                         return False
692                     elif isinstance(obj, ObjectMember) and obj.class_ is cls:
693                         return False
694 
695             return False
696 
697         ret = []
698 
699         # search for members in source code too
700         namespace = '.'.join(self.objpath)  # will be empty for modules
701 
702         if self.analyzer:
703             attr_docs = self.analyzer.find_attr_docs()
704         else:
705             attr_docs = {}
706 
707         # process members and determine which to skip
708         for obj in members:
709             try:
710                 membername, member = obj
711                 # if isattr is True, the member is documented as an attribute
712                 if member is INSTANCEATTR:
713                     isattr = True
714                 elif (namespace, membername) in attr_docs:
715                     isattr = True
716                 else:
717                     isattr = False
718 
719                 doc = getdoc(member, self.get_attr, self.config.autodoc_inherit_docstrings,
720                              self.object, membername)
721                 if not isinstance(doc, str):
722                     # Ignore non-string __doc__
723                     doc = None
724 
725                 # if the member __doc__ is the same as self's __doc__, it's just
726                 # inherited and therefore not the member's doc
727                 cls = self.get_attr(member, '__class__', None)
728                 if cls:
729                     cls_doc = self.get_attr(cls, '__doc__', None)
730                     if cls_doc == doc:
731                         doc = None
732 
733                 if isinstance(obj, ObjectMember) and obj.docstring:
734                     # hack for ClassDocumenter to inject docstring via ObjectMember
735                     doc = obj.docstring
736 
737                 doc, metadata = separate_metadata(doc)
738                 has_doc = bool(doc)
739 
740                 if 'private' in metadata:
741                     # consider a member private if docstring has "private" metadata
742                     isprivate = True
743                 elif 'public' in metadata:
744                     # consider a member public if docstring has "public" metadata
745                     isprivate = False
746                 else:
747                     isprivate = membername.startswith('_')
748 
749                 keep = False
750                 if ismock(member) and (namespace, membername) not in attr_docs:
751                     # mocked module or object
752                     pass
753                 elif (self.options.exclude_members and
754                       membername in self.options.exclude_members):
755                     # remove members given by exclude-members
756                     keep = False
757                 elif want_all and special_member_re.match(membername):
758                     # special __methods__
759                     if (self.options.special_members and
760                             membername in self.options.special_members):
761                         if membername == '__doc__':
762                             keep = False
763                         elif is_filtered_inherited_member(membername, obj):
764                             keep = False
765                         else:
766                             keep = has_doc or self.options.undoc_members
767                     else:
768                         keep = False
769                 elif (namespace, membername) in attr_docs:
770                     if want_all and isprivate:
771                         if self.options.private_members is None:
772                             keep = False
773                         else:
774                             keep = membername in self.options.private_members
775                     else:
776                         # keep documented attributes
777                         keep = True
778                 elif want_all and isprivate:
779                     if has_doc or self.options.undoc_members:
780                         if self.options.private_members is None:
781                             keep = False
782                         elif is_filtered_inherited_member(membername, obj):
783                             keep = False
784                         else:
785                             keep = membername in self.options.private_members
786                     else:
787                         keep = False
788                 else:
789                     if (self.options.members is ALL and
790                             is_filtered_inherited_member(membername, obj)):
791                         keep = False
792                     else:
793                         # ignore undocumented members if :undoc-members: is not given
794                         keep = has_doc or self.options.undoc_members
795 
796                 if isinstance(obj, ObjectMember) and obj.skipped:
797                     # forcedly skipped member (ex. a module attribute not defined in __all__)
798                     keep = False
799 
800                 # give the user a chance to decide whether this member
801                 # should be skipped
802                 if self.env.app:
803                     # let extensions preprocess docstrings
804                     skip_user = self.env.app.emit_firstresult(
805                         'autodoc-skip-member', self.objtype, membername, member,
806                         not keep, self.options)
807                     if skip_user is not None:
808                         keep = not skip_user
809             except Exception as exc:
810                 logger.warning(__('autodoc: failed to determine %s.%s (%r) to be documented, '
811                                   'the following exception was raised:\n%s'),
812                                self.name, membername, member, exc, type='autodoc')
813                 keep = False
814 
815             if keep:
816                 ret.append((membername, member, isattr))
817 
818         return ret

820     def document_members(self, all_members: bool = False) -> None:
821         """Generate reST for member documentation.
822 
823         If *all_members* is True, document all members, else those given by
824         *self.options.members*.
825         """
826         # set current namespace for finding members
827         self.env.temp_data['autodoc:module'] = self.modname
828         if self.objpath:
829             self.env.temp_data['autodoc:class'] = self.objpath[0]
830 
831         want_all = (all_members or
832                     self.options.inherited_members or
833                     self.options.members is ALL)
834         # find out which members are documentable
835         members_check_module, members = self.get_object_members(want_all)
836 
837         # document non-skipped members
838         memberdocumenters: List[Tuple[Documenter, bool]] = []
839         for (mname, member, isattr) in self.filter_members(members, want_all):
840             classes = [cls for cls in self.documenters.values()
841                        if cls.can_document_member(member, mname, isattr, self)]
842             if not classes:
843                 # don't know how to document this member
844                 continue
845             # prefer the documenter with the highest priority
846             classes.sort(key=lambda cls: cls.priority)
847             # give explicitly separated module name, so that members
848             # of inner classes can be documented
849             full_mname = self.modname + '::' + '.'.join(self.objpath + [mname])
850             documenter = classes[-1](self.directive, full_mname, self.indent)
851             memberdocumenters.append((documenter, isattr))
852 
853         member_order = self.options.member_order or self.config.autodoc_member_order
854         memberdocumenters = self.sort_members(memberdocumenters, member_order)
855 
856         for documenter, isattr in memberdocumenters:
857             documenter.generate(
858                 all_members=True, real_modname=self.real_modname,
859                 check_module=members_check_module and not isattr)
860 
861         # reset current objects
862         self.env.temp_data['autodoc:module'] = None
863         self.env.temp_data['autodoc:class'] = None
864 
865     def sort_members(self, documenters: List[Tuple["Documenter", bool]],
866                      order: str) -> List[Tuple["Documenter", bool]]:
867         """Sort the given member list."""
868         if order == 'groupwise':
869             # sort by group; alphabetically within groups
870             documenters.sort(key=lambda e: (e[0].member_order, e[0].name))
871         elif order == 'bysource':
872             if self.analyzer:
873                 # sort by source order, by virtue of the module analyzer
874                 tagorder = self.analyzer.tagorder
875 
876                 def keyfunc(entry: Tuple[Documenter, bool]) -> int:
877                     fullname = entry[0].name.split('::')[1]
878                     return tagorder.get(fullname, len(tagorder))
879                 documenters.sort(key=keyfunc)
880             else:
881                 # Assume that member discovery order matches source order.
882                 # This is a reasonable assumption in Python 3.6 and up, where
883                 # module.__dict__ is insertion-ordered.
884                 pass
885         else:  # alphabetical
886             documenters.sort(key=lambda e: e[0].name)
887 
888         return documenters
889 
890     def generate(self, more_content: Optional[StringList] = None, real_modname: str = None,
891                  check_module: bool = False, all_members: bool = False) -> None:
892         """Generate reST for the object given by *self.name*, and possibly for
893         its members.
894 
895         If *more_content* is given, include that content. If *real_modname* is
896         given, use that module name to find attribute docs. If *check_module* is
897         True, only generate if the object is defined in the module name it is
898         imported from. If *all_members* is True, document all members.
899         """
900         if not self.parse_name():
901             # need a module to import
902             logger.warning(
903                 __('don\'t know which module to import for autodocumenting '
904                    '%r (try placing a "module" or "currentmodule" directive '
905                    'in the document, or giving an explicit module name)') %
906                 self.name, type='autodoc')
907             return
908 
909         # now, import the module and get object to document
910         if not self.import_object():
911             return
912 
913         # If there is no real module defined, figure out which to use.
914         # The real module is used in the module analyzer to look up the module
915         # where the attribute documentation would actually be found in.
916         # This is used for situations where you have a module that collects the
917         # functions and classes of internal submodules.
918         guess_modname = self.get_real_modname()
919         self.real_modname: str = real_modname or guess_modname
920 
921         # try to also get a source code analyzer for attribute docs
922         try:
923             self.analyzer = ModuleAnalyzer.for_module(self.real_modname)
924             # parse right now, to get PycodeErrors on parsing (results will
925             # be cached anyway)
926             self.analyzer.find_attr_docs()
927         except PycodeError as exc:
928             logger.debug('[autodoc] module analyzer failed: %s', exc)
929             # no source file -- e.g. for builtin and C modules
930             self.analyzer = None
931             # at least add the module.__file__ as a dependency
932             if hasattr(self.module, '__file__') and self.module.__file__:
933                 self.directive.record_dependencies.add(self.module.__file__)
934         else:
935             self.directive.record_dependencies.add(self.analyzer.srcname)
936 
937         if self.real_modname != guess_modname:
938             # Add module to dependency list if target object is defined in other module.
939             try:
940                 analyzer = ModuleAnalyzer.for_module(guess_modname)
941                 self.directive.record_dependencies.add(analyzer.srcname)
942             except PycodeError:
943                 pass
944 
945         docstrings: List[str] = sum(self.get_doc() or [], [])
946         if ismock(self.object) and not docstrings:
947             logger.warning(__('A mocked object is detected: %r'),
948                            self.name, type='autodoc')
949 
950         # check __module__ of object (for members not given explicitly)
951         if check_module:
952             if not self.check_module():
953                 return
954 
955         sourcename = self.get_sourcename()
956 
957         # make sure that the result starts with an empty line.  This is
958         # necessary for some situations where another directive preprocesses
959         # reST and no starting newline is present
960         self.add_line('', sourcename)
961 
962         # format the object's signature, if any
963         try:
964             sig = self.format_signature()
965         except Exception as exc:
966             logger.warning(__('error while formatting signature for %s: %s'),
967                            self.fullname, exc, type='autodoc')
968             return
969 
970         # generate the directive header and options, if applicable
971         self.add_directive_header(sig)
972         self.add_line('', sourcename)
973 
974         # e.g. the module directive doesn't have content
975         self.indent += self.content_indent
976 
977         # add all content (from docstrings, attribute docs etc.)
978         self.add_content(more_content)
979 
980         # document members, if possible
981         self.document_members(all_members)
982

1119                     return self.__all__.index(name)
1120                 else:
1121                     return len(self.__all__)
1122             documenters.sort(key=keyfunc)
1123 
1124             return documenters
1125         else:
1126             return super().sort_members(documenters, order)

1183 class DocstringSignatureMixin:
1184     """
1185     Mixin for FunctionDocumenter and MethodDocumenter to provide the
1186     feature of reading the signature from the docstring.
1187     """
1188     _new_docstrings: List[List[str]] = None
1189     _signatures: List[str] = None
1190 
1191     def _find_signature(self) -> Tuple[str, str]:
1192         # candidates of the object name
1193         valid_names = [self.objpath[-1]]  # type: ignore
1194         if isinstance(self, ClassDocumenter):
1195             valid_names.append('__init__')
1196             if hasattr(self.object, '__mro__'):
1197                 valid_names.extend(cls.__name__ for cls in self.object.__mro__)
1198 
1199         docstrings = self.get_doc()
1200         if docstrings is None:
1201             return None, None
1202         self._new_docstrings = docstrings[:]
1203         self._signatures = []
1204         result = None
1205         for i, doclines in enumerate(docstrings):
1206             for j, line in enumerate(doclines):
1207                 if not line:
1208                     # no lines in docstring, no match
1209                     break
1210 
1211                 if line.endswith('\\'):
1212                     line = line.rstrip('\\').rstrip()
1213 
1214                 # match first line of docstring against signature RE
1215                 match = py_ext_sig_re.match(line)
1216                 if not match:
1217                     break
1218                 exmod, path, base, args, retann = match.groups()
1219 
1220                 # the base name must match ours
1221                 if base not in valid_names:
1222                     break
1223 
1224                 # re-prepare docstring to ignore more leading indentation
1225                 tab_width = self.directive.state.document.settings.tab_width  # type: ignore
1226                 self._new_docstrings[i] = prepare_docstring('\n'.join(doclines[j + 1:]),
1227                                                             tabsize=tab_width)
1228 
1229                 if result is None:
1230                     # first signature

1325     def format_signature(self, **kwargs: Any) -> str:

1327             kwargs.setdefault('unqualified_typehints', True)

1329         sigs = []

1331                 '.'.join(self.objpath) in self.analyzer.overloads and

1341             # append signature of singledispatch'ed functions
1342             for typ, func in self.object.registry.items():
1343                 if typ is object:
1344                     pass  # default implementation. skipped.
1345                 else:
1346                     dispatchfunc = self.annotate_to_first_argument(func, typ)
1347                     if dispatchfunc:
1348                         documenter = FunctionDocumenter(self.directive, '')
1349                         documenter.object = dispatchfunc
1350                         documenter.objpath = [None]
1351                         sigs.append(documenter.format_signature())
1352         if overloaded:
1353             actual = inspect.signature(self.object,
1354                                        type_aliases=self.config.autodoc_type_aliases)
1355             __globals__ = safe_getattr(self.object, '__globals__', {})
1356             for overload in self.analyzer.overloads.get('.'.join(self.objpath)):
1357                 overload = self.merge_default_value(actual, overload)
1358                 overload = evaluate_signature(overload, __globals__,
1359                                               self.config.autodoc_type_aliases)
1360 
1361                 sig = stringify_signature(overload, **kwargs)

1366     def merge_default_value(self, actual: Signature, overload: Signature) -> Signature:
1367         """Merge default values of actual implementation to the overload variants."""
1368         parameters = list(overload.parameters.values())
1369         for i, param in enumerate(parameters):
1370             actual_param = actual.parameters.get(param.name)
1371             if actual_param and param.default == '...':
1372                 parameters[i] = param.replace(default=actual_param.default)
1373 
1374         return overload.replace(parameters=parameters)

1376     def annotate_to_first_argument(self, func: Callable, typ: Type) -> Optional[Callable]:
1377         """Annotate type hint to the first argument of function if needed."""
1378         try:
1379             sig = inspect.signature(func, type_aliases=self.config.autodoc_type_aliases)
1380         except TypeError as exc:
1381             logger.warning(__("Failed to get a function signature for %s: %s"),
1382                            self.fullname, exc)
1383             return None
1384         except ValueError:
1385             return None
1386 
1387         if len(sig.parameters) == 0:
1388             return None
1389 
1390         def dummy():
1391             pass
1392 
1393         params = list(sig.parameters.values())
1394         if params[0].annotation is Parameter.empty:
1395             params[0] = params[0].replace(annotation=typ)
1396             try:
1397                 dummy.__signature__ = sig.replace(parameters=params)  # type: ignore
1398                 return dummy
1399             except (AttributeError, TypeError):
1400                 # failed to update signature (ex. built-in or extension types)
1401                 return None
1402         else:
1403             return None

1486     def _get_signature(self) -> Tuple[Optional[Any], Optional[str], Optional[Signature]]:
1487         def get_user_defined_function_or_method(obj: Any, attr: str) -> Any:
1488             """ Get the `attr` function or method from `obj`, if it is user-defined. """
1489             if inspect.is_builtin_class_method(obj, attr):
1490                 return None
1491             attr = self.get_attr(obj, attr, None)
1492             if not (inspect.ismethod(attr) or inspect.isfunction(attr)):
1493                 return None
1494             return attr
1495 
1496         # This sequence is copied from inspect._signature_from_callable.
1497         # ValueError means that no signature could be found, so we keep going.
1498 
1499         # First, we check the obj has a __signature__ attribute
1500         if (hasattr(self.object, '__signature__') and
1501                 isinstance(self.object.__signature__, Signature)):
1502             return None, None, self.object.__signature__
1503 
1504         # Next, let's see if it has an overloaded __call__ defined
1505         # in its metaclass
1506         call = get_user_defined_function_or_method(type(self.object), '__call__')
1507 
1508         if call is not None:
1509             if "{0.__module__}.{0.__qualname__}".format(call) in _METACLASS_CALL_BLACKLIST:
1510                 call = None
1511 
1512         if call is not None:
1513             self.env.app.emit('autodoc-before-process-signature', call, True)
1514             try:
1515                 sig = inspect.signature(call, bound_method=True,
1516                                         type_aliases=self.config.autodoc_type_aliases)
1517                 return type(self.object), '__call__', sig
1518             except ValueError:
1519                 pass
1520 
1521         # Now we check if the 'obj' class has a '__new__' method
1522         new = get_user_defined_function_or_method(self.object, '__new__')
1523 
1524         if new is not None:
1525             if "{0.__module__}.{0.__qualname__}".format(new) in _CLASS_NEW_BLACKLIST:
1526                 new = None
1527 
1528         if new is not None:
1529             self.env.app.emit('autodoc-before-process-signature', new, True)
1530             try:
1531                 sig = inspect.signature(new, bound_method=True,
1532                                         type_aliases=self.config.autodoc_type_aliases)
1533                 return self.object, '__new__', sig
1534             except ValueError:
1535                 pass
1536 
1537         # Finally, we should have at least __init__ implemented
1538         init = get_user_defined_function_or_method(self.object, '__init__')
1539         if init is not None:
1540             self.env.app.emit('autodoc-before-process-signature', init, True)
1541             try:
1542                 sig = inspect.signature(init, bound_method=True,
1543                                         type_aliases=self.config.autodoc_type_aliases)
1544                 return self.object, '__init__', sig
1545             except ValueError:
1546                 pass
1547 
1548         # None of the attributes are user-defined, so fall back to let inspect
1549         # handle it.
1550         # We don't know the exact method that inspect.signature will read
1551         # the signature from, so just pass the object itself to our hook.
1552         self.env.app.emit('autodoc-before-process-signature', self.object, False)
1553         try:
1554             sig = inspect.signature(self.object, bound_method=False,
1555                                     type_aliases=self.config.autodoc_type_aliases)
1556             return None, None, sig
1557         except ValueError:
1558             pass
1559 
1560         # Still no signature: happens e.g. for old-style classes
1561         # with __init__ in C and no `__text_signature__`.
1562         return None, None, None
1563 
1564     def format_args(self, **kwargs: Any) -> str:

1568             kwargs.setdefault('unqualified_typehints', True)

1570         try:

1572         except TypeError as exc:
1573             # __signature__ attribute contained junk
1574             logger.warning(__("Failed to get a constructor signature for %s: %s"),
1575                            self.fullname, exc)

1578         if sig is None:

1589         for i, sig in enumerate(self._signatures):
1590             if sig.endswith(' -> None'):
1591                 # Strip a return value from signatures of constructor in docstring (subsequent
1592                 # entries)

problem_statement:
inherited-members should support more than one class
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I have two situations:
- A class inherits from multiple other classes. I want to document members from some of the base classes but ignore some of the base classes
- A module contains several class definitions that inherit from different classes that should all be ignored (e.g., classes that inherit from list or set or tuple). I want to ignore members from list, set, and tuple while documenting all other inherited members in classes in the module.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
The :inherited-members: option to automodule should accept a list of classes. If any of these classes are encountered as base classes when instantiating autoclass documentation, they should be ignored.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
The alternative is to not use automodule, but instead manually enumerate several autoclass blocks for a module. This only addresses the second bullet in the problem description and not the first. It is also tedious for modules containing many class definitions.

393     def _print_Integral(self, integral):
394         f = integral.function
395 
396         # Add parentheses if arg involves addition of terms and
397         # create a pretty form for the argument
398         prettyF = self._print(f)
399         # XXX generalize parens
400         if f.is_Add:
401             prettyF = prettyForm(*prettyF.parens())
402 
403         # dx dy dz ...
404         arg = prettyF
405         for x in integral.limits:
406             prettyArg = self._print(x[0])
407             # XXX qparens (parens if needs-parens)
408             if prettyArg.width() > 1:
409                 prettyArg = prettyForm(*prettyArg.parens())
410 
411             arg = prettyForm(*arg.right(' d', prettyArg))
412 
413         # \int \int \int ...
414         firstterm = True
415         s = None
416         for lim in integral.limits:
417             x = lim[0]
418             # Create bar based on the height of the argument
419             h = arg.height()
420             H = h + 2
421 
422             # XXX hack!
423             ascii_mode = not self._use_unicode
424             if ascii_mode:
425                 H += 2
426 
427             vint = vobj('int', H)
428 
429             # Construct the pretty form with the integral sign and the argument
430             pform = prettyForm(vint)
431             pform.baseline = arg.baseline + (
432                 H - h)//2    # covering the whole argument
433 
434             if len(lim) > 1:
435                 # Create pretty forms for endpoints, if definite integral.
436                 # Do not print empty endpoints.
437                 if len(lim) == 2:
438                     prettyA = prettyForm("")
439                     prettyB = self._print(lim[1])
440                 if len(lim) == 3:
441                     prettyA = self._print(lim[1])
442                     prettyB = self._print(lim[2])
443 
444                 if ascii_mode:  # XXX hack
445                     # Add spacing so that endpoint can more easily be
446                     # identified with the correct integral sign
447                     spc = max(1, 3 - prettyB.width())
448                     prettyB = prettyForm(*prettyB.left(' ' * spc))
449 
450                     spc = max(1, 4 - prettyA.width())
451                     prettyA = prettyForm(*prettyA.right(' ' * spc))
452 
453                 pform = prettyForm(*pform.above(prettyB))
454                 pform = prettyForm(*pform.below(prettyA))
455 
456             if not ascii_mode:  # XXX hack
457                 pform = prettyForm(*pform.right(' '))
458 
459             if firstterm:
460                 s = pform   # first term
461                 firstterm = False
462             else:
463                 s = prettyForm(*s.left(pform))
464 
465         pform = prettyForm(*arg.left(s))
466         pform.binding = prettyForm.MUL
467         return pform

492             for i in range(func_height + 1):

518             pretty_func = prettyForm(*pretty_sign.right(pretty_func))

524     def _print_Sum(self, expr):
525         ascii_mode = not self._use_unicode
526 
527         def asum(hrequired, lower, upper, use_ascii):
528             def adjust(s, wid=None, how='<^>'):
529                 if not wid or len(s) > wid:
530                     return s
531                 need = wid - len(s)
532                 if how == '<^>' or how == "<" or how not in list('<^>'):
533                     return s + ' '*need
534                 half = need//2
535                 lead = ' '*half
536                 if how == ">":
537                     return " "*need + s
538                 return lead + s + ' '*(need - len(lead))
539 
540             h = max(hrequired, 2)
541             d = h//2
542             w = d + 1
543             more = hrequired % 2
544 
545             lines = []
546             if use_ascii:
547                 lines.append("_"*(w) + ' ')
548                 lines.append(r"\%s`" % (' '*(w - 1)))
549                 for i in range(1, d):
550                     lines.append('%s\\%s' % (' '*i, ' '*(w - i)))
551                 if more:
552                     lines.append('%s)%s' % (' '*(d), ' '*(w - d)))
553                 for i in reversed(range(1, d)):
554                     lines.append('%s/%s' % (' '*i, ' '*(w - i)))
555                 lines.append("/" + "_"*(w - 1) + ',')
556                 return d, h + more, lines, 0
557             else:
558                 w = w + more
559                 d = d + more
560                 vsum = vobj('sum', 4)
561                 lines.append("_"*(w))
562                 for i in range(0, d):
563                     lines.append('%s%s%s' % (' '*i, vsum[2], ' '*(w - i - 1)))
564                 for i in reversed(range(0, d)):
565                     lines.append('%s%s%s' % (' '*i, vsum[4], ' '*(w - i - 1)))
566                 lines.append(vsum[8]*(w))
567                 return d, h + 2*more, lines, more
568 
569         f = expr.function
570 
571         prettyF = self._print(f)
572 
573         if f.is_Add:  # add parens
574             prettyF = prettyForm(*prettyF.parens())
575 
576         H = prettyF.height() + 2
577 
578         # \sum \sum \sum ...
579         first = True
580         max_upper = 0
581         sign_height = 0
582 
583         for lim in expr.limits:
584             if len(lim) == 3:
585                 prettyUpper = self._print(lim[2])
586                 prettyLower = self._print(Equality(lim[0], lim[1]))
587             elif len(lim) == 2:
588                 prettyUpper = self._print("")
589                 prettyLower = self._print(Equality(lim[0], lim[1]))
590             elif len(lim) == 1:
591                 prettyUpper = self._print("")
592                 prettyLower = self._print(lim[0])
593 
594             max_upper = max(max_upper, prettyUpper.height())
595 
596             # Create sum sign based on the height of the argument
597             d, h, slines, adjustment = asum(
598                 H, prettyLower.width(), prettyUpper.width(), ascii_mode)
599             prettySign = stringPict('')
600             prettySign = prettyForm(*prettySign.stack(*slines))
601 
602             if first:
603                 sign_height = prettySign.height()
604 
605             prettySign = prettyForm(*prettySign.above(prettyUpper))
606             prettySign = prettyForm(*prettySign.below(prettyLower))
607 
608             if first:
609                 # change F baseline so it centers on the sign
610                 prettyF.baseline -= d - (prettyF.height()//2 -
611                                          prettyF.baseline) - adjustment
612                 first = False
613 
614             # put padding to the right
615             pad = stringPict('')
616             pad = prettyForm(*pad.stack(*[' ']*h))
617             prettySign = prettyForm(*prettySign.right(pad))
618             # put the present prettyF to the right
619             prettyF = prettyForm(*prettySign.right(prettyF))
620 
621         prettyF.baseline = max_upper + sign_height//2
622         prettyF.binding = prettyForm.MUL
623         return prettyF
624

653     def _print_matrix_contents(self, e):
654         """
655         This method factors out what is essentially grid printing.
656         """
657         M = e   # matrix
658         Ms = {}  # i,j -> pretty(M[i,j])
659         for i in range(M.rows):
660             for j in range(M.cols):
661                 Ms[i, j] = self._print(M[i, j])
662 
663         # h- and v- spacers
664         hsep = 2
665         vsep = 1
666 
667         # max width for columns
668         maxw = [-1] * M.cols
669 
670         for j in range(M.cols):
671             maxw[j] = max([Ms[i, j].width() for i in range(M.rows)] or [0])
672 
673         # drawing result
674         D = None
675 
676         for i in range(M.rows):
677 
678             D_row = None
679             for j in range(M.cols):
680                 s = Ms[i, j]
681 
682                 # reshape s to maxw
683                 # XXX this should be generalized, and go to stringPict.reshape ?
684                 assert s.width() <= maxw[j]
685 
686                 # hcenter it, +0.5 to the right                        2
687                 # ( it's better to align formula starts for say 0 and r )
688                 # XXX this is not good in all cases -- maybe introduce vbaseline?
689                 wdelta = maxw[j] - s.width()
690                 wleft = wdelta // 2
691                 wright = wdelta - wleft
692 
693                 s = prettyForm(*s.right(' '*wright))
694                 s = prettyForm(*s.left(' '*wleft))
695 
696                 # we don't need vcenter cells -- this is automatically done in
697                 # a pretty way because when their baselines are taking into
698                 # account in .right()
699 
700                 if D_row is None:
701                     D_row = s   # first box in a row
702                     continue
703 
704                 D_row = prettyForm(*D_row.right(' '*hsep))  # h-spacer
705                 D_row = prettyForm(*D_row.right(s))
706 
707             if D is None:
708                 D = D_row       # first row in a picture
709                 continue
710 
711             # v-spacer
712             for _ in range(vsep):
713                 D = prettyForm(*D.below(' '))
714 
715             D = prettyForm(*D.below(D_row))
716 
717         if D is None:
718             D = prettyForm('')  # Empty Matrix
719 
720         return D

889     def _print_BasisDependent(self, expr):
890         from sympy.vector import Vector
891 
892         if not self._use_unicode:
893             raise NotImplementedError("ASCII pretty printing of BasisDependent is not implemented")
894 
895         if expr == expr.zero:
896             return prettyForm(expr.zero._pretty_form)
897         o1 = []
898         vectstrs = []
899         if isinstance(expr, Vector):
900             items = expr.separate().items()
901         else:
902             items = [(0, expr)]
903         for system, vect in items:
904             inneritems = list(vect.components.items())
905             inneritems.sort(key = lambda x: x[0].__str__())
906             for k, v in inneritems:
907                 #if the coef of the basis vector is 1
908                 #we skip the 1
909                 if v == 1:
910                     o1.append(u"" +
911                               k._pretty_form)
912                 #Same for -1
913                 elif v == -1:
914                     o1.append(u"(-1) " +
915                               k._pretty_form)
916                 #For a general expr
917                 else:
918                     #We always wrap the measure numbers in
919                     #parentheses
920                     arg_str = self._print(
921                         v).parens()[0]
922 
923                     o1.append(arg_str + ' ' + k._pretty_form)
924                 vectstrs.append(k._pretty_form)
925 
926         #outstr = u("").join(o1)
927         if o1[0].startswith(u" + "):
928             o1[0] = o1[0][3:]
929         elif o1[0].startswith(" "):
930             o1[0] = o1[0][1:]
931         #Fixing the newlines
932         lengths = []
933         strs = ['']
934         flag = []
935         for i, partstr in enumerate(o1):
936             flag.append(0)
937             # XXX: What is this hack?
938             if '\n' in partstr:
939                 tempstr = partstr
940                 tempstr = tempstr.replace(vectstrs[i], '')
941                 if u'\N{right parenthesis extension}' in tempstr:   # If scalar is a fraction
942                     for paren in range(len(tempstr)):
943                         flag[i] = 1
944                         if tempstr[paren] == u'\N{right parenthesis extension}':
945                             tempstr = tempstr[:paren] + u'\N{right parenthesis extension}'\
946                                          + ' '  + vectstrs[i] + tempstr[paren + 1:]
947                             break
948                 elif u'\N{RIGHT PARENTHESIS LOWER HOOK}' in tempstr:
949                     flag[i] = 1
950                     tempstr = tempstr.replace(u'\N{RIGHT PARENTHESIS LOWER HOOK}',
951                                         u'\N{RIGHT PARENTHESIS LOWER HOOK}'
952                                         + ' ' + vectstrs[i])
953                 else:
954                     tempstr = tempstr.replace(u'\N{RIGHT PARENTHESIS UPPER HOOK}',
955                                         u'\N{RIGHT PARENTHESIS UPPER HOOK}'
956                                         + ' ' + vectstrs[i])
957                 o1[i] = tempstr
958 
959         o1 = [x.split('\n') for x in o1]
960         n_newlines = max([len(x) for x in o1])  # Width of part in its pretty form
961 
962         if 1 in flag:                           # If there was a fractional scalar
963             for i, parts in enumerate(o1):
964                 if len(parts) == 1:             # If part has no newline
965                     parts.insert(0, ' ' * (len(parts[0])))
966                     flag[i] = 1
967 
968         for i, parts in enumerate(o1):
969             lengths.append(len(parts[flag[i]]))
970             for j in range(n_newlines):
971                 if j+1 <= len(parts):
972                     if j >= len(strs):
973                         strs.append(' ' * (sum(lengths[:-1]) +
974                                            3*(len(lengths)-1)))
975                     if j == flag[i]:
976                         strs[flag[i]] += parts[flag[i]] + ' + '
977                     else:
978                         strs[j] += parts[j] + ' '*(lengths[-1] -
979                                                    len(parts[j])+
980                                                    3)
981                 else:
982                     if j >= len(strs):
983                         strs.append(' ' * (sum(lengths[:-1]) +
984                                            3*(len(lengths)-1)))
985                     strs[j] += ' '*(lengths[-1]+3)
986 
987         return prettyForm(u'\n'.join([s[:-3] for s in strs]))

989     def _print_NDimArray(self, expr):
990         from sympy import ImmutableMatrix
991 
992         if expr.rank() == 0:
993             return self._print(expr[()])
994 
995         level_str = [[]] + [[] for i in range(expr.rank())]
996         shape_ranges = [list(range(i)) for i in expr.shape]
997         for outer_i in itertools.product(*shape_ranges):
998             level_str[-1].append(expr[outer_i])
999             even = True
1000             for back_outer_i in range(expr.rank()-1, -1, -1):
1001                 if len(level_str[back_outer_i+1]) < expr.shape[back_outer_i]:
1002                     break
1003                 if even:
1004                     level_str[back_outer_i].append(level_str[back_outer_i+1])
1005                 else:
1006                     level_str[back_outer_i].append(ImmutableMatrix(level_str[back_outer_i+1]))
1007                     if len(level_str[back_outer_i + 1]) == 1:
1008                         level_str[back_outer_i][-1] = ImmutableMatrix([[level_str[back_outer_i][-1]]])
1009                 even = not even
1010                 level_str[back_outer_i+1] = []
1011 
1012         out_expr = level_str[0][0]
1013         if expr.rank() % 2 == 1:
1014             out_expr = ImmutableMatrix([out_expr])
1015 
1016         return self._print(out_expr)

1023     def _print_Piecewise(self, pexpr):
1024 
1025         P = {}
1026         for n, ec in enumerate(pexpr.args):
1027             P[n, 0] = self._print(ec.expr)
1028             if ec.cond == True:
1029                 P[n, 1] = prettyForm('otherwise')
1030             else:
1031                 P[n, 1] = prettyForm(
1032                     *prettyForm('for ').right(self._print(ec.cond)))
1033         hsep = 2
1034         vsep = 1
1035         len_args = len(pexpr.args)
1036 
1037         # max widths
1038         maxw = [max([P[i, j].width() for i in range(len_args)])
1039                 for j in range(2)]
1040 
1041         # FIXME: Refactor this code and matrix into some tabular environment.
1042         # drawing result
1043         D = None
1044 
1045         for i in range(len_args):
1046             D_row = None
1047             for j in range(2):
1048                 p = P[i, j]
1049                 assert p.width() <= maxw[j]
1050 
1051                 wdelta = maxw[j] - p.width()
1052                 wleft = wdelta // 2
1053                 wright = wdelta - wleft
1054 
1055                 p = prettyForm(*p.right(' '*wright))
1056                 p = prettyForm(*p.left(' '*wleft))
1057 
1058                 if D_row is None:
1059                     D_row = p
1060                     continue
1061 
1062                 D_row = prettyForm(*D_row.right(' '*hsep))  # h-spacer
1063                 D_row = prettyForm(*D_row.right(p))
1064             if D is None:
1065                 D = D_row       # first row in a picture
1066                 continue
1067 
1068             # v-spacer
1069             for _ in range(vsep):
1070                 D = prettyForm(*D.below(' '))
1071 
1072             D = prettyForm(*D.below(D_row))
1073 
1074         D = prettyForm(*D.parens('{', ''))
1075         D.baseline = D.height()//2
1076         D.binding = prettyForm.OPEN
1077         return D

1103     def _print_hyper(self, e):
1104         # FIXME refactor Matrix, Piecewise, and this into a tabular environment
1105         ap = [self._print(a) for a in e.ap]
1106         bq = [self._print(b) for b in e.bq]
1107 
1108         P = self._print(e.argument)
1109         P.baseline = P.height()//2
1110 
1111         # Drawing result - first create the ap, bq vectors
1112         D = None
1113         for v in [ap, bq]:
1114             D_row = self._hprint_vec(v)
1115             if D is None:
1116                 D = D_row       # first row in a picture
1117             else:
1118                 D = prettyForm(*D.below(' '))
1119                 D = prettyForm(*D.below(D_row))
1120 
1121         # make sure that the argument `z' is centred vertically
1122         D.baseline = D.height()//2
1123 
1124         # insert horizontal separator
1125         P = prettyForm(*P.left(' '))
1126         D = prettyForm(*D.right(' '))
1127 
1128         # insert separating `|`
1129         D = self._hprint_vseparator(D, P)
1130 
1131         # add parens
1132         D = prettyForm(*D.parens('(', ')'))
1133 
1134         # create the F symbol
1135         above = D.height()//2 - 1
1136         below = D.height() - above - 1
1137 
1138         sz, t, b, add, img = annotated('F')
1139         F = prettyForm('\n' * (above - t) + img + '\n' * (below - b),
1140                        baseline=above + sz)
1141         add = (sz + 1)//2
1142 
1143         F = prettyForm(*F.left(self._print(len(e.ap))))
1144         F = prettyForm(*F.right(self._print(len(e.bq))))
1145         F.baseline = above + add
1146 
1147         D = prettyForm(*F.right(' ', D))
1148 
1149         return D

1151     def _print_meijerg(self, e):
1152         # FIXME refactor Matrix, Piecewise, and this into a tabular environment
1153 
1154         v = {}
1155         v[(0, 0)] = [self._print(a) for a in e.an]
1156         v[(0, 1)] = [self._print(a) for a in e.aother]
1157         v[(1, 0)] = [self._print(b) for b in e.bm]
1158         v[(1, 1)] = [self._print(b) for b in e.bother]
1159 
1160         P = self._print(e.argument)
1161         P.baseline = P.height()//2
1162 
1163         vp = {}
1164         for idx in v:
1165             vp[idx] = self._hprint_vec(v[idx])
1166 
1167         for i in range(2):
1168             maxw = max(vp[(0, i)].width(), vp[(1, i)].width())
1169             for j in range(2):
1170                 s = vp[(j, i)]
1171                 left = (maxw - s.width()) // 2
1172                 right = maxw - left - s.width()
1173                 s = prettyForm(*s.left(' ' * left))
1174                 s = prettyForm(*s.right(' ' * right))
1175                 vp[(j, i)] = s
1176 
1177         D1 = prettyForm(*vp[(0, 0)].right('  ', vp[(0, 1)]))
1178         D1 = prettyForm(*D1.below(' '))
1179         D2 = prettyForm(*vp[(1, 0)].right('  ', vp[(1, 1)]))
1180         D = prettyForm(*D1.below(D2))
1181 
1182         # make sure that the argument `z' is centred vertically
1183         D.baseline = D.height()//2
1184 
1185         # insert horizontal separator
1186         P = prettyForm(*P.left(' '))
1187         D = prettyForm(*D.right(' '))
1188 
1189         # insert separating `|`
1190         D = self._hprint_vseparator(D, P)
1191 
1192         # add parens
1193         D = prettyForm(*D.parens('(', ')'))
1194 
1195         # create the G symbol
1196         above = D.height()//2 - 1
1197         below = D.height() - above - 1
1198 
1199         sz, t, b, add, img = annotated('G')
1200         F = prettyForm('\n' * (above - t) + img + '\n' * (below - b),
1201                        baseline=above + sz)
1202 
1203         pp = self._print(len(e.ap))
1204         pq = self._print(len(e.bq))
1205         pm = self._print(len(e.bm))
1206         pn = self._print(len(e.an))
1207 
1208         def adjust(p1, p2):
1209             diff = p1.width() - p2.width()
1210             if diff == 0:
1211                 return p1, p2
1212             elif diff > 0:
1213                 return p1, prettyForm(*p2.left(' '*diff))
1214             else:
1215                 return prettyForm(*p1.left(' '*-diff)), p2
1216         pp, pm = adjust(pp, pm)
1217         pq, pn = adjust(pq, pn)
1218         pu = prettyForm(*pm.right(', ', pn))
1219         pl = prettyForm(*pp.right(', ', pq))
1220 
1221         ht = F.baseline - above - 2
1222         if ht > 0:
1223             pu = prettyForm(*pu.below('\n'*ht))
1224         p = prettyForm(*pu.below(pl))
1225 
1226         F.baseline = above
1227         F = prettyForm(*F.right(p))
1228 
1229         F.baseline = above + add
1230 
1231         D = prettyForm(*F.right(' ', D))
1232 
1233         return D

1456     def _print_Add(self, expr, order=None):
1457         if self.order == 'none':
1458             terms = list(expr.args)
1459         else:
1460             terms = self._as_ordered_terms(expr, order=order)
1461         pforms, indices = [], []
1462 
1463         def pretty_negative(pform, index):
1464             """Prepend a minus sign to a pretty form. """
1465             #TODO: Move this code to prettyForm
1466             if index == 0:
1467                 if pform.height() > 1:
1468                     pform_neg = '- '
1469                 else:
1470                     pform_neg = '-'
1471             else:
1472                 pform_neg = ' - '
1473 
1474             if (pform.binding > prettyForm.NEG
1475                 or pform.binding == prettyForm.ADD):
1476                 p = stringPict(*pform.parens())
1477             else:
1478                 p = pform
1479             p = stringPict.next(pform_neg, p)
1480             # Lower the binding to NEG, even if it was higher. Otherwise, it
1481             # will print as a + ( - (b)), instead of a - (b).
1482             return prettyForm(binding=prettyForm.NEG, *p)
1483 
1484         for i, term in enumerate(terms):
1485             if term.is_Mul and _coeff_isneg(term):
1486                 coeff, other = term.as_coeff_mul(rational=False)
1487                 pform = self._print(Mul(-coeff, *other, evaluate=False))
1488                 pforms.append(pretty_negative(pform, i))
1489             elif term.is_Rational and term.q > 1:
1490                 pforms.append(None)
1491                 indices.append(i)
1492             elif term.is_Number and term < 0:
1493                 pform = self._print(-term)
1494                 pforms.append(pretty_negative(pform, i))
1495             elif term.is_Relational:
1496                 pforms.append(prettyForm(*self._print(term).parens()))
1497             else:
1498                 pforms.append(self._print(term))
1499 
1500         if indices:
1501             large = True
1502 
1503             for pform in pforms:
1504                 if pform is not None and pform.height() > 1:
1505                     break
1506             else:
1507                 large = False
1508 
1509             for i in indices:
1510                 term, negative = terms[i], False
1511 
1512                 if term < 0:
1513                     term, negative = -term, True
1514 
1515                 if large:
1516                     pform = prettyForm(str(term.p))/prettyForm(str(term.q))
1517                 else:
1518                     pform = self._print(term)
1519 
1520                 if negative:
1521                     pform = pretty_negative(pform, i)
1522 
1523                 pforms[i] = pform
1524 
1525         return prettyForm.__add__(*pforms)

1527     def _print_Mul(self, product):
1528         from sympy.physics.units import Quantity
1529         a = []  # items in the numerator
1530         b = []  # items that are in the denominator (if any)
1531 
1532         if self.order not in ('old', 'none'):
1533             args = product.as_ordered_factors()
1534         else:
1535             args = list(product.args)
1536 
1537         # If quantities are present append them at the back
1538         args = sorted(args, key=lambda x: isinstance(x, Quantity) or
1539                      (isinstance(x, Pow) and isinstance(x.base, Quantity)))
1540 
1541         # Gather terms for numerator/denominator
1542         for item in args:
1543             if item.is_commutative and item.is_Pow and item.exp.is_Rational and item.exp.is_negative:
1544                 if item.exp != -1:
1545                     b.append(Pow(item.base, -item.exp, evaluate=False))
1546                 else:
1547                     b.append(Pow(item.base, -item.exp))
1548             elif item.is_Rational and item is not S.Infinity:
1549                 if item.p != 1:
1550                     a.append( Rational(item.p) )
1551                 if item.q != 1:
1552                     b.append( Rational(item.q) )
1553             else:
1554                 a.append(item)
1555 
1556         from sympy import Integral, Piecewise, Product, Sum
1557 
1558         # Convert to pretty forms. Add parens to Add instances if there
1559         # is more than one term in the numer/denom
1560         for i in range(0, len(a)):
1561             if (a[i].is_Add and len(a) > 1) or (i != len(a) - 1 and
1562                     isinstance(a[i], (Integral, Piecewise, Product, Sum))):
1563                 a[i] = prettyForm(*self._print(a[i]).parens())
1564             elif a[i].is_Relational:
1565                 a[i] = prettyForm(*self._print(a[i]).parens())
1566             else:
1567                 a[i] = self._print(a[i])
1568 
1569         for i in range(0, len(b)):
1570             if (b[i].is_Add and len(b) > 1) or (i != len(b) - 1 and
1571                     isinstance(b[i], (Integral, Piecewise, Product, Sum))):
1572                 b[i] = prettyForm(*self._print(b[i]).parens())
1573             else:
1574                 b[i] = self._print(b[i])
1575 
1576         # Construct a pretty form
1577         if len(b) == 0:
1578             return prettyForm.__mul__(*a)
1579         else:
1580             if len(a) == 0:
1581                 a.append( self._print(S.One) )
1582             return prettyForm.__mul__(*a)/prettyForm.__mul__(*b)

1584     # A helper function for _print_Pow to print x**(1/n)
1585     def _print_nth_root(self, base, expt):
1586         bpretty = self._print(base)
1587 
1588         # In very simple cases, use a single-char root sign
1589         if (self._settings['use_unicode_sqrt_char'] and self._use_unicode
1590             and expt is S.Half and bpretty.height() == 1
1591             and (bpretty.width() == 1
1592                  or (base.is_Integer and base.is_nonnegative))):
1593             return prettyForm(*bpretty.left(u'\N{SQUARE ROOT}'))
1594 
1595         # Construct root sign, start with the \/ shape
1596         _zZ = xobj('/', 1)
1597         rootsign = xobj('\\', 1) + _zZ
1598         # Make exponent number to put above it
1599         if isinstance(expt, Rational):
1600             exp = str(expt.q)
1601             if exp == '2':
1602                 exp = ''
1603         else:
1604             exp = str(expt.args[0])
1605         exp = exp.ljust(2)
1606         if len(exp) > 2:
1607             rootsign = ' '*(len(exp) - 2) + rootsign
1608         # Stack the exponent
1609         rootsign = stringPict(exp + '\n' + rootsign)
1610         rootsign.baseline = 0
1611         # Diagonal: length is one less than height of base
1612         linelength = bpretty.height() - 1
1613         diagonal = stringPict('\n'.join(
1614             ' '*(linelength - i - 1) + _zZ + ' '*i
1615             for i in range(linelength)
1616         ))
1617         # Put baseline just below lowest line: next to exp
1618         diagonal.baseline = linelength - 1
1619         # Make the root symbol
1620         rootsign = prettyForm(*rootsign.right(diagonal))
1621         # Det the baseline to match contents to fix the height
1622         # but if the height of bpretty is one, the rootsign must be one higher
1623         rootsign.baseline = max(1, bpretty.baseline)
1624         #build result
1625         s = prettyForm(hobj('_', 2 + bpretty.width()))
1626         s = prettyForm(*bpretty.above(s))
1627         s = prettyForm(*s.left(rootsign))
1628         return s

1630     def _print_Pow(self, power):
1631         from sympy.simplify.simplify import fraction
1632         b, e = power.as_base_exp()
1633         if power.is_commutative:

1635                 return prettyForm("1")/self._print(b)
1636             n, d = fraction(e)
1637             if n is S.One and d.is_Atom and not e.is_Integer:
1638                 return self._print_nth_root(b, e)
1639             if e.is_Rational and e < 0:
1640                 return prettyForm("1")/self._print(Pow(b, -e, evaluate=False))
1641 
1642         if b.is_Relational:
1643             return prettyForm(*self._print(b).parens()).__pow__(self._print(e))
1644 
1645         return self._print(b)**self._print(e)
